# Known bugs and unverified features

Every bug found in Margo Engine is logged here with a repro and its cause, fixed or not, and an open one stays here
until it is fixed. Entries are newest first. A heading starts with the state (Open, Fixed with its date, Corrected);
an entry gives the **Repro**, the **Cause** and, once fixed, the commit and the regression test that keeps it fixed.
"Needs a maintainer decision" marks a fix that would change what a check accepts or touch the frozen core. Report a
new bug as [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs) describes.

### Open: person-still's Lantern prop changes 992 to 993 pixels between roughness 0.3 and 0.8, under its 1,000 bar (KB-HUMANS-PROPSKY1, humans test)

- Repro: `node packages/humans/test/person-still.mjs` (and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`) on the workstation, 2026-11-28, at
  origin/main 23b89ba321 plus the KB-SKIN-BULGE1 change. Its log prints `prop {"lit":993,"off":0}` (WebGL2: 992), and
  the assertion "the sky reflection on the prop reads its roughness" wants more than 1,000; the outfit beside it
  changes 7,556 pixels and passes.
- Ruled out: the skinning. The same run with the person drawn by dual quaternion skinning (the old default) prints
  the same 993, and the prop is an unskinned Lantern on the left of the frame.
- Cause not found yet: the prop does join the sky (`joined` true, `off` 0), so its reflection is there but small at
  this framing; whether the prop's framing, the sky's overcast fill or the bar moved is still to be measured. The bar
  is not lowered.

### Open: a Character Creator coat skirt swings out whole at bent hips, its hem a ring around the legs (KB-SKIN-SKIRT1, humans)

- **Repro:** `addPerson` on the Fauld cast's old man (`civ_old_man.glb`), the skin sheet
  (`node packages/humans/test/skin-sheet.browser.mjs --model=<file>`), rows "seated" and "elbows and knees at full
  flexion": the coat's hem leaves the legs and hangs as a ring around them, the back panel swung forward with the front.
  Blender 5.3 with its own importer shows the same with linear and with Preserve Volume skinning (frames
  `blender-hips90-*` in the rigging lane's `rigging-frames/g9`), so it is the weights, not Margo's skinning.
- **Cause:** every one of the coat's 2,478 hem vertices, front, back and sides alike, is weighed about 0.28 right thigh,
  0.27 left thigh, 0.24 waist and 0.21 pelvis (Character Creator's even skirt weighting, which keeps a skirt whole
  between the legs on a walk). At 90 degrees of hip flexion the whole hem turns about half way with both thighs, so the
  back of the coat swings forward and up as far as the front.
- **Fix to build:** garment weights rebuilt from the body and the layers under them where the cloth is close, and
  inpainted where it hangs free (Abdrashitov et al. 2023), with the even skirt kept only between the legs; the body
  under this coat is cut away, so the trousers and shirt are the source there. Owner: `@margoengine/humans` (a garment
  pass in `addPerson`) or `@margoengine/rigging` (the weight solver, rigging group 9 or 10).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a coat balloons at a raised shoulder and over bent hips under dual quaternion skinning (KB-SKIN-BULGE1, animation)

- **Repro:** the old man's skin sheet as above, row "arms raised: left 90 to the side, right 170 overhead": under
  `addPerson`'s dual quaternion default the coat's right side panel swells into a sack from armpit to hip; the bent hip
  rows put a round bulb over each knee. `skinning: 'linear'` shows neither (frames `skin-sheet-civ_old_man-*` and
  `cmp-*` in `rigging-frames/g9`).
- **Cause:** the panel's vertices are weighed between the spine, the collarbone and the upper arm twist bones (0.24,
  0.22 and 0.41 on average near the shoulder). Dual quaternion blending turns each such vertex about the bones' own
  joint by a blend of their angles, keeping its distance from that joint, so cloth far from the shoulder swings out on
  an arc as the arm rises (the bulge Kavan et al. 2008 describe on the outside of a bend).
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/animation/cor`, skinning about optimized centres of rotation (Le and Hodgins 2016), is
  `addPerson`'s default: each vertex turns about the middle of the surface weighed like it, so the panel turns about
  itself and its middle moves as a linear blend would. Regression tests: `packages/animation/tests/cor.test.js` and
  `scripts/animation-cor-tests.js`. Also fixed on the way: influence blocks were shared between models of one asset
  whatever their skinning mode, so a linear clone could have read a blend skin's share-packed joint indices; the block
  key now names the mode (the same tests).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a Character Creator collarbone read 13 to 15 degrees depressed on a walk, as its A pose rest was taken as its zero (KB-RIG-CLAVICLE1, rigging)

- **Repro:** `addPerson` on the Fauld cast's Character Creator old man (`civ_old_man.glb`), the pose sheet
  (`packages/humans/test/pose-sheet.browser.mjs --model=<file>`): idle read `l_sternoclavicular` depression -13.5 and
  `r_` -13.0, talk -12.1 and -10.5, the walk -15 on both sides, against clinical ranges of about -9
  (`private/handoffs/rigging-frames/g6` in the rigging lane worktree).
- **Cause:** the sternoclavicular zero is the rest pose unless the rest holds the collarbone raised, which the fit read
  from the rest bone's direction in the thorax against Ludewig et al. 2009's direction with the arm at the side. A
  Character Creator clavicle bone does not lie along the collarbone: its head sits 6 cm off the midline and it aims at
  the shoulder joint's centre (12.4 cm long, read in Blender 5.3 with its own importer), so its A pose rest read 2.3
  degrees up, below the 5.9 of an arm at the side, and the raised rest was kept as zero. The bone's direction alone
  cannot tell where the collarbone is: the rig's body mesh is cut away under the clothes between 4 and 9 cm from the
  sternal end, so the collarbone's own line cannot be read from the skin either, and one fixed offset is not borne out
  by the clips (where they hang the arm the bone sits from 29 degrees below level to 7.5 above, by clip and side).
- **Fix:** the drop is read from the motion. `rhythmDrops` (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts`) takes, over the frames
  that hang the arm within 30 degrees of the side, the median elevation and retraction the collarbone loses from its
  rest, less what the rhythm still gives for that lift; the fit's new `drop` option takes the zero back by it, never
  past the rhythm between the rest arm's lift and the side (7.1 up and 9.1 back for the old man's 60 degree A pose).
  `addPerson` calibrates it from a model's clips with the hinge rolls. Old man sheet (`rigging-frames/g7`): the idle
  and talk depression warnings are gone, the walk's right one is gone, and the raised arm rows read 0 warnings.
- **Still read, and true:** the walk's left collarbone, depression -15 held and -19.1 raw (4.2 past its stop). The clip
  drops the left collarbone about 34 degrees below its rest while the right rises 3 (Blender, the bone's line against
  level), so it is the clip's own asymmetry, not the zero.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/clavicle-rhythm.test.js` (an A pose rest with no drop keeps its rest as zero;
  with the clips' drop it reads the drop, capped by the rhythm; `rhythmDrops` reads a hanging frame's drop less the
  rhythm for its lift; neither existed before the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: an arm raised past 120 degrees drew the collarbone back past a recalled retraction range (KB-RIG-GIRDLEELLIPSE1, rigging)

- **Repro:** `packages/humans/test/pose-sheet.browser.mjs`, the rows "arms raised" and "arms raised forward overhead",
  on the code-built body and the Fauld old man: `sternoclavicular retraction -19.8 deg, 1.1 past its clinical range of
  -18.7 (kapandji)`.
- **Cause:** the clavicle's retraction range was Kapandji's 20 degrees, recalled, not read. The coupling drives the
  collarbone by Ludewig et al. 2009's bone pins, 19.8 back from the side at 120 degrees of elevation, and a measured
  study puts the whole motion further: Sahara et al. 2007 (vertically open MRI, 7 subjects, 14 shoulders,
  https://europepmc.org/article/MED/17474135) measure 30.6 degrees of clavicle retraction against the thorax over arm
  abduction.
- **Fix:** the human table's sternoclavicular retraction takes Sahara 2007's 30.6 as its measured row, with the recalled
  Kapandji row kept after it (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy-human.ts`); the raised arm rows read 0 warnings on both
  bodies (`rigging-frames/g7`).
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy-human.test.js` (the table's rows by source and their provenance count).
### Fixed 2026-11-28: a biome species' `color` hue and value did nothing (KB-BIOMES-SPECIESCOLOR1, biomes)

- **Repro:** a `SpeciesRule` with `color: { hue: 0.2, value: 0.3 }`: its objects jitter like every other species'.
- **Cause:** the field was declared in `packages/biomes/src/define.ts` and never carried into the placed species.
- **Fix:** `PlacedSpecies.color`, and `BiomeObjects` passes the jitter to the species' leaf and stone scatters (a hue
  past half a turn is half a turn). Test: `packages/biomes/tests/contact.test.js`.

### Open 2026-11-28: the horizon ring takes no relief shading (KB-BIOMES-HORIZONRELIEF1, biomes)

- **Repro:** the alpine shot of `packages/biomes/tests/browser-check.html` with `relief` on and off: the horizon
  ring's rock pixels read the same both ways (mean and spread of luma over the flat mask's red 0.357 and 0.067), while
  the world's rock changes (0.345 to 0.283).
- **Cause:** `BiomeView.attach` gives `TerrainReliefLighting` the world's terrain only; the horizon ring is a second
  terrain made once the ground weights are in.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the alpine rock look check went over its grain ceiling with relief lighting on (KB-BIOMES-ROCKSHADOW1, biomes)

- **Repro:** `node packages/biomes/tests/browser-check.mjs` on the parent of db1a71d802: rock light and dark 0.108
  over its 0.104 (0.086 with `relief: false`).
- **Cause:** the check pools the world's rock and the horizon ring's. The ring's cone peaks in the valley's materials
  (KB-BIOMES-HORIZONCONE1, KB-BIOMES-HORIZONALTITUDE1) raised the pooled spread, and relief lighting's share on the
  world's rock (0.073 to 0.091) carried it past the ceiling. That share is the sky-view factor: it dims only the sky's
  blue term, so the look's luma over the flat mask's red moves with the mix of sun and sky. Relief changes no albedo
  and no normal, and this shot holds no cast shadow (the sun is overhead).
- **Correction:** an earlier version of this entry blamed cast shadows and set `relief: false` in the check. Both were
  wrong, and the check draws relief again.
- **Fix:** db1a71d802 (the horizon ring's mountains and materials). With relief on the check measures 0.097, ceiling
  unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/biomes/tests/browser-check.mjs` (relief on: 0.108 on the parent, 0.095 at db1a71d802).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a snapshot taken before a step that grew the rigid world would not restore, or replayed to another hash (KB-PHYS-LAYOUTHASH1, physics)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="first step restores" packages/physics/tests/world-rigid-solver.test.js`: a chain of
  four `spherical` joints in a `PhysicsWorld`, `takeSnapshot()` before the first `advance`, 30 frames, `restoreSnapshot`, 30 frames
  again. First refused ("The snapshot holds 506 regions and the solvers name 507", as in `modal-sound.test.js`, "sounds a real
  joint rupture once and replays"); with that fixed, the replay ended at another hash with every body to the bit.
- **Cause, two of them:** (1) the first step sizes the locks' Newton solve for the joints' paths (`NEWTON`, grown inside the step
  by `place_newton`), and `RigidSolver.extraState()` named every scratch column with rows, so the region list grew by one. NEWTON
  is workspace: every word of it is written inside a step before it is read there, and no step carries it into the next. (2) The
  header's count of layouts (`layout`, which tells JS to bind its views again) lay inside the hashed state range, so a snapshot
  from before any growth wrote the old count back over a world laid out after it. It says where the words lie, as the offsets
  do. Any growth inside a step does the same, the pairs' too (`broad.rs`), so (2) was on main as well.
- **Fix:** the kernel names its workspace columns (`WORKSPACE` in `layout.rs`, `world_workspace`, `KernelWorld.workspaceColumns()`)
  and `extraState()` leaves them out; the count of layouts moved next to the multibody stamp, outside `state_ranges`, so neither
  `World::hash` nor a snapshot carries it. Every world's hash changes once with this (the replay goldens are rebuilt).
- **Regression:** the test above, `modal-sound.test.js`, and `a_world_grown_before_its_first_step_hashes_and_steps_as_one_its_step_grew`
  in `packages/physics/kernel/tests/canonical.rs` (growing a world changed its hash before the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a subtree reference could not be a child of selector, sequence or any builder (KB-BEHAVIOR-SUBTREEBUILD1, behavior)

- **Repro:** the behavior README's "Reusable subtrees" example under `npm run check:readmes`: `selector(subtree('guard'))`
  failed with TS2345, `SubtreeNode` not assignable to `NodeSpec`, so a typed program could not build a tree that uses
  references without casts.
- **Cause:** the root entry's composite and decorator builders take `NodeSpec` children, and `/subtrees` exported only
  `subtree`, `resolveTree`, `validateTree` and `SubtreeTree`.
- **Fix:** ac1c5838e0: `/subtrees` exports the same twelve builder functions typed with `SubtreeSpec` children.
- **Regression:** `packages/behavior/tests/subtrees.test.js` (the entry's builders are the root's and build reference
  trees that validate and resolve; undefined before the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: BiomeWorld.create({ workers: n }) in Node failed each job with a bare ReferenceError (KB-BIOMES-NODEWORKERS1, biomes)

- **Repro:** `BiomeWorld.create({ workers: 3 })` in Node, then `world.tile(4, 4)`: `ReferenceError: Worker is not
  defined` (the docs/workers.md example under `check:readme-run` in Node).
- **Cause:** an explicit worker count started `BiomeWorkers` with the default `new Worker` spawner where no Web Worker
  exists; only the automatic count checked for one.
- **Fix:** 7e7f27f8f0: `BiomeWorkers` (the page-side `/workers` entry, so the worker file keeps its size) throws
  MargoError `'unsupported'` naming `createWorker` when the world is made.
- **Regression:** `packages/biomes/tests/workers.test.js` ("workers asked for where Web Workers do not exist").

### Fixed 2026-11-28: build:packages stopped on missing umbrella files for /procedural/forbs and /terrain/ground-contact (umbrella)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/build-modern.js --precompiled --only=margoengine` on main ad2ee43b94: "build:packages finished
  without these declared export targets", `dist/procedural/forbs` and `dist/terrain/ground-contact`.
- **Cause:** the forbs and ground-contact commits regenerated the margoengine, game and kit-viz exports but did not commit
  the five `src` files `node scripts/umbrella.mjs` writes; `umbrella.mjs --check` (tests/umbrella.test.js) reports it.
- **Fix:** ac8c52c4a6: the generated files.
- **Regression:** `tests/umbrella.test.js` (already catches it; local CI runs it).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a scene warmed with warmUp drew aerial perspective from empty atmosphere tables, so far hills had no haze (KB-SKY-TABLESKEY1, sky)

- **Repro:** `scripts/web-demos/still-frame.mjs ten-thousand-trees` on main 4469d88656 (it calls `warmUp` of
  `@margoengine/quality` before its first frame), on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer: the distant hills have no blue
  haze. The same build rendered without stopping at a missing pipeline shows the haze; the two frames differ by a mean
  of 2.9 levels per channel, in the far terrain.
- **Cause:** `AtmosphereTables.upload` (`packages/sky/src/atmosphere-luts.ts`) stored the atmosphere's key before it
  made its two compute pipelines. warmUp's stopped-frame route throws at the first pipeline that is still compiling,
  the transmittance table's included; the retried frame then found the key already stored and never baked either
  table, for as long as the atmosphere did not change.
- **Fix:** the key is stored after both tables are encoded, so a frame stopped anywhere before that bakes them on the
  next frame.
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/aerial.test.js` (a transmittance pipeline that throws once: the next frame
  dispatches the 32 x 8 and 32 x 32 bakes once each; 0 and 0 before the fix).
### Fixed 2026-11-28: a world built again named its GLTFWeather effects otherwise, so a seek did not match a run (KB-WEATHER-GLTFSEEK1, weather)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/weather/tests/seek.test.js`: "a weather replayed 1 steps equals a continuous run"
  failed with `name: 'weather-gltf-2'` against `'weather-gltf'`.
- **Cause:** the KB-WEATHER-GLTFTWO1 fix named each effect by a counter over every `GLTFWeather` the program had made
  (`packages/weather/src/gltf.ts`), so the second world of a seek, or a film's second shot, got new names, and a
  lookup by name found nothing.
- **Fix:** option `name` (default `'weather-gltf'`); `GLTFWeather.attach` without one takes the first free of
  `weather-gltf`, `weather-gltf-2`, ... in the engine's scene, so the names follow the scene.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/gltf.test.js` ("GLTFWeather names follow the scene"); `seek.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a second VolumetricClouds layer on one engine threw "Invalid plugin" (KB-SKY-CLOUDTWO1, sky, weather)

- **Repro:** `VolumetricClouds.attach(engine, {bottom: 650, top: 1300})` and then a second
  `VolumetricClouds.attach(engine, {bottom: 250, top: 450})` (low scud under a rain deck): the engine threw
  `Invalid plugin`.
- **Cause:** the plugin's `name` and its frame-graph pass were both the fixed text `'sky:volumetric-clouds'`
  (`packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`), and core refuses a second plugin of one name (the class of
  KB-WEATHER-GLTFTWO1). `Weather`'s flash link and `WeatherDrive` looked a layer up by that exact name, so they could
  reach one layer only.
- **Fix:** option `name` (default `'sky:volumetric-clouds'`), fixed text so a world built again names its layers the
  same; the pass takes the plugin's name. `Weather` and `WeatherDrive` reach every layer named
  `'sky:volumetric-clouds'` or `'sky:volumetric-clouds:<name>'` (`isCloudLayerName`).
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/cloud-layers.test.js`; `packages/weather/tests/air.test.js` ("the drive finds
  every cloud layer by the name prefix").

### Fixed 2026-11-28: an explicit fitAnatomy map threw when the table's naming had read the same bone (KB-RIG-MAPWINS1, rigging)

- **Repro:** the animator README example "Solvers on a fitted body": `fitAnatomy` on the UAL1 mannequin with
  `map: { vl3: 'spine_01', ... }` threw "Bone spine_01 is mapped to both vl5 and vl3", since the table now reads Unreal
  names itself (KB-RIG-UENAMING1) and maps spine_01 to vl5.
- **Cause:** `fitAnatomy` (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts`) added the map's joints on top of the naming's and kept
  the naming's joint for a bone the map placed elsewhere.
- **Fix:** a bone the map places is the map's; the naming's guess for that bone gives way.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy-human-bundled.test.js` ("an explicit map wins").

### Fixed 2026-11-28: an IK arm reaching across the chest passed through the trunk, palm up (KB-RIG-REACHTRUNK1, rigging, animator)

- **Repro:** `packages/humans/test/pose-sheet.browser.mjs --model=<the Character Creator old man>`, row "reach across
  the chest (IK, right)": `checkPose` failed it with the upper arm and the forearm 4 percent of stature from the
  trunk's axis, and the hand lay palm up.
- **Cause:** `solveLimbIK` (`packages/animator/src/ik.ts`) kept the swivel the idle pose bent to, which dropped the
  elbow into the belly, and knew nothing of the body's volumes; `solveChain` (`packages/rigging/src/ik.ts`) left the
  forearm twist and the hand as the idle clip held them.
- **Fix:** `solveLimbIK` takes `avoid` and searches the swivel nearest the wanted one that keeps the limb out of the
  body as it keeps the shoulder in range; `rigging/ik` passes the table's measured volumes (now shared with the pose
  checker in `packages/rigging/src/body-volumes.ts`). An arm ends with the forearm at its anatomical zero and the hand
  at the body's neutral unless the chain says `hand: 'keep'`.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/ik-reach-across.test.js`; the pose sheet fails an IK row with a limb through
  the body.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: two biomes unit checks were red on main (KB-BIOMES-CHECKS-RED1, biomes)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/biomes/tests/no-raw-division.test.js` named `hydrology.ts:663` and `:664` (from the
  drainage structure map, bed921d181), and `gpu-chain-bound.test.js` failed with "test:gpu chains 3 checks".
- **Cause:** both landed without these tests being run. The raster step divided a cell index with raw `%` and `/`; and
  `meadow-grass-check.mjs` was added to `test:gpu` (5c3686d2b2) beside its own `test:gpu:meadow-grass` (7da58ecd87), so
  it also ran twice.
- **Fix:** the step uses `imod` and `idiv` (the same values for a cell index), and `test:gpu` chains its two checks
  again; the meadow check keeps running as `test:gpu:meadow-grass`.
- **Regression:** `packages/biomes/tests/no-raw-division.test.js` and `packages/biomes/tests/gpu-chain-bound.test.js`.

### Open 2026-11-28: a hull of two closed boxes face to face is refused as an open seam (KB-SEA-SLAMSEAM1, physics seakeeping)

- **What:** `HullSolver` throws "The slam hull has an open or inconsistently wound seam" for the uneven hull of the coupling test, a wide box aft and a narrow one forward, each closed and wound outward, meeting at x = 0.
- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, "on a hull uneven fore and aft, heave drives pitch with the sign the strips give it" (fails on main since debcbf19fd, hull slamming; the KB2161 branch does not touch seakeeping).
- **Cause:** the slam validation (`packages/physics/src/seakeeping/slamming-validation.ts`) welds vertices by position and wants every edge on exactly two triangles. The test's boxes are 4 by 4 grids a face, so the aft box's x = 0 face and the fore box's x = 0 face share vertices at z = 0 and +-0.75; those edges sit on four triangles, two of each box, wound in balance. The hull is closed (two closed shells touching), but the check counts it open.
- **Fix to make:** accept an edge whose triangles pair up with balanced winding (count even, orientation zero), or validate each shell apart, with the test above as the regression; never reshape the test's hull to pass.

### Open 2026-11-28: every app that imports physics emits the wind-traction kernel's two Wasm files (KB-PHYS-TRACTIONWASM1, physics aero)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/game/tests/physics-entry.test.js`, "neither the game kit root nor its physics entry
  emits a Wasm file": an app build of `export { Physics } from '@margoengine/game/physics'` emits
  `assets/wind-traction-kernel-*.wasm` and `assets/wind-traction-kernel-shared-*.wasm`. Red in local CI at 06d91dbf50.
- **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/aero/traction-phase.ts` (AERO-01 native wind traction, d4370faed2) loads its kernel with
  `new URL('./wind-traction-kernel.wasm?no-inline', import.meta.url)`, and the module is reachable from the physics root,
  so a bundler emits both files for any app that steps a world. Every other physics kernel ships as a blueprint inside the
  package's JavaScript, or behind its own optional entry.
- **Owner:** AERO-01 (Codex, in flight). Found by lane P; not changed, as the row's work is in progress. The fix is the
  blueprint form the other kernels use, or the `import()` of the phase behind the entry that opts into native traction.

### Open 2026-11-28: Above the Treeline's scanned rocks are 1.3 to 1.5 times too bright and blotchy (KB-TREELINE-ROCKGRADE1, film asset)

- **Repro:** measure `showcase-films/treeline-rocks/textures/rock_moss_set_0{1,2}_granite.jpg` in the film's asset
  library. 33.3 and 22.2 percent of the atlas texels are empty (black). Linear luma over the covered texels is 0.2596
  and 0.2233, where the script's target (0.75 x measured granite) is 0.173, ratios 1.50 and 1.29. Luma of 16 px blocks
  varies by a coefficient of 0.46 and 0.50 (95th over 5th percentile 4.7 and 5.0); the normal maps tilt 13.1 and 28.0
  degrees on average (95th percentile 31.6 and 87.3).
- **Cause:** `grade()` in the film's `build_treeline_rocks.py` scales the albedo by `target / lin.mean(axis=0)` over
  every texel, the empty ones included, so covered texels come out brighter than the target by the empty share. The
  blotches are the scan's own half-desaturated moss over a strong normal map on meshes cut to 3,000 triangles. The fix
  belongs to the film's asset owner: average covered texels only and soften the albedo toward its local mean.

### Open 2026-11-28: a biome species' `lod` changes nothing (KB-BIOMES-DEADFIELDS1, biomes)

- **Repro:** give a `SpeciesRule` `lod: [10, 20, 30]` and draw it with `BiomeView`: the objects change level exactly as
  without it.
- **Cause:** `BiomeObjects` takes its rings from `radius` (`[r * 0.15, r * 0.4, r]`); nothing reads `rule.lod`.
  (`sink` and `alignToGround` were the same until KB-BIOMES-SINK1, `color.hue` and `color.value` until
  KB-BIOMES-SPECIESCOLOR1.)

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a biome species' `sink` and `alignToGround` did nothing, so stones stood on the surface (KB-BIOMES-SINK1, biomes)

- **Repro:** a `SpeciesRule` with `sink: 0.2, alignToGround: 0.65` drawn by `BiomeView`: upright objects on the
  surface, their downhill side clear of the ground on a slope.
- **Cause:** both fields were declared in `packages/biomes/src/define.ts` and never carried into the placed species or
  the scatters.
- **Fix:** `PlacedSpecies` carries them and `BiomeObjects` passes them to each species' `ScatterTiles`. Test:
  `packages/biomes/tests/contact.test.js` ("a species sink and alignToGround reach its scatters").

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a textured scatter's occlusion map did nothing under a Sky (KB-SCATTER-SKYAO1, scatter)

- **Repro:** a `Scatter` with `textures.occlusionRoughnessMetal` occlusion 128 in a scene with
  `Sky.attach(engine, { lighting: { ambient } })`: exactly as bright as with occlusion 255.
- **Cause:** the Sky replaces core's `frame.ambient` term with its own `margoAmbient`; Scatter multiplied only the
  former.
- **Fix:** one helper (`packages/shared/occlude-ambient.js`) multiplies every ambient term. Test:
  `packages/scatter/test/contact.browser.mjs` (1.000 against 0.502 before and after).

### Open 2026-11-28: the timber-valley blowup shows single bright pixels through conifer foliage, 15 and 46 ppm (KB-LOOK-TV-SPECKLE, procedural, biomes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-blowup.json --once --seconds 1.1` (RTX A6000,
  WebGPU, supersample 2, 8 sub-frames, TAA): `speckle` early 21.3 ppm and mid 46.4 ppm, bound 5 (`animatedFeature`).
  38 of 44 early speckles are bright: sky or fire glow through a gap in dark foliage.
- **Cause 1 (fixed):** a conifer spray's band started 12 percent along its branch and narrow, so the sprays of a whorl
  never met round the stem; sky showed beside the trunk at every whorl of the near firs (1261,603 and 1271,681 on the
  early probe). `generateConiferMesh` now starts each whorled spray at the stem's axis with its inner rows covering the
  angle to the next spray. Regression: `packages/procedural/test/conifer-hub.test.js` (a ring round the stem at every
  whorl is 100 percent open before, 0 after). Early 44 to 31 speckles (21.3 to 15.0 ppm); mid 96 to 95.
- **Cause 2 (open):** most of what is left, and nearly all of mid, sits in the smoke band at y 945 and below. Not
  sub-pixel sprays drawn at the wrong ring: with the screen-space rings of KB-BIOMES-SCREENLOD1 (`lodPixels: 1`) a
  full-size fir's middle sprays stay over a rendered pixel past the 800 m ring (0.39 m at 2160 rows and 45 degrees is a
  pixel at about 970 m), and an A/B on current main (rings off, then on) read early 19.8 to 25.1 ppm and mid 47.4 to
  48.4. The speckles are the distant canopy's gaps against the fire glow, seen behind and between near leaves
  (blowup early, x 1600 to 1760, y 1040 to 1077). Next: the far canopy's coverage against a bright background (the
  imposter's cut-out at distance, and the middle mesh's gaps), not its ring.
- **Rail-line, traced (2026-11-28, open):** the rail-line early probe's 167 speckles (150 bright) are nearly all single
  pixels of the smoke sky inside dark crowns 25 to 275 m off, on the full-detail mesh (the film's tree rings are 300,
  800 and 2,000 m): per pixel of the depth AOV, 4 ppm under 25 m, 150 ppm at 25 to 50 m, 311 at 50 to 90, 949 at 90 to
  120, 2,148 at 180 to 240. Each pixel is about 32 samples (2 x 2 supersample, 8 jittered sub-frames), so the values
  are the box-filtered coverage, not sampling noise. A reconstruction filter does not remove them: a Gaussian of
  sigma 0.5 output pixel on the probe takes early 81 to 11 ppm and mid 38 to 4.8, so the shot tool's area filter
  (`tools/shot/pixels.js`) is not the cause. Marked on the frame they sit on the trunk lines, and an orthographic
  side view of each species' detail-2 mesh (`generateConiferMesh`, 9 yaws, pixels of 6, 12 and 20 cm) puts every
  crown speckle in the inner tenth of the crown's width: grand fir 5,652 ppm of crown at 12 cm, Douglas-fir 2,824 at
  20 cm, red cedar 4,905 at 12 cm, all at the stem. Cause 1's fix closed the whorl round the stem seen from above;
  seen from the side the stem column between whorls holds only the spray bases and the stem, since sprays are flat
  bands at the whorl's height and only sprays pointing at the camera project onto the stem. Fix to decide: Douglas-fir
  bears internodal branches between whorls (D. A. Maguire, M. Moeur and W. S. Bennett, "Models for describing basal
  diameter and vertical distribution of primary branches in young Douglas-fir", Forest Ecology and Management 63(1),
  23-55, 1994), which the generator does not build; grand fir has few internodal shoots and flat, layered branches
  (H. Ishii, E. D. Ford and D. G. Sprugel, comparative crown study of P. menziesii, A. amabilis and A. grandis,
  Eurasian Journal of Forest Research, 2003), so some light between its tiers is real. Counts per growth unit are
  still needed from the full texts before the generator gains internodal branches.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a voxel path tracer render reset AMD's integrated graphics within seconds (KB4037, voxel-pathtracer; was "Batch 160 AMD voxel denoise watchdog")

- **Repro:** `MARGO_GPU=amd GPU_POWER=low-power node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs --max 25 -- node
  packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs --report=denoise-materials denoise-materials` on the workstation
  (Ryzen 9 9950X's two-unit RDNA2 graphics, driver 32.0.21042.62, Edge 158): about 25 s into the 480 x 300, 16,384
  sample reference the page lost its device (`DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED`) and Windows logged LiveKernelEvent 141
  (WATCHDOG-20261128-0854.dmp). The same on origin/main 0f282397e6, so KB-BL1 (2026-11-11) had not fixed it.
- **Cause, measured:** every submission timed in the page (each `queue.submit` to its `onSubmittedWorkDone`): the
  reference's first trace bands, 16 rows x 480 pixels x 7 samples (53,760 paths), took 554, 1,031 and 2,410 ms, and
  the third tripped Windows' 2 s watchdog (AMD preempts compute only between packets). The RTX A6000 traces the same
  bands in 4 ms, so this GPU is 140 to 600 times slower on this scene, far past the sixteenth of `SUBMIT_WORK` a new
  tracer started at (65,536 paths at 8 bounces, sized for a GPU 16 times slower than the A6000). The pacer could not
  have saved it: the smallest piece a band could be was 8 rows (one workgroup high) of the whole width with all of a
  run's samples (26,880 paths here), and `renderImage` planned a whole 7-sample run (about 150 pieces, 45 s on this
  GPU) before tracing it, so a budget the pacer cut after the costly middle of the image took effect only at the next
  run: with column pieces alone, pieces planned at a run's start still took up to 1,341 ms.
- **Fix (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/dispatch.ts`, `src/tracer.ts`, `src/shaders.ts`):** a band of the fewest rows
  that is still over the budget is cut into pieces of whole columns, multiples of 8 (`planTrace`/`traceChunks`
  `colStep`; `Frame.band` gives the trace kernel the piece's first column and width, the row stride stays the tile's).
  `renderImage` makes its pieces one at a time (`traceChunks`), each reading the budget the pacer measured last, and a
  new tracer starts at a 128th of `SUBMIT_WORK` (8,192 paths). Sample runs still follow `SUBMIT_WORK` alone, and every
  pixel takes each run once whatever its pieces, so no image depends on the GPU's speed. The WebGL2 route, which
  windows its own parts, is unchanged. `FRAME_BYTES` 800 to 816.
- **Evidence:** the same reference on AMD, timed per submission for 600 s on the fixed build: no device loss, the
  worst submission WORST ms (pieces fall to one 8 x 8 workgroup, about 0.45 s each in the costly middle: one thread
  runs its 7 samples in turn, so that is this GPU's floor, a speed item for the speed phase). Before: lost at the
  third costly band. RTX A6000: `determinism` (one smallest piece a submission, now an 8-column piece) gives 18,432
  of 18,432 values bit for bit, and the four mesh GPU tests and the resampled, guiding, media, spectral, mesh and compose (`--backend=compat`) checks give the same sets of readback hashes on the old and new builds (1,259 distinct, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer). Not run to the end on AMD: at this speed the two 16,384-sample references
  take hours.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/dispatch-budget.test.js` "a budget under 8 rows of the image cuts
  renderImage bands into column pieces within it (KB4037)", "a viewport band too wide for a slow GPU is cut into column
  pieces that cover it once (KB4037)" and "renderImage sizes each piece from the budget measured last, within one run
  of samples (KB4037)" (all three fail on the old build); "a new tracer's first submissions carry a 128th of the
  budget"; `assertCovers` now checks every pixel, not every row.
- **Still open:** a run's samples are fixed for determinism, so one thread's 7 to 16 samples are the shortest piece;
  a GPU and scene slow enough to take 2 s for those (more bounces, slower hardware) would still reset. Not seen; the
  floor measured here is about a quarter of the watchdog.
- **Sources:** C. D. Polychronopoulos, D. J. Kuck, "Guided Self-Scheduling: A Practical Scheduling Scheme for
  Parallel Supercomputers", IEEE Transactions on Computers C-36(12), 1987, https://doi.org/10.1109/TC.1987.5009495
  (chunks sized as the work is handed out, not fixed in advance); S. F. Hummel, E. Schonberg, L. E. Flynn, "Factoring:
  a method for scheduling parallel loops", CACM 35(8), 1992, https://doi.org/10.1145/135226.135232 (chunk sizes for
  loop iterations of varying cost); T. Aila, S. Laine, "Understanding the Efficiency of Ray Traversal on GPUs", HPG
  2009, https://doi.org/10.1145/1572769.1572792 (ray cost varies widely across an image); Microsoft, [Timeout
  Detection and Recovery (TDR)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/timeout-detection-and-recovery).

### Fixed 2026-11-28 (in part 2026-11-11): mesh PBR inlined twelve texture filters into the Direct3D 11 surface program, and the surface program held its material (KB5451)

- **Repro:** a mesh-PBR tracer on the WebGL2 layer over ANGLE Direct3D 11 with Chromium's
  `--disable-gpu-shader-disk-cache`, timing each GL link and first draw: the staged `surface` program took 177 s to link and 356 s more at its first
  draw (58% of a 362 s ready, 550 s image; dev PC, RTX A6000, busy, diagnostic).
- **Cause:** `pbrMaterial` called the bilinear `pbrTexture` filter once per texture slot (eleven direct calls plus the
  clearcoat normal map through `pbrMappedNormal`). HLSL functions are inline by default, so fxc built one copy of the
  filter per call: 21 copies in the `trace` entry and 17 in `preview`.
- **Fix:** `pbrMaterial` reads every slot but the normal map through ONE `pbrTexture` call in a loop whose bound is
  the record's slot count (word 3, written by `mesh-pbr-build.ts`), a value the compiler cannot see, so it keeps one
  rolled body (the technique the coverage kernel already uses, docs/limits.md). The same calls with the same
  arguments: same values. `pbrMapNormal` takes the texel the loop read.
- **Evidence:** inlined filter copies (a call-graph walk of each WGSL module the tracer makes under the test's fake engine) went
  from 21 to 10 in `trace`, 17 to 6 in `preview`, 42 to 20 in total; the Direct3D 11 image hash is the same
  (1711753600) before and after; the surface program's cold link plus first draw went from 533 s to 305 s on the
  busy machine (diagnostic only: the unchanged `hit` program moved from 157 s to 257 s in the same pair).
- **Still open:** the other staged programs (`hit`, `shadow`, an unlabeled one) still take minutes cold on Direct3D
  11, so the 120 s `renderImage` signal with the disk cache off is not yet met. Next: the same loop-bound treatment
  for `pbrVisible`'s alpha reads and the traversal loops in `hit` and `shadow`, proven by the same counts.
- **Measured 2026-11-28 (lane A):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr-lobes-browser.mjs`
  (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11, a fresh profile each run, so cold) passes, but its first image arrives 314 s after
  `ready`; later images and the ANGLE Vulkan leg take under a second. The draw-time compiles of four 7-output programs
  hold it: 74 to 173 s each by the first-draw wait. Binding the framebuffer before `linkProgram`, or declaring the
  outputs as one array, leaves the link at about 1 s and the first draw as long (ANGLE links against one output either
  way), so the cost cannot be moved to the parallel link. Inlined statements of the surface program: 21,211, of which
  the layer's storage-word loads are 15,596 (1,114 copies). Fixed in part: `triangleNormal` calls `meshWorldNormal`
  once (it was in both branches), the dielectric side test takes the triangle normal once (`triangleWrongSide`), and
  the tangent frame reads `meshWorld` once per branch. Surface program 21,211 to 18,425 statements, paired offline fxc
  144.2 to 106.5 s; emitter program 79.6 to 75.2 s. Same output: 122 GPU readbacks of `test:gpu:mesh-pbr`,
  `mesh-deform`, `mesh-attributes` and `mesh-pbr-lobes` hash the same before and after (native WebGPU, repeatable run
  to run). Regression: `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr.test.js` "the mesh helpers compute each hit value
  once per call site (KB5451)". Still open: the cold first image is far above 120 s; next are the 941 storage loads
  (meshX 19 copies of 12 loads, pbrVertex 21, rowAt 27, meshCorner 27) and the two pbrMapNormal copies.
- **Measured 2026-11-28, second round (lane A, paired offline fxc, `ps_5_0`, per-pair minimum of 2 rounds, loaded
  machine):** a branch-free storage-word select (`v & mask` of `equal(ivec4(o & 3), ivec4(0,1,2,3))`, OR of the four
  lanes) in place of the layer's nested `c < 2 ? ...` select made the surface program slower, 141.2 to 228.5 s, and
  the emitter program 90.3 to 119.1 s, though it removes three branches from each of the 907 inlined `_ld0f` copies:
  dropped. Filling only the first n of the surface program's 7 outputs: 1 output 40.2 s, 2 39.4 s, 4 108.4 s, 6
  141.0 s, so outputs 3 and 4 hold most of the compile. ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end links against the first output
  only and compiles again at the first draw for the bound 7-target layout, on the GPU thread, so the four 7-output
  programs compile one after another; statement cuts inside them gave 5 to 30 percent each and two of them were
  slower. Reaching 120 s from 314 s needs a structural change to what each staged program writes (fewer outputs per
  program, or the heavy material terms behind outputs 3 and 4 moved out of the 7-output programs), not more cuts.
- **Fixed in part 2026-11-28, third round (lane A):** mesh PBR's shading normal (`triangleShading`) and material
  (`pbrMaterial`) were 10,800 of the surface program's 17,900 inlined statements; with both stubbed the program
  compiled in 12.5 s against 123.9 s (paired offline fxc). Each now runs in a staged program of its own, `shading`
  and `material`, between `vertex` and `surface` (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/compat-staged.ts`, SURFACE_CALLS):
  both read the path state only, so each is computed under a guard that holds wherever its call runs (the conjunction
  of the branches around it), kept in three new state fields, and the call site reads them. `pbrMaterial` changes
  nothing private but `pbrLayer`, which its program saves and restores and the call site sets from the kept copy. Only
  tracers whose shader calls `pbrMaterial` get the two programs; WebGPU's shader is not touched. The purity check
  read `h.mesh!=0u&&motion<1.0` as taking the address of `motion` (`&motion`); `assigns` now skips `&&`. The same
  misreading (`&&h.inst`, `&&done`) had marked programs as writers of `h`, `done` and `medium`, so every tracer's
  state pages are now laid out with fewer pages rewritten per program; the resampled, guiding, media, spectral, mesh
  and compose (`--backend=compat`) GPU checks give the same 1,332 readback hashes before and after (821 on the
  layer). Paired
  offline fxc (2 rounds, per-pair minimum): the old surface program 94.2 s, the new surface 14.1 s, shading 3.7 s,
  material 9.6 s. Cold first image of `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr-lobes-browser.mjs`
  (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11 leg, fresh profile, busy workstation, old and new builds run back to back): 272 s before,
  200 and 193 s after. Same output: the four mesh GPU tests (`mesh-pbr`, `mesh-deform`, `mesh-attributes`,
  `mesh-pbr-lobes`) give the same set of readback hashes before and after on native WebGPU and on the layer (244 in
  all, the layer's `getBufferSubData` reads hashed too); only the order the layer's reads finish in differs. Entry
  sizes stay under their ceilings (the staged route is in the lazy compat chunk). Regression:
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js` "mesh PBR evaluates its shading normal and material in
  programs of their own before surface (KB5451)". The cold first-draw waits left were `sample` (mesh emitter
  radiance, 83 s), `post` (labelled `hit` before; 45 s) and `shadow` (28 s).
- **Fix (2026-11-28, emit and the texel loop):** the staged route evaluates a mesh emitter's radiance in a program
  of its own, `emit`, drawn between `sample` and `shadow` for the light kind that samples mesh emitters only (kind 5;
  `StagedTrace.emits`). sampleMeshEmitter draws its three random numbers first and everything after them depends on
  those draws, the shading point and private words alone, so on this route it returns the face's record offset (bit
  30 set, so the word stays a normal f32) and its two draws through the light kind's own `radiance` words, and `emit`
  runs the same code after the draws (`z_meshEmitted`) for the radiance. The stager refuses a shader where `sample`
  reads that radiance again, changes a private word the emitter code reads, or reaches the call by more than the
  light kind. A first version kept the record in 4 new state words: mesh PBR's state went from 280 words (10 pages)
  to 11 pages and every program's state load and store grew with it, slower cold; a whole Hit (35 words) took 12
  pages, 17 texture units with finish's 5 sums, and the layer refused it. `pbrTexture` on this route also fetches
  its nearest tap and its four bilinear taps in one loop bounded by the texture's filter word, the same taps in the
  same order, decoded and mixed in the same expressions: Direct3D's compiler had inlined five `pbrPixel` copies
  (ten `pbrAddress`) into every texture fetch. WebGPU's shader is not touched. Paired offline fxc over all ten
  (now eleven) staged programs, 2 rounds, per-program minimum: 89.6 s to 68.0 s (sample 29.7 s to 4.1 s plus emit
  8.1 s, shadow 17.7 to 15.9 s, post 20.1 to 17.9 s). Cold first image of
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr-lobes-browser.mjs` (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11, fresh
  profile, old and new alternating, the workstation quiet): old 94 and 91 s, new 80 and 77 s, under the 120 s bar.
  Same output: the four mesh GPU tests and the resampled, guiding, media, spectral, mesh and compose
  (`--backend=compat`) checks give the same sets of readback hashes before and after on WebGPU and the layer (1,576).
  The lazy compat chunk grows from 13,503 to 14,856 B gzip; the root entry by 1 B (the chunk's name). Regressions:
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js` "mesh emitters evaluate their radiance in a program of
  its own between sample and shadow (KB5451)" and `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr.test.js` "the WebGL2
  route's texel loop gives pbrTexture's values bit for bit (KB5451)" (CPU WGSL interpreter, nearest and bilinear,
  sRGB and not). The 120 s bar is met on a quiet machine (80 and 77 s); the loaded runs (167 to 205 s while other
  lanes ran) are time only and wait in the busy-machine retest list for the quiet rerun before release (manager
  ruling, 2026-11-28); the bar is unchanged. The largest cold programs left are `post` and `shadow` (about 16 to
  18 s each offline).
- **Sources (the split):** S. Laine, T. Karras, T. Aila, "Megakernels Considered Harmful: Wavefront Path Tracing on
  GPUs", HPG 2013, https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2013-07_megakernels-considered-harmful-wavefront-path-tracing-gpus
  (a path's work cut into small kernels that pass the path state through memory, which keeps each kernel small for
  the compiler and the register file); D. van Antwerpen, "Improving SIMD Efficiency for Parallel Monte Carlo Light
  Transport on the GPU", HPG 2011, https://doi.org/10.1145/2018323.2018330 (stream compaction between path stages);
  P. S. Heckbert, "Fundamentals of Texture Mapping and Image Warping", MS thesis, UC Berkeley, 1989,
  https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/1989/CSD-89-516.pdf (bilinear reconstruction as two linear
  interpolations of four taps, the order the loop keeps); R. W. Scheifler, "An Analysis of Inline Substitution for a
  Structured Programming Language", CACM 20(9), 1977, https://doi.org/10.1145/359810.359830 (code growth from
  inlining every call site, which the single tap avoids).
- **Sources:** Microsoft, "Function Declaration Syntax" (HLSL `inline` is the default; one copy of the body per call),
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-function-syntax ; Microsoft,
  "for Statement" (`loop` keeps flow control, `unroll` copies the body; without an attribute the compiler unrolls
  when it can), https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-for .
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/mesh-pbr.test.js` "pbrMaterial reads every texture slot through
  one filter call in a loop bounded by the record (KB5451)" (fails on the old build: 11 calls) and "pbrMaterial gives
  the same values as one filter call per slot (KB5451)" (24 values bit-identical on the CPU WGSL interpreter).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a shot drawn in sub-frames showed what moves fast as stepped copies, not a smear (KB-LOOK-TV-SUBSTEP1, shot tool, scenes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-blowup.json --once --seconds 1.1` (RTX A6000,
  WebGPU, 8 sub-frames over a 180 degree shutter): the near swaying crown at the right of the mid probe (x 1600 to 1920,
  y 100 to 420) draws as eight hard copies a few pixels apart, a staircase trail on each leaf against the sky.
- **Cause:** the shot tool's sub-frames are sharp pictures one slice of the shutter apart (1 / 480 s here); a surface
  moving more than a pixel a slice leaves gaps between its copies. Nothing filled the slice between them.
- **Fix:** each sub-frame blurs over its own slice. The shot tool gives the page each sub-frame's share of the motion
  since the frame drawn before (`shutterShare` in `tools/shot/shot-file.mjs`: the slice over the time since, at most 1)
  through a new `shot.page.shutter` hook; `@margoengine/scenes/timber-valley` at film quality adds
  `@margoengine/post/motion-blur` after TAA's resolve on TAA's velocity (`parts.motionBlur`, 180 degrees, McGuire,
  Hennessy, Bukowski and Osman 2012, "A Reconstruction Filter for Plausible Motion Blur", I3D), and the timber-valley
  shot page sets its shutter from the hook. The same crop now shows one smooth smear.
- **Regression:** `tests/shot-file.test.js` (shutterShare tiles the open shutter: 1 within a kept frame, 1/9 for its
  first sub-frame after the gap, the shutter for a frame drawn alone, 0 with no frame before; `page.shutter` must name a
  function), `tests/shot-film-hook.test.js` (the hook gets each sub-frame's share before its frame is drawn) and
  `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs` (film adds the motion blur at 0.5, a preview none).
- **Measured, blowup `--once --seconds 1.1`:** shimmerMoving early 0.50 to 0.48, mid 2.07 to 2.02 (the smear over the sky,

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the blowup's early motionBlur read 11.7 percent (bound 5) on near leaves that sway against the camera (KB-LOOK-TV-MBVEL1, headless look)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-blowup.json --once --seconds 1.1` (RTX A6000,
  WebGPU, 1920 x 1080, supersample 2, 8 sub-frames, 180 degrees): `look.md` early motionBlur 11.8 percent, 391 sharp of
  3,324 edges, before and after KB-LOOK-TV-SHIMMER2 part (b).
- **Cause:** the check, not the frames. `motionBlur` took each pixel's travel from the camera's motion alone (depth
  reprojection). The sharp edges sit on the near swaying crown at the right of the frame (x 1280 to 1660), travel 9.9 px
  by the camera but 7.2 px by the engine's own velocity: the leaves sway against the camera's sweep, so they move less
  than the camera moves the place they cover, and are smeared by what they really move.
- **Fix:** `motionBlur(frame, motion, { velocity })` judges each pixel by its surface's own travel when the probe has the
  engine velocity (`MovingFrames.velocity`, `shot.moving.velocity`); `checkProbe` passes it. Blowup early 11.8 to 0.00
  percent (1,003 edges over 8 px), mid 0.61 to 0.88 (10,220 edges), bound 5 unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js` (a bar moving 2 px under a 12 px camera sweep, drawn sharp,
  fails by the camera's motion and passes by its velocity; the same bar really moving 12 px still fails).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: warmUp made ten-thousand-trees take 33 s instead of 18 s to start on the WebGL2 layer (KB-QUALITY-WARMSERIAL1, quality, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** a paired A/B of `scripts/web-demos/startup-profile.mjs ten-thousand-trees --backend=webgl2`, the build of
  7bcf8d002b^ (no warmUp) and of 7bcf8d002b (warmUp) taking turns, 4 rounds each on the loaded workstation: time to
  ready 17.7, 17.7, 17.9, 19.3 s before and 33.2, 34.7, 39.7, 51.9 s after (minimum 17.7 against 33.2 s, far past the
  round-to-round spread). The pictures are the same; long tasks total about 10 s before (one of 9.3 s) and 9 to 29 s
  after (none over 0.7 s).
- **Cause:** warmUp (`packages/quality/src/warm.ts`) stopped each warm frame at the first pipeline that did not exist,
  waited for that one pipeline's async compile, then rendered the frame again: 45 rounds, one link at a time, each
  repeating the frame's CPU compute passes. The first route built here (whole warm frames held in the layer's queue
  until their programs linked) started in 21 s but replayed the held frame in one task of 3.3 to 5.4 s. A probe build
  timed it: one command buffer of 5,611 commands, 4.2 s of a 4.3 s task, with 2,473 `checkFramebufferStatus` calls
  (1.7 s, KB-COMPAT-FBSTATUS1) and 150 `getBufferSubData` read-backs of CPU compute passes (0.9 s), each waiting for all
  the GPU work queued before it. No shader compiled at a draw in that task (the trace's Direct3D compile events: none).
- **Fix:** with KHR_parallel_shader_compile the layer's queue carries a link hold
  (`Symbol.for('margoengine.queue.holdsLinks')`, `packages/shared/queue-hold.js`): while it is on, a submit that may use
  a program still linking waits in the queue, with the writes and submits after it in order, until each of those
  programs has linked and drawn once. warmUp takes that frame route when the mark is there: whole frames with the hold
  on, ending after `frames` frames in a row that made no new pipeline (browser WebGPU and the layer without the
  extension keep the stopped-frame route). The queue replays held work in tasks of about 50 ms, a command buffer
  resuming between commands outside a render pass, each task after the first once a fence shows the GPU has run the one
  before; and framebuffer status is read once per attachment signature. Paired A/B against main 4469d88656, taking
  turns, 4 rounds, per-round minimums: ready 28.2 to 17.7 s, longest task 1,012 to 1,011 ms, long tasks in total 11.7
  to 5.6 s, 2,862 to 3,018 framebuffer status reads to 111 to 113; WebGPU 11.6 against 11.4 s (one round). A frame with
  the clock stopped is byte for byte the same on both backends once both builds have the sky fix KB-SKY-TABLESKEY1
  (main's stopped route left aerial perspective's tables empty, so its frame lacked the far haze).
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/link-hold.test.js` (links side by side, no early `LINK_STATUS` read,
  order kept, the replay sliced between passes with a fence between slices), `packages/quality/test/warm.test.js` (the
  frame route: 4 rounds where the stopped route takes 8, peak 5 links pending), `packages/water/test/warm-up.browser.mjs`
  (both backends; the layer reads no link status early).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the WebGL2 layer read checkFramebufferStatus for every new framebuffer and every new texture (KB-COMPAT-FBSTATUS1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `scripts/web-demos/startup-profile.mjs ten-thousand-trees --backend=webgl2` on main 4469d88656: 2,878 to
  2,954 `checkFramebufferStatus` calls in the start (1.6 to 2.7 s), 2,473 of them inside one 4.3 s task of a probe
  build (Chrome on ANGLE Direct3D 11). Each call waits for the GPU process to run every command before it.
- **Cause:** `Replayer.makeFramebuffer` checked each framebuffer it made, and `Replayer.zero` (`clearLevels`) checked
  the scratch framebuffer each time it zeroed a new texture: every bind group's storage texture and every buffer's data
  texture is one. Completeness depends only on what kind of image is attached where (GL ES 3.0.6 section 4.4.4: each
  attachment's object type, internal format, renderbuffer samples and, for a mutable texture, its level; WebGL 2.0
  adds equal widths and heights and one image per colour point), never on which texture it is.
- **Fix:** `CompatDevice.framebufferStatus(signature)` checks once per attachment signature (kind, internal format,
  size, point, and the first colour point of a repeated image) and reuses the answer; an incomplete signature is still
  reported for every framebuffer that has it, with the same text. A status read on a lost context is not kept. Paired
  A/B of the start, main against the warm-frame route of KB-QUALITY-WARMSERIAL1 with this fix, taking turns, 4 rounds:
  2,878 to 2,954 reads before, 109 to 113 after.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/framebuffer-status.test.js` (6 framebuffers of one signature: 12 reads
  before, 2 after); `packages/webgl2-compat/test/passes.test.js` gives its second stand-in format a signature of its own.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a Character Creator walk's skin travels forward while its hips bone stays put (KB-HUM-SKINDRIFT1, animator)

- **Repro:** `packages/humans/test/pose-sheet.browser.mjs --model=<the Character Creator old man>`: sample the walk at 0,
  6 and 12 seconds with `person.play('walk', {fade: 0, at})`. The hips bone's local translation reads the same each
  time, yet the drawn skin is further forward at each time, out of the frame by 6 seconds.
- **Cause:** the skin was right. The walk keys its travel (13.5 m over 12 s) on `CC_Base_BoneRoot`, the skin's top
  joint above the hips, and leaves `CC_Base_Hip`'s own translation in place, so the hips' world position travels with
  the root (6.74 m at 6 s). The sheet, like `addRootMotion` and warping, took the travel from the hips, which on this
  rig carry none: root motion took nothing and warping measured a 0 m/s clip.
- **Fix:** `rootMotionJoint(animation)` (`packages/animator/src/travel-joint.ts`) finds the bone the clips move
  farthest, nearest the root; `addRootMotion`'s `joint` and warping's `speedJoint` default to it. The pose sheet draws
  the whole walk in place with `addRootMotion(animator, {apply: false})`.
- **Regression:** `tests/modern-animator-travel-joint.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a stooped body's up leans with its trunk, so ground heights read along a slope (KB-RIG-FRAMEUP1, rigging)

- **Repro:** `addPerson` on the Fauld cast's Character Creator old man: `person.body.frame.up` is
  [0, 0.992, 0.127], 7.3 degrees forward of the model's vertical. `checkPose(body, pose, {ground})` on the walk drawn in
  place at 5.98 s reports `r_metatarsophalangeal_1` 2.1 percent of stature below the ground while the joint stands
  0.041 m up in the world, 0.016 m above the ground; with the walk's travel left in (6.7 m forward) the same toe reads
  0.11 m higher than it is, so `checkClip` misses ground and foot-slide faults on a walk that travels.
- **Cause:** `fitAnatomy` reads `up` from the hips to the spine above them (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts`,
  `species.frame.top`), so a body that stands stooped in its rest pose gets its trunk's lean as up; the ground checks
  of `packages/rigging/src/validate.ts` measure height along that up.
- **Fix needed:** a vertical for the ground checks that does not lean with the trunk: the normal of the rest feet's
  sole plane (heels and toes of a standing rest), or the rig space's up when the species gives one. `body.frame` feeds
  the anatomical zeros too, so the change reruns the anatomy, IK and pose sheet tests.
- **Fix:** `body.frame` gains `vertical`, the world's up: the rig's axis nearest the trunk's up (within 30 degrees)
  when the rest feet stand level on it (each weight-bearing joint at its mirror's height, below the hips), otherwise
  the trunk's up; `fitAnatomy({vertical})` passes one. The stature and every height and ground test of
  `rigging/validate` are measured along it; the anatomical angles still read against the trunk's frame, so the
  zeros are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/frame-vertical.test.js` (a body leaned 7.3 degrees forward: vertical, stature,
  a toe 0.016 m up reads clear in place and after 6.7 m of travel, and one 0.034 m down reads 0.034 m).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: every `procedural:rock` of a biome is the same stone (KB-BIOMES-ROCKSEED1, biomes)

- **Repro:** Above the Treeline before 2026-11-28 (talus of `procedural:rock` over the upper meadow and scree): every
  stone has one silhouette, only turned and scaled, which reads as copies from 2 to 30 m.
- **Cause:** `partsOf` in `packages/biomes/src/objects.ts` built the `rock` key from `generateRockMesh(1, ...)`, seed
  1 for every species and instance, and a species drew one mesh through its `ScatterTiles`, so the seeded forms of
  `@margoengine/procedural` (block, slab, wedge, shard, pebble) never appeared.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a terrain under a floating origin changed 0.1 percent of its pixels when the origin rebased in place (KB-TERRAIN-REBASEROUND1, terrain)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/terrain/test/origin.browser.mjs`, stack `stream`: the streamed
  ground at 1e7 m with the origin on the lattice, then rebased onto the camera in place (the camera keeps its world
  pose): 79 of 76,800 pixels changed by one level of 255 (99.897 percent equal against the 99.9 percent bar), 66
  natively (99.914), each a single channel scattered over the near ground. With the 16x anisotropic sampler of
  KB-TERRAIN-GRAZESMEAR1 the WebGL2 layer failed the bar; with the isotropic one it read 99.932.
- **Cause:** the lit draw worked in local coordinates, world less the origin's shift. A rebase in place changes every
  local number, so every float32 rounding derived from them changed: the clip position (the camera matrix's
  translation and the product with a local vertex), each layer's texture coordinate (local position plus a `wrap` of
  a different size) and its screen derivatives (differences of interpolated local positions). The texture unit rounds
  coordinates to sub-texel steps and the level to a fraction, and an anisotropic footprint takes several such taps, so
  a fraction of pixels moved across an 8-bit rounding step. Measured on the RTX A6000 with each part swapped in a
  scratch build: eye-relative texture coordinates alone left 45 pixels, an eye-relative clip position alone 64, both 5.
- **Fix:** the floating-origin terrain draws relative to the eye (Cozzi and Ring 2011, "3D Engine Design for Virtual
  Globes", chapter 5; Ohlarik 2008, "Precisions, Precisions"). The vertex writes `Output.eye` from `Frame.view`, the
  ring's lattice less the eye computed in float64, plus the ring-relative grid offset, and the clip position is
  `camera * (eye, 0)` plus `Frame.column` (the camera matrix times the local eye, float64). The lit shader's last step
  (`eyeShader`) reads every layer sample at the eye-relative point plus the layer's `eyeWrap` and `eyeTone` (the eye
  less the anchor, less whole macro repeats), with derivatives of that point; the virtual texture's bake keeps the
  local reading, the same texels either way. Rebased in place the stream now changes 5 pixels on the WebGL2 layer and
  3 natively (99.993 and 99.996 percent), the float32 rounding of the camera matrix's own translation that is left.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/origin.test.js` ("a rebase in place keeps the eye-relative ring lattice and
  layer wraps bit-identical") and `packages/terrain/test/origin.browser.mjs` on both backends.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the ground between a meadow's far tussocks smeared into flat blotches at low angles (KB-TERRAIN-GRAZESMEAR1, terrain)

- **Repro (before):** the FG-16 whole scene (a BiomeView temperate meadow from 0.9 to 6 m up, Bruneton sky, shadows,
  TAA, auto-exposed tonemap): past a few metres the ground texture between the grass clumps read as soft blotches with
  no grain. `node packages/terrain/test/anisotropy.browser.mjs`: flat ground with one grey value-noise texture seen 3.4
  degrees down from 1.2 m kept a luma deviation along the rows of 2.36 past about 25 m and 4.53 nearer (RTX A6000).
- **Cause:** the terrain's one layer sampler (`packages/terrain/src/index.ts`) filtered isotropically. Seen from eye
  height a pixel's footprint on the ground is 10 to 40 times longer than it is wide, and an isotropic filter takes the
  mip level of the long side, so the detail across the view averaged away.
- **Fix:** the sampler filters anisotropically, `maxAnisotropy: 16` (WebGPU's largest; every filter is linear, as it
  needs). The WebGL2 layer maps it to `EXT_texture_filter_anisotropic`. The same rows now hold 4.35 and 6.93 on both
  backends, and the meadow frames show the ground's grain between the tussocks.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/anisotropy.browser.mjs` (real GPU; `MARGO_COMPAT=1` for the WebGL2 layer).

### Open 2026-11-28: the oak imposter and middle ring change the tree by more than turning it 45 degrees does (KB-PROCEDURAL-OAKIMPOSTER1, procedural)

- **Repro:** `packages/procedural/test/broadleaf-lod.test.js` measures `broadleafLevels('english-oak')` from 8 azimuths
  and elevations 0, 10 and 30 degrees (coverage inside the near outline and mean luminance, the rule of
  `conifer-lod.test.js`). The near tree turned 45 degrees changes by 9.3 percent (coverage) and 9.9 (luminance). The
  middle ring (seed 1) differs by 5.4 and 8.7 percent and passes; seed 2 differs by 8.0 and 9.3 against its own 4.5 and
  5.7. The three-card imposter differs by -14 to +9 percent (coverage) and -22 to +9 (luminance).
- **Cause:** the near cards overlap about 11 deep, so coverage saturates near 0.8 and the middle ring's fewer, wider
  cards match it only on average, with the noise of a different random placement (hence the 2.25 times width). Three
  vertical cards each hold one baked view: seen between two cards the oblique cards add coverage the near tree does not
  have, and seen from 30 degrees above they lose the dome of the crown.
- **Fix needed:** a view-dependent or soft-alpha bake (fewer artefacts than three fixed views), or a horizontal cap
  card, judged on the same measure; the test holds the imposter at its measured ceiling (0.16 coverage, 0.25
  luminance) until then.
- **Progress (middle ring, 2026-11-28):** the open-grown oak (wider crown, 7,248 near card faces) made every fourth
  card at one width fail: at 2.25 times the side coverage was 9.0 percent off, at 1.9 coverage passed and luminance was
  7.5 (the near tree's own 45 degree change 5.28 and 4.71). The cause: every k-th card samples all cards, while the
  view shows mostly the bright outer ones (visible pixels by light row 37.7, 33.3 and 21.4 percent against a card
  population of 28.6, 42.1 and 29.2), so the middle ring was 3.3 percent darker at equal cover. The middle ring is now
  chosen by visibility (stratified pruning over 12 views, per-mass sizes solved to the near coverage;
  `middleCards` in `broadleaves.ts`). Measured, worst of 24 views against the tree's own change: oak seeds 1 to 5
  coverage 1.9 to 2.6 percent (own 4.5 to 6.7), luminance 1.8 to 4.9 (own 4.7 to 9.1); old and sapling oak and beech
  seeds 1 and 2 pass. Still failing, the middle ring of the black alder: seed 1 luminance 5.73 against 5.42, seed 2
  coverage 6.24 against 3.87 and luminance 5.65 against 5.05, seed 3 luminance 6.57 against 5.16 (its middle wood
  takes up to 2,900 of the 4,000 triangles, leaving it 255 to 360 cards). `test/broadleaf-lod.test.js` holds oak
  seeds 1 to 3. The imposter part stays open.
- **Progress (black alder middle ring, fixed 2026-11-28):** two limits, not the method. The middle ring kept at most a
  quarter of the near cards, and the alder has only about 1,540 (the oak 3,624, where 800 binds), so 363 to 385 cards;
  seed 2's first-order wood took 2,918 triangles, leaving 266. Now the middle ring keeps at most half the near cards and
  its wood at most 1,500 triangles (`MIDDLE_WOOD`; the thinnest first-order limb ends go first, found by bisection on
  their radii, a parent kept before its child). Worst of 24 views against the tree's own change: alder seeds 1 to 5
  coverage 2.4 to 2.9 percent (own 3.3 to 7.3), luminance 1.5 to 4.0 (own 3.4 to 6.1); old and sapling alder, beech
  seeds 1 to 3, old and sapling beech, oak seeds 1 to 5, old and sapling oak all pass. The mature oak's middle ring is
  unchanged. `test/broadleaf-lod.test.js` now holds alder seeds 1 to 3 and the wood budget.

- **Repro:** the FG-16 meadow frames (`BiomeView` temperate preset, its oaks 50 to 300 m away): each crown is two or

  `@margoengine/procedural/trees` already grows, then clustered leaf cards), near, middle and imposter levels as the
  conifers have, judged on whole-scene frames. A planner-sized job across procedural and biomes.
- **Progress (step A, 2026-11-28):** `@margoengine/procedural/broadleaves`, `/broadleaf-species` and
  `/broadleaf-settings` build the oak, beech and alder with limbs, shed inner branches, alpha-cut leaf cards and three

- **Progress (step B, 2026-11-28):** biomes draws `procedural:broadleaf` and the oak, beech and alder keys from
  `/broadleaves` (white canopy over its atlas; the seasons scale it by the tinted mean leaf colour, hue kept when a
  tint would pass 1). FG-16 frames on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer now show limbs, sky through the crowns and ragged
  outlines. Judged beside open-grown summer Quercus robur photographs (Wikimedia Commons), still open: (1) the crowns
  read too open and spindly, limbs showing where a summer oak shows a broad, mostly closed dome on a short bole, so the

  (4) one mature oak takes about 0.5 s to grow (plan bound 30 ms; move the loop to `trees-kernel` or cut the work).
  The sync default (step C) is not done.
- **Progress (oak form, 2026-11-28):** for (1), the oak's crown now runs from Hemery's line to the free-standing
  crowns of Coombes, Martin and Slater 2019 (25.5 dbh at `open` 1), its open-grown height levels off at 21.3 m (Bean),
  limbs pitch from -22 degrees, spray cards tilt 40 to 65 degrees and fill masses go wherever a sampled spot lies a

  seeds 1 to 10, 7 pass; seeds 5, 6 and 9 read 0.206 to 0.217 (holes inside the crown). (2) to (4) and step C open.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a meadow seen from a few metres up showed the edge of the dense near grass as a band (KB-BIOMES-GRASSRING1, biomes, scatter)

- **Repro (before):** the FG-16 wide shot (camera 6 m up): the ground within 20 m was a dense sward and beyond it the
  grass thinned at once, a line across the frame. `packages/biomes/tests/meadow-grass-check.mjs`, 6 m up looking 20
  degrees down: the share of ground the grass covers fell from 97.6 to 31.9 percent between 14 and 18 m (RTX A6000).
- **Cause:** the near layer held 3 clumps a square metre per unit of density (120 for the temperate preset) and the
  field about 10; the near layer shrank over its last 4 m (`edgeShrink`) as the field faded in (`inner`, `innerFade`),
  so the density fell about twelve times within 4 m (`packages/biomes/src/objects.ts`, `NEAR_GRASS`).
- **Fix:** scatter gains `edgeThin`: instances drop out one by one, each at its own hashed distance, over a band before
  the last LOD, so the count falls linearly to none while survivors keep their size and place (the thinning of Cook,
  Halstead, Planck and Ryu, "Stochastic Simplification of Aggregate Detail", SIGGRAPH 2007). Biomes' near layer now
  reaches 40 m and thins over its outer 32 m, and the field runs under it to the camera at 0.45 candidates a square
  metre per unit of density (1,000,000 at most, was 0.25). The same check now covers 92 to 100 percent from 10 to 60
  m with no fall over 4 points between 2 m bins, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; the wide frame shows no band. Cost:
  the field places up to 74 percent more clumps.
- **Regression:** `packages/biomes/tests/meadow-grass-check.mjs` (real GPU; `MARGO_COMPAT=1` for the WebGL2 layer),
  `packages/scatter/test/inner.browser.mjs` (`edges` cases, `--compat` too) and `packages/scatter/test/tiles.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the lens drops' glint added light over empty pixels without covering them (KB-WEATHER-LENSGLINT1, weather)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs`, "lens drops over nothing": `LensDrops` alone on a
  `TransparentCanvas` with an empty scene put light on 1,783 pixels whose coverage was 0.
- **Cause:** the composite added the glint (up to 0.08 and more where drops overlap) to the premultiplied colour and
  kept the sampled alpha, 0 where the scene holds nothing. The test's coverage reading missed it too: over a white page
  added light clips at white and reads as covered.
- **Fix:** the glint covers by its own luminance, alpha = a + (1 - a) glint (Porter and Duff 1984,
  https://graphics.pixar.com/library/Compositing/paper.pdf), so an opaque pixel keeps alpha 1 and its colour is
  unchanged. The test now reads coverage from a grey page. 1,893 pixels covered, none bare, the same on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000).
- **Regression:** that test.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a BiomeView meadow drew its grass as sparse tufts on bare ground (KB-BIOMES-SPARSEGRASS1, biomes)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/biomes/tests/meadow-grass-check.mjs`: a temperate grassland from 0.9 m up, grass

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a Material mesh given to a `GLTFWeather` under the scene's `Puddles` failed to compile (KB-WEATHER-GLTFTWICE1, weather, materials)

- **Repro:** Last Tram: `Puddles.attach(engine, {...})` and `GLTFWeather.attach(engine, {puddles: {...}})`, then
  `gltfWeather.add(model)` on a model built from Material meshes (the film passes every model to its receivers, a
  `GLTFWeather` among them). The shader failed with "redeclaration of 'WeatherPuddles'" and of every
  `weather_puddle_*` function, and had it compiled the surface would have been wetted twice.
- **Cause:** the KB-WEATHER-MATERIALSWET1 fix joins every Material mesh to the scene's `materialSurface` effects by
  itself, and a Material mesh is a gltf/pbr model, so `GLTFWeather.add` gave it a second effect carrying the same
  puddle and snow WGSL. Nothing told one side about the other.
- **Fix:** the explicit call wins. `GLTFWeather.add` counts the model in a registry the weather entries share
  (`packages/weather/src/gltf-served.ts`) and its remover and `dispose` count it out; the `materialSurface` effect of
  `Puddles`, `Snow` and `PrecipitationCover` gains `skips(model)`, true while any `GLTFWeather` has the model, and the
  materials queue (`packages/materials/src/scene-surfaces.ts`) joins a mesh any of its scene's effects skips to none of
  them, so it takes puddles, snow and cover from its `GLTFWeather` alone. Regression:
  `packages/weather/tests/material-wet-browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) draws a Material ground given to a
  `GLTFWeather` under the scene's `Puddles`: it compiles and matches the scene's Puddles alone and the GLTFWeather alone
  (mean difference 0), where before the fix the page threw the eight redeclaration errors. Unit tests:
  `packages/weather/tests/material-surface.test.js` (the skip follows every GLTFWeather that has the model) and
  `packages/materials/tests/scene-surfaces.test.js` (a skipped mesh joins none and rejoins when handed back).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: Puddles and Snow left `@margoengine/materials` surfaces dry (KB-WEATHER-MATERIALSWET1, weather, materials)

- **Repro:** Last Tram (`examples/showcase-films/last-tram.js`) with `Puddles.attach(engine, {wetness: 0.98, rain:
  0.72, coverage: 0.39})`: the core `PbrMaterial` ground darkened, held puddles and rain rings, while the asphalt
  strips, platform and ballast drawn with `Material` from `@margoengine/materials` kept their dry colour and roughness,
  so the film had to set a wet-looking roughness on them by hand.
- **Cause:** `SurfaceHook` (`packages/weather/src/scene-patch.ts`) patched only core's mesh shader, at the top of its
  `fragment` function. A Material mesh draws with gltf/pbr's shader, which the materials package rewrites
  (`built-material.ts`); it had no surface hook for the weather entries to reach, so `weather_puddle_surface` and the
  snow cover never ran there.
- **Fix:** each Material mesh joins its scene's surface hooks by itself (`packages/materials/src/scene-surfaces.ts`):
  before each draw the material queue gives the mesh, through gltf/pbr `addLighting`, the `materialSurface` lighting
  effect of the scene's `weather-puddles`, `weather-snow` and `weather-cover` plugins in their order, and takes it away
  when they go. `Puddles`, `Snow` and `PrecipitationCover` offer that effect: it wraps gltf/pbr's whole `surface()`
  (after every map, triplanar and parallax read) with the same WGSL as on core meshes, bound in group 2 at slots
  166 to 169, the snow's vertex lift included. Only meshes with a lit material join; `mesh.sceneSurfaces = false`
  keeps one dry.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/material-wet-browser.mjs` draws the same ground as a core mesh and
  as a Material mesh, dry, wet with standing water and rain rings, and snowed on, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: the
  wet and snowy Material match the core surface (mean relative difference under 1e-7, no pixel off by 2 percent),
  where before the fix every one of the 38,072 ground pixels differed by 34 percent on average. Unit tests:
  `packages/weather/tests/material-surface.test.js` and `packages/materials/tests/scene-surfaces.test.js`.
