### Fixed 2026-11-28: liquid and underwater fog over the empty part of a transparent canvas were see-through (KB-WATER-LIQUIDALPHA1, water)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs` on a `TransparentCanvas`: through the middle of a dense 0.8 m
  `ParticleLiquid` ball over nothing the page showed with coverage 0.004, 1,397 pixels added light while covering
  nothing, and 3 m under a sea 34,426 of 76,800 pixels did the same under `Underwater`.
- **Cause:** both composites wrote the scene's alpha, which is 0 where the scene holds nothing, whatever the liquid or
  the water put in the pixel. Whitewater over empty pixels added its colour and no coverage the same way.
- **Fix:** each writes the coverage its medium makes: the liquid 1 - (1 - Fresnel) T (1 - a) with a the scene alpha
  where the refracted ray ends and T the Beer-Lambert transmittance's Rec. 709 luminance; whitewater composites its
  alpha with its colour; underwater 1 - (1 - a) T of the view path, over the submerged share (Porter and Duff 1984,
  https://graphics.pixar.com/library/Compositing/paper.pdf). An opaque scene keeps alpha 1. Dense ball 0.91, clear
  liquid 0.020 (its reflection), under water every pixel covered, the same on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000).
- **Regression:** the same GPU test, the "liquid over nothing" and "under water" cases.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: parse3MF refused a package of more than 1,024 model parts, so Margo could not read its own 10,000-part export (KB-3MF-PARTLIMIT1, loaders)

- **Repro (before):** `export3MF(NodePerformanceTest.glb, {assembly: 'components', production: {separateParts: true}})`
  writes 10,000 parts; `parse3MF` on it threw `loaders/3mf: archive has 10003 entries, more than the limit of 10000`,
  and with `maxEntries` raised, `too many model parts` at the 1,025th part. No option lifted the second.
- **Cause:** a hard-coded `models.size >= 1024` in `read3MF` (`packages/loaders/src/threemf.ts`), and the shared ZIP
  default of 10,000 entries, though each production part is its own entry.
- **Fix:** `ThreeMFOptions.maxModelParts`, default 65,535 (every part a ZIP without ZIP64 can hold; the root counts),
  and 3MF's `maxEntries` default follows it (in `parse3MFKeystore` too). `maxBytes`, `maxTriangles` and
  `maxEntryBytes` still bound the work. The other ZIP formats keep 10,000 entries.
- **Regression:** `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-part-limit.test.js` (fails before the fix) and the NodePerformanceTest
  read-back in `packages/exporters/tests/threemf-part-prune.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: rebase:main left docs/api-surface.md with a wrong Unexported figure and a short total (KB-REBASE-SURFACE1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `npm run api:check` on main 66546e10a1: `webgl2-compat` read 313 unexported (the reports hold 307) and the
  totals line 18,715 exported names (the rows sum to 18,722). `tests/api-report-scope.test.js` "committed API totals
  include every package table row" failed there too.
- **Cause:** two. `mergeApiSurfaceRows` summed both sides' differences for the Unexported and `any` cells even when both
  sides had made the same change, so efdf5d9a0e's 304 to 307 was added again at 9ef46f22c1 (310) and 1b3dfe2214 (313).
  And two commits that each added exports to different rows wrote the same totals line, which git merges without a
  conflict, so no generator ran (b84c368435, 5 short; 33d8c6be64, 2 more).
- **Fix:** a cell both sides changed alike is counted once; one they changed differently has its package's report built
  again; the totals are counted from the rows, in `mergeScopedApiSurface` and as a last step of `rebase:main`.
- **Regression:** `tests/rebase-main.test.js`, both "(KB-REBASE-SURFACE1)" tests.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a pixel a blended grass blade covered kept the ground's motion in TAA and MotionBlur (KB-SCATTER-BLENDVEL1, scatter)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scatter/test/velocity.browser.mjs`, a still camera over a `GrassScatter` in wind
  with `ScatterVelocity`: 35,899 of the 256 x 256 pixels moved. The covered rings blend each blade over the ground by
  its coverage, so pixels whose colour was mostly blade still carried the ground's vector (zero for a still camera),
  which is what MotionBlur and TAA then followed there.
- **Cause:** the velocity pass tests depth for equality, so it reached only the pixels a blade wrote depth to: an
  opaque core, or the hashed coverage-depth stage, which keeps a fragment with probability equal to its coverage. A
  blended fragment that lost the hash wrote no depth and so no vector (`packages/scatter/src/velocity.ts`).
- **Fix:** after the depth-equal stages each covered stage is drawn again, depth-tested in front of the depth there
  (`greater`, core's reversed depth) and writing none, keeping fragments the blade covers by at least
  `ScatterVelocityOptions.coverage` (default 0.5), far rings first. 37,608 pixels move now (37,584 on the WebGL2 layer
  against 35,849). Regression: `packages/scatter/test/velocity.browser.mjs` (the `coverage: false` run against the
  default, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: tree LOD rings were chosen by distance alone, whatever the lens or resolution (KB-BIOMES-SCREENLOD1, scatter, biomes)

- **Repro:** `BiomeObjects` set every tree's rings at `[0.15 r, 0.4 r, r]` metres; scatter's cull picked a ring by
  the instance's distance only, so a spray's size on screen at the hand-over followed the camera's field of view and
  viewport height: through a wide lens or on a small viewport a middle spray could fall under a pixel before the
  imposter took over.
- **Fix:** scatter `lodSize` (the near and middle mesh's finest feature at scale 1) and `lodPixels` (default 1): each
  of the first two rings ends at its distance or where that feature, times the instance's scale, projects under
  `lodPixels` viewport pixels (from the camera's pixel footprint each frame), whichever is first. The ends move only
  past 5 percent of footprint drift and are set from the footprint plus that 5 percent (hysteresis, and never under a
  pixel). The cull text is unchanged without `lodSize` (`screenRingCode`), and the WebGL2 candidate kernel and
  ScatterTiles take it. Biomes measures each tree's spray width (`foliageWidth`, area-weighted tenth percentile of the
  triangles' narrowest widths) and passes it when `BiomeObjects` is given `lodPixels`. Not on by default: on the
  timber-valley blowup it raised speckle (KB-LOOK-TV-SPECKLE above), so the manager decides the default. Source:
  Luebke, Reddy, Cohen, Varshney, Watson and Huebner, Level of Detail for 3D Graphics (2003), ch. 4.
- **Regression:** `packages/scatter/test/lod.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and `--compat`): at 256 and 512 rows, 45 and 30
  degrees and scale 1 and 2, each ring hands over within 2 percent of where its feature projects to a pixel, the ends
  scale with resolution and scale, a drawn feature is never under a pixel, a 3 percent zoom keeps the rings and a 10
  percent one moves them; `packages/scatter/test/screen-lod.test.js`; `packages/biomes/tests/objects.test.js`,
  "with lodPixels".

### Fixed 2026-11-28: motionBlur called a correctly smeared mover narrower than its smear sharp, and passed a half-length one (KB-LOOK-TV-MBNARROW1, headless look)

- **Repro:** a bar 12 px wide moving 64 px a frame, exposed over a 180 degree shutter as a continuous smear (256
  sub-frames), read by `motionBlur(frame, motion)`: 100 percent sharp (24 of 24 edges). The same bar smeared over half
  that length passed, and so did its 8 sharp copies.
- **Cause:** the check calls an edge sharp when its 10 to 90 percent ramp is under a quarter of the travel (half the
  180 degree smear). A box blur of length L over a bar of width w < L ramps over w, not L, with a plateau of L - w, so
  a narrow mover's ramp is its own width however well it is blurred. The ramp was also every sample in the band across
  the whole profile, so a short mover's rise and fall added up and a half smear passed; and `stepped` measured its ramp
  without its end sample and read its jumps one pixel apart from the ramp's start, so a jump split across two reads
  was two half jumps and a narrow staircase was missed.
- **Fix:** `edgeSpan` takes the contiguous ramp round the edge's crossing and, for a profile that holds a plateau past
  90 percent and comes back inside the window, the ramp plus that plateau, which is the mover's smear over the
  sub-frames' travel (0.8 w + L - w + 0.2 w = L). An edge is sharp when its ramp is under half the smear and its span
  under 0.625 of it, the same share (a wide edge's ramp is 0.8 of its smear). A ramp under 1.6 px gets no span: a
  sharp bar, or a streak under 2 px wide that cannot be told from one. `stepped` counts the ramp's end samples and
  slides its one-pixel read a sample at a time. No bound changed (ruling, 2026-11-28: a check that flags a correctly
  rendered blur is a check defect).
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js`, "(KB-LOOK-TV-MBNARROW1)": the smeared 12 px bar at
  64 px passes (100 to 0 percent sharp); drawn sharp, half smeared or as 8 sharp copies it fails (the half smear read
  0 percent before).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a swaying near leaf's soft fringe read as shimmer, its trail holding the sky's velocity (KB-SCATTER-FRINGEVEL1, headless look)

- **Repro (before):** `shimmerMoving` on the timber-valley blowup mid probe (8 sub-frames, 180 degrees, with the engine
  velocity): 1.72 percent off (bound 0.5), most in a band along the near leaves' soft edges at x 1700 to 1920. Row 460,
  x 1716 to 1756: geometry 16 to 223 of 255, depth 0 and the sky's velocity; the leaf's own starts at x 1755.
- **Cause:** not scatter. The geometry mask is the mean over the sub-frames (it steps in eighths, 32, 64 ... 223), while
  depth and velocity are the last sub-frame's: the fringe is the leaf's trail across the shutter, sky by the last
  sub-frame, so TAA's velocity and `ScatterVelocity` were right. The leaf, near the lens, moves 63 px a frame on screen
  (53 px of it the camera's parallax), but `shimmerMoving`'s blur reach sized its smear from its motion past the camera
  (10 px, a 2.5 px reach) and centred it, when the 8 sub-frames lay a 30 px trail behind its last position
  (`packages/headless/src/look.ts`, `blurReach`).
- **Fix:** the reach takes the mover's whole screen velocity against pixels whose surface moves otherwise, runs back over
  the travel between the first and last sub-frame plus half a slice's blur (`MovingFrames.subframes`, which `checkShot`
  passes from the render), reaches half a slice ahead, and is applied to the next frame too with `nextVelocity` and
  `back`. Mid 1.72 to 0.53, early 0.44 to 0.28. The 0.53 left is one-pixel rims on near conifer sprays whose sway is
  under half a pixel past the camera (KB-LOOK-TV-SHIMMER2).
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js`, "(KB-SCATTER-FRINGEVEL1)" (80 pixels reached before,
  768 now).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a spinning bullet's strike at 300 m/s throws it sideways by a speed that follows the substeps, as substeps reuse the step's contacts (KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK1, physics kernel, contacts)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/next-ccd.test.js`'s dynamic plate scene, seed 9, bullet 64 alone with the plate (a 4 x 4 x
  12 cm steel box at 300 m/s, spinning at about 30 rad/s, ccd on, no gravity): after the strike it leaves at 45.4 m/s along the
  face with 8 substeps (the default), 10.7 m/s with 32 and 17.6 m/s with 64, spinning at 650, 230 and 440 rad/s. The answer does
  not settle as the step shrinks. Energy is lost, not made (3 percent of the kinetic energy is left), the tangential impulse is
  0.15 of the normal, inside the cone, and in the full scene its later hit on bullet 170 conserves momentum exactly.
- **Cause (traced 2026-11-28, lane P):** contacts are found once a step and every substep reuses those points with gaps
  read from the new poses (`kernel/src/solver.rs`, header). After the strike's first corner the bullet turns about 1.4 rad a
  default substep and some 11 rad over the step, so the corners that meet the plate later in the step are not in the
  manifold the step began with. More substeps cannot recover them: at a 1/60 s step the knock runs 45.4, 24.7, 10.7, 17.6,
  16.9, 5.5, 10.0, 4.4, 4.6, 0.87, 0.74 m/s at 8 to 8,192 substeps (the repro scene, bullet 64 alone, two steps), away from the answer. A finer
  step, which finds contacts again, does settle: 8 substeps at 1/61,440 s and 1/245,760 s give 63.8 and 64.3 m/s (spin 445
  and 429 rad/s), so the default 45.4 m/s is 30 percent under the kernel's own converged knock. Not chaos: perturbing the
  spin by 1e-9 to 1e-3 moves the knock by under 0.2 m/s at any fixed substep count. The Rapier 3D oracle (devDependency,
  tests/oracle.js) shares the method and the behaviour: at 1/60 s its knock runs 2.8, 11.3, 10.4, 10.5, 14.7, 14.7, 25.4,
  49.7 and 71.9 m/s at 1 to 512 solver iterations, and its fine-step limit is about 91 m/s (91.3 and 91.8 at 1/61,440 and
  1/245,760 s, rebounding at 16 to 17 m/s where the kernel's inelastic point leaves at 2 m/s).
- **Fix plan, tried (planner, 2026-11-28):** finding the points again between substeps is the same as stepping at dt/8 with
  one substep, and it lands the bar flat: 0.68 m/s at 8 substeps, 57 m/s only at 4,096. The strike is five impacts within
  3 ms, the first two 24 microseconds apart at up to 3,900 rad/s, all inside 1.5 default substeps, so they must be met in
  time order; and the default's 45.4 m/s was luck, as bullets 10, 100 and 150 left at 0.28, 4.98 and 0.16 m/s.
- **Fix (lane P, 2026-11-28):** strike pieces (`kernel/src/strike.rs`, from `solve_island`): an island with a dynamic CCD body
  cuts each substep at the time its CCD pairs may next touch (conservative advancement: the least gap of their points, at
  least 2 percent of the thinnest CCD piece, over the normal speed plus each body's spin across the normal times its reach;
  a ball's spin about its centre and a revolved shape's about its axis do not count), and from the first cut to the step's
  end every piece finds the island's pairs again (`narrow.rs` `refresh_pair`) and remakes their rows (`solver.rs`
  `prepare_rows`), each new point carrying what the point it continues held. A pair whose replaced points touched is marked
  `PAIR_STRUCK` for the step's events. An island that never cuts runs its substeps as before, to the bit. Knock at 8, 16, 32
  and 64 substeps against the kernel's fine step (1 substep at 1/(60 x 32,768) s): bullet 64 60.9, 62.5, 62.2, 62.2 against
  63.2 m/s (before 44.3, 24.7, 10.7, 17.6); bullet 10 63.7 against 63.1 (before 0.28); bullet 100 69.9 against 72.5 (4.98);
  bullet 150 63.1 against 61.3 (0.16). Islands with a joint, coupling or multibody, a kinematic body, or a mesh, compound,
  filtered or modified pair take no pieces yet: KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK2.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/strike.rs` (the four bullets within 10 percent of the fine step; bullet 64
  within 10 percent at 8 to 64 substeps; a CCD cylinder rolling at 30 m/s steps bit for bit as one without CCD, so it takes
  no piece), `kernel/tests/threads.rs` (two plates struck by spinning CCD bars, the same bits on 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads).

### Open 2026-11-28: a tumbling CCD body in an island with a joint, a kinematic body or a mesh still strikes on the step's points (KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK2, physics kernel, contacts)

- **Repro:** the KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK1 scene (`kernel/tests/strike.rs`, bullet 64 of seed 9) with the plate as a two-triangle mesh,
  as a kinematic body, or with the bar on a joint: `strike_bound` gives such an island no pieces, so it strikes on the step's
  points, as KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK1 measured before its fix (not measured again on these variants).
- **Cause:** strike pieces (`kernel/src/strike.rs`) find a pair's points again on the island's own thread, so they take only
  pairs that write their own row (`threadable`: no mesh or compound pair, which makes and frees parts, and no filtered pair,
  which calls out) and no contact modifier; a kinematic body is read at the step's stages, not between them; and a joint,
  coupling or multibody would need its carried impulses scaled to each piece and its stamps claimed per piece. Those islands
  run their substeps whole.
- **Needed to close:** the narrow phase's part pairs found on an island (or the struck pair's parts found again on the world
  between pieces), kinematic poses read at a piece's time into its substep, and the joints' and multibodies' scaling, each
  with the same bar as KB-PHYS-CCDKNOCK1 and the threads test held.

### Open 2026-11-28: a floating body's carried water swaps energy with it as its draft changes (KB-LOADS-ADDEDRATE1, physics)

- **Repro:** a 0.1 m sphere at half the water's density let go 0.04 m above its rest on still water, `LoadSolver` at 60
  steps a second, drag 0: its energy with the water it carries (Lamb's added mass, (1/2) A v^2) swings by 13 % of
  m g r within a swing and drifts about 10 % over 20 s; with drag (the default) the body still ends below its start.
- **Cause:** the added mass scales with the submerged volume and the solver holds A dv/dt = F. Lagrange's equation for
  a kinetic energy (1/2) v^T A(q) v gives A dv/dt = F - (1/2) (dA/dt) v (Lamb 1932, art. 136-137).
- **Tried:** the rate term with each body's last submerged volumes as snapshot state, exact in energy over a step;
  it closed the sphere's swing to 1.5 % but damped the undamped wall-sided box of KB-LOADS-HEAVEGAIN1 by 0.15 % a
  swing (`tests/loads-floating.test.js`), so it was not landed. The term taken at the step's energy-neutral pose
  (as the buoyancy is) is the next try.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: two limits rows were short of cells, the USD texture factors and water on a transparent canvas (KB-LIMITS-USDZCELL1, usdz, water, docs)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/claims-file.test.js`, "every table row in docs/limits.md has as many cells as its

### Open 2026-11-28: a film seek cannot move GPU cloth, so it restarts at every cut (KB-FILM-CLOTH1, physics gpu-cloth)

- **Repro:** a cloth from `@margoengine/physics/gpu-cloth` in a film rendered scene by scene: `seek` from
  `@margoengine/cutscene/seek` replays every clock's `advanceTime` to the scene's film time, but the cloth has none, so
  it starts each scene hanging from its pins at rest. `node scripts/check-film-time.mjs` lists
  `packages/physics/src/gpu-cloth.ts:598`.
- **Cause:** `GPUCloth.onPreUpdate(delta)` adds the frame delta to `pending` and plans the frame's substeps from the
  physics world's pin and collider poses after its step; with no `advanceTime` the seek leaves it alone, and the world
  it reads is not replayed either.
- **Fix wanted (owner of SOFT-01, docs/physics-work-queue.md):** `advanceTime(delta)` owing the frame's steps as
  `GPUFlock` does (KB-FILM-FLOCK1), fed the replayed world poses, with a seek check on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
  Until then `scripts/film-time-reviewed.json` names this entry for the hit.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: ten-thousand-trees hung on the WebGL2 layer; warmUp could not warm terrain, Water or Bloom (KB-WATER-WARMUP1, quality, water, post)

- **Repro (before):** `node scripts/web-demos/controls.mjs ten-thousand-trees --backends=webgl2`: "hung: a page script
  took over 15000 ms". `scripts/web-demos/startup-profile.mjs ten-thousand-trees`: one 9.3 s task at the first frame,
  3.1 s of it in a `checkFramebufferStatus` behind the water surface program's compile for its three targets (ANGLE
  Direct3D 11 compiles it again at its first draw) and 2 s in its `LINK_STATUS`.
- **Cause:** the demo made every pipeline synchronously in its first frame. `warmUp` (`@margoengine/quality/warm`) makes
  them with the async API, and the layer's async path draws each program once and waits on a fence without blocking,
  but warmUp failed on this scene three ways: (1) terrain's surface height makes a new pipeline layout on every call,
  warmUp keyed layouts by identity, so every retry missed again (256 rounds, 128 synchronous fallbacks); (2) Water
  stored its surface depth texture and then made its depth copy pipeline only when that texture changed, so a frame
  stopped at the copy pipeline left none, and `bindDepth` threw; (3) `OutputKey` (Bloom and ten other post stages)
  remembered the new output in `changed`, before the stage built its pipeline, so a stopped frame left Bloom with none.
  (2) and (3) made warmUp restore the device and finish synchronously.
- **Fix:** warmUp keys bind group and pipeline layouts by their descriptors (layouts made from the same descriptor are
  group-equivalent in WebGPU); Water keys its depth copy pipeline by depth format and samples and sets the key only
  once the pipeline exists; `OutputKey.changed` only compares and `done()` keeps the fields after the build, called by
  every stage. The demo calls `warmUp` before `engine.start()`.
- **Numbers (loaded workstation, one run each):** WebGL2 layer longest task 9.3 s before, 0.7 s after; ready 21 s
  before, 32 s after (the warm-up compiles one pipeline per round, 45 rounds, 22 s; the page answers throughout).
  WebGPU ready 13 s with a 4 s warm-up. `controls.mjs ten-thousand-trees`: ok on both backends.
- **Regression:** `packages/quality/test/warm.test.js` ("makes its layouts again on every call"),
  `packages/water/test/warm-up.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`; rebooted before), `tests/output-key.test.js`
  (a build that throws is tried again; every stage calls `done()`).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a film seek could not move a GPU flock, so it restarted at every cut (KB-FILM-FLOCK1, vfx)

- **Repro:** `GPUFlock.attach(engine, options)` in a film rendered scene by scene: `seek` from
  `@margoengine/cutscene/seek` found no `advanceTime`, so the flock started each scene at its seed state.
- **Cause:** `onPreUpdate` kept only the last frame delta for the simulate pass, so steps without a draw were lost.
- **Fix:** `advanceTime(delta)` owes each frame step and the next simulate pass runs them in order (runs of equal
  steps in one pass; runs of two lengths each in its own submit, since the sim uniform is written by the queue).
  Regression: `packages/vfx/test/flocking-check.mjs` (seekEven, seekMixed; WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) and
  `tests/film-time.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a 3MF with `production: {separateParts: true}` copied every resource group whole into each part (KB-3MF-PARTCOPY1, exporters)

- **Repro (before):** `export3MF(NodePerformanceTest.glb, {assembly: 'components', production: {separateParts: true}})`
  (`examples/assets/khronos`, 10,001 mesh nodes): RangeError "ZIP would exceed 268435456 bytes". The same scene with
  `assembly: 'components'` alone is 10,402,277 B, and with `production: true` in one part 10,056,754 B.
- **Cause:** a part may refer only to resources in itself (production extension 3.2), so the writer copies into each
  part the resource groups its object names (`resourcesOf`, `packages/exporters/src/threemf.ts`). It copied a group
  whole: this scene's one `basematerials` holds about 10,000 entries with their `pbmetallicdisplayproperties`, and
  every part carried both, past `encodeZIP`'s 256 MiB, which it counts uncompressed.
- **Fix:** `prunedPart` gives each part copies of its indexed groups (base materials, colour, texture coordinate,
  composite and multiproperties groups and display properties) cut to the entries its object reaches, through
  `multiproperties` layers, composite `matindices` and display properties index for index, and renumbers the object's
  `pindex`, `p1` to `p3`, the layers' `pindices` and `matindices` to match; textures and other whole resources are
  copied as before. Resources are read once for all parts, so the scene exports in 8.8 s (it scanned every resource
  for every part, about 92 s, once the size was fixed). NodePerformanceTest in separate parts is now 22,603,139 B,
  10,000 parts of 4,155 to 7,286 B, against 10,363,111 B as components. Regression test
  `packages/exporters/tests/threemf-part-prune.test.js`: a scene of metallic, translucent and vertex-coloured boxes
  reads back through `parse3MF` and `parse3MFMaterials` with the same groups, colours and positions in separate parts
  as in components, each part's groups holding one entry; and NodePerformanceTest's parts stay under 16 KiB.
  `parse3MF` reads at most 1,024 model parts, so Margo's own reader still refuses this 10,000-part file (limits.md).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: IK folded elbows and knees backwards, and no solver read a joint range unless the caller built one (KB-RIG-IKANATOMY1, rigging, animator)

- **Repro (before):** a standing body with straight legs; `solvePoseIK` on hip, knee, ankle with a pole behind the
  leg, or `addFootPlacement` with `pole: [0, 0.5, -4]` on a 15 cm step: the knee folds backwards (flexion -30 degrees
  and worse). 600 seeded reaches around a hip or a shoulder reversed the hinge in more than 50. `addFullBodyIK` let each
  spine joint turn 0.8 rad (46 degrees) in any direction; `addLookAt` turned a head to a target behind it (177 degrees
  at the neck); a free `addCCDChain` bent an elbow past straight. Scott saw it on the human demos: "the elbows are
  closest to the body".
- **Cause:** the solvers had no model of a body. `solveTwoBoneIK` and FABRIK put the middle joint wherever the pole
  said, a straight limb had no bend side at all (`bendSides` returns null for it), limits were opt in per rig
  ("Omitted joints are free") and the spine had one isotropic `maxBend`.
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/animator/ik`: `setAnatomy(owner, body)` names the fitted body of an Animator, a Skeleton or
  a pose, and every solver obeys it by default: `solveLimbIK` (two-bone IK by swivel angle, the hinge about its own
  axis between straight and its stop, the pole only inside the shoulder's or hip's range), per-joint and shared-region
  limits in full-body IK, look-at, CCD chains, FABRIK chains and contact IK. `limits: false` turns it off by name
  (`body: null` on a CCD chain or a contact, where `limits` is the list of limits).
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/ik-anatomy.test.js` (10,000 reaches per limb on seven rigs; the same
  reaches with `limits: false` must still show the fault), `packages/rigging/tests/ik-anatomy-animator.test.js`,
  the reach sheet `packages/rigging/tests/ik-reach-sheet.browser.mjs` and the Blender referee
  `packages/rigging/tests/ik-blender-check.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: clampPose narrowed a gated twist a second time (KB-RIG-GATEORDER1, rigging)

- **Repro (before):** a knee at flexion 78.7, abduction 44.2, twist 63.1 degrees: `clampPose` leaves the twist at
  34.98; a second `clampPose` on the result moves it to 34.43.
- **Cause:** `clampAngles` in `packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts` read the twist's gate (a knee twists only when
  bent) from the flexion before the swing was brought inside its ellipse, which lowers the flexion a little.
- **Fix:** the swing is settled first and the gate is read from it. `clampTurn` in `@margoengine/animator/ik` does
  the same.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/ik-anatomy.test.js`, "a pose brought inside its ranges once is inside".

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the Animator's built-in `footIK` option bent a leg by its pole alone, also on a fitted body (KB-ANIM-FOOTIK-ANATOMY1, animator)

- **Repro (before):** an Animator made with the `footIK` option on a body named by `setAnatomy`, with a pole behind the
  leg: the knee followed the pole backwards. `addFootPlacement` on the same body bent it the anatomical way.
- **Cause:** `Animator.foot` in `packages/animator/src/index.ts` called `solveTwoBoneIK` directly, the one limb solve
  that did not go through `placeLimb`.
- **Fix:** on an Animator with a fitted body the foot goes through `poseTools().placeLimb`, so the leg obeys the body.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/ik-anatomy-animator.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a pole behind the limb could still turn a fitted arm or leg over (KB-ANIM-POLEBEHIND1, animator)

- **Repro (before):** `addIKChain` on a fitted Animator, arm chain, pole above and behind the shoulder: the shoulder
  turned the arm over toward the pole, to the edge of its twist range.
- **Cause:** `packages/animator/src/ik.ts` took the swivel the pole asks for and only then held it in range, so a pole on
  the far side of the limb pulled the swivel to the edge of the shoulder's or hip's range.
- **Fix:** a pole whose swivel is more than 90 degrees from the comfortable one (the one that leaves the shoulder or
  hip nearest neutral) is left out, and the limb takes the comfortable swivel.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/ik-anatomy-animator.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a cupped hand at rest read as a twisted wrist (KB-RIG-HANDARCH1, rigging)

- **Repro (before):** `fitHuman` on a Character Creator rig, whose relaxed hand is cupped: the wrist's rest read
  pronation, and clips were held off a real wrist turn.
- **Cause:** the radiocarpal frame took its roll from the first knuckle pair of `across`, which included the ring and
  little metacarpals; those move with the arch of the hand (Kapandji, *The Physiology of the Joints*, vol. 1).
- **Fix:** `packages/rigging/src/anatomy-human.ts` lists the index-middle pair first, the fixed part of the hand.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy-hand-forearm.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a forearm twist bone made the hand's pronation spill into the forearm bone (KB-RIG-TWISTBONE1, rigging)

- **Repro (before):** a Character Creator arm (`CC_Base_L_ForearmTwist01` and `02` under the forearm) with the hand
  pronated past the wrist's range: `clampPose` moved the excess into the forearm bone, twisting the skin a second time.
- **Cause:** the wrist's twist range was its own alone, so its excess spilled up the chain; a rig with twist bones turns
  the hand itself for pronation and lets the twist bones spread it along the skin.
- **Fix:** `fitAnatomy` (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts`) finds a bone under the forearm, through bones that are no
  joint, lying along it; the wrist's twist range then takes the forearm's pronation as well and nothing spills.
- **Regression:** `packages/rigging/tests/anatomy-hand-forearm.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a reversed-elbow clip taught addPerson a 105 degree shoulder roll (KB-HUM-ROLLTRUST1, humans)

- **Repro (before):** `addPerson` on a humanoid whose clip bends the left elbow 70 degrees the wrong way: calibration
  read a 105 degree upper arm roll from it and flipped the elbow hinge, so the held clip kept the reversed bend.
- **Cause:** `hingeRolls` takes the axis a clip bends a hinge about as the truth; a clip that bends it backwards gives
  the mirrored axis.
- **Fix:** `packages/humans/src/index.ts` calibrates shoulders and hips only and trusts a roll only up to 30 degrees
  (`ROLL_TRUST`); real rigs measure under 5 (the Character Creator old man of the Fauld cast).
- **Regression:** `packages/humans/test/anatomy-defaults.test.js`.

### Open 2026-11-28: a Character Creator ring finger rests 12.8 degrees past its supination stop (KB-RIG-RINGROLL1, rigging)
- **Learned 2026-11-28:** the pose sheet's held and played rows read many fingers at exactly the stop (MCP supination
  -10.0, CMC1 pronation 40.0) because those rows pass through `clampPose`, which pins a value past the stop at the
  stop; the raw clip (`anatomy: {limits: false}`) reads past it (idle: MCP4 supination -10.5 to -11.6, talk -12.5; CMC1
  pronation up to 53.7). So the checker is reading true; the cause stays the zero this row names.

- **Searched 2026-11-28:** no measured angle for the obliquity of the ring or little finger interphalangeal flexion
  axes was found. Hollister et al. 1995 (the thumb's interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal axes, Clin Orthop Relat
  Res) measure the thumb's interphalangeal axis parallel to its flexion crease and not square to the phalanx, which
  gives ulnar deviation and pronation with flexion, but for the thumb only; the finger convergence on the scaphoid
  tubercle (Kapandji, vol. 1) is described, not measured. An MRI hand model (Stillfried et al. 2014, DLR,
  https://elib.dlr.de/85039/) fits per-finger joint axes and is the next source to read for the angle.
- **Searched again 2026-11-28:** Stillfried et al. 2014 (https://elib.dlr.de/85039/1/StilHilSetSma14_MRI.pdf, read in
  full) fit hinge axes to the ring and little finger interphalangeal joints from MRI of one hand, but print no axis
  angles against the phalanges (only fit errors, 0.9 mm and 2.6 degrees at PIP4, and ranges); a search for a measured
  obliquity of the finger flexion axes found only the finite helical axis spread of the PIP (4.9 degrees). No angle to
  build from.
- **Repro:** `addPerson` on the Fauld cast's Character Creator old man (`civ_old_man.glb`), then
  `jointAngles(person.body, person.body.rest)`: `l_metacarpophalangeal_4` and `r_` read flexion 2.6, abduction 9.7,
  rotation -12.8 degrees, past the -10 supination stop. `packages/humans/test/pose-frames.browser.mjs --model=<file>`
  prints it for the seated pose with limits off.
- **Cause:** `fitAnatomy` rolls each segment by the bend axis of a hinge below it that is bent in the rest pose
  (`packages/rigging/src/anatomy.ts`, "A hinge below that is bent"). The ring finger's interphalangeal axes are oblique,
  so curled fingers converge toward the scaphoid (Kapandji, vol. 1); the fit reads that obliquity as a roll of the
  proximal phalanx.
- **Fix needed:** the human table gives the interphalangeal axes of the ring and little fingers their measured
  obliquity, so the rest bend reads as flexion about an oblique axis and the phalanx keeps no roll. It needs a measured
  source for the angle first.

### Open 2026-11-28: Character Creator thumbs are held up to 22 degrees off the walk clip (KB-RIG-THUMB1, rigging)
- **Learned 2026-11-28:** the pose sheet's held and played rows read many fingers at exactly the stop (MCP supination
  -10.0, CMC1 pronation 40.0) because those rows pass through `clampPose`, which pins a value past the stop at the
  stop; the raw clip (`anatomy: {limits: false}`) reads past it (idle: MCP4 supination -10.5 to -11.6, talk -12.5; CMC1
  pronation up to 53.7). So the checker is reading true; the cause stays the zero this row names.

- **Searched 2026-11-28:** Cooney et al. 1981 (the kinesiology of the thumb trapeziometacarpal joint, J Bone Joint
  Surg Am 63:1371) place the trapezium's axes at median 48 degrees of flexion, 38 of abduction and 80 of pronation from
  the third metacarpal's and measure 53 degrees of flexion and extension, 42 of abduction and adduction and 17 of
  rotation; Hollister et al. 1992 (the axes of rotation of the thumb carpometacarpal joint, J Orthop Res 10:454) find
  two fixed axes, flexion in the trapezium and abduction in the metacarpal, neither square to the bones nor to each
  other (about 124 degrees apart in vivo, Chang and Pollard). Neither gives the joint's angles at a relaxed, opposed
  rest against a thumb beside the index, which this row needs, so the zero stays as fitted.
- **Searched again 2026-11-28:** Stillfried et al. 2014 (MRI-based skeletal hand movement model, DLR,
  https://elib.dlr.de/85039/, read in full) fit the thumb's CMC as two or three non-intersecting axes on one hand and
  give its errors (2.6 mm, up to 17.2 degrees in one posture) but no angles of the joint at a relaxed rest; the axes
  themselves are only in their OpenSim model file. Crisco et al. 2015 (the envelope of physiological motion of the
  first carpometacarpal joint, J Biomech Eng, 44 subjects by CT) and Halilaj et al. 2015 (76 patients and 44 controls,
  CT with the hand relaxed) measure motion from a braced or relaxed posture but report no angles of that posture
  against the trapezium's axes in their abstracts. No relaxed, opposed rest angle was found; the zero stays as fitted.
- **Repro:** the same old man, walk clip at 0.3 s with `anatomy: {limits: false}`: `r_carpometacarpal_1` reads
  pronation 54.4 and `l_` 47.6 against a 40 degree stop, and the rest pose already reads abduction 39.1 and rotation
  28.6. On the fitted body the thumbs are held at the stop, up to 22 degrees from the clip.
- **Cause:** the relaxed Character Creator thumb rests opposed, in front of the palm, and its rest angles are counted
  against ranges measured from a thumb lying beside the index. The CMC1 joint needs a zero for an opposed rest thumb.
- **Until then:** `anatomy: {map}` can leave the thumbs out, or `roll` can turn them by hand.

### Open 2026-11-28: the coupling solver has no wrist and finger tenodesis (KB-RIG-TENODESIS1, rigging)
- **Repro:** `couplePose(body, poseFromAngles(body, { l_radiocarpal: { flexion: -60 } }))` on any fitted human: the
  fingers stay where the pose holds them. In a relaxed real hand they curl as the wrist extends and open as it flexes.
- **Cause:** no measured ratio of finger flexion to wrist extension for a relaxed hand was found in an open source
  (two searches, 2026-11-28: the tenodesis literature found describes the effect and its surgical use, not a joint
  curve). Building it from a guessed ratio would break the table's rule that every number has a source row.
- **Searched again 2026-11-28:** Latz et al. 2019 (31 subjects, biaxial electrogoniometers) measure the active MCP range
  of each finger at five wrist positions (index flexion and extension 84.7 at neutral down to 25.9 at 80 degrees of
  wrist extension), which is the active range, not where a relaxed finger rests; Akasaka et al. 2020 measure a
  surgical tenodesis in cadavers. No relaxed-hand curve of finger flexion against wrist extension was found.
- **Next:** a measured source (a motion capture study of the relaxed hand through wrist range, or a cadaver study of
  passive finger excursion), then a `tenodesis` coupling in `human.couplings` and a rule in
  `packages/rigging/src/coupling.ts` with the same fill semantics as `finger-curl`.

### Open 2026-11-28: the UAL mannequins have no naming `fitHuman` knows, so they get no body (KB-HUM-UALNAMES1, rigging)

- **Repro:** `addPerson` on Quaternius's UAL1 mannequin (`UAL1_Standard_RM.glb`, Unreal names `upperarm_l`,

### Fixed 2026-11-28: on the WebGL2 layer a page linked its synchronous pipelines one at a time (KB-COMPAT-SYNCLINK1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `demos/ten-thousand-trees/?backend=webgl2` on Chrome, ANGLE over Direct3D 11 (RTX A6000, loaded
  workstation): 31 and 33 s to `data-ready`, against about 38 s for the whole `controls.mjs` run on WebGPU. A Chrome
  trace of the page (`devtools.timeline`, `gpu`, `gpu.angle`) shows the GPU process's worker threads running one
  `D3DCompile` at a time for 15 s (11 to 26 s), the GPU main thread in `Program::MainLinkLoadEvent::wait` for the same
  15 s and the page in `getProgramParameter(LINK_STATUS)` for 14 s of a 19 s animation frame. Page JavaScript was under
  2 s; the terrain and tree generation took 6 s on four workers before it, with the GPU idle.
- **Cause:** `createRenderPipeline` (synchronous) read the program's `LINK_STATUS` and binding table in the call, and the
  compute tiers did the same for a synchronous `createComputePipeline`. That read waits until the program has linked,
  so a frame that made 50 pipelines handed the driver one link, waited for it, and only then handed it the next:
  `KHR_parallel_shader_compile` never had two links to run side by side. WebGPU reports a pipeline's errors
  asynchronously, so nothing required the read there.
- **Fix:** with `KHR_parallel_shader_compile` a synchronous render pipeline leaves its link to the driver's threads
  (`CompatDevice.deferLink`) and is checked at its first draw, by the pop of the validation scope open when it was made
  (the pop waits for the link by polling `COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR`, without blocking, and gets its error), or by itself a
  few milliseconds after the driver reports it done (an uncaptured error then). A synchronous compute pipeline's
  programs are checked at its first dispatch. Without the extension, and for a program already checked, nothing
  changes. The same draws and the same GL calls are made; only when the link status is read moves.
- **Numbers (before and after builds taking turns, two rounds, loaded workstation, a local profiling script):**
  ready 30.9 and 33.3 s before, 21.2 and 22.0 s after; time in `LINK_STATUS` 14.1 and 14.3 s before, 3.2 and 2.6 s
  after; longest task 19.0 and 19.2 s before, 9.7 and 9.2 s after. The trace after shows six compiles side by side in
  the first second of the frame.
- **Same output:** the demo with its clock stopped (`performance.now`, `Date.now` and animation frame times frozen,
  reduced motion) draws the same frame byte for byte with the old and new builds on the WebGL2 layer and on WebGPU.
- **Still open:** the rest of the first frame is the water surface program, the largest (66,747 GLSL characters): its
  link (about 3.8 s on one worker) and, as it writes three colour outputs, its compile again at its first draw on the GPU
  main thread (3.0 s, KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1), one after the other. The pipelines are made at the first frame, after the
  6 s of generation in which the GPU is idle; making them before (async creation at attach) would hide both.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/sync-link.test.js` (a stand-in WebGL2 whose links finish on command:
  no `LINK_STATUS` read while the driver links, four reads once it is done, a refused program reported to the scope it
  was made in or as an uncaptured error, no read when a compute pipeline is made, and the old check without the
  extension).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: 17 README examples failed their type check, two of them on real API defects (KB1867b; shader, materials, sky, READMEs)

- **Repro:** `npm run build:packages`, then `node scripts/check-readme-types.mjs`: 17 new errors in the cameras,
  exporters, gltf, headless, loaders, machinery and sky READMEs (0 on the known list).
- **Cause, API:** (1) the loaders give extra per-vertex scalars as bare arrays (`LoadedGeometry.attributes`, PCD
  `intensity`, VTK scalars, COLLADA channels), while `MeshGeometry.attributes` took only `{data, type}` (93e29395ee): the
  COLLADA example's `createMesh(engine, binding.geometry, ...)` failed its type check, and a node material reading such a
  channel with `attribute(name, 'f32')` threw "is undefined". (2) `galacticOfDirection` took only a `[x, y, z]` tuple,
  so `galacticDirection`'s own `number[]` or `Float32Array` output could not go back in.
- **Cause, examples:** 15 examples left a nullable canvas, an untyped parameter, a literal 3MF function graph or an
  optional `indices` unhandled, or were fenced `js` with TypeScript in them.
- **Fix:** a bare array in `attributes` is one `f32` per vertex (`packages/shader/src/attribute.ts`, the materials type;
  shader whole-package ceiling 20,880 B to 20,910 B for 27 B); `galacticOfDirection` takes any three numbers; the
  examples type their values (`Shot`, `ThreeMFImplicitFunction`) and handle what they read. The README type check
  reports 0 errors over 2,319 examples.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a plate held well inside its friction slipped on a deck pitching far from it (KB-PHYS-CONECUT1, physics kernel, contact solver)

- **Repro:** a plate (0.24 m square, one box collider) on a kinematic deck 140 m long that pitches 4 degrees at 9 s about
  its own middle, the plate 60 m from it, with friction 0.138, 1.3 times what the pitch asks of it. In 36 s it slid
  2.24 mm across the deck; 30 m out 0.24 mm, 10 m out 0.03 mm. On the storm deck of `packages/physics/tests/deck-props.test.js`
  the held plate moved 1.84 mm (its bar is 2 mm), and 3.7 to 3.9 mm with the friction at 1.29, 1.3001 or 1.31 times the
  demand: the test passed at 1.3 by chance, and any change to the contact solver (KB-PHYS-RESTDEPTH1's fix) could fail it.
- **Cause:** a pair's friction took one Gauss-Seidel sweep over its points, the first point turning each substep. The
  four corners' shares came out uneven (0.46 to 3.75 of 8.9 x 1e-4 N s at the first steps), so the busiest corner reached
  its cone, mu times its own normal impulse, while the plate as a whole held 30 percent inside its cone. The relaxing pass
  then cut that corner's anchor alone. Cut one corner at a time, the four anchors stopped agreeing with any rigid move of
  the plate (x drifts of -32, -57, -246 and -4 micrometres at 3.3 s), so the corners pushed against each other at their
  cones (one +5.1, one -4.3 x 1e-4) and the plate slipped where the deck turned fastest and asked least. Farther out the
  load swings more with the pitch (alpha r), so the uneven share met the cone sooner.
- **Fix:** in the relaxing pass, which decides the cuts, the friction rows sweep a pair's points until no impulse moves
  by more than rounding, as the normal rows do (`friction_rows` in `kernel/src/solver.rs`), and a point's anchor is cut by
  its cone only from the last sweep's answer. The shares then follow the anchors, a corner saturates only when the patch
  does, and the held plate on the storm deck moves 0.88 to 0.97 mm at every factor from 1.29 to 1.4 (it was 1.5 to
  3.9 mm). The pushing pass keeps its one sweep: swept to the end as well, its anchors' pull did work that no relaxing pass
  took back, and a web of joints and contacts gained 2e-3 of the work its kinematic bodies did
  (`kernel/tests/stability.rs` `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` allows 1e-6).
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`
  `a_plate_held_near_its_friction_rides_a_deck_pitching_far_from_it` (the plate 60 m out at 1.3 times the demand stays
  within 0.1 mm for 36 s; it slid 2.27 mm). The chair of five colliders still crept on the storm deck, 2.8 cm (it was
  2.0): that was several pairs on one body, KB-PHYS-MULTIPAIRCREEP1, fixed 2026-11-28.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a contact's resting depth jumped between two branches, so a small change of g flipped it (KB-PHYS-RESTDEPTH1, physics kernel, contact solver)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/next-parameters.test.js`, "the solver settings do what they say", the case "a tenth
  the size, the default damping ratio": a 5 cm ball on a box with `contactHertz` 60 and `allowedPenetration` 0.003, 900
  steps. At 9.81 m/s^2 it rested at the allowed depth plus g / omega^2 (6.9e-5 m past it), the soft spring's equilibrium;
  at 9.80665 and 9.82 it rested at the allowed depth exactly (2e-9 m short of it).
- **Cause:** a point inside the slop is closed to the slop's depth by a rigid speculative row (Catto's soft step), one
  past it by the soft spring. The rigid row closes the point to the slop to within the gap's float32 rounding. Closed a
  rounding short, the point stayed in the rigid row, which then held the load at zero speed with no give; closed a
  rounding past, it was the spring's and sank by g / omega^2. Which side it landed on followed the fifth digit of g.
- **Fix:** a point within the gap's rounding of the slop (two units of the last place of the largest coordinate in the
  gap's sums: the bodies' centres and the two points) counts as closed and is the soft row's (`normal_rows` in
  `kernel/src/solver.rs`), so it sinks on to where its spring holds the load whatever g is. A point farther inside the
  slop still closes rigidly, so a cube set down on a slope does not tilt downhill. An earlier try that made every loaded
  point within its give of the slop the soft row's, with the load the point carried last substep in a new column, held
  the depth too but moved the storm deck's plates and chairs past their bars; that was KB-PHYS-CONECUT1 above, fixed first.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`
  `a_resting_depth_is_continuous_in_the_load_inside_and_past_the_slop` (g from 2 to 20 m/s^2, the ball dropped from 1 cm,
  set down inside the slop and past it: at rest within 1e-7 m of the slop plus g / omega^2), and the case above in
  `next-parameters.test.js`, now run at 9.81, 9.80665 and 9.82 (it fails at 9.80665 without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: tapered deck inflow took the height of its dry neighbor (KB-SEA-DECKEDGEHEIGHT1)

At a green-water inlet inside the deck raster, the normal points into the receiving cell. A step
outwards selected the NaN of the excluded cell and rejected the published deck inflow. The inlet
record now takes its bed half a cell inside the normal in grid units.

The hull-wide upper cut can lie above a lower deck section. Its zero breadth used to remove that
station even when lower cuts had a wetted profile. The station now uses the keel depth at the top
cut and looks for breadth across the lower cuts. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/hull-slamming-workers.test.js`
checks the retained stations of a sheer hull and exact agreement of the native and TypeScript tables.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the roll-decay test used a free hull for a hinged box (KB-SEA-HEELDECAY1, physics seakeeping)

### Open 2026-11-28: a tissue's sliding attachment misses the analytic normal response by 1.6 times its rounding bound (KB-SOFT-SLIDEATTACH1, physics soft, SOFT-05)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="sliding attachment" packages/physics/tests/coupling/tissue.test.js`: the
  particle ends at 0.5100431 against the closed form 0.5100446, 1.5e-6 off, where the bound is 16 float32 spacings of the
  0.5 m length (9.5e-7). Red on main at bfb7d64cd8.
- **Cause (traced 2026-11-28, lane P):** a missing term in the closed form's world, not rounding: the soft world's face air
  drag acts on the tissue. `SoftBodies` steps `airDrag` for any body with triangles (`packages/physics/src/soft.ts`, the
  `body.airDrag && body.airLoads === 0 && body.triangleList.length > 0` line), and `setSurface()` gives a body of cells its
  boundary faces, which its doc names as what a surface collider is made of; `setAirDrag` documents the air for "a body of
  triangles (a cloth, a trimesh)". So every box, solid and volumetric body takes a flat plate's drag on each surface face.
  Measured with the test's scene: the particle's step falls short by 1.49e-4, 7.8e-5 and 3.1e-5 of its displacement at
  bone offsets of 1/32, 1/64 and 1/128 m (the shortfall follows the speed, as quadratic drag does), by the same 1.49e-4 with
  the elastic modulus set to 0.001 Pa, and by under 7e-6 (float32 rounding) with `setAirDrag(false)`, for 2 to 64 passes.
- **Fix:** skip the face air for a body with cells (`body.cellRange.count === 0` beside the triangle check, as adaptive
  tearing and the cloth-only flags already test), so the code keeps its documented contract and the tissue test passes
  unchanged. `soft.ts` belongs to SOFT-01, SOFT-04 and SOFT-06 (claimed in docs/physics-work-queue.md and edited within
  the hour), so it is left to that owner; a closed shell's faces (`SoftBodyDesc.volume` without cells) each take a whole
  plate's drag too, front and back, which that owner should weigh at the same time.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: next-hull's exact-predicate test could not load the hull source (KB-PHYS-HULLTESTLOAD1, physics tests)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="a hair above a face" packages/physics/tests/next-hull.test.js`: "Cannot
  find module src/rigid-errors.js imported from src/hull.ts".
- **Cause:** the test imports `src/hull.ts` itself to reach `beyond`. Since DYN-01 (e4b589866a) hull.ts imports

### Fixed 2026-11-28: touching a collider after its neighbour's body was removed read and wrote past the body rows (KB-PHYS-RETIREDPAIR1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** three boxes in a pile, stepped until they touch. Remove the bottom body, then, before the next step, do any
  of these to the middle box: `touch_collider` (what a change of collision groups calls), `wake_touching_pairs`,
  `set_collider_state` (sensor and back) or `set_body_enabled` (off and on). The native build stops with
  STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION. Found while the replay scene ran on with a world that had stopped: 220 iterations of removals
  and edits with no step between them, then a change of groups on a collider whose neighbour was gone.
- **Cause:** `retire_collider` sets the removed collider's `COLLIDER_BODY` to NONE at once and leaves its pairs for the
  next step's broad phase to drop. Until that step the other collider's pair list still holds the pair, and
  `pair_bodies` gives NONE for the removed side. `wake_pair` woke row NONE, `end_touches_as` zeroed its `SLEEP_TIME` and
  `set_body_enabled` read `is_awake(NONE)`: row 4,294,967,295 of the body columns. Natively that is 16 GiB past the column;
  in Wasm the address wraps, so it read and wrote the word before the column. Nothing numeric is involved: no NaN or
  large speed is needed.
- **Fix:** a pair with a retired collider names no body on that side, and the walks pass it by (`pair_retired` and
  `wake_pair` in `kernel/src/events.rs`): the live body still wakes, the pair keeps its contacts for the step that drops
  it, and it joins no list. Regression: `packages/physics/kernel/tests/retired_pair.rs` (both tests end in an access
  violation without the fix; with it the pile falls onto the floor, the middle box at y 0.5 and the top one at 1.5 within
  0.02 m).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the tundra's sedge and lichen drew as half-metre bright green grass (KB-TUNDRA-GRASS1; procedural, biomes)

- **Repro:** a `BiomeView` of the tundra world from 1.1 m: wide green blades about half a metre tall everywhere.
- **Cause:** the tundra preset's `sedge` and `lichen` details both named `procedural:grass`, the meadow grass mesh and
  its green.
- **Fix:** `generateSedgeMesh` (seven 4 mm leaves arching to 10 to 19 cm; Carex bigelowii stands 10 to 50 cm with blades
  1.5 to 4 mm, Native Plant Trust, Go Botany) and `generateLichenMesh` (a cushion under 5 cm) in
  `@margoengine/procedural`; `procedural:sedge` is drawn in the cured-grass colour of the ground table (ECOSTRESS wild
  oat litter) and bends with the wind, `procedural:lichen` in a chosen pale grey-olive (lichens lack green vegetation's
  peak at 0.55 um: Petzold and Goward 1988, Remote Sensing of Environment 24(3)). A sedge draws 21 triangles and a
  lichen 14 where each drew the grass's 6.
- **Left:** the tufts read thin from above; the ground between them carries the cover.
- **Regression:** `packages/procedural/test/foliage.test.js` "the sedge is a short tuft of narrow leaves and the lichen

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a background that is not a colour string drew a near-black sky with no error (KB-BIOMES-BLACKSKY1; core)

- **Repro:** a page that sets `engine.scene.background = [0.42, 0.55, 0.75]`, then `BiomeView.attach` on the tundra preset
  world with `radius: 600`, camera 2 m over the ground looking at the horizon: the sky drew near black (5,6,9). The same
  page with `'#6b8cbf'` draws that blue, so the biomes had no part in it.
- **Cause:** a background is a `#rgb` or `#rrggbb` string. Core read any other value as no colour
  (`packages/core/src/renderer.ts` passed only strings on, and `packages/shared/clear-color.js` took every non-string
  as unset), so it cleared to its own near-black colour. The type refuses an array; plain JavaScript got no message.
- **Fix:** only undefined, null and false are unset. Every other value reaches the colour check and throws
  `RangeError: Invalid color; use #rrggbb` at the next render, as a malformed string already did; the WebGL2 preview
  renderer does the same. Core + stage stays at 25,149 B gzip (raw 61,864 to 61,848).
- **Test:** `tests/clear-capture.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the biomes' snow stood about four times rougher than measured snow (KB-SNOW-RELIEF1; biomes)

- **Repro:** the layer pixels of `materialPixels('snow', MATERIALS.snow)`: at `bump` 0.35 and the 4 m repeat the drawn
  height has a root mean square of 34.7 mm at the 128-texel mip (32.7 mm after the near filter).
- **Cause:** the value was chosen by eye. A laser profiler on a Svalbard glacier read 0.5 to 9.2 mm on snow surfaces,
  wavelengths 4 to 50 cm (Lacroix et al. 2008, Journal of Glaciology 54(187), 753-762,
  https://doi.org/10.3189/002214308786570863); the noise of the snow layer holds wavelengths in that range.
- **Fix:** `MATERIALS.snow.bump` 0.09: 8.9 mm at the 128-texel mip, 8.4 mm after the near filter, the rough end of the
  measured range (a wind-worked surface). The far ring's snow uses the same value, at its own repeat.
- **Regression:** `packages/biomes/tests/view.test.js` "snow relief stands within the measured root mean square height of
  snow surfaces".

### Fixed 2026-11-28: terrain ground with `bump` drew as black and white speckle near the camera (KB-TUNDRA-GROUNDNOISE1; terrain)

- **Repro:** a `BiomeView` of the tundra world, camera 1.1 m over the ground: the snow and tundra ground drew as black and
  white speckle in diamond-shaped cells; with `bump: 0` on the materials it drew smooth.
- **Cause:** `TerrainLayer.bump` took its height from the same sampler read as the colour. Near the camera that is the
  finest mip, so every texel of grain was a height step of up to half a repeat per unit of luma (root mean square slopes
  1.2 on the tundra material and 5.3 on rock at 256 texels over 4 m, `materialPixels`), a bilinear height has one slope
  a texel (facets), and the screen derivative of the hardware's rounded filter weights drew dotted lines along texel
  edges.
- **Fix:** `packages/terrain/src/shader.ts`: where a pixel covers less than 1/128 of a repeat, the height is the layer's
  128-texel mip through a cubic B-spline over 16 exact texel loads a projection, handing over to the colour sample's mip
  by 1/64 (past that the picture is as before); tinted layers and the floating origin shift it as they do the colour.
  Cubic B-spline basis: Sigg and Hadwiger 2005, GPU Gems 2 chapter 20.
- **Measured:** on a grey noise texture with texel grain from 2 m, pixel contrast 28.9 before, 8.5 after (RTX A6000, the
  same on both test paths); the bumped near-view spread stays 4.28 times the flat one (4.29 before).
- **Left then:** the biomes' snow relief stood above the measured height of snow (KB-SNOW-RELIEF1).
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/bump.browser.mjs` (`smoothBump`, `grainBump`, `grainBumpWeighted` bounds) and
  `packages/terrain/test/surface.test.js` "the bump height is read from exact texel loads, tinted and under a floating
  origin as the colour (KB-TUNDRA-GROUNDNOISE1)".

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a Water added to SceneTargets drew nothing, and its SSR capture drew with TAA's jittered camera (KB-WATER-CAPTURECAM1; water)

- **Repro (before):** `SceneTargets.add(water, {ground: false})` (`@margoengine/post/mrt`): the targets hold no water
  pixel once frames move time on (`delta` above 0), with or without TAA (0 px in
  `packages/post/test/scene-targets-taa-browser.mjs`'s water case).
- **Cause:** the capture drew only the view its colour pass had drawn this frame, and bound that pass's uniform.
  `SceneTargets` runs at order -4.5, before the water's colour pass (order 4), so it found no view and drew nothing
  (`packages/post/test/scene-targets-water-browser.mjs` draws with `delta: 0`, which skips the clear, so it passed);
  a capture after the pass (SSR) drew from the colour pass's camera, TAA's jittered one.
- **Fix:** the capture writes frame values of its own from the context's unjittered camera
  (`packages/shared/temporal-camera.js`) at this frame's time, and before this frame's draw it uses the view drawn last
  (`packages/water/src/index.ts`).
- **Regression test:** `node packages/post/test/scene-targets-taa-browser.mjs` (and `--compat`, in post `test:gpu`):
  the water covers 5,855 px of the targets, and TAA's jitter moves none of them.
- **Weak spot left:** on the very first frame no surface has been drawn, so that frame's targets hold no water.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: shrubs drew as flat bright green blobs on the slopes (KB-SHRUB-BLOBS1; procedural, biomes)

- **What:** in timber-valley stills every shrub on the slopes was a smooth mint to lime dome with a hard outline.
- **Cause:** `generateShrubMesh` was three closed smooth hemispheres, and biomes painted them the broadleaf green,
  linear (0.14, 0.3, 0.05), about three times a leaf's reflectance.
- **Fix:** the shrub is separate leaves in the same box (spherical leaf angles, normals out of the shrub; 1,080, 432 and
  144 triangles by detail level, each level keeping the full level's cover: Cook, Halstead, Planck and Ryu, "Stochastic
  simplification of aggregate detail", SIGGRAPH 2007, https://graphics.pixar.com/library/StochasticSimplification/),
  and biomes paints it (0.065, 0.11, 0.035) (Jacquemoud and Baret, "PROSPECT: a model of leaf optical properties
  spectra", Remote Sensing of Environment 34, 1990, https://doi.org/10.1016/0034-4257(90)90100-Z; Hosgood et al.,
  "Leaf Optical Properties EXperiment 93", JRC EUR 16095 EN, 1995).
- **Regression:** `packages/procedural/test/shrub-leaves.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the tundra shrub drew as smooth domes, and no shrub had wood (KB-SHRUB-TUNDRA1; procedural, biomes)

- **What:** in a close still of the tundra world every dwarf birch was a smooth brown or ochre mound; the shrub fixed in

- **Cause:** `generateTundraShrubMesh` was six closed hemispheres; `generateShrubMesh` had 20 cm diamond leaves and no

- **Fix:** both are separate rounded leaves (13 cm on the shrub, 7 cm on the tundra shrub, larger than the 6 to 12 cm
  of hazel and the 0.6 to 2 cm of dwarf birch at the top end and above, to hold cover within the triangle count) on
  woody stems from the new `generateShrubStemsMesh` and `generateTundraShrubStemsMesh`; biomes draws stems and leaves
  as two parts, with copper-red twigs and green leaves on the dwarf birch.
- **Regression:** `packages/procedural/test/shrub-leaves.test.js`, `packages/biomes/tests/objects.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the USD importers dropped texture factors, and the default one emission and occlusion (KB-USDZ-FACTORS1, usdz)

- **What:** a textured file written by `exportUSDZ` read back through `@margoengine/usdz` with a white base colour
  factor, roughness 1 and metalness 1, whatever the file's `inputs:scale` said; the default importer also left out
  `emissiveColor`, its texture and `occlusion`, `previewSurface()` left out `occlusion`, and both left out a normal
  map's scale.
- **Repro:** `exportUSDZ` of a material with `color: [0.5, 0.25, 1]`, `roughness: 0.4`, `metalness: 0.6`, `emissive:
  [0.5, 0, 0]` and base colour, metal-rough and emissive textures, then `parseUSDZ(file).document.materials[0]`.
- **Cause:** `material()` in `packages/usdz/src/index.ts` and `surface()` in `preview-surface.ts` set the factors to 1
  for a textured input and never read the `UsdUVTexture`'s `inputs:scale` or `inputs:bias`; the default `material()`
  never read `inputs:emissiveColor` or `inputs:occlusion`.
- **Fix:** `packages/usdz/src/preview-factors.ts`, for both importers. A scale glTF's factors hold stays a factor
  (colour, roughness, metalness, opacity, emission with `KHR_materials_emissive_strength` past 1, normal scale,
  occlusion strength) and the file's image is kept; anything else is written into the pixels when the model is created.
- **Regression:** `packages/usdz/tests/texture-factors.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the dune coast's fog hazed the sea by the seabed's distance and painted the far sea out (KB-SCENES-SEAFOGDEPTH1, scenes)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --views=surf --out=<folder>` (camera 3.1 m
  up, far plane 30 km): rows 511 to 538 of `surf.png` are one flat (188, 188, 186) in every column, a one-pixel
  (191, 191, 189) line on row 511, and the waves start at row 539, about 130 m out. `visibility=50000` gives the same
  rows. With only the fog's bare-pixel fill off (KB-SKY-BAREBELOW1) the same rows show the sea's waves, and rows 512 to
  517 the unhazed (199, 199, 197) strip of KB-WATER-HORIZONBAND1's "left" note.
- **Cause:** `PresetScene` hands the sky's fog `post.depthTexture`, the scene depth before the water, and the dune coast
  scene kept it. The water draws its surface into its own depth (`water.depthTexture`, documented for this use), so the
  fog never saw the sea: it hazed each sea pixel by the distance to the seabed behind it, and where the view's rays pass
  over the seabed mesh's far edge (x 1300, 8 m deep; row 539 is the last ray that meets it, at 468 m) the pixel read as
  nothing drawn, which the fog fills with the fog at infinity since KB-SKY-BAREBELOW1 and skipped before it (the
  unhazed 199 strip).
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/scenes/dune-coast` points the sky fog's depth at `water.depthTexture` (the post depth until the
  water has drawn). After: the far sea's waves reach the horizon, hazed by their own distance; rows 513 to 517 read 190
  to 194, neutral, against the deck's 188 to 189. No other scene pairs a Water with the preset fog (fauld-blast has no
  fog).
- **Regression:** `packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs`, surf view: the luma spread of the rows between the horizon
  and the seabed's edge (0.477 to 0.497 of the height) must pass 2; 0.73 before (the flat fill), 8.56 after on WebGPU
  and 7.01 on the WebGL2 layer.
- **Left:** those few far rows sit 2 to 6 codes over the deck at ranges where the haze is near full; not traced, and in
  the water's grazing shading if anywhere (SEA-02, see KB-WATER-FARROWS1).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a hard-edged peach band lay under the dune coast's cloud deck at the sea horizon (KB-WATER-HORIZONBAND1, water)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --views=surf --out=<folder>`, `surf.png`
  rows 512 to 517 at x 910: about (219, 210, 196), warm and brighter, under the overcast deck (189, 190, 187, rows 500 to
  510), with a one-pixel top edge and the same peach in the far glints.
- **Cause (measured):** the sky's 64 x 32 reflection map in the surf view holds the grey deck in row 15, the last row
  above the horizon, (0.127, 0.128, 0.124), and in row 16, the first below it, (0.209, 0.160, 0.105): below the
  horizon the sky has no cloud (the ground hides it) and fades its clear, warm horizon toward the ground. The Water
  holds every reflected ray at or above the horizon (`skyTap` at y 0, the callback route's `reflectionRay` at 0.02),
  but the bilinear filter at v 0.5 (or 0.4936) still took half (or 0.29) of row 16. The far sea, which reflects the
  horizon at grazing incidence, drew that share of the clear horizon as a band.
- **Fix:** `aboveHorizon()` in `packages/water/src/index.ts` holds a horizon tap's v at the centre of the last row above
  the horizon (0.5 - 0.5 / the map's rows), on both the HDR (`skyTap`) and the callback route, so a horizon tap reads

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the sky's environment map held a cloudless horizon below the horizon under an overcast deck (KB-SKY-ENVBELOW1, sky)

- **Repro:** the dune coast surf view (overcast, `clouds: 1`), `Sky.reflectionTexture` read back by a compute copy (64 x
  32): row 15, just above the horizon, (0.127, 0.128, 0.124), the deck; row 16, just below, (0.209, 0.160, 0.105), warm
  and brighter; rows 18 on (0.007, 0.009, 0.006).
- **Cause:** `skyEnvironment` (`packages/sky/src/environment.ts`) takes `daySky` of the ray held at the horizon and mixes
  it toward the ground colour by `smoothstep(-0.2, 0.02, y)`, but hands `cloudSky` the unheld ray, which for y below 0
  hits the ground and returns the clear sky: just under the horizon the map is the clear horizon, not the deck.
  Anything lit or reflected from that band (an object's lower hemisphere, a reflection that filters across the horizon)
  takes a warm light an overcast day does not have.
- **Fix:** `skyEnvironment` hands `cloudSky` the ray held at the horizon and mixes toward the ground colour after the
  clouds. Overcast map (`Sky.attach(engine, {hours: 11, clouds: {coverage: 1, depth: 30}})`, 64 x 32): row 16 went from
  (0.543, 0.553, 0.567), the clear horizon, to (0.245, 0.259, 0.289), the deck under row 15's (0.346, 0.365, 0.408) and
  fading toward the ground; the clear map is unchanged. At night the rows below the horizon now fade to the ground as by
  day, where the night gradient ran under the horizon before.
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/environment-below-check.mjs` (in `test:gpu`; passed on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer,
  RTX A6000), which failed before with row 16 1.5 times the deck's luminance.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the WaterWake README example ran out its 20 s page limit (KB-WATER-WAKEREADME1, physics solver SEA-04)

- **Repro:** `npm run check:readme-run -- --packages=water` on the workstation (RTX A6000, Node 26): "water/readme-a-physics-
  wake-drawn-waterwake-m-224548: Example did not finish within 20 s while settling". The example advances a
  `WakeSolver` on a 256 x 128 grid for ten seconds (`world.advance(10 * 30)` frames at 30 Hz) before one frame.
- **Measured (lane C, the example's solver alone in Node, counting calls):** the wake steps at its default 60 Hz
  (rate level 0), so the ten seconds are 598 steps, each 3 forward and 2 inverse real 2D transforms (the earlier note's
  "10 a step" counted two steps a frame; this example has no current, tension or viscosity, so `updateWaterVelocity`
  takes no transform). 31.1 ms a step, 18.6 s, 96 percent in `RealFft2` of `@margoengine/math/fft`.
- **Cause:** `RealFft2.forward` ran the whole complex 2D transform, every one of the nx columns, and kept nx / 2 + 1 of
  them; and the Stockham loop ran every radix-2 stage (all of a 256-point transform) through its generic p-loop, with a
  modulo and a table index for each of the 4 terms of each output pair.
- **Fix (`packages/math/src/fft.ts`):** `forward` transforms the rows and only the columns it keeps, each column being
  its own transform; the radix-2 stage is written out with the same operations in the same order (a sum still starts
  at 0, so a -0 sum stays +0), so every result keeps the Rust twin's bits (kernel-common's `fft.rs` is untouched).
  Measured the same way: 9.5 ms a step, 5.7 s for the example's solver; the README example passes (55 of 55 water
  examples). The README's limit and its ten seconds did not change.
- **Regression:** `packages/math/test/fft.test.js`: a 16 x 8 forward runs 8 rows and 9 columns (24 before; fails on the
  parent), the written-out stage matches the generic loop bit for bit at lengths 2 to 1,024 with random and signed-zero
  inputs, and the existing Rust vectors still match.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the water surface program took over 5 s to link on the WebGL2 layer (KB-WATER-GL2LINK1, water)

- **Repro (before):** `demos/ten-thousand-trees/?backend=webgl2` (BiomeView with `water: { rivers: 'auto' }`) on Chrome,
  ANGLE over Direct3D 11: timing `getProgramParameter(LINK_STATUS)` per program showed the water surface program at
  5.5 to 11.5 s on a loaded machine, against 0.6 to 1.6 s for every other program; `node scripts/web-demos/controls.mjs
  ten-thousand-trees --backends=webgl2` reported the page as not started.
- **Cause:** a shader compiler inlines every call (HLSL has no real calls) and Direct3D's compiler unrolls a loop
  whose bound it can count, and ANGLE compiles the program's HLSL inside the link. The surface fragment held 24 inlined
  copies of `noise()` (five ripple layers, five capillary octaves, six whitecap, four surf, two foam layers, grain, the
  wind patch), 26 of `skyTap()` (five taps in each of `skyLobe()`'s call sites) and two `refractionBisect()` call
  sites. Offline `fxc` (ps_5_0) on ANGLE's own HLSL: 6,000 instruction slots, 114 samples, 92 sincos; stubbing `noise()`
  alone halved the slots and the compile time, while `[loop]` on every existing loop only took it to 5,958 (the old
  loops were not the cost). The 18 loops the first note blamed were not it.
- **Fix:** each repeated call sits once in a loop over an array of its arguments, every argument written out as before,
  and the loop's bound is `waterLoops(n)` = n + `frame.sea.z`, a frame uniform lane Water always leaves 0, so no compiler
  can count it (the rule of KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1). The sums around the calls keep their written order. A ripple layer and
  a capillary octave are split around their noise (`rippleLayerAt`/`rippleLayerSlope`, `shortOctaveAt`/`shortOctaveSlope`), each
  half called with the layer's literal arguments: a first version read the octaves' wavenumbers from a table, so
  `k/3.77` and `9.81/k` were divided at run time where the literal had been folded, and 84 of 307,200 bytes of a sea
  frame came out 1/255 apart on WebGPU; a ripple loop that summed its weighted layers in the loop moved one byte on the
  layer (multiply and add no longer fused the same way). `refractionCrossing` has one `refractionBisect` call site.
  After: 7 `noise()`, 5 `skyTap()`, 1 `refractionBisect()` sites; offline fxc of the first, table-driven version
  (same call sites) 3,175 slots, 42 samples, 36 sincos; the final version was not compiled offline.
- **Numbers:** the surface program's link in the demo (a local profiling script, before and after builds taking
  turns, two rounds, workstation loaded): 6.44 and 6.76 s before, 3.19 and 2.97 s after; all eight programs 12.1 to
  8.9 s. Standalone link of the module (shader disk cache off, minimum of two): 4.5 to 8.8 s before, 3.1 to 3.2 s
  for the first, table-driven version. The fragment's inlined size under the corpus gate's model (`scripts/support/wgsl-inline.mjs`) went from
  251,507 to 157,264 characters (KB-CORPUS-OPTICS1). `controls.mjs ten-thousand-trees` passes on both backends
  (WebGL2: ok in 119 and 138 s; one run while GPU tests ran beside it reported a page script over 15 s).
- **Same output:** three scenes (an HDR-sky sea, a plain sea, a refracting beach with surf) rendered with the old and
  new builds on one page are byte for byte the same on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer over ANGLE Direct3D 11 (RTX
  A6000); the old build against a copy of itself is also identical on both, so the check is deterministic.
- **Still open:** Water creates its pipeline with the synchronous `createRenderPipeline`, so the link blocks the page
  (since KB-COMPAT-SYNCLINK1 only at its first draw, and side by side with the other links of the frame);
  the surface writes three colour outputs, so ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end compiles it again at its first draw
  (KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1) and LINK_STATUS shows about half the cost. Async readiness (`createRenderPipelineAsync`, on the
  layer `KHR_parallel_shader_compile`) is not done.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/surface-copies.browser.mjs` (fragment call sites and unrolled copies of
  `noise`, `skyTap` and `refractionBisect`; fails on the old build with 24, 26 and 2 sites).
- **Sources:** Microsoft, "for statement (HLSL)", https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-for;
  ANGLE, UnrollFlatten_test.cpp, https://chromium.googlesource.com/angle/angle.git/+/HEAD/src/tests/compiler_tests/UnrollFlatten_test.cpp;
  ANGLE group, "Solving slow compilation of long loops with texture sampling", https://groups.google.com/g/angleproject/c/0zfeMdGzzyQ;
  Dawn, "HLSL: force FXC to never unroll loops" and its revert, https://dawn.googlesource.com/tint/+/11d09f2fe7c006b78f7319e876e4ced43f0c1a60;
  ANGLE, HLSLCompiler.cpp (its X3531/X4014 retries). The link times were measured here.
- **Also fixed here:** `packages/water/test/whitecaps.browser.mjs` counted `RangeError`s from `setWhitecaps`, which has
  thrown the documented MargoError `'unsupported'` since a62634a9bf, and `water.test.js` read the ripple turns from
  `rippleSlope(p,...)` calls; both now read what the code does.

### Open 2026-11-28: a Sarrus linkage's loop error grows as it moves and stays when it stops (KB-PHYS-SARRUSLOOP1, physics solver)

- **Repro:** the parked rig `sarrus-rig.ts` (links 0.8 m, four 1 kg point links of radius 0.02 m, five hinges from a
  fixed base and a position-driven crank, no gravity, 2 degree 60 Hz steps from 48 degrees). The deck's gap from
  `sarrusPose` reads 2.2e-5 m at 49 degrees, 3.4e-4 at 56, 2.1e-3 after 73 and back to 30, 3.4e-3 back at 48, and holds
  each figure unchanged for 300 steps at rest. The error is four of the five hinges pulled apart along their links by the
  same amount (2.6 mm each at the end), with every turning row within 2e-7 rad.
- **Cause (corrected 2026-11-28, fix built, not landed):** not the near singular push the first note named. `push_share`
  (`kernel/src/joints.rs`) adds what the joint before gave a shared body (`carried`) to what this joint gives it. Where a
  joint's body A goes on along the path and its body B came before, it wrote this joint's gain on A into `carried` and
  then read that as the joint before's gain on B. The Sarrus path runs J0 J1 J4 J3 J2 and J4 and J3 are that way round,
  so the deck and a knee each read 2,800 rad/s (two hinge gains that cancel, added to each other) and the push was cut to
  1e-4 to 1e-6 of itself every substep. The pivot at 4.5e-5 of its row is real and harmless: it scales with I / (m L^2).
- **Measured with the fix (five lines, reading `carried` before it is replaced), on a held-back build:** the gap at rest
  1.2e-7 to 1.6e-7 m (was 3.4e-3 and growing), the worst while driven 2 degrees a step 1.44e-5 m (was 2.4e-3). A kernel
  test of the loop is written (`sarrus_loop.rs`, worst 2.2e-5 m at 49 degrees without the fix).
- **Why it is not landed:** the wrong sum was also hiding a second defect, which the replay scene shows
  (`kernel/tests/replay.rs`: 48 to 96 random bodies, 24 random joints with anchors up to metres apart, bodies moved by
  hand, 10,000 steps). Fastest spin, and body-steps past 1,000 rad/s, over the whole run:

  | Build | Block solver, levels on | Sweeps, levels on | Block solver, levels off | Sweeps, levels off |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `main` | 273 rad/s, 0 | 4,431 rad/s, 593 | 284 rad/s, 0 | 586 rad/s, 0 |
  | fix alone | 5,965 rad/s, 1,239 | 4.4e8 rad/s at step 1948, then NaN and the world stops | 289 rad/s, 0 | 858 rad/s, 0 |
  | fix and a damped push | 2,401 rad/s, 609 | 1,703 rad/s, 725 | 777 rad/s, 0 | 261 rad/s, 0 |

  "Levels" are the islands' own substep levels (`adaptive_substeps`). That table is the fixture's seed only, and two things
  read from it were wrong. Over five seeds of the scene (the stream's seed xor n * 0x9E3779B9, n 0 to 4) `main` itself
  passes 1,000 rad/s in each of the four builds: worst 5,040 rad/s (sweeps) and 4,660 (block) with levels on, 1,280 and
  17,000 with levels off. So a spin over 1,000 rad/s is this scene's own and no sign of a defect, and "with levels off no
  build passes 1,000 rad/s" held for one seed. What the fix changes: 2 of 10 runs with levels on leave the numbers (seed 0
  with the sweeps at step 1948, seed 3 with the block solver at step 509) and 0 of 10 with levels off. That run-away is
  KB-PHYS-LEVELSPIN1 below, a defect of its own; the wrong sum had been cutting the pushes that feed it.
- **State:** the fix is not on `main`. Alone it passes `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers`; the whole kernel suite has
  not been run on it. It lands with `sarrus_loop.rs` once KB-PHYS-LEVELSPIN1 is fixed, and the Sarrus rig and its demo
  wait for it. The damped push (Levenberg 1944, Marquardt 1963, Wampler 1986, Nakamura and Hanafusa 1986) stops both
  run-aways and is not worth landing: over the same seeds it has the fastest spins of any build (35,200 and 90,000 rad/s
  with levels on, 15,300 with levels off). The access violation that followed the first run-away was a separate bug,
