  pool):** each frame's value follows the lit minus shadow L* (correlation 0.99; L* from -6 to +12 within 0.2 s),
  not the albedo left inside the strata (albedo b* difference -0.3 to 0.9, correlation 0.22) and not position on
  screen (cutting the strata further into 32-pixel tiles leaves a per-frame spread of 2.9 b*). The same frames with
  the shutter closed (`subframes` 1, so no motion blur and masks of the drawn instant) read the same (spread 3.6 b*
  against 3.4), so the blur is not it either (it was a mask defect of its own, KB-SHOT-SHUTTERMASK1). With
  `fire=none` (no fire, so no pall either: a clear sun) the drift is gone: lit minus shadow 8.4 b* and 33 L* in
  every frame, spread 0.6 b*. Under the pall the sun's beam is 1 percent of the light, so lit and shaded ground of
  one surface differ by about 0.3 L* from the sun, while the fire's light, which the trees shade too and which moves
  and flickers along the shot, changes the same ground by 5 to 12 L*. T6 compares ground the sun's mask splits; what
  it measures here is the fire's light on that ground, which the probe's `light` record (sun and sky only) and the
  sun masks do not hold. Not yet split: the fire's point lights against its flame and ember sprites over the ground.
  The fix needs the fire's light on the ground as an AOV (strata of like local light, as of like albedo), a new
  SceneTargets output: asked of the manager.
- **Cause (2026-11-28, lane B, the same 4.5 s with the shutter closed, per-frame b* spread):** not the fire's light
  but its flame volumes drawn over the ground. Baseline 3.55; the flames' glow off (`glow` 0) 3.55; the embers off 3.55;
  the fire's light on the haze and pall off (`WeatherDrive` `fireLight` 0) 4.10; the smoke columns off 3.54; the flame
  bodies off (`opacity` 0) 0.87; everything the fire draws off 0.96. A flame volume is drawn after the scene, so the
  sun's masks (SceneTargets, the surfaces only) still count the ground behind it as lit or shadowed ground, and the
  flames move and flicker along the shot. The probe's own frames hold too few shadow interiors to see it in one frame.
- **Fix:** TAA gains `reactiveMask` (read only: the coverage mask its resolve read, which flames, smoke, weather and
  water already draw), the timber-valley shot page gives it as the `over` AOV (every timber-valley shot lists it), and
  T6 (`bounce`, `shadowTint`, `packages/headless/src/look.ts`) leaves out ground any of it covers, records
  `detail.over` (percent left out) and reports `missing` below `GROUND_MIN_PIXELS` (30) lit or shadowed pixels left.
  The blowup pools 15 frames 2 apart round each probe (`probePool`, the ruled pooling), since one frame now holds 22
  to 24 shadowed interior pixels. Bound unchanged, fire kept; no core or stage change. Only T6 reads `over`: the
  flames' own look is still held by every other check.
- **After:** the closed-shutter 4.5 s run with `over`: per-frame spread 0.98 b* (3.55 without), mid shadowTint 1.10 b*
  pooled (bound 0.0416, pass), bounce 93.2 percent (pass).
  The blowup itself (`--once --seconds 1.6`, 8 subframes, 180 degree shutter, its 15-frame pool): early shadowTint
  0.70 b* and mid 0.37 b* (bounds 0.0366 and 0.0448, pass), bounce 94.4 and 97.3 percent (pass), b4c0bdc9a1.
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js` ("T6 leaves out ground an effect is drawn over"),
  `packages/taa/test/reactive-mask.test.js` ("taa.reactiveMask is the mask the last resolve read"),
  `packages/taa/test/reactive-browser.mjs` (WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: T6 compared different surfaces in the sun and in the shade (KB-LOOK-TV-TINTMATCH1, headless look check)

- **Repro (before):** the timber-valley blowup, `--once --seconds 1.1`: mid bounce 103.6 percent and shadowTint 0.036
  b* (bound 0.0448), with and without TAA. Shadowed ground brighter than lit ground cannot happen for one surface under
  one light: the lit and shadow masks held different surfaces, so the check measured their albedo difference.
- **Cause:** `bounce` and `shadowTint` (`packages/headless/src/look.ts`) averaged all lit and all shadowed ground
  interiors, whatever the surface.
- **Fix:** they take an optional `albedo` (`albedoOf(frame, masks)` builds it from grey masks `albedo-r`, `albedo-g`,
  `albedo-b`; `checkProbe` passes it on). The ground is cut into strata of like albedo (`GROUND_ALBEDO_LEVELS`, 16 per
  sRGB channel), each stratum's lit and shadowed means are compared alone and the strata pooled with the
  Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel weight n_lit n_shadow / (n_lit + n_shadow) (Cochran 1954, doi:10.2307/3001616; Mantel and
  Haenszel 1959, doi:10.1093/jnci/22.4.719); a surface seen on one side only does not count, and with no stratum on both
  sides the check reports `missing`. The timber-valley shot page draws the albedo with a second `SceneTargets` (one takes
  at most 7 outputs) and every timber-valley shot lists the three masks. Bounds unchanged. Regression:
  `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js` ("compare like surfaces"): sand mostly lit, ash mostly shaded under one
  light; the old masks read the tint more than 5 b* too warm and the bounce under half of either surface's, the strata
  give a value between the two surfaces' own. After the fix the blowup still misses at mid: KB-LOOK-TV-TINTRES1.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the aftermath shot no longer loaded: burning the valley out took longer than the shot tool waits (KB-SCENES-BURNTSLOW1, vfx)

- **Repro (before):** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-aftermath.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out <folder>`
  on main 1604e1a464 (RTX A6000, WebGPU): "page.waitForFunction: Timeout 180000ms exceeded" in `untilQueued`
  (`tools/shot/render.mjs`, `PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` 180 s), every run, with and without KB-SCENES-TVTAA1; the shot page with
  the shot's query (`fire=burnt&weather=smoke&hour=10&date=1910-08-22`) took 193 s to be ready.
- **Cause:** since 7d96ac7993 (KB-VFX-DARKTRAILS1) `fire: 'burnt'` settles the fire until nothing burns (`burnOut`,
  `FireFront.settle`), 2.8 days of fire time in 0.5 s steps. KB-VFX-BURNOUTWORK1 kept each spent cell's spread rates,
  but `settle` still visited every cell in `burning` every step, and 99.9 percent of those visits were cells past their
  flames adding their kept travel toward neighbours a slow backing or flanking fire takes hours or days to reach:
  on the 8 m grid 754,532,995 such visits in 471,341 steps.
- **Fix:** inside `settle` a cell past its flames leaves the step loop as a record (`packages/vfx/src/fire-front.ts`,
  `lazify`, `reach`, `flush`). For each way still open it works out the step its float32 travel reaches 1, the sum the
  steps would make: inside one float32 binade fround(a + s) - a is the same for every a (but for a rounding tie, which
  is stepped one at a time), so a run of steps is one multiply, bit for bit the step-by-step sum. That step's visit
  happens in light order with the flaming cells, so the same cell lights a neighbour first and the embers draw the same
  random numbers; a neighbour lit by another cell closes the way in the step the visit would have found it. Steps where
  only such records wait are counted, not run. Every record goes back into `burning` with its travel brought up to date
  before `settle` yields, stops or is aborted, and when the kept rates no longer hold, so `advanceTime` and every getter
  see the state the steps would have left. The 180 s page wait is unchanged.
- **After (work counted, timber-valley's fire, smoke weather, seed 1910, `.lane/burn/lazycount.mjs` in lane B's
  worktree):** 8 m grid: the same burn as stepping it (sha256 of the burn texture, fire time, embers, spots and crowning
  cells equal: 237,470.5 s, 255,310 cells burnt, 105,120 embers, 8,171 spot fires), carrying visits 754,532,995 to
  435,164 (1,734 times fewer), steps run 471,341 to 398,724, full spread evaluations 6,246,622 either way. 4 m grid
  (the film's): 245,753.5 s, 1,025,344 cells burnt, 1,454,522 carrying visits, 25,095,798 full evaluations;
  stepped instead, the same burn (equal hash) with 1,769,337,899 carrying visits in 487,907 steps (1,216 times
  more). The shot page is ready in 34.4 s (was 193 s), and the aftermath shot renders.
- **Regression test:** `packages/vfx/test/fire-front-lazy.test.js`: a fire with crowns, slope, a building, spotting and
  three ignitions (two of them later) settles to the same burn, cell for cell, as the same fire stepped with
  `advanceTime`, with under a twentieth of the carrying visits (10,033 against 17,392,485; fails without the fix: the
  same count both ways); settles stopped after 1, 777, 3,600 and 5,000.5 s, stepping on, and a change of wind and
  moisture mid-burn match the stepped fire at every stop; an aborted settle and a reset fire do too.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: scatter motion vectors drew a streamed forest from destroyed buffers (KB-SCATTER-VELTILES1, scatter)

- **Repro:** a `ScatterTiles` scatter with `ScatterVelocity` added to TAA; stream a tile in with `setTile` so a ring
  needs more instances. The next frame's submit failed with "[Buffer (unlabeled)] used in submit while destroyed"
  (found by lane B's forest film shots, one velocity pass per swaying scatter).
- **Cause:** `ScatterTiles` destroys and remakes its LOD ring instance buffers, and its record and table buffers, as the
  held tiles change, and tells the colour pass (`instancesChanged`). `ScatterVelocity` (`packages/scatter/src/velocity.ts`)
  made its ring bind groups once per pipeline and view and kept them, so they still pointed at the destroyed buffers.
- **Fix:** each view keeps, with its bind groups, the buffers they were made from (instance rings, the WebGL2 route's
  counts, the pose bindings) and makes them again when any of them is replaced. Regression:
  `packages/scatter/test/velocity-tiles.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and `--compat`; fails with the destroyed-buffer error
  without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: an EXR whose colorInteropID names other primaries decoded as Rec.709 (KB-EXR-INTEROPID1, environment)

- **Repro:** `encodeEXR` of one pixel (1, 0, 0) with `colorInteropID: 'lin_ap1_scene'` (linear ACEScg) and no
  `chromaticities`, then `parseEXR`: the pixel stayed (1, 0, 0), `primariesConverted` false; linear sRGB is about
  (1.705, -0.130, -0.024).
- **Cause:** no reader in `packages/environment` read the attribute. OpenEXR 3.4 added it and says it supersedes
  `chromaticities` for most purposes ("Technical Introduction", https://openexr.com/en/latest/TechnicalIntroduction.html).
- **Fix:** all three readers follow the ASWF Color Interop Forum's reading order
  (https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/ColorInterop/blob/main/Recommendations/04_OpenEXRFiles/OpenEXRFiles.md):
  ACES container flag, `data`, a known ID, then `chromaticities` as the fallback, so a known ID wins when both are
  present. IDs, primaries and transfer functions are those of "Color Space Encodings for Texture Assets and CG
  Rendering",
  https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/ColorInterop/blob/main/Recommendations/01_TextureAssetColorSpaces/TextureAssetColorSpaces.md
  Regression: `packages/environment/tests/exr-interop-id.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: comments and a README still named a one million vertex limit that core and gltf/pbr no longer have (KB-VERTCAP-TEXT1; voxel-edit, loaders, mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** `partitionMesh`'s options and doc comment and the `./mesh` row of the voxel-edit README said a core
  `Geometry` takes at most 1,000,000 vertices; the `maxPartVertices` comment of `@margoengine/loaders` and the
  `SculptView.attach` comment of mesh-edit (with its limits row) said gltf/pbr takes 1,000,000.
- **Cause:** both limits rose (core to 11,184,810, `packages/loaders/src/geometry.ts`; gltf/pbr to 16,777,216 a
  primitive, `packages/gltf/src/parts.ts`) and only the loaders' core text followed (KB0097).
- **Fixed:** the texts name the limit that does bind: a materials mesh's 1,000,000 vertices, and for `SculptView` the
  storage binding its one part must fit. No limit changed. Regression: `tests/vertex-limit-text.test.js` (it named the
  five lines on the old tree).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a soft body held off the ground only after its vertex-block passes sank by twice its load (KB-SOFT-CONTACTSPLIT1, physics soft kernel)

- **Repro:** a 10 cm cube of 1 MPa rubber on `setSolver('vertex-block')`, standing on a fixed floor, pressed by 100 N on
  its top at 20 pieces of 20 passes: its top sank by a strain of 1.98% where p / E is 1% (4.2% at 10 pieces, 1.35% at
  40); a hemisphere pressed on the floor sank by three to seven times Hertz's approach.
- **Cause:** `packages/physics/soft-kernel/src/world.rs` meets the colliders after the passes (`apply_contacts`), so the
  passes solved each piece as if the base were free: the floor took the base back each piece while the rest of the body
  went on into it, and the free-translation step of the vertex-block solve (`solve_vertex_block_translation`) moved the
  whole body back towards where its load would carry a free body.
- **Fix:** `hold_still_contacts` holds each vertex off the still bodies it touches inside the vertex-block passes, right
  after its block update, booking the push as the contact's impulse (so friction and the velocity pass see it), and a
  body so held has no free translation, as a pinned one has none. Regression:
  `packages/physics/tests/soft-cells.test.js` ("a body pressed on the ground comes to its static deflection"). Since
  2026-11-28 (second change) the constraint solver's cells are held inside each pass too (`hold_constraint_cells`: a 100 kPa
  cube pressed on the floor at 20 x 20 sank 45% before, 1.41% after; "a constraint-solved body pressed on the ground"),
  and the `'fem'` solve holds a particle resting on a still body at zero normal velocity inside its conjugate gradients,
  filtering the residual and search directions as Baraff and Witkin (1998, section 5.3) constrain particles, letting go
  one the floor pulls at the next piece.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a steady force on a soft body was a kick at the step's start (KB-SOFT-FORCEKICK1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** the cube above with its base pinned, pressed by 100 N through `addParticleForce`: at 20 pieces of 20 passes
  its top came to rest at a strain of 0.37% (vertex-block) or 0.10% (fem), where the same load as gravity gave 0.9%.
- **Cause:** `SoftBodies.applyForces` added each force's whole F dt to the particles' velocities before the first piece;
  the damping and the implicit solves took most of that kick before it loaded the body.
- **Fix:** it writes each particle's acceleration to new kernel columns (`ax`, `ay`, `az`), which the kernel takes with
  gravity at the start of every piece. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/soft-cells.test.js` ("a steady force loads a
  damped body to its static deflection").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the clouds' two-stream check read the deck's map in the sky's old units (KB-SKY-LAYERUNIT1, sky)

- **Repro:** `node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs cloud-bounds` on main after 2e2a10a637: "two-stream down at
  tau 5: sum 0.18 want 0.75" on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`; it passed at 2e2a10a637's parent.
- **Cause:** 2e2a10a637 (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1) draws the sky's reflection map, and the deck `VolumetricClouds` lay over it
  (`Sky.environmentLayer`), at 2 to the exposure times `Sky.pictureScale` (0.1447 by day in the check), as intended;
  the check still took the sun's irradiance in sky units (6.4), and the `environmentLayer` doc still said "at the
  sky's exposure". The deck's light itself did not change: divided by the scale, down, up and sum are the parent's to
  4 digits (tau 5: 0.624, 0.226, 0.907; tau 20: 0.420, 0.502, 0.954; tau 80: 0.189, 0.738, 0.955).
- **Fix:** the check takes the sun's irradiance in the map's units (times `sky.pictureScale`), bounds unchanged, and
  the `environmentLayer` doc names the unit (`packages/sky/src/base.ts`).
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/cloud-bounds-check.html` (features-check cloud-bounds) on WebGPU and
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: create3MFMesh made a material for every group, so a coloured scan crashed the page (KB-3MF-SCANGROUPS1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `create3MFMesh` on the 3MF Consortium's `examples/material/kinect_scan.3mf` (3mf-samples 665e20dc4d,
  282,544 triangles, 57,464 groups, one per first-corner vertex colour): the browser tab crashed.
- **Cause:** one `Material` and one draw per group, though groups that differ in vertex colour alone look alike
  (`packages/loaders/src/threemf-mesh.ts`).
- **Fixed:** groups that look alike share a material, and opaque ranges that follow each other are one draw.
  Regression: `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-finish-gpu-check.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: create3MFMesh smoothed normals across the edges of a box (KB-3MF-CREASE1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `create3MFMesh` with its defaults on the Consortium's `multiprop-opaque.3mf` and
  `multiprop-translucent.3mf`: the cubes shade as rounded blobs, and the translucent one has dark curved lines.
- **Cause:** `'smooth'` shared one normal among all the faces at a position, at any angle.
- **Fixed:** faces more than `creaseAngle` (default 40 degrees) apart keep their own normals. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-finish-gpu-check.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a second 3MF property resource of one id silently replaced the first (KB-3MF-DUPID1, loaders)

- **Repro:** two `colorgroup` or `basematerials` elements with the same `id` (the Consortium's
  `MUSTFAIL_Chapter5a_DuplicatedBaseMaterials.3mf`): the file loaded with the second one's colours.
- **Cause:** property resources went into maps by id without a check (`packages/loaders/src/threemf.ts`).
- **Fixed:** a `syntax` error names the id. Regression: `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-materials.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a build of beam lattices alone said only that it held no triangles (KB-3MF-LATTICEONLY1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `parse3MF` on the Consortium's `examples/beam lattice/pyramid.3mf`.
- **Cause:** the core reader did not note that an object it built nothing of was a lattice.
- **Fixed:** the error names the object and `parse3MFEvaluated`. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-materials.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a transmissive material ignored its colour map in the light it passed (KB-MAT-TINTMAP1, materials)

- **Repro:** on a #cccccc background draw a quad with `new Material({ transmission: 1, roughness: 0.5, ...o })` and
  read the middle pixel. `color: [1, 0, 0, 1]` gave (202, 2, 2); `map` set to a red texel gave (202, 202, 202), the
  same as no colour at all, and so did a red `layered()` layer, with or without `new Transmission()`. The Consortium's
  `multiprop-translucent.3mf` therefore drew without its two picture layers. KHR_materials_transmission tints the
  transmitted light by the whole base colour, baseColorTexture included.
- **Cause:** only a material with a physical map (slot 5 and up) took the physical-maps shader, whose tint draw reads
  the surface. A transmissive material with only a base map, or with a feature such as `layered()`, kept gltf/pbr's
  frame-only tint draw, one constant `color` x transmission x volume attenuation (`Material.tint`). The pass rows read
  the same because the opaque capture holds only the background there.
- **Fixed:** a transmissive material with a base map (slots 0 to 4) or any feature takes the physical-maps shader too
  (`mapped`, `packages/materials/src/built-material.ts`), so its tint draw multiplies by the surface's base colour and
  transmission. Regression: `packages/materials/test/tint-map-browser.mjs` (20 rows: colour, map, map with a
  transmission map, layer and none; two-draw and dual-source; with and without the pass), WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a JPEG 2000 stream with a marker of 0xFF30 to 0xFF3F was refused as cut (KB-J2K-BAREMARKER1, decoders)

- **Repro:** `decodeJPEG2000` on test codestream `p0_02.j2k` of Rec. ITU-T T.803, which holds the marker 0xFF30 in its
  main header, threw `failed` ("ends inside a header it needs").
- **Cause:** every marker of a header was read with a length field; those sixteen markers stand alone (T.800 A.1).
- **Fixed:** they are stepped over (`jpeg2000-kernel/src/codestream.rs`). Regression: `cargo test` there,
  `markers_without_a_segment_are_stepped_over`; `packages/decoders/tests/jpeg2000-conformance.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a JP2 file with an ICC profile decoded with the wrong colours (KB-J2K-ICC1, decoders)

- **Repro:** `file5.jp2`, `file7.jp2` and `file8.jp2` of Rec. ITU-T T.803 differed from their sRGB references by up to
  126, 96 and 19 levels of 255. A colour box of a method Part 1 does not define also hid the box after it.
- **Cause:** the restricted ICC method (T.800 I.3.2, J.8) was recorded and never applied, and the first colour box was
  taken whatever its method.
- **Fixed:** the profile goes through the package's ICC reader to sRGB at 8 or 16 bits (`src/jpeg2000-codec.ts`,
  `src/icc.ts`), and a box of another method is ignored (I.5.3.3). Differences are now at most 2. Regression:
  `packages/decoders/tests/jpeg2000.test.js` "a JP2 file with a restricted ICC profile decodes to sRGB" and
  `cargo test`, `the_first_method_part_1_defines_names_the_colour`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a dense smoke column drew one flat colour (KB-VFX-SMOKEFLAT1, vfx, weather)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-ridge-smoke.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out
  <folder>`: early flat 7.60 percent (bound 5), mid 3.85; the flat pixels are the column (8-bit 90, 58, 32 over a
  quarter of the frame).
- **Cause:** a lit billboard took its ambient (`base * ambient`) and the air's light (`VFXLit.air`, added into the
  ambient) the same from every side. On the ridge the weak smoke-dimmed sun gave a ball at most 0.024 of directional
  light against 0.10 of ambient and 0.31 of the firelit pall's light, so about 97 percent of the column's light did not
  depend on the normal, and overlapping puffs gave one colour.
- **Fix:** `packages/vfx/src/lit.ts` splits both by the isotropic view factors of a tilted surface, (1 + n_y) / 2 of
  the upper hemisphere and (1 - n_y) / 2 of the lower (Liu and Jordan, Solar Energy 7(2):53-74, 1963; Duffie and
  Beckman eq. 2.15.1), a two-stream split of the diffuse light (Meador and Weaver, J. Atmos. Sci. 37:630-643, 1980):
  the ambient from above with the ground's albedo of it from below (`VFXLit.ground`, default 0.2), the air's light from
  below with the layer's reflectance of it from above (`VFXLit.airReflectance`, default `PALL_REFLECTANCE`, the
  slab reflectance of a thick smoke pall). Both keep their mean over every normal. `SmokeOptions.ground` and
  `.airReflectance` and `FireFront.airReflectance` carry them, and `WeatherDrive` writes its haze's reflectance
  (`hazeReflectance`) with the air. Real frames (RTX A6000, WebGPU, 1920 x 1080): ridge-smoke early flat 7.60 to 2.45,
  mid 3.85 to 0.0075, every other bar within its bound (early grain 0.069 to 0.085, bound 0.5); the column's puffs are
  lit from below by the fire and darker on top.
- **Aftermath column darker, by design (measured):** the timber-valley aftermath still (`--views=aftermath
  --query=weather=smoke`, 960 x 540) draws its column darker than before the split (box x 0.4-0.6, y 0.3-0.6: 8-bit
  26,22,22 to 22,15,13; sky and haze unchanged at 86,52,36; crush 0). The camera looks 31 degrees up at it, so the
  billboard normals (side plus the camera plane's normal times sqrt(1 - |uv|^2)) average n_y -0.34: the sky's ambient
  (0.1 grey there) comes in at 0.77 of its mean and the fire's air light (0.013, 0.006, 0.002, small after the burn) at
  1.18 to 1.20, so the column takes 0.82, 0.79, 0.78 of its old linear light, which the tonemap's toe stretches at
  these codes. Proof: the same frame with every column's split set to its old mean (`ground` 1, `airReflectance`
  1, 1, 1) matches the frame before the split (0.02 percent of pixels differ, by 1 code); the crane view of the same
  column, 2.9 degrees up, changes only 26,22,22 to 26,20,20. A burnt floor has a lower albedo than the default 0.2, so
  the real undersides are darker still; nothing writes the burnt ground's albedo onto the columns yet.
- **Weak spot left:** the column still reads as stacked smooth balls; the puffs have no noise of their own and no
  self-shadowing inside the column (Beer-Lambert to its edge).
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/lit.test.js` (the shader's split and its means, from the uniform the effect
  writes), `packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js` (a column and a front carry the values),
  `packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js` (the drive writes the reflectance), and the real-GPU `checkLit` of
  `node packages/vfx/test/features-check.mjs` (every third pixel of the ball against the split, at the defaults and at
  given values, 1x and 4x MSAA, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: by night a far ridge in the haze stood pale against the firelit sky over it (KB-SKY-NIGHTRIDGE1, sky)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=ridge --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>`: the
  hazed far ridges read 8-bit (169, 122, 105) under a sky of (154, 97, 36) right over them (640 x 360, RTX A6000).
- **Cause:** the sky fog takes the sky's radiance toward the ray as the colour a far ground fades to. By night the
  dome is the night sky seen through the low haze layer (`layerTransmittance`, t^(1 / sin e)) with the layer's glow
  (`scatteredLight`) in front (`lowLayer`, KB-SKY-NIGHTPALL1), but the fog took the night sky as it is above the layer,
  so a fully hazed ridge never met the sky over it.
- **Fix:** `look.ts` splits `lowLayer` into `hazeLayer` (the layer without the fires) and the fires' glow; the fog
  passes its sky colour through `hazeLayer` (`fog.ts`; without a look it is the colour as it is), and adds the fires'
  light on the haze itself as before (KB-SKY-HAZEGLOW1). By day the layer leaves the sky as it was, so the day frame
  is unchanged.
- **Regression:** `node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs` (`look`, `nightRidge`: the same pixels over the night sky
  and over a plane the fog hides fully, under a layer with its glow and a fire, WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the fires' layer glow stopped short of the haze's own light under an exp2 sky fog (KB-WEATHER-FIRESIGHT1, weather)

- **Repro:** timber valley under smoke: `WeatherDrive` wrote `atmosphere.fireSight` 1,142 m while the sky fog's own
  fire track (`fog.ts`, 2 / density) ran 1,978 m.
- **Cause:** the drive wrote `2 / extinction` for "the sky fog's 2 / density", but it gives an `'exp2'` sky fog (the
  default falloff) the density `extinction / sqrt(3)`, so the two differed by sqrt(3); only an `'exp'` fog matched.
- **Fix:** the sight is `2 /` the density the sky fog has (`packages/weather/src/drive.ts`), or `2 / extinction` with
  no fog.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js` ("the fires' sight is the sky fog's own 2 / density").

### Open 2026-11-27: the water draws flat grey below its surface in the floating example (KB-WATER-UNDERGREY1, water)

- **Repro:** `examples/floating.html` on WebGPU, camera above the swell: the parts of the floating bodies below the
  surface and the water around them are one flat grey, with no depth fade, refraction or tint of the body under it.
- **Cause:** not traced. The floating physics draws nothing there (`LoadSolver` only moves the bodies); the colour is
  the `Water` surface pass's underwater and transmission look, which belongs to the ocean lane.
- **For:** the ocean lane (`packages/water`). Noted by the SEA-12 lane, which does not change water rendering.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: booleans refused a solid holding a triangle with no area (KB-BOOL-FLAT1, mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** `batchBooleanMeshes` on a closed box with one edge split on one side and closed by a triangle whose
  three corners are in a line threw `TypeError`; a displacement step can make such triangles.
- **Cause:** every boolean checked its input with the editing rule that each face has area.
- **Fixed:** the three booleans remove such triangles first, keeping the solid closed (Botsch and Kobbelt 2001;
  `packages/mesh-edit/src/flat-triangles.ts`). Regression: `packages/mesh-edit/tests/boolean-flat-triangles.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a 3MF boolean could colour a cut face a hair below 0 (KB-3MF-CUTCOLOUR1, loaders)

- **Repro:** a clipped lattice with two property colours read back vertex colours of -6e-17, which a material
  refuses (`Invalid prepared PBR color`).
- **Cause:** a point on a face edge interpolated just outside the face triangle it is shaded from
  (`packages/loaders/src/threemf-csg.ts`).
- **Fixed:** the interpolated colour is clipped to 0..1. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-evaluate.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: createMeshes and createPBRMeshes smoothed the edges of a box without normals (KB-LOAD-CREASE1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `createMeshes` on a cube of 8 shared vertices with no normals: one normal a corner, along the diagonal,
  so the faces shaded as a blob.
- **Cause:** both took `toGeometry`'s rule for a file without normals, which smooths across every edge.
- **Fixed:** they smooth only faces within `creaseAngle` (40 degrees, as `create3MFMesh`) with the geometry
  package's `creasedNormals`, copying a vertex where its sides differ. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/crease.test.js`. `creasedNormals` with no tolerance now looks in one cell instead of 27
  when it welds corners, which took 2.6 s of the 4.6 s on a 2.4 million triangle field (now 1.6 s in all, on the
  development PC under load).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: createPBRMeshes refused a colored scan as too many parts (KB-LOAD-PBRGROUPS1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `createPBRMeshes(engine, await parse3MF(file))` on a strip of 9,000 triangles with a color of its own
  at every corner: "more than 4096 parts".
- **Cause:** `parse3MF` groups triangles by their first corner's color, for `createMeshes`, which draws one color a
  group; `createPBRMeshes` made a part of every group although the vertex colors already carry the color.
- **Fixed:** with vertex colors, neighboring groups that differ in color alone are one part. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/crease.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: volume data on a displacement mesh and a short composite were accepted (KB-3MF-VOLDATA1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `parse3MFVolumetric` on `<d:displacementmesh v:volumeid="5">`, or on a `<composite>` with one
  `<materialmapping>` for a `basematerials` group of two.
- **Cause:** the reader looked for `volumeid` on `mesh` and `levelset` only, so the first was dropped without a
  word, and it asked only that a composite have some mapping.
- **Fixed:** both are a `syntax` error, as the volumetric extension (5.2 and 5.2.2) rules them out. Regression:
  `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-volume-sample.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: isolated darker pixels on the flat sides of a cut displacement mesh (KB-3MF-DOTS1, mesh-edit, loaders)

- **Repro:** `parse3MFEvaluated` on a cube of side 10 with a 32 x 32 sine height map on its top (height 2.5) minus
  a box from (4.3, -1, 4) to (20, 5.2, 20), drawn with one flat-shaded material at 640 x 640 with the engine on
  WebGPU: single pixels on the flat sides about 18 % darker than their neighbours. 1,333 of the 12,146 triangles
  were thinner than 1e-4 units and 2 had no area.
- **Cause:** the exact boolean kept every point its BSP trees cut into the input faces, among them points a few
  Float32 steps from a real corner and points along straight edges. Rounded, they made needles and caps whose normals
  are rounding noise, and the 3MF reader fanned faces with corners in a line into more of them.
- **Fixed:** before rounding, the exact boolean takes out the points that are no corner of the solid, by exact tests,
  so the surface is the same (`packages/mesh-edit/src/boolean-simplify.ts`). The new `precision: 'float32'` option
  rounds to Float32 and removes triangles thinner than 2^-20 of their coordinates, keeping the solid closed; the 3MF
  reader uses it, and fans a face from its centre when a fan from a corner would give such a triangle. The repro now
  has 3,534 triangles, none thinner than 1e-4. In the render, pixels 7 % or more below their eight neighbours' median
  went from 10 to 3; those 3 are also in the picture of the displaced cube before any boolean (creases of the faceted
  top). Regression: `packages/mesh-edit/tests/boolean-exact.test.js`,
  `packages/loaders/tests/threemf-evaluate.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: in an AR session a post effect made solid meshes see-through (KB-XR-AREFFECTS1, shared, materials)

- **Repro:** `node packages/xr/tests/ar-effects.browser.mjs` (stand-in headset, engine route, WebGPU and the WebGL2
  layer, RTX A6000). Before the fix, at 1 sample every one of 7,284 solid pixels of the left eye was see-through under
  Tonemap and DOF, 6,383 under the shared scene-depth capture (`acquireDepth`: water, html, contact lights), and 6,085 to
  6,383 under `StencilBuffer` at 1 and 4 samples on a device without `depth32float-stencil8`.
- **Cause:** the AR blit takes alpha from the eye's depth coverage, and three passes drew the scene into a depth of
  their own without giving it back: `SceneTarget` at 1 sample (`packages/shared/msaa.js`), `acquireDepth` at 1 sample
  (`packages/shared/gpu.js`) and `StencilBuffer` at every sample count (`packages/materials/src/stencil-buffer.ts`).
  The compositor's depth layer, filled from the eye's depth, was empty with them too, in VR as well.
- **Fixed:** each copies its depth into the attachment it replaced: `SceneTarget` in its final resolve (or restore), as
  at 4 samples, and only where both have one size (upscaling captures draw smaller); the other two through `DepthCopy`.
  Later desktop passes now depth-test against the scene at 1 sample too. One more full-screen depth pass a frame per
  such capture at 1 sample. Regression: the same check.
- **Sources:** WebXR Augmented Reality Module, W3C, section 2.4 "XR Compositor Behaviors" (an alpha-blend display
  composites the layer over the real world by its alpha), https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-ar-module-1/ ; WebXR Layers
  API, W3C, section 3.5 "XRProjectionLayer" (the compositor may use the depth attachment, which is expected to represent
  the rendered scene), https://www.w3.org/TR/webxrlayers-1/ ; WebXR Depth Sensing, W3C (the occlusion pass that reads
  the same eye depth), https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-depth-sensing-1/ .
- The 1,137 pixels of alpha 241 first seen at 4 samples were not a depth bug: the page's line wrote no depth
  (KB-XR-ARNODEPTH1).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: in AR, content that writes no depth was only as opaque as its brightest channel (KB-XR-ARNODEPTH1, xr, shared)

- **Repro:** `node packages/xr/tests/ar-effects.browser.mjs` (and its layer half): the line with its default
  `depthWrite: false`. Before the fix its green pixels had alpha 241 of 255 under Tonemap (1,137 at 4 samples), a black
  line had alpha 0, and under TAA every empty pixel became opaque once the eye's alpha was used.
- **Cause:** core clears a view to an opaque colour (core colours have no alpha), so the eye's alpha was 1 everywhere and
  the AR blit (`packages/xr/src/eyes.ts`) could only take depth coverage, or the brightest channel where no depth was
  written. TAA, not told the eye is premultiplied, wrote alpha 1 into its history.
- **Fixed:** right after the main pass xr's AR alpha pass writes alpha 0 on every sample nothing drew (depth-0 triangle,
  depthCompare 'equal', alpha-only mask), as TransparentCanvas does, so later draws leave their coverage in alpha; the blit
  takes the largest of depth share, that alpha and the brightest channel; AR eyes mark the engine premultiplied for the
  session (`markPremultiplied`, shared/straight-display.js). Regression: the same check's depthless round (40 checks
  failed without the fix). Transparent meshes need nothing more: core's main pass (order 0) draws only core meshes,
  which have no blending, and gltf/pbr draws every model, glTF and materials blended primitives included, at order 1,
  after the alpha pass. The same check's veil round (added 2026-11-27) holds a depthless glTF BLEND pane and a
  materials pane at alpha 0.6 to their own 153 of 255 under no effect, Tonemap and TAA, WebGPU and the layer, 1x and 4x.
- **Sources:** T. Porter and T. Duff, "Compositing Digital Images", SIGGRAPH 1984,
  https://graphics.pixar.com/library/Compositing/paper.pdf ; A. R. Smith, "Image Compositing Fundamentals", Microsoft
  Technical Memo 4, 1995, http://alvyray.com/Memos/CG/Microsoft/4_comp.pdf ; WebXR Device API (W3C), XREnvironmentBlendMode
  'alpha-blend', https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-ar-module-1/#xrenvironmentblendmode-enum ; WebGPU (W3C), GPUColorWrite and
  depth compare, https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/ .

### Fixed 2026-11-27: SSAO and DOF lost passes drawn after the scene, lines among them (KB-POST-LATEDRAW1, post, dof)

- **Repro:** `node packages/post/test/late-draw-browser.mjs` (and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`). Before the fix a `Lines` pass
  at its default order 20 drew nothing under SSAO at 4 samples; under DOF it was lost at 4 samples when `Lines` attached
  after DOF, and a pass at order 29 was lost at 1 and 4 samples.
- **Cause:** SSAO made the capture's final resolve in its extraction (order 10), and DOF computed its blur at 20 and 21:
  later draws landed in the multisampled capture after its last resolve, or outside DOF's blur, though the contract is
  "post-processing resolves at 30".
- **Fixed:** SSAO makes the final resolve in its composite (30); DOF's blur passes run at 29.8 and 29.9. Regression: the
  same check, over every capturing effect, both attach orders, orders 20 and 29.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: on the WebGL2 layer at 4 samples AR eye edges differed from WebGPU (KB-XR-AR4XCOMPAT1, xr)

- **Repro:** `node packages/xr/tests/ar-effects.browser.mjs`: with no effect the layer's left eye differed from WebGPU's
  by more than 2 in 512 bytes (largest 191).
- **Cause:** the layer cannot read one sample of a 4x texture (GLSL ES 3.00 has no multisample samplers), so each of the
  AR blit's four depth loads returned the resolved depth and coverage read 0 or 4 of 4.
- **Sources:** OpenGL ES 3.0.6, Khronos, section 4.1 "Per-Fragment Operations",
  https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/es_spec_3.0.pdf ; GLSL ES 3.10, Khronos (adds `sampler2DMS`),
  https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.1/GLSL_ES_Specification_3.10.pdf .
- **Fixed:** on the layer at 4 samples the blit counts coverage with a depth-tested pass into a 4x `r8unorm` target,
  whose resolve is the share of drawn samples (depth tests run per sample there). Regression: the same check compares
  the two backends' eyes (0 bytes differ by more than 2 after; largest difference 0). A capturing effect's depth copy still reads the resolved depth there, so under an effect the
  layer's edges stay all or nothing ([Limits](limits.md#xr-ar-edges-on-the-webgl2-layer)).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: SceneFade also drew into offscreen target views (KB-FADE-TARGETVIEW1, post)

- **Repro:** `node packages/post/test/scene-fade-target-browser.mjs` (and `--compat`), before the fix (RTX A6000): half
  way through a fade a 64 x 32 target view in the canvas's format had 924 bytes of the canvas snapshot blended into it;
  an `rgba16float` target made WebGPU refuse the whole frame ("Attachment state of [RenderPipeline] is not
  compatible"), and the WebGL2 layer changed 7,068 of its bytes.
- **Cause:** `SceneFade.draw` (`packages/post/src/scene-fade.ts`) did not test `context.view?.target`: it blended the
  snapshot into the target with a pipeline made for the canvas format.
- **Fixed:** the pass skips views with a `target`, before its uniform write. Regression: the check above, with the
  target view before and after the canvas view and alone.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: damaged JPEG 2000 files could trap the decoder or keep it busy for minutes (KB-J2K-HOSTILE1, decoders)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/decoders/tests/jpeg2000-fuzz.test.js` against the decoder of 45ad3faad: 13 of
  10,086 inputs trapped the Wasm module or returned an invalid layout, and 3 gave no result within 10 s.
- **Causes:** the tile count overflowed Wasm's 32-bit `usize`; a JP2 box length near 2^64 overflowed its end; a region
  of interest shift of 32 or more overflowed the unshift; every mapped or subsampled channel was resampled to the
  picture whether read or not; a picture without a sample gave an empty result; each tile header held a table of every
  component; and tile-components, precincts, progression changes and packet visits had no bound a few bytes could not
  pass. By reading, 31 bit-planes of damaged data could also overflow the 5-3 lifting, the reversible component
  transform and the level shift.
- **Fixed:** in `packages/decoders/jpeg2000-kernel`: 64-bit counts and saturating box ends, channels built only when
  read, sparse per-component tables, wrapping lifting, a per-tile structure budget, a 2^20 tile-component limit, packets
  bounded by the bytes that can hold them and a per-decode work budget ([Limits](limits.md#jpeg-2000-decoding)).
  Regression: the fuzz run, `jpeg2000-browser.mjs` and four crate tests.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: TAA dropped history at silhouettes on alternate frames, so edges flickered with the jitter (KB-TAA-EDGE1, taa)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs`, with `TAA` at full size on the path that already
  measures `TAAUpscale`: a thin bright post 4 m from a camera orbiting it, a wall at 44 m. The post's edge alternated 3.26
  sRGB levels a pixel and frame with the fast camera and 2.92 with the slow one on WebGPU (RTX A6000); TAAUpscale reads
  0.19 and 0.13 on the same path, and the bound is 0.25. On the WebGL2 layer: 5.27 and 2.81.
- **Cause:** the default resolve took each pixel's own motion and expected depth and tested each bilinear history tap
  against that one depth. At a silhouette the jitter moves the edge across the pixel centre, so the surface a pixel
  samples, and with it the motion and expected depth, changed from frame to frame; history was dropped on alternate
  frames and the raw jittered sample showed. TAAUpscale already used closest-depth motion and a footprint test.
- **Fix:** the default resolve (`packages/taa/src/shader.ts`) takes the motion and expected depth of the nearest surface
  in the 3x3 neighbourhood (largest valid expected depth, so a 4x silhouette pixel whose motion mean is a false depth
  takes its neighbour's surface) and keeps history when that depth lies inside the depth range of the 3x3 history
  footprint round the reprojected point; a disocclusion (the surface absent from the whole footprint) is still
  rejected, and the colour clamp removes what the footprint's other surface brings. `stochastic` keeps its own range
  test. Sources: B. Karis, "High Quality Temporal Supersampling", SIGGRAPH 2014 (velocity of the closest depth in a 3x3
  neighbourhood); M. Salvi, "An Excursion in Temporal Supersampling", GDC 2016; AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2
  documentation, 2022 (depth and motion dilation); D. Nehab et al., "Accelerating Real-Time Shading with Reverse
  Reprojection Caching", Graphics Hardware 2007 (the depth test against a cached depth); L. Yang, S. Liu and M. Salvi,
  "A Survey of Temporal Antialiasing Techniques", Computer Graphics Forum 39(2), 2020 (such tests fail at depth edges
  under subpixel motion).
- **After:** 0.179 fast and 0.225 slow on WebGPU; a box crossing the wall leaves 0 red pixels behind it (4,139 drawn).
  On the WebGL2 layer at 4x: 2.89 and 0.335 until KB-TAA-COMPATEDGE2 was fixed (0.175 and 0.231 since); with
  `antialias: false` the layer reads the same as WebGPU, 0.275 and 0.147 on both.
- **Regression:** `packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs` asserts TAA's edge alternation at most 0.25 fast and slow on
  WebGPU (fails before: 3.26 and 2.92) and no trail behind the box on both backends.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: on the WebGL2 layer at 4x a TAA silhouette alternated with a fast camera (KB-TAA-COMPATEDGE2, taa, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs` (RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11): TAA's post
  edge alternated 2.89 sRGB levels with the fast camera and 0.335 with the slow one (bound 0.25; WebGPU 0.179 and
  0.225); at `antialias: false` the layer read 0.275 and 0.147, as WebGPU does.
- **Cause:** read back at the post's edge (row 240): GLSL ES 3.00 has no `sampler2DMS`, so the layer's motion resolve
  sees only the mean of a pixel's four object samples (KB-TAA-COMPATEDGE1). A pixel the post 4 m away half covers over
  the wall at 44 m read as one surface of expected depth 0.0077 (post 0.0253, wall 0.0022) moving 3.36 px (post 0.44,
  wall 4.28), a surface that is not there. The resolve's closest-depth choice (KB-TAA-EDGE1) then gave that false motion
  to the wall pixel beside it. Second, the layer's depth resolve is one sample (a blit), so TAA's history kept the wall's
  depth at pixels where WebGPU's nearest sample keeps the post's: WebGPU with its depth resolve forced to sample 0 reads
  0.39 fast.
- **Fixed:** object velocity shaders (TAA's, `RawShaders`, `ScatterVelocity`) write log2 of the expected depth in the 4x
  target's spare `z`. By Jensen's inequality log2 of the mean depth exceeds the mean of log2 depth only where the
  samples' depths differ; above a gap of 1/32 (any mix of depths 1.6 times apart or more, far above a plane's own spread
  and float16 rounding) the motion resolve gives the pixel the motion and expected depth of the nearest unmixed surface
  of its 3x3 that is nearer than its mean, and a new 1x depth32float target gives TAA's history that surface's depth:
  what WebGPU's nearest sample gives. Only the layer's 4x route draws the extra pass (one fullscreen depth write);
  WebGPU's calls change only in the shader text. Sources: Karis 2014 and AMD FSR 2's depth and motion dilation (as
  KB-TAA-EDGE1). After: 0.175 fast and 0.231 slow on the layer (WebGPU 0.179 and 0.225, unchanged).
- **Regression:** `packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs` now asserts the 0.25 bound on the WebGL2 layer as well
  (fails before: 2.89). Left: surfaces closer than 1.6 times in depth still mix their motions by coverage there.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: TAA variance clipping moved a transparent canvas's colour and alpha apart (KB-TAA-ALPHACLIP1, taa)

- **Repro:** `node packages/post/test/alpha-views-browser.mjs`: `rejection: 'variance'` before Tonemap left a partly
  covered pixel 3.2 of 255 from the plate's colour times its alpha in a half-width view (2.65 on a full one), against
  0.9 without TAA.
- **Cause:** colour was clipped towards the variance box's centre in YCoCg while alpha was clamped on its own, so the two
  moved by different shares.
- **Fixed:** the transparent canvas's resolve clips colour and alpha as one point of one box
  (`packages/taa/src/alpha.ts`); 1.1 of 255 after. Opaque canvases keep their shader. Regression: the same check.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a 4x texture made on a lost WebGL2 context threw a false unsupported error (KB-COMPAT-LOSTMSAA1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** lose the layer's context (`WEBGL_lose_context`) and render a frame with 4 samples before the loss event
  arrives: `render` threw "WebGL2 compatibility cannot do 4x multisampled rgba8unorm textures (this WebGL2 has no
  multisample RGBA8 renderbuffers)".
- **Cause:** `getInternalformatParameter` answers null on a lost context (WebGL 2.0, 3.7), and during a GPU reset
  before `isContextLost()` turns true; `createTexture` read null as a format without 4x samples.
- **Fixed:** in `packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/resources.ts`, null for a renderable format refuses nothing: the
  loss event loses the device, as WebGPU makes textures on a lost device without errors. A format without 4x samples is
  still refused. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/lost-report.test.js` and `lost-context-browser.mjs`.

### Open 2026-11-27: one half-view frame under Tonemap read back untone-mapped on the WebGL2 layer (KB-POST-HALFVIEW-ONCE1, post)

- **Repro:** not reproduced. `node packages/post/test/scene-background-browser.mjs --compat` failed once in a full post
  `test:gpu` chain (RTX A6000, other work loading the CPU): `Tonemap #808080 half view` drew 128 where 116 is right,
  the value of the frame drawn just before it (no effect, same view, an engine since disposed). 12 reruns of the test
  and 300 repeats of the two draws, with and without a loaded CPU, all drew 116.
- **Cause:** not established, narrowed on 2026-11-27 (RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11). An instrumented run of the same
  draws recorded, for each, every image the layer gave the canvas, the canvas read in the render's own task, the
  uniform words of each full-screen draw, the console and the screenshot: in 882 draws, 378 of them beside a second GPU
  browser and all under CPU load, each frame was presented once, Tonemap's uniforms were as written, canvas and
  screenshot agreed, and the page printed nothing. A second probe of the layer's present path alone (a new context each
  round, the old one lost) took 1,000 screenshots at once after the present, 700 of them with a GPU load, and none was
  stale. A new device is a new WebGL2 context, so no target of it can hold the earlier frame's value. Losing the
  Tonemap engine's context before its render reproduces the failure exactly (that frame and its comparison read 128,
  every later case is right, no console line), because the page keeps the frame before; whether the context was lost in
  the failed run was not recorded, and that run's harness dropped the page's console on a failed check.
- **Next:** the check now names the layer on the next failure: it reads the canvas in each render's task and the
  device's loss, and the shared harness (`packages/post/test/post-browser.mjs`) prints page errors and warnings as they
  arrive.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: volume files drew Beer-Lambert in display space, up to 22 levels off (KB-VOL-TINT-DISPLAY1, gltf)

- **Repro:** `node packages/gltf/scripts/test-screen-transmission-browser.mjs` (and `--compat`), case `slab-default`: one
  unit-scale slab loaded by `parseGLTFAsync`, IOR 1, roughness 0, specular 0, KHR_materials_volume thicknessFactor 1,
  attenuationColor 0.1/0.5/0.9, attenuationDistance 1, over a grey backdrop of 230. The spec's T = c^(d/D), d the path
  through the slab, through the same display transform gives 56,164,219 at the view's edge; the default route (the tint)
  drew 78,168,219 (red 22 levels high, 1x and 4x, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, RTX A6000).
- **Cause:** `withTransmission` kept volume files on the tint, a multiply blend in the beauty pass: the display-encoded
  backdrop times the encoded transmittance. Every draw on a display target writes D(L) = sRGB(PBR Neutral(L)), and a blend
  (dual-source included) gives a x dst + b; a x D(L) = D(T L) for every L holds only for a pure power curve, which PBR
  Neutral's black offset and shoulder are not, and WebGPU has no framebuffer fetch. So no shader or blend change makes the
  tint exact on a display target.
- **Fix:** volume files take the screen-transmission pass by default, which reads the scene copy decoded to linear light
  (exact to 1 level on the slab, native and --compat, 1x and 4x). Its volume path is now the tint's refracted chord through
  the slab, thickness x det(M) / |cof(M) r . n| in world units (`margoVolumeChord`, transmission.ts), in place of the
  thickness times the mean axis scale: on the slab the plain thickness missed the chord by 3 levels at the view's edge, and
  against Cycles on AttenuationTest the chord beat the thickness and the back-face depth phase on every row (docs/limits.md).
  `transmission: false` keeps the tint, exact on an HDR target only (limit in docs/limits.md).
- **Regression:** the `slab-default` and `slab-pass` cases gate worst <= 1 level against the spec with the per-pixel chord;
  `slab-tint` is measured into the report. Volume and IOR proof budgets re-recorded (tests/reference-rendering.test.js).
- **Sources:** KHR_materials_volume (Khronos 2021: T = c^(x/d), rasterizers estimate x from thickness); Khronos PBR
  Neutral tone mapper (2024); W3C WebGPU and WGSL specifications (blend state, dual_source_blending); Porter and Duff 1984,
  "Compositing Digital Images" (blending is linear in the destination); Wyman 2005, "An Approximate Image-Space Approach
  for Interactive Refraction" (the d_V back-face distance measured and not landed).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: DOF, TAA and SceneFade lost the alpha of a transparent canvas (KB-ALPHA-TEMPORAL1, dof, taa, post)

- **Repro:** on a `TransparentCanvas`, TAA wrote alpha 1 (an opaque black page behind the scene); DOF kept the sharp pixel's alpha under blurred colour and encoded premultiplied colour for display; SceneFade drew the snapshot's colour with the fade weight as alpha, so empty pixels darkened to half-opaque black.
- **Cause:** each filter handled three channels. TAA's history, DOF's gathers and SceneFade's blend had no coverage to filter, and TAA and DOF decoded or encoded premultiplied colour as if it were straight.
- **Fixed:** premultiplied linear colour throughout (Porter and Duff 1984), alpha filtered with colour's weights: `packages/taa/src/alpha.ts` (TAAUpscale's opaque alpha, the same fault, included), `packages/dof/src/alpha.ts`, a constant-weight dissolve in `packages/post/src/scene-fade.ts`. TAA's `Sharpen` leaves coverage edges unsharpened (sharpening colour alone moved an edge pixel 1.7 of 255). An opaque canvas keeps its shaders. Regression: `packages/taa/test/alpha-browser.mjs`, `packages/dof/tests/gpu/alpha-check.mjs`, `packages/post/test/scene-fade-alpha-browser.mjs` and `alpha-rim-browser.mjs`, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: water, caustics and lens-drop composites drew a light rim on a transparent canvas (KB-WATER-ALPHARIM1; water, post, weather)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs`: a box on a `TransparentCanvas` with `Underwater` alone put
  silhouette pixels 37.5 of 255 above the face colour at their coverage, `LensDrops` 31.5 (no effect: 0.7). The same
  code shape is in `ParticleLiquid`, water's `Caustics` and post's `SurfaceCaustics`.
- **Cause:** the display curve was applied to premultiplied colour (`vec4f(toDisplay(c),a)`); KB-POST-ALPHARIM1 fixed
  that in post's other effects and left these.
- **Fix:** each builds its pipeline through `displayFor` (`packages/shared/straight-display.js`) and keys it on the
  canvas mark; an opaque canvas keeps its shaders byte for byte. All five read 0.7 of 255 on WebGPU and the WebGL2
  layer (RTX A6000). Entry sizes: water/caustics 6,395 to 6,703 B, water/underwater 9,071 to 9,366 B, weather/lens
  4,075 to 4,398 B gzip.
- **Left then, fixed since:** liquid and underwater fog over empty pixels (KB-WATER-LIQUIDALPHA1).
- **Regression:** the GPU test above and `packages/post/test/straight-display.test.js` "every display shader that keeps
  a sampled alpha is built through displayFor, in every package".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the aftermath shot shimmered 0.61 percent at mid, all of it the crest conifers' parallax against the sky (KB-LOOK-TV-SHIMMER3, look check; fixed by TAA, KB-SCENES-TVTAA1)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-aftermath.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out <folder>`
  (RTX A6000, WebGPU; supersample 2, 8 subframes): mid shimmerMoving 0.607 percent (bound 0.5), the shot's one failing
  bar; the same before and after KB-SKY-FIREDAY1 and KB-SKY-HAZEGLOW1.
- **Measured (sh2-occ split of the mid probe):** 49.3 percent of the off pixels are surfaces the next frame covers or
  uncovers, 49.2 percent are within 3 px of a depth edge, 1.3 percent other, none in the sky; every one lies on the
  ridge-line conifers' tips against the sky (`.lane` map in the lane B handoff 50). Scatter and biome causes ruled out
  on these frames: no off pixel inside a tree mass (a hard LOD switch, `lodFade: 0` in biomes, or sway would show
  there), and the silhouettes are already antialiased by the shot's supersampling. A warp by camera motion cannot
  match a surface the next frame shows for the first time, as KB-LOOK-TV-SHIMMER2 found for rail-line.
- **Next:** a ruling on the check (leave out pixels the next frame occludes or disoccludes, as optical-flow benchmarks
  do) or on the shot. A TAA change (lane A) would need history rejected where the reprojected depth disagrees, a
  neighbourhood clamp in YCoCg (Karis 2014; variance clipping, Salvi 2016) so thin dark tips against a bright sky
  neither ghost nor crawl, and motion vectors for the plants' sway; none of it lowers the disocclusion share the
  check counts. The bound stays 0.5.
- **Accepted 2026-11-27 (manager's ruling, lane B landing):** main 0.581 to 0.607 with the sky in engine units
  (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1, KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1). Per class, percent of the frame, main to landing: occluded 0.22 to 0.30, depth
  edges 0.30 to 0.30, sky 0.05 to 0.00, other 0.02 to 0.01. Main's sky behind the crest read luma 158 (washed out, the
  defect those fixes remove) over ground 28; the landing's 77 over 45 shows the tips. Bound unchanged.
- **With TAA (KB-SCENES-TVTAA1), measured 2026-11-27:** once the shot loaded again (KB-SCENES-BURNTSLOW1), the same
  command gives shimmerMoving 0.092 early and 0.300 mid (were 0.253 and 0.607), inside the 0.5 bound, and every other
  aftermath bar passes (chromaSmear 0.115 and 0.098 to 0.033 and 0.014, speckle mid 0.48 to 0 ppm, shadowTint 6.15 and
  6.27 b* unchanged). The shot has no failing bar left; the bound stays 0.5.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a far ridge the haze hid fully took the haze's fire glow, the sky over it the smoke layer's, two laws for one light, so the ridge stood 6 codes lighter (KB-SKY-HAZEGLOW1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-valley-aerial.json --once --seconds 1.1
  --out <folder>` (RTX A6000, WebGPU) with KB-SKY-FIREDAY1 in: look bar mid banding 0.227 percent (bound 0.2; 0.0087
  before FIREDAY1). The banded pixels were not 8-bit steps but one edge: at x 1176 of the 1920 x 1080 mid probe the sky
  read (148, 118, 81) down to row 266 and the fully hazed far ridge (154, 121, 82) from row 267, both flat over 50 rows
  (the sky's low rays beyond `fireSight` take one point a column, the far ridge the fog's saturated colour), so the
  banding rule (two flat runs of 6 or more with a 1.5 to 12 step) counted the ridge line. Before FIREDAY1 the same edge
  was 23 codes (131 over 154), over the rule's 12, so it was not counted.
- **Cause:** the fog draws a far ground as the sky's radiance toward it (KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1) plus its fires' glow on
  the haze (`fog.fireSpots`, `fireHaze`: the mean of the falloff along the ground path to 2 / density, in the haze's
  colour), while the sky's rays over it took only the layer's glow (`atmosphere.fireSpots`, `fireLayer`: the falloff
  at the one point where the ray meets the lit height, no farther across than `fireSight`, in the layer's colour). A
  ray just over the ridge crosses the same haze as the ray to it, so the two must meet (Koschmieder 1924); they
  differed by the two laws, the two colours (about 2.2 : 1 here) and the two reaches (`fireSight` 1142 m, the fog's
  path 1978 m). Ruled out: 8-bit plateaus in the sky (the step is a depth edge, `steps.mjs` map), a coarse lookup.
- **Fix:** one law for one light. The sky draws the haze's glow toward each of its own rays (`fireSky` in
  `fire-spots.ts`): the layer's glow seen through the haze under it, t of it, and the haze's own glow in front, 1 - t,
  by the fog's own closed form (`fireTrackWgsl`, which the fog now compiles from the same source, its WGSL text
  unchanged) along the ray's ground path to the fog's path end, t the low layer's transmittance along the ray (as
  `lowLayer` sees the night through it); a slab's airlight in front of what is behind it (Sun, Ramamoorthi, Narasimhan
  and Nayar, SIGGRAPH 2005). The look block carries the fog's spots in sky units (floats 144 to 207, `LOOK_FLOATS` 144
  to 208; `writeHazeFires` divides out the exposure and picture scale the fog adds them after) and `VolumetricClouds`
  takes the same in front through their veil (`Clouds` floats 168 to 231, `CLOUD_FLOATS` 168 to 232). Without haze
  spots the sky draws the layer's glow as before. After (same shot): mid banding 0.0017 percent, early 0.0009, the
  ridge line at x 1176 154, 121, 82 on both sides; against main no failing bar of valley-aerial, ridge-smoke or
  rail-line is worse.
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/look-check.html` with `features-check.mjs look` (`hazeGlow`: the same
  pixels, 0.4 to 9 degrees up, over the sky and over a plane 50 km out in exp2 fog, a fire 1.5 km ahead: worst
  relative difference 0 with the fix, 0.52 without, on WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1), `packages/sky/test/look.test.js`
  and `packages/sky/test/volumetric-clouds.test.js` ("the haze's fire glow is in front of ...").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: by day a burning valley's smoke layer took none of its fires' light while the haze under it did, so every far ridge was lighter than the sky over it (KB-SKY-FIREDAY1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=ridge --out=<folder>` (RTX A6000,
  WebGPU, 640 x 360) with KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1, KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1 and KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1 in: the fully hazed far ridge
  read (153, 120, 81) under a sky of (131, 108, 76) right above it, the ridge 23, 12 and 4 codes lighter than the sky
  (main: 121 codes darker, the dark cut-out those fixes removed). Koschmieder (1924) wants a fully hazed far ground to
  meet the horizon sky.
- **Cause:** the look's `lowLayer` added the fires' light on the layer (`atmosphere.fireSpots`, `fireLayer`) by the
  night's share (`frame.sun.w`) alone, like the layer's even glow; but the day sky holds only the even glow (`air3` in
  `daySky`), so by day the spots were drawn nowhere in the sky, while the sky fog adds the same fires' light to the haze
  (`fog.fireSpots`, `fireHaze`) at every hour. The excess in the haze had the spots' own colour ratio (about 2.4 : 1 :
  0.26). Ruled out: the cloud deck (this scene's sky has no `clouds` option, and with its `VolumetricClouds` disposed
  the sky above the ridge read the same 131, 108, 76).
- **Fix:** `lowLayer` adds `fireLayer` at every hour (the even glow keeps its night share, as the day sky has its own),
  and `VolumetricClouds`, which stand above the layer, take the same fires' light in front through their veil
  (`writeVeil` writes `atmosphere.fireSpots` and `fireSight` into floats 104 to 167 of the `Clouds` uniform, in the
  dome's sky units), so a cumulus over the pall is not a dark blot on it. Both draw one WGSL (`fireLayerWgsl` in
  `fire-spots.ts`). After, same still: the ridge (154, 120, 80) under a sky of (150, 119, 81), 4, 1 and -1 codes.
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/look-check.html` with `features-check.mjs look` (a fire spot on the layer
  must raise the day frame in the fire's colour; without the fix it is [0, 0, 0]), `packages/sky/test/look.test.js`,
  `packages/sky/test/volumetric-clouds.test.js` ("the fires' light on the layer is in front of the clouds").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the sky settings table never wrote fog.scaleHeight or fog.base (KB-SKY-FOGROWS1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** `applySkySettings({sky}, {'fog.scaleHeight': 400, 'fog.base': 80})` on a sky with `fog` left
  both unset; `node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs settings` stopped at "fog.scaleHeight = 3000 changes the
  frame" (0 pixels), after "atmosphere.layerTransmittance" (by day it leaves the frame exact by design, KB-SKY-NIGHTPALL1)
  and "atmosphere.fireSight" (it reaches only `atmosphere.fireSpots`, which has no row).
- **Cause:** `applySkySettings` copied the fog part through a hand-kept list of five keys (density, start, height,
  falloff, color); the scaleHeight and base rows added with the height falloff were never in it.
- **Fix:** the keys come from the fog rows themselves (`FOG_KEYS`). The GPU check gives layerTransmittance a night
  sun, base a height falloff and scaleHeight 20 m (the pillars' height), and leaves out fireSight (look.test.js proves
  it). With that the check passed every fog row and stopped at "look.zenithStrength = 0.65 changes the frame" (max 1
  level, 0 pixels). That row passes on main (677 pixels): KB-SKY-SANDGREY1 draws the sky in the engine light's units,
  and under the page's sun of 1 the frame metered a displayed log-average luminance of 0.018 (main 0.30), so a tint at
  the same luminance moved no pixel by 2 levels. The check's base (and the KB-SKY-NU-EDGE1 glow frame) now takes
  `tonemap.exposure` 3, which meters it at 0.29; no bound changed. The whole settings check passes on WebGPU and
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (121 rows move the frame; glow slope 0.91 a degree, bound 2.5).
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/settings.test.js` ("values land on the options they name"; fails with the
  five-key list).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: every ray below the horizon took the horizon's haze, so a fully hazed far ground was one flat colour (KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1, sky and weather)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley `ridge-smoke` shot (`--once --seconds 1.1`, RTX A6000, WebGPU) with
  KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1 in: the far ground past `BiomeView`'s 4 km world edge, all haze, read nearly one code, (124, 82,
  32), down the whole lower left, and the look check's early flat rose to 12.9 percent (bound 5).
  `packages/sky/test/fog-below-check.html` shows it alone: a ground 1 km under the eye hidden fully by haze is the same
  colour down the middle column to 0 parts in 10^3.
- **Cause:** the sky fog takes the sky's radiance toward each ray with the ray's y clamped to 0.0001
  (`packages/sky/src/fog.ts`), so every ray below the horizon reads the horizon in its own azimuth. A long path's
  in-scatter is the haze's own light along the actual ray (S. Hillaire, "A Scalable and Production Ready Sky and
  Atmosphere Rendering Technique", EGSR 2020, https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.14050: the aerial-perspective volume
  integrates in-scatter along each camera ray; E. Bruneton and F. Neyret, "Precomputed Atmospheric Scattering", EGSR
  2008, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8659.2008.01245.x: the in-scatter to a ground point is S(x, v) - T(x, x0) S(x0,
  v) for the ray's own v below the horizon; A. J. Preetham, P. Shirley and B. Smits, SIGGRAPH 1999,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/311535.311545: aerial perspective L0 Fex + Lin along the view ray). A ray going down meets
  haze deeper in the layer, lit by less of the light from above: in an absorbing haze the diffuse light falls as e^(-k
  tau) with the vertical optical depth tau (the two-stream diffusion mode, W. E. Meador and W. R. Weaver, J. Atmos.
  Sci. 37, 630-643, 1980; H. C. van de Hulst, "Multiple Light Scattering", 1980), so the far ground seen steeper is
  darker, and redder in smoke, whose blue is absorbed faster.
- **Fix:** sky `fog.lightDecay` (k per channel, default [0, 0, 0]): a ray at sine of elevation -d and optical depth x
  takes the fog's colour times (1 - e^(-x (1 + c))) / ((1 + c) (1 - e^(-x))), c = k d, the exact in-scatter of a layer
  the same in every horizontal direction, whatever its height profile, since the vertical optical depth to a point is d
  times the ray's (CPU mirror `fogBelowLight`). Rays at or above the horizon are unchanged. `WeatherDrive` writes k
  from its dust, smoke, ash and spray (`hazeLightDecay`: their albedos and asymmetries mixed by extinction with the
  clean rest of the air) while they colour the fog, and gives back what the fog had when they leave. Not covered: the
  change of the phase angle to the sun between the horizon and the actual ray, and shadows in the air (cloud and smoke
  column shadows).
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/fog-below-check.mjs` (WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1: the hazed ground's ratio
  against no decay is the CPU mirror's to 8.4e-4; without the shader term it is off by 0.39),
  `packages/weather/tests/haze-below.test.js`, `packages/sky/test/fog-height-falloff.test.js` (`fogBelowLight`).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: under a smoke pall a fully hazed ridge ended at a colour of its own, not at the sky above it (KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1, weather)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley `ridge-smoke` shot (`tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-ridge-smoke.json`, `--once
  --seconds 1.1`, RTX A6000, WebGPU) with KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1 in: the far ridge on the left, all haze, read one flat
  (119, 73, 10) against the sky right above it at (98, 66, 24), a hard 8.7-code edge between two flat areas. The look
  check counted it as banding: early 0.81 percent (bound 0.2), up from 0. The output's 8-bit encode was not the cause:
  the gradients beside it step one code at a time under the shot tool's blue-noise dither. The "ridge" is the far
  ground `BiomeView` draws past the world's 4 km edge (in neither the shot page's geometry nor its depth mask).
- **Cause:** while smoke, ash or spray was most of the air, `WeatherDrive.tintFog` wrote `sky.fog.color`, the haze's
  diffusion colour times the light on it. A set colour replaces the fog's default, the sky's own radiance toward each
  ray, and the sky draws the same load its own way (its glow `scatteredLight` and dimmed `sunColor`, KB-AIR-SKYLIGHT1).
  So the two models of one airlight disagreed, and a path long enough ended at the drive's colour, not at the horizon
  sky behind it, which it must (Koschmieder 1924; the aerial perspective of A. J. Preetham, P. Shirley and B. Smits,
  "A Practical Analytic Model for Daylight", SIGGRAPH 1999, https://doi.org/10.1145/311535.311545, where the inscatter
  of a long path tends to the sky's radiance in that direction).
- **Fix:** when the sky draws the whole load (an atmosphere the drive writes, or a sky with a look or air controls,
  whose glow and sun colour are not held) and no dust is in it, `tintFog` takes the set colour off for the load's
  time, so the fog takes the sky's radiance toward each ray; the colour it had comes back after. Dust, which the sky
  does not draw, and a sky that does not draw the load keep the haze's own colour. The fires' haze spots still add on
  top (`packages/weather/src/drive.ts`, `drawsLoad`).
- **After:** the same shot reads early banding 0 percent, mid banding 0.037 percent (0.151 with KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1 alone),
  mid flat 6.20 percent (7.09 before the sky work, 7.21 with it). Rail-line and valley-aerial improve on every bar but
  rail-line's `shadowTint`, -5.3878 to -5.3955 b* early and -2.5917 to -2.6043 mid (bound 0.09 up).
- **Early flat, settled by KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1.** With this fix alone it read 12.9 percent in 8 bits (11.3 before the sky work, 8.55 with
  KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1 alone). On the shot tool's float frame before its dither (the same 65 x 65 windows of identical
  pixels, frame 9) it is 10.06 percent before and 11.66 percent after, mid (frame 30) 5.82 and 4.88: the change itself
  makes the far ground flatter, not the 8-bit encode. The far ground is all haze in both: before, its colour fell on two
  codes, (96, 58, 4) and (95, 57, 4); after, nearly all of it on one, (124, 82, 32). Why a fully hazed far ground is
  one colour at all was the haze's light not varying with the ray below the horizon, fixed as KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1. With
  all of the sky work (and KB-SKY-FIREDAY1) the shot reads early flat 7.29 percent (main 11.27), mid flat 3.85 (7.09),
  banding 0 at both. The early flat left over the bound of 5 is the smoke column, flat on main too (vfx, open).
- **Rail-line `shadowTint` (accepted, 2026-11-27):** -5.3878 to -5.3955 b* early, -2.5917 to -2.6043 mid (bound 0.09
  up). The shadowed ground is unchanged (b* 22.3985 against 22.3974); the term moves because far lit ground hazes
  toward the horizon sky's b* (far lit 44.1 to 40.4, the sky just above the horizon 25.2 and 26.7), the direction
  Koschmieder's law requires. The check's bound is unchanged.
- **Regression test:** `packages/weather/tests/smoke.test.js` ("a sky that draws the load leaves the fog on its own
  radiance, gives back the colour after, and dust still tints"; fails with the colour written).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a sky that lights the scene drew its picture in its own units, too bright against the ground (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** any `Sky` with `lighting` (the `PresetScene` presets: Preetham, a sun of 5): the sky's light map
  was in the sun's units since KB-SKY-SUNUNITS1, but its backdrop, fog, reflection map and the clouds, air and shafts
  drawn over it were not, 1 / lightScale = 1.38 times too bright against the ground (Bruneton at a sun of 3 about 6
  times). On the scenes (640 x 360 or 960 x 540, RTX A6000, WebGPU, top 15 percent against bottom 25 percent of the
  frame): dune coast `killdevil-from-flat` sky (238, 239, 235), the far dunes in the fog (219, 218, 213), sand (189,
  179, 154); timber-valley ridge sky (238, 205, 167) over ground (108, 73, 30), 2.6 times its luminance; Fauld fr001
  overcast sky (232, 223, 205).
- **Cause:** the 2026-11-16 fix (51d1897352 and 3838e08512, `sunlitSky` and the default exposure balance) was reverted
  the same evening (53d30d4f55, c6e31496ae, 3050f3bcc6); KB-SKY-SUNUNITS1 then scaled the light map alone, so the
  picture kept the sky's units. Putting the old exposure balance back as it was would scale the light map twice.
- **Fix:** `Sky.pictureScale` (lightScale by day while the sky lights the scene, fading to 1 with the night blend) is
  added to the exposure float that the backdrop, environment and fog shaders read, and the light buffer's scale is
  lightScale / pictureScale; VolumetricClouds, AerialPerspective, LightShafts and TornadoCloud take it with the exposure.
  `SkyOptions.balance: false` keeps the old units; a sky that only draws a backdrop and the night are unchanged. After,
  same views: dune coast sky (232, 232, 229) with its cloud structure showing, the far dunes (195, 194, 189), the sand
  unchanged (189, 179, 154); timber-valley ridge sky (130, 108, 81) over ground (128, 89, 43); Fauld fr001 sky (214,
  205, 188), an overcast grey instead of cream. The sky's share of the light on level ground is unchanged (0.18
  Preetham, 0.06 Bruneton, `sky-light-units-check.mjs`, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer), so the map is scaled once.
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/sky.test.js` ("a sky that lights the scene draws in the engine light units,
  the light map scaled once"; fails without `pictureScale`).
- **Weak spot:** the sand under the overcast preset was already sand-coloured near the camera and does not change: what
  moves is the sky and the distant fog over it. Shot look bars (`tools/shot/cli.mjs <shot> --once --seconds 1.1`,
  before / after): rail-line `lights` 4 discs / 1 and 0 (now passing), speckle 188 and 136 / 119 and 74 ppm;
  valley-aerial shimmerMoving 0.51 / 0.42 and 0.37 percent (now passing), speckle 17.4 / 12.1 ppm; ridge-smoke early
  `flat` 11.3 / 8.55 percent. Ridge-smoke early `banding` 0 / 0.81 percent (bound 0.2) and mid `flat` 7.09 / 7.21
  percent with this fix alone; with KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1, KB-SKY-HAZEBELOW1 and KB-SKY-FIREDAY1 banding 0 at both and mid
  flat 3.85.

### Open 2026-11-27: the shot tool's 8-bit encode leaves a colour on an exact code without dither (KB-SHOT-DITHERMOD1, tools/shot; held: needs its own plan)

- **Repro:** `tools/shot/pixels.js` `resolveFrame` adds a blue-noise dither of (rank + 0.5) / 4096 - 0.5, inside
  plus or minus half a level (rectangular), before rounding to 8 bits. timber-valley `ridge-smoke`, `--once --seconds
  1.1` (RTX A6000, WebGPU), early probe (frame 9), the look check's flat (65 x 65 windows of identical pixels) on the
  float frame before the dither and on the 8-bit frame after it: 10.06 against 11.27 percent at commit cb2603fc5c, and
  11.66 against 12.95 percent with the sky and haze work (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1, KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1).
- **Cause:** the canvas is 8-bit, so a constant area reaches the encode on an exact code (55 percent of the float values
  of a valley-aerial frame lie within 0.001 of one), and a rectangular dither of one level's width moves a value
  within 1/8192 of a code in no pixel: the noise there is none, beside full noise half a level away. That is the noise
  modulation of rectangular dither; a triangular dither of two levels' width makes the error's power the same for every
  value (S. P. Lipshitz, R. A. Wannamaker and J. Vanderkooy, "Quantization and Dither: A Theoretical Survey", J. Audio
  Eng. Soc. 40(5), 1992; R. A. Wannamaker, S. P. Lipshitz, J. Vanderkooy and J. N. Wright, "A Theory of Nonsubtractive
  Dither", IEEE Trans. Signal Process. 48(2), 2000, https://doi.org/10.1109/78.823966). So how many pixels of a flat area
  the look checks count depends on where its colour falls between two codes.
- **Held:** a triangular dither changes what every look bar sees, and the flat check would need a redesign that keeps it
  exactly as strict; that needs its own plan (manager, 2026-11-27).
- **Seen 2026-11-27 (lane B, KB-SKY-HAZEGLOW1):** ridge-smoke early flat 7.29 to 7.60 percent (main 11.27): the whole
  rise is in the top-left sky (grid cells 150 to 3753 and 3187 to 5249 pixels), where the haze's fire glow leaves the
  sky within one code over about 250 rows (124, 82, 32 to 33); the smoke column's cells did not change.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a fire's burn-out worked out every spent cell's spread again each step (KB-VFX-BURNOUTWORK1, vfx)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley `fire: 'burnt'` (`burnOut`, smoke-day weather, seed 1910): the aftermath shot's
  build ran past its time limit, about 11 minutes on the film's 4 m grid. Work counted on the 8 m grid
  (`.lane/burn/count.mjs 8` in lane B's worktree): 471,341 steps of 0.5 s to the fire going out at 237,470.5 s,
  760.8 million cell visits, 754.3 million of them (99.1 percent) cells past their flames that only carry the front
  on to the neighbours it has not reached yet (a slow backing or flanking fire takes days to reach some).
- **Cause:** each visit worked out the cell's wind, Rothermel behaviour, canopy and crown fire again, though none of
  their inputs change while the wind, the fuel moistures and the step hold (the fuel map, slopes and stands are fixed
  when the front is made).
- **Fix:** the front keeps each carrying cell's travel a step to each neighbour, and whether the front goes on into it
  as an active crown fire, keyed on the wind, the four moistures, the wind reduction, the foliar moisture, the crown
  switch and the step; any change works them out again, and a wind field (sampled each step) keeps nothing. A spent
  cell then only adds the kept steps, the same float sums in the same order as before, so the burn is identical
  (`packages/vfx/src/fire-front.ts`, `carry`, `carryOn`).
- **After:** the same 8 m burn-out ends at the same 237,470.5 s after the same 471,341 steps and 760,779,617 cell
  visits, with 255,310 cells burnt, and works out a cell's spread in full 6,246,622 times instead of 760.8 million (122
  times fewer; counted as wind samples).
- **Regression test:** `packages/vfx/test/fire-front-carry.test.js`: a fire with crowns, slope, spotting and two
  ignitions comes out cell for cell the same with its wind as an array (kept) and as a constant field (nothing kept),
  as does one whose wind and moisture change mid-run; the kept run samples the wind under a fifth as often (fails
