  without the fix: 18,290,011 samples both ways).

### Corrected 2026-11-27: timber-valley's fire on the film's 4 m grid looked three times slower than on the 8 m grid (KB-VFX-FIREGRID1, vfx and scenes; not a grid or fuel-map defect)

- **Report:** with the scene's fuel, ignitions and smoke-day weather (`FireFront` seed 1910), one day of fire time
  burnt 3.7 km2 on the film's 4 m grid (fuel map step 8) against 12.1 km2 on the 8 m grid (step 16).
- **Measured:** the grid is not the cause: the same fuel map (step 16) on the 4 m grid burnt 741,916 cells, 11.87 km2,
  against 12.08 km2 on the 8 m grid. Nor is the fuel map: steps 8 and 16 give the same fuel areas (FM8 6.3, FM5 4.5,
  FM10 4.5, FM1 1.3 km2) and differ only on about 1 km2 of patch edges, evenly both ways. Over seeds 1 to 4 on the 8 m
  grid the day's burnt area is bimodal on either fuel map: about 64,000 cells (4.1 km2) or about 197,000 (12.6 km2);
  seed 3 gives 196,465 cells on step 8 and 67,286 on step 16, seed 4 about 197,000 on both. The fire either throws a
  spot across one of the valley's fuel breaks into the next stand or does not (`spotting` 0.02, lognormal flights),
  and a different grid or fuel map draws a different random sequence from the same seed.
- **What it means:** a preview on the 8 m grid does not foretell the film's burn, though both are valid outcomes of the
  same fire. Script: .lane/burn/burn.mjs <cell> <weather> <days> <fuel step> with SEED in lane B's worktree.
- **Closed as not a bug (2026-11-27):** the same fuel map burns the same on the 4 m and 8 m grids, and the seed decides
  whether an ember crosses a break. The film (`timber-valley-shot.html`, `quality` film) and the preview
  (`quality: 'preview'`) both give `FireFront` the scene's `seed` (default 1910), so they share a seed. That alone
  does not make them burn the same, though: the grid and fuel map change how many draws each step takes from it, which
  is how one seed burnt 3.7 km2 on one grid and 12.1 km2 on the other above.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: ambient occlusion drew a fine pattern over distant flat sand (KB-POST-GTAOFAR1, post; was KB-WATER-FARGRID-KH1's sand half)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --shots=<file> --out=<folder>`
  with the query `cam=880,30,-450&aim=600,3,300&fov=35`: the sand some hundreds of metres out carried one-pixel rows
  and a checker. With `&occlusion=0` it was gone: the mean second difference between pixel rows over (500, 560) to
  (760, 700) fell from 11.5 to 0.55 (RTX A6000, WebGPU).
- **Cause:** the AO blur (`packages/post/src/shaders.ts` `blurShader`) weighed each tap by its depth against the
  centre's, with sigma 0.1 x radius. Far ground at a grazing angle has rows metres apart in depth, so the vertical pass
  rejected every tap and the 4 x 4 sample pattern stayed.
- **Fix:** the depth weight compares a tap with the depth the centre's own plane has there: inverse view depth is
  affine across a plane in screen space (view depth itself for an orthographic view, flag `settings.w` from
  `ssao.ts`), predicted from the centre and its nearer neighbour along the blur axis. The dune view's rows metric is
  11.55 to 0.56 (no AO 0.50). Creases now lose 4.7 percent of their total darkness to the blur, against 1.3 before: an
  accepted difference in [limits.md](limits.md) (GTAO and SSAO blur row).
- **Regression:** `packages/post/test/gtao-far-browser.mjs` (both backends): row-to-row change 0.0709 and 0.0619
  before, 0.0311 and 0.0276 after, bound 0.045. `gtao-sky-browser.mjs` (both backends) checks the crease against a CPU
  replica of both blur passes (1.2e-6), its outer rows, its minimum and its total darkness; `ssao.test.js` pins the
  orthographic flag.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: timber-valley's cumulus showed as flat white blobs on the mountain slopes (KB-SKY-CLOUDBLOB1; scenes, sky docs)

- **Repro:** timber-valley under cover 0.2 to 0.3, from the valley floor toward the ridges: a smooth white patch lies
  against the slopes below the ridge line, with no shape or shading.
- **Cause:** a cloud layer's `bottom` and `top` are metres over world y = 0 (the option's text said "above the
  ground"). The scene left them to the cumulus type's 1,000 to 2,500 m on a floor 870 m up with ridges to about 1,900 m,
  so the layer ran through the mountains and only its thin foot showed over the floor.
- **Fix:** the scene passes `bottom` and `top` 2.5 and 4 km over the valley's floor (the lifting condensation level of
  a dry August afternoon, Lawrence 2005), and the `VolumetricCloudOptions.bottom` text says what it is measured from.
  The same views now show rounded cumulus with shaded bases over the ridges (RTX A6000, WebGPU).
- **And:** applying a look family then deleted those heights and the cloud type, since the sky's apply writes every
  row it is not given back to its default; `applyLookFamily` now keeps the layer's `type`, `coverage`, `bottom`, `top`
  and `density` (`packages/scenes/test/look-family-parts.test.js`).
- **Regression test:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs` (the cloud base stands over the highest
  ground).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: timber-valley's animated-feature look could not reach its ground or its creek (KB-BIOMES-LOOKFAMILY1; biomes, scenes)

- **Repro:** the scene's default `look: 'animatedFeature'` changed the sky and fire only, and giving the family the
  view's water threw "Water settings windSpeed, windDirection and fetch need a Water made without options.waves".
- **Cause:** a `BiomeView` built every water, a creek included, with the ocean's two fixed swell trains (`SEA`), and a
  `Water` with fixed trains takes no wind, so no water look with a wind could be applied to it; a `wind` the caller gave
  was ignored for the same reason. The ground materials already had their target (`applyLookFamily`'s `biomes`), and
  the scene passed neither.
- **Fix:** on a landlocked world, or with a `wind`, the view's water takes `SEA` without the swell, under that wind (2
  m/s over 100 m by default); a world the sea reaches keeps the swell. The scene passes the family to the ground and the
  water. No new option.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/biomes/tests/view-sea-horizon.test.js` (the family applies to a landlocked view's
  water; threw before) and `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs` (the creek's water takes the family's
  colour).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: timber-valley's creek showed as stray slabs of water on a flat floor from views along the valley (KB-BIOMES-RIVERSTEP1, near half; scenes)

- **Repro:** `@margoengine/scenes/timber-valley`, view `creek` after attaching with the camera near the world's centre:
  no channel in the ground, and one flat slab of water lying on the floor some way off (blue over red 0.39 in the water
  ahead of the bank).
- **Cause:** since 9176e5cdd4 a `BiomeView` anchors its clipmap rings where the camera stood at attach. The scene's
  views lie up to 2 km from there, so the creek (14 m wide) drew on 32 m cells that missed its channel; the water showed
  only where a vertex happened to fall in it.
- **Fix:** the scene passes `clipmap: { anchor: 'camera' }`, so the fine rings follow the camera
  (`packages/scenes/src/timber-valley.ts`). The creek now reads as one channel with its banks (blue over red 2.73,
  RTX A6000, WebGPU).
- **Regression test:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs` (the creek bank assertion; 0.39 before,
  bound 1.3).
- **Still open:** the far half, below.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: seen from far off, a narrow creek broke into separate patches of water (KB-BIOMES-RIVERSTEP1, far half; water, biomes)

- **Repro:** the `aerial-west` view of timber-valley, or ten-thousand-trees with `water: { rivers: 'auto' }`: past a few
  hundred metres the creek was a row of separate blue patches, then only the riverbed paint. With the view's default
  fixed clipmap anchor the patches reached the camera once the flight left its start.
- **Cause:** a clipmap ring's cells grow with distance from its centre (16 and 32 m from about 500 m) past the channel's
  14 m width. The ring takes the ground at its vertices only, so the water, 0.3 m under the banks, showed where a vertex
  fell in the channel and was covered by triangles bridging the banks elsewhere.
- **Fix:** new optional entry `@margoengine/water/banks` (`WaterBanks`), attached by `BiomeView` to its river and lake
  water (`packages/biomes/src/view.ts`): each water vertex moves toward the eye along its view ray until it stands as
  high as the rings' geometric error there (slope 0.25 times twice the ring spacing less a texel, at most 2 m), which
  keeps its pixel and only brings its depth nearer, and fragments over the view's own 2 m heights at or above the surface
  are dropped, so the waterline follows the heightmap, not the rings. Near the camera, where the rings sample every
  texel, nothing changes. Sources: Losasso and Hoppe 2004 (geometry clipmaps), Strugar 2009 (CDLOD morph), Ulrich 2002
  (per-level geometric error), Lengyel 2000 (projected depth offset); see `packages/water/src/banks.ts`.
- **Regression test:** `node packages/water/test/banks.browser.mjs` and `--compat` (a 6 m channel under rings of 2 m
  cells from 300 m up: the channel's centre column showed water in 153 of 400 rows before, 400 of 400 with the banks,
  and no water pixel past its walls; WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer).
- **Note for the terrain and biomes owners:** the terrain rings and BiomeView's default anchor are unchanged; the fix
  lives in the water, which reads the terrain's heightmap and ring layout.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: past a landlocked world's edge the view showed a flat blue plane (KB-BIOMES-WORLDEDGE1; biomes)

- **Repro:** timber-valley from 2,200 m, looking past the edge: a flat blue band lies between the far mountains and the
  sky. Seen first (2026-11-17) from the `fire-line` view, before the view drew any far ground.
- **Cause:** two. Nothing drew ground past the edge (fixed earlier by `BiomeView`'s `horizon` far ground); and a view
  with rivers always gave its water the sea's horizon, at sea level, which showed past the end of the far ground.
- **Fix:** the water reaches to the horizon only where an edge of the world stands at or below sea level
  (`packages/biomes/src/view.ts`).
- **Regression test:** `packages/biomes/tests/view-sea-horizon.test.js` (a landlocked valley's water has no horizon, a
  coast's has).
- **Weak spot left:** the far ground takes each corner's materials from the nearest edge texel, so it draws long
  smeared streaks running outward from the edge (KB-BIOMES-HORIZONSTREAK1, fixed).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the far ground past a world's edge drew long streaks (KB-BIOMES-HORIZONSTREAK1, biomes)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley, camera at (-1500, 1400, 0) looking at (-3200, 900, 300): bands of material and
  light ran straight outward from the world's edge to the horizon.
- **Cause:** every far corner took its nearest edge texel: `BiomeView`'s horizon terrain copied its material weights
  (`#horizonTerrain`) and `horizonHeights` carried its height out until the mountains took over, so one edge texel's
  material ran the whole 12 km and its relief ran out as a ridge (a 200 m edge spike stood 169 m over its side 128 m
  out).
- **Fix:** each far corner takes the mean of a stretch of edge round its nearest texel, an eighth of its distance wide
  each way (`HORIZON_SPREAD`, `horizonEdgeMean` on prefix sums round the edge loop), for its height and its material
  weights, so the edge blurs out with distance, and the weights give way to the whole edge's mean over the ramp the
  heights give way to the mountains in (`blend`; `packages/biomes/src/horizon.ts`, `view.ts`). A valley leaving the
  world still carries on near the edge (the existing test holds it within 10 m 64 m out). On the repro view the far
  ground is now one even ground past the ramp; within about a kilometre of the edge the edge's own broad patches still
  carry on as soft wedges, as the edge's continuation is meant to (RTX A6000, WebGPU, 960 x 540).
- **Regression test:** `packages/biomes/tests/horizon.test.js` (one odd edge texel does not run out to the horizon as a
  streak; `horizonEdgeMean` round the loop).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: volumetric clouds drew full white through a smoke pall (KB-SKY-PALLCLOUD1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley `weather=smoke&fire=none&date=1910-08-22&hour=10`, view `aftermath`: a cumulus low
  on the left was the brightest thing in the frame, code (251, 246, 250) against the pall's (206, 155, 134).
- **Cause:** the day sky takes the smoke layer through `atmosphere.sunColor` and `scatteredLight`, and the night sky
  sees what is above the layer through `layerTransmittance`; `VolumetricClouds` composite over the sky after it and
  read none of the three, so they drew as on a clear day.
- **Fix:** the clouds stand above the layer and are seen through it: their light times `layerTransmittance` to the
  power 1 / sin e along each ray (floored at 3 degrees, as the sky's own), times the sky's `sunIntensity`, plus the
  layer's glow (`scatteredLight` in sky units, through the new `Sky.zenithSun`) over their opacity, in the picture and
  both deck maps (`packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`, `writeVeil`). The same cloud now draws (221, 151, 69), a
  little darker than the sky beside it (RTX A6000, WebGPU, 960 x 540).
- **Regression test:** `packages/sky/test/volumetric-clouds.test.js` (a low haze layer in the sky dims and veils the
  clouds seen through it).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the WebGL2 layer refused targets with write mask 0 and no fragment output (KB-COMPAT-SILENTTARGET1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/silent-targets-browser.mjs`: a three-target pass with depth
  writes and an async pipeline whose fragment writes only location 0, targets 1 and 2 with write mask 0 (valid WebGPU);
  on ANGLE Direct3D 11 the warm draw and every draw raised GL_INVALID_OPERATION "Active draw buffers with missing
  fragment shader outputs", reported as an internal GPU error. Found by `ssr.add(raw)` with a depth-only raw mesh.
- **Cause:** the layer kept every target's draw buffer on (`CompatRenderPipeline`, `CompatProgram.warmed` in
  `packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts`); WebGL2 checks the active draw buffers against the program's outputs
  whatever the colour mask.
- **Fix:** a target with write mask 0 has its draw buffer off for the pipeline's draws (one split group of the written
  targets, through the existing split path) and in the warm draw.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: TAA gave instanced primitives camera motion only (KB-TAA-INSTMOTION1, taa, gltf)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/taa/test/instance-velocity-browser.mjs`: two Box.glb instances (gltf/pbr
  `PBRInstances`) under a still node and camera, the right one moving; no pixel of either box was reached by TAA's
  object velocity pass, so the moving instance held the camera's motion (0) and smeared in history.
- **Cause:** `drawMotion` (`packages/taa/src/index.ts`) returned for any primitive with `instances`: TAA had no
  previous instance transforms.
- **Fix:** TAA keeps a GPU copy of each drawn instance buffer's rows, taken after every velocity pass, and the velocity
  program (`instancedVelocity`, `src/shader.ts`) moves each vertex by node x instance matrix now and then (reverse
  reprojection per instance: Nehab et al. 2007; Yang, Liu and Salvi 2020, section 4.1). gltf/pbr's instance buffer
  gains `COPY_SRC`. Copies of buffers no longer drawn are freed.
- **Regression:** the same check: every moving-box pixel carries 0.6 to 1.4 times its median motion, no standing-box
  pixel moves (WebGPU; in `test:gpu`). It fails on the parent (no box pixel reached).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: on the WebGL2 layer some silhouette pixels of a moving mesh kept part of the camera's motion (KB-TAA-COMPATEDGE1, taa, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `node packages/taa/test/instance-velocity-browser.mjs --compat`: 25 of 10,812 pixels of the moving box
  (its right edge, x 475 and 476, and a few on its lower left edge) read 0.4 to 0.5 times the box's motion while their
  expected depth is the box's own (about 0.0159), so none of their four samples is sky. The same 25 pixels show with
  the two boxes as plain gltf/pbr meshes moved by their nodes (a control run), so instancing is not the cause; WebGPU
  gives every pixel its full motion.
- **Cause (proven 2026-11-27, lane A, on 24ce05b217):** coverage, not the 'equal' test. These are silhouette pixels
  where the box covers 2 of the 4 samples and the sky the rest. The WebGL2 layer reads every sample of a 4x texture
  from its blit-resolved copy (GLSL ES 3.00 has no sampler2DMS), so TAA's motion resolve (`src/index.ts`,
  `motionResolve`) cannot pick the nearest sample and takes the mean of the four. The camera pass reads one resolved
  depth per pixel and broadcasts one value to all four samples; where the depth resolve kept a box sample, that value
  is the box's reprojected depth with the camera's motion (0), not `skySample`. The mean then halves the motion and
  passes the expected-depth filter. Evidence on an RTX A6000 (patched built copy of the object pass, the same 25
  pixels each time): depth test 'equal' or 'greater-equal' with cull 'none': 10,787 of 10,812 pixels right; cull
  'back' with depth 'always': still 10,787, so no front-facing fragment reaches the missing samples; cull 'front'
  with 'always' (back faces cover them): 10,808; the same scene at `antialias: false` (1 sample): 10,819 of 10,819
  right. WebGPU reads single samples, and its resolve takes the box's sample.
- **Fix (2026-11-27, lane A, approved as a bug fix):** at 4x on the WebGL2 layer only (`compatTier`), the object
  velocity draws write a coverage channel: the 4x motion target is rgba16float (4 more bytes a sample; WebGPU keeps
  rg16float and its nearest-sample resolve) and every object velocity shader writes `vec4f(velocity, 0, 1)` (TAA's own,
  `RawShaders`' and `ScatterVelocity`'s, which now follow `frame.targets`). The camera pass writes the 1x targets itself
  and the 4x ones start cleared, so their mean is c x (object, 0, 1); the resolve writes mean / c where c > 0 and keeps the
  camera's value elsewhere. That is the proposed unmixing, object = (mean - (1 - c) x camera) / c, with the camera's
  share 0 in the 4x targets, and exact for one moving surface per pixel; two moving surfaces in one pixel mix by
  coverage. Regression: `instance-velocity-browser.mjs --compat` (now in `test:gpu:compat`; 10,787 of 10,812 before,
  11,013 of 11,013 after) and `far-velocity-browser.mjs`, which now requires every box pixel within 0.6 to 1.4 times the
  median motion, not only above 0 (`--compat` before: 32,133 of 32,264 gltf pixels; after: all 32,517 in both cases, and
  all 32,512 on WebGPU).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a voxel-pathtracer unit test failed on a loaded machine; the viewport ignored the fixed band budget (KB-VPT-BANDS-LOAD1, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** `packages/voxel-pathtracer` unit suite (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) 15 times while 28 CPU
  burners and a loop of the points build ran: 2 of 7 finished runs failed "agx tone mapping is computed in the display
  shader" (`tests/tracer.test.js`) with `11 !== 3`; 12 runs beside the points build alone all passed.
- **Cause:** the viewport cuts its trace into row bands sized by `WorkPacer` from wall-clock times (`src/dispatch.ts`).
  Loaded, the fake GPU's submissions read as slow, the bands shrank, and the frame made band bind groups (the trace
  layout's 11 entries, a buffer at binding 2 too) and a band uniform buffer after the display group. The test took the
  last group with a buffer at binding 2 as the display group and compared GPU bytes the bands had changed. The fixed
  band budget `voxelTraceWork` that pins bands in tests applied to `renderImage` only, not to the viewport.
- **Fix:** both routes band through one `bandWork` (`src/tracer.ts`), so `voxelTraceWork` pins the viewport's bands as
  well; the test pins it and finds the display group by its layout.
- **Regression:** `tests/tracer.test.js` "agx tone mapping ... (forced bands)": 8-row bands, as a loaded machine gives,
  must band the viewport and keep 3 display bindings and the same GPU bytes; it fails on the parent. The GPU
  determinism case (`browser-check.mjs determinism`, WebGPU and `--compat`) passes with the change.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the timber-valley aftermath drew a black frame under its smoke weather (KB-LOOK-TV-CRUSH1, KB-SKY-SMOKE-BLACK1; scenes)

- **Repro:** `@margoengine/scenes/timber-valley` with the `aftermath` preset (weather `smoke`, fire `burnt`, 22 August
  10:00). On 2026-11-17 the crush bar read 72 percent and the sky drew black. On main before this fix the sky drew a
  very dark red, the ground black, 27.5 percent of pixels at or under code 16 and crush 0.26 percent (bound 0.1 for
  `animatedFeature`).
- **Cause:** two. The sky took the sun's dimming with nothing for the light the smoke scatters down; that half was
  fixed on 2026-11-18 (`atmosphere.scatteredLight`, KB-AIR-SKYLIGHT1). The other half was the scene: its `smoke`
  weather asked for load 0.6 (1,800 micrograms of PM2.5 through a 2 km layer, optical depth 14), where the direct sun
  is 1e-6 of clear air's and the haze holds 1 percent of the red light and 0.08 percent of the green. That is dark at
  noon, not the "day under thick smoke" the setting names. `fog.ts` leaving sky pixels alone is not part of it: the sky
  takes the layer through `sunColor` and `scatteredLight`.
- **Fix:** `weatherState('smoke')` in `packages/scenes/src/timber-valley.ts` takes the load of the weather package's own
  `WEATHER_LOOKS.wildfireSmoke` (0.35: about 1.6 km, the direct sun a dim red disc, 20 percent of the red light and 8
  percent of the green in the haze). The same view now reads 0 percent crush and no pixel at or under code 16, under an
  orange-grey sky with the ridges visible (RTX A6000, WebGPU, 960 x 540).
- **Regression test:** `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley.test.js` (the smoke day is daylight; fails on 0.6).
- **Still open on this view:** the distant haze was much darker than the sky behind it (KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1, fixed), dark beaded
  trails cross the upper left at film quality (KB-VFX-DARKTRAILS1), and a cloud low on the left drew white through
  the pall (KB-SKY-PALLCLOUD1, fixed).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: under a smoke load the ground haze was far darker than the sky behind it (KB-SKY-PALLHAZE1, weather and sky)

- **Repro (before):** timber-valley `view=aftermath&weather=smoke` (load 0.35, 640 x 360, RTX A6000, WebGPU): the ridge
  on the right read code (70, 40, 1) against the sky right above it at (173, 126, 101); in the ridge view (fire on)
  the hazed ridges read (114, 79, 30) under a sky of (238, 205, 167), a flat brown cut-out. A path long enough should
  end at the sky's own horizon radiance (Koschmieder 1924).
- **Cause (measured):** the two were in different units. `WeatherDrive.tintFog` wrote `sky.fog.color` as the haze's
  colour times `hazeLight`, a share where 1 is the zenith sun's light on a white surface, and the fog pass drew a set
  colour as it is (engine radiance). The sky drew the same layer's light (`atmosphere.scatteredLight`) as the share times
  its zenith sun over pi in sky units (`look.ts`): 4 pi x 0.55 / pi = 2.2 times the fog's for Preetham, times the
  sky's exposure, and the sky itself was a further 1.4 times too bright against the ground (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1).
- **Fix:** `tintFog` multiplies the haze colour and the fog's fire spots by `Sky.zenithSun` x
  `atmosphere.sunIntensity` x 2^exposure x `Sky.pictureScale` over pi (`hazeUnits`, `packages/weather/src/drive.ts`),
  the units the sky draws its own haze in; a sky target without `zenithSun` keeps the old share. With the sky balanced
  (KB-SKY-SANDGREY1) a share of 1 is the engine sun's light on a white surface, 5 / pi under the presets. The same
  views now read: aftermath ridge (88, 52, 2) against the sky (86, 52, 31); ridge view ridges (141, 101, 49) under a
  sky of (130, 108, 81), the far ridges layered into the haze in the aerial-west view.
- **Regression test:** `packages/weather/tests/smoke.test.js` ("the fog colour under a load is in the units the sky
  draws its haze in"; fails on the share drawn as it is).
- **Weak spot (fixed by KB-SKY-HAZEHORIZON1):** the haze kept the smoke's own orange where the sky above it was greyer,
  so a ridge read as an orange band rather than vanishing into the sky's colour.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the "burnt" valley still burned, under dark beaded trails at film quality (KB-VFX-DARKTRAILS1, scenes)

- **Repro (before):** `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.html?view=aftermath&weather=smoke&fire=burnt&date=1910-08-22&hour=10&w=960&h=540`
  (film quality, 60 frames): wavy strings of dark soft blobs filled the upper left; all 12 smoke columns still carried
  2 to 66 MW after the scene's `settle(86400)`.
- **Cause:** `fire: 'burnt'` ("run until nothing burns") stopped the fire after one day of fire time, and a surface
  fire in the valley's timber litter runs on for days. Measured with the scene's fuel, ignitions and smoke-day weather:
  on the 8 m grid 188,822 of 257,138 fuelled cells burnt and 20 still burning after one day, out after about two; on
  the film's 4 m grid 233,036 of 1,034,173 burnt after one day and 625,729 after a day and a half.
- **Fix:** the scene runs the fire with `burnOut` until it goes out (at most `BURN_OUT_LIMIT`, 30 days, past which it
  throws a coded error rather than show a burning "burnt" valley) (`packages/scenes/src/timber-valley.ts`). The same
  view now shows no smoke column and no trails (RTX A6000, WebGPU); the scene's build on the film grid takes about
  11 minutes, most of it the fire. Which effect drew the trails was not traced further: they went with the columns.
- **Regression test:** `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley.test.js` (burnOut runs a fire past a day to its end and
  refuses one that never ends).
- **Weak spot:** in the smoke day's light the south wall's trees read as dark silhouettes, so this frame does not show
  whether they are charred.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: SnapshotRendering's stats lost a recording dropped before the next frame (KB-CULL-SNAPSTATS1, culling)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/culling/test/snapshot.test.js`: draw a frame that records, call `reset()` (or restore
  the device, or dispose) and read `stats`; `recorded` was one short.
- **Cause:** a recording is counted when the plugin next looks at the view, and `reset`, `onDeviceRestored` and
  `dispose` threw the bundle or the view away without looking. Found writing the entry's first unit test.
- **Fixed:** `reset` counts each view's recording before dropping it, and restore and dispose go through it.
- **Regression test:** `packages/culling/test/snapshot.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the tests gate did not count the coupling tests (KB-QUALITY-COUPLINGTESTS1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `npm run quality -- --gate=tests` on 1806536124: nine physics entries, `tissue`, `rail`, `seismic`,
  `lightning`, `strands`, `outdoor-sound`, `drainage-fog`, `vortices` and `aeolian`, read as imported by no test.
- **Cause:** `npm run verify` runs `packages/*/tests/coupling/*.test.js`, and the gate's file pattern stopped at
  `packages/*/tests/*.test.js`. The two other items were real: `@margoengine/audio/outdoor` and
  `@margoengine/culling/snapshot` had browser checks only.
- **Fixed:** the gate counts the coupling folder and its helpers; both entries have unit tests
  (`packages/audio/tests/outdoor.test.js`, `packages/culling/test/snapshot.test.js`).
- **Regression test:** `tests/quality-tests-globs.test.js` (every test folder the verify command names counts; the
  coupling case fails on the old pattern).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the lock left out gltf's lines and points peers, so the api gate crashed (KB-LOCK-GLTFPEERS1)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/package-lock-sync.test.js` or `npm run quality -- --gate=api` on a5342703e3: hygiene
  threw "package-lock.json is stale" before the gate measured anything.
- **Cause:** a5342703e3 added `@margoengine/lines` and `@margoengine/points` to gltf's package.json as optional peers
  and dev dependencies, without the lock. Behind it `site/llms-full.txt` was stale too, the next thing hygiene refuses.
- **Fixed:** the lock regenerated offline (`npm install --ignore-scripts --package-lock-only --offline`; ten lines, no
  new package or version) and the llms files rebuilt. The gate now runs through and reports its own items.
- **Regression test:** `tests/package-lock-sync.test.js` ("package-lock.json lists each workspace with the
  dependencies of its package.json" fails on the old lock).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the quality gate measured a tree another session was writing in (KB-QUALITY-CROSSTREE1)

- **Repro:** during a gate run in one lane's folder, another session's uncommitted sky edits sat in it: `sky/sun`
  read 2,462 B against a 2,379 B budget and its API read as changed, and both passed once the files were restored
  (2026-11-16).
- **Cause:** a session wrote into another lane's tree, and the gate neither said what uncommitted files it was reading
  nor noticed that they changed under it. `push:main` already refused to push a changed tracked file.
- **Fixed:** `npm run quality` lists the uncommitted files it measures and fails when one is written, added, restored
  or committed during the run, or HEAD moves (`scripts/quality/tree-watch.js`). Files that were already there and stay
  still are listed, not refused: a gate is often run on one's own uncommitted work. Regression:
  `tests/quality-tree-watch.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: some tests' random generator lost its low bits and repeated early (KB-TEST-LCG1)

- **Repro.** `seed = (seed * 1103515245 + 12345) >>> 0` from seed 3 repeats after 6,445 draws with a period of 419, so a
  test drawing many random cases from it checked the same few again. Found writing the tilemap search tests.
- **Cause.** The product passes 2^53, where a float drops the low bits that `>>> 0` or a mask keeps. 55 places in 51
  files used it. Several also took a remainder of the raw state, whose low bits repeat early in any generator modulo a
  power of two.
- **Fix.** Every product is `Math.imul(seed, 1103515245)`, a remainder by 2^31 is the mask `0x7fffffff`, and draws
  that took a remainder of the raw state shift it down first. The exporters triangle-code test now counts its codes over
  16 triangle orders: they appear in about 4 of 10 orders, and its former one order had them by chance.
  `tests/lcg-generators.test.js` checks each file that holds the multiplier for both faults. The page filed with a
  browser vendor in `docs/upstream-reports/KB1042f` stays as filed.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: sciviz progressive rendering and glTF wide strokes left the active scene's plugin, not their own (plugin scene owner (sciviz), KB-OWN-STROKES1; sciviz, gltf)

- **Repro:** a figure whose renderer is in a second scene, `new ProgressiveRendering(figure)`, the default scene active:
  the constructor's duplicate check looked at the active scene, and `dispose()` removed a `sciviz-progressive` plugin
  from the active scene and left its own registered. A glTF model with wide points or lines loaded into a second
  scene: its `gltf-lines` and `gltf-points` plugins stayed in that scene after the last model was disposed, because
  the dispose compared and removed them in the active scene. `SciRenderer.dispose` removed `sciviz:<n>` from the
  active scene when its own scene had already taken it out. `npm run hygiene` (scripts/support/plugin-scene-owner.mjs)
  found packages/gltf/src/strokes.ts on main, and listed the two sciviz calls as open.
- **Cause:** one-argument `engine.removePlugin(name)`, `engine.hasPlugin(name)` and `engine.plugins` act on the active
  scene (packages/sciviz/src/progressive.ts, packages/sciviz/src/render.ts, packages/gltf/src/strokes.ts).
- **Fix:** each removes through `engine.sceneOf(plugin)` and removes nothing once it is no longer attached; the
  progressive check runs inside `inSceneOf` with the attach. The check's OPEN list is empty; its self-test of the
  OPEN rules uses a throwaway repository.
- **Regression:** packages/sciviz/tests/scene-owner.test.js "progressive rendering joins, checks and leaves the scene
  its figure is in, not the active one", packages/gltf/test/strokes.test.js "a model loaded into a second scene takes
  its plugins out of that scene, whichever scene is active" (both fail on the old source) and
  tests/plugin-scene-owner.test.js "the two sciviz sites are fixed".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the points pixel size check was in no GPU chain (KB-POINTS-GPUPLAN1)

- **Repro.** `node --test tests/modern-extension-suite.test.js tests/parallel-check.test.js` on a829b78da's parents:
  `packages/points/tests/pixel-density-browser.mjs: browser test file(s) that nothing check:gpu-packages runs

- **Cause.** KB-POINTS-CSSPX1 added the check without naming it in the package's `test:gpu` chain, so it never ran in

- **Fix.** `packages/points/package.json` `test:gpu` runs it after the scale check.
- **Regression test:** `tests/modern-extension-suite.test.js` ("the plan runs every GPU check file, and each one left
  out says why").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: build:packages failed on main, core plus glTF was over 30 KiB (KB-BUILD-COREGLTF30K)

- **Repro.** `npm run build:packages` on 829b78dab4: every package builds, then `sizeRecords` in
  `scripts/build-modern.js` stops with `Core + glTF exceed 30 KiB gzip` (core 22,525 B + gltf 8,323 B = 30,848 B,
  128 B over). Local CI passed this step at 3b3db1b109 and failed it at 25d5368704.
- **Cause.** The two core features of 2026-11-27, snapshot rendering (4ea24d04d1, +110 B) and multi-draw (c04ed9040d,
  +46 B), raised the core-only and core + stage limits but left this third limit, which had 28 B to spare. The glTF
  figure here bundles the `@margoengine/math` helpers the root imports, so it reads higher than its entry size record
  (7,442 B).

- **Regression test:** `tests/modern-core-budget.test.js` ("core + the glTF root stay below the 30 KiB gzip gate of

- **Repro.** `node packages/decoders/scripts/test-real-textures.mjs <folder>` on a folder holding only the 34 KTX2

### Fixed 2026-11-27: materials/interior-mapping loaded the glTF material models on import (KB-INTERIOR-STATIC1)

- **Repro.** `npm run quality -- --gate=sizes --details`: the entry measured 31,075 B and carried leak items for

  plain arithmetic.

  until the caller imports it").

### Open 2026-11-27: advancing wake transmits flow through the Wigley hull (KB-SEA04-STEM1)

- **Repro.** The [Wigley comparison](../packages/physics/scripts/sea04-stem.md) drives the actual `HullSolver` and

  source gives 16.42 and 14.53 mm at the stem, against 43.84 and 39.94 mm measured. The depth-banded source
  gives 9.52 and 9.28 mm.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a closed soft body floated by its wetted area, not its displaced volume (KB-SOFT-CLOSEDBUOY1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `soft.water = {density: 1025}` and a `SoftBodyDesc.volume` ball of density 300: each particle under the water
  took the buoyancy of its share of the body's volume, so the lift followed the share of the surface under water (h / 2R
  for a sphere at draft h) where Archimedes asks for the submerged volume (h^2 (3R - h) / 4R^3); the ball floated at the
  wrong draft for every density but half the water's, and carried a flat disk's added mass.
- **Cause:** `SoftBodies.waterLoads` modelled every body as particles (a rope's segments, a cloth's faces); a closed body's
  particles are only its surface.
- **Fix:** a body that holds a volume or a gas takes the water's hydrostatic pressure on each face below the waterline,
  clipped where it crosses it (`wettedDepth`), which sums to the displaced water's weight for any shape; a sphere's added
  mass (half the displaced water); drag on upstream faces only. `body.displacedVolume()` reports it. Regression:
  `packages/physics/tests/soft-volume.test.js` ("in water a soft volume floats where Archimedes says"), held by the
  test's own clip of the mesh to |a| / g + 1e-4 at densities 300, 500 and 700.

### Open (below Margo) 2026-11-27: on ANGLE D3D11 a draw into a fresh texture is sometimes lost while the page is captured (KB-ANGLE-CAPTUREDRAW1, browser; webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node <script>` over a page that makes a 2 x 2 `Texture` from an `ImageBitmap`, a
  `Material({ map })` and a mesh, renders twice, disposes them and repeats, reading the canvas with a Playwright
  element screenshot after each cycle (RTX A6000, Edge and Chrome 158, ANGLE D3D11): one cycle in about three runs of
  ten (the 3rd to the 9th) samples the texture as black (2, 2, 2 where 155, 154, 154 is right), with no error. Native
  WebGPU is right. Without the screenshots, reading the copy back in the page instead: 0 lost cycles in 120.
- **Not Margo's GL state:** the copy is `Replayer.copyBitmap` (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts`), whose
  last draw writes the destination level. In a lost cycle that level reads (0, 0, 0, 0), its cleared value, right
  after the draw, while the source texture read just before the draw holds the bitmap, and the framebuffer, viewport,
  masks, program, units, samplers and uniforms read back with `getParameter` match a kept cycle. A trace of every
  WebGL2 call (names, objects, arguments, all deletes at the prototype, so collected objects too) is the same in lost
  and kept cycles. Byte uploads in place of the bitmap and canvas uploads are lost too, so the `ImageBitmap` path is
  not the cause.
- **Cause, below Margo:** every WebGL2 call of a Margo run, recorded with its payloads and replayed on a bare context
  with no Margo code, lost the draw in 4 of 4 replays with canvas screenshots between cycles and in 0 of 3 without.
  `docs/upstream-reports/KB-ANGLE-CAPTUREDRAW1/lost-draw.html` (raw WebGL2, the layer's calls for one copy written by
  hand) loses 6 of 120 cycles under `node docs/upstream-reports/run-page.mjs docs/upstream-reports/KB-ANGLE-CAPTUREDRAW1/lost-draw.html --browser=edge --shots=30 "--query=cycles=30&shots=1&v=bytes"`
  (`--shots` screenshots the page's canvas between steps) and 0 of 180 without captures. With a plain `texelFetch`
  fragment shader in place of the converting one it lost 0 of 180, with a uniform offset or a second sampler added 0
  of 120 and 0 of 90; the converting shader without its second sampler lost 2 of 90, without the points draw 1 of 90,
  with nothing deleted 9 of 90, with a flush after the draw 7 of 90, into an RGBA8 target 2 of 50. So the capture,
  which the GPU process runs between the page's frames, sometimes leaves the page's next draw of that shader without
  effect; the same class as "ANGLE D3D11 flipped blit left the next draws' fragment uniform blocks reading zero" below.
  Whether ANGLE's D3D11 state or the NVIDIA driver drops it is not settled; the replay needs an ANGLE report.
- **Margo:** not worked around. Nothing in the page's call stream decides which cycle loses its draw, so no change to
  the layer's calls is proven to avoid it, and a redraw or readback after the copy would only hide it. Pages that
  check pixels on the layer can read them with `readPixels` in the page instead of a screenshot. The recorder,
  replayer and failing recording stay outside the repository (lane C's `.lane/kbx-rec.js`, `kbx-replay.html`,
  `kbx-trace-fail.json`).

### Open 2026-11-27: a soft body's damped springs lose momentum to float32 rounding (KB-SOFT-F32MOMENTUM1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** with no gravity and no air drag, `SoftBodyDesc.volume(sphereGeometry(0.4, 16, 12), {density: 100})` at
  the origin, `applyImpulse([0, 3, 0])`, 120 steps of 1/60 s: the centre of mass carries 2.99758 N s, not 3 (8e-4
  lost). With `damping: 0` it carries 3.00037; moved to y = 3, where every particle's y lies in one binade [2, 4), it
  carries 3.00054 with the default damping; at y = 100 it carries 2.99177.
- **Cause:** the soft kernel (`packages/physics/soft-kernel/src/world.rs`, `solve_edge`) stores particle positions as
  absolute float32. Each damped edge correction moves its two particles by equal and opposite amounts far below a
  position's ulp; rounding keeps the move on a particle in a finer binade and drops it on one in a coarser one, so the
  pair's momentum no longer cancels; the next pass, seeing the particle unmoved, issues the same correction again, so the
  loss runs one way while the body moves. Far from the origin the integration step itself loses digits.
- **What was tried (2026-11-27):** an origin a body at its centre does not cure it, since the measured loss is at the
  world origin, where a body's own frame is the world's; what removes it is a frame in which the body's particles share
  one float exponent on each axis (at y = 3 the loss is gone). Kahan-compensated corrections in `solve_edge` double
  count, because an iterative solve reissues a lost correction (3.05 N s at y = 100). Moving the edge damping to the
  velocities (as `thread_damping` does for sheets) conserves momentum (3.00045 N s) but lets a 1 g box leave a 1 kg
  particle cloth at 8.3 m/s where an elastic bounce allows 6.6, so it is not landed. The fix is a body frame whose
  per-axis offset puts every particle in one binade, which every soft solve, contact and GPU handoff must read.
- **Kept honest by:** `packages/physics/tests/soft-volume.test.js` ("an impulse moves a soft volume at J / M") holds
  momentum to 1e-3 of the impulse, the measured loss, and `docs/limits.md` states it.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: glTF points and lines drew 1 px wide whatever width the file gave (KB-GLTF-STROKEWIDTH1, gltf, exporters)

- **Repro:** `exportGLB` a scene with a 4 px `Line` or a 6 px `PointCloud` (the width goes in the primitive's `extras`
  as `lineWidth` or `pointSize`), or take a CAD file with `BENTLEY_materials_line_style` `width: 3`, and load it with
  `loadGLTF` or `parseGLTFAsync`: every point and line drew 1 px wide. `exportModel` of that model then wrote the
  primitives without their `extras`, and the scene writers without `_WIDTH` or `extras`, so a round trip lost the widths.
- **Cause:** gltf/pbr drew POINTS and LINES with the `point-list` and `line-list` topologies, which rasterize 1 px on
  WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, and read no width; the model writers copied attributes but not primitive `extras`.
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/gltf/strokes` (lazy, loaded for a file that asks for a width) hands such primitives to scene-wide
  `gltf-lines` and `gltf-points` plugins of `@margoengine/lines` and `@margoengine/points`, which draw them as instanced
  quads at the width in CSS pixels or world units, following the node; the model skips its 1 px draw of them. The
  writers keep `extras` and `_WIDTH` and skip those plugins. Regression: `packages/gltf/test/strokes.test.js`,
  `packages/exporters/tests/plugin-lines-points.test.js` (round trip), and `npm run test:gpu:strokes` in packages/gltf
  (widths measured in the frame on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a point cloud's pixel size is written as CSS pixels but drawn in target pixels (KB-POINTS-CSSPX1, points, bvh, animation, gltf)

- **Repro:** on a canvas drawn at device pixel ratio 2, a `PointCloud` with `size: 4` (pixels) covers 4 target pixels, 2
  CSS pixels. `exportGLB` writes `pointSize: 4, pointSizeUnits: 'pixels'`, which the exporters README and
  `@margoengine/gltf/strokes` read as CSS pixels, so the reloaded cloud covers 8 target pixels, twice the original.
- **Cause:** `PointsPlugin` sizes pixel points in pixels of the drawn target unless an owner sets `pixelScale` (sciviz
  sets CSS pixels), while `@margoengine/lines` widths and the glTF extras convention are CSS pixels. The exporter reads
  `material.size` as it is and cannot know the target's ratio from the cloud.
  `DeformedPoints` also sized in view pixels, `SurfelPlugin` and pixel sprites ignored any scale, and
  `@margoengine/bvh` picking took `size` as drawing-buffer pixels.
- **Fix:** CSS pixels everywhere a point or sprite pixel size is read: the plugin's and surfels' default scale is the
  target's width over the canvas's CSS width (the `@margoengine/lines` formula), the sprite shader multiplies its pixel
  offset by it, `PointRaycaster` scales sizes and clamps, `DeformedPoints` scales its size, and the glTF stroke reader's
  own override is gone. Drawn sizes grow on canvases backed above 1 pixel per CSS pixel (docs/limits.md).
  Regression: `packages/points/tests/pixel-scale.test.js`, `packages/bvh/tests/points.test.js`,
  `packages/animation/tests/deformed-points.test.js` and `packages/points/tests/pixel-density-browser.mjs` (WebGPU and
  the WebGL2 layer, with a reloaded GLB).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: tests picked a build's compat-*.js chunk by listing order (KB-COMPAT-CHUNKPICK1, scatter, shadows tests)

- **Repro:** a package build holds two `compat-*.js` chunks once two of its entries import `packages/shared/compat.js` (vfx,
  culling and sky builds do); their content hashes decide which one `readdirSync` names first. Scatter's `order` and
  `audit-132` tests and the shadows allocation probe imported the first one, and scatter's attributes check held every
  `packages/shadows/dist/compat-*.js`, so a build that split the shared chunk out would give them the wrong module or
  hold the package's own static import.
- **Fix:** `tests/support/compat-chunk.js` gains `compatChunkFile`; the four pick the chunk by its export (`compatChunk`,
  `compatChunkFile`). webgl2-compat's isolation and routes tests already kept only the chunk imported by `import()`.
  Regression: `tests/compat-chunk.test.js`, the pick under a listing that names the shared chunk first, and a scan that
  fails on any test that picks a `compat-*.js` by name alone or globs over all of them.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a soft body on flat ground kept a face contact its corners already held (KB-SOFT-FACEROWS1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `SoftBodyDesc.volume(sphereGeometry(0.4, 16, 12))` dropped from 1.5 m on a box floor: 240 steps took about
  40 s, steps at rest up to 0.8 s, with 150 to 340 face-contact rows (480 at most) on a ball of 352 triangles.
- **Cause:** a face contact on a flat face is held by its corners' particle contacts (the distance to a plane is affine
  over the triangle), so `SoftBodies` drops it; the check compared the contact's curvature with 0, but the kernel marks
  a flat face -1 (`kernel/src/face.rs`, `contact_feature`; 0 is a sharp edge or corner), and the documentation of
  `KernelFaceContacts.curvature` said 0. Every lower triangle kept its row, and the exact contact and friction solves
  grow with the square of the rows.
- **Fix:** the check takes curvature below 0 on the face and on each corner's contact, and leaves out only the faces of a
  fixed collider (against a moving body the face row carries its push back and friction: with every collider, a 1 g box
  fell through a cloth, soft.test.js "a contact is stable at a mass ratio of a thousand"); the documentation says -1. The
  same drop takes 1.1 s, 48 rows at rest and 105 at most. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/soft-volume.test.js`
  ("a ball on flat ground keeps no face contact its corners already hold"), at most one row a lower triangle.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a closed soft body felt a flat plate's air drag on both sides of every face (KB-SOFT-CLOSEDDRAG1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** a ball of `SoftBodyDesc.volume` coasting at 5 m/s with `setAirDrag` on slowed as a drag coefficient of
  1.17, 2.5 times the 0.47 measured for a sphere below the drag crisis (Achenbach 1972).
- **Cause:** `SoftBodies.airDrag` gave every face a flat plate's 1.17 whichever way it moved, leeward faces in the wake
  included.
- **Fix:** a body that holds a volume or a gas takes the air on its windward faces only, at a cube face's 1.05 (Hoerner
  1965), which sums to 0.525 on a sphere. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/soft-volume.test.js` ("a closed volume
  feels the air on its windward side").

### Open (below Margo) 2026-11-27: on WebKit's Windows build the voxel traversal on the WebGL2 layer now and then loses its device (KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1, browser; webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** Playwright WebKit 27.2 on Windows 11, RTX A6000:
  `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs --browser=webkit --cases=voxel-pathtracer`.
  Four runs from 22:05 to 22:12 gave the layer row "AbortError: The device was lost before the buffer mapped"; seven
  runs after 22:13 passed (19,200 of 19,200 pixels agree in both views). The same page under the harness
  (`MARGO_COMPAT=1`, `openBrowser({browserName:'webkit'})`) passed every time.
- **Cause:** not found. The layer's device context fired no `webglcontextlost` (a listener on every WebGL2 context the
  pages made saw only the probe context's own release), and the System log has no display driver reset then. The other
  ways the layer loses a device are a failed load of its lazy compute or read-back part and `destroy()`; the error did
  not say which.
- **Margo:** the map's `AbortError` now carries the loss's message ("... mapped (The compute part of the WebGL2
  compatibility layer did not load: ...); map it again ..."), so the next occurrence names its cause
  (`test/task-polling.test.js`, "a map aborted by its own buffer destroy names the destroy, and a device loss names the
  loss"). Open until a failing run is read with it.
- **Read (2026-11-27, 25 more runs):** 2 lost (runs 7 and 12), 23 passed. Both say "The WebGL2 context was lost": a real
  context loss, not a destroy or a lazy part that failed to load. With page logging on (run 12) WebKit printed
  "WebGL: context lost." 82 s into the page, near the end of a run that takes 80 to 100 s; no `webglcontextlost` event
  reached the device canvas's listener; the layer found it when `isContextLost()` turned true during a framebuffer
  status check (`makeFramebuffer`). The probe context's own release is the only event seen.
- **Cause (2026-11-27, proven):** below Margo. WebKit's Windows build loses a WebGL context when one call that waits on
  its GPU process waits 15 s: `docs/upstream-reports/KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1/sync-timeout.html` reads a long program's
  `LINK_STATUS`, which returns after 15,000 to 15,001 ms every time (2,500 to 8,000 statements) with the context lost;
  Edge 158 on the same PC and the same ANGLE Direct3D 11 waits 30,151 ms and keeps it. The traversal reaches that
  wait because over Direct3D 11 a program with more than one color output (each compute dispatch the layer draws)
  compiles again at its first draw, even after `KHR_parallel_shader_compile` reported it linked, and that compile
  runs inside the next waiting call, the layer's framebuffer status check. Timed in the matrix page (WebKit, a quiet
  machine): the traversal's first render made five such waits of 1.4, 5.6, 4.8, 6.5 and 8.5 s (12.7 s at most with
  40 busy CPU threads), after one draw each; the second view, same programs, renders in 87 ms. On a loaded machine one
  passes 15 s. The page waits do not depend on the draw's own work: the second draw of the same program waits 0 ms.
- **Margo:** not worked around. The layer cannot wait the compile out without blocking: a fence's status query waits
  on the same GPU process (first poll 1,068 ms), binding the program's framebuffer layout before the link does not
  stop the draw-time compile, and the page cannot tell WebKit's Windows build from Safari (both report macOS). The lever
  Margo has is the voxel programs' own Direct3D 11 compile time (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-d3d11-case-seconds.json`).
  Report draft: `docs/upstream-reports/KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1/report.md`.
- **Margo, 2026-11-28:** that compile cut in part, with the same output bit for bit (30 images of eight cases on
  WebGPU and on the layer over Direct3D 11): the camera ray takes its sines and cosines from two reductions instead
  of six (`preciseSinCos`), and the voxel walk records its hit in one `found()` instead of ten. Paired offline fxc
  compiles on a loaded machine: start 5.40 to 4.16 s and hit 7.11 to 5.84 s. The shadow and last loop programs hold
  neither function and their HLSL is the same byte for byte, so their paired times (5.27 against 5.89 s, 6.45 against
  6.94 s) show only the load (operational playbook, section 5, KB-COMPAT-LOSTWHY1). Still open: those two programs'
  own 5 to 7 s compiles, quiet-machine seconds, and a rerun of the WebKit matrix row, so whether every wait now stays
  under 15 s is not shown; the upstream report waits on Scott.
- **Seen in Chrome too, 2026-11-28:** in `demos/ten-thousand-trees` on the layer the water surface (three outputs)
  compiles again at its first draw for 3.0 s on Chrome's GPU main thread (`D3DCompile` there, one call), after its 3.8 s
  link on a worker; the page waits for it in the next framebuffer status check. Chrome keeps the context; it is the
  largest single wait left on that page's start after KB-COMPAT-SYNCLINK1.

### Open (below Margo) 2026-11-27: on WebKit's Windows build the WebGL2 layer copies unpremultiplied ImageBitmaps wrong (KB-WEBKIT-BITMAPALPHA1, browser; webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** Playwright WebKit 27.2 on Windows 11:
  `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs --browser=webkit`, row
  `bitmapCopies` on the layer is a bug ("the layer breaks a copy rule"). Without Margo:
  `docs/upstream-reports/KB-WEBKIT-BITMAPALPHA1/bitmap-alpha.html` draws a `premultiplyAlpha: 'none'` bitmap over
  opaque black and reads (100, 201, 60, 255) for the pixel (100, 201, 60, 1), where Edge reads (0, 1, 0, 255).
- **Cause:** below Margo: that build's 2D `drawImage` composites a straight bitmap as premultiplied. The layer learns a
  bitmap's alpha state, which no API states, by comparing the bitmap's uploaded bytes with a 2D canvas copy of it
  (`copyBitmap`, `packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts`). Here the two are equal for every bitmap, so a straight
  one is taken as premultiplied: copied into a premultiplied destination it keeps its colour, and by the same branch a
  copy into a straight destination divides its colour by alpha (read from the shader: brighter where alpha is between
  0 and 1). Opaque bitmaps are right either way.
- **Margo:** not worked around. Every 2D draw tried gives the same bytes, and a premultiplied bitmap may also hold
  colour over alpha (one taken from a WebGL canvas), so the bytes alone cannot decide. The browser matrix first named
  the `UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL` upload as the cause; that upload works (a canvas filled by `putImageData`
  uploads premultiplied). Edge, Firefox and Safari 27.2 on macOS (2026-11-15) keep both copy rules.

### Open (below Margo) 2026-11-27: an AMD Radeon's native WebGPU gets a helper function's derivative wrong when only a per-pixel branch uses it (KB-AMD-HELPERDERIV1, driver; browser)

- **Repro:** Edge 158, AMD Radeon integrated graphics of a Ryzen 9 9950X (driver 32.0.21042.62), Windows 11, native
  WebGPU: `MARGO_GPU=amd node packages/webgl2-compat/test/features-browser.mjs`, case `derivativeBranch.helper`. A
  fragment computes `d = slope(r)` (a function returning `vec2f(dpdx(r), dpdy(r))`) in uniform control flow, then uses
  `d.x` only inside `if (esc) { loop that sums d.x; return }`. For `r = 0.5 x^2 + 1.5 y^2` native returns d.x = -r (-0.5,
  -3.5, -10.5, -21.5 along the first row) where the differences are 1, 3, 5 and 7: the neighbour reads as 0. The same
  derivatives written in the entry point are right, and an RTX A6000 is right in every form.
- **Cause:** below Margo: WGSL defines a derivative taken in uniform control flow wherever it is used (W3C, "WebGPU
  Shading Language", "Derivatives" and "Uniformity"); on this GPU the compiled shader reads it as if taken inside the
  branch. The browser's WGSL translation or the AMD compiler is the owner; which of the two was not isolated.
- **Margo:** the WebGL2 layer returns the exact differences on both GPUs (it keeps such values in uniform control
  flow, the entry of 2026-11-15). `features-browser.mjs` now holds the layer to the exact values
  (`test/derivative-check.mjs`) and reports what native does. A shader of your own that must run right natively on this
  GPU should take the derivative in the entry point, or use its value outside the branch too.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: packages that loaded a WebGL2 route by import() drew their first frames differently until it arrived (KB-COMPAT-READY1, culling, dof, sky, splats, vfx, compute, voxel-pathtracer, scatter)

- **Repro:** the class KB-SCATTER-ATTRCOMPAT1 found in shadows. On the WebGL2 layer each of these packages fetches its
  compatibility route with `loadCompatRoute` when it attaches; until it arrives it waits or runs its WebGPU route on
  the layer's CPU tier. `packages/dof/tests/dof.test.js` ("DOF alone on the WebGL2 layer shows the sharp scene"): the
  first frames of a page show the scene sharp, later ones blurred, and nothing told a caller when frames stop changing.
- **Cause:** `packages/shared/compat.js` said "no frame is drawn differently" while the route loads; that held only
  where a check measured it. A check or film frame drawn on a loaded machine before the route differs from one after.
- **Fix, per package:** a `ready` promise (`routeSettled` in `packages/shared/compat.js`), documented in the README
  ("Exact first frames on the WebGL2 layer") and awaited by the package's own checks: dof 99d57ea87e, vfx 699d0c511d,
  splats e279aba67e, compute 60dc62f075 (`ComputeFrame.ready`), sky c59a9a2aa7, culling f7197f4315 (`CulledMeshes`,
  `CulledInstances`, `DynamicInstances`) and scatter's `Scatter` (the commit closing this row); voxel-pathtracer's
  `ready` already waited for its route kernel. The owed list of `scripts/quality/compat-route-proofs.json` is empty.
- **Regression:** each package's ready test (`packages/dof/tests/dof.test.js`, `packages/sky/test/compat-ready.test.js`,
  `packages/culling/test/compat-ready.test.js`, `packages/scatter/test/compat-ready.test.js` and the others named in
  those commits); the class check is the quality step `compat-routes` (5b24bdc8eb, `tests/quality-compat-routes.test.js`),
  which fails on any file that loads a route with neither `ready` nor a recorded proof of identical frames.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a remote voice was silent in Chromium (KB-NETCODE-VOICESILENT1, netcode)

- **Repro (before):** two pages joined by `PeerMesh` and `MediaSession` in Edge 158, A with `startVoice()`: B got the
  `remote` event and the packets (8,353 bytes in 2 s), but its meter read 0, no `speaking` event came, the inbound RTP
  report said audio level 0 and nothing could be heard. The same stream on a media element read 0.354 for A's tone.
- **Cause:** Chromium decodes a remote WebRTC voice only while a media element plays it; a
  `MediaStreamAudioSourceNode` alone gets silence (Chromium issue 933677). `MediaSession` played voices through Web
  Audio only (`packages/netcode/src/media.ts`), and its tests used stand-in streams.
- **Fix:** each remote voice is also held by a muted `Audio` element, released when the voice goes. Sound still comes
  from the Web Audio graph alone, so volume, mute and `spatial` work as before.
- **Regression:** `packages/netcode/tests/browser/media.mjs` (real Chromium, fake microphone: "B hears A speaking"
  failed before) and `packages/netcode/tests/media.test.js` "KB-NETCODE-VOICESILENT1".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a listener who had not clicked yet never heard anything (KB-NETCODE-VOICEGESTURE1, netcode)

- **Repro (before):** a page that joins a room and makes a `MediaSession` without an `audioContext` before any click or
  key press: when a voice arrived, the session's own context started `suspended` and stayed so after later clicks. The
  context is private, so the app could not resume it. `dispose()` also left that context open.
- **Cause:** browsers start an `AudioContext` made without user activation suspended until `resume()` runs after a
  gesture; nothing called it, and nothing closed the context.
- **Fix:** a context the session makes is resumed on the first `pointerdown`, `pointerup`, `keydown` or `touchend` of
  the page and closed by `dispose()`; a context passed in stays the caller's.
- **Regression:** `packages/netcode/tests/browser/media.mjs` (the untouched listener, strict autoplay policy) and
  `packages/netcode/tests/media.test.js` "KB-NETCODE-VOICEGESTURE1".

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a measured cloth on the vertex-block solver gained energy and hung past its elastica (KB-SOFT-VBDBEND1, physics soft)

- **Repro (before):** the 10-cell cantilever of `packages/physics/tests/soft-bending.test.js` (flannel's warp, KES-FB2 B
  0.288 gf cm^2/cm, 282 g/m^2, 46.2 mm out, the cotton shirting's measured threads) on `setSolver('vertex-block')`: at the
  default 8 pieces and 2 passes the tip flailed through 13 to 143 degrees and the strip's energy climbed without damping;
  at 20 passes it hung at 64.7 degrees where the elastica and the exact solve hold 46.0. With rigid threads it settled.
- **Cause:** the passes start from the inertial first guess, which stretches a stiff measured thread; a few Gauss-Seidel
  sweeps lower the step's potential from there but can end above its value at the particles' previous place, and then the
  piece puts energy into the sheet (the energy estimate of implicit Euler needs the result no higher than the previous
  place). The bending's Hessian was already in each block (k R_i^2 I, exact). Past that, one sweep carries a strip's bending a
  cell at a time, so 2 sweeps a piece left the measured cantilever creeping for tens of seconds.
- **Fix:** each block step is halved until it lowers the block's potential (backtracking), the passes start from the point
  of the segment from the previous place to the guess with the least potential, so a piece ends no higher than where it
  began, and the blocks take at least 8 sweeps a piece, alternating direction (`BLOCK_SWEEPS`, soft-kernel/src/cloth_block.rs).
  The cantilever now hangs within 0.3 degrees of the elastica at the defaults, and the undamped strip never rises above
  its starting energy.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/soft-bending.test.js` "on the vertex-block solver the strip settles on the same
  elastica at the default passes, and never gains energy".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a cloth pressing on the body it is lashed to lost linear momentum (KB-SOFT-LASHCONTACT1, physics soft)

- **Repro (before):** no gravity; a 4 by 7 sail of `FABRICS.sailcloth` (1 m by 6 m, from [0, 1, 0]) with a `SailForce` in a
  10 m/s wind, its seven luff particles tied by `attachParticle` to a free 200 kg box hull at [0, 0.5, 3] (half extents
  [0.5, 0.25, 3.5]), 60 steps: the hull's and the sail's linear momentum was [27.22, -13.96, -0.85] N s where the summed
  impulse of the sail's load was [27.58, -13.79, -1.07] (1.3 percent). With the hull clear of the sail it matched.
- **Cause:** two leaks. (1) The contact passes after the exact solve (`apply_contacts` in soft-kernel/src/world.rs and
  `apply_faces` in face.rs) held a particle's or a face's slide back by friction as a displacement of the cloth alone: the
  body was never given the reaction (a comment still said the velocity pass gave it, which stopped when friction moved into
  the exact solve). The sail's particles start 0.08 m over the hull, inside their 0.53 m contact radius (the circumradius
  of a 0.33 by 1 m cell's triangle), so the contacts that thrust them off the hull ran in those passes with full friction.
  (2) The exact solve added each Newton step's body impulse to the body's f32 total; contacts of that thrown sail asking
  for what no motion gives ran it for hundreds of small steps, and each one's impulse below the total's f32 spacing was dropped.
- **Fix:** the passes' friction is a positional constraint along the slide, shared by the cloth's and the body's
  generalized inverse masses along it, the body taking the reaction at the contact point (Mueller et al. 2020, section
  3.5), measured against the body's point as this piece's corrections have moved it (so a light body that follows the
  slide is not pushed again for it); the exact solve sums each body's impulse in f64 and hands it over once a piece. The sail on its hull now matches
  its impulse to 1e-5 of it.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/sail.test.js` "a sail lashed to its hull and pressing on it keeps the momentum
  its contacts trade with the hull (KB-SOFT-LASHCONTACT1)" (1.3 percent before, against a bound of 0.1 percent).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a resting vehicle's dampers read the end-of-step velocity of a substepped body (KB-PHYS-VEHICLEREST1, physics)

- **Repro:** `Vehicle.car(physics, chassis)` on a floor (the quick start of `packages/physics/README.md`), 300 steps:
  the chassis does not move, yet `chassis.linearVelocity[1]` reads -0.0715 m/s every step, and each spring rested at
  0.1826 m where `rest - sag` is 0.1785 m (compressed 4.6% less than its static sag). A body held still by any per-step impulse
  (`applyImpulse` from `beforestep`) shows the same -0.0715 m/s.
- **Cause:** the kernel takes n substeps a step and adds gravity in each (v += g h, x += v h, h = dt / n), while an impulse from
  `beforestep` acts once at the start. A body ends the step `g dt (n - 1) / (2 n)` further along gravity than its mean speed
  over the step, -7/16 of `g dt` at 8 substeps for one held still. `Vehicle`'s damper (`vehicle.ts`, the suspension loop)
  read that end-of-step velocity as a compression speed and carried part of the weight with it. Rapier, one step with gravity
  added once, reads 0 there.
- **Fix:** the damper reads the step's mean speed: the contact point's velocity less `g dt (n - 1) / (2 n)` times each dynamic
  body's gravity scale (the chassis's, less the ground body's under `groundReaction`), from `physics.substeps` and
  `physics.gravity`. A still car's dampers read 0 and each spring rests at the static sag to 1e-5 m. Drive, grip and anti-roll
  keep the velocity they read. Two steps after full throttle a front wheel now carries 2,803 N where it carried 2,850 N, as
  an unloading wheel takes the extension damper (0.5 of critical) where the phantom compression kept the compression one
  (0.3).
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/vehicle-car.test.js` "a car rests on four springs that carry a quarter of its weight
  each" (each spring at `rest - sag` to 1e-5 m; read 0.18259 before), and "the debug lines show each suspension ray" reads each
  tyre's push line against its own load (push times load is the 1,200 N drive to 0.5 N; it compared with the static quarter
  load to 0.02 before). The Rapier oracle files `next-vehicle.test.js` and `next-vehicle-wheels.test.js` and the other vehicle
  files pass (48 of 48), and `packages/road` driving (14 of 14).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a bounce took friction from its compression only, so balls slid through bounces that grip (KB-PHYS-BOUNCEFRICTION1, physics)

- **Repro:** a 57 g tennis ball (shell inertia, `setMassProperties`) meeting a fixed floor of friction 0.23 and restitution 0.77 at
  3.72 m/s, 20 degrees above the surface, with no spin: it kept 0.916 of its speed along the surface, where Coulomb's law gives
  0.852 and Cross (2002) measured 0.84; at 45 degrees it slid off at 0.770 where it grips and leaves rolling at 0.645 (measured
  0.60 to 0.68 on three surfaces). A ball struck sideways into a touching line kept all of its sideways speed.
- **Cause:** `kernel/src/solver.rs` solved friction in the relaxing pass within mu times the normal impulse that stopped the
  approach, and then `solve_impacts` added the restitution impulse along the normal alone; `collide_pairwise` rubbed nothing.
  The tangential impulse was held to mu m v_n where it is mu (1 + e) m v_n.
- **Fix:** after a struck point is sent off, its pair's friction is solved again, unbiased, in the cone of the whole impulse;
  a strike resolved pair by pair brings the slip toward rest within mu times its own impulse (PK60 in `docs/clean-room.md`).
  Regression: `packages/physics/tests/rigid-materials.test.js` "an oblique bounce is the rigid ball's exact solution" and
  `packages/physics/tests/rigid-validation.test.js` "a ball struck sideways into a touching line slides under Coulomb friction
  through the strike".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a domino wave ran slower in a row of small dominoes than in the same row scaled up (KB-PHYS-DOMINOSCALE1, physics)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/rigid-measured.test.js`: the 0.2 m row at the defaults against the 48 mm row with its
  tolerances and step scaled to it (`lengthUnit: 0.24`, `fixedTimestep` times sqrt(0.24)), the same in every dimensionless
  number, gave wave speeds over sqrt(g H) of 1.54 and 1.53 at d/H 0.23 and 0.33 at 0.2 m and 1.40 and 1.35 at 48 mm.
- **Cause:** `kernel/src/sat.rs` held a face as the reference while another feature beat it by up to `FACE_BIAS`, 1 mm, a bias
  fixed in metres that `lengthUnit` does not reach. On a domino 7.2 mm thick that is a seventh of its thickness: the leaning
  domino kept its own side as the contact normal while its edge pressed on the next one, so the push and the friction leaned
  with it.
- **Fix:** the bias is 1 mm for shapes reaching 0.2 m or more from their centre, and half a percent of the smaller shape's
  reach below that (`face_bias`), so the feature choice is the same at every size; larger shapes step as before. The scaled
  rows now give 1.60 and 1.53 against 1.57 and 1.51. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/rigid-measured.test.js` "a row scaled
  in every dimension topples at one speed". The other runs of the old entry stand: the step, substeps and contact stiffness
  are not scale terms. What is left at the defaults is resolution, now in `docs/limits.md`: at 60 Hz a 48 mm domino's fall,
  sqrt(H / g) = 70 ms, spans four steps (a 0.2 m one nine) and the 0.2 mm slop is 3 percent of its thickness, so the default
  row runs at 1.37 mean over the five spacings against 1.47 at 0.2 m; with `lengthUnit: 0.05` and a 1/240 s step it matches
  all five of Larham's measurements within 0.1 (same file, "real 48 mm dominoes").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a strike carried through a ball bounced off both of its contacts and made energy (KB-PHYS-BOUNCECHAIN1, physics)


- **Repro:** with no gravity, three spheres of restitution 1 in a row 2 mm apart, the first struck at 1 m/s, left at -0.5,
  0.5 and 1 m/s, 1.5 times the energy (five balls: 4 times).
- **Cause:** `kernel/src/solver.rs` noted a struck point's approach speed inside the pushing pass, after the pairs solved
  before it had pushed its bodies, so the push the first pair gave the middle ball was the second pair's approach, and
  restitution bounced both.
- **Fix:** `note_approach` notes every bouncy point's normal speed before the warm start (the pre-solve speed of Müller et
  al. 2020) and a strike bounces from that; pairs without restitution are skipped. Regression:
  `packages/physics/tests/rigid-validation.test.js` "Newton's cradle".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the tracked vehicle threw plain RangeError and TypeError (KB-PHYS-TRACKEDERR1, physics)

- **Repro:** `new TrackedVehicle(physics, chassis, {tracks: []})` threw a `RangeError` with no help link, where
  `Vehicle`, `Vehicle.car`, `Motorcycle`, the tyre models and `Drivetrain` throw a `MargoError` linking
  margoengine.com/errors#vehicles (P5 DYN-04, 2026-11-27).
- **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/tracked.ts` was left out of that change because an open terramechanics branch edited
  the same file.
- **Fix:** every refusal in `tracked.ts` (the constructor, `setInput`, `track`, the motion state and `shearShare`) is
  `invalidVehicle`, a `MargoError` (code `unsupported`, or `state` for a chassis of another world) linking the vehicles
  entry. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/vehicle-tracked.test.js` "a tank refuses what makes no sense, and a
  disposed one lets go".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: check:dev-servers called `npx vite build` a server start (KB-DEVSERVERS-BUILD1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/check-dev-servers.mjs --docs-only`: `tools/margo-convert/README.md:138` and `:227`,
  "`npx vite build` starts a server that no check covers" (48d01e498a, 1ec57ee7bc).
- **Cause:** the documented-command rule took any `npx`, `vite` or `next` line holding the word `vite`, `next`, `dev`,
  `start`, `serve` or `preview` for a server start, `vite build` and `next build` included, which write files and exit.
- **Fix:** `scripts/support/doc-start-command.mjs` `startsServer` leaves the build commands out, one chained part at a
  time, so `vite build && vite preview` is still a start. Regression: `tests/dev-servers.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the voxel path tracer's GPU stall watch failed a case that waited on cold shader compiles (voxel-pathtracer tests)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:gpu:stall -w @margoengine/voxel-pathtracer` on the WebGL2 layer over ANGLE
  Direct3D 11 (2026-11-16): the first tracer's cold fxc compiles held the page's thread for over 10 s and the watch
  (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/progress.mjs`) fired its 10 s stall limit with "2 pipelines compiling".
- **Cause:** the watch counts finished GPU work, so a wait on the shader compiler looked like a GPU wait that never
  resolves.
- **Fix:** while the page's last answer had a pipeline compiling, the limit is the compile limit
  (`MARGO_GPU_COMPILE_MIN` minutes, default 3) when that is longer; a compile that never ends still fails there, and a
  stall with nothing compiling fails at the stall limit as before. Ported from the unlanded lane-E commit e78e881c05.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/progress.test.js` (fails on main before the port). The stall check
  passes on native WebGPU (17.2 s) and on the layer (42.0 s), RTX A6000.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: VFX ribbons, mesh particles and Flame wrote no TAA reactive mask (KB-TAA-PARTICLEMASK2, vfx)

- **Repro:** `TAA.attach(engine)` with a fast `VFX` that has `ribbons` (`heads: false`) or `mesh`, or a `Flame`:
  `taa.velocity.resolved` alpha (the mask TAA read) is 1 everywhere, as with no mask, so the strips, pieces and tongues
  average into the history they have no motion vectors for. Billboards had written the mask since KB-TAA-PARTICLEMASK1.
- **Cause:** those three draw in passes of their own, and only the billboard draw (`base.ts` `drawReactive`) drew into
  the shared particle mask (`packages/shared/reactive-mask.js` `reactiveTarget`).
- **Fix:** each draws its coverage into the shared mask while TAA reads masks, or as the effect's (or flame's)
  `reactive` option says: ribbons their strips' alpha, mesh particles 1 over their pieces (depth tested against what
  they just wrote), `Flame` its march opacity (glow left out), all with the shared `reactiveBlend` (max).
  Regression: `packages/vfx/test/reactive-sources-check.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; on the parent the ribbons,
  mesh and flame rigs read 1 everywhere, as their `reactive: false` twins), which also covers billboards drawn by an
  order-independent pass (`addEffect`), a path that had no mask test; `reactive` validation in
  `packages/vfx/test/flame.test.js`.
