### Fixed 2026-11-26: moving the world origin displaced a retained water reading (KB-LOADS-ORIGINMIRROR)

- **Repro:** Move the world origin back one 4,096 m cell between ticks in a staggered coupling. The reader steps first.
  Its 1.5 m distance to the writer's retained point becomes −4,094.5 m.
- **Cause and fix:** The solver cells moved while the current and previous field samples stayed in the old frame.
  Both retained cells now move atomically with the solver cells. Hydro's retained flow and its Loads consumers use
  the live cell, including before the first Hydro step after a shift.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/world.test.js` checks both mirrors and atomic rejection of a retained-cell
  overflow. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/loads-swim-actuators.test.js` checks paired water and body impulses
  against the unshifted swimmer and verifies exact replay.

### Open 2026-11-27: the ordinary hull wake pressure and projected volume do different work (KB-LOADS-WAKEWORK, physics loads)

- **Repro:** In a periodic 48 × 32 finite-depth wake, drive a 2 × 1 × 1 m box (draft 0.5 m) at 1.25 m/s.
  Over 60 ticks the free rigid hull lost 451.938 J while the wake gained 226.089 J with feedback enabled.
- **Cause:** The triangle pressure uses the local surface rise through depth. The projected volume uses a
  finite-depth modal transfer and normalized grid support. The pressure return is not the adjoint of that
  source. The prescribed work meter and the optional `SurgeWakeCoupling` and `FreeHullWakeCoupling` match
  the kick on their supported guides. The ordinary hull solver's return pressure for arbitrary motion and
  original-shot verification remain open.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: reindexing hull triangles reversed wet section segments (KB-LOADS-STRIPWINDING)

- **Repro:** Cyclically rotate each triangle's indices on an outward-wound, eccentric box. One slice returned
  0.3583 m² for a 0.975 m² section. The closed First Wake render-derived hull put a submerged wave source
  38.02 m off its centreline, outside its 7.75 m half-beam.
- **Cause and fix:** Each sliced triangle's starting index set the direction of its cut segment. This could
  reverse individual terms in the Green area and first moments although the mesh still wound outward.
  Use the direction of the oriented edge crossing to order the two cut endpoints.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js` checks all cyclic triangle variants
  against exact rectangular sections and checks the signed wake volume and first moment on both arena layouts.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: projected advancing sources apply the beam twice (KB-LOADS-WAKEWIDTH)

- **Repro:** In `coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, advance the 2 × 1 × 1 m eccentric hull at 1.5 m/s with a
  submerged source on 0.25 m cells. The longitudinal Fourier coefficient is 0.016374 m³. Integrating the
  end-face flux and finite-depth transfer with the known bilinear weights gives 0.016987 m³.
- **Cause and fix:** The lateral Gauss points already encode beam. Spreading each point by half the entire
  beam applies an extra filter that stays as the grid tightens. Base the numerical radius on the longitudinal
  station interval and the caller's minimum. The exact end-face mode, signed volume, first moment and
  frame-zero replay pass on both arena layouts.

### Open 2026-11-27: First Wake’s authored stern sweeps into the quay (KB-LOADS-FIRSTWAKEQUAY, First Wake)

- **Repro:** In the archived First Wake scene, transform the Survey ship’s GLB positions by the scale and
  waterline offset in `main.js` and the pose in `timeline.js`. At vessel time 8.42 s an underwater vertex at
  x = −22.585 m reaches z = −16.347 m. The quay’s actual wet face there is z = −10.55 m.
- **Cause:** The ship’s heading follows the tangent of the early sideways departure. It rotates the long stern
  through the wall before the centre has enough clearance. A slower sideways departure clears the wall in a
  geometry diagnostic. Production playback still needs the corrected track and a resolved reflected wake.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: film seek from frame zero lost the accumulator layout (KB-LOADS-FRAMEZERO)

- **Repro:** Snapshot a world with buoyancy and a pending 5 N·s rigid impulse before it advances. The first step
  used to allocate the force and impulse sums, after which restoring the initial checkpoint failed.
- **Cause and fix:** The registry now reserves a sum when the first contributor publishes its shape. Summation
  and draining still occur in the owner step.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/world-frame-zero-accumulator.test.js` checks the rigid body receives the
  impulse once and replays both accumulators. `packages/water/test/flood-rigid-drag.browser.mjs` seeks to frame zero
  and replays independent buoyancy and accepted flood momentum on WebGPU and WebGL2.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: torque about a locked axis turned a rigid body (KB-LOADS-AXISMOBILITY)

- **Repro:** Tilt a box with unequal principal inertia and lock rotation about world X. Give it an angular impulse
  or held torque about world X. The free Y or Z axes move.
- **Cause and fix:** Integration projected the velocity after applying the inverse inertia. It now projects
  the angular input as well, matching the effective mobility used by contact constraints. The separate
  `bodyMobility` port publishes this response without changing the existing `bodies` layout.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/world-rigid-solver.test.js` compares published response with all six impulse
  directions and held torque using a rotated rigid body and a frame-zero restore.
- **Load consumers:** `packages/physics/tests/loads-coupled-radiation.test.js` checks zero mobility on locked
  axes and the retained reaction for ordinary and coupled held wrenches in TypeScript and both Wasm variants.
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/projected-drag-settlement.test.js` checks the accepted horizontal Flood impulse
  and its moment against the exact water response at a supported body, with replay.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a supersampled edge pixel half plants and half lit ground was in both masks (KB-LOOK-MASKTIE1, shot tool)

- **Repro:** rail-line shot `--once --seconds 1.1` (supersample 2): `probes/mid.plants.png` and `mid.lit.png` both read
  128 on 14,504 to 15,904 pixels, `plants` and `shadow` on 1,173 to 1,259 (up to 12 percent of the shaded mask), and
  `lit` and `shadow` on about 25, though the page's SceneTargets masks never mark one sample twice (plants is
  1 - t.ground, the ground masks need t.ground above 0.5).
- **Cause:** `resampleMask` (`tools/shot/pixels.js`) took a 2 x 2 footprint with two of four samples covered to
  `Math.round(127.5)`, 128, and the look checks read 128 and above as inside, so an exact half counted as inside for
  both masks of a complementary pair.
- **Fix:** coverage rounds to the nearest level with an exact half rounding down (127.5 to 127, with 1e-7 for the
  weights' float error), so 128 means more than half covered and two masks that share no sample can never both read
  inside. The rail-line probes now read 0 pixels in every pair (lit 41.96 and 43.12 percent, shaded 0.38 and 0.44,
  plants 33.33 and 32.04 early and mid).
- **Regression:** `tests/shot-capture.test.js`, "masks that share no sample stay disjoint after the downsample" (fails
  with round half up); `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-masks-check.mjs` asserts the rail-line masks disjoint and
  within their coverage bounds (in the scenes `test:gpu`).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the rail-line shot's motionBlur read 60.5 and 46.5 percent (bound 0 to 5) (KB-LOOK-TV-MOTIONBLUR1, shot look checks)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-rail-line.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out <dir>`:
  `look.md` read motionBlur 60.5 percent early and 46.5 mid.
- **Cause:** the check, not the frames. `@margoengine/headless/look` `motionBlur` called an edge sharp when its 10 to
  90 percent width was under half its travel to the next frame, taking the whole travel as a 180 degree shutter's
  smear. A shutter of A degrees is open for A / 360 of the frame interval (Potmesil and Chakravarty, "Modeling motion
  blur in computer-generated images", SIGGRAPH 1983, https://doi.org/10.1145/964967.801169; Cook, Porter and
  Carpenter, "Distributed ray tracing", SIGGRAPH 1984, https://doi.org/10.1145/964965.808590), so the shot tool's
  sub-frames (`subframeOffsets`, over shutter / 360 / fps) smear an edge across half its travel at 180 degrees, and
  every correctly blurred edge (measured 0.3 to 0.5 of the travel, none under 0.1) read as sharp.
- **Fix:** an edge is sharp under half the shutter's smear (`shutter` option, default 180 degrees: a quarter of the
  travel); `checkShot` takes the angle from `manifest.render` when the shot drew sub-frames, and a frame drawn without
  them is still judged at 180. The rail-line probes read 0.55 and 0.60 percent. Regression:
  `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js` (an 8 sub-frame 180 degree bar passes, one sub-frame and a 90 degree
  bar judged at 180 fail, the probe's own angle applies).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the WebGL2 layer accepted a compute pipeline past its workgroup limits at creation (KB-COMPAT-WGSIZE1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** on the layer's device (maxComputeInvocationsPerWorkgroup 256), `createComputePipeline` with
  `@compute @workgroup_size(512) fn main() {}` returned a pipeline with no validation error; the first dispatch's
  build threw the planner's RangeError out of the submit. A `@workgroup_size(1, 1, 128)` kernel (Z limit 64) or more
  than 16384 bytes of workgroup variables were never refused. The browser corpus compute part
  (`npm run test:browser:compute -w @margoengine/webgl2-compat`) failed on the 12 recorded kernels past 256
  invocations and did not count its 23 subgroup refusals.
- **Cause:** `CompatComputePipeline` checked binding counts at creation but no workgroup limit.
- **Fix:** creation checks each `@workgroup_size` axis, their product and the workgroup variables' bytes (override-sized
  arrays included) against the device's limits, and reports a validation error (`GPUPipelineError` from the async
  call). The browser corpus compute part asserts and counts both refusals. Regression:
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/compute-limits.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a recorded animation kernel never ended on zero-filled buffers and reset the GPU in the browser corpus compute part (KB-COMPAT-CORPUSFBO1, animation)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:browser:compute -w @margoengine/webgl2-compat` (Chrome, ANGLE Direct3D 11, RTX A6000)
  failed on the record after `animation 8b858be2e0a8c694 main`: `sky 8bd2180e7c0c8ef7 main` (its helper program "did
  not link", or an incomplete framebuffer 0x8cdd), and in some runs `compute 8c376d839a33176a main` too. The fewest
  records that failed: those two animation and sky records through `window.dispatchAll` of `test/corpus-draw.html`.
- **Cause:** the page dispatches every kernel with zero-filled stand-in buffers. `morphWeightShader`
  (`packages/animation/src/morph-gpu.ts`) binary-searched a track's keys from `track.keys-1u`: with 0 keys it wrapped
  to 4294967295, the midpoint `(lo+hi+1u)/2u` wrapped to 0 and the loop never ended. A `readPixels` after the dispatch
  blocked 5,547 ms (the Windows GPU watchdog) and the reset landed in the next record's report. With 1 key the same
  dispatch finished in 1 ms. The engine's own inputs always have at least one key.
- **Fix:** the search starts at `max(track.keys,1u)-1u` and takes its midpoint as `lo+(hi-lo+1u)/2u`, so it ends on
  any buffer contents, with the same result for every valid track. The corpus holds the new source in place of the old
  one: `record-wgsl-corpus.mjs --add --drop=8b858be2e0a8c694` (the new flag refuses a module the corpus does not hold
  or one a suite still creates). The corpus compute part passes: 1144 pipelines dispatched, none failed. Regression:
  `packages/animation/tests/morph-gpu.test.js` "ends on any buffer contents",
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus.test.js` "a recording drops only".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: after a GPU reset the WebGL2 layer reported the loss as its own link failure or an incomplete framebuffer (KB-COMPAT-LOSSREPORT1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** as KB-COMPAT-CORPUSFBO1: after the hanging dispatch, the next CPU-tier storage texture upload threw
  "The compatibility layer's own masked::texelFetch(t, p, 0) program did not link (a bug: report it)" with an empty
  log, or reported the validation error "The render pass attachments do not form a complete WebGL2 framebuffer (status
  0x8cdd)", before `device.lost` resolved.
- **Cause:** Chrome learns of the reset in the synchronous query that waited for it but sets `isContextLost()` and
  queues CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL only for a later task. Measured again with raw WebGL2 (Chrome, ANGLE Direct3D 11, RTX
  A6000): a hanging draw, then `readPixels` returned at 5,423 ms; right after it a fresh program's LINK_STATUS was false
  with an empty log, a fresh shader's COMPILE_STATUS false, `checkFramebufferStatus` 0x8cdd, `getError` 0 four times
  and `isContextLost()` false. One task later `getError` gave CONTEXT_LOST_WEBGL with `isContextLost()` true, and
  `webglcontextlost` fired 1 ms after. No synchronous signal exists, so the layer's checks at the failing call
  (`CompatDevice.report`, `CompatRenderer.helper`) could not tell the loss from a real failure.
- **Fix:** `CompatDevice` judges every error read from GL in a later task, in one place (`reportable`): the
  uncaptured dispatch (already a task of its own), `popErrorScope` (resolves in order, `null` on a lost device, as
  WebGPU) and the async pipeline rejections (`settlePipeline`). On a context lost by then the device is lost
  (`'unknown'`) and the error dropped; on a live context it is reported as raised. The helper program that does not
  link is an `internal` error through that path, reported once, not a synchronous throw. Every other GL status read
  was checked: pipeline links (`LinkedProgram.finish`) and compute refusals report through the same path; the
  adapter probes (highp int, fresh clears, inverse trig) decide only workarounds for the adapter's own new context;
  the zeroing check in `drawsClears` only skips the zeroing; the preview renderer and `webglPicking` throw `failed` on
  a lost context by contract. Proved on two real resets: a helper link and a render pass right after the reset (one
  with `isContextLost()` still false) threw nothing, raised no error, both scopes resolved `null` and `device.lost`
  resolved `'unknown'`. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/lost-report.test.js` (all four fail on the parent).
  Since 2026-11-27 also in a real browser on every `test:gpu`: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/lost-context-browser.mjs`
  crashes the browser's own GPU process (CDP `Browser.crashGpuProcess`, not a driver reset), builds a helper program
  and a new framebuffer while `isContextLost()` is still false on both contexts, and checks that nothing throws, the
  scope resolves `null`, both devices are lost (`'unknown'`) and no uncaptured error is raised (3 of 3 runs pass at
  cd4508a015; the helper case threw the "did not link" fault before this fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the WGSL corpus recorded on 2026-11-26 failed six webgl2-compat tests (KB-COMPAT-CORPUSRED1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** at 3d585ad959, after `npm run build -w @margoengine/webgl2-compat`, run
  `node --test packages/webgl2-compat/test/{compute,corpus,interpret,wgsl-corpus-check}.test.js`: six fail, five with
  `Unknown function 'subgroupAdd'` (code `wgsl-type`) and one with modules moved from scatter and compute to shared
  and sciviz; `npm run test:browser -w @margoengine/webgl2-compat` fails on 18 `enable clip_distances;` translations
  and khronos-gallery's material.
- **Cause:** four, all brought out by the re-recording. (1) The WGSL checker typed none of the subgroup and quad
  built-in functions, so compute's 23 subgroup kernels (built only when the device has `subgroups`) died with an
  uncoded type error before the layer's coded refusal. (2) `writeCorpus` re-derived a module's owner from labels a
  later recording merged in, so writing the read corpus again moved modules. (3) The corpus checks expected a
  translation for modules behind `enable subgroups;` and `enable clip_distances;`, extensions the layer does not
  offer (materials uses clip distances only on `clip-distances`), and for 12 compute kernels sized 512 and 1024 on
  adapters granting more than WebGPU's default 256 invocations. (4) `glsl-corpus-browser.mjs` linked
  khronos-gallery's material (module 7ba63815075dd8da, recorded on WebGPU with its base maps apart: 19 layer units)
  where the device refuses it before linking; on the layer gltf/pbr asks the device first and packs the base maps.
- **Fix:** the checker types the WGSL subgroup functions (subgroupAdd to quadSwapDiagonal) behind
  `enable subgroups;`, compute and fragment stages only, with subgroupBroadcast's and quadBroadcast's const lane
  range, and asks for the enable on a call or a subgroup built-in value without it. `writeCorpus` keeps a settled
  owner. One corpus rule, in `test/support/corpus-refusals.mjs`, asserted in compute.test.js, glsl-corpus-browser.mjs
  and corpus-draw-browser.mjs: an unmapped enable is refused with the coded error naming it, counted per name against
  the recorded counts (compute 23 `subgroups`, GLSL 18 `clip_distances`), the 12 kernels past 256 invocations are
  refused by the planner and counted, and a pipeline past the texture units is refused as the device refuses it
  (`unitsRefusal`, the device's own wording) and must belong to a recorded module with its cause. Nothing left the
  corpus and no check loosened. Regression: `test/wgsl-front-end.test.js` "subgroup built-in functions",
  `test/corpus.test.js` "re-recording keeps an owner", `test/compute.test.js` corpus tier test. khronos-gallery's
  full material on the layer: `scripts/compat-units-gpu-check.js --compat` (all 13 maps, image light, both shadow
  kinds, clustered light, bounce) passes.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: `Water` refused bad options with plain RangeError and TypeError (KB-WATER-CODED1, water)

- **Repro:** `new Water({ color: [2, 0, 0] })` or `water.setSeaLevel(NaN)` threw a `RangeError` with no `code` and no
  help link; `new Water({ sea: {} })` a `TypeError`.
- **Cause:** the `Water` class predated the coded-error convention: 28 refusals in `packages/water/src/index.ts` and 3 in
  `sea-state.ts` (which the `wind` option and `setWind` reach) were never moved.
- **Fixed:** each throws MargoError `unsupported` with a link to errors#ocean, and `setSeaLevel`, `setWind` and
  `setWaveHeight` after `dispose()` throw `disposed`. `setFog` keeps the plain errors of the fog check that every fogged
  entry shares (`packages/shared/fog.js`), and the `water/settings` helper keeps its row checker's errors. Regression:
  `packages/water/test/coded-errors.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: paddle and wading loads settle with the final wet cells (KB-LOADS-ACTUATORDRY)

- **Repro:** Put a moving paddle or legged body over a 2 µm periodic water cell and draw it down to
  0.5 µm in one step. The body receives a drag impulse while the shallow water drops the staged
  reaction at its dry threshold.
- **Cause and fix:** The legacy adapters computed both impulses using the pre-transport water.
  `ShallowWaterSolver.withFloodLoads` computes the paired exchange after wet/dry transport and
  publishes only the accepted body reactions. Use this factory for changing wetness.
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/loads-paddle.test.js` and `loads-wading.test.js` check wet momentum,
  drying rejection and replay.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a limp ragdoll's spine was drawn 7 cm off its body after a 3 s fall (KB-RAGDOLL-LIMPDRAW1, physics)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="limp: the ragdoll falls" packages/ragdoll/tests/ragdoll.test.js` on main at
  256a80a04, with the DYN-07 changes taken out and physics and ragdoll rebuilt: "spine drawn at its body: 0.069 is not 0
  within 0.02". The other 98 ragdoll tests pass.
- **Cause:** not found yet. Found while landing DYN-07 (the debug view and the character bridge), which does not change it:
  the same assertion fails with and without those changes. The node's drawn position and its body's position part after
  the fall, so either the joint holding the spine to the hips drifts (a physics change on main since the test last passed)
  or the pose written into the bones lags the bodies.
- **Cause found (lane P, 2026-11-28, main at 601556ae42, 0.0206 against 0.02):** the pose is written right; the joints open.
  Measured in the hips body's frame, the three joints on the hips (spine and both thighs) stand 2.0 and 1.9 cm off their
  anchors after 180 frames, while the joints along each limb (head on spine, shin on thigh) hold to 0.1 mm. The hips is a
  branch: `walk_path` (`kernel/src/joints.rs`) ends every path there, so the three joints meet by block Gauss-Seidel at
  `jointLooseShare` 0.2, and the hips capsule (r 0.05 m, 1 g) is fifteen times lighter than a thigh. Each path's push moves
  mostly the light hub, the next path moves it back, and the error closes slowly while loads hold it open. Without friction
  or limits the gap still stands 3 to 4 cm open at rest (`joint: {type: 'free'}`, floor friction 0); at `jointLooseShare` 1
  it closes to 0.1 mm, and a stiffer default would break the rings and grids the 0.2 share was chosen for. Native repro, no
  floor and no gravity: a 1 g hub with three 15 g arms started 2 cm off their anchors is still 3.2 mm open after 1 s and
  0.26 mm after 2 s, where a path of the same bodies closes in a step. With sleep on (the JS default) the island can sleep
  with the gap open (1.0 cm, frozen).
- **Fixed 2026-11-28:** the paths that meet at branch bodies are one group (`group_trees`, `kernel/src/joints.rs`, union-find over the paths, Tarjan 1975, Efficiency of a good but not linear set union algorithm, https://doi.org/10.1145/321879.321884), and a group whose moving bodies hold no loop (its joints between two moving bodies one fewer than those bodies) is a tree: its paths are listed together and the lock projection solves the whole tree exactly in one Newton step on its matrix J W G^T, which takes any topology (Baraff 1996, Linear-time dynamics using Lagrange multipliers, https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~baraff/papers/sig96.pdf, solves any acyclic joint graph exactly). A second cause showed once the tree was one solve: `push_share` read each joint's push on the hub as its own, and each alone spins a 1 g hub hard where the three nearly cancel, so the step was cut to a share that closed 3e-5 m an iterate and a swinging hub opened 1.65 mm in half a second. A body's gain is now summed over every joint of the path or tree that holds it, as it was for the two joints of a body inside a path. A group with a loop (rings, grids) stays loose and is left to the passes (KB-PHYS-LOCKGRIDSLOW1).
- **Measured:** the native hub started 2 cm off, no gravity: 4.0e-3 m open after a step before, 8.3e-9 m now; hung by an arm and swinging 3 s: 1.3e-6 m (before: 0.8 mm from the first step, 4 mm started off). `ragdoll.test.js` 22 of 22, "limp: the ragdoll falls" included (bar 0.02).
- **Regression:** `a_light_hub_between_heavy_arms_holds_its_joints` in `packages/physics/kernel/tests/joints.rs` (fails after one step without the tree group, and at 2.3 mm in the swing with the group but per-joint gains); "limp: the ragdoll falls, its joints hold together" in `packages/ragdoll/tests/ragdoll.test.js`.
### Open 2026-11-27: a flexible pipe in strongly sheared flow swings 40 % short of the measurement across it (KB-PHYS-RODVIVSHEAR1, physics loads)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/rod-viv.test.js`, Fu et al. (2025)'s linearly sheared pipe at 1.0 m/s (their Fig. 12):
  the rod swings 0.235 D RMS across in the measured second mode where the test measured 0.407 D (-42 %), and 0.085 D in
  line in the second mode where it measured 0.104 D in the third (-18 %). The bow is within 22 % (the paper's CFD +24 %), and
  the same pipe at 0.6 m/s is within the paper's CFD on every quantity.
- **Cause, so far:** not the Reynolds scaling (without it, 0.229 D), not the discretisation, and only in part the damping:
  the rod's damping is stiffness-proportional, so the pipe's 2.58 % at its first mode is 5.7 % at its second; matched at the
  second it swings 0.246 D. Strip wake models feed a mode only where the local shedding frequency meets it, so a strongly
  sheared flow feeds less span than the measurement shows; the paper's CFD resolves the wake along the span and is within
  5 %.
- **Ruled out (2026-11-27):** the drag's damping outside the lock-in span (a mean drag of 0.5 or 0.25 in place of 1 leaves
  the swing at 0.27 D and 0.24 D, so the swing is short of excitation, not over-damped); locking each wake's frequency to its
  segment's own cross-flow frequency within a band of the local shedding (30 %: 0.246 D; 60 %: the third mode, 0.11 D).
- **Tried (2026-11-27), not landed:** the synchronization model of Thorsen, Saevik and Larsen (2016, its open preprint and
  Thorsen's 2016 thesis): an excitation 1/2 rho D U^2 C_v(y0 / D) cos phi whose phase locks to the velocity across within
  f D / U of 0.10 to 0.26, with their C_v (optimised on the NDP riser, read from their Fig. 7) and synchronization function
  (their Fig. 4), no new fitting. With their damping in place of the drag's across, it takes this case to 0.453 D (+11 %),
  but the towed pipe at 1.6 m/s swings 1.4 D in its first mode, and the 0.4 m/s and 0.6 m/s shear cases run 42 % and 128 %
  high. With the drag's damping kept beside theirs: -6 % and +14 % on the towed pipe, but +45 % on the 0.6 m/s shear and
  -35 % here. Their excitation was fitted to a different riser; no variant without new fitting matches all four cases.
- **Calibrated (2026-11-27), not landed:** the same model with its C_v scaled to the two towed cases (half its height): the
  towed pipe within -2 % and -9 % across, but the gentle shear +47 % and the strong shear -15 % in its first mode where the
  test shows the second, and the towed pipe at 1.6 m/s flips to a first-mode swing of about 1 D at nearby scalings. A fit
  on uniform flow does not carry to shear.
- **Open:** a model of the wake's correlation along a sheared span (the paper's own CFD, which resolves the wake strip by
  strip, is within 5 % on this case).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a pinned rod blew up at coarse steps under high tension, and at fine steps when stretched (KB-PHYS-RODSTRING1, physics rod)

- **Repro:** a `Rod` of 48 links, 7.9 m, 1.77 kg/m, bending stiffness 1 N m^2, pinned at both ends and brought to 48 kN (its
  pinned ends stretched 3 %), then plucked: at 30 and 60 steps a second it swung to hundreds of metres; at 2,400 the kernel
  stopped it (a link past 1e15).
- **Cause:** two. The tension's stiffness across the links reached them only through the pins' reach along the tree, held
  explicitly (about 2,000 rad/s on a link at 48 kN). And a pin that gives held across at h^2 k = 10^6 m, a stiffness that
  grows as 1 / h^2: at 2,400 steps a second a rounding gap of 3e-8 m was a pull of 10^6 N on a link, whose turn with the link
  the solve held explicitly.
- **Fix:** the tree's solve holds the tension's stiffness per link (`add_tension_stiffness`, Tournier et al. 2015's
  geometric stiffness, by the tension's share of each joint's turning stiffness); a pin that gives holds across at a thousand
  times its give (`pin_spring`, PIN_GIVE). Regression `packages/physics/tests/rod.test.js`, "a cable whose tension dwarfs its
  bending stiffness stays whole at 30, 60, 600 and 2,400 steps a second" (its swing within the pluck's 0.76 mm at each).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: KVLCC2 was too course-stable in shallow water (KB-SHIP-SHALLOW1, physics ship)

- **Cause:** Ankudinov et al.'s 1990 factors on KVLCC2 raise Y'v and N'r faster than captive tests measure, and N'v
  slower. The hull-propeller-rudder interaction constants also stayed as in deep water. Captive tests show N'r growing much
  more slowly than N'v at h/T 1.5: 1.22 against 2.61 times deep on KVLCC2 (Nguyen et al. 2020), 1.19 against 2.33 on
  Esso Osaka (Kijima et al. 1984). Ankudinov gives 1.55 against 2.10.
- **Fix:** a hull can carry its own measured table (`ManoeuvringModel.shallow`), which `shallowWater` uses in place of
  Ankudinov's factors (`packages/physics/src/ship/shallow.ts`). KVLCC2's table, `KVLCC2_SHALLOW`, holds:
  - its linear hull derivatives;
  - surge derivatives and resistance;
  - a_H, x'_H, gamma_R, 1 - t_P, w_P and epsilon,
  each from captive tests at h/T 2.0, 1.5 and 1.2 (docs/clean-room.md).
- **Calibration:** one value, N'r at h/T 1.2, where the captive tests disagree twofold. It is fitted to KRISO's 20/5
  overshoot there.
- **Checked against data not fitted:**
  - At h/T 1.2: KRISO's 20/10, FHR's two 20/5 overshoots, and the turn's reach, all within 20 percent.
  - At h/T 1.5: the reach within 10 percent, and the 20/10 28 percent under.
  - At h/T 2.0: the reach within 11 percent.
  The 20/5 at h/T 1.5 stays 45 percent under KRISO's 8.0, an accepted difference recorded with its cause in
  docs/limits.md.
- **Test:** "banks and shallows against measurement" and "in shallow water a hull's derivatives and added masses are
  Ankudinov's or its own table's" in `packages/physics/tests/ship.test.js`.
- **History:** filed at 2.1 and 3.3 degrees of 20/5 overshoot at h/T 1.2 and 1.5, where KRISO measured 3.8 and 8.0.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: KCS heeled out too far as it started a turn and too little in the steady turn (KB-SHIP-HEEL1, physics ship)

- **Fix:** the steady-turn roll moment is a near-cancellation: the hull's outward moment (-0.13 q d) against the rudder's
  inward one (+0.08). The rudder's roll lever sets the steady heel, and the roll damping sets the peak. Fukui et al. print
  neither for KCS. Both are now fitted to MARIN's measured final and largest roll (5.09 and 16.98 degrees), in
  `packages/physics/src/ship/kcs.ts`: the lever 0.236 d below the water plane (where the geometric centroid is 0.54 d) and
  the decay coefficient a = 1.0.
- **Checked against data not fitted:**
  - KRISO's largest roll (15.0 to 15.5): within 12 percent.
  - The two sides' mean steady roll against 4.58 to 5.09: within 10 percent.
  - The turn stays inside the measured advance and tactical diameter.
  - The 20/20 and 10/10 first overshoots: 5 to 7 percent under the measured band.
- **Test:** "KCS heels outward in its turn" in `packages/physics/tests/ship.test.js`.
- **Also found on the way:** the measured rudder force has the same 35/20-degree ratio as the model's (Yun et al. 2021,
  C_Ry), so the rudder's force is not what was wrong.
- **Not fixed by this:** the steady turn's speed (0.41 to 0.44 of approach) and drift (16 degrees) stay below the
  measured 0.44 to 0.50 and 19 to 19.7. They do not set the heel: steady heel moved under 0.04 degrees across a sweep of
  the hull's derivatives.
- **History:** first filed after a time-boxed search. Its largest heel was 19 degrees and its steady heel 2.9 to 3.7.
- **Ruled out before the fit (2026-11-27):**
  - The roll damping: the decay coefficient from 0.035 to 0.4 moves the peak only from 19.1 to 16.9 degrees and leaves
    the steady heel unchanged. The peak is quasi-static, set by the early turn's speed.
  - The added roll inertia: 0 to 0.4 of the ship's own moves the peak by 2 degrees and leaves the steady heel unchanged.
  - The heel terms in surge, sway and yaw: with all of them off the steady heel is 3.1 degrees.
  - c_gamma: no effect.
  - The surge cross term: X'_vr + m'_y in place of X'_vr - m'_y slows the turn to 0.28 of the speed and the heel to 0.3
    degrees, so the reading in `kcs.ts` stands.
  - The wake change with drift: symmetric constants give 3.3 degrees on both sides.
  - GM 0.60 m and KM / d 1.3839 match SIMMAN's and Fukui et al.'s particulars.
  - Fukui et al.'s added masses: they set the split of the combined captive terms, not the steady heel.

### Open 2026-11-27: a capsule-chain rod under tension over a bollard blows up (KB-PHYS-RODWRAP1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** a `Rod` of 48 links (radius 5 mm, nylon) draped half a turn over a fixed cylinder of radius 0.2 m, a free
  10 kg body pinned to each end, gravity on: it blows up within two seconds, with friction 0.3 or 0.
- **Cause:** the contacts act on each link through its own mass, a few grams, while the rope's tension of about 100 N runs
  through the multibody's implicit tree solve after the contact passes, so the exchange gains energy each substep.
- **Tried (2026-11-27, branches `claude/rodwrap-wip` to `-5`, not landed):** the tree's contacts with fixed bodies in its
  own implicit solve, with rounds that let go of pulling points and slide those past friction. A chain on a floor and a
  draped rope rest, and two plain bugs of that code were found (a fixed root's stale contact list; sliding friction past
  the stop); but the contact set flips between rounds under tension, and the variants either never slide on a slope or
  do not rest. A fix that keeps the contact passes needs the contacts and the tension in one solve.
- **What to use instead:** a rope over bollards, pulleys or fairleads is `WrappedRope` (`@margoengine/physics/wrapped-rope`), whose
  wraps carry the capstan law exactly (`packages/physics/tests/wrapped-rope.test.js`). The capsule-chain `Rod` stays the
  rope for free spans, contact with moving bodies and bending.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a weight on a rope's end was thrown off, or blew the world up (KB-PHYS-PINFREE1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/rod.test.js`, "a weight on a rope's end hangs still": a rope pinned at the top with a
  free 2 kg body on its end. The weight went 19 m up in 3 s; a 50 g weight blew the world up at once.
- **Cause:** a rod's end is pinned to the body in the multibody's tree solve, a stiff implicit spring (PIN_STIFFNESS times
  the link's mass) to the body's anchor taken as moving at its speed. That is right for a fixed or massive body. A free
  body took the whole spring back explicitly afterwards, so stiff pins to light bodies gained energy every substep.
- **Fix:** for a dynamic body, the pin's spring eliminates the body's velocity within the step. With W the body's
  mobility at its anchor, C and the pull are taken through (I + C W)^-1, and the body takes the same impulse back. A fixed
  or kinematic body keeps C as it was.
- **Regression:** the test above, at 2 kg and 50 g.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: SEA-12 first-frame buoyancy uses the updated centre of mass (KB-LOADS-INITIALCOM)

- **Repro:** Turn a submerged sphere's body 90° about Y and move its local mass centre 0.375 m along X through
  `setMassProperties` or a collider translation. The initial rigid port still reports the origin, so the first
  buoyant step loses the expected torque from the 0.375 m arm.
- **Cause and fix:** Native `update_mass` updated the body-local centre and left the world centre unchanged until
  the solver ran. The mass update now stores both centres, using the body's current rotation and origin.
  `packages/physics/tests/loads.test.js` checks the first published centre and the independent buoyancy torque for
  both edits. [Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics, section 3.3.1](https://modernrobotics.northwestern.edu/nu-gm-book-resource/3-3-1-homogeneous-transformation-matrices/)

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a rod in a PhysicsWorld lost its wake state on a seek (KB-PHYS-RODSEEK1, physics)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/rod.test.js`, "a seek equals a continuous run": a riser in a current with
  vortex-shedding loads, stepped by `RigidSolver`, snapshotted, run on, restored and re-run.
- **Cause:** the rod's water loads keep van der Pol wake oscillators in JavaScript, outside the kernel. `RigidSolver`
  snapshotted and hashed only the kernel's memory, so a restore put the rod back with the wake of the later time, and the
  re-run went another way.
- **Fix:** attachments with `takeState` and `restoreState` are listed by `physics.statefulAttachments()`. `RigidSolver`
  keeps their words in a world region of its extra state, written after each step and put back into them when a restore
  changed it. `segmentLoads` sizes its state when the rod is made (`prepare`), so it has one length. A stateful
  attachment added after the world began is refused with a coded error.
- **Regression:** the test above, which fails without the region, and the frame-rate check beside it.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: GPU picking hit a one-sided material on instances seen from its culled side (KB-PICK-MIRRORROWS1, selection)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/material-back-side-gpu-check.js` (WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, RTX A6000 and Intel Arc
  140V): every instanced pick row read `[true,true]` where `[false,false]` is wanted, at 4x and 1x ("front instances
  back automatic gpu" and the explicit and back-instance rows); the drawn picture of the same rows was right.
- **Cause:** d31534edc1 (KB-PICK-INSTMOVE1) drew instanced primitives through `PickingPrimitives` and picked one with
  any mirrored row (the fixture's second row has x scale -1) from both sides, on the reading that the colour pass then
  draws it unculled. The colour pass does draw it with no pipeline culling, but its shader tests each face against
  the row's handedness (gltf/pbr `model.ts`, `face`), so a front-only or back-only material stays one-sided on every
  row; picking took the whole set as double-sided.
- **Fix:** the instanced pick shader carries each row's handedness (the sign of its matrix determinant, a flat
  varying) into its face test with the node's, and the `side` of such a primitive is no longer turned to double. One
  shader serves picking and the selection mask, so both follow.
- **Regression:** `scripts/material-back-side-gpu-check.js` (840 checks, 0 failures on both back ends; 8 failed
  before); `packages/selection` CPU tests and `instanced-move`, `picking`, `models` and `hit-details` browser checks
  pass.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: OIT `blending: true` failed every frame on a glass with a thickness map (KB-OIT-BLENDTHICK1, gltf)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/oit/test/gpu/real-check.mjs` (RTX A6000 and Intel Arc
  140V): GlassVaseFlowers under `OIT.attach(engine, { blending: true })` gave "In entries[10], binding index 10 not
  present in the bind group layout", then "[Invalid CommandBuffer] is invalid" on every submit. Passed on 6a79dc30b
  (2026-11-25), failed on 3b3db1b10 (2026-11-26).
- **Cause:** gltf builds a draw's group 1 from the material's maps, while each pipeline's `layout: 'auto'` holds only the
  bindings its own entry points statically use (WebGPU, "default pipeline layout"; WGSL, "Statically Accessed",
  W3C Candidate Recommendations, https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/ and https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/). 212d482e00 (KB4000)
  put a transmissive material with a thickness map on the extended shader, which binds that map at slot 20 (binding
  10). Only the transmission tint (`margoTint`, `margoVolumeTint`) reads it; under OIT blending the lit draw is the
  `transparent` entry, which never does, so its layout had no binding 10 and the group was invalid. Earlier
  per-case guards in `textureGroup` (packed base maps, unauthored physical maps, the view block) covered other
  bindings of the same class.
- **Fix:** gltf notes, when it makes a pipeline, which bindings of each group its vertex and fragment entry points reach
  (`staticBindings` in `packages/gltf/src/group.ts`: functions reachable from the entry points by name, the resources
  they name; shader text ships with no comments, KB-WGSL1), and `pipelineGroup` binds only those. The thickness map
  stays in the tint's group and out of the lit draw's.
- **Regression:** `packages/gltf/test/static-bindings.test.js` (the reachability, and the OIT blending shader of a
  thickness-mapped glass: `transparent` binds no slot 20, `margoTint` does); `packages/oit/test/gpu/real-check.mjs`
  passes on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (failed on main). gltf CPU tests (610), `scripts/test-gltf-browser.mjs`,
  `scripts/gltf-pbr-materials-gpu-check.js`, `packages/gltf/scripts/test-extensions-browser.js`,
  `packages/gltf/scripts/test-native-volume.mjs` and `packages/oit/test/gpu/blending-check.mjs` pass. gltf/pbr is
  91,150 B gzip.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: rain and hail streaks drew negative light at 4x (KB-SKY-STREAKCENTROID1, sky and weather)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/sky/test/sleet-check.html` through `features-check.mjs sleet`, reading Bloom's HDR
  capture: 7 pixels of the rain frame at 4x below 0 (to -0.0305), on the RTX A6000 and AMD RDNA2 alike; none at 1x. On
  AMD one of them was the check's "worst" 0.1 (the relative step of a channel near 0).
- **Cause:** the rain streak's opacity is `(1 - uv.x^2) mix(0.15, 1, uv.y)` and hail's `1 - uv.x^2`, with `uv` from
  the quad's corners. At 4x a pixel is shaded when any sample is covered, at its centre, which can lie outside the
  streak, so `uv` extrapolated past 1 and the opacity went negative; straight alpha blending then pushed the frame below
  its own value, under 0 on dark ground.
- **Fix:** the varyings of the rain and snow overlay (`packages/sky/src/weather.ts`) and of hail
  (`packages/weather/src/hail.ts`) use centroid sampling (`@interpolate(perspective, centroid)`, WGSL; `centroid` on
  the WebGL2 layer), which keeps them at a covered point of the primitive, and the opacity terms clamp at 0 for
  rounding.
- **Regression:** `sleet-check.html` counts pixels below 0 in every frame and `features-check.mjs sleet` requires none
  (7 before, 0 after on the RTX A6000, AMD and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`). Its "drew elsewhere" count now takes a pixel sleet
  moves by one half-float step where neither kind alone moved the resolved mean (1 on AMD, 2 on the RTX A6000 after) into
  the one-step budget with the others, as for rain and snow pixels.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: orthographic SSAO blurred differently with the eye inside the part (KB-SSAO-ORTHOBLUR1, post)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_GPU=amd node scripts/ssao-gpu-check.js`: "orthographic SSAO depends on the eye position
  along the view: 96 bytes over 2, worst 5" (93 bytes on the RTX A6000 at eaf8d4cc82). Reading SSAO's own textures for
  the far eye and the eye inside the part: depth, gbuffer, view depth (a constant 5.5923 apart) and the raw occlusion
  agree, and the blurred occlusion differs by up to 0.0395, on the RTX A6000 and AMD alike.
- **Cause:** with the eye inside the part, surfaces behind it have a negative orthographic view depth (37,536 pixels
  here). The bilateral blur (`packages/post/src/shaders.ts`, `blurShader`) took its plane prediction only where the
  centre and its neighbour were above 0, a perspective rule, so those pixels compared every tap with the centre's own
  depth and blurred apart from the same pixels seen from farther away.
- **Fix:** in orthographic views the prediction needs both depths non-zero (0 marks no surface); perspective keeps
  above 0.
- **Regression:** `scripts/ssao-gpu-check.js` now also reads back the blurred occlusion for both eyes and requires them
  within one display level: 0.0395 before, 0.0002 after natively and 0.0031 on the WebGL2 layer (one kernel sample of one
  pixel crosses its depth test at 6 m and not at 0.4 m, float32 rounding of the sample position). The picture check
  passes after on AMD, the RTX A6000 and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a radius-0 light beside a sized light shaded 13 to 16 ulps off on AMD (KB-CLUSTERED-SIZEDZERO1, clustered)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_GPU=amd node scripts/clustered-sphere-light-gpu-check.js` (workstation AMD RDNA2 iGPU,
  WebGPU): "roughness 0.05: radius 0 beside a sized light shades as before, bit for bit: {"ulps":16}" and the same at
  roughness 0.5 with 13. The RTX A6000 and the WebGL2 layer passed. Found working KB-GPU-PRECHECKS1.
- **Cause:** the sized shader (some light has a `radius`) wrote each point-light term as a `select` between the point's
  and the sphere's value (`nl`, `sl`, `sh`, `norm`), so a radius-0 light computed the same values through different
  expression graphs (`dot(n, sl)` for `nl` in G, `ggxDOf(n, sh) * norm`). WGSL lets a compiler contract and reorder float
  arithmetic, and AMD's did so differently in the two graphs.
- **Fix:** `packages/clustered/src/shader.ts` keeps the plain loop's statements as they are (`nl`, `d`, `g` and
  `fresnel` become `var`) and overwrites them only inside `if(rs>0.0){...}`, with the same sphere terms as before
  (Karis 2013; Snyder 1996), so a radius-0 light runs the plain shader's own text.
- **Regression:** `packages/clustered/tests/sized-radius-zero.test.js` (the sized loop holds every plain statement in
  order and no select on the radius; fails before) and the GPU check above, which passes after on AMD, the RTX A6000 and
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: the rain shafts' light over a small lit yard was speckle, one step in hundreds of metres (KB-SKY-RAINSTEP1, sky)

- **Repro:** Last Tram sky stills (sky-round-4) show a grainy, even orange sky with no curtains; on the bench, the film's
  deck, scud, mist, ground lights and four rain cells from the yard looking north at 10 degrees: the drops' light has a
  mean neighbour difference of 0.21 of its mean (the whole sky 0.09), bright speckles over the horizon.
  `node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs rain-shaft` case `yard` (a 140 m lit disc under the camera in 1 to 4 mm/h):
  0.68 at origin/main 981400fadb.
- **Cause:** `cloudRain` in `packages/sky/src/rain-shafts.ts` marched the air band in 16 even steps (500 m over 8 km)
  and took the ground lights at one point per step, at the drop's own height. The light of a disc on the drops changes
  over its radius and the drop's height, a few tens to a hundred metres near the camera, so a yard under the camera was
  hit by no step or by one, and each pixel's jitter decided which.
- **Measured first, ruled out:** that the drops' light was on another scale from the deck's (the coordinator's
  suspect). Under an overcast base lit by an even ground the rain keeps the base's brightness (1.15 times it,
  `features-check.mjs rain-shaft` case `even`), so the shafts show only where the light round them differs from the
  base's behind them. In the film the drops' light without the yard (0.002 to 0.009) is what they hide where the base
  behind is even and a quarter of it where the base is over the city; the even glow was the near air over the yard,
  the rain's optical depth and the mist.
- **Fix:** the steps grow with distance from a second step of a quarter of the smallest cell or ground light radius
  (`cloudStepPower`, as the cloud march spaces its steps; `rainNearStep` written in cell 0's spare float), each sample
  stratified in its own step, and each step takes the ground lights' mean along its own ground track
  (`cloudGroundTrack`, the closed-form line integral the mist already uses) in place of one point.
- **Regression:** `features-check.mjs rain-shaft` case `yard`: the drops' light within 5 percent of the CPU integral
  (0.998) and a neighbour difference under 0.03 (0.008 after, 0.68 before), WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: sleet's rain drew the drops of the whole precipitation's intensity, not of its own share (KB-SKY-SLEETLAW1, sky)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs --max=6 -- node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs sleet` on an RTX
  A6000 (origin/main 50e4e322ce, after `npm run build:packages`), WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` alike: "sleet off by more
  than one half-float step", 354 of 399 rain-only pixels differ from the rain drawn alone (worst 0.43), against a 1 %
  budget. It passed on 8d31e3f9d5.
- **Cause:** 7c9dbd15d2 gave each raindrop a size from Marshall and Palmer's law. Without `rainRate`, `drawKind` in
  `packages/sky/src/weather.ts` read the law at `80 * intensity^3` of the whole precipitation, while the rain's
  particles are its share of it: sleet at 0.6 with half snow drew rain at 0.3's particles with rain at 0.6's drops
  (bigger, faster, other streaks).
- **Fix:** the law reads `80 * (intensity * share)^3`, the rain's own rate, so sleet's rain is the rain at its share of
  the intensity; plain rain (share 1) and an explicit `rainRate` or `rainFrom` are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/sleet.test.js` "sleet's rain takes the drop sizes of the rain drawn alone at its
  share of the intensity" (the law's slots of the rain uniform; fails before) and the GPU check above, which passes after
  on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: 399 and 431 rain pixels at 4x and 1x, 0 off by a step.
- **Source:** J. S. Marshall and W. McK. Palmer, "The distribution of raindrops with size", J. Meteor. 5, 165 to 166,
  1948, https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0469(1948)005%3C0165:TDORWS%3E2.0.CO;2 (the law is of a rain's own rainfall rate).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: five package GPU checks failed in the rerun made for the clear colour fix (KB-CLEAR-CHECKS1)

### Fixed 2026-11-27: an `-srgb` view target without `viewFormats` failed with a raw validation error (KB-VIEW-SRGB-ERROR1, core)

- **Repro:** `engine.render({ views: [{ camera: engine.camera, viewport: [0, 0, 1, 1], target: { color } }] })`
  with `color` an `rgba8unorm-srgb` texture created without `viewFormats: ['rgba8unorm']`: native WebGPU reports a
  validation error for `createView` and the view draws nothing; the WebGL2 layer draws it.
- **Cause:** core draws such a target through a view in its non-srgb twin format (KB-VIEW-SRGB1), which WebGPU makes
  only of a texture that names the twin. `GPUTexture` does not expose `viewFormats`, and core adds no check of its own.
- **Fix:** core makes that view inside a validation error scope when the target's format is not the one it draws in;
  a refusal becomes `TypeError: Invalid view target: add viewFormats ['rgba8unorm']` (the format named is the twin),
  linked to the errors page's `views` entry, which the next frame throws. The uncaptured-error handler keeps the first
  failure of a frame (`??=`), so the raw command-buffer error that follows does not replace it. No package can hold
  it: the view is made inside core's frame. Size (`npm run measure:size`, RTX A6000 workstation): core + stage 24,910 B
  to 24,989 B gzip (raw 61,246 to 61,423), under the 25,000 B limit, which is unchanged. The WebGL2 layer still draws
  such a target, as before.
- **Regression:** `packages/core/tests/view-srgb.browser.mjs`, the target without `viewFormats`: native WebGPU must
  report the coded error (the parent reports `MargoError: [Invalid CommandBuffer] is invalid due to a previous error`
  and fails it); the WebGL2 layer must draw it. `tests/support/core-draw-gpu.js` gains the device's error scopes.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: `bounce` and `shadowTint` averaged the ground masks' edge pixels, where the frame mixes lit and shadowed ground (KB-LOOK-TV-BOUNCE1, headless)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-rail-line.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out <dir>`
  with `page.query` `{"weather": "calm"}`: bounce 146.5 percent early and 117.7 mid (bound 10 to 35), shadowed ground
  brighter than lit ground under a full sun. The default (blowup) shot read 114.6 and 130.3.
- **Cause:** the shaded-ground mask of that shot is mostly strips a few pixels wide between plants and trunks. The
  masks come from a sharp capture, while the frame is resolved from 2 x 2 supersamples with 8-subframe motion blur,
  depth of field and bloom, so a strip's edge pixels hold the lit ground's light (mixed pixels: P. Fisher, "The pixel:
  a snare and a delusion", Int. J. Remote Sensing 18(3), 679-685, 1997, https://doi.org/10.1080/014311697219015).
  `bounce` and `shadowTint` averaged every mask pixel. Split by mask erosion on the calm early probe: 146.5 percent with
  the edges, 45.1 with one pixel off, 17.2 with two, 15.0 with three and 15.1 with four, and divided by the captured
  albedo the same; the scene's lights (sun 3.21 at 29.5 degrees up, ambient 0.1) give 19 percent on level soil. The
  terrain shading was right; the measure was not.
- **Fix:** `meanLab` in `packages/headless/src/look.ts` averages each ground mask's interior, `GROUND_INSET` (1/360 of
  the frame's shorter side: 3 pixels at 1080p, 1 at 360p) in from every edge, as `grain` and `speckle` already read
  their masks' interiors. The bound is unchanged. Rail-line shot after the fix: calm reads bounce 15.0 and 25.1 percent
  and shadowTint 19.1 and 17.5 b* (pass); blowup see KB-LOOK-TV-PALL1.
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js`, "T6 bounce and shadowTint read the ground masks inside
  their edges": 9-pixel shadow strips under a 5 x 5 blur read 31.6 percent before the fix against 23.6 sharp, and the
  same 23.6 after it.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: under the blowup's smoke pall the rail-line ground's shadows hold 73 to 87 percent of the lit ground and are 1 to 2 b* cooler (KB-LOOK-TV-PALL1, headless/look, sky, shot tool)

- **Repro:** the rail-line shot above at its default weather (blowup, 16:00), after KB-LOOK-TV-BOUNCE1: bounce 72.9
  percent early and 86.8 mid (bound 10 to 35), shadowTint 1.91 and 1.04 b* (bound 3 or more).
- **Cause:** the light under the pall. The scene record (`--measure`) gives a sun of intensity 0.249 and colour
  [1, 0.30, 0.04] (3.9 percent of the calm sun's luminance) and the same white ambient 0.1, so level soil takes
  0.0167 of its albedo from the sun and 0.1 from the sky: 86 percent in shadow, which the frame reads. A dense smoke
  pall does this to real light: at Izana in August 2023, with aerosol optical depth 2.25 to 3.63 at 500 nm, direct
  normal irradiance fell 72 to 99 percent and global only 21 to 27 percent (R. D. Garcia et al., "Impact of spectral
  aerosol radiative forcing at the Izana observatory during the August 2023 extreme wildfires", Atmos. Meas. Tech. 19,
  3151-3167, 2026, https://doi.org/10.5194/amt-19-3151-2026), so nearly all the light is diffuse and shadows fade; smoke
  absorbs blue, so the diffuse light is not cooler than the sun's.
- **Decision owed:** the T6 bound (10 to 35 percent, cooler shadows) describes sunlit ground. Scott decides whether a
  shot under a smoke pall is held to it, is exempt from T6, or the blowup is lit differently. No bound was moved.
- **After KB-TERRAIN-SKYAMBIENT1 (2026-11-26):** the ground now takes the smoky sky's own light instead of the white
  floor, and the blowup reads bounce 93.4 and 91.3 percent, shadowTint 0.33 and 0.68 b*: the diffuse light under the pall
  is brighter and warmer than the floor was, as the Izana measurements describe. Still the same decision; no bound moved.
- **Decision (Scott, 2026-11-26, "Limits that follow the light"):** the T6 limits are derived per shot from its own
  lights; the sunlit 10 to 35 percent and 3 b* stay the clear-sun case, never loosened beyond what the lights predict.
- **Fix:** the T6 limits held every shot to sunlit ground because the look checks saw only frames and masks, not the
  light. `@margoengine/sky` gains `Sky.irradiance(normal?)`, the light its shader took, read back from the GPU; the shot
  tool records each probe's `light` (core's sun and that irradiance on level ground, or `lighting.ambient` x
  `radiance[3]` with no sky); `@margoengine/headless/look` `lightBounds` gives the diffuse fraction d and the limits:
  unchanged up to `CLEAR_SUN_DIFFUSE` (0.3336, Erbs, Klein and Duffie 1982 at the clear-sky clearness index 0.65, Fakra et
  al., Renewable Energy 36(1) 298-306, 2011, https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5259), above it `bounce` x d / 0.3336 and the
  tint floor x (1 - d) / (1 - 0.3336). Rail line: blowup d 0.943 and 0.942, limits 28.3 to 99.0 and 28.2 to 98.8
  percent, tint floors 0.25 and 0.26 b*, read 93.4 and 91.3 percent and 0.33 and 0.68 b* (pass); calm d 0.340 and
  0.400, limits 10.2 to 35.6 and 12.0 to 42.0 percent, read 17.6 and 28.9 (pass). Calm's light is more diffuse than a
  clear sky's at its sun (29.5 degrees up, under the valley's cloud deck), so its limits moved by what d predicts.
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js`, "T6 limits follow the light": a clear sun keeps exactly
  10 to 35 and 3 b*; the pall's frame passes under the pall's light and fails under a clear sun; sunlit 20 percent
  shadows fail under the pall. `packages/sky/test/sky-light-units-check.mjs`: `Sky.irradiance()` predicts the measured
  plate share within 0.003 on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: terrain's ambient light was a white floor, not the sky's light or `lighting.ambient` (KB-TERRAIN-SKYAMBIENT1, terrain, sky, biomes)

- **Repro:** `packages/terrain/src/shader.ts`, the fragment: `linear=direct*frame.radiance.xyz*frame.light.w+base*frame.radiance.w`.
  The terrain `Frame` had no ambient field, and `Sky.add(terrain)` threw (terrain's `addLighting` takes `shader` and
  `bindings`, the sky gave `pbr` and `bindings`).
- **Cause:** core meshes, gltf/pbr and materials take the sky's nine-coefficient irradiance (`skyIrradiance`) or
  `lighting.ambient` times `radiance[3]`; terrain took only `radiance[3]`, which the sky sets to its ambient floor
  (0.1 in timber valley), white. Shaded ground was lit by a grey floor while a rock beside it was lit by the blue sky.
- **Fix:** terrain's frame gains `ambient` (`lighting.ambient`, 192 bytes, the floating-origin anchor after it) and its
  term is core's, albedo x `radiance[3]` x `lighting.ambient`. `Sky` implements terrain's lighting contract: `shader`
  leaves the source, `finish` (after every other effect) puts `skyLighting` at group 1, bindings 8, 10 and 11, in the
  flat term's place, keeping what earlier effects multiplied it by (layer occlusion, relief sky visibility) and a
  `HemisphereLight` beside it, as the sky does on core meshes (nine harmonics, Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan, "An Efficient
  Representation for Irradiance Environment Maps", SIGGRAPH 2001, https://doi.org/10.1145/383259.383317; split-sum
  reflections, Karis, "Real Shading in Unreal Engine 4", SIGGRAPH 2013 course). `BiomeView` adds its ground and far
  ground to its `sky`.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/sky-ambient.test.js` (`Sky.add(terrain)` threw before the fix; the patch, its
  order with `TerrainMaterials` and its bindings) and `packages/terrain/test/sky-ambient.browser.mjs` on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer, the same pixels on both (RTX A6000): no sun and `lighting.ambient` [1, 0.5, 0.25] draw flat grey
  ground at sRGB (82, 50, 14) against (74, 74, 74) white, grey before; a clear noon sky added to the terrain draws
  (20, 22, 31) against (19, 19, 19) without.
- **T6 after it, rail-line shot `--once --seconds 1.1`:** calm bounce 17.6 and 28.9 percent (was 15.0 and 25.1),
  shadowTint 14.9 and 12.8 b* (was 19.1 and 17.5), both inside their bounds; blowup see KB-LOOK-TV-PALL1.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the calm rail-line shot read penumbra grain 0.92 and 0.81 from the plants' own detail, not shadow noise (KB-LOOK-TV-PENUMBRA2, headless look bar)

- **Repro:** the rail-line shot with `{"weather": "calm"}`, `--once --seconds 1.1`: penumbra 0.919 code early and 0.810
  mid (bound 0.7). The default blowup shot passes (0.576 and 0.593 after KB-TERRAIN-SKYAMBIENT1).
- **Cause:** the `penumbra` mask (`@margoengine/post/mrt`) is every sun-facing surface whose sun visibility is partial,
  plants included, and `penumbra` measured it with Immerkaer's estimator ("Fast Noise Variance Estimation", CVIU 64(2),
  300-302, 1996), which assumes the image is smooth where it measures. With the page's `plants` mask (MASKOCCLUDE1),
  same interior and estimator: penumbra on ground 0.558 and 0.504; penumbra on plants 1.218 and 0.921; plants fully lit
  or fully hidden, where no shadow filter runs, 1.610 and 1.289, more than in the penumbra. Foliage texture detail is
  not shadow noise: the estimator counts the plants' needles, leaves and their edges as grain, the bias Tai and Yang
  correct by leaving edge pixels out ("A fast method for image noise estimation using Laplacian operator and adaptive
  edge detection", ISCCSP 2008, https://doi.org/10.1109/ISCCSP.2008.4537384).
- **Fix (manager's ruling, option a with two conditions; the estimator is unchanged everywhere):** `penumbra` reads the
  ground only, the penumbra mask less the `plants` mask, bound still 0.7, and needs `PENUMBRA_MIN_PIXELS` (2,055)
  interior pixels, where the estimate's relative standard error is 5 percent, so a sliver cannot pass. The new
  `penumbraPlants` holds the plants in the penumbra to the plants out of it in the same frame (ratio, bound 1), so
  shadow-filter noise on foliage still fails. The rail-line shot now records the `plants` mask. Calm, early and mid:
  penumbra 0.558 and 0.504 over 22,396 and 9,782 pixels, penumbraPlants 0.756 and 0.714; blowup 0.377 and 0.433,
  penumbraPlants 0.624 and 0.592 (`tools/shot/cli.mjs ... --once --seconds 1.1`, both through `checkProbe`).
- **Regression:** `packages/headless/tests/look-clean.test.js`, "regression KB-LOOK-TV-PENUMBRA2": a fixed leaf texture
  under the penumbra fails the old whole-mask reading and passes the new pair; noise put on the ground in the penumbra
  fails `penumbra`, the same noise on the plants fails `penumbraPlants` and not `penumbra`; and "T1 penumbra and
  penumbraPlants need PENUMBRA_MIN_PIXELS".

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a wind field's turbulence swept past a point at kilometres a second half an hour in (KB-WEATHER-WINDDRIFT1, weather)

- **Repro:** `new WindField({speed: 20, direction: 0.6, gust: 0.8, turbulence: 0.44})`, sampled at one point every
  1/30 s from t = 1800 s: steps of up to 6.07 m/s a frame (9.1 during a machine's blend), against a few tenths at t = 0.
  In the timber-valley rail-line shot, the scatter wind read from it swung strength 0.86 to 0.61 and turned 9 degrees in
  40 ms, and every plant shook.
- **Cause:** `sample` carried the noise by `directionAt(t) x speed x t`, the gusting direction times the whole elapsed
  time, so a wobble of 0.06 rad/s moved the pattern 36,000 x 0.06 m a second. `WeatherMachine` also changed the mean
  wind under a pattern placed by `speed x t`, so a blend made it jump.
- **Fix:** the pattern is carried by the integral of the mean wind (Taylor 1938): `drift(t)`, `set(options, at)`
  rebases it at the machine's time, and `resetTime` calls `resetDrift()`. Sources in docs/clean-room.md.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/wind-drift.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: tonemap's settings check on the WebGL2 layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11 differed by one pixel in group `local` about half the time (KB-TONEMAP-LOCALD3D1, tonemap)

- **Repro:** `node packages/tonemap/tests/settings-browser.mjs --compat` on the workstation (RTX A6000, Chrome, ANGLE
  Direct3D 11): it failed 2 of 4 runs, then 4 of 6 and 2 of 3, at "local: the sweep's last frame is what writing its
  values once draws" or "local: the defaults written leave the frame exact", one pixel (green 176 against 177).
- **Cause:** the check compared frames that each drew the scene again, and on this driver the same draw does not
  always give the same half floats. Every compared frame's scene target was copied to a buffer without a wait and read
  at the end: 4 values at 4 fixed places inside the white box (two of them diagonal neighbours) take one of two states
  one step apart (16677 or 16678, 16796 or 16795), flipping between frames of one effect as well as between rebuilt
  effects, with antialias on and off. Every WebGL call of two such consecutive frames was recorded (name, arguments,
  the hash of every uniform and buffer upload, the identity of every texture, framebuffer, program and buffer): both
  frames made the same 133 calls on the same objects with the same data and still drew different values. So the
  difference is below the WebGL API (ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end or the driver) and the engine cannot make it exact;
  `LocalExposure` only lifts the step across an 8-bit boundary. A GPU wait after each frame changed the timing enough
  to hide it, which is why waits and more frames seemed to cure it. The earlier "not seen with `--use-angle=gl`" was
  SwiftShader, not OpenGL (see KB-TONEMAP-CURVEGL1).
- **Fix:** the check renders the scene's HDR frame once, keeps it in a texture (copied texel for texel by
  `textureLoad`) and gives it to every effect it compares as `options.source`, so the exact comparisons tonemap one
  input. No comparison is loosened: every channel of every pixel still has to match.
- **Regression:** `packages/tonemap/tests/settings-browser.mjs` asserts that every compared frame of every group
  tonemaps the kept frame ("every compared frame tonemaps the kept HDR frame"); an effect that captures the scene
  itself, as every effect of the old check did, fails it on every run. Native passed, and the WebGL2 layer on Direct3D 11
  passed 6 of 6 runs (2026-11-26).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: with `--use-angle=gl`, tonemap's settings check saw no GPU object from `tonemap.curve` (KB-TONEMAP-CURVEGL1, tonemap)

- **Repro:** `node packages/tonemap/tests/settings-browser.mjs --compat` with Chrome started with `--use-angle=gl`
  (workstation, RTX A6000): 3 of 4 runs failed at "tonemap.curve is live: false because it makes GPU objects".
- **Cause:** two things. Headless Chrome on this PC does not run ANGLE's OpenGL back end with that flag: the WebGL2
  renderer is SwiftShader (`ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero)))`), and in 2 of 3 runs its
  first context was lost about 2 ms after the engine was made, so the engine restored itself on a new device. The
  check counted GPU objects by wrapping the methods of the first device only, so after the restore every count stayed
  0: the "makes GPU objects" assertions failed, and the "60 frames made no GPU objects" ones passed without counting
  anything.
- **Fix:** the check wraps the device's class instead of one device, calls `engine.rebootDevice()` itself before it
  starts so the counter has to follow a restore on every run, pushes its validation scope on the device it then has,
  and fails with "the device was replaced during the check" if the device changes later (a scope on a lost device
  would hide its errors).
- **Regression:** the same check: with the old per-device counter, its own `rebootDevice()` leaves every count at 0
  and "tonemap.curve is live: false because it makes GPU objects" fails on every run, on every backend. With
  `--use-angle=gl` (SwiftShader) it passed 3 of 3 runs.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: on the WebGL2 layer a camera that moved every frame was shown no traced image (KB-VPT-ROUTE-MOVING, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro:** at 7e04c03161, `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs denoisehistory`
  (RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11): "moving camera, 1 sample a frame for 30 frames: RMS 185.86 (raw frames 185.86, still
  camera 4.99)" and the case fails; on WebGPU the same case reads 5.44, 16.00 and 2.78. The canvas is as far from the
  converged image with the denoiser as without it, which is what a frame with no traced sample gives. At 6e77101bc2
  the `denoisemoving` case (below) reads 186.28 denoised and 186.28 raw on the layer.
- **Cause:** on the layer's route a frame starts a batch of samples that lands in a later frame: its last census is
  read back, which WebGL2 delivers in a later task (`#routeViewport` in `packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/tracer.ts`). A
  camera change restarted the view, a batch that landed after a restart was dropped (its epoch was not the view's),
  and a view with no samples draws nothing. A camera that moved every frame therefore never got a sample on screen
  until it rested. `denoisehistory` moved the camera every frame; nobody saw it fail because `test:gpu:denoise`
  stopped earlier on the layer (KB-L5a-10).
- **Fix:** a restart for a camera move alone no longer drops the route's work. A batch that starts an image runs on
  through camera moves and is shown when it lands, as the image of the camera it was traced with: the denoiser
  reprojects its history into that camera, and the display writes that camera's first-hit depth. The view keeps that
  image (`held`) until a batch for a later camera lands, so a moving camera sees an image one batch behind (a frame
  or two) in place of none. A batch that would only add samples to an image the camera has left is still dropped, so
  the new camera's first batch starts sooner, and a restart for anything else (scene, options, size, a restored
  device, a released view) drops the batch and the held image as before. `stats.samples` still counts the samples of
  the view's own camera (0 while a held image shows). WebGPU traces inside the frame and is unchanged.
- **Measured (RTX A6000, layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11):** `denoisemoving` (30 frames, the camera moving every frame and
  never waiting for a sample; 8-bit RMS of the last frame against the converged image at the last position): 4.38
  denoised and 16.07 raw, against 16.09 for one raw sample of a resting camera (WebGPU: 4.14, 16.09, 16.09).
  `denoisehistory` and `denoisedisocclusion` read as before on both (5.47, 16.00, 2.80; 6.49, 4.74, 4.64).
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/route-moving.test.js` (CPU, a recording device of the layer: every
  frame of a moving camera draws the image of the camera one frame before, a batch for a camera that was left is not
  added, a scene change drops both), and the `denoisemoving` case of `tests/browser-check.mjs` in `test:gpu:denoise`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a collider of several kernel shapes raises its events and contact pairs once for each piece (KB-PHYSICS2D-PAIRS1, physics2d)

- **Repro:** a ball rolling along a `trimesh`, `polyline`, concave `polygon`, `compound` or `heightfield` collider in
  `@margoengine/physics2d`. It raised `contactstart` and `contactend` each time it crossed from one piece (triangle,
  segment or convex part) to the next, where Rapier raises one `contactstart` while the two colliders touch at all.
  `physics.contactPairs(collider)` listed one pair for each pair of pieces, and `contactPair(a, b)` returned the first
  of them, so `contactPair(a, b).touching` and `intersectionPair(a, b)` could read false while another piece touched.
- **Cause:** the facade (`src/physics.ts`, `collectEvents` and `contactPairs`) passed on the kernel's events and
  contacts per kernel shape without aggregating by unordered collider pair.
- **Fix:** `Physics2D` tracks active shape-pair touch counts per unordered `Collider2D` pair (rebuilt on `restore`),
  emitting start only when count rises from 0 and end only when count drops to 0, and `contactPairs` aggregates all
  shape manifolds for each `other` collider into a single `ContactPair2D`.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics2d/tests/set-shape.test.js` "multi-shape colliders aggregate contact events and contactPair per collider pair (KB-PHYSICS2D-PAIRS1)".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: `Collider2D.setShape` refuses an outline of several kernel shapes (KB-PHYSICS2D-SETSHAPE1, physics2d)

- **Repro:** `collider.setShape({ shape: 'trimesh', ... })`, or any concave polygon, polyline or compound, threw
  `RangeError`. Rapier's `setShape` takes any shape.
- **Cause:** `setShape` only used the kernel's `set_shape_core`, which replaces one convex core in place.
- **Fix:** single-convex-to-single-convex keeps the in-place `shape_set_core` fast path; multi-shape or non-convex
  outlines atomically replace the collider's kernel shapes under the same `Collider2D` via `Physics2D.replaceColliderShapes`,
  preserving settings, seams, explicit mass / mass properties, and carrying active touching pairs across the swap without
  raising duplicate start events. Parity row C2-09 is now DONE.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics2d/tests/set-shape.test.js` "setShape replaces multi-shape outlines in place and preserves settings, mass mode and touching state (C2-09, KB-PHYSICS2D-SETSHAPE1)".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a long thin body that hit a wall hard and spinning swung through it after the first contact (KB-PHYSICS2D-CCD-SPIN1, physics2d)

- **Repro:** a 2 m by 0.1 m box with `ccd: true`, moving at 150 m/s and turning at 8 rad/s toward a 0.1 m thick wall,
  in the own 2D kernel (`packages/physics2d/kernel`). `ccd` set it back to the first touch. On the next step the contact
  turned it at about 112 rad/s about the touching end, and the step swept the rest of its length through the wall: its
  centre ended beyond the wall at step 4.
- **Cause:** continuous collision (`kernel/src/ccd.rs`) left a pair that already touched when a step began to the
  contact solver alone, so that a body at rest is not pinned at time 0. The contact solver sees only the closest points
  of the manifold at the step's start, and a turn of 1.9 rad inside one step is not covered by them.
- **Fix:** a touching pair is swept too, by the same conservative advancement, against the gap it began with: it is
  stopped only where that gap closes by more than four times the linear slop (`TOUCHING_ALLOWANCE`, the penetration the
  contact solver takes out in a step). A body resting on or sliding along a face keeps its gap and is not stopped; a long
  body whose turn drives its length into the face is caught where it would go through.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics2d/kernel/tests/ccd.rs`
  "a_long_bar_hitting_a_wall_hard_and_spinning_does_not_swing_through_it_after_the_first_touch" (spins 8, -8 and
  20 rad/s, 60 steps), with "a_body_resting_on_the_floor_is_not_pinned_by_ccd" still passing.

### Fixed in part 2026-11-26: the voxel path tracer had no subsurface under a diffuse surface (KB1673, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** a `media` material is a cloud: a ray that grazes its edge crosses little of it and sees through,
  so a block of it has soft, see-through edges and lets shadow rays pass. `{ type: 'media', subsurface: true }` was
  an unknown field. Against MagicaVoxel's `_sss` block (the six `G` boards, 1,024 samples) the fitted sun-lit cloud
  matches the block's middle within 2 levels but leaves a bright rim of differences along every edge.
- **Cause:** the tracer had no surface on a medium. Chiang, Kutz and Burley 2016 ("Practical and Controllable
  Subsurface Scattering for Production Path Tracing", SIGGRAPH Talks, <https://doi.org/10.1145/2897839.2927433>) put a
  diffuse interface on the volume and derive the walk's single-scattering albedo from the colour the surface shows
  (their equation 1; it agrees within 0.001 with the inverse of van de Hulst's half-space albedo
  (1 - s)(1 - 0.139 s) / (1 + 1.17 s), s = sqrt(1 - albedo), "Multiple Light Scattering", 1980).
- **Fix:** `subsurface: true` on a `media` material (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/shaders.ts`, `scene.ts`): a cosine
  lobe into the volume at its surface, an isotropic walk, a cosine lobe out where lights are sampled; the volume blocks
  shadow rays; `bounceLimits.subsurface` (now up to 256) caps the walk. WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer give the same
  numbers.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs subsurface` (in `test:gpu:light-transport`):
  a dense white cube cut after 1, 2, 6 and 12 steps returns 0.207, 0.324, 0.532 and 0.650 against an independent
  half-space walk's 0.204, 0.320, 0.528 and 0.644 (bound 0.01); surfaces of colour 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 return 0.205,
  0.506 and 0.800 (bound 0.02); the floor under the cube is black under the sun where a plain medium lets exp(-2)
  through. `tests/contracts.test.js` checks the field and the 256 cap. Both fail on the parent.
- **Still open (MagicaVoxel's `_sss`):** the mapping keeps the fitted sun-lit cloud, because no setting of the new
  model beats it on the references on disk. What the diffuse interface explains, measured on the `G` boards: the crisp
  edges; the black shadow behind the block (0 to 5 levels in both, 6 to 9 with the cloud); the light the block throws
  on its neighbours at diffuse cap 4 and not at cap 2 (entering and leaving are two diffuse events); and the sky-lit
  level, when the walk is cut after 3 steps per diffuse cap: a half-space walk returns 0.529 after 6 steps and 0.648
  after 12, a ratio of 0.816 against MagicaVoxel's (136 / 149)^2.2 = 0.818, and a dense block renders 139 and 153
  against its 136 and 149. What it does not: under the sun at 60 degrees that dense block renders 221 and 242 against
  190 and 205, and at the fitted density the top darkens toward the faces the sun does not light, where MagicaVoxel's
  stays flat across and rises toward the sun. One colour, one density and one sun angle are on disk; telling its
  model apart needs MagicaVoxel renders at other densities, colours and sun angles, and a view of the side faces.
- **Measured and rejected 2026-11-27 (KB1673, KB1664 job 1): the diffuse interface with the sun sampled inside the
  volume.** The two models each match half of what is on disk: the sun-lit cloud of the mapping (sun sampled at each
  scattering point through its own volume) matches the sun-lit top and its slope toward the sun, the diffuse interface
  (`subsurface`) the sky-lit level, the crisp edges and the black shadow. Joined (a local build, not kept): a
  `subsurface` volume that is also `sunlit` samples the sun at every scattering point of its walk, through its own
  volume only, leaves the sun out where the walk leaves, and keeps the sky to the exit lobe. This is plain next-event
  estimation in a medium (Novak, Georgiev, Hanika and Jarosz, "Monte Carlo Methods for Volumetric Light Transport
  Simulation", Eurographics STAR 2018, <https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.13383>), which connects straight through the
  boundary; Koerner, Novak, Kutz, Habel and Jarosz, "Subdivision Next-Event Estimation for Path-Traced Subsurface
  Scattering", EGSR 2016, <https://doi.org/10.2312/sre.20161214>, show such a connection is not consistent with a
  boundary that bends light, and Wrenninge, Villemin and Hery, "Path Traced Subsurface Scattering using Anisotropic
  Phase Functions and Non-Exponential Free Flights", Pixar Technical Memo 17-07, 2017,
  <https://graphics.pixar.com/library/PathTracedSubsurface/paper.pdf>, gather light only where the walk leaves, as
  the tracer's `subsurface` does; whether MagicaVoxel makes the straight connection was the question. Measured on the
  `_sss` cloud tile of board G (`_d` 0.05, white, on a black base; 512 samples; WebGPU, RTX A6000; green channel,
  8-bit; centre, then five points across the top toward the sun, then the rim on the sun side): MagicaVoxel, sun at 60
  degrees: 189, 182 to 201, rim 206; sky: 135, rim 138. The mapping as it is: 191, 184 to 199, rim 187; sky 137, rim
  132. Joined at extinction 0.7 a voxel (the mapping's): 194, a hump 183, 196, 190; sky 145. At 3 and at 10: 203 flat
  across; sky 135, rim 144. So the walk does not take its sun light by straight connections from inside a diffuse
  interface: dense enough for the sky level, the sun reaches only the first voxel and the top is flat and 14 levels
  bright; at the cloud's density the walk leaves through the side faces and the top humps. Rejected; the mapping is
  unchanged. What is left is the sun-facing rim, 19 levels darker than MagicaVoxel's (187 against 206; corners 173
  against 200): light entering through the sun-facing side and leaving through the top near the edge. Telling that
  apart still needs the side-view and other-density renders that `tests/magicavoxel/sss-refs.cjs` writes the scenes for
  (on hold).
