### Fixed 2026-11-26: on ANGLE Direct3D 11 a nested loop's `continue` ran the outer loop's update, and a lone case ran whatever the selector (KB-LOOP-D3D11, KB-SW2, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-control-flow-browser.mjs` on Windows (Chrome 157, RTX
  A6000): native WebGPU and the layer on ANGLE Vulkan give the CPU reference's sums for all fifteen shapes; the layer
  on ANGLE Direct3D 11 gets twelve wrong (an outer `for` with a `select` in its init, condition or update or an `&&` in
  its condition, a `while` whose `&&` calls a function, each around a loop that continues; a switch with one case and
  an empty default, alone or in a loop).
- **Cause (KB-LOOP-D3D11):** read in the HLSL ANGLE made of the guide's program (`WEBGL_debug_shaders`). ANGLE's
  Direct3D 11 back end splits a loop header holding `?:`, `&&` or `||` into statements; it rewrote the guide's
  `for (uint j = guided ? 0u : 1u; j <= count; j++)` as `for (; s; )` and put `j++; s = j <= count;` before every
  `continue` in the body, the inner face loop's too. A hidden face therefore advanced `j` and the face loop went on
  with it, so the guide chose a wrong face (KB-VPT-GUIDE-D3D11). The layer's GLSL was a faithful translation, and the
  `break` was not at fault. The same shape is in `glassCandidates` (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/shaders.ts`, its
  group loop starts at `select(1u, 0u, inGlass)` and its candidate loop continues): with two or more light-sampled
  glass instances a skipped candidate dropped the next group. `glasslight` reads the same before and after, since each
  of its scenes has one such instance. It is also in sciviz's AMR ray march (`packages/sciviz/src/amr-shader.ts`, the
  `visit` loop's `&&` condition around a node walk and a sample loop that continue), where a skipped node or a missing
  sample advanced `visit` and could end the march early.
- **Cause (KB-SW2):** found by the same test's switch shape. ANGLE drops no-op clauses from the end of a switch,
  leaving `switch (x) { case 1: { ... } break; }`, and Direct3D 11's compiler then runs that lone case's body for every
  selector. A second case, or a default with a statement, is right.
- **Fix:** the layer's GLSL (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/glsl/emit.ts`) writes a `for` or `while` whose header holds
  `?:`, `&&` or `||` with no header when a loop inside it continues (`while (true)`, the condition first, a `for`'s
  update after a `do { } while (false)` body), and writes an empty default clause first. Every other loop and switch
  is emitted as before. In the layer's WGSL corpus (3,256 modules) the loop shape is in the four recorded variants of
  the trace kernel's `glassCandidates`, and no switch has one case and an empty default; the guide's program and the
  AMR shader are not in the corpus. A scan of the 21 source files holding a loop with `continue` finds the shape in
  those two only.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-control-flow-browser.mjs` (in the package's `test:gpu`) and the
  two KB-LOOP-D3D11 and KB-SW2 tests in `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: path guiding was wrong on the WebGL2 layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (KB-VPT-GUIDE-D3D11, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** on Windows (Edge 158, RTX A6000), `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node
  packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding-browser.mjs`: the first leg runs on the WebGL2 layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11
  and stops at "guided squared error 807472.092169678 must beat baseline 350.04741706417326 by 2x". WebGPU and the
  layer on ANGLE Vulkan read 10.24 against 350.05.
- **Cause:** the loop in `guidedSurface` (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/guiding.ts`) that picks which visible face
  of a guide box to sample skipped hidden faces with `continue` and left with `break` once the pick was used up. On
  ANGLE Direct3D 11 that six-step loop chose a wrong face. A point on it was still sampled, but `boxPdf` weighs a
  direction by the face a ray enters through, so those samples got another face's density and far too much weight.
  Found by rewriting one loop at a time: the pdf loop alone changed nothing (807,472.092169678 again), the face loop
  alone gives 10.238534781150044, the number ANGLE Vulkan gives. The same GLSL is right on ANGLE Vulkan and the same
  WGSL on WebGPU. The translated HLSL, read later, shows ANGLE's loop rewrite at fault, not the `break`: the outer
  loop's update ran at the face loop's `continue` (KB-LOOP-D3D11, fixed in the layer).
- **Fix:** the face is picked under a flag (`open`), with no `continue` or `break` in the loop; the random numbers
  and their order are unchanged, so WebGPU and ANGLE Vulkan give the numbers they gave.
- **Regression:** `tests/guiding-browser.mjs` gains a leg on the layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (`--use-angle=d3d11`, on
  Windows); `tests/guiding.test.js` fails on a `break` in any loop the guide adds to the shader.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a sped-up water took a tide and a wind on other clocks without a word (KB-SURGE-SCALE1, physics hydro, surge and space)

- **Repro (before):** a `ShallowWaterSolver` at `timeScale: 600` with a `SurgeSolver` reading the tide of a
  `CelestialSolver` at its default scale of 1, or with a `wind` field that gives no scale: both were accepted. The
  tide then ran 600 times slower than the water, and a storm's wind 600 times slower than its pressure (the pressure is
  a function of the water's time, the wind was read at the world's).
- **Cause:** the world's time-scale check sees only solvers that declare `timeScale()`, and the celestial solver took a
  `timeScale` parameter without declaring it; the water read its wind and rain at the world's time whatever its scale.
- **Fix:** the celestial solver declares its scale (a frozen or reversed sky counts as the world's), so a surge at
  another scale is refused its tide. The water refuses a wind or rain whose `timeScale` (1 when it gives none) is not its
  own, with a `state` error naming the fix. The surge's coupling test, which had paired a sky at 3,600 with a water at 1,
  now runs both at 3,600.
- **Regression:** "a surge and a tide refuse what they cannot be made from, naming the fix" in
  `packages/physics/tests/surge.test.js` (a wind with no scale, a wind at 60, and a sky at 1, each refused by a water at
  600; a wind at 600 accepted).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a tensile seam in a cell with no volume reported its points outside the cell (KB-SOFT-SEAMFLAT1, physics/soft)

- **Repro:** `tetrahedron().setTensileSeam({...})` (the volumetric-cut test's cell), then `desc.positions[11] = 0` so the cell is
  flat after `setCells` checked it, then `soft.create(desc)`: the refusal read "A tensile seam point is outside its cell".
- **Cause:** `bindTensileSeam` divided by the cell's determinant without checking it, so every cell coordinate was not
  finite and `locate` blamed the points; its orientation was `Math.sign(determinant)`, 0 for such a cell (the class
  `tests/modern-zero-determinant-normals.test.js` checks).
- **Fix:** the seam refuses a cell whose determinant is within `MIN_TET_DETERMINANT` (the bound `setCells` uses) with a coded
  `unsupported` error naming the cell, and the orientation is `determinant < 0 ? -1 : 1`. SOFT-04 file, changed by lane P
  with the manager's go.
- **Regression:** "a tensile seam rejects points outside its material cell and purely face-aligned triangles" in
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/volumetric-cut.test.js`.
- **Open for the SOFT-04 owner (KB-SOFT-FLATCELLMSG1):** `SoftBodyDesc.setCells` (`packages/physics/src/soft.ts`, the flat-cell
  check) says "Cell N must be flat: its four particles lie in one plane." when it refuses a flat cell; it should say the
  cell must not be flat. Not changed here: soft.ts is the laptop session's file.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a tracked vehicle facing along its up axis ignored every steer (KB-PHYS-TRACKEDUP1, physics)

- **Repro:** `new TrackedVehicle(physics, chassis, { tracks: [{ position: [-1, 0, 0], length: 2 }, { position: [1, 0, 0], length: 2 }], forward: [0, 1, 0] })`
  built a vehicle, and `setInput({ steer: 1 })` drove both belts at the same speed.
- **Cause:** each track's side was `Math.sign(dot(position, cross(up, forward)))`; with forward along up the cross product is
  zero, so every side was 0 and the steer term dropped out. The class check `tests/modern-zero-determinant-normals.test.js`
  flagged the sign of a triple product.
- **Fix:** the constructor refuses a forward along +Y or -Y with a coded `unsupported` error, and a track's side is read from
  its offset along the sideways axis, 0 only for a track on the centre line (no lever arm about up, so steer leaves it alone).
- **Regression:** "a tank refuses what makes no sense, and a disposed one lets go" in
  `packages/physics/tests/vehicle-tracked.test.js` (forwards [0, 1, 0] and [0, -2, 0] refused).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: a body that touches through several colliders crept under a changing load that one collider holds (KB-PHYS-MULTIPAIRCREEP1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** the storm deck of `packages/physics/tests/deck-props.test.js` (roll 20 degrees at 12 s, pitch 4 degrees at 9 s,
  heave 2 m at 9 s, the prop 60 m aft), friction 1.3 times the deck's friction demand, 36 s at 8 substeps, ported to the
  kernel in doubles. A plate of one box collider moved 0.85 mm; the same plate cut into two box colliders on one body moved
  4.7 mm, and cut into four 11.8 mm. The test's chair (a seat on four legs, five colliders) crept 2.9 cm, and kept creeping
  (about 1 cm more each 36 s). A constant load held it: on a floor tilted to tan 0.47 against friction 0.72 the chair stayed
  within a micron.
- **Cause, as measured:** three things, each one pair at a time. (1) Each pair's friction was solved alone, with a cone of
  its own points' normal impulses: when the load changed, the pair solved first took the change and met its share of the
  cone while the body's other pairs still held, and its anchors were cut. (2) Anchors cut one point at a time agree with no
  move of the body, so the points pushed against each other at their cones; on a body of several colliders the normal load
  is shared among many points in no fixed way, and a lightly loaded point met its cone in nearly every substep while the
  patch held well inside its limit surface ((|F| / C)^2 + (T / T_max)^2 at most 0.68 for the chair). (3) A point the narrow
  phase finds new starts with no anchor: when a leg of the rocking chair lifted and came down again, its four points let go
  of where the chair stood, and the chair crept along with each rock. Sweeping the patch's friction to convergence alone
  took the two-box plate to 1.3 mm and the chair to 1.3 cm; more sweeps (64, 256) did not help, and 256 tipped the chair.
  Handing a cut point's lost pull to the uncut anchors made it far worse (the two-box plate 10.8 cm). Fitting the anchors
  with a shift and a turn by least squares held the deck props, but its turn, read from a few loaded points close together,
  reached lightly loaded points far off that took load the next step: in a stack of three bodies of two boxes each the
  anchors grew to hundreds of metres in two seconds and the top two slid off at 7 cm/s (`compound_boxes_stack`).
- **Fix:** the pairs between the same two bodies whose normals agree are one friction patch (`group_patches` in
  `kernel/src/solver.rs`, from the step's canonical lists, so it is the same at any thread count). In the relaxing pass a
  patch's pairs leave their friction to its last pair, which sweeps every point of the patch until it settles or 16 sweeps
  (`patch_friction`); the anchors are still cut point by point from the last sweep, and then all take the patch's shift,
  the mean of its anchors weighted by each point's normal impulse (`fit_patch_anchors`), which never reaches past the
  anchors it is taken of. The same mean is taken once a step when the patch is made, so a point new this step (no load yet)
  takes the patch's anchor. A body with one collider, and the pushing pass, take the path they took before. The plates of
  one, two and four colliders now move 0.85, 0.92 and 0.86 mm, and the chair 1.3 mm; the tilted chair stays within 0.03 mm.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`
  `a_plate_cut_into_four_colliders_rides_the_storm_deck_as_one_collider_does` (each under 1 mm, and two or four colliders
  no more than one plus 0.1 mm; they moved 4.7 and 11.8 mm), `a_chair_rides_the_storm_deck_as_a_plate_does` (under 2 mm;
  2.9 cm) and the guard `a_chair_rests_on_a_floor_tilted_near_its_friction` (under 0.5 mm and 1 mrad, which gates on
  single anchors failed at 5 to 23 cm); `kernel/tests/compound.rs` `compound_boxes_stack` guards the fit;
  `packages/physics/tests/deck-props.test.js` holds the chair to 2 mm with the plate. `kernel/tests/threads.rs` carries a
  chair and a four-box plate in its scene, bit for bit at 1 to 8 threads.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a prop on a deck that rolls and pitches at once slid where its friction held it (KB-PHYS-SPINBCH1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** a block 57 m aft on the storm deck above, driven on a smooth path (`setNextVelocity`), moved 1.4 mm in 36 s;
  roll alone or pitch alone left it within 0.1 and 0.3 mm.
- **Cause:** on a smooth path a body's pose is exp(a(t)) times its start, a(t) a cubic in rotation vectors, and each
  substep it was spun at (b - a) / h for the vectors at the substep's ends. When the spin's axis swings through a step,
  the turn the poses make, exp(b) exp(a)^-1, is not b - a, because rotations do not commute. A prop's friction followed
  the spin while the deck's surface followed the poses.
- **Fix:** the spin is the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff series of the poses' turn to third order, b - a + (a x b) / 2 +
  (a + b) x (a x b) / 12. It is computed from the vectors rather than read off the two quaternions, whose f32 rounding
  would move a point 60 m out by 6 microns a substep. The velocity is the centre's, carried round by that turn.
- **Regression:** `a_smooth_path_spins_each_substep_by_the_turn_its_poses_make_when_its_axis_swings`
  (`packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`): the spin is within the fourth-order bound of the poses' turn at every substep
  of a half-radian step, and b - a misses by ten times more.

### Open 2026-11-26: a prop on a moving deck slips at 32 substeps and more, though friction holds it at 8 and 16 (KB-PHYS-FINECONE1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `a_plate_rides_a_deck_on_a_smooth_path_for_minutes_at_any_substeps` (`packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`)
  with the world's substeps set to 32 or 64: the plate, at friction five times its need, slips about 4 cm in six minutes,
  where at 8 and 16 it holds within 0.2 mm.
- **Cause, as measured:** the contacts are soft constraints of 120 Hz and damping ratio 10, so at fine substeps the
  anchors' pull back of a drift d is close to a fixed speed (bias_rate d, about 37 d per second), set in one pushing
  substep. The relaxing pass then takes that speed back in one go. That impulse does not shrink with the substep, but the
  friction cone a substep holds, mu N h, does. Past about 32 substeps (h under 1/2,000 s) the take-back alone saturates
  the cone at the plate's corners, and each saturation cuts the anchors a little, so the plate slips by the cuts.
  Clamping the anchors to what the cone can pull in a substep instead made a cube at tan 0.49 against mu 0.5 creep and a
  pyramid sleep late, so it was not kept. Gating the relaxing pass's cut by the impulse's direction, or by the impulse
  the pushing pass held, took the 32-substep slip from 4 cm to 2.5 mm, but let a resting chair rock and creep
  (`a_chair_rests_on_a_floor_tilted_near_its_friction` guards it, KB-PHYS-MULTIPAIRCREEP1), so neither was kept.
- **Plan:** ration the anchors' pull to the cone over the step rather than the substep, or solve the anchor and the
  relaxing take-back as one friction row. Until then, keep a world that carries loose props on a moving deck at 16
  substeps or fewer (the default is 8).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a prop on a deck driven to its pose slipped at each step's change of speed (KB-PHYS-KINJUMP1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `a_plate_rides_a_deck_turning_about_an_axis_far_away` (`packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`) run for six
  minutes: the plate, at friction five times its need, slipped 3.6 mm at the world's 8 substeps.
- **Cause:** a kinematicPosition body moved at one speed through a step, (target - pose) / dt, and changed speed only at
  the step's start. A prop on it had to take the whole change of the step in the first substep. Friction holds at most mu
  N h a substep, so wherever the deck's acceleration passed mu g / substeps (0.06 g at 8 substeps and mu 0.5) the prop
  slipped in that substep.
- **Fix:** targets can carry a velocity (`body.setNextVelocity(linear, angular)`, flag SMOOTH_PATH, columns TARGET_LINEAR_X
  and START_LINEAR_X). The body then moves along the cubic Hermite path of its pose, its target and its speeds at both ends,
  each substep at its chord, so its speed changes through the step and is the same across a step's end. Every
  kinematicPosition body's substep pose is now taken along its path from the step's start in one product
  (`kinematic_pose`), not built up from the substeps before.
- **Regression:** `a_plate_rides_a_deck_on_a_smooth_path_for_minutes_at_any_substeps`: six minutes at 8 and 16 substeps,
  within 1e-3 m (0.09 mm measured, 21 cm with the slide tallied at the step's levers); `a_kinematic_body_on_a_smooth_path_lands_on_its_targets_and_moves_through_the_step_at_its_chords`;
  `kernel/tests/threads.rs` with a smooth body under a stack (the same bits on 1 to 8 threads).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a prop slid off a turning deck far from its axis through friction it did not need (KB-PHYS-ANCHORLEVER1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs` `a_plate_rides_a_deck_turning_about_an_axis_far_away`: a deck
  pitching 4 degrees at 9 s and a plate 60 m from the axis, friction 0.5 against a need of 0.1. The plate slid 4 mm each
  pitch, 1.4 cm in 36 s; the slip grew with the distance from the axis (0.1 cm at 3 m) and was the same at three times the
  friction.
- **Cause:** each point's slide was tallied from the speeds at the step's levers, which are fixed for the step. A turning
  body carries its anchor round, so the tally missed the centripetal w^2 r of a lever r, and missed it the same way every
  substep.
- **Fix:** each point's slide is the move of its two material anchor points over the substep: each centre's step, its speed
  times h, and each arm's turn by the substep's spin t = w h, t x arm - t x (t x arm) / 2, at the arm the body has now. It
  is written as a series because an arm less its turned self in f32 is its rounding. A ball or a capsule is read at the
  point it touches, its core's nearest point plus its radius along the normal as the normal rows read it, since a point
  fixed in a rolling ball rolls up off the floor (`next-mesh-seam.test.js`, a capsule rolling across two meshes, kept). Reading the slide off the poses
  instead took in their rounding (a unit of the last place where a resting box moves a fiftieth of one in a substep) and
  made a pile's top boxes jitter, so it was not kept. The solve's levers stay the step's.
- **Regression:** the test above, the plate at the origin and the axis 60 m off, within 1e-3 m over 36 s (0.7 mm measured,
  1.8 cm before).

### Open 2026-11-26: a body far from the origin falls behind its own speed, and slides off a moving deck (KB-PHYS-POSEROUND1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** a deck driven to its pose each step at 17 m/s from 1 km out, its targets worked out in doubles, and a box
  resting on it at its speed (`World` with a KINEMATIC_POSITION deck at x = 1000, the box at friction 0.5): the box falls
  back along the deck 0.43 m a minute, though friction holds it well inside its cone.
- **Cause:** an f32 pose 1 km out moves only in whole units of its last place, 6.1e-5 m. Each substep's move of 0.0354 m
  rounds down the same way, so the box loses 1.2e-4 m every step, and no friction acts on a move a pose cannot make.
- **Tried:** carrying each move's rounding into the next (compensated summation in doubles) held the box to one unit of the
  last place. It also made the residual speeds of resting bodies move them, which the rounding had held still: tall
  piles' residue spread more from moment to moment, and a 210-cube pyramid slept at step 420 where it sleeps by 300
  (`a_pyramid_settles_at_one_pass_a_substep`). So it was not kept.
- **Plan:** a floating origin, `physics.shiftOrigin(offset)` moving every body, target and cached box by an offset. That
  is the remedy rival engines with f32 poses give, and it keeps a scene's working area near the origin. Until then, keep a
  moving scene within a few hundred metres of the origin.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a faded occluder turned solid for the length of a level cross-fade (KB-LOD-FADECOMBO1, lod)

- **Repro:** `LODFade` and `OccluderFade` (`@margoengine/lod/fade`, `@margoengine/lod/occluder-fade`) on one engine; a
  wall with two mesh levels stands between the camera and a target and is faded to `minOpacity` 0.25. Switch its level:
  halfway through the cross-fade the incoming level drew every pixel of its share, so the target was hidden again
  behind 422 of the 1,024 pixels of a 32 by 32 block (`node packages/lod/test/fade-combo-check.mjs`, "both fades", on
  WebGPU), and after the switch the new level took `fadeTime` to fade out again. With Geometry levels the ghost that
  keeps the old geometry on screen drew solid the same way. Each fade alone was exact.
- **Cause:** the two discards themselves combine as intended: a pixel draws when the occluder tile keeps it AND the
  level's noise threshold keeps it, and the levels' thresholds are complementary. But `OccluderFade` keeps its fade per
  mesh (or model) and finds meshes by rays, which pass hidden meshes: the incoming level was hidden until the switch,
  and a ghost is a pooled mesh, so each started at opacity 1 when `LODFade` showed it.
- **Fix:** in lod. `LODFade.begin` (`packages/lod/src/fade.ts`) announces what now draws in place of the outgoing
  level (the incoming mesh or model, and the ghost of a Geometry level) through `standIn` of the shared
  `packages/lod/src/fade-pattern.ts`; `OccluderFade` listens (`onStandIn`) and gives it the outgoing level's fade as it
  stands, in the same call, before a frame draws. From there each is stepped on its own sight lines. No public export
  changed.
- **Regression:** `packages/lod/test/fade-combo-check.mjs` (in the package's `test:gpu`): every pixel of the block
  against `occluderKeeps` and `fadeKeeps`, for core meshes, materials meshes and Geometry levels, each fade alone and
  both together, at the end of the occluder fade, on its way out and on its way back, 0 differing pixels on WebGPU and
  on the WebGL2 compatibility layer; and `packages/lod/test/occluder-fade.test.js`, "a level that cross-fades in, and
  the ghost of a swapped geometry, take the occluder fade at once", on the CPU.
- **Still:** `OccluderFade` dithers core meshes, models and materials meshes; an `Imposter` or `ImposterFrames` level
  is drawn by the LOD system's own shader, which the occluder fade does not patch, so it stays solid in a sight line
  and a switch to or from one hands nothing over (docs/limits.md, occluder fade).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: wind ripples on sand under the sea drew a fine grid through the water (KB-TERRAIN-SANDWET1, terrain)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 on main after KB-WATER-SEABEDMAZE1, once the refraction reached the near
  bed: a fine regular grid of lines over the near water. Turning the sand ripples off removed it.
- **Cause:** `TerrainColors`' wind ripples (`packages/terrain/src/colors.ts`) were drawn on every sand pixel, the sea
  floor and the swash zone included, where wet sand forms none; seen at a grazing angle the 10 cm ripples aliased.
- **Fix:** with a `wetness` record the ripple relief is scaled by one less the record's moisture (`terrainMoisture`),
  so wet and submerged sand is smooth; without a record nothing changes.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/colors.test.js` "wet and submerged sand carries no wind ripples".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: TAA averaged the moving sea into a sideways smear (KB-WATER-TAASMEAR1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 (`examples/kitty-hawk`, 3.6 m up over the sea, TAA on): the near water is
  smeared sideways, no crisp crest or trough. Its lowest quarter measured 0.52 mean horizontal luma step and 1.50 mean
  Laplacian (stills at 1920 x 1080); with TAA off, the same frame measured 1.08 and 3.27. Motion blur and depth of field
  changed nothing (with motion blur off, and at f/8 and f/64, the frames measured the same).
- **Cause:** Water draws no motion vectors and wrote no reactive mask. Its waves move the surface's look (the
  reflections, the ripples, the crests) every frame, so TAA reprojected history by the camera alone and blended ten
  frames of moving waves into one.
- **Fix:** Water writes TAA's reactive mask, `water.reactiveTexture`: 1 where the fastest train's crests move a pixel
  or more a frame, falling to 0 under a quarter pixel, 0 where nothing moves or no water is drawn. Water publishes it on
  the pass context for the frame's encoder and view (`packages/shared/reactive-mask.js`, like the surface depth) and TAA
  reads every published mask by itself, the maximum of several (a sea and a river, or its own `reactive`), compiling the
  masked resolve the first frame one appears. No scene wires it.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/near-detail.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): a plain stage with Water
  and `TAA.attach(engine)`, nothing wired, after 24 moving frames: the parent kept 0.34 of the near sea's fine relief,
  the fix keeps 1.0. The mask reads 1 over the moving near sea and 0 above the horizon and with nothing moving;
  `packages/taa/test/reactive-mask.test.js` covers the registry (encoder and view tags, several publishers).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the near sea had no ripples finer than 30 cm (KB-WATER-NEARDETAIL1, water)

- **Repro:** the same s18 frame: the water 5 to 9 m from the camera, where a pixel covers a few millimetres, is a
  smooth wash of sky reflection with no fine ripples, under a 12 m/s wind.
- **Cause:** Water's shading normal carried its four ripple layers (5 m down to 30 cm) and two short wind-sea bands
  only, at 0.02 to 0.08 RMS slope, while a 12 m/s sea holds most of its slope (Cox and Munk's 0.064 mean square) in
  waves of a metre down to a centimetre.
- **Fix:** with `chop` above 0, five octaves of short-crested gravity-capillary waves (25 cm to 1.8 cm) join the
  normal, each with the slope variance of Elfouhaily et al.'s short-wave spectrum (1997) at the friction velocity of a
  16 x `chop` m/s wind, moving at its own phase speed and fading as a pixel covers it; the variance an octave keeps
  resolved leaves the glint lobe's unresolved share, so the total slope stays Cox and Munk's at every distance.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/near-detail.browser.mjs`: the near sea's 2 to 5 cm relief at chop 0.75 was 1.8
  luma levels; now 13.7 (bar 6).
- **Judged:** a fresh s18 still: the near water shows fine bright and dark ripples and glints, darker between them,
  and its lowest quarter measures 4.12 horizontal step and 17.8 Laplacian (was 0.52 and 1.50). Left: the swell's crest
  pattern is the four authored trains, long-crested toward the horizon, and the whitecaps lie in soft bands along the
  swell crests (KB-WATER-WHITECAPBANDS1, SEA-13).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: white water was lit as a flat grey sheet, and surf foam on a sea without whitecaps took no sky light (KB-WATER-WHITEWATERLIGHT1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 (`examples/kitty-hawk`, 6 m up over the surf under an overcast deck): every
  pixel of dense white water is the same grey, smooth like the sky's reflection on the water round it and little brighter
  than it, so the surf reads as a pale sheet, not foam. A sea with surf or shoreline foam and `whitecaps` 0 drew that foam
  black under a sky with no sun and no ambient.
- **Cause:** `packages/water/src/index.ts` lit foam as albedo times (ambient plus N.L sun plus sky), with a fixed
  albedo, the wave's smooth normal and a 0.95 cover, so dense foam had one radiance (0.72 L under a uniform sky of
  radiance L); and the sky term was added only while `whitecaps` was above 0, so other foam had the scene's ambient alone.
- **Fix:** foam is a multiple-scattering bubble layer lit from above (foamLight): the sky's cosine-weighted radiance
  lights every kind of foam; dense foam reflects 0.84 to 0.87, a deep layer's value (Kokhanovsky 2004, Frouin et al.
  1996), and sparse foam is a thinner two-stream layer under its cover over the dark water, toward measured whitecaps
  (Whitlock et al. 1982, Koepke 1984, Dierssen 2019); the bore's lumps turn its normal for the sky and the sun, hollows
  see less sky, and the relief fades where a pixel covers a lump. Dense foam is opaque (cover 1).
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/whitewater-light.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer), from straight
  above under a uniform grey HDR sky with no sun or ambient: dense whitecap foam's brightest twentieth was 0.725 L with a
  variation of 0.003, now 0.86 L with 0.061; surf foam with no whitecaps was 0 against water at 0.0006, now 0.36
  with a variation of 0.064. whitecaps.browser.mjs keeps its caps crisp and soft-edged (30.6% and 40.1%, parent 31.0%
  and 40.4%) and whitecap-coverage its counts.
- **Judged:** a fresh s18 still: the near roller shows bright lumps and grey hollows and reads as foam over the smooth
  reflection. Left: the lumps are drifting noise, not advected with the roller; the water's sky (the clear Bruneton map
  under the scene's volumetric deck) is bluer than the overcast seen above it, which tints foam and reflection alike.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the surf's rollers were long, even, pale bands (KB-WATER-SURFBANDS1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 (`examples/kitty-hawk`, the dune coast, 6 m up looking out over the
  surf): every breaking crest draws one unbroken grey band across the whole frame, the same width and tone along its
  length, with straight smooth edges. Real surf breaks in short-crested sections: white water starts and stops along a
  crest, its toe is ragged and its body has holes and streaks.
- **Cause:** `packages/water/src/surf.ts` broke every crest by one breaker index from the phasor envelope. The
  envelope carries the swell's directional spread only as a modulation 2 pi / (k dtheta) long, and across a saturated
  surf zone the index is past 1 everywhere, so each roller ran 70 to 114 m along the shore at one strength. The water
  fragment (`index.ts`) gated the roller by a noise it could never fall below at full foam, so the band had no holes.
- **Fix:** the breaker index swings by 0.3 along each crest in sections 0.45 surf wavelengths over the deep spread
  long, riding the crest (their second coordinate is the lead swell component's phase in cycles), which makes crest
  ends (Baker et al. 2023, Phillips 1985); the white water's density follows the swing, a finer noise moves the toe,
  and the fragment's roller has holes and lace. The sections lie along the swell's fixed deep mean direction.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/surf-crests.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): along 240 m of a 1:50
  beach under the dune coast's swell, the longest breaking section was 114, 73 and 112.5 m at three times with 2 to 6
  sections; now 39, 46 and 37.5 m with 7 to 9 sections, gaps 29 to 55% of the shore.
- **Left:** the white water was lit as a flat sheet, fixed by KB-WATER-WHITEWATERLIGHT1.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the near seabed showed a contour maze through the water (KB-WATER-SEABEDMAZE1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 (`examples/kitty-hawk`, 6 m up over about a metre of surf-zone water): the
  bed under the near water was a maze of hard-edged rings in two tones, with a flat band along the foot of the frame.
  `node packages/water/test/refraction-grazing.browser.mjs` on the previous shader: 61.1% of the water misses the bed.
- **Cause:** Water's screen-space refraction (`packages/water/src/index.ts`), not the terrain and not caustics (the dune
  coast draws none). Painting the fallback bottom red showed 36% of the s18 water drawing it. The bent ray's hit is
  found by reprojecting it onto a texel's view-depth plane until it lands on the same texel; on a bed seen at a grazing
  angle that plane crosses the bed at a shallow angle, so each guess overshoots the last and never settles. The crossing
  search that follows bracketed the right crossing, then handed it back to the same reprojection, which failed again.
  Every such pixel took the flat fallback bottom, and the rippled normals made the hit/miss boundary a maze of contour
  rings. Where the bent ray left the frame (the near water at the foot of the frame) the search stopped, so the
  fallback drew a hard band there.
- **Fix:** a bisected crossing whose texel's view depth lies within the ray's own (5 cm or 2% of the distance, the
  thickness test of McGuire and Mara 2014) is the hit; a silhouette, where the occluder stands metres in front, is
  still refused. A ray that leaves the frame takes the crossing before the edge if it has one, else the last texel it
  crosses on screen.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/refraction-grazing.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): a bed painted
  light then dark under a rippled sea seen from 6 m; 61.1% of the water missed the bed before, 0.00% after, and none
  along the foot of the frame.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a synchronous raycast threw on every skinned or morphing model (KB-BVH-SYNCPOSE1, bvh, animation)

- **Repro:** `const model = await loadGLTF(engine, 'Fox.glb'); Animation.attach(model);` then
  `new Raycaster().intersectEngine(engine)` (or `intersectMeshes`, `intersectObjects`, `SceneBVH.intersect`,
  `RaycastSnapshot.capture`): MargoError `unsupported`, "Deformed PBR mesh cannot be picked synchronously", as soon as
  the model was visible. The same with a `Skin` on a `createMesh` mesh and with a `GeometryCachePlayer`. Only
  `await raycaster.intersectModel(model)` and `intersectPosed(skin.picking)` answered.
- **Cause:** a deformer writes the pose into a GPU buffer (`primitive.deformed`), and a GPU buffer cannot be read back
  synchronously. The CPU held only the bind-pose vertices, so the synchronous paths of `@margoengine/bvh` had nothing
  correct to test and refused. Nothing gave them the pose: the deformers kept their arithmetic in WGSL only, although
  every input of it (node matrices, inverse binds, influences, morph deltas and weights, the cache frame) is on the CPU.
- **Fix:** a deformer registers a CPU evaluation of its pose for each primitive it writes
  (`packages/shared/pose-source.js`, a weak registry like the mesh sources). `Animation` evaluates the deformation
  shader's arithmetic (`packages/animation/src/pose.ts`: morph targets, then the blend of four or eight joint
  matrices, positions and normals) from the node matrices and morph weights as they are at the call; `Skin` gives the
  vertices `picking` already posed; `GeometryCachePlayer` gives the floats it uploads. In bvh, `primitiveEntry`
  (`packages/bvh/src/raycaster.ts`) is the one place every synchronous path reads a primitive through: while
  `deformed` is set it returns the posed vertices, their bounding sphere and a tree over them, refitted bottom-up when
  the pose's revision changes and never rebuilt. `Raycaster.intersect`, `castCandidates`, `getPrimitiveBVH`,
  `computePrimitiveBVHAsync`, `SceneBVH` and the snapshot capture all go through it. A deformer with no CPU pose still
  refuses with `unsupported`; the bind pose is never tested in its place.
- **Cost:** per ray and deforming primitive that passes visibility, `layers` and `filter`, one palette evaluation
  and comparison (two 4x4 products and 16 comparisons per joint), a second when the ray crosses its sphere; per new
  pose one pass over the vertices to pose them, one for the sphere and one refit of the tree (each node once). An
  unchanged pose costs no vertex work. Nothing is kept for a model that is never queried.
- **Research:** Ingo Wald, Solomon Boulos and Peter Shirley,
  [*Ray Tracing Deformable Scenes Using Dynamic Bounding Volume Hierarchies*, 2007](https://doi.org/10.1145/1186644.1186650)
  (refit a tree whose topology was built once; quality holds while the deformation keeps the mesh coherent);
  Christian Lauterbach, Sung-Eui Yoon, David Tuft and Dinesh Manocha,
  [*RT-DEFORM: Interactive Ray Tracing of Dynamic Scenes using BVHs*, 2006](https://doi.org/10.1109/RT.2006.280213)
  (refit, with a rebuild when a node's box grows against its children's); Daniel Kopta, Thiago Ize, Josef Spjut, Erik
  Brunvand, Al Davis and Andrew Kensler,
  [*Fast, Effective BVH Updates for Animated Scenes*, 2012](https://doi.org/10.1145/2159616.2159649) (tree rotations
  during the refit). The fix takes the plain refit of the first: one character primitive, a few rays a frame, and a
  skin keeps its parts together. The rebuild test and the rotations are not built (docs/limits.md). The pose arithmetic
  is glTF 2.0 sections [3.7.2.2 and 3.7.3](https://registry.khronos.org/glTF/specs/2.0/glTF-2.0.html), as the shader has it.
- **Regression:** `packages/bvh/tests/deformed-sync.test.js` (900 rays against a brute-force scan of a bent sphere
  outside its bind bounds, one evaluation and one refit per pose, `SceneBVH` and `RaycastSnapshot`; every test throws
  `unsupported` on the code before) and `packages/animation/tests/sync-pick.test.js` (a skinned strip against its
  closed form, a morph target, a moved joint, a `Skin`, a geometry cache). On a real GPU
  (`packages/bvh/tests/gpu-build-browser.js`, RTX A6000, D3D12): at three times of the Fox's clip every CPU position
  is within 1.00 float32 step of the largest coordinate of the GPU's read-back position, normals within 1e-4, and 102
  synchronous first hits equal `intersectModel`'s.
- **Left:** the three open entries below.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a synchronous raycast refused a model skinned with a skinning mode (KB-BVH-SYNCPOSE-DQS1, animation)

- **Repro:** `Animation.attach(model, {skinning: dualQuaternionSkinning})`, then `raycaster.intersectEngine(engine)`:
  MargoError `unsupported` (`packages/animation/tests/sync-pick.test.js` pinned the refusal).
- **Cause:** a `SkinningMode` gave its blend as WGSL only (`shader`, and `encode` for the palette), so `Animation`
  registered no CPU pose with one.
- **Fix:** `SkinningMode.blend(palette, joints, weights, position, normal, share)`, optional: the mode's blend on the
  CPU (`packages/animation/src/shader.ts`). `dualQuaternionSkinning` and `blendSkinning` give it as `skinDualQuaternion`
  (Kavan, Collins, Zara and O'Sullivan, I3D 2007 and ACM TOG 27(4) 2008, cited in `dqs.ts`). `poseVertices`
  (`pose.ts`) runs it after the morph targets with the palette `encode` wrote and, for a mode with `share`, the share
  in the first joint index's upper 16 bits; `Animation` registers a CPU pose for a mode with `blend`. A mode without it
  still refuses.
- **Tests:** `sync-pick.test.js`: a joint column weighed half on each bone turns by half the angle about the joint
  (closed form), a ray there hits the dual quaternion pose and misses the linear one, and a mode without `blend`
  refuses; `blendSkinning` poses by share (0, 0.25, 1). `scripts/animation-dqs-tests.js` compares `Animation`'s CPU pose
  with the read-back GPU pose for every tube and pose of both modes (35,640 checks, 9.5e-7 at most, RTX A6000, WebGPU).
  `Animation` needs WebGPU, so the WebGL2 layer runs no deformation pass to compare.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: blendSkinning drew a node without shares all linear (KB-DQS-NOSHARE1, animation)

- **Repro:** `Animation.attach(model, {skinning: blendSkinning})` on a skinned node with no
  `extras.fbxSkinning.blendWeights`: the GPU drew the linear skin, though the mode says such a node is all dual
  quaternion.
- **Cause:** `Animation` packed shares into the first joint index only when the node had them; without them the upper
  16 bits stayed 0, which the shader reads as share 0 (linear).
- **Fix:** a mode with `share` gets every vertex's share packed, 65535 (all dual quaternion) for a node without shares
  (`packages/animation/src/index.ts`), also in the influences the CPU pose reads.
- **Tests:** `sync-pick.test.js` (the CPU pose of a share-less `blendSkinning` node equals `dualQuaternionSkinning`'s)
  and `scripts/animation-dqs-tests.js` (a share-less blend tube read back from the GPU against `skinDualQuaternion`).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a synchronous raycast refused a model whose morph weights are sampled on the GPU (KB-BVH-SYNCPOSE-MORPHGPU1, animation)

- **Repro:** `MorphWeightPlayer.attach(engine, 'Talk').add(animation)`, then `raycaster.intersectEngine(engine)`:
  MargoError `unsupported`, also after `player.remove(animation)` (`packages/animation/tests/sync-pick.test.js`).
- **Cause:** the player writes the weights straight into the deformation arena on the GPU, so `primitive.weights` is
  not what is drawn, and after a `remove` the GPU keeps the last weights it wrote. `Animation` gave no CPU pose for a
  morphed primitive from the first `add` on, rather than pose from stale weights.
- **Fix:** `MorphWeightPlayer.weightsInto(animation, primitive, out)` samples the weights its dispatch writes on the
  CPU (`packages/animation/src/morph-gpu.ts`): the copy's float32 time, wrapped as `time % duration`, then
  `sampleTrackInto`, which the shader repeats term for term; weights no track drives stay the primitive's. While a
  player drives a copy, `Animation`'s CPU pose takes those samples. `remove` and `dispose` write the weights the last
  dispatch drew into `primitive.weights`, so they say what the GPU keeps (a copy never drawn keeps its own).
- **Tests:** `packages/animation/tests/sync-pick.test.js` (the ray follows the player's time, loops, and holds the last
  drawn weights after `remove`; it threw `unsupported` before); `scripts/animation-morph-gpu-tests.js` compares
  `weightsInto` with the weights read back from the GPU for 70 copies, STEP, LINEAR and CUBICSPLINE, looping and held
  (1.85e-6 at most, RTX A6000, WebGPU). The player needs WebGPU, so the WebGL2 layer has nothing to compare.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a synchronous raycast refused a BatchedMesh, and AssemblyBVH refused every deformed mesh (KB-BVH-SYNCPOSE-BATCHED1, materials, machinery)

- **Repro:** `BatchedMesh.attach(engine, material, {...})`, add an item, then `raycaster.intersectObjects(engine, [batch.mesh])`:
  MargoError `unsupported`. And `AssemblyBVH` of `@margoengine/machinery` over any mesh under GPU deformation, an
  `Animation`'s included: MargoError `unsupported` from its own check (`packages/machinery/src/spatial.ts`).
- **Cause:** `BatchedMesh` places its items in a compute pass and registers no CPU pose
  (`packages/shared/pose-source.js`), though its item matrices and source vertices are on the CPU. `AssemblyBVH` reads
  `primitive.vertices` itself and refuses when `deformed` is set; it does not ask for the CPU pose.
- **Fix:** `BatchedMesh` registers a CPU pose source while its compute pass writes the primitive
  (`packages/materials/src/batched.ts`): `batchShader`'s arithmetic term for term (position through the item matrix,
  normal through its cofactor columns times the handedness, tangent w flipped on a mirror, colour times the tint, hidden
  and free slots collapsed to the origin), evaluated on demand once per change into one array. `AssemblyBVH` reads
  `posedVertices` for a deformed primitive and refuses only a deformer with no CPU pose; a new pose revision is a move:
  `rebuild()` builds that geometry's BVH again in place and refits the part spheres, and a raycast or snap before it
  throws 'state' (`packages/machinery/src/spatial.ts`).
- **Regression:** `packages/materials/tests/batched.test.js` (a synchronous raycast hits items where their matrices
  draw them, misses moved, hidden and removed items; the pose of a mirrored, stretched, tinted item term for term) and
  `packages/machinery/test/runtime.test.js` (an AssemblyBVH holds a deformed part at its pose, throws 'state' on a new
  pose and hits it after `rebuild()`); all three fail on the parent.
- **Not covered:** the pose against the GPU's own output was not read back on a device (the pass is unchanged, and the
  CPU twin is in float64 rounded to float32, as `Animation`'s is).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the waterline of a flowing sea on a beach drew a sawtooth (KB-WATER-SHORESAW1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot kh-establish (`examples/kitty-hawk`, the dune coast, looking south along the
  beach): where the surf meets the flat sand the waterline was a row of teeth, the nearest several metres long.
- **Cause:** two places took the sea's level where the coastal flow has no water.
  - The water mesh: a vertex whose four coastal texels were all dry stood at the sea's level, so the triangle from the
    last wet vertex up the beach dived under the sand within one mesh cell (2.34 m on the dune coast), and the sand
    covered the water from where it dived. The waterline stepped with the mesh.
  - The fragments: a dry texel's depth, clamped to 0, put the end of the water on the dry texels' centres, a staircase of
    the coastal grid's cells (0.78 by 3.9 m on the dune coast), as a still surface's did before its signed depth.
- **Fix:** a dry vertex takes the level of the nearest wet texel within its mesh cell and one texel (`coastalReach`), so
  the surface stays flat across the swash front and meets the sand where the bed rises to it. A dry texel's signed depth
  is the wet texels' level over its ground, so the water ends between texels where that level meets the bed, and a
  quad with no wet texel draws none. Caustics and the surface capture read the same signed depth.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/shoreline.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): a calm sea on a diagonal
  1:50 beach ends on a straight line (1.04 px off it before, 0.00 after), and a pond held 3 m above the sea stands at its
  level on the dry texels within a mesh cell of its waterline (0 m before).
- **Left:** far along the dune coast's beach the run-up still steps by a few pixels where the swash reaches a cell
  further in one 3.9 m row of the flow than the next; that is the flow grid's resolution (docs/limits.md).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a flat, hard-edged pale patch in the surf zone wherever the swell groups fell into a lull (KB-WATER-FOAMPATCH-KH1, water)

- **Repro:** the Kitty Hawk film's shot s18 (`examples/kitty-hawk`, the dune coast at its default 1.2 m surf, camera at
  the waterline looking east): a lens-shaped pale patch with a sharp lower edge lay in the swash zone about 9 m out, with
  no crest in it, and moved with the wave groups.
- **Cause:** Water holds its shoreline foam band and its foam lines off where the surf breaks (on a breaking beach the
  surf's own foam takes their place). It read how hard the swell broke at that instant, from the envelope of the swell
  trains. Two trains of 72 m and 41 m cancel in each wave group's lull, the envelope falls to nothing and breaking reads
  0, so inside the surf zone both foam terms came on at full strength (0.35 and up to 0.67 of white) over the whole lull,
  with edges as sharp as the breaking ramp.
- **Fix:** the gate reads the steady share of breaking waves (`Surf.zone` in `packages/water/src/surf.ts`): Battjes and
  Janssen's Q_b from the sea's root-mean-square height over the depth-limited height, which does not beat with the
  groups. The surf foam still follows the breaking crests.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/surf-lull.browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): the dune coast's two trains
  on a 1:50 beach reach lulls at 23 of 29 surf-zone probes, the zone does not move with them and the shoreline gate stays
  shut at every phase.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a box held to the sea stirred a calm sea, drained the box and ran waves ahead of the sea (KB-FLIP-SEABAND1, physics, flip)

- **Repro:** a `FlipSolver` box held to a calm sea (`elevation` 0, `water` at rest; 24 x 8 x 1 cells of 10 cm, band 4)
  moved at 0.15 m/s within half a second, circling in the band's lower corners. Under a 3 cm, 1 m wave
  (`packages/physics/tests/flip.test.js`) the box lost 1.45 percent of its water in 2.4 s. With the band fixed, the waves
  inside ran 0.18 to 0.25 rad ahead of the sea, the mean level stood 7 mm high, and neither converged with the cells.
- **Cause:** three faults in how the band holds the sea.
  - The band took the sea's velocity after gravity and before the pressure solve. Its faces lost part of their g dt, so
    the solve made a pressure hydrostatic in the interior but not in the band, and its horizontal gradient drove the
    circulation.
  - The refill topped up only band cells holding no particle. A cell left a particle or two short by a wave kept the
    shortfall, while particles above the sea's surface were always removed, so the box drained.
  - The density projection moved particles out of the band's full cells into the interior, which the band then
    topped up again, pumping water in. The pumping raised the level and the waves.
- **Fix:** the band takes the sea's velocity before gravity, as every face does. Each band cell holds eight particles
  times its share under the sea's surface, giving up its highest and taking new ones at its free octants. The density
  projection treats the band as a wall and moves no band particle. A calm box now stays under 1 mm/s. A wave passes
  with its phase within 0.012 rad and its mean within 1.5 mm (cells of 1.25 cm), converging with the cells, and the box
  keeps its water to 0.06 percent.
- **Regression:** "a box held to a calm sea stays still (KB-FLIP-SEABAND1)" and the water count added to "a box held
  to the sea passes the sea's waves through" in `packages/physics/tests/flip.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a README that named a listed entry left the known-entries list stale, and test:changed never ran the test that checks it (KB-README-ENTRIES1, scripts)

- **Repro:** document an `exports` subpath that `scripts/support/readme-entries-known.json` still lists, in the package
  README only (react `./post` and `./tonemap` in e6b371f6f, animation `./mixer` in beaccae9f), then run the fast gate.
- **Cause:** `tests/package-readmes.test.js` fails on a listed entry the README now names, but it is a root test and
  `rootTests` in `scripts/test-changed.mjs` chose only the mutation pins, so no package's tests read the README and the
  gate stayed green until the full verify.
- **Fix:** the known list is shrunk, and `npm run test:changed` runs `tests/package-readmes.test.js` when a package
  README or manifest, the known list or `scripts/readme-entries.mjs` changes.
- **Regression:** "test:changed runs the README entry test when a package README, a manifest or the known list changes
  (KB-README-ENTRIES1)" in `tests/check-merge-affected.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: rebase:main wrote a size-history row twice when upstream already had it (KB-REBASE-HISTORYDUP1, scripts)

- **Repro:** a branch commit whose `scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json` carries a `history` row that `main` also has
  and the commit's parent lacks (the same change landed twice, or a commit made on a file taken from `main`), plus a
  row of its own; `npm run rebase:main`. The shared row is in the settled file twice. `main` held three such rows
  (commit `200b488af`), and `34e7aeb91` landed a fourth (`c32e306e0`) that `feaf75203` removed by hand.
- **Cause:** `mergeSizes` in `scripts/rebase-main.mjs` appended every row of the replayed commit that the commit's
  parent lacked, compared as `JSON.stringify` text. It never looked at upstream's rows, and the same row with its keys
  in another order counted as new.
- **Fix:** rows are compared by date, commit and reason (the key of `historyMissing` in `scripts/quality/ratchet.js`)
  against the parent's and upstream's rows, so the result is upstream's rows, then the commit's new ones, each once.
  The quality gate now fails on a baseline that holds a row twice (`historyRepeated`), and the three rows on `main`
  are single again. The other files the script settles take upstream's copy or merge by key (`docs/api-surface.md`),
  so they cannot repeat a row.
- **Regression:** `tests/rebase-main.test.js` ("sizes.json history merges by identity"), which also proves
  `droppedHistory` still reports a lost row; `tests/quality-gate.test.js` ("no baseline holds a history entry twice").

### Fixed 2026-11-26: one terrain or water in two capture effects draws the first effect's outputs (KB-CAPTURE-TWOEFFECTS1, terrain, water)

- **Repro:** add one `Terrain` to SSR and to `SceneTargets` (`ssr.add(terrain); targets.add(terrain)`): the second
  effect's capture stage carries SSR's three-output `MargoSSR` under its own two to seven targets, a pipeline error
  on the GPU. Water with two effects of the same target formats drew the first effect's stage for both, and with
  different formats rebuilt its capture pipeline and bind groups on every draw.
- **Cause:** a model takes one hook, shared by every effect through `shareCapture` (`packages/shared/capture.js`),
  which forwards `declarations()` to the effect drawing now. Terrain cached its capture stage by the lit shader alone
  (`captureCode`), and water kept one capture pipeline keyed without the declarations.
- **Fix:** both key the stage and pipeline by the declarations this draw's effect returns; water keeps one pipeline
  (and its bind groups per view) per key. Regression: `packages/terrain/test/capture.test.js` and
  `packages/water/test/capture.test.js` ("in two effects").

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the instance attributes check on the WebGL2 layer differed once in its first case (KB-SCATTER-ATTRCOMPAT1, shadows, scatter test)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/scatter/test/attributes.browser.mjs` (workstation, RTX A6000): it failed once
  in 6 runs at its first case (samples 1, custom false, edited false, restore false), `ScatterInstances` and
  `AttributedScatter` drawing different pixels, run right after the 22 WebGPU scatter browser checks and while
  `npm run quality` ran; the next 5 runs passed all 18 cases, as did one run on origin/main.
- **Cause:** not the scatter upload, the layer's buffer sync or the read-back. On the WebGL2 layer the first `Shadows`
  of a page fetches its compatibility route by `import()` (`packages/shadows/src/index.ts`, KB-COMPAT-CPUBUDGET1), and
  until it arrives the nearest-depth reduction waits, so the PCSS blocker search spans its widest and the penumbrae
  differ. Later `Shadows` take the cached route at once. `waitForPipelines` counts pipelines only, so under load the
  first reference frame was drawn before the route and its pair after it; 12 busy cores made it fail 5 runs in 20.
  Nothing told a caller when the frames stop changing.
- **Fix:** `Shadows.ready`, a promise that settles once the route (or, if it failed, the WebGPU kernel) is in place,
  at once on WebGPU and whenever the route loaded before. The check awaits it before its frames.
- **Tests:** `packages/scatter/test/attributes.browser.mjs` holds the route until the first reference frame is shown
  (10 s at most), so a page that draws before `ready` fails its first case every time (3 of 3 without the await, at
  samples 1, custom false, edited false, restore false); with it, 18 of 18 cases on the WebGL2 layer (3 runs) and on
  WebGPU. `packages/shadows/test/compat-route-wait.test.js`: `ready` is pending until the route and the next frame
  reduces on it; settled at once on WebGPU and once the route is cached.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: water added to SceneTargets or MeshBlend built an invalid capture stage (KB-WATER-TARGETS1, water, post)

- **Repro:** `targets.add(water)` on a `SceneTargets` whose outputs are not exactly three, or `meshBlend.tag(water)`:
  the water capture fragment returned `MargoSSR(specular, weight, normal)` while that effect's `MargoSSR` has one field
  per output, so the shader did not compile; SceneTargets also gave water gltf's `margoCapture` form.
- **Cause:** water's capture (`captureShader` in `packages/water/src/index.ts`) wrote SSR's three fields itself for
  every effect, and SceneTargets and MeshBlend took any shader declaring a `struct Surface` for a gltf/pbr one; water
  declares its own `Surface {position, normal, crest}`.
- **Fix:** water writes SSR's fields only for SSR's own `MargoSSR` and calls the hook's `margoSSR(n, v, base, metal,
  rough)` for any other effect (body colour with the foam it shows, roughness, not metal; `margoPosition` where
  declared). SceneTargets and MeshBlend match gltf's `Surface` by its `base` field, and SceneTargets reads the sun
  direction from a Frame's `light` or water's `sun`. Regression: water `test/capture.test.js`, post
  `test/scene-targets.test.js` and `test/mesh-blend.test.js`, and post `test/scene-targets-water-browser.mjs` (WebGPU
  and the WebGL2 layer: one water in SceneTargets with four outputs, MeshBlend and SSR, no GPU error, 7,988 water
  pixels at height 0, none of them lit ground).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a water capture after the post stack was replaced bound the destroyed scene depth (KB-WATER-STALEDEPTH1, water)

- **Repro:** water added to `SceneTargets`, then the post stack replaced (`meshBlend.dispose()`, `SSR.attach`): the
  next frame failed with "Destroyed texture ... used in a submit" (post `test/scene-targets-water-browser.mjs`).
- **Cause:** the capture reused the bind groups of the surface's last draw, which hold the scene depth. SceneTargets
  captures at order -4.5, before the water draws at 4, so the first frame after the swap bound the old stack's depth.
- **Fix:** the depth-dependent groups are made in one place (`bindDepth`), called by the surface draw and by a
  capture whose scene depth changed since that draw. Regression: water `test/capture.test.js` (a new depth is bound
  once, before the capture draws) and the GPU proof above.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a ScatterTiles capture after its rings grew bound the destroyed ring buffers (KB-SCATTER-CAPTURESTALE1, scatter)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-rail-line.json --once --seconds 1.1` failed every
  run with "[Buffer (unlabeled)] used in submit while destroyed" once the page added `view.objects` to SceneTargets.
- **Cause:** `ScatterTiles` grows a ring by replacing its instance buffer and calling `instancesChanged()`, which made
  the colour, shadow and cull bind groups again but kept the capture ring groups, so the next capture bound the
  destroyed buffer. The WebGL2 route's arrival also kept capture stages built before the route counted its rings.
- **Fix:** `instancesChanged()` clears the capture ring groups, and the route's arrival forgets the capture stages and
  groups. Regression: scatter `test/capture.test.js` (a replaced ring is bound in the next capture); the rail-line
  shot runs with no GPU error.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: water beside a solid box ran faster than beside the liquid box's own sides (KB-FLIP-SOLIDSLIP1, physics, flip)

- **Repro:** Martin and Moyce's dam break (`packages/physics/tests/flip.test.js`) on a floor of two solid rows instead of
  the box's own floor: the front ran 0.8 to 6.8 percent ahead of their measured times from Z = 5 on, where the box's
  floor keeps it within 2.8 percent. At 0.3 s the front stood at 8.65 column widths against 8.16.
- **Cause:** three places read the faces inside a solid as the liquid's neighbours. After the pressure solve the grid
  zeroed every face touching a solid, including the faces wholly inside it. The extrapolation kept the particles'
  transfer to those faces, with APIC's affine part reaching into the wall. The transfers' stencils interpolated across
  the solid's side, where at the box's own sides they clamp. Water within half a cell of a solid read a velocity and
  gradient that the box's sides do not give.
- **Fix:** faces inside a wall are left to the extrapolation, which never takes them as known and fills them from the
  liquid (the density projection's displacement too). The transfers clamp at a solid's side as at the box's
  (`wallFaces`, the `walls` argument of `toGrid`, `toParticles` and `sampleVelocity`). A solid floor or wall now gives
  the box's own result to round-off.
- **Regression:** "water slips along a solid as along the box's own sides: a dam break runs alike on either floor" in
  `packages/physics/tests/flip.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a ship and a hull solver on one body counted its sway and yaw damping twice (KB-SHIP-DAMP1, physics ship and seakeeping)

- **Repro (before):** a 7 m hull at 0.6 m/s, kicked to 0.08 m/s in sway, held by a `ShipSolver` and floated by a
  `HullSolver`: 1 s on it swayed at 0.049 m/s, where the same hull under the ship solver alone swayed at 0.076 m/s.
- **Cause:** the ship's MMG derivatives already hold the hull's sway and yaw damping and its added mass, and the hull
  solver added its own strip-theory radiation and added mass in the same rows. Only the ship's added mass could be
  switched off, by a flag in the scene.
- **Fix:** each force component has one owner. The ship solver writes `manoeuvringClaims` (one word a body row: its
  surge, sway and yaw damping, and their added mass unless `addedMass: false`), and the hull solver reads it, as it
  reads `deckClaims`, leaving its radiation in those rows and their rows and columns of the added mass out.
- **Regression:** "a HullSolver on a ship leaves the surge, sway and yaw the ship claims" in
  `packages/physics/tests/ship.test.js` (a sway kick and a yaw kick within 1 percent of the ship alone).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a cloth torn in two failed to rebuild its surface (KB-SOFT-SPLITDENSITY1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="cloth torn in two" packages/physics/tests/soft-cells.test.js` failed on
  `main` with "A trimesh with a mass or a density must be a closed surface".
- **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/soft-split.ts` copied `density: collider.density()` into the rebuilt surface
  collider (since ef1a72d01, which rebuilt query surfaces after cuts), so an open piece was given a density and failed
  the closed-trimesh check. That held for a torn cloth and for a cut skinned body, whose skin the blade leaves open.
  Found by the SOFT-04 verification in [physics-solver-audit.md](physics-solver-audit.md).
- **Fix:** the density is carried only when the mesh the surface collider is made from (the skin when there is one,
  else the triangles) is closed, tested with `closedSurface` (moved to `soft-volume.ts`). An open piece gets its surface
  with no density, as before ef1a72d01. The follow-up preserves query-only mode even for a closed fragment.
  An inherited volume collider requires positive signed volume on the current mesh.
- **Regression:** the test above, and "a piece keeps its surface density when its mesh is closed and has none when the cut
  or tear left it open" in the same file (fails on the previous code for the skinned cut).

### Open 2026-11-26: position-based liquid clamps hide compression (KB-PBF-CLAMP1, physics pbf)

- **Repro:** a resting 10 × 30 × 10 particle column 60 cm tall in `PbfSolver` settles to 72% of its height after 4 s
  with the fast preset and 83% with the precise one, still sinking.
- **Cause:** `packages/physics/pbf-kernel/src/lib.rs` rescales every particle's velocity to a global energy budget
  and shrinks every correction when any one is large, instead of substepping; the clamps hold the energy test while
  the column compresses. Found by the FLUID-02 verification in [physics-solver-audit.md](physics-solver-audit.md).
- **Progress:** The artificial-pressure increment now scales with the substep squared and preserves rest for
  an underfilled free-water pair. XSPH viscous smoothing also uses local reciprocal weights, covered by the
  detached-cloud regression in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/pbf.test.js`. The global pressure correction scales
  and the column compression remain open.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: Picking attached to a scene of more than 4096 gltf/pbr models stopped every frame (KB-PICK-BUDGET1, selection)

- **Repro:** `node examples/package-benchmarks/textured-instancing-gpu.mjs` (RTX A6000, Edge, WebGPU and the WebGL2
  layer): after the pick checks attach `Picking`, the timing leg builds 5,000 materials `createMesh` meshes and
  `engine.render()` throws `RangeError: Picking source budget exceeded; register at most 4096 sources.` from
  `PickingPrimitives.discover` (Picking's capture pass). The frame comparisons and picks before it pass.
- **Cause:** `discover` (packages/selection/src/picking-primitives.ts) counts each discovered model against the
  4096-source budget meant for `add`, and throws inside the render graph, so a large scene fails every frame instead of
  picking within the budget or reporting once. Found while fixing KB-SHADOW-INSTFIT1. The draw also threw every frame
  past 65,536 primitives a pass and past 64 pipeline variants, the same class.
- **Fix:** the models of a scene count against no budget: `discover` finds them all, the 4,096 cap counts only sources
  registered with `add` (refused once, at `add`), and the per-frame primitive and variant caps are gone (the per-source
  primitive check stays at `add` and attach). Limits in docs/limits.md, "Models and sources per `Picking`".
- **Regression:** `packages/selection/test/many-models.browser.mjs` (5,000 models: four frames render without an error,
  picks hit the first and the last, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer); `packages/selection/test/models.test.js` (5,000
  discovered models, the last picked).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: an instanced caster kept the cascades unfitted, so textured-instancing-gpu.mjs failed (KB-SHADOW-INSTFIT1, shadows)

- **Repro (before):** `node examples/package-benchmarks/textured-instancing-gpu.mjs` (RTX A6000, Edge 158, WebGPU)
  failed `instanced matches meshes`: mean difference 0.148 of 255 and 0.35% of pixels over 8 (bars 0.5 and 0.2%);
  with shadows alone, mean 0.86 and at most 109, softer edges on the instanced form.
- **Cause:** without `distance`, `Shadows` tightens its cascades to the casters only when every caster has CPU bounds
  (`range()` in `packages/shadows/src/index.ts`, d0695c5fc). `staticPrimitive` and the model loop rejected any
  primitive with `instances`, and `worldSphere` would have read only the node's single local box, so the same boxes
  drawn as one instanced mesh got cascades from the near plane to 500 and coarser texels than as separate meshes.
- **Fix:** an instanced gltf/pbr or materials caster counts as bounded: `nodeBounds` takes the union of the node's
  local box moved by each drawn instance's matrix (the rows the draw uploads; centre and absolute extents, Arvo 1990),
  cached per node until the rows' new `PBRInstances.version` or `count` changes. A node drawing no instance adds
  nothing; displacement still keeps the safe range. Both frame comparisons now match exactly (mean 0, at most 1) on
  WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
- **Regression:** `packages/shadows/test/instanced-range.test.js` (fits like separate meshes; rows read again only
  after `needsUpdate`, `setMatrixAt` or `count`); real GPU: `examples/package-benchmarks/textured-instancing-gpu.mjs`.

### Open 2026-11-26: a grid-particle plunging breaker does not converge with the grid, and plunges only when taller than Erinin et al.'s (KB-FLIP-CREST1, physics, flip)

- **Repro:** after `npm run build -w @margoengine/physics`, run `node packages/physics/scripts/check-breaker.mjs 0.55 0.0125`,
  then with cells of 0.009 and 0.0065 (steepness S, cell size in m; Erinin et al.'s packet, 0.91 m deep, a 5.6 m box,
  their measures: the crest point's speed at jet formation and the jet tip's velocity at impact, both from cubic fits).
  At S = 0.55, from 1.25 to 0.9 to 0.65 cm:
  - the crest at its highest is 150, 168 and 182 mm (Erinin et al.: 107.8 to 111.5 mm);
  - jet formation to impact takes 146, 183 and 208 ms (148.9 to 169.7);
  - the tip travels 295, 384 and 477 mm (240.1 to 284.1);
  - the crest moves at 1.71, 1.84 and 1.94 m/s (1.511 to 1.536);
  - the tip strikes at 2.29, 2.10 and 2.76 m/s (1.904 to 2.010);
  - jet tip over crest is 1.34, 1.14 and 1.42 (1.24 to 1.33).
  At S = 0.46 the crest reaches 122, 127 and 132 mm and spills (at 0.65 cm a curl lasting 29 ms). Crests of Erinin
  et al.'s height do not plunge at these grids.
- **Cause:** the crest's overturning is not resolved, even at 0.65 cm (about 180 cells a wavelength). Ruled out or
  fixed along the way:
  - The measure: the old one (fastest particle over highest particle) was not theirs. It now follows their jet tip on
    the profile.
  - The depth: the box was 0.6 m of deep-water theory against their 0.91 m. It is now finite-depth linear theory at
    their depth.
  - The box's band: it stirred calm water, drained the box and ran waves ahead (KB-FLIP-SEABAND1, fixed). A 3 cm wave
    now passes in phase, converging with the cells.
  - Surface tension: by Taylor (1959) and Culick (1960), a jet tip 5 to 10 mm thick retracts at
    sqrt(2 sigma / (rho e)) = 0.12 to 0.17 m/s. A liquid without it runs its tip 6 to 9 percent fast at lab scale,
    against a gap of half again in height.
  What is left grows with refinement: the focusing crest still gains height as the cells shrink, and Margo plunges only
  crests 1.4 to 1.7 times Erinin et al.'s.

  Checked with the upstream gauges as the control (Erinin et al.'s group is fixed by its gauge record, not by S):
  - Gauges from x = -2.6 to 0.5 m read the box's surface (its highest particle) against the sea's linear packet. Up to
    the focus the box carries the group as the sea gives it, at both 1.25 and 0.9 cm cells: the rms surface within 2 to
    18 percent of the packet's, the crests within 1 to 5 percent of each other from x = -2.6 to -1.0 m. At S = 0.3 the
    crest stays within 5 to 30 percent of linear, as crest asymmetry gives.
  - The grids part only from the focus on: 146 against 155 mm at x = 0, and 148 against 165 mm at 0.5 m (S = 0.55).
  So the coarse grids do not damp the focusing group, and the box's band (8 cells at its ends, 1.8 m or more from the
  break) does not touch the face. The difference is made at the steepening crest itself.
  Erinin et al.'s crest at breaking (108 to 112 mm) sits at the linear focus height of the packet they ran (about
  109 mm at S = 0.5). Margo's crest reaches 1.3 to 1.5 times its linear height before it overturns. A real crest tips
  over sooner, so Margo's crest resists overturning for want of resolution at its tip. Their crest stands
  near the packet's linear focus height (about 103 mm at S = 0.55). Two of the solver's own limits work against
  overturning: its first-order placement of the free surface, and two bodies of water joining about a cell before they
  touch (docs/limits.md, "Grid-particle liquids").
- **Status:** open. A converged plunger needs the crest refined well below a centimetre, a narrow band or adaptive grid
  round the crest (Ferstl et al. 2016), and a sharper free surface. These are FLUID-03 tiers not yet built. Until then
  `docs/limits.md` and the README give these figures, not a match.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a view drawn into an `-srgb` texture stored core's colours encoded twice (KB-VIEW-SRGB1, core)

- **Repro:** one core mesh (`new PbrMaterial({ color: '#e0a050' })`) and `engine.scene.background = '#808080'`, no
  plugin. `engine.render({ views: [{ camera: engine.camera, viewport: [0, 0, 1, 1], target: { color } }] })` with
  `color` a 64 x 64 texture, read back with `copyTextureToBuffer`. In `rgba8unorm` the background holds 128,128,128
  and the mesh's centre 182,125,43. In `rgba8unorm-srgb` the background held 188,188,188 and the centre 220,186,114,
  the sRGB encoding of those bytes (Intel Arc 140V, Edge 158, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).
- **Cause:** everything that draws a frame writes display colour, already sRGB-encoded: core's fragment shader ends
  with its tone map and sRGB encoding (`packages/core/src/shaders.ts`), core writes a background's bytes as the clear
  value, and the packages' own pipelines end with the same display transform. Core handed the pass a default view of
  the caller's texture, in the texture's own format, and an `-srgb` attachment encodes what is written to it once more
  (WebGPU, "Render pass color attachments": the clear value and the fragment output are converted to the view's
  format). The second encode came from the attachment view's format.
- **Fix (core):** core draws an `-srgb` target through a view in its non-srgb twin format (`rgba8unorm` for
  `rgba8unorm-srgb`, `bgra8unorm` for `bgra8unorm-srgb`), the one reinterpretation WebGPU's `createView()` allows. The
  pass context's `format` is the twin, so core's pipeline, its 4x colour (which resolves into that view), both clear
  paths (the attachment clear of a whole view, the drawn clear of a partial one), core's own clear colour and every
  package pipeline built for the pass write the target as they write the canvas, at once and with no shader change. The
  texture stores byte for byte what a `rgba8unorm` target stores, and sampling it returns linear light, which is what
  an `-srgb` format is for. Nothing is kept per target but the 4x colour, made in the twin format, so a device restore
  needs nothing more. Any other target and the canvas are drawn as before, byte for byte (their view's format is
  their own). An engine's canvas is never `-srgb` (`getPreferredCanvasFormat` returns `bgra8unorm` or `rgba8unorm`, on
  the WebGL2 layer too).
- **What a caller changes:** WebGPU makes such a view only of a texture that names the twin in `viewFormats`, so an
  `-srgb` target is created with `viewFormats: ['rgba8unorm']` (or `['bgra8unorm']`). Without it WebGPU reports a
  validation error for the view and the view draws nothing, where it drew the wrong colours before; the WebGL2 layer
  makes the view either way. `PassContext.view.target.color` is still the caller's texture, in its own format.
- **Why core:** core makes the view of a view's target and gives the pass its format; no package sees the target
  before the pass exists. A package could only draw the frame into a texture of its own and copy it, one more texture
  and copy for each such view each frame, with a view drawn without that package left wrong. The failure it prevents:
  wrong colours (every colour too light, #808080 as 188) in every frame drawn into an `-srgb` texture, which is the
  format a caller picks to sample the frame as linear light.
- **Packages:** none draws into a view's target except through the pass, and none in the tree passes an `-srgb`
  target of its own. Five already wrote linear colour when the pass format was `-srgb` (`@margoengine/lines`,
  `sciviz`'s lines, `shader/raw`, the inspector's mesh debug, `vfx/flame`), and were right alone while core and the
  rest were not; with the pass in the twin format they write display colour like everything else. Their `-srgb`
  branch stays for a capture a caller makes in an `-srgb` format of its own.
- **Regression:** `packages/core/tests/view-srgb.test.js` (the view, the pass format, core's pipeline, the 4x colour
  and the clear colour for `-srgb` and other formats, and the canvas) and `packages/core/tests/view-srgb.browser.mjs`
  on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: a `rgba8unorm` and a `rgba8unorm-srgb` target read back equal byte for byte with 4x
  MSAA and with 1 sample, for a background and a mesh, core's own clear colour, two half views with their own clear
  colours, `ColorBackground`'s own pipeline, `Tonemap`'s capture, and after a device restore (11 cases a backend, Intel
  Arc 140V). On the code before the fix every case differs and the background reads 188.
- **Sources:** W3C, "WebGPU" (GPU for the Web working group, Candidate Recommendation 2024), `GPUTexture.createView()`
  and `GPUTextureDescriptor.viewFormats` (a view's format is the texture's or one of its `viewFormats`, which differ
  from it only in `-srgb`), https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-gputexture-createview and
  https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-gputexturedescriptor-viewformats; IEC 61966-2-1:1999, "Multimedia systems and
  equipment - Colour measurement and management - Part 2-1: Default RGB colour space - sRGB" (IEC, 1999),
  https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/6169.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: core's own clear colour came out lighter and bluer once a post effect captured the scene (KB-CLEAR-DEFAULT1, core)

- **Repro:** an empty scene with no `background` draws 5,6,9. With `Tonemap.attach(engine)` it drew 7,20,38, and the
  same under `PostStack.attach(engine, [new Tonemap()])` (Intel Arc 140V, Edge 158, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; the
  two `info` lines `packages/post/test/scene-background-browser.mjs` printed before this fix). A background of the same
  displayed colour, `'#050609'`, draws 0,1,4 there.
- **Cause:** core's clear colour is one set of numbers, 0.018, 0.023, 0.035 (`defaultClear`,
  `packages/shared/clear-color.js`), and `captureClearColor` returned them untouched for every target: display values
  on the canvas, and the same numbers read as linear light in an HDR capture, about thirteen times the light of the
  colour the canvas shows. KB-CLEAR-CAPTURE1 gave a `background` colour the decode for a linear capture and left core's
  own colour out of it.
- **Fix (core):** `captureClearColor` takes core's own colour down the path of a background: on a capture that holds
  linear light (a float format, or an `-srgb` one) it returns the colour decoded with the sRGB transfer function (IEC
  61966-2-1), 0.00139, 0.00178, 0.00271, one array made once, so a frame allocates nothing and the clear-colour cache
  holds one more entry; on the frame's own target and a display-encoded capture it returns the numbers as before. Both
  of core's clear paths read it (the attachment clear of a whole view, also when it joins the next pass in an empty
  scene, and the drawn clear of a partial view), and so does post's partial material clear (SSR, SSGI), so every
  capture that hands core its target follows: the `SceneTarget` users (PostStack, Bloom, Tonemap, DOF, SSAO, creative
  PostProcessing, RenderGraph, and TAA, upscaling, transitions and materials' opaque colour inside one), environment
  captures (CubeCamera, reflectors) and XR eye views. Unchanged: a frame with no capture, byte for byte (the canvas, a
  view's `target` of any format); display-encoded captures (FXAA, SMAA, TAA on the canvas format); the WebGL2 preview
  renderer and sciviz tiles, which never clear a capture and keep the bytes-only `clearColorValue`; captures that clear
  their own target (reflection probes, clustered bounce, water, the renderer of `@margoengine/xr`). No export, option
  or shader text changes.
- **Why core:** the value is chosen inside core's draw, where `scene.background` is unset and only core knows that its
  own colour is about to clear a capture. A package cannot reach it: a capturing package could only set a background
  itself (changing the scene it was asked to draw) or clear its target in a pass of its own, one more render pass per
