  capture and view each frame in every capturing package, with a capture written against the public pass context left
  wrong. The failure it prevents: a backdrop of the wrong colour in every frame drawn through an HDR effect, a
  reflector or a cube capture by a scene that sets no background, which is the zero-configuration default.
- **What changes on screen:** with no `background`, a frame under an HDR effect has the backdrop a `#050609`
  background has there: 0,1,4 under Tonemap and PostStack and 0,2,5 under Bloom (7,20,38 before), darker and no longer
  blue-tinted. A reflector or cube capture sees the backdrop at its linear value (0.0014, 0.0018, 0.0027, for 0.018,
  0.023, 0.035 before). With no effect nothing changes: 5,6,9.
- **Checks drawn over the unset backdrop:** the package GPU checks that can draw core's clear into a capture were run
  again on WebGPU and, where a check has one, its `--compat` run: 240 passed and 11 failed. No check was
  changed. The 11 were logged as KB-CLEAR-CHECKS1: three checks had measured against the old backdrop and now name
  it, two had test bugs of their own, and six fail without this fix too (KB-GPU-PRECHECKS1).
- **Regression:** `tests/clear-capture.test.js` (the value per format for an unset colour; core's attachment and drawn
  clears on a capture, on the canvas and on a view's own float or `-srgb` target); real GPU:
  `packages/post/test/scene-background-browser.mjs`, on WebGPU and with `--compat`: with no background, 5,6,9 with no
  effect, and under Tonemap, Bloom and PostStack the computed display value and the pixel a `#050609` background draws,
  in an empty scene, beside a mesh and in a half-canvas view (21 more cases, 84 a backend). On the code before the fix
  the CPU test fails and the 18 effect cases are wrong on both backends.
- **Sources:** IEC 61966-2-1:1999, "Multimedia systems and equipment - Colour measurement and management - Part
  2-1: Default RGB colour space - sRGB" (IEC, 1999), https://webstore.iec.ch/en/publication/6169; W3C, "WebGPU" (GPU
  for the Web working group, Candidate Recommendation 2024), GPURenderPassColorAttachment `clearValue`,
  https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-gpurenderpasscolorattachment-clearvalue; Khronos Group, "Khronos PBR Neutral Tone
  Mapper" (Khronos 3D Formats working group, 2024), the curve the check computes its expected pixel with,
  https://github.com/KhronosGroup/ToneMapping/tree/main/PBR_Neutral.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a scene's background colour came out lighter once a post effect captured the scene (KB-CLEAR-CAPTURE1, core)

- **Repro:** `engine.scene.background = '#808080'` draws 128,128,128. With `Tonemap.attach(engine)`,
  `Bloom.attach(engine)` or `PostStack.attach(engine, [new Tonemap()])` it drew 181,181,181 (182 under Bloom);
  `'#07090f'` became 15,29,53 and `'#2a6cba'` 99,166,216 (Intel Arc 140V, Chromium, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).
  `ColorBackground` of `@margoengine/environment` under the same `Tonemap` draws 116,116,116, the tone-mapped linear
  colour.
- **Cause:** core wrote the colour's sRGB bytes as the clear value of every colour target (`clearColorValue`,
  `packages/shared/clear-color.js`, used by `packages/core/src/renderer.ts`), also when a pass had redirected the draw
  into a linear HDR capture, so the display transform encoded them a second time.
- **Fix (core):** core's draw gives `captureClearColor(color, capture)` the format of a capture's target: the pass
  context's colour target when it is not the frame's own attachment. A capture that holds linear light takes the colour
  decoded with the sRGB transfer function (IEC 61966-2-1): a float format (rgba16float, the WebGL2 layer's
  rg11b10ufloat), which the display transform encodes later, or an `-srgb` format, whose clear value WebGPU encodes on
  store. Both of core's clear paths use it (the attachment clear of a whole view, the drawn clear of a partial one), so
  every capture that hands core its target is fixed at once: the `SceneTarget` users (PostStack, Bloom, Tonemap, DOF,
  SSAO, creative PostProcessing, RenderGraph, and TAA, upscaling, transitions and materials' opaque colour inside one)
  and environment captures (CubeCamera, reflectors), in XR eye views too. A display-encoded capture (FXAA, SMAA, TAA on
  the canvas format) keeps the bytes. So does the frame's own target, the canvas or a view's `target` of any format,
  where core's own shader writes display colour: a frame with no capture draws byte for byte as before. An unset
  background kept core's clear colour on every target until KB-CLEAR-DEFAULT1 (above). Captures that clear their own target
  (reflection probes, clustered bounce, water, the renderer of `@margoengine/xr`) never drew the background and are
  unchanged. Post's partial material clear (SSR, SSGI) passes the format too, so it writes what core's whole-view
  clear writes. Core's material colours and the clear share one decode (`toLinear`). The bytes-only
  `clearColorValue` stays for the targets that are always display-encoded (the WebGL2 preview renderer, sciviz media
  tiles), so their bundles carry no decode.
- **Why core:** the clear value is made inside core's draw from the view's `#rrggbb` string, the only form a view's
  clear colour takes. A capture could hand core only another 8-bit hex string, too coarse for linear light (#07090f
  would become #010101), or switch core's clear off and clear its target in a pass of its own: one more render pass
  for every capture and view each frame, in every capturing package, with a capture written against the public pass
  context left wrong.
- **What changes on screen:** under an HDR effect a background is light in the scene, tone-mapped with it: #808080
  shows as 116 (181 before), #07090f as 0,2,9 (15,29,53 before) and #2a6cba as 11,101,183 (99,166,216 before), each
  as `ColorBackground` draws it. A reflector or cube capture sees the background at its linear value. With no effect
  nothing changes.
- **Regression:** `tests/clear-capture.test.js` (the value per format; core's attachment and drawn clears on a
  capture, on the canvas and on a view's own float or `-srgb` target); real GPU:
  `packages/post/test/scene-background-browser.mjs`, on WebGPU and with `--compat` (three colours under Tonemap, Bloom
  and PostStack, in an empty scene, beside a mesh and in a half-canvas view, against the computed display value and
  against `ColorBackground`; with no effect, the bytes as given). On the code before the fix the CPU test fails and
  the GPU check reports all 54 effect cases wrong on both backends.
- **Sources:** IEC 61966-2-1:1999, "Multimedia systems and equipment - Colour measurement and management - Part
  2-1: Default RGB colour space - sRGB" (IEC, 1999), whose decode is v / 12.92 up to 0.04045 and ((v + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4 above;
  W3C, "WebGPU" (GPUWeb working group, 2024 Candidate Recommendation), GPURenderPassColorAttachment `clearValue`, converted
  to the attachment's format like a shader output (https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#dom-gpurenderpasscolorattachment-clearvalue).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the look masks saw ground through plants and trees, so bounce read over 100 percent (KB-LOOK-MASKOCCLUDE1, scatter, biomes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/timber-valley-rail-line.json --once --seconds 1.1 --out <dir>`
  (blowup, 16:00): T6 bounce reads 193 percent early and 184 percent mid (bar 10 to 35): shadowed ground brighter than
  lit ground, which no light can give. `probes/mid.shadow.png` marks shaded ground where the frame shows bright green
  plants, and `mid.lit.png` marks the dark soil of the track.
- **Cause:** the page's `SceneTargets` masks (`litGround`, `shadedGround`, `penumbra`) draw only what is added to the
  targets, here the terrain; the forest, plants and snags are `ScatterTiles` (`@margoengine/scatter`, fed by
  `@margoengine/biomes/objects`), which have no capture hook (`setCapture`, as Terrain, Water, gltf/pbr and voxel
  have), so the mask pass draws the ground behind them unoccluded. The checks then average plants as "shadowed ground"
  and soil as "lit ground". The same gap keeps scattered objects out of SSR, SSGI and every other capture pass.
- **Owed:** `ScatterTiles.setCapture` (scatter: the instanced draw with its wind and LOD into a capture pass) and
  `BiomeView.setCapture` forwarding to the terrain and its objects, so a page adds the whole view once; a regression
  test of a plant in front of shaded ground; then KB-LOOK-TV-BOUNCE1 (sun to sky-ambient ratio) is measured again.
  Until then the timber-valley bounce, shadowTint and penumbra numbers are not evidence.
- **Progress 2026-11-26:** `Scatter.setCapture` (every subclass, `ScatterTiles` included), `SceneTargets.add(model,
  {ground: false})`, `BiomeObjects.setCapture` and `BiomeView.setCapture` landed, with the timber-valley page adding
  `view.objects` as not ground; post `test/scene-targets-scatter-browser.mjs` proves a plant over shaded ground on
  WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer. Still owed: `ScatterInstances` capture, `scenes/test/timber-valley-masks-check.mjs` on the
  rail-line shot, then BOUNCE1 and PENUMBRA1 measured again.
- **Measured again 2026-11-26** (rail-line shot, `--once --seconds 1.1`, plants in the masks, after
  KB-SCATTER-CAPTURESTALE1): bounce 104.8% early and 121.1% mid (bound 10 to 35), shadowTint 0.29 and -1.41 b* (bound
  3 or more), penumbra 0.804 code early (bound 0.7) and 0.445 mid (pass). Plants in the masks did not bring bounce into
  range, so BOUNCE1 stays open on its own cause; `ScatterInstances` capture and the masks check are still owed.
- **Measured again 2026-11-26** after KB-LOOK-TV-BOUNCE1 (the T6 checks read the masks' interiors): calm passes T6;
  blowup reads bounce 72.9 and 86.8 percent and shadowTint 1.91 and 1.04 b*, the light under the pall
  (KB-LOOK-TV-PALL1). `ScatterInstances` capture and the masks check are still owed.
- **Progress 2026-11-26:** `ScatterInstances.setCapture` landed (scatter), proven by
  `post/test/scene-targets-scatter-browser.mjs` with instanced plants on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer. Still owed:
  `scenes/test/timber-valley-masks-check.mjs`. Measured on the rail-line probes (1920 x 1080, masks at 128): plants
  34 percent of the frame, lit ground 43 to 44, shaded 0.5 to 0.6; 14,504 to 15,904 pixels are both lit and plant and
  1,173 to 1,259 both shaded and plant (up to 12 percent of the shaded mask), which the check must explain or fail.
- **Closed 2026-11-26:** the overlap was the shot tool's rounding of half-covered edge pixels (KB-LOOK-MASKTIE1); with it
  fixed, `packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-masks-check.mjs` finds the plants, lit and shaded masks disjoint on both
  probes. BOUNCE1 and PENUMBRA1 are tracked in their own entries.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the night sky dome showed clear stars through a smoke pall (KB-SKY-NIGHTPALL1, sky and weather)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=fire-line --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>`: the
  valley under the blowup's smoke (smoke about 0.6, optical depth about 14) glowed orange (KB-WEATHER-FIREHAZE1), while
  the sky above the ridge was a clear starry night blue, which no pall that thick lets through.
- **Cause:** a `WeatherDrive` wrote the load's light into the sky as `atmosphere.scatteredLight` and dimmed
  `sunColor`, and both reached only the day sky (`daySky` in `packages/sky/src/look.ts`); the night dome (stars,
  moon, twilight) and the clouds over it were drawn whatever the load, and `scatteredLight` held only the sun's share
  (times the sine of its height, 0 at night), so the moon's and the fires' light on the layer never reached the dome.
- **Fix:** sky's look gains `atmosphere.layerTransmittance` (the layer's direct share straight up). The look's
  `cloudSky` wraps the sky's own (`cloudSkyAbove`) in `lowLayer`: the night share of the sky and its clouds
  (`frame.sun.w`) is seen through the layer, t^(1 / sin e) along each ray (Beer-Lambert through a flat layer, e floored
  at 3 degrees as `sunTransmittance` floors the sun), and the layer's glow (`scatteredLight`, which the day sky
  already adds) shows in front of it; the sky pass, its reflections and its light all call `cloudSky`. With the
  defaults (1 and 0) the result is c * 1 + 0, exactly as before, and by day (`frame.sun.w` 0) the frame is exact. The
  drive writes `layerTransmittance` from `sunTransmittance(state, pi / 2)` and adds to `scatteredLight` the moon's
  and twilight's scattered share (as the sun's: hazeLight less the direct share times the sine of the source's height,
  over `lighting.intensity`, as `airLight` takes them) and the fires' light sent back down,
  `hazeReflectance(state)` (new, the two-stream slab reflectance, W. E. Meador and W. R. Weaver, "Two-Stream
  Approximations to Radiative Transfer in Planetary Atmospheres", J. Atmos. Sci. 37(3), 630-643, 1980,
  https://doi.org/10.1175/1520-0469(1980)037%3C0630:TSATRT%3E2.0.CO;2) times `fireHazeLight`.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js` ("at night under a pall the sky takes the layer
  transmittance and its moonlit and firelit glow"), `packages/sky/test/look.test.js` ("the night share of the sky and
  its clouds are seen through the low layer"), and on a real GPU `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs look` (WebGPU
  and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, RTX A6000): the day frame with a layer set is exact, a half layer takes the high band to
  0.447 of the clear night, a pall of 1e-6 puts the night and its clouds out (below 1e-4), and the glow is even over
  the dome in its own colour.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a fire's glow on its smoke ignored the scene's light units (KB-VFX-GLOWUNITS1, vfx and weather)

- **Repro:** packages/vfx/src/lit.ts: a glow of irradiance E lit a puff as a sun of intensity pi E / 1,000 would,
  whatever the scene's sun was. In a scene whose sun is 5 (timber valley) the column glow was pi / 5 of what the haze
  of KB-WEATHER-FIREHAZE1 takes (which refers 1,000 W/m^2 to the sky's `lighting.intensity`); in a scene lit in lux
  (`lighting.intensity: SUN_ILLUMINANCE`, about 108,000) the glow was invisible.
- **Cause:** the glow's unit was fixed at 1,000 W/m^2 = intensity pi; nothing told the lit puffs the scene's noon sun.
- **Fix:** `VFXLit.noon` (default pi, the old reference) is the engine intensity of the noon sun the glow is referred to;
  the uniform's power is written times noon / pi, so a glow of E is E / 1,000 of that sun in any units. `SmokeOptions.noon`
  passes it on, `FireFront.noon` writes it on every column (made before or after), and `WeatherDrive` sets each front's
  `noon` from its sky's `lighting.intensity` every frame, the reference its haze already uses. Regression:
  packages/vfx/test/lit.test.js (sun 5, lux, 1 and pi give the same share), packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js,
  packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js. Real frames (timber valley, 22:00, 960 x 540, aerial-west): the columns' lit
  bases brighten by up to 45, 33, 27 levels (noon 5 against the old pi). The ridge and fire-line views frame no column,
  so they are unchanged bit for bit. Weak spot left: KB-VFX-COLUMNAMBIENT1.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: dune grass grew indoors in the camp, and the Wright flights climbed nose-high (KB-SCENES-CAMPGRASS1, KB-FLYER-LEVEL1)

- **Repro:** `grassCover({grass: 1})` of `@margoengine/scenes/dune-coast` was above 0 inside the hangar and shed
  (x -96 to -62.5, z 27.5 to 32.5); `wrightFlightPose` flew a sin^0.5 rise and fall with a fast climb off the rail.
- **Cause:** the dune coast's cover had no mask for the camp yard; the flight height was one arch over the whole flight.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a Fauld tunnel shot stopped on a GPU error (KB-SCENES-TUNNELGPU1, vfx)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_ASSET_LIBRARY=<library> node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr091.json --stills --out <dir>`
  (state `fire`, NVIDIA Ampere, WebGPU): the page reported `[Invalid CommandBuffer] is invalid due to a previous error`
  after its probe frame, with all 35 WGSL modules compiling.
- **Cause:** the first error was WebGPU's refusal of a texture used as a writable depth attachment and as a sampled
  texture in one pass: a `Flame` with `depth: () => stack.depthTexture` (the scene's own capture, as the tunnel fire
  gives it) bound that depth in its depth pass, which writes it. With `fog` as well, the depth pass's bind group also
  named the fog its shader never reads.
- **Fix:** the depth pass has its own module that samples no scene depth (its depth test keeps what stands in front) and
  binds the flame's uniform alone. The shot renders its still.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/flame.test.js` (the depth pass's shader and bindings) and
  `packages/vfx/test/flame-check.mjs` step `scene` (a real GPU, WebGPU and WebGL2: no error over a captured depth in
  fog, and a wall hides the flame).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the firelit smoke pall at night glowed evenly (KB-SKY-PALLFALLOFF1, sky and weather)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=ridge,fire-line --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>`:
  the sky dome and the haze over the valley were one orange, so the ridge did not stand out against the sky; a firelit
  pall is brightest over the fire front and falls off with distance and height.
- **Cause:** `WeatherDrive` gave the sky layer and the sky fog one colour each (`fireHazeLight`, the box mean over
  `smokeWidth`) everywhere. A first attempt with one softened point over the fires' centre left the fire-line view
  nearly black (mean 12.5): this scene burns in two stretches about 3 km apart, and the point sat between them.
- **Fix:** `WeatherDrive` clusters the fires' burning segments (`FireFront.segments()`) into up to eight sources;
  sky's look and fog take up to eight `fireSpots` that add, the layer where each ray meets it and the haze as the exact mean along the ray
  as far as 2 / density, with `atmosphere.fireSight` holding the sky's low rays to the same reach; `WeatherDrive` writes
  them (`fireLayerLight`), keeping the even light for fires that do not say where they burn. At 22:00 on an RTX A6000,
  960 x 540, the ridge shows dark against a sky brightest toward the fires; mean levels fire-line 20.3 (the check wants
  over 15), ridge 33.3, aerial-west 23.5.
- **Not covered:** the light of one scattering from a source below a flat layer: light the smoke carries sideways by
  scattering again is not modelled, and rays take the layer at one lit height each spot.
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js` (a spot over each source, eight at most, restore),
  `packages/sky/test/look.test.js` and `sky.test.js` (the
  uniforms and WGSL) and `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs look` (GPU, WebGPU and WebGL2: the falloff, the sight,
  two spots adding, the haze's mean along the ray).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a smoke layer under a roof read as separate puffs far from its fire (KB-VFX-ROOFDOTS1, vfx and scenes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr096.json --stills --out <folder>`: dark round puffs
  showed one by one in the haze over the casings.
- **Cause:** the layer under a `ceiling` ran out radially with puffs of one size, so they thinned as 1 / distance and
  no longer overlapped; walls only hid the part that ran into them instead of turning it along the tunnel.
- **Fix:** `SmokeOptions.gallery` (two walls under the roof): the layer turns along the gallery both ways
  (Delichatsios 1981) at the ceiling jet's speed where it meets the walls, fills it wall to wall and passes neither;
  the Fauld tunnels give each fire's smoke its gallery (`fauldGallery`). Real frame: fr096's dots are one continuous
  layer. Weak spots left: that layer reads flat black, and two round puffs show at its lower edge. Regression:
  packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js, packages/vfx/test/smoke-check.mjs, packages/scenes/test/fauld-tunnels.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the Fauld fire frames were nearly black beside their flames (KB-FAULD-FIREDIM1, vfx and scenes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr095.json --stills --out <folder>`: mean 8-bit luma 1.3;
  fr091 11.5 and fr094 11.4, their walls unlit beside the fires.
- **Cause:** a large fire's light was its flames' silhouette at their displayed peak (1 in the pre-exposed frame), so it
  lit a wall at the displayed flame times its solid angle, 4 to 5 stops under the card metering every other state of
  the store uses. Nothing could raise the light without raising the flames (`Fire` `power` scales both). The smoke,
  the exposure value and the lamps were not the cause: scaling only the firelight lit the same frames.
- **Fix:** `keyDistance` on `Flame` and `Fire` meters the light on a white card (intensity pi d^2); the Fauld
  tunnels' fire and after states use 2 m (`FIRE_KEY_DISTANCE`). Real frames fr091 to fr096: mean luma 19 to 43. Weak
  spots left then: KB-VFX-FIRESHADOW1 (fixed) and fr096's smoke reading flat black. Regression:
  packages/vfx/test/flame.test.js.

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr095.json --stills --out <folder>`: mean 8-bit luma 1.6,
  the frame nearly black (38.3 while the fire's light passed through walls, before KB-VFX-FIRESHADOW1).
- **Cause:** the layout's lamp marked `fire` at plan (61, -9, 0.6) stands inside the `tn_stack_a` casings at world

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a large fire's light passed through walls (KB-VFX-FIRESHADOW1, vfx and scenes)

- **Repro:** the same fr095 still before the fix: the aisle round the corner from the fire lit evenly, the brick wall
  and the stacks with no shadow of the piers between.
- **Cause:** `Fire` passed `castShadow` (default true) to its hearth lights only; the volume of a fire with a
  `flameLength` made up to four `Flame` lights with no `castShadow`, and `Flame` had no such option. In the Fauld
  scene the lamps also took every shadow slot.
- **Fix:** `FlameOptions.castShadow` (default false for a bare `Flame`): the light is one point at the footprint's
  middle that casts through `LocalShadows`, so one slot holds all of it; `Fire` passes its `castShadow`, and a large
  fire that casts now needs `LocalShadows` attached, as documented for every `Fire`. `lampShadowBudget` in the Fauld
  tunnels leaves each fire its slot and texels. Real frames: fr091, fr092 and fr094 show the posts', bomb's and
  rubble's shadows (mean 14.7, 20.3, 11.2, before 21.9, 43.4, 19.1); fr093 35.2 (43.1); fr096 unchanged; fr095 is
  KB-FAULD-FIREINSTACK1. GPU: flame-check passes on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, and its `shadow` step reads 71.7
  unshadowed and 23.0 shadowed on the ground behind a wall. Regression: packages/vfx/test/flame.test.js,
  packages/vfx/test/flame-check.mjs, packages/scenes/test/fauld-tunnels.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a fire's sparks drew white under a tungsten white balance (KB-VFX-EMBERWHITE1, vfx)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr091.json --stills --out <folder>`: the embers beside the
  flames were white streaks while the flames were orange.
- **Cause:** a `Fire` with `flameLength` kept the hearth kit's embers at intensity 5 (birth colour 1, 0.6, 0.2), set for
  the hearth close-up's own exposure. Its `Flame` volume holds every channel under its `peak` (1) through a camera
  shoulder; the sparks were five times that in red and three times in green, so under the tunnel's exposure and
  3,200 K balance every channel clipped and they read white.
- **Fix:** beside a flame volume the embers' brightest channel over their life is the flame's peak radiance
  (`Flame.peakRadiance`, its `peak` times its `radiance`, new) times the fire's `power`; a hearth fire with particle
  flames keeps its kit's embers. Real frame (fr091 mid still, RTX A6000): spark pixels with red over 120 in the spark
  field 963 before, 401 after; of them near white (green and blue over 170) 126 before, 0 after; mean blue 130 to 91.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/fire.test.js`, "a flame volume's embers are no brighter in any channel than the
  flame's peak, at any power" (fails on the parent: the embers stood at 5 times the peak).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: smoke indoors climbed through the roof and veiled its own fire (KB-VFX-SMOKEROOF1, vfx and scenes)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr091.json --stills --out <folder>`: no flame showed, the
  tunnel beyond the rubble was black and pale flat ovals stood beside it. With the fire's smoke off the flames showed.
- **Cause:** `Smoke` had no roof. A fire under 3.2 m of tunnel ran its 60 s open-sky plume: puffs climbed tens of
  metres, grew tens of metres wide, and their billboards, depth tested at their centres, hung over the whole view; the
  lamps lit patches of them. The column over a lit `Fire` was also lit twice, by the fire's own lights and by its
  `glow`, referred to a daylight sun.
- **Fix:** `SmokeOptions.ceiling` (the column stops at the roof and spreads under it, Alpert 1972); a lit `Fire`'s
  column defaults `glow` to 0; the Fauld tunnels give each fire's smoke its roof (`fauldFireSmoke`). Real frame: the
  flames and sparks show and the pale ovals are gone; the shot stays dark. Regression: packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js,
  packages/vfx/test/fire.test.js, packages/vfx/test/smoke-check.mjs, packages/scenes/test/fauld-tunnels.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: nodes reading a particle's age could not attach beside over-life curves (KB-VFX-NODESLIFE1, vfx)

- **Repro:** a `VFX` with `overLife` and a `nodes` graph reading `age`: attach threw "VFX over-life needs its simulation
  shader".
- **Cause:** `nodes` rewrites the kernel's slot load to read the particle's cold half, and `overLife` looked for the old
  statement word for word.
- **Fix:** `overLife` anchors on the load whatever it reads. Regression: packages/vfx/test/nodes.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a smoke column over a fire at night read blue-black above its base (KB-VFX-COLUMNAMBIENT1, vfx, weather)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=aerial-west --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>`: the
  columns were lit orange only near their source point and read as dark blue-black shapes against the orange pall above.
- **Cause:** a column's puffs took the glow of one point at its base (falling as 1 / d^2 over the km the column climbs)
  and the engine's moonlit ambient; the firelit pall round them, and the rest of the burning front, gave them no light.
- **Fix:** `VFXLit.air` (vfx): the light of the air round the particles as shares of the noon sun, which adds
  `air * noon / pi` to the ambient (light of that share from every side shows a ball E / pi). `SmokeOptions.air` and
  `FireFront.air` carry it to the columns, and `WeatherDrive` writes on each front its fires' light on the pall over it
  (the spots of `fireLayerLight` at the front's heat-weighted centre plus the even `fireHazeLight`). Real frame
  (aerial-west at 22:00, 640 x 360, RTX A6000): the column's mean 8-bit colour 2.4, 3.1, 7.6 before, 58.0, 32.1, 7.6
  after, against the pall's 82.7, 53.5, 21.1: a warm column a little darker than the lit pall, not a blue-black hole.
- **Also:** `timber-valley-still.mjs` added `--query` to its own fixed comparisons, so `--query=hour=22` made the day
  still a night one and the run stopped on "the night sky is dark and blue" (day and night read 53.6 / 101.2 alike).
  Only the views asked for take `--query` now.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/lit.test.js` (the air term in any scene units), `packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js`
  (a column and a front carry it), `packages/weather/tests/air-load.test.js` (the drive writes the pall's light).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the smoke haze over a burning valley took no light from the fire (KB-WEATHER-FIREHAZE1, weather and vfx)

- **Repro:** `node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=ridge --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>` after the
  KB-WEATHER-NIGHTHAZE1 fix: the blowup's smoke haze was moonlit only and read black (3, 1, 0 under the ridge), while a
  valley burning under a smoke pall at night glows orange from below.
- **Cause:** the sky fog's colour (`WeatherDrive.tintFog`) was lit by the sun, the moon and the twilight sky only; the
  fire fronts the drive reads for their smoke gave the haze no light, and a front reported no light to give.
- **Fix:** `FireFront.radiantPower` (vfx) reports the flames' radiant power, the 0.3 of the release its smoke columns
  glow with (`RADIANT_SHARE`, pinned equal to the smoke entry's `RADIANT_FRACTION`); `fireHazeLight(watts, width)`
  (weather) turns it into light on the haze, the box model's light as `smokeFromEmission` is its smoke (the upward half,
  the point-to-disc view factor of the box's area at the layer's middle, over that area, a share of the noon sun's
  1,000 W/m^2 in the flames' orange), and the drive adds it to the light on the sky fog (`fireLight`, default 1, 0 off).
  Real frames (960 x 540, 22:00, blowup): the ridge view's lower half went from 2.6, 1.1, 0.2 to 82.8, 47.9, 5.7, the
  town's to 43.8, 24.3, 3.7 and the fire line's to 37.7, 22.4, 3.9: the valley glows orange under the smoke. Weak spots
  left: the glow is even over the whole haze (the sky fog has one colour, so no falloff away from the fire), and the sky
  dome stays a starry blue over the pall (KB-SKY-NIGHTPALL1).
- **Regression:** `packages/weather/tests/smoke.test.js` (fires light the smoke haze from below: black with no radiant
  power, the box model's orange with it, `fireLight` scaling, moonlight adding) and `packages/vfx/test/fire-front.test.js`
  (`radiantPower`: 0 before ignition, then 0.3 of the release, one share with the smoke columns).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the moving look evidence read distances from an 8-bit depth mask (KB-SHOT-DEPTH8BIT1, tools/shot)

- **Repro:** a shot with `shot.moving` at `depthScale` 2000 (the timber-valley shots) with ground within a few metres
  of the camera: those pixels read 255 in `probes/<name>.depth.png`, `distanceFromNearness` gave them 0, and their
  motion was that of a sky 5,000 m away; ground farther off moved in steps of metres. CPU proof: at that scale 3 m
  reads as no distance.
- **Cause:** the pages wrote exp(-distance / depthScale) into an `r8unorm` target and the tool rounded every mask to
  8 bits again; the area filter then mixed silhouette pixels with the background, which is no distance of either.
- **Fix:** storm-light, timber-valley-shot.html and the shot test scene draw the mask as `r32float`; on moving probes
  the tool keeps the floats (`probes/<name>.depth.f32`), taking the nearest surface of each pixel's footprint, and
  `writeMoving` reads them. The PNG masks are unchanged in meaning. A coarser mask format warns.
- **Regression:** `tests/shot-motion.test.js` (3 m and 500 m at scale 2000: 8 bits fail, floats within 0.1%, and
  the motion from the `.f32` file), `tests/shot-capture.test.js` (`resampleNearness`); real GPU:
  `tools/shot/test/moving-check.mjs` (the floats are written and round to the PNG).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: ship lamp glints read the sea's roughness as GGX alpha, the sun glint as perceptual (KB-SHIPLAMP1, water)

- **Repro (before):** packages/water/test/ships.browser.mjs, "sun and lamp glint at one roughness": a lamp 10 km away
  along the sun's glint direction, as bright at the sea as the sun, lit 1168 pixels at a peak of 84 where the sun lit
  686 at 250 (lampRoughness null, so both took the Water's roughness).
- **Cause:** packages/water/src/ships.ts `shipLamps` wrote `a2 = max(rough^2, 1e-4)` (alpha = rough), with no slope
  variance, no Smith G and an extra N.L, while index.ts `directionalGlint` writes alpha = rough^2, a2 = alpha^2 + the
  waves' unresolved slope variance (`frame.foam.y`): two conventions for one roughness on one surface.
- **Fix:** index.ts `seaGlint(n, v, l, rough)` is the Water's one glint lobe (GGX D with the variance, Schlick-Smith G,
  Fresnel); `directionalGlint` and `shipLamps` both call it, so the far lamp now lights 685 pixels at 250. The lamp
  function moved beside the glint functions after `struct Output`, since WaveQuery compiles the surface part before it
  alone. `lampRoughness` is a perceptual roughness like the Water's (README, settings row); `SHIP_LOOKS.calmNight` moved
  from 0.06 to 0.25 (alpha 0.0625, the old lobe's width).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: seven GGX D sites still cancelled in float32 near a narrow lobe's peak (KB6016d)

- **Repro (before):** the `nh^2 (a2 - 1) + 1` denominator in float32 at roughness 0.03 (a2 = 8.1e-7), with the half
  vector 2e-5 to 8e-4 rad off the normal: D off by more than 10 % against f64 (tests/smith-shaders.test.js, "in float32
  the vector GGX denominator keeps D"; KB6016c measured +28 % for core's copy on the GPU).
- **Cause:** KB6016c moved core and the shared `ggxD` / `ggxDOf` to `|n x h|^2 + a2 nh^2`, but seven sites kept the
  scalar form: shared `ggxDenominator(nh)` (environment probe prefilter, environment cube prefilter pdf, voxel-pathtracer
  `ggxD`, water directional glints), shared `ggxNamed` (materials' lobes), and two written by hand (water ship lamp
  glints, FFT ocean glint). Near the peak 1 - nh^2 is a few float32 steps of nh^2 while a2 is about 8e-7, so the
  rounding of nh alone moved D.
- **Fix:** shared `ggxDenominatorOf(n, h, nh, a2)` writes `max(|n x h|^2, step(nh, 0)) + a2 nh^2` over the vectors (the
  scalar export is gone) and `ggxNamed` takes `n` and `h`; every site passes its vectors. The environment cube prefilter
  passes its tangent-space sample (n = (0, 0, 1)), whose sin is computed without cancellation by `importanceGGX`; the
  voxel-pathtracer's `ggxD(a2, n, h)` clamps n.h itself. Where n.h >= 0 the value is unchanged in exact arithmetic.
- **Regression:** tests/smith-shaders.test.js: no package or shared source writes the cancelling form (literal or
  template, which also fails on the parent's `${nh}*${nh}*(${a2}-1)+1`), the scalar export is gone, each former caller
  passes n and h, `ggxDenominatorOf` and the `ggxNamed` D equal the textbook D (and a2 / pi where h faces away), and the
  float32 evaluation of both forms. GPU: the test:gpu and browser chains of environment, materials, voxel-pathtracer and
  water on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
- Sources: as KB6016c (Walter, Marschner, Li and Torrance 2007, eq. 33; Guy and Agopian, "Physically Based Rendering in
  Filament", section 4.4.1; Goldberg 1991); Karis 2013, "Real Shading in Unreal Engine 4" (the GGX importance sample the
  cube prefilter draws).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: rebase:main ran the checkout and commit hooks for every commit, so main moved before it ended (KB-REBASE-HOOKS1, scripts)

- **Repro:** on a Windows laptop with the git-lfs hooks installed, `npm run rebase:main` on a branch of four to ten
  commits while `main` took a landing about every minute: 2.5 to 5 minutes, and `npm run push:main` was refused.
- **Cause:** `git rebase` runs `post-checkout` and `post-commit` as it goes; `git lfs` in them took 5 to 30 s each
  (`GIT_TRACE2_PERF`), once per commit and per generated conflict. Then its conflict-marker scan read every tracked
  file, 39 s for 23,156 files.
- **Fix:** the commits are replayed without a checkout (`git merge-tree --write-tree`, `git commit-tree`) and the branch
  moves once (`git reset --keep`). Generated conflicts are settled there as before; any other conflict, a merge commit,
  signed commits, changed tracked files or a git older than 2.40 go to `git rebase`, which stops for a person. The
  `pre-push` hook is untouched. Hooks run by the tested two-commit rebase: 12 before, none after. The marker scan now
  reads only the files `git grep` finds a marker-like line in, with the same findings.
- **Regression:** `tests/rebase-main.test.js`: a two-commit branch replays without running any git hook; a replay never
  overwrites an untracked file that main adds.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the selection outline of an instanced mesh marked its instances where its vertex shader did not move them (KB-SEL-INSTMOVE1, selection)

- **Repro:** the scene of `packages/selection/test/instanced-move.browser.mjs` (two instanced quads moved 1.5 units by
  a material plugin), then `Selection.attach(engine).set([mesh])`: no outline where the quads draw, on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer (the equal-depth mask was drawn at the unmoved place, where no surface is).
- **Cause:** `packages/selection/src/index.ts` `drawModels` marked gltf/pbr instanced primitives through `ModelDraws`
  `addInstances` (CPU world matrices, unmoved vertices), and its `mark` filter kept them out of `PickingPrimitives`.
- **Fix:** the filter and that branch are gone: gltf/pbr instanced primitives are marked by `PickingPrimitives` with the
  mask, through the same instanced pick shader as GPU picking (`instancedDepth` after the vertex move,
  KB-PICK-INSTMOVE1). `ModelDraws` keeps only models without gltf/pbr mesh sources.
- **Regression:** `packages/selection/test/instanced-move.browser.mjs` (both back ends: outline pixels at both drawn
  places, none at the unmoved places); `packages/selection/test/models.test.js` (the mask draws one instanced draw).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GPU picking of an instanced mesh tested the instances where its vertex shader did not move them (KB-PICK-INSTMOVE1, selection)

- **Repro:** `createInstancedMesh` of two 0.8 wide quads stood at y = +1.5 and -1.5 by their instance matrices, whose
  material plugin moves every vertex 1.5 units right; `Picking.attach(engine)`, then `pick` where they draw answered
  null and `pick` where they would stand unmoved answered the instances (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).
- **Cause:** `packages/selection/src/picking.ts` drew gltf/pbr instanced primitives through its own model pipeline, one
  CPU-built world matrix per instance near the pixel and the unmoved vertex position; gltf/pbr's `pickingPrimitives`
  left out the instances, so the pick shader the plain primitives and every shadow pass draw through (the
  `displacement` caster) never saw them.
- **Fix:** gltf/pbr `pickingPrimitives` carry the primitive's `instances`; `PickingPrimitives` draws such a primitive
  once over all its rows through the shadow casters' `instancedDepth` transform after the material's vertex move (the
  same order as the shadow passes), with a flat row so row k writes the primitive's first ID + k (the `margoRow` a
  row-reading material plugin already names). Picking reserves one ID run per instanced primitive and decodes the
  instance from it; a primitive with mirrored rows was picked from both sides (wrong for one-sided materials, see
  KB-PICK-MIRRORROWS1: each row's faces now follow its own handedness).
  Hit details read the instance's world matrix for the normal.
- **Regression:** `packages/selection/test/instanced-move.browser.mjs` (both back ends: the drawn places hit instances
  0 and 1, the unmoved places miss); `packages/materials/test/instance-attributes-browser.mjs` now asserts
  `instancedThere`; `packages/selection/test/models.test.js` (one instanced draw, one ID per row).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GPU picking missed a mesh its shader moved past its geometry's bounds (KB-PICK-MOVED1, selection)

- **Repro:** `createMesh` of a 0.8 wide quad whose material plugin moves it 1.5 units; `Picking` at the drawn place
  answered null (the `picking` check of `packages/materials/test/instance-attributes-browser.mjs`).
- **Cause:** the picking pass culled each primitive by its unmoved geometry's bounding sphere before drawing it through
  its displacement caster.
- **Fix:** a primitive whose material displaces is not culled by that sphere, as gltf/pbr's frustum test and the shadow
  passes already do. Regression: the check above.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a material plugin's output point never ran on unlit, normal and matcap materials (KB-MAT-PLUGINUNLIT1)

- **Repro:** `new UnlitMaterial({features: [materialPlugin({name: 'paint', output: 'color = vec3f(1.0, 0.0, 0.0);'})]})`
  drew white.
- **Cause:** those shadings return from the fragment entry before the lit code, where the point was inserted.
- **Fix:** the point runs on the colour of the early return too. Regression: `packages/materials/test/plugins.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a material plugin taken off and put back in one step left shadows bound to a destroyed buffer (KB-MAT-PLUGINCAST1)

- **Repro:** `material.features = []; material.features = [plugin];` on a material whose plugin has uniforms and a vertex
  point: the material kept the caster record bound to the buffers the first line destroyed.
- **Cause:** the caster record was keyed by the plugins' ids, which a detach and re-attach kept.
- **Fix:** a plugin takes a new id when its last detach frees its buffers. Regression:
  `packages/materials/test/instance-attributes.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a CSP test's Wasm block also rejected Node's own parser module, after another test had ended (KB-CSP-STUB1, tests)

- **Repro:** on Node 22.12, `node --test packages/decoders/tests/csp.test.js` (CI job "node22 unit tests"): every test
  passes, then the file fails with 'Test "draco worker preserves CSP code and help: WebAssembly.CompileError" ...
  generated asynchronous activity after the test ended ... "EvalError: Wasm blocked by Content Security Policy"'.
- **Cause:** that EvalError is the one the later "JPEG XL worker reports blocked compilation" test throws from its
  `WebAssembly.instantiate` stub. The first draco test makes the file's first `Response`, which starts Node's HTTP code;
  it compiles its parser in the background and instantiates the compiled module later (inferred from the report: Node
  attributes the rejection to the test that started the work, and Node 26 does not load it then). When that call landed
  on the stub it rejected with nobody to handle it. No decoder worker is at fault: the draco worker had already replied.
  `packages/exporters/tests/basis-loading.test.js` counted and blocked `instantiate` calls after its own `Response`, with
  the same exposure.
- **Fix:** `stubCompile` (`tests/support/wasm-csp.js`) blocks compilation from bytes and streams, as a CSP does, and
  passes an already compiled `WebAssembly.Module` through; both tests use it.
- **Regression:** `packages/decoders/tests/csp.test.js`, "a blocked-compilation stub leaves a module already loading in
  the process alone", which makes the same race on every Node.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: half floats needed DataView.setFloat16 on Node 22, and were rounded twice (KB-NODE22-HALF1, decoders/shared)

- **Repro:** on Node 22.12, `node --test packages/decoders/tests/tiff.test.js`: "TIFF 16, 32 and 64-bit float with the
  floating point predictor (Predictor 3)" fails with `view.setFloat16 is not a function`. Separately, on any Node,
  `f16Bits(1 + 2 ** -11 + 2 ** -40)` (also behind `floatToHalf` and `toHalf`) gave 0x3c00 where `setFloat16` stores
  0x3c01.
- **Cause:** the test's TIFF writer called `DataView.setFloat16` and its expectation `Math.f16round`, neither of which
  Node 22 has; no shipped source calls either (`npm run check:node-apis` reads shipped files only, so nothing checked
  the tests CI runs on Node 22). The binary16 encoders narrowed a number to binary32 first, rounding it twice.
- **Fix:** the writer stores `f16Bits` (`packages/shared/f16.js`), which now narrows with rounding to odd (Boldo and
  Melquiond, IEEE Transactions on Computers 57(4), 2008, https://doi.org/10.1109/TC.2007.70819) so it rounds once;
  `floatToHalf` (`@margoengine/environment`) and `toHalf` (`@margoengine/materials`) use it instead of their own copies.
  Binary32 inputs encode as before. The TIFF reader already decoded half floats itself.
- **Regression:** `packages/decoders/tests/tiff.test.js`, "TIFF half floats and the binary16 encoder need no built-in
  float16, and match it where it exists", and `tests/node-apis.test.js`, "the Node 22 test files and their helpers use
  no API newer than Node 22.12 without a feature test" (named "no built-in float16 API" until KB-NODE22-TESTS1).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: some tests CI runs on Node 22.12 import APIs it lacks (KB-NODE22-TESTS1, tests)

- **Repro:** on Node 22.12, `npm run test:node22`: files that import `registerHooks` from `node:module` (in
  `packages/biomes/tests`, `packages/mesh-edit/tests`, `packages/gltf/test/auto.test.js`,
  `packages/blender/tests/pbr-ext-close.test.js`, `packages/webgl2-compat/test/routes.test.js`) or `zstdCompressSync` /
  `zstdDecompressSync` from `node:zlib` (`packages/decoders/tests/streams.test.js` and `zstd-destination.test.js`,
  `packages/exporters/tests/basis-native.test.js` and `basis-zstd.test.js`, `packages/splats/test/zstd.test.js`) can fail
  with "does not provide an export named".
- **Cause:** both arrived after Node 22.12 (22.22 has them), and `scripts/check-node-apis.mjs` reads shipped sources
  only. `tests/node-apis.test.js` checked the Node 22 test files for the float16 APIs alone.
- **Fix:** the test files take both from `scripts/support/node-compat.mjs`, which reads the module namespaces and has a
  stand-in for each. `moduleHooks(rules)` applies module hooks written as plain rules
  (`scripts/support/node-compat-hooks.mjs`) through `module.registerHooks`, or through `module.register` where that is
  missing, so the biomes, mesh-edit, glTF, Blender and WebGL2 route tests run on Node 22.12 too. `zstdDecompressSync` is
  node:zlib's or the engine's own decoder (`packages/shared/zstd.js`). No shipped source used either API.
- **Follow-up, same day (no skipped tests):** the first fix gave `zstdCompressSync` no stand-in, so the 13 tests that
  need Node-made streams (decoders `streams` and `zstd-destination`, splats `zstd`) passed `{ skip: noZstd }` and did
  not run on Node 22.12. Now `zstdCompressSync` falls back to `scripts/support/zstd-store.mjs`, a frame writer after
  RFC 8878 (Y. Collet, M. Kucherawy, 2021, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8878) that stores the input in raw blocks
  of at most 128 KiB, with the content size, window descriptor and XXH64 content checksum (xxHash specification,
  Y. Collet, https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/dev/doc/xxhash_spec.md) the tests ask for; it serves the tests
  of frames, checksums, limits and aborts. The tests of Huffman, FSE and match decoding read streams Node compressed
  once (`zstdFixture`; `packages/decoders/tests/fixtures/zstd`, `packages/splats/test/fixtures/zstd`): on a Node with
  Zstandard the helper compresses again and fails when a checked-in file is missing or no longer decodes to the
  test's input (`MARGO_ZSTD_FIXTURES=write` rewrites them). `zstdConstants` stands in for the `ZSTD_c_*` numbers of
  `zlib.constants`, which Node 22.12 lacks too. The stage, voxel-pathtracer and react tests, the Firefox matrix driver
  and the sciviz AIS script that still imported `registerHooks` or a zstd function by name take them from the helper;
  the hook rules gained an error code, a module source and a redirect by resolved URL for them.
- **Regression:** `tests/node-apis.test.js`: "the Node 22 test files and their helpers use no API newer than Node 22.12
  without a feature test" now scans for every API in the table (a named import of `registerHooks` or a zstd function
  fails it), "no test or script anywhere names a node: API that Node 22.12 lacks without a feature test" reads every
  tracked source file that is not shipped, as code and as text, and "the stand-ins for registerHooks and zstd work, on
  this Node and as on Node 22.12" runs them with `MARGO_NODE_COMPAT=fallback`. `tests/zstd-store.test.js` decodes the
  writer's frames with Node and with the engine (empty, exactly 128 KiB, several blocks) and checks `zstdFixture`.
  With the stand-ins forced the three files run 69 tests, 0 skipped (13 skipped before).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: rebase:main built API reports for every touched package, so a push lost the race for main (KB-REBASE-SLOW1, scripts)

- **Repro:** a branch that adds exports entries to a package and to the re-export packages (`margoengine`, the kits),
  rebased while `main` takes a landing every few minutes: `npm run rebase:main`, then `npm run push:main`. Four rounds
  on 2026-11-25 each took 7 to 9 minutes and each push was refused with "HEAD does not contain origin/main".
- **Cause:** `scripts/rebase-main.mjs` ran `api-report.js --update` once for every package the branch changed any file
  of, whenever a generated file conflicted (`docs/api-surface.md` conflicts on its totals line at nearly every landing).
  Each run builds the stale packages and loads every package's declarations.
- **Fix:** a report is built only when both sides changed it, for its package alone; any other report replays as it is,
  and `docs/api-surface.md` is merged row by row and entry by entry. For the branch above the report runs go from six per
  round to none. `npm run api:check` after the rebase stays the check.
- **Regression:** `tests/rebase-main.test.js`: a branch that adds entries builds no report and the merged surface holds
  both sides; a report both sides changed builds its own package only.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: solvers that push on bodies could not share a world (KB-PHYS-BODYROWS1, physics framework)

- **Repro:** a world with a `SoftSolver` (a curtain on a hull) and a `HullSolver`: the first step threw "Contributors
  "hull" and "soft" add different lengths to field "bodyForces"". The same held for any of the hull, ship, entry and
  deck-water solvers with the soft, air or rigid solver's own pushes.
- **Cause:** each solver sized its body-set contributions by its own convention: the rigid, soft and air solvers by the
  kernel's capacity, the hull, ship, entry and deck-water solvers one past their highest row; the field's sum refuses
  contributions of different lengths.
- **Fix:** the world fixes its body rows once (its `bodyRows` option, or the rigid solver's kernel capacity), and every
  solver that pushes on bodies sizes by them (`SolverHost.bodyRows`, `bodyRowsOf`), refused with the fix when they are not
  fixed yet or its rows do not fit (docs/physics-framework.md, section 5).
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/body-rows.test.js` (a hull, its ship model, a curtain and its deck
  water in one world; the refusals) and "a curtain in a barge that lists as it floods hangs plumb" in
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`.

### Open 2026-11-26: defects found by the physics solver audit, Claude solvers (KB-PHYS-AUDIT2, physics, weather)

Found by the audit in [physics-solver-audit.md](physics-solver-audit.md); each is fixed by the row's owner with a
regression test.

- **SEA-14, fixed 2026-11-28.** The crown-onset test uses the density of the sampled liquid in the Taylor–Culick
  retraction term, which previously hard-coded 1025 kg/m³. The threshold regression in
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/entry.test.js` passes the same impact through 1000 and 1200 kg/m³ water and
  observes a crown only in the denser case.
- **SEA-01, calibration and independent checks separated.** The 10, 20 and 30 m/s runs against the stable fetch curve exercise the same calibration relation. The independent Lake George gauges are held out of the forcing and provide separate measured results in `packages/physics/scripts/sea01-lake-george-measured.mjs`. Depth-limited significant-height and peak-period accuracy remain open.
- **SEA-10, the flooding solve can stop unconverged without a word.** **Cause:**
  `packages/physics/src/seakeeping/flooding.ts` ends its 200-sweep loop silently. Also, the iron-ore cargo default
  grain is 1e-4 m while the code's own comment gives about 0.012 m for taconite pellets.
  **Fixed 2026-11-26:** each step reports the sweeps it took for the water and the air (`FloodResult.sweeps`, 200 when
  it went on unsettled) and the docs say what that means; the grain comment now gives the default (the tracer
  material's fines, 1e-4 m) and tells a taconite cargo to pass 0.012. **Regression:**
  `packages/physics/tests/flooding.test.js`, "a vented box filling through a hole".
- **SEA-12, floating bodies have no righting moment, and the buoyancy is not exact.** **Repro:** float a heeled box
  with `LoadSolver`; it does not right itself. **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/loads/solver.ts` applies buoyancy at
  the shape's centre and takes the submerged volume from an equivalent ellipsoid (a box prism is exact only upright),
  while the catalog row says exact submerged-volume buoyancy. **Fixed 2026-11-26.** The live rigid solver
  receives the displaced-volume moment from a clipped box or mesh surface, or from the analytic ellipsoid cap.
  **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/loads.test.js`, “SEA-12 a heeled box and triangle mesh return the exact
  displaced volume and righting moment”.
- **FLUID-03, particles said to be jittered are seeded on a lattice, and a particle that would enter a solid stays
  put.** **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/flip/transfer.ts` describes jittered seeding while `solver.ts` places
  particles at exact octant centres, and `solver.ts` holds a particle in place instead of projecting it out of the
  solid. **Fixed 2026-11-26:** the lattice is kept and documented, because jittered seeds set still water moving at
  6 mm/s and gave water at rest in a deck a sideways load (measured; three tests caught it). A particle carried into a
  solid now comes out at the solid's nearest face on the side it came from, never through a thin solid. Regression: "a
  particle carried into a solid comes back out at the face it went in by, never through a thin one" in
  `packages/physics/tests/flip.test.js`.
- **AERO-01, rotated bodies get the wrong panels.** **Repro:** rotate a non-box collider 45° in a steady wind.
  **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/aero.ts` builds panels from the world-axis bounding box as if it were a body-frame
  box.
- **AERO-03, stalled panels count profile drag twice.** **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/flight.ts` adds section
  profile drag on top of the stalled-panel normal force. **Fixed 2026-11-26 (4b4f1329ea):** profile drag covers only
  the attached part of a panel; a fully separated plate or flapping panel carries the normal force alone. Regression:
  "profile drag is absent from fully separated plate and flapping panels" and "profile drag covers only the attached
  area of a wing in spatially varying flow" in `packages/physics/tests/flight.test.js`.
- **ATMO-01, two wind-direction conventions in one package.** **Cause:** `weather/src/boundary-layer.ts` reads
  direction 0 as +x while `weather/src/wind.ts` reads it as +Z.
- **ATMO-01, gusts repeat with height.** **Repro:** sample the boundary-layer gust at 4 m and 260 m. **Cause:** the
  turbulence box wraps vertically every 256 m, so the vertical velocity does not vanish at the ground and the two
  heights match.

### Open 2026-11-26: defects found by the physics solver audit (KB-PHYS-AUDIT1, physics)

The audit in [physics-solver-audit.md](physics-solver-audit.md) read every solver built by Codex. Missing pieces are
listed there and the rows are REOPENED; these are the defects, each to be fixed by the row's owner with a regression
test.

- **DYN-05, reversed curve load fixed.** The former signed square of wheel speed reversed lateral acceleration.
  Bogies and carbody now use speed squared with the surveyed curvature sign for both travel directions.
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/rail.test.js` checks both curve hands and `rail.browser.mjs` checks that wet
  forward and reverse passes at the same curve station lean toward the same outside rail.
- **DYN-05, a flange can never climb.** **Repro:** any flange contact; L/V never exceeds 1. **Cause:** `car.ts` caps
  the flange force at the vertical load, so no Nadal check can ever trip.
- **ICE-05, warm surface ablation fixed.** The backward Stefan update formerly ran the warm boundary energy
  through the full ice and prescribed snow thickness. Surface energy now consumes ice at the boundary freezing
  point. `packages/physics/tests/ice.test.js` verifies the same melt depth at equal applied surface heat on thin
  and thick columns, proportional response to the transfer coefficient and finite complete melt.
- **BREAK-03, sustained crush support fixed.** A pressed body with a sensor collider used to pass through an
  already contacted patch because the latch suppressed all subsequent normal reactions. A unilateral, damped
  backing step now carries the continuing load without creating a new damage event. The six-second fixed
  and reciprocal movable-support regression is in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/crush.test.js`.
- **BREAK-03, crush contact ignored surface friction.** Oblique contact transferred a normal impulse and
  left slip unaffected. A configured dry coefficient now bounds the tangential reaction at the same point,
  including after the first contact. Coverage is in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/crush.test.js`.
- **ATMO-07, a lightning leader can stall with no flash and no error.** **Repro:** a domain where the leader runs out
  of candidate cells before it reaches ground or a target. **Cause:** `packages/physics/src/lightning/index.ts` ends
  growth silently.
- **DYN-04, host transcendentals in state-feeding vehicle code, fixed 2026-11-28 (lane P).** `tyres.ts`, `vehicle.ts`,
  `motorcycle.ts` and `tracked.ts` called `Math.atan`, `Math.sin`, `Math.exp`, `Math.hypot` and `**` in forces that feed
  the world hash (an alias `const atan = Math.atan` hid two of them), and `npm run check:pinned-math` did not scan them.
  They now use `@margoengine/math/pinned` (`tan` as pinned `sin / cos`, a cube and a quaternion's length by exact
  products and `Math.sqrt`), and the four files are on the gate's always-checked list. Regression:
  `tests/check-pinned-math.test.js` "the vehicle code that feeds a world is held to pinned maths"; the vehicle and road
  suites pass (53 and 14).
- **SOFT-06, the pV test cannot fail.** **Repro:** `tests/coupling/gas-pressure.test.js` asserts pV is constant, but
  `soft.ts` computes pressure as nRT/V, so it holds by construction; the public "conserves pV" claim rests on it.
  Also, doc comments in `soft.ts` and `soft-split.ts` say a cloth is never split, while `splitOnTear: 'all'` splits it.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a hull that has lost its buoyancy sank with no drag (KB-SEA-SINKDRAG1, physics seakeeping)

- **Repro:** a 20 by 4 by 8 m box barge floating at 2 m with one compartment filling most of it, holed at the bow and
  vented (`HullSolver` with `compartments` and `openings`): it settles as it floods and goes under at about 25 s, then
  falls faster and faster (17.7 m/s at 50 s) and pitches over, where a hull this shape falls at about 4 m/s.
- **Cause:** the hull solver's loads model a floating hull (the waves it makes, its roll's bilge eddies); nothing takes
  the form drag of a hull moving through the water once it is under, which sets a sinking hull's speed.
- **Fix:** each wet piece facing the way the hull moves takes the stagnation pressure 1/2 rho C (v . n)^2 (Newton's impact
  law, C = 1.05, Hoerner's cube), v relative to the water at the centre of mass, the roll's part left to the roll damping,
  in the share the hull has gone under past the displacement it floats at (a floating hull's surface models keep theirs).
  The barge now sinks at about 4 m/s flat, then pitches bow down and falls edge-first at about 10 m/s.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, "a box going down under the sea falls at the speed
  its form drag allows" (terminal speed to 0.1 percent; without the drag, ever faster).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a demo page marked ready after it had shown an error (KB-DEMO-STATUS1, examples)

- **Repro:** `tests/demo-status.test.js`: 56 example pages wrote `data-ready` and their status text themselves. An
  error shown by `onError` (a lost device, an uncaptured GPU error) was overwritten a moment later by the ready line,
  with `data-ready` still set, so a page check passed a page that had failed.
- **Cause:** no shared helper: each page set the flag and the text on its own path, and the ready path never asked
  whether an error had been shown.
- **Fix:** `examples/demo-status.ts` (`demoStatus`) is the one place that marks a page ready, loading or failed; after
  an error `ready` changes nothing, the error text stays, `data-ready` is removed and `data-error` holds the message.
  Every page uses it.
- **Regression:** `tests/demo-status.test.js` (the helper's behaviour, and a scan that fails on any example that writes
  `data-ready` itself).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: visual vortices supplied neither full wind nor loads (PA-31)

- **Repro:** Sample the eyewall of a 150 hPa hurricane or put a rigid object and a water grid under a moving vortex.
- **Cause:** The visual weather sample capped mean wind and the storm had no physical consumer.
- **Fix:** Sky reports the full speed. A matching `StormVortex` drives plant sway and publishes real rigid loads,
  pressure forcing, and wind stress for the world-stepped water.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/vortices.test.js` covers the >60 m/s case, real rigid debris,
  a moving shallow-water reach and the CY-14 gale. The Sky hurricane and tornado suites check shared balances.

### Fixed 2026-11-26 (the report only; the kill is attributed, not proven): the flood bounds test process once ended without a report (water)

- **Repro:** Not reproduced. In one `test:changed` run of 70 packages on the Windows workstation (CPU load about 88%),
  `npm run test` in packages/water reported `test/flood-bounds.test.js` as failed after 270 s with only
  `'test failed'`: no subtest, assertion, fatal error or Windows crash event. The file then passed alone (18 of 18,
  508 s) and in a second run of the package's tests (261 of 261, exit 0, peak resident memory at exit 171 MiB).
- **Cause:** Not proven. The signature is the one KB-TEST-FILEEXIT1 describes, a file process ended from outside (Node
  26.13 reports a `taskkill /F` of one as a bare 'test failed'), and it is not a timeout kill: `test:changed` and
  `run-with-timeout` print `timed out` / `TIMEOUT after N min`, and water sets no per-file limit. The failure came after
  3c08d37a1 landed, so the kill was either from scripts without that fix (another lane's unrebased worktree runs the
  scripts of its own checkout) or from a cause not found. The leading explanation is the first; it is attributed by
  signature, not shown.
- **Fixed (the reporting gap):** Node's own failure event for such a file carries the child's exit code, signal and
  duration, which the default reporter drops. `scripts/support/test-exit-reporter.mjs` wraps the spec reporter and adds
  `test file ended without a result: <file>, exit code <n>, signal <s>, after <ms> ms`; `test:changed` sets it for every
  package and root test run (`NODE_OPTIONS=--test-reporter`, so the nested `node --test` of a package script gets it).
  The next occurrence names itself; a lane that runs `node --test` by hand can pass `testExitEnv()` the same way.
  Checked on the fixed tree: three copies of `flood-bounds.test.js` at once beside four CPU hogs under
  `run-with-timeout --max=18` all passed (18 of 18, about 16 min each).
- **Regression:** tests/test-exit-report.test.js kills a running test file from outside and checks the report names its
  exit code, signal and time (it fails without the reporter: only 'test failed' is printed).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: simulated earthquake loads lacked a propagating ground field (EARTH-08)

- **Repro:** Trigger a moment below a layered site. Scene shake parameters could move a camera, but the ground
  did not propagate a wave or supply different site accelerations to structures.
- **Cause:** The engine had no solver for the site's elastic propagation and free-surface response.
- **Fix:** `SeismicGround` propagates P and SV waves and publishes surface acceleration, building response,
  and soil cyclic demand. `SeismicInertialLoad` moves coupled rigid bodies in their support reference frame.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seismic.test.js` checks the analytic wave branches, a
  free surface and layered site, live body recoil, and replay in both memory modes.

### Fixed: rejected seismic work could change the accepted section (EARTH-08)

Elastic, surface and building fields previously advanced in place, and a later invalid support
could leave the rigid force buffer partly written. These stages now publish only after checking
the whole candidate. Initial material callbacks can safely grow plain world memory before the
initialized bank is copied. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seismic.test.js` checks numeric failure,
late force rejection, separate owning memories and signed-origin replay.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: outdoor sounds played before the pressure wave arrived (PA-64)

- **Repro:** Send a brief sound from 3 km away. Its old positional path pans and attenuates the sound as soon as it plays.
- **Cause:** Panning and Doppler act on the source's current pose. The graph carried no travel time or air absorption.
- **Fix:** `OutdoorSound` solves the acoustic path and `OutdoorAudio` applies its delay and broad spectral response.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/outdoor-sound.test.js` checks air, diffraction and reflection.
  `packages/audio/tests/outdoor-sound.browser.mjs` measures the added arrival delay in real PCM.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a glTF wall added to LightBounce did not stop the bounce in the visibility maps (KB-BOUNCE-OCCLUDE1, clustered)

- **Repro:** packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js, the table-by-the-wall room given as gltf/pbr primitives: before, only
  core meshes' triangles (`occluderMeshes` of the frame's batches) were scene occluders, so a model added with
  `bounce.add` occluded through its captured texels alone, and the wall the table hides from the lantern let the room's
  VPLs light the ground outside (over 5% of the unblocked bounce at three receivers, where an exact cast gives 0).
- **Cause:** `LightBounce.rebuild` built the visibility maps' scene occluders from core's batches only; PR #150 drew added
  models into the captures but never gave their triangles to `sampleSurfaces` (imperfect shadow maps sample every surface
  of the scene: Ritschel et al., ACM TOG 27(5), 2008, doi:10.1145/1409060.1409082).
- **Fix:** `bounceModelMeshes(model, store)` reads an added model's public `primitives` (20-float vertices, node matrix,
  instance rows; the primitives the capture draws, nodes shown in the transform store), and the rebuild samples them
  with core's meshes. `BounceMesh.stride` (default 6) lets `sampleSurfaces` read gltf/pbr's vertex layout.
- **Regression:** the CPU test above (the model's occluders equal the core meshes' to 1e-5, under 2% of unblocked behind
  the wall, filters for BLEND, tint, after-opaque, unlit, lines, skinned and hidden nodes), and the `wallModel` row of
  scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (the rooms' wall as a glTF box: 36 occluder pieces,
  the core wall's 36; the dark room 0). Skinned primitives, terrain and voxel still occlude through their captures only
  (docs/limits.md).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a clearcoat from `materials.install` reflected its full base albedo into SSR and LightBounce captures (KB-BOUNCE-CAPTURE2, gltf)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js` with its `installed` row: the LightBounce patch as a glTF quad with
  KHR_materials_clearcoat 1 drawn by `materials.install`, added with `bounce.add`, bounced exactly the uncoated patch's
  light onto the wall (ratio 1.000 at both points), where the same coat on a materials `Material` (`clearcoat: 1`) bounced
  0.955 and 0.959 of it, the base layer's 1 - F_coat(n.v) share (KHR_materials_clearcoat, "Layering"; F0 0.04 head on).
- **Cause:** gltf/pbr builds the capture shader by appending a `capture` entry point (`capturePBR`) after
  `materialExtensionShader` had run the extension's surface edits on every `let s=surface(i,front);`. The appended entry
  built the plain surface, so `materialClearcoatLighting` never ran there and its `materialCoatKeep` stayed 1, and the
  capture's base-layer weight `k` read only the native `layers` (none on an extension coat). SSR's capture shares the
  path, so its split-sum weight under an installed coat was too high as well.
- **Fix:** `capturePBR(code, declarations, keep)` multiplies `k` by the extension coat's `keep` expression, and
  `PBRModel`'s capture derivation applies `materialExtensionSurface` to the appended entry, as the SSAO occlusion entry
  already does. A materials `createMesh` mesh (a gltf/pbr model) needed nothing: `bounce.add(mesh)` and its clearcoat were
  right already, and the GPU check now holds them (`materials` and `coated` rows).
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/extensions.test.js ("a material extension coat weighs k by its keep"), and the
  `installed`, `materials` and `coated` rows of scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js on WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`
  (0.9548 and 0.9586 of the core patch, within 1% of 0.96; the materials patch 1.0000; the JS twin within 2%).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: sand ripples aliased into moire on frames under 1080 lines (KB-TERRAIN-SAND3, terrain)

- **Repro:** `packages/terrain/test/sand-footprint.browser.mjs`: flat sand from 20 m up, rendered at 960 x 540 and
  480 x 270 and compared with a 3840 x 2160 frame filtered down to each (a Gaussian of 0.5 small pixels). Mean sRGB
  luma error was 1.90 and 2.76 steps with ripples on (0.07 and 0.12 with them off).
- **Cause:** the `sandSurface` ripple clamp took its pixel footprint as the distance over 1,000, one pixel of a
  1080-line frame at 50 degrees, whatever the frame's real size. A 540-line pixel is 1.7 times wider and a 270-line one
  3.5 times, so 0.1 m ripples stayed on where a pixel no longer resolves them.
- **Fix:** `TerrainColors` takes the footprint once per pixel as the longer of `dpdx` and `dpdy` of the position, at the
  top of the shared per-pixel block where control flow is uniform (as the mesh blend and rock surface do), and passes
  it to every mesh's `terrainSurface`. Errors now 1.10 and 0.66 (RTX A6000, Edge 158).
- **Regression:** the test above (under 1.4 steps with ripples, under 0.3 without), in terrain's `test:gpu`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a long multibody chain gained energy until it left the numbers (KB-PHYS-MBSYM1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/multibody_chain.rs`: a 1 m chain of 24 or 64 capsules of radius 1 cm on spherical
  joints, held as one multibody from a fixed wall, released level under gravity. Before the fix the 24-link chain ran past
  10^5 m/s within two seconds and the 64-link one was refused as past the numbers at step 19. From the public API, the same
  happens with `physics.addMultibody` on 24 or more slender links.
- **Cause:** the projection onto the joint space (`project_tree`, Featherstone's articulated-body pass written for impulses)
  is exact only on symmetric inertias. Each link's rotational inertia was built a column at a time from f32 rotations, so it was
  asymmetric in its last bits. The pass from the last link to the first (A - A S D^-1 S^T A, then P^T A P) keeps a symmetric
  matrix symmetric, but it grows any asymmetry about 3.5 times a link. Near the root the rotational block was as asymmetric as
  it was large, D = S^T A S stopped being the matrix of the least change of energy, and the "projection" put energy in: up to
  60 % of the chain's kinetic energy in one step.
- **Fix:** each link's inertia is built from its principal axes in doubles, each entry once and mirrored. D, each link's
  articulated inertia and its transport to the parent are made symmetric (`symmetric`, the mean of each pair) at every link.
  The pass is then the Schur complement of a symmetric positive definite matrix, which is stable. The replay hashes are
  unchanged (no replay scene has a multibody).
- **Regression:** `a_long_slender_chain_falls_with_no_more_energy_than_it_had`: 600 steps of 24 and 64 links. No link moves
  faster than its share of the fall to hanging straight down allows, sqrt(2 (E0 - E_min) / m); the nearest reach 0.597 and
  0.454 of it.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the order bodies woke in changed how the world moved (KB-PHYS-ORDER1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/canonical.rs`: two worlds with the same rows, one with its awake list put back in
  a shuffled order (as if its bodies had woken in that order); their bodies differed after 45 steps.
- **Cause:** a step works through its lists in the order they were filled: the awake list in wake order (which numbered the
  islands and ordered each island's bodies), the active pairs in the order they were found and swapped out. Gauss-Seidel
  passes give different bits in a different order, so history the world does not hold as state decided its path, against
  rule 4 of docs/physics-framework.md section 7 (iteration order never depends on allocation order).
- **Fix:** at the start of every step and again after the island build's wake-ups, the awake list is put in body order and
  the active pairs in the order of their colliders and parts (`canonical_lists`, a stable bottom-up merge sort through
  scratch columns). Islands are numbered by their lowest body, and bodies, pairs and events come in row and collider order.
- **Regression:** the test above (600 steps, three wake orders shuffled again every 50 steps, and a snapshot restored at step
  300, bit for bit). The joint web's seed 1 now takes another path, on which its drivers do 1.7e12 J of work and a body
  reaches 172 km/s with no energy gained; `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` bounded speeds at 1e5 m/s, a figure with
  no derivation, and now bounds them by the range a step refuses past (RANGE) and, from the energy ledger, each body's speed by
  sqrt(2 K / m): K the energy the bodies were given so far less their height energy, m its own mass (seeds 1 to 60 reach at
  most 0.792 of it).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a held hull's deck volume fed by the sea's inflow took about half its water's weight (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD2, physics flip)

- **Repro:** a box hull (2 m by 1 m by 1 m, a dynamic body held still by its locks) with its deck 0.2 m under still fresh
  water, `HullSolver` writing `deckInflow` and `DeckWaterSolver` (inflow on, the deck box on the deck, cells [20, 6, 10] of
  0.1 m). The deck volume takes the inflow and settles at 0.438 m^3 (4,297 N), but its load on the hull (its forces region,
  y) settles at -2,198 N after 6 s. KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1's fix brought the same case from +1,124 N; its regression (0.3 m of
  water placed at the start, no inflow) takes the full weight.
- **Cause:** the water was right to the load; the particles were not right to the water. Each particle stands for an
  eighth of a cell of water, but the inflow put its particles along the bulwark whether a cell there was full or not,
  and particles then clustered where the flow converged and against the walls that stop them (FLIP's known volume loss):
  at 6 s the deck's particles stood 16.8 to a cell, so the liquid the grid kept, and its load, were half the water they
  counted.
- **Fix:** the inflow puts each particle in the first cell inward from the bulwark with room for it (fewer than eight),
  and the liquid now runs the implicit density projection of Kugelstadt, Longva, Thuerey and Bender (IEEE TVCG 27(4),
  2021) after each advection: the particles' density on the grid, held at 1 or more beside the air and to 0.5 to 1.5,
  with the walls sampled as water at rest, drives a second pressure solve whose gradient moves the particles apart.
  The same case now holds the hull with -4,578 N for 4,393 N of water (within the grid's bound), its particles at 7.2 a
  cell.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/deck-water.test.js`, "the deck volume claims its hull, so the hull carries one
  deck load, not two": the deck volume's load equals its water's weight within rho g l b h / 2.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: deck water on a hull held still loaded it with a fraction of its weight (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1, physics/flip)

- **Repro:** a dynamic hull held by locks (or by contacts, joints, a mooring) with a `DeckWaterSolver` on it: 0.3 m of
  water on a 2 m by 1 m deck (5,886 N) held the hull with -237 N; with the exceedance solver's inflow and the real hull
  solver, +1,124 N against -4,297 N.
- **Cause:** the deck volume carries its water as added mass in an implicit solve, M (M + A)^-1 (F + W) - W, which takes
  the hull as free: the water's weight went into a fall the hull never made, so little of it reached a hull something
  else held.
- **Fix:** the solve carries every other load on the hull too, seen in what moved it at the last step (M a_last less the
  load held and the weight), as the hull solver does: M (M + A)^-1 (F + A a_last + W + O) - W - O. A held hull takes the
  water's weight; a free one still falls with its water at g.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/deck-water.test.js`, "a dynamic hull held by locks takes its deck water's
  weight as the deck load (KB-FLIP-DECKLOAD1)".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a box mesh was filled with a tunnel by `SoftBodyDesc.volumetric` (KB-SOFT-HOLLOWBOX1, physics soft cells)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/soft-cells.test.js`, "the volume constraint and the skin go with the pieces of a body that is cut",
  and "a box mesh is filled by every cube of its lattice, whichever way its faces are cut into triangles". A 0.4 m box mesh of
  twelve triangles with `SoftBodyDesc.volumetric(vertices, indices, 0.1)` came out with 360 cells instead of 384 and a surface
  of 232 triangles instead of 192, with an edge four triangles met at. `soft.create` of it with a volume target threw
  "A body that holds its volume needs a closed surface whose triangles face outward" (since SOFT-06 added that check).
- **Cause:** `insideMesh` in `soft-volume.ts` counted a +x ray through a triangle with inclusive edge tests, so a ray exactly on
  the diagonal two triangles of a face share crossed both. Every cube centre level with a face diagonal (the lattice centres
  with y equal to z here) crossed two diagonals, an even count, and read as outside. The cubes in the middle of the box were
  left out, a tunnel along x, and the body's surface pinched at it. Before SOFT-06 only the volume was checked, so the hole
  went unseen.
- **Fix:** the crossing is counted watertight: each edge is measured once, in one canonical direction, for the triangles that
  share it, and a ray on an edge is nudged symbolically (Woop, Benthin and Wald 2013; Edelsbrunner and Muecke 1990), so it crosses
  the surface once. With both triangulations of the faces and three lattice sizes the box fills every cube.
- **Regression:** the two tests above (the second fails on the previous code: 60 of 64 cubes for a 4 cube box).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: on the WebGL2 compatibility layer, test:shot's sky-coverage check loses the device on the orrery shot (KB-SHOT-COMPATLOST1, environment; was tools/shot)

- **Repro:** on an Apple M6 Mac (ANGLE on Metal), `npm run build:packages`, then `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:shot`. Two
  runs out of two failed the same way. `determinism-check.mjs` passes all its cases. `sky-coverage-check.mjs` passes its
  first two shots (cabin-hearth-kettle, cabin-window-snow). On its third, orrery-dolly (the page with no sky), the page
  logs `AbortError: The device was lost before the buffer mapped; map it again on the restored device`, and the shot
  tool fails on that page error (`tools/shot/render.mjs`, the console handler). `moving-check.mjs` and
  `look-masks-check.mjs` did not run after it. On WebGPU, `npm run test:shot` passes.
