- **Cause:** half found. The line is a `console.error` of an uncaught DOMException, and the orrery's `start()` prints
  its rejection exactly so (examples/orrery/main.ts). The readback that waits is the light probe bake's copy back
  (`LightProbes.copyOnce`, after `await probes.bake({ bounces: 3 })` while the page loads): it turned an aborted map
  into the coded "bake interrupted" error only once the device was restored, so a map cut off by a loss before the
  restore left `bake()` as the raw DOMException. The layer also gave the device-loss text when only the buffer had been
  destroyed during its map. What loses the context on ANGLE Metal is still not known. "Third page in the same browser"
  does not hold: `shoot()` opens a fresh browser for each shot (tools/shot/render.mjs), and a page holds 3 WebGL2
  contexts (adapter probe, its lost probe and the device), far under Chrome's cap.
- **Fixed (2026-11-26):** the layer names the cause that aborted a map ("The buffer was destroyed before it mapped" or
  the device loss), and a bake whose readback map aborts rejects with the coded `state` "Light probe bake interrupted"
  error. Regressions: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/task-polling.test.js` ("a map aborted by its own buffer destroy names
  the destroy...") and `packages/environment/tests/probes.test.js` ("a device lost during the bake readback rejects
  with the coded interruption..."); both fail on the old code. A loss during the bake still fails the orrery's load.
- **Laptop runs (Intel Arc 140V, Chrome, 2026-11-26):** no loss on ANGLE Direct3D 11 or ANGLE Vulkan. Vulkan
  (`BROWSER_ARGS='["--use-angle=vulkan"]'`) passes the whole sky-coverage check; orrery-dolly alone passes on
  Direct3D 11. On Direct3D 11 the three shots in a row failed differently: orrery-dolly never asked for its first frame
  within `PAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 s, `untilQueued`). Alone it took 133 to 185 s from page open to its first kept frame
  (Vulkan: 41 s); a CPU profile of the load has 28.5 % in `getProgramParameter` (program links waited on
  synchronously from pipeline variants), 10.8 % in `getError` and 8 % in the layer's CPU compute runtime. Still open:
  the ANGLE Metal loss (rerun on the Mac with the new texts to see whether it is a loss or a destroy) and the orrery's
  Direct3D 11 load time on the layer against the shot tool's 180 s wait.
- **Same on main:** main's tools/shot fails the same way. The film hook added for PA-03 does not change it.
- **Windows run (RTX A6000, Chrome, 2026-11-27, main cd4508a015):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node tools/shot/test/sky-coverage-check.mjs` passes all three shots, orrery included, so the loss is specific to ANGLE Metal. A rerun on the M6 Mac with the new loss texts is the only way forward; no cause is claimed.
- **Cause (M6 Mac, Chrome 156, ANGLE Metal, 2026-11-27, main f3a7cb1d62):** the orrery alone fails within 6 s; Chrome
  logs "GL_INVALID_OPERATION ... ContextMtl.mm, checkCommandBufferError ... Metal command buffer execution failed", then
  the context is lost, during `probes.bake({ bounces: 3 })`. The orrery passes with its reflection probes at 64 px or
  without them, and fails with one bounce or without its volume. `packages/environment` probe-capture at 256 px on the
  layer reads black where 16 and 128 px pass, and passes at 256 px with `samples: 256` (the sampled filter), on native
  WebGPU on the Mac, and on the layer on Windows. The default bake's exact GGX prefilter ran each rough level as one
  dispatch whose every output texel loops over all of level 0: 65,536 texels at 256 px, 16,384 at 128 px. Chunking
  that loop: 65,536 per texel failed whatever the chunk's total reads (2^20 to 2^24), 32,768 and 16,384 passed, with
  or without waiting for each submit, and a 2^26-read chunk of 16,384 passed. So the per-texel loop length decides it.
- **Fixed (2026-11-27):** `LightProbes` runs the exact prefilter after each bounce's capture in chunks of at most 2^14
  source texels per output texel and 2^24 reads, one submit each; a chunk that does not reach the last texel keeps its
  float32 running sum in a storage buffer for the next (same additions, same order). A 256 px probe takes 96 submits a
  bounce. Regression: `packages/environment/tests/probes.test.js` ("the exact prefilter of a 256 px probe loops over at
  most 2^14 source texels per dispatch"), which fails on the old code. On the M6 Mac probe-capture at 256 px and
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node tools/shot/test/sky-coverage-check.mjs` pass (all three shots, orrery included; WebGPU passes too). Measured byte for byte (2026-11-27,
  NVIDIA Ampere, Chrome 158, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer): a 128 px probe's stored texels from the chunked filter (its
  64 px level in 4 chunks) and from the one-dispatch filter match in all 43,680 words, checked by
  `packages/environment/tests/probe-capture-browser.js` ("chunked prefilter equals one dispatch").
- **Again on main feca833059 (RTX A6000, 2026-11-27, packages rebuilt):** the same command passes all three shots. The
  device loss has reproduced only on the M6 Mac (ANGLE on Metal); this row stays open until a Mac session reruns it.
  The Direct3D 11 load time above is a separate failure, seen on the Arc 140V laptop.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GitHub CI's lint failed every pull request, and quality checked less there (KB-CI-MERGEBASE1, .github/workflows/ci.yml)

- **Repro:** any pull request (PR 68, job 139720307693): `npm run lint` stops with `fatal: Not a valid object name
  origin/main`.
- **Cause:** `actions/checkout@v4` checks out a pull request's merge commit at depth 1 with no origin/main, and
  scripts/lint.mjs diffs against the merge base with origin/main. The test job's `npm run quality` has two readers of
  the same merge base (scripts/quality/ratchet.js `droppedHistory`, scripts/support/unit-readers.mjs
  `changedAgainstMain`) that treat a missing one as nothing to check, so a pull request's dropped baseline history and
  changed documents' readers went unchecked.
- **Fixed:** the lint and test jobs check out the whole history (`fetch-depth: 0`). Regression: tests/ci-checkout.test.js
  follows each CI job's npm scripts through their imports and fails on a job that reaches `git merge-base` without a
  full checkout (it named `lint` and `test` on the old ci.yml).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: GitHub CI's bundler matrix and Node 22 tests failed on CI setup, not on code (KB-CI-PWVERSION1, KB-CI-ORACLE1, KB-CI-FIXTURES1, ci)

- **Repro:** PR 68: "End-user proof on Node 22" (job 139720307968) stopped in `modern:test:bundlers` with
  `Executable doesn't exist` for chromium-headless-shell 1255; "node22 unit tests" (job 139720354973) had 29
  `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for packages/physics/tests/oracle/dist/index.js, `Missing Required test fixture` in gltf,
  environment and loaders, and `cannot start chromium` in ecs.
- **Causes:** (1) scripts/bundler-matrix.mjs installed Playwright at npm's latest, and scripts/modern-package-tests.js at
  the devDependency range, while CI's `npx playwright install chromium` fetched the browsers of the installed version.
  (2) The physics comparison oracle was built only by the package's own `npm test`, and CI runs the test files after
  `build:packages`. (3) The test and Node 22 jobs never fetched the Required external test assets or installed
  Chromium.
- **Fixed:** both fixtures pin the installed Playwright (scripts/support/playwright-version.mjs); `build:packages` builds
  the oracle; both jobs fetch the assets (cached on the asset list) and install Chromium before the tests.
  Regressions: tests/ci-playwright.test.js, tests/build-test-fixtures.test.js and tests/ci-test-jobs.test.js, each
  failing on the old file.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: the branches of a multibody under a fixed root were islands that walked each other's links (KB-PHYS-MBISLAND1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/next-multibody.test.js`, "two branches under a fixed root are one island, and swing as
  mirror images of each other": two pendulums hung from one fixed root by one `addMultibody` tree.
- **Cause:** joints unite only moving bodies into an island, so under a fixed or kinematic root each branch was an island of
  its own. Each island's substeps walk every multibody tree they reach (`mb_roots`), from the root through every link, so one
  island projected and placed the other branch's links in its own substeps. Solved one island at a time this re-did work on
  links already consistent; solved at once on threads it would write another island's bodies.
- **Fix:** the moving links of a multibody whose root does not move are one island (`unite_multibodies`). Branches under a
  root that does not move do not move each other, so the physics is unchanged: the replay scenes' state hashes are the same.
- **Regression:** the test above (two islands before).

### Fixed 2026-11-26: check:rust-kernels built the physics kernels with flags they no longer shipped with (KB-RUST-KERNELFLAGS1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/rust-kernel-tests.test.js`: "every kernel that ships as Wasm is built for wasm32 with the
  shipped flags" fails, `WASM_RUSTFLAGS` (`-C target-feature=+simd128`) against the 3D kernel blueprint's `RUSTFLAGS`,
  which since 8fbdc409d4 (K05) add the world-memory link flags (`--import-memory`, the slot's `--global-base` and the
  exported stack and data symbols). The test runs in hygiene, so hygiene is red on main.
- **Cause:** each physics kernel is now built with its own slot's link flags (packages/physics/scripts/build-*-kernel.mjs,
  `rustFlags(slot, shared)`), while scripts/rust-kernel-tests.mjs builds every kernel that ships as Wasm with the one
  `WASM_RUSTFLAGS` of scripts/support/wasm-kernel.mjs, so check:rust-kernels no longer checks the build that ships.
- **Fix (31623dc844):** `packages/physics/scripts/build-kernel.mjs` composes the 3D kernel's `RUSTFLAGS` (and the
  threaded build's) from `WASM_RUSTFLAGS` and its link arguments, so the shipped code generation is the one
  check:rust-kernels builds with. The flags' text and the blueprints are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `tests/rust-kernel-tests.test.js` checks the composition and that the link arguments carry no code
  generation (9 of 9 pass on 2026-11-27).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a box face resting on a block's edge was held at one end at a time and rocked for ever (KB-PHYS-EDGEHOLD1, physics kernel, contacts)

- **Repro:** `packages/voxel/tests/debris.test.js`, "with physics a piece is a dynamic body of its cells mass that falls onto
  the voxel floor and comes to rest", with the block solver on: the L-shaped piece came to lie on the edge of the pillar's
  stump and on one corner of its beam, and still moved at 0.03 to 0.16 m/s after 20 s, sinking 4 mm. The same rocking state
  stepped on with the sweeps did not settle either.
- **Cause:** the separating axis test kept last step's edge pair when it came within the face bias (1 mm) of the best face
  (`sat_coherent`, the held-edge margin `-FACE_BIAS`). An edge pair gives one point. Where it ties a face, its two edges lie
  near parallel along that face, so the closest points clamp to one end of the block's edge: the manifold held that end
  alone, the other side fell until it struck, and the held point hopped to the other end. The geometry query, with no
  history, chose the face and clipped both ends.
- **Fix:** an edge pair must beat the face by the bias whether or not it was held, the rule Gregorius (GDC 2015) gives:
  faces win ties. A held face still wins its own ties, so the reference face stays coherent. Over 1,734 poses of a plank on
  a cube's edge (turns of -40 to 40 mrad in 5 mrad steps about its length and in the face's plane, its edge 0 to 30 cm past
  the cube's), a held edge pair now gives the manifold a test with no history gives on every pose; before, 1,499 lost an end.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/sat.rs` `a_face_resting_on_a_parallel_edge_keeps_both_ends_after_an_edge_pair`
  (one point with the held edge pair before), and the voxel debris test above with the block solver.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: the joint webs' energy ledger read a kinematic body's speed as energy gained (KB-PHYS-LEDGER1, physics kernel tests)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/stability.rs` `the_energy_ledger_reads_the_same_in_a_moving_frame`: a kinematic
  hub drags a 1 kg box on a spherical joint 0.2 m out of place. At rest the ledger reads no gain; with hub and box moving at
  50 m/s it read -4,800 J. With the block solver, web seed 17 of `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` reached a state where
  one step read 3.4 MJ of work as a gain against the 73 kJ its bodies gained (2.7 percent of the run's kinematic work, bound
  one part in a million).
- **Cause:** the native ledger `solver::DRIVEN` left out the work a kinematic body does through a joint's position-bias push
  (the `BIASED` flag) but counted the relaxing pass's taking back of that push. A push p from a body at speed u is the work
  p . u whatever it is for, so the ledger's "energy no force made" grew with the frame's speed.
- **Fix:** every impulse a kinematic body hands on counts. A push taken back nets nothing, and one left behind still shows as
  a gain of about p b / 2 (b the bias speed). All 60 web seeds gain nothing with either solver; the joint-drift proof
  `a_joint_does_not_turn_its_drift_into_speed` measures speed directly and still fails on the drift bug it was made for. No
  shipped code changes: the ledger is native only.
- **Regression:** the moving-frame test above (-4,800 J before), within f32's rounding of the box's kinetic energy.

### Fixed 2026-11-25 Open-channel and flood models had no link to changing sediment beds (HYDRO-03)

The shallow-water field now drives suspended load, bedload and bank exchange. The production TerrainBed
receives conservative elevation changes, and the same concentration controls the Flood tint.
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/sediment.test.js` compares a moving and a fixed bed and verifies solid
mass. `packages/water/test/sediment-source.browser.mjs` verifies the rendering link. Flood-body
feedback, debris impact and dam breach still have their own work-queue rows.

### Open 2026-11-25 RITS-10 atmospheric-river scene still needs its watershed inputs wired

- **Repro** Re-render RITS-10 at 7:55–8:20 and 9:48–10:15 and check the terrain, streams and valley floor.
- **Cause** The original scene has no connected precipitation → catchment → flood solver inputs. The engine fixture
  routes rain and melt, checks water volume in the flood and reads the resulting inundation into Biomes. The demo review
  remains open until the scene consumes those fields and flood depth appears in the shot.

### Fixed 2026-11-25 orbital dynamics and Event Horizon's stationary beaming (SPACE-01)

The orbital catalog had mean-element satellite propagation and lacked a world-stepped N-body solver. The
Event Horizon beaming view sampled redshift and discarded the moving emission magnitude. Its real-adapter
fixture also drove wall-clock time while the raw shader reads the engine's shader clock.
`packages/physics/tests/orbit.test.js` checks the new conservative and atmospheric dynamics.
`packages/shader/test/black-hole-check.mjs` uses the actual shader clock and checks moving emission,
repeatable explicit disk time and inward advection. The live demo uses the same clock for flare timing.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: remote water changed local bank erosion (KB-SEDIMENT-LOCALBANK1)

The bank closure subtracted the mean speed of every wet cell from the wet edge's speed magnitude. A remote
pool could change the erosion of a separate reach and channel-normal flow could move a bank. The closure now
uses the signed bank-parallel velocity and the weighted mean of the connected local wet section. Both sides
move the same accounted volume. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/coupling/sediment.test.js` verifies remote
pool isolation and the signed mass balance on both axes. Its float32 overflow test also verifies preservation
of each accepted buffer and the previous work receipt after a rejected candidate.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: finite extreme orbital forces and periapsis motion (KB-ORBIT-RANGE1)

A finite inverse-square force could disappear or reject when its squared separation or intermediate
strength left float64 range before source mass was applied. The native kernel scales extreme pairs
while preserving force direction. Near a parabolic periapsis, subtracting nearly equal terms in
Kepler's equation lost displacement and velocity precision. The residual and half-angle radius now
retain those terms. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/orbit.test.js` checks both physical values
and coded input corrections. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/orbit-threads.test.js` checks that a
failed singular step leaves the earlier accepted orbit and worker work intact.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: thin uniform acoustic columns visited each reflection (KB-SOUND-03-FOLD)

A 1/60 s tick in a uniform 2⁻²⁰ m column at 1,920 m/s needed 33,554,432 identical crossings.
The solver now folds the straight unfolded path, applies each boundary's signed pressure factor by
integer powers and updates the beam by its full uniform drift. A separate overflow at large launch waists
came from squaring the complex beam coordinates before finding the norm and phase. Scaling those
coordinates preserves the phase and width when the unscaled products leave float64 range.
Regression: `packages/physics/tests/underwater.test.js` covers both failures and ensures that a reflection
count outside exact integer range leaves the previous accepted ray intact.

### Fixed 2026-11-25 underwater sound lacked depth refraction and water-column arrivals (SOUND-03)

The air propagation path used a fixed sound speed and had no depth axis for water. In a layered water column
it could not reproduce a turning ray or its delayed pressure at a receiver. The optional underwater solver
traces both the ray and its paraxial beam. See the turning-point and multi-reflection cases in
`packages/physics/tests/underwater.test.js` and the registry reader in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/underwater.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: fixed ice geometry could not respond to world-clock heating (ICE-05)

The signed ice ports now follow the live world cell. A malformed late condition or unaligned field
lease preserves all accepted ice geometry and exchanges. The mixed-site and real lava cases exercise
the signed state, phase closures and world replay. `packages/physics/tests/coupling/ice.test.js`

The prior ice render shapes had no phase-change state. A pulse delivering fusion, sensible and vaporisation
energy to a thin sheet could neither melt it nor return the resulting drainage and steam in the world.
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/ice.test.js` reproduces that forcing and checks the returned mass and absorbed
power. EARTH-10 can connect using the layouts requested in the [work queue](physics-work-queue.md#framework-requests).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: missing time-varying celestial forcing and tracker backtracking (SPACE-02)

Fixed the missing clock-driven celestial fields used by the sea, boundary layer and tracker calculations. The optional physics/celestial solver now publishes Earth-fixed tidal forcing and insolation and locates solar and lunar eclipses. Regression tests reproduce uniform tracking and adjacent shading from SOLARFIELD-2 and SOLARFIELD-3 and verify slope-aware backtracking, per-row tolerance and wind stow. See [physics-solvers.md](physics-solvers.md) and the [package README](../packages/physics/README.md#celestial-ephemeris-tides-and-insolation-margoenginephysicscelestial).

### Open 2026-11-28: analytic grazing eclipse contact errors (SPACE-02)

Run `node packages/physics/scripts/space02-celestial-measured.mjs`. The default analytic orbit plus circular-disc model produces 168 s of totality in Stephenville against a 9.9–15.9 s span from the published camera frames. The lunar apparent limb and higher-precision contact calculation remain open. [Measured contacts](limits.md#space-02-measured-eclipse-contacts-near-the-edge-of-totality)

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a WgslMaterial could not read a borrowed 32-bit float texture, so the depth-texture demo drew black (KB-DEPTHTEX-BLACK1, materials)

- **Repro:** `npm run visual:update` on a186f625f0 (RTX A6000, Edge 158.0.4370.33): `depth-texture-high` and `-phone`
  captured an all-black canvas in 4 of 4 runs with no page or WGSL error. The page's status, watched as it changed,
  briefly read `MargoError: Texture samples 32-bit float texels, which needs the device feature float32-filterable`.
  Chrome 158 gave the same; not a browser change.
- **Cause:** f6f22a4977 (2026-11-20, borrowed-object rule) added a `float32-filterable` refusal to the shared bind of
  every Texture made from a GPUTexture. A WgslMaterial reads such a texture with `textureLoad`, which needs no
  filtering (as its docs say), so DepthTexture's r32float `distance` threw on the first frame, core stopped the loop
  and the demo then wrote its ready text over the error and reported ready. The visual check took the black canvas.
- **Fix:** the refusal stays only where texels are filtered: material map slots (`sampled`) and envMap, each now
  checked after the bind so a function source, whose format is known only then, is refused too. The demo keeps an
  error on screen and never reports ready after one. Class guard: `scripts/visual-regression.js` fails a view that
  showed an error text at any moment, even one other text replaced (`scripts/support/shown-errors.js`); on the bug
  build it fails both depth-texture views with the MargoError above. A guard on GPU work was tried first and dropped:
  gameplay-sandbox and windy-meadow stop their loop on purpose under reduced motion, so they submit no work either.
  Regressions: "a borrowed 32-bit float GPUTexture binds to a WgslMaterial without float32-filterable" in
  packages/materials/test/texture-formats.test.js (fails on the old code) and tests/visual-shown-errors.test.js.
  Other demos still write their ready text over an onError message; the guard catches them in the visual check.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: `GPUSceneBVH`'s buffers were missing from the borrowed GPU object registry, so hygiene failed (bvh)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/borrowed-gpu.test.js` on f9634050e1: five `bvh:GPUSceneBVH` members are unlisted.
- **Cause:** the new class exposes the buffers it creates, and its push added no rows to `scripts/borrowed-registry.json`.
- **Fix:** five exempt rows (the package makes them; no caller object is held). Regression: `tests/borrowed-gpu.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: native glass with the shared scene depth or a sciviz volume left the glass's own picture on screen (materials, KB-FILM-NEST2)

- **Repro:** a transmissive glTF material in a scene that also holds water, `html`, clustered contact shadows (the
  shared scene depth) or a sciviz volume, with no HDR post effect: with the shared depth at 4x, one frame on a new
  background reads the frame before (`packages/materials/test/native-glass-browser.mjs` `hdrNesting`, `scene depth 4x`).
  On a recorded pass list the glass presents a colour nothing has drawn into and the later capture writes after it, at
  4x for both and at 1x for the sciviz volume (`packages/materials/tests/native-glass-nesting.test.js`).
- **Cause:** captures nest, but the native glass capture presented at order 29 whatever had begun inside it: the shared
  depth begins at -15 and ends at 10000, the volume depth begins at -0.001 and ends at 39. The glass copied its own
  empty target to the frame, and the inner capture then wrote the scene into the glass's target, which was not shown
  again until the next frame.
- **Fix:** the glass presents at 29 only while it still owns the frame's colour; with a capture still open inside it,
  it presents at 10000.5, after every such capture has ended (`packages/materials/src/native-glass.js`). Scenes with no
  inner capture draw the same passes as before. A frame graph keeps a target until its last user is done (O'Donnell,
  "FrameGraph: Extensible Rendering Architecture in Frostbite", GDC 2017, https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1024612);
  no source treats this engine's pass orders.
- **Regression:** the two tests above, the GPU one on native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: on ANGLE Direct3D 11 a lit glTF scene with image light, both shadow kinds and LightBounce crashed the GPU process (KB-BOUNCE-COMPATUNITS1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/compat-units-gpu-check.js --compat` (Edge, default
  ANGLE Direct3D 11, RTX A6000): a gltf physical material with all 13 maps (or the 5 + 5 peak) under Environment
  lighting, Shadows `soft`, a shadowed Clustered spot (LocalShadows) and LightBounce. Every WebGL context was lost at
  the first lit draw, shown as "The compatibility layer's own present program did not link (a bug: report it)". The
  same scene drew on ANGLE Vulkan and GL, and on Direct3D 11 with one texture unit fewer.
- **Cause:** ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end gives a std140 uniform block that holds one array of 50 or more rows a shader
  resource after the stage's textures (a StructuredBuffer, its HLSL `register(t15)` and `register(t16)` here); the lit
  fragment program had 15 texture units and two such blocks, 17 resources, and past 16 the browser's GPU process ends
  at the program's first draw (exit 0xC000001D). A raw WebGL2 page shows it with no Margo code:
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-srv-crash-repro.mjs` (16 samplers and one `uvec4[50]` block crash, `uvec4[49]`
  does not; 14 samplers and 3 blocks crash, 13 do not; ANGLE Vulkan draws every case). The layer's unit count (15 of
  16) was right; the blocks are not texture units to GL. Second defect: a lost context surfaced as a layer bug (the
  present program "did not link"), as a validation error (a framebuffer "not complete") or as a thrown
  transferToImageBitmap, because the context is lost at once and its webglcontextlost event comes a task later.
- **Fix:** the GLSL back end (glsl/emit.ts `fitShaderResources`) counts a stage's texture units and uniform blocks
  together; past the stage's limit (`translateWGSL` `textureUnits`, from MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS and
  MAX_VERTEX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS) each block declares its rows inside a struct, the same std140 layout, which ANGLE
  keeps as a constant buffer. Stages that fit are byte for byte as before. A lost context now loses the device
  (`device.lost`, reason 'unknown'): errors are not raised after it, the present stops, and the layer's helper
  programs return unlinked instead of throwing.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js` (the struct form past the limit, per stage, and the plain
  form within it), `packages/webgl2-compat/test/lost-context-browser.mjs` and `scripts/compat-units-gpu-check.js
  --compat` (both in webgl2-compat's test:gpu; the check passes on native WebGPU, ANGLE Direct3D 11 and Vulkan).
  The room the plan in the row asks for landed after it: glTF slots sharing a texture bind it once (2026-11-25), gltf
  materials past the device limit pack their base maps, and the layer counts units per stage before linking and
  refuses past a limit with code `unsupported` (errors#texture-units) (2026-11-26; `packages/gltf/test/materials-ext.test.js`,
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/device.test.js`). A scene that needs more than 16 units even packed still gets that
  coded refusal.
- **Sources:** Direct3D 11 has 128 shader resource slots, 16 sampler slots and 14 constant buffer slots per stage, so
  the 16 is ANGLE's own table, not the API's (Microsoft, "Direct3D 11.3 Functional Specification", 2015, section 21
  limits, https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/archive/D3D11_3_FunctionalSpec.htm). A struct member of a
  std140 block holding one uvec4 array keeps offset 0 and a 16-byte stride, so the layout is unchanged (Khronos, "OpenGL
  ES Version 3.0.6", 2019, section 2.12.6.4, https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/es_spec_3.0.pdf), and a
  `#define` maps each row read onto it (Khronos, "The OpenGL ES Shading Language 3.00", 2016, section 3.4,
  https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/GLSL_ES_Specification_3.00.pdf). ANGLE's source was not read; its
  behaviour comes from the raw repro.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: fsm's equivalent mutants named lines that had moved (KB-MUTATION-PINS1, scripts, mutation)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/mutation.test.js` on main at caf466b4c: "every listed equivalent mutant exists" failed on
  `fsm/final line 110 || -> &&`; after that pin, 13 more fsm pins (final, index, inspect, invoke, scxml) failed the same way.
- **Cause:** scripts/mutation.mjs pins each equivalent mutant by line. Its fsm pins matched the sync's unformatted fsm
  sources (ff88a70e7); main holds the formatted ones (c333e1023, put back by the restore caf466b4c), whose lines moved.
  Each file still has the same mutants in the same order. Nothing in the fast gate ran tests/mutation.test.js when a
  mutation target changed, so the stale pins reached main and showed only in local CI's full verify.
- **Fixed:** each pin moved to the line of the mutant with the same id (d8cade908), every reason checked against its new
  line. `npm run test:changed` now also runs tests/mutation.test.js when scripts/mutation.mjs or a mutation target's
  source changes (`rootTests`, scripts/test-changed.mjs).
  Regression: tests/mutation.test.js, and tests/check-merge-affected.test.js ("test:changed runs the mutation pins").

### Fixed 2026-11-25: `npm run build:packages` failed on Node 22.12.0 (KB-NODE22-BUILD1, scripts)

- **Repro:** CI's Node 22.12.0 jobs (run 45703324344) stopped in `build:packages`: `SyntaxError: The requested module
  'node:module' does not provide an export named 'registerHooks'`.
- **Cause:** `scripts/support/record-reads.mjs`, which the build imports for its job names, imported `registerHooks` by
  name; Node has it from 22.15, and a missing named export fails the load.

  Not run on Node 22.12 here; CI's 22.12.0 jobs are that proof.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a world's restore did not rewind `Physics.stepCount` (KB-PHYS-STEPCOUNTSEEK1, physics world, rigid solver)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/world-rigid-solver.test.js`, "a seek by restore rewinds the Physics's step count". A
  `PhysicsWorld` with a `RigidSolver`; advance 12 ticks, `takeSnapshot()`, advance 60, `restoreSnapshot()`:
  `physics.stepCount` stayed 72, so anything inside the Physics that reads its clock as `stepCount * fixedTimestep` (a
  `SailForce` whose wind is a function of time, a load clocked by it, `Physics.advance(frame, fps)`) read the wrong time
  after a seek.
- **Cause:** the rigid solver's state was the kernel's columns; `stepCount` is a field of the Physics object, not in a
  region, so a restore left it where the run had reached.
- **Fixed:** the rigid solver keeps the count in a region of its own (`stepCount`, one f64, extra state), written after
  every step; a restore that changed it is put back into the Physics before the next step. The air's loads in a world
  already took the world's tick from the `AirSolver` (`packages/physics/tests/coupling/air.test.js`). Regression: the test
  above (positions, velocities, the step count and the world's hash equal a continuous run's).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: an air load left a stray force on a body when it stopped (KB-AERO-FORCERESIDUE1, physics fields and flight)

- **Repro:** three boxes with their own `addForce([0.3, 0, -0.17])` in a gusty `WindForce` for 90 steps, then
  `wind.remove()` and one step: each box's force column read about (0.300001, -1.4e-7, -0.1700003) and a torque of 1e-8,
  not its own force.
- **Cause:** `HeldLoad` changed the force it held by the difference from the last step's, so the f32 columns re-rounded the
  running sum every step and taking the last load off left that rounding behind (the class of KB-SOFT-FORCERESIDUE1).
- **Fixed:** the air's loads (`WindForce`, `WingForce`, `RotorForce`, `LiftingGas`) are summed by body in f64 and held for
  one step only: the sum goes into the columns before the step and exactly what the columns took (the difference of two
  f32 values) comes off after it (`packages/physics/src/air-hold.ts`). In a world the same sums go through `bodyForces`
  (`AirSolver`), which the rigid solver adds and takes off the same way, so a world and Physics alone are the same bits.
  Results of a scene with air loads change at f32 rounding from before; the physics is unchanged. Regression:
  `packages/physics/tests/world-air-solver.test.js`, "stepped alone, an air load comes off exactly when it stops".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a 20 m/s sea with unlimited fetch seemed to grow past the Pierson-Moskowitz height (KB-SEA-FULLDEV1, physics waves)

- **Repro (as filed):** `WaveSolver` with one periodic cell, a steady 20 m/s wind and `warmUp: 72 * 3600`: the significant
  height was 122 percent of 0.21 U^2 / g (10 m/s: 106 percent).
- **Cause:** the reference. Pierson and Moskowitz's 0.21 is in the wind at 19.5 m; in U10 it is 0.241, and Alves, Banner
  and Young's re-analysis (2003) gives 0.254 (band 0.233 to 0.272). The 20 m/s run was also only half as developed (g t /
  U10 1.27e5 against 2.54e5 at 10 m/s).
- **Fixed:** the test runs each wind to g t / U10 = 2.5e5 and holds the sea to Alves et al.: 0.221 at 10 m/s and 0.281 at 20,
  each within 15 percent, the peak within 10 percent. The remaining rise with wind (1.27 against the data's 1.02) is ST4's
  u* scaling, published for this family (pure u* scaling gives 1.30 to 1.45; ST4 with the DIA reaches 0.266 at 20 m/s, Liu
  et al. 2019), and is recorded as an accepted difference in docs/limits.md. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/waves.test.js`,
  "with unlimited fetch the sea grows to the fully developed sea Alves, Banner and Young measured (KB-SEA-FULLDEV1)".

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a strong wind grew the sea too fast, and the fetch law was flatter than measured (KB-SEA-GROWTH1, physics waves)

- **Repro (as first filed):** `WaveSolver` with `cells: [30, 1]`, `cellSize: 4000`, `periodic: ['z']`, a steady 20 m/s wind
  and `warmUp: 12 * 3600`: the significant height at 6 to 118 km fetch was 1.84 to 5.04 m against JONSWAP's 0.79 to 3.51 m.
  After the first fix (ST4 and third-order propagation, 526cc95c9) a 48-cell grid still grew energy as chi^0.66 against
  Kahma and Calkoen's chi^0.9.
- **Cause:** four parts.
  - WAM Cycle 3's input and whitecapping scale with u*, and SWAN's drag fit raises u* / U10 with the wind.
  - First-order upwind propagation smeared the energy downwind.
  - The grids were too coarse at the coast. The young waves' fast growth was spread over too long a fetch, so short
    fetches ran high and the law flattened. Every source-term constant tried left the slope at 0.62 to 0.66; refining the
    cells alone took it to 0.74 (0.80 in friction-velocity scaling against the law's 0.79).
  - The reference: Kahma and Calkoen's U10-scaled composite is the highest of the published laws at long fetch.
- **Fixed:**
  - ST4 is the default and propagation is ULTIMATE QUICKEST (526cc95c9).
  - The sheltering is calibrated on a resolved grid against Kahma and Calkoen's stable law in friction-velocity scaling,
    the community's protocol (Liu et al. 2019). There it is within 4.6 percent rms at 20 m/s and 3.8 at 30 (validation),
    and the published TEST471 roughness cap is restored.
  - The README and docs/limits.md state the resolution a coast needs.
  - `frictionVelocity(x, z)` reports u*.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/tests/waves.test.js`, "a gale of 20 m/s grows the sea along its fetch as Kahma and
  Calkoen measured, in friction-velocity scaling (KB-SEA-GROWTH1)": e* within 15 percent below and 25 above the law, and the
  slope in 0.7 to 0.9. WAM Cycle 3 fails it at 1.6 times the law, and a grid of twice the cell gives 0.68.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a cloth attached to a rigid body blew up when its free particles took impulses (KB-SOFT-ATTACHKICK1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `SoftBodies.attach(physics)`, gravity 0; a 4 by 7 cloth whose first row is `attachParticle`d to a 50 kg box;
  every step, before `physics.step()`, `applyParticleImpulse(p, [0.1, 0, 0])` on the 21 free particles. After 30 steps the
  box and cloth held about (-5,743, 4,255, 19,751) kg m/s against the 63 kg m/s applied (a mesh of the same triangles too).
- **Cause:** two parts. The cloth's rigid edges were swept on their own while the links to the box were solved exactly
  against a ghost of the box per link, so the sweep pulled a linked particle off its anchor every pass and the exact solve
  handed the correction to the box, over and over; and an edge between two particles linked to one box is held by the box
  already, a redundant row whose large, cancelling multipliers rounded into the box's impulse one row at a time.
- **Fixed:** the soft kernel's exact solve (`soft-kernel/src/rigid.rs`) holds a sheet's edges, the links and the contacts
  with bodies in one system with each body an unknown of six degrees of freedom (Shinar, Schroeder and Fedkiw 2008), leaves
  out an edge whose ends are both linked to one body (a redundant constraint, Tournier et al. 2015), sums a body's impulse
  from the rows in f64 before rounding it, and does not let a particle linked to a body also collide with it. Regression:
  `packages/physics/tests/soft.test.js`, "a cloth linked to a rigid body keeps its momentum when its free particles are
  kicked", woven and mesh.

### Corrected 2026-11-25: two boxes on one floor seemed to change each other's paths, but they touched (KB-PHYS-LOCALITY1, physics kernel)

- **Repro (as first filed):** `packages/physics/tests/locality.test.js`, a fixed floor, box A (0.6 m) resting at the origin and box
  B (0.4 by 0.8 by 0.4 m) dropped 2 m away with a spin; pushing A by 0.05 N s along x before each step moved B by 2.2 cm after 30
  steps, and B was the same bits after 10 or 20.
- **Cause:** not a leak. A weighs 0.216 kg, so each push adds 0.23 m/s: after 28 steps A is at x 1.45 moving about 4.4 m/s, its
  face at 1.75 m reaches B's at 1.8 m in step 29, the two boxes become one island with a pair between them (a native trace shows
  islands 2 and 1 solving pair until step 28, then 1 island and 2 pairs), and B is struck in step 30. That is why 10 and 20 steps
  matched and 30 did not. Islands already step on their own state: with B 8 m away it was the same bits after 30 and 60 steps.
- **Fix:** the test's geometry. B is now 20 m away, the test asserts that A never comes within a metre of it, and B is the same
  bits after 30, 60 and 90 steps with and without the push (also with no floor). It stays as the guard that an island's
  substep level is a function of its own state alone.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a 30-row pyramid at one pass a substep creeps instead of resting (KB-PHYS-PILECREEP1, physics kernel, contact solver)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`, `a_pyramid_of_thirty_rows_settles_at_one_pass_a_substep` (465 metre cubes, 4 substeps of one pass, sleeping off, 30 s). With gravity 9.80665 m/s^2 its fastest cube moves at 5.6 mm/s at 30 s (bound 1 mm/s) and the pile has moved 8.9 cm; at 9.81 it passed at 0.59 mm/s, but the 26- and 28-row piles of the same test helper already crept at 1.1 mm/s. Gravity is the only change: the old code with gravity set explicitly to 9.80665 gives the same bits (fastest 3bb76fa9, moved 3db5bae7 as f32 words).
- **Cause:** not yet found. The pile sits at the edge of what one pass a substep settles (the eighth-rate chain spring of `CHAIN_LOAD`), so a 0.03 percent change of the load tips it into a slow creep. A pile that rests at one g and creeps at another is a solver defect, not a tolerance.
- **Owner:** the contact solver's rebuild (with KB-PHYS-BLOCK1 and KB-PHYS-WALL1). Blocks moving the engine to standard gravity.
- **Cause, found:** a one-cube-thick slab tips out of its plane. The chain contacts at one pass take the eighth-rate spring (30 Hz at 240 Hz substeps), and a patch of springs resists a turn with k = K b^2 / 12; the r rows above an interface lean on it with W h = [r (r + 1) / 2] m g r / 3, so the slab stands only while r (r + 1) < omega^2 / (4 g) = 906, r < 29.6. Thirty rows sit on the edge, which is why a 0.03 percent change of g tipped it.
- **Fix:** an island's contacts get the stiffness its structures need not to tip, from the bodies' masses and the contacts' shape alone (`kernel/src/tilt.rs`, `tilt_gains`, a discrete Hardy inequality along each support path), and where that would need a contact stiffer than a quarter of the substep rate, the island steps at a finer level of substeps (`island_level`, up to the 7,680 Hz tick), the rest of the world as before. The 20- and 30-row piles hold at 7.5e-5 to 4.3e-4 m/s from 30 to 90 s at both 9.81 and 9.80665, and the 50-row pile at 8.4e-4 to 9.6e-4 m/s from 15 to 75 s (measured once, 4 minutes a run, too long for the suite).
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs` `a_pile_of_twenty_rows_holds_still_for_ninety_seconds` and the two thirty-row tests beside it (fastest under 1 mm/s at 30, 60 and 90 s, and no more than a quarter over its 30 s figure later).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a default cloth stretched under a heavy body and sprang it off (KB-SOFT-LOOPSTRETCH1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/soft.test.js`, "a contact is stable at a mass ratio of a thousand either way, and a
  cloth holds a body or tears, never lets it through": a 1,000 kg box on a cloth of 1 kg particles. The cloth's "rigid"
  edges stretched up to 28 percent under it and gave the energy back, so the box bounced clear and walked off a free edge.
- **Cause:** the exact solve held only rigid edges without a loop; a cloth's edges, all loops, were left to the
  Gauss-Seidel sweep, whose stiffness depends on its iterations and the mass ratio (Macklin, Mueller and Chentanez 2016),
  and the box's contacts were not in any solve with the edges, so the contact pushed the sheet, the edges pulled it back
  into the box, and the contact pushed the box out.
- **Fixed:** a woven sheet's threads (and a triangle mesh's edges) are solved exactly with their loops (fast projection,
  Goldenthal, Harmon, Fattal, Bercovier and Grinspun 2007), together with the links and the contacts with bodies, the bodies
  six-degree-of-freedom unknowns and the contacts' multipliers bounded at zero (MPRGP, Dostal and Schoberl 2005), Newton
  steps taken as far as an Armijo line search allows (Nocedal and Wright 2006) until every row is within its tolerance. The
  threads are springs of the fabric's measured tensile stiffness (KES-F, Luible 2008), held rigid past the strain they were
  measured to (Provot 1995), so the cloth stretches as cotton does; a 1,000 kg box now rests on the cloth. Rows with no
  compliance are damped Levenberg-Marquardt style (contacts by sqrt(f32 epsilon) of their diagonal, edges and links by
  their violation squared up to that), so redundant ones (a flat mesh's edges, a light body pinched by a sheet) keep
  bounded multipliers. A default cloth
  costs more to step: see docs/limits.md. Regression: the test above, `soft-kernel/tests/threads.rs`, and in soft.test.js
  "an inextensible sheet holds its threads within 0.1 percent at any pass count and load".

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a hull's motion lost energy to its own step (KB-SEA-STEPDAMP1, physics seakeeping)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, "held up by its buoyancy alone, a hull heaves and rolls
  on at the amplitude it was let go at", and "on a hull uneven fore and aft". A box held up by its buoyancy alone lost 31
  percent of its heave in 8 cycles at 60 steps a second (half that at 120), and a driven hull's pitch was 5.2 percent off.
- **Cause:** three errors first order in the step. The hull's load was taken at the middle of the step, energy-neutral
  only if the rigid step integrated a held force exactly; it takes 8 symplectic-Euler substeps, which move a body by
  (v + F dt (s + 1) / (2 s m)) dt, so the neutral point is (s - 1) / (2 s) of the step. The pose there moved the body's
  origin with its centre of mass's velocity, leaving out the spin's w x r when the two differ. And the radiation force,
  convolved up to the step's start, lagged the load by that fraction of a step.
- **Fixed:** the rigid solver publishes each body's substeps in the `bodies` port (word 24); the hull takes its load at
  (s - 1) / (2 s) of the step, turns the origin about the centre of mass, and carries the radiation force to the same
  point along its last two values (kept as state). Regression: the tests above (the pitch test's bound is 3 percent).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a hull's heave drove its pitch the wrong way (KB-SEA-COUPLESIGN1, physics seakeeping)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, "on a hull uneven fore and aft, heave drives pitch with
  the sign the strips give it". A hull wide aft and narrow forward, driven in heave, pitched half a cycle out of phase with
  the coupled frequency-domain answer.
- **Cause:** the radiation memory summed the heave-pitch coupling as -int b33 x. In the body's axes a pitch rate about z
  moves a section at x along +y at w_z x, so the coupling is +int b33 x (as the added mass already had it). A box, even fore
  and aft, has no coupling, so the earlier tests could not see it.
- **Fixed:** the sign, in `memory.ts`. Regression: the test above (it also checks that the wrong sign fails).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a hull's sway added mass at infinite frequency was the rigid-lid value (KB-SEA-SWAYLID1, physics seakeeping)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/coupling/seakeeping.test.js`, "driven sideways, a box sways and rolls as the coupled
  frequency-domain equations say", and `tests/seakeeping.test.js`, "a swaying and rolling section". A box driven in sway
  moved too little; a half circle's sway added mass at high frequency is 0.405 of rho pi R^2 / 2, not rho pi R^2 / 2.
- **Cause:** the sway added mass at infinite frequency was taken as Lewis's formula for half the mirrored double body,
  which holds under a rigid lid. At high frequency the free surface holds the potential at 0, so in sway the image moves
  against the section, and the limit is smaller. The rigid-lid value is the zero-frequency limit.
- **Fixed:** the lateral added mass at infinite frequency comes from the sections' radiation solution, carried to xi = inf
  (`memory.ts`); the rigid-lid formula is renamed `swayAddedMassRigidLid`. Regression: the tests above.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a world stepped every rigid and soft solver at 60 Hz (KB-PHYS-WORLDLEVEL1, physics world)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/world-rigid-solver.test.js`, "a Physics stepped 240 times a second steps at level 2 in
  a world". A `Physics` at 1/240 s added to a `PhysicsWorld` threw "the world asked for 0.0166 s".
- **Cause:** a world asks a solver its `stableRate()` after `init`, but `RigidSolver` and `SoftSolver` gave it a closure
  over the level `describe()` saw, which runs before `init` (when the Physics is not known yet): 0, always.
- **Fixed:** `stableRate()` reads the level `init` set, in both (and in `HullSolver`). Regression: the test above.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a body a cloth held kept a stray force that grew every step (KB-SOFT-FORCERESIDUE1, physics soft)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/world-soft-solver.test.js`, "the push on a body goes through the ports". A 2 kg box
  rests on a cloth for 120 steps; between steps, its force column should hold only its own force (0).
- **Cause:** the soft step held the box up with a force for the rigid step and took the same f64 force off after it. The
  kernel's force columns are f32, so what they took was the force rounded, and taking off the unrounded force left the
  rounding behind: a stray force that grew a little every step the cloth held the box.
- **Fixed:** what the columns took (the difference of two f32 values, which is exact) is what comes off, in
  `SoftBodies.afterStep` and in the `RigidSolver` for `bodyForces`. The force now comes off at the end of the rigid step in
  both, so a world and Physics stepped alone stay the same bits.
- **Regression:** the test above, stepped alone and in a world.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: the two halves of a cut soft body threw each other about (KB-SOFT-CUTTHRASH1, physics soft and kernel)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/soft-cells.test.js`, "a soft cube with a surface collider cut in two ...". The halves
  start touching along the cut, each one's corners on the other's surface collider. They moved up to 0.19 m in the first
  step and 1.6 m in later ones, and sank to 0.125 m under the top of the box they fell on. They then came back, so the old
  test, which looked only at the 360th step, passed.
- **Cause:** three things together.
  - A body of cells has a closed surface wound outward, but its surface collider was oriented only for a body that holds a
    volume or has a skin, so the collider had no inside.
  - Where a particle or a soft triangle touches a mesh at no distance, the kernel's queries had no offset to take a normal
    from. A particle took the reverse of its own move, and a triangle took the manifold's arbitrary axis, here -y on a top
    face (`kernel/src/probe.rs`, `kernel/src/face.rs`). So both halves were pushed along and into each other.
  - With contacts in the exact solve, the same contacts held a light body twice over.
- **Fixed:**
  - A surface collider is oriented when its triangles close a surface wound one way (`closedSurface` in `soft.ts`).
  - On an oriented mesh, a contact at no distance takes the surface's own normal there: the angle-weighted pseudonormal of
    the triangle, edge or corner it is on (Baerentzen and Aanaes 2005).
  - Contacts with a soft body's own surface or deformable collider stay with the contact passes, since that surface moves
    with particles of the same solve.
  - The halves now separate once by their contact thickness and settle on the box.
- **Regression:** the test above now checks every step: no particle moves further in a step than its fall allows plus that
  one separation, and none goes under the box's top. Also `kernel/tests/face_sides.rs`, where a cut face, a face along an
  edge and a face at a corner, and particles at each, get the surface's normal, never one into the mesh or along it.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: cloth friction against rigid bodies counted each contact's push twice (KB-SOFT-FRICTION2X, physics soft)

- **Repro:** a 30 cm cloth on a fixed box tilted 35 degrees, friction 0.5: it should slide (tan 35 = 0.70 > 0.5) and held.
- **Cause:** a contact's position pass held the slide back by up to the coefficient times its push, and the velocity pass
  after it held it back again by the coefficient times the same push, so a sliding cloth stuck at about twice its friction;
  and the position pass moved only the particle, so a light cloth was carried along under a heavy box sliding on it.
- **Fixed:** friction is one bounded solve after the contacts' (staggered projections, Kaufman, Sueda, James and Pai 2008),
  |lambda_t| <= mu lambda_n over the sheet's rows and the body together, and the velocity pass takes out only the normal
  speed. The cloth holds at 20 degrees and slides at 35. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/soft.test.js`, the two cloths
  over a sharp box edge (friction twice and under half the edge-friction threshold).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a commit made from a stale working tree undid seven landed commits and no check caught it (KB-STALE-TREE1, scripts)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/check-mass-deletion.mjs --range fe35673035..3bcef614ed`. The weather resetTime commit
  3bcef614ed came from `git reset origin/main` with the working tree still on 11d2f98b93, then a commit of every file:
  it put 29 files back to their older bytes and deleted 3, undoing 68cb2b78f6, 8f494c3d4e and b903b6a4c1 (text MSDF,
  outline-msdf.ts gone), 90bf32fccf and 7bb4305fdf (blender bake_noise), f958b80511 (water borrowed-GPU registry),
  78bbd86dd9 (the reflection cone size ceilings, so post/ssr, water/reflector and environment/reflector and refractor
  went red) and fe35673035 (parity recount). It removed 1,528 lines, far under MASS-DELETION's 20,000.
- **Cause:** check:mass-deletion bounded only how much a commit deletes, not whether it puts files back to bytes an
  earlier commit changed.
- **Fix:** the files are restored with lane B's weather changes kept (sizes.json keeps its weather budgets and
  history row). check:mass-deletion (run by rebase:main, push:main and check:merge) fails on STALE-REVERT when a
  commit puts more than 2 non-generated files back to their bytes before an earlier commit of the last 500 changed
  them, unless a `Reverts: <sha> <why>` body line (or git revert's own line) names that commit. Over the 60 commits
  from 2ed1a656dd to 5a2f2b7850 it flags 3bcef614ed only. Test: `tests/check-mass-deletion.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a tiny video's default bitrate was a few hundred bits a second (KB-HEADLESS-TINYRATE1, headless)

- **Repro:** `packages/video/test/demux-check.mjs` on Edge 158.0.4370.33 (RTX A6000): a 16 x 16 solid colour encoded
  as AV1 by `encodeVideo` read back 6 levels off (green drew as 6, 253, 5), past the check's 5.
- **Cause:** the default bitrate was `width * height * fps / 10` with no floor, 256 bits a second for that clip.
- **Fix:** the default is at least 100,000 bits a second; the same clip reads within 5 and VP9 within 2. A caller's
  `bitrate` is used as given. Test: `packages/headless/tests/video.test.js` (the default bitrate).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a long test file ends with no result in its package run (KB-TEST-FILEEXIT1, humans, water, scripts, process kills)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:changed` on the workstation (2026-11-25, lane A, a change to packages/shared, so every package
  runs): `packages/humans/test/fit.test.js` failed after 122 s and `packages/water/test/flood-bounds.test.js` after 257 s, each
  as 'test failed' at the file with no failing or cancelled subtest and nothing on stderr. Run alone
  (`node --test-reporter=tap --test test/<file>` in the package folder) both pass, 30 of 30 in 315 s and 18 of 18 in 345 s.
- **Cause:** the file's process was ended from outside by a tree kill aimed at another process's old pid. On Node
  26.13, `taskkill /F` on a running `node --test` file process gives exactly that report: 'test failed' at the file, the
  test in flight neither failed nor cancelled, nothing on stderr. Running out of memory does not: V8 prints `FATAL ERROR
  ... heap out of memory` and its stack to stderr, which the runner passes on. A pid names a process only while it runs;
  once it has exited and its last handle is closed Windows gives the number to a new process (measured on the
  workstation: after 295 process starts, 51 s), and a test file is the process the lanes start most often. Margo's
  scripts ended trees by bare pid in about 30 places (`taskkill /T /F <pid>`, `endTree(pid)`, run-with-timeout's
  `killTree(pid)`), several of them after the target could have exited: a limit timer cleared only on `close`, which
  waits for every pipe and so fires after the exit when a grandchild holds one; a cleanup that kills a pid it kept
  (template-browser-check's `finally`, jupyter-steps' second `killTree`); an asynchronous
  taskkill during which Node sees the exit and closes its handle. `taskkill /T` also follows `ParentProcessId`, which
  may name a parent that has exited or a newer process that took its pid (Microsoft, "Win32_Process class",
  https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-process; "Process Handles and Identifiers",
  https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/procthread/process-handles-and-identifiers: the identifier is valid only
  until the process ends, a handle until it is closed). Which lane's kill hit these two files was not caught live; the
  minutes between the file's start and its end match a pid kept past its process's exit and reused.
- **Fixed:** every tree kill on Windows goes through scripts/support/shutdown.mjs, by one of two routes. A child
  process this one started is ended by `killChildTreeSync`: `taskkill /T /F` run synchronously and only before Node has
  seen its exit, so Node still holds its handle and Windows cannot give its pid to anyone else during the kill (fast,
  about 1 s); a child whose exit was seen is not ended by pid at all. A bare pid is ended by `killOwnTree` /
  `killOwnTreeSync`: one PowerShell reads the process table, walks this process's own tree with each child created no
  earlier than its parent, ends the pid and its tree only if it is in it, and ends each process through a handle
  checked against its creation time, so a pid that has become another run's process is left alone (4 to 20 s on the
  loaded workstation). `endTree` and both `killTree`s take either and pick the route; run-with-timeout, runWithTimeout's
  CLI, the dev-server probe, the browser host's unlisted-tree end, verify, mutation, node22-tests, the reference
  renderers, the shot queue, draco-resources, test-unity and the netcode and voxel-net checks pass the child.
  test-watch's hung-run stop now uses the creation-checked walk (its own walk followed `ParentProcessId` unchecked);
  test-unity's orphan kill checks each start time. Not covered: taskkill's own walk below a live child follows
  `ParentProcessId`, and Microsoft does not say whether it checks creation times (docs/limits.md, "Process tree
  kills"). Regression: tests/process-kill.test.js (a process not below this one survives `endTree`, `killTree` and
  `killOwnTreeSync`, which the old taskkill route ended; a child whose exit was seen is not killed by pid; a child's
  whole tree, a detached grandchild included, still ends by every route; and a scan that fails on a raw `taskkill` or
  a `ParentProcessId` walk outside the helper, which verify and so check:merge run). A second report fits the same
  class but was not traced: `npm run check:owners -- --packages=post` on the laptop (ea4937f59, 67 to 99% CPU, other
  lanes' GPU suites running) failed `post/SSAO.attach` with `page.goto: net::ERR_ABORTED` for tests/modern-game.html,
  as a page server or browser ended from outside would.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: the browser host sometimes exited mid-run in check:owners on the WebGL2 layer (KB-HOST-COMPATEXIT1, scripts, browser host)

- **Repro:** `npm run check:owners -- --packages=environment,lines,creative,lod,selection,shader` on the workstation (2026-11-25, lane A): after 82 fixtures passed, `creative/TextureRenderTarget (WebGL2 compatibility)` failed with `browser host <pid> ended (stdout closed) before it answered` (`HOST_GONE`). `--packages=creative` alone then passed 234 of 234. Handoff 11 of lane A recorded the same exit at `post/SSGI.attach (WebGL2 compatibility)` on 2026-11-24; post alone passed today. Not tied to one fixture: both runs had other GPU work on the machine, and both were long multi-package runs.
- **Cause:** the host ended with nothing on stderr, so something outside it killed it. When the suite cannot list Chromium's
  processes within `LIST_PROCESSES_MS` (5 s, which a loaded PC misses), the host ends the tree by pid (`taskkill /T /F`).
  `endOwned` killed the browser through its handle first and started that taskkill after, in the background, while the
  suite moved on to its next leaf. Windows reuses a pid once no handle to its process is left, and Node closes its handle
  when it sees the exit, so the browser's pid was free while taskkill, which reads the process table through WMI, still
  ran. The next leaf's browser host (or any process that took the pid, or had it as parent) was ended with it.
- **Fixed:** `endOwned` (scripts/support/browser-host.mjs) ends an unlisted tree by pid while the browser still runs and
  kills it through its handle and closes its pipes (Chromium ends itself when its pipe closes) only after, and never ends a tree by the pid of a browser that had already exited.
  Regression: tests/browser-host.test.js (both KB-HOST-COMPATEXIT1 cases fail on the old order). The exit was not caught
  live with this fix in place. The listed-children kill (`process.kill` by pid, pids read moments before) kept a far
  smaller window of the same kind; closed the same day: on Windows `endOwned`'s default `endListed` ends each listed pid
  through a handle to a process whose StartTime is no later than the listing (`listedAt`, sent by the suite), then waits
  for it (`waitSignaled` with `kill`, scripts/support/shutdown.mjs). Regression: tests/browser-host.test.js ("spares a
  pid whose process started after it", fails on the bare-pid kill).
  The handle kill first reported every listed child as a survivor in 1 real close of 5: .NET's Process.Kill throws
  Win32Exception (access denied) for a child Chromium is already ending, and the waiter's script, stopping on errors,
  fell to its error path, which keeps every pid. Kill now takes that exception as done and WaitForExit still reports a
  child that stays; 24 real closes left no survivor. Regression: tests/browser-teardown.test.js ("a child already
  terminating", fails without the catch).
  That waiter killed and waited one pid at a time, and with Edge (the host's default channel) a killed child's process
  object can stay unsignalled for the whole bound after its exit code is set: the first listed renderer held the loop
  for up to `REAP_MS` and every later child (GPU, network, storage) ran on, so tests/browser-teardown.test.js ("a real
  browser: close ends its main process") failed 4 runs of 4 from b7468ab58 on (bisected; it passed on 30629b4eb). Fixed
  2026-11-26: `waitSignaled` ends every checked pid first, then waits for them all against the one deadline; the
  children now end 1 to 4 s after the end request instead of up to `REAP_MS`. Regression: tests/browser-teardown.test.js
  ("every child is ended before the first wait", fails on the kill-then-wait loop). Then KB-HOST-KILLLATE1 below.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: a hosted Chromium close returned before its listed children were ended (KB-HOST-KILLLATE1, scripts, browser host)

- **Repro:** `node --test --test-name-pattern="close ends its main process" tests/browser-teardown.test.js` on the
  laptop (2026-11-26, other lanes' suites running): 8 of 13 runs passed after the KB-HOST-COMPATEXIT1 waiter fix. In
  four scripted closes, two left every child (renderers, GPU, network, storage) running at the close's return; they had
  ended 1 to 4 s later.
- **Cause:** since b7468ab58 the host ends listed children through Windows PowerShell (`waitSignaled` with `kill`), which
  takes seconds to start on a loaded PC, while the close waits only `TEARDOWN_GRACE_MS` (2 s). The bare-pid
  `process.kill` before it was synchronous but could end a recycled pid. A terminating Edge child then also stays
  unsignalled past the test's 10 s `waitSignaled`, so it counts as running.
  The listing time never reached that check either: `startHost`'s `end` sent no `listedAt` and the host's request
  parser dropped it, so start times were compared with the host's request time.
- **Fixed:** the host acknowledges the end request only once the listed children have been ended (`endOwned`'s
  `ended`: the default `endListed` kills through checked handles and returns; `settle` then waits for their teardown
  for the time the bound has left), so the suite's grace starts after the kill. The wait stays inside `CLOSE_LIMIT_MS`
  (worst case about 17 s: listing, PowerShell's start bounded at 10 s, grace). `end` sends `listedAt` and the host
  passes it on. A warm waiter kept beside the host was the larger alternative, not needed. The real close test passed
  20 of 20 runs alone (laptop at 90% CPU from other lanes; 8 of 13 before). Regression: tests/browser-host.test.js
  ("acknowledges the end only once the listed children have been ended", "sends the listing time with the end
  request"; both fail on the old host and suite).
- **Heavy load, fixed 2026-11-26:** beside four CPU hogs (100% CPU) it still passed only 16 of 20. Traced over 18 timed
  kills: in 4 the kill's Windows PowerShell had not started within `waitSignaled`'s 10 s bound, was ended there, and
  no child was killed; in the other 14 it took 1.9 to 5.4 s and every child had exited. (Killed Edge children also
  stayed unsignalled past 10 s in 13 of those 14, which the close test does not wait on: it waits only for pids still
  running.) The host now starts its PowerShell at launch and keeps it waiting (`startKiller` in
  scripts/support/shutdown.mjs), so the end request costs no PowerShell start; with that process not ready, gone or
  silent past 10 s the kill falls back to `waitSignaled` as before, and a process that missed its bound is not used
  again. It ends with its host, closed or not (Node starts each child in a job that kills it on close). The real close
  test then passed 20 of 20 beside four CPU hogs (3.1 min, 100% CPU). Regression: tests/killer.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: tatami floated over sunk flights between joined floors (KB-PROC-WELLMATS1, procedural, building plans)

- **Repro:** random plans 559, 590 and 803 of the uneven-floor walk in `packages/procedural/test/building-reach.test.js`: Japanese houses whose sunk steps had floor mats 0.2 to 0.6 m over their treads.
- **Cause:** a sunk flight's well cut the floor and base of its block but not the floor coverings.
- **Fixed:** the well cuts the `mats` and `fabric` parts too.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a wing with its front inside the main block got no door (KB-PROC-WINGDOOR1, procedural, building plans)

- **Repro:** random plan 1071 of the same walk: a two storey wing at another floor level, joined by nothing, with no outer door, so all six of its rooms were cut off.
- **Cause:** outer doors stand only on a block's front side, and the fallback that adds one never tried another stance.
- **Fixed:** after every block's front has been tried, one is turned about on its footprint (width and depth changing places on a quarter turn), its stair keep-outs and window fit moved with it.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: one in ten rules buildings had no stair, so storeys could not be reached (KB-PROC-NOSTAIR1, procedural, buildings)

- **Repro:** `generateBuilding({style: 'western-1910-brick', width: 13, depth: 6.9})` returned an empty `stairs`; 42 of 400 random plans of the multi-storey styles did. `packages/procedural/test/building-reach.test.js` walks every storey.
- **Cause:** a stair was placed only inside a room the partition grid happened to make, with no fallback. The same walk found that partitions stopped short of their crossings (a see-through square of wall thickness), a partition too short for a doorway was built solid and shut its room off, and a partition could run into an outer door.
- **Fixed:** a stair hall is made by taking partitions down, else a spiral, else a fixed ladder; a stair never divides a room; crossings have a post; too short a partition is left out; a partition stops 1.2 m short of an outer door.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: wings at other floor levels met the main block with open ledges and no steps (KB-PROC-JOINLEVEL1, procedural, building plans)

- **Repro:** `generateBuildingPlan({style: 'western-1910-house', width: 12, depth: 8, storeys: [3.2, 3.2], wings: [{at: [6.5, 0], width: 5, depth: 6, plinth: 0.2, storeys: [2.9, 2.9]}]})`: floors at 0.2 and 0.6 m met with nothing between them. The walk over 300 such plans in `packages/procedural/test/building-reach.test.js` found 722 rooms cut off or open ledges.
- **Cause:** joined blocks were cut into each other with no regard to their floor levels; a block's rooms were taken to run to the top of its roof, so a lower block's attic opened the higher floors of the other; partition doorways and stairs of a wing took no account of the part of it the main block covers.
- **Fixed:** unequal floors get a doorway and steps within the stair code's figures, or a wall and the wing its own door; rooms end at the eaves; a wing's stair and doorways keep to the part of it that shows; a room is listed while any of it shows.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: joined building plans left wing and tower storeys cut off (KB-PROC-PLANREACH1, procedural, building plans)

- **Repro:** the walk over 500 random plans in `packages/procedural/test/building-reach.test.js` (before the fix most failed): the default L plan's wing was walled off from the main block, upper floors had a slot at each join, a tower's extra storeys had no stair, and a tower over the only front door left no way in.
- **Cause:** the inside face of each wall counted as indoor geometry, which only earlier blocks cut, so the main block's stayed across every join; floors were cut back to the other block's outer walls; wings and towers were always built without stairs; curtains of windows cut away stayed hanging.
- **Fixed:** inside faces are cut where the other block has a room, floors where it has a room and with no margin; towers and wings with floors the main block lacks get stairs that keep out of one another; partitions keep 1.2 m off joins; a door is added where none is left; curtains come down with their windows.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: a tower side under 3 m passed the plan's check and then threw about a building width (KB-PROC-TOWERSIZE1, procedural, building plans)

- **Repro:** `generateBuildingPlan({tower: 'front-left', towerSize: 2.5})`: RangeError "Invalid building width".
- **Cause:** `towerSize` allowed 2.5 m, under the 3 m least width of the block it builds.
- **Fixed:** `towerSize` is 3 to 12 m, refused by its own name. Regression: `packages/procedural/test/building-reach.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: every rules building's ground floor flickered between floor and foundation (KB-PROC-FLOORFIGHT1, procedural, buildings)

- **Repro:** `packages/procedural/test/building-interiors.test.js`, "the foundation never shares the plane of the ground floor"; seen from inside in `packages/procedural/test/buildings-browser.mjs` as a sawtooth of two colours across the floor.
- **Cause:** the foundation (`base`) was one box over the whole footprint topped at the ground floor's level, the same plane as the top of the floor slab, so the depth test picked either.
- **Fixed:** the foundation is a ring under the walls (it still shows its 2 cm ledge) with a fill inside it that stops under the slab. Regression: the test above.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: every importer of the display module carried the inverse display curve (KB-SIZE-DISPLAYINV1, shared, bundle size)

- **Repro:** `tests/display-neutral-inverse.test.js`, "a bundle that uses the forward display curve carries nothing of the inverse": bundle `export { displayShader } from 'packages/shared/display.js'`; the output held `((254.5/255+.055)/1.055)**2.4` and the white constant. In the sky cloud entries this was +51 B (volumetric-clouds base 11,262 to 11,313 B gzip) and +54 B (compat-clouds base 23,870 to 23,924), both over their ceilings.
- **Cause:** 6ef3c82192 put the inverse (KB4000) into `shared/display.js`. Its constants are computed when the module loads and its WGSL is a template literal holding one of them, which the bundler does not drop from a module another export is used from.
- **Fixed:** the inverse is in `shared/display-inverse.js`, imported only by `gltf/transmission`. Regression: the test above.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: SSAO and GTAO occluded one-pixel tips of a lone face's silhouette (KB-SSAO-SILHOUETTE1, post, normal reconstruction)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/ssao-silhouette-browser.mjs`: a box facing the camera with nothing near it, turned about the view axis in 12 steps, should read occlusion 1 everywhere. On WebGPU 4 silhouette pixels read down to 0.78 at 2 of the turns; on the WebGL2 layer, whose 4x sample positions leave more one-pixel tips, 1 to 3 pixels read down to 0.72 at 10 of them. Found as the 2.3 of 255 left on the WebGL2 layer by the KB-POST-ALPHARIM1 check.
- **Cause:** the extract pass built each pixel's normal from the neighbour with the smaller depth step, and a background neighbour (depth 0, reversed Z at infinity) counted as a neighbour. At a tip of the silhouette, where both neighbours on one axis are background, the step went to infinity, the normal turned sideways and the hemisphere kernel sampled the face itself.
- **Fixed:** a background neighbour is no surface; a silhouette pixel takes the step to its covered side, and a pixel with no surface neighbour on an axis takes the camera-facing normal, as degenerate pixels already did (`extractShader` in `packages/post/src/shaders.ts`; the closer-neighbour choice of J. Turanszki, "Improved normal reconstruction from depth", 2019). Regression: the test above, both backends, SSAO and GTAO. `scripts/ssao-gpu-check.js`, `ssao-resolve-browser.mjs` and `gtao-sky-browser.mjs` pass unchanged on both backends.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: post effects used alone on a transparent canvas drew a light rim on silhouettes (KB-POST-ALPHARIM1, post, display transform)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/alpha-rim-browser.mjs` (WebGPU, and MARGO_COMPAT=1 for the WebGL2 layer): a box turned about the view axis on a `TransparentCanvas` with SSAO, GTAO, SSGI, SSR, Afterimage or LensFlare alone put silhouette pixels 36 to 37.5 of 255 above the face colour at their coverage, Bloom 37.5; Tonemap had the same fault until GAP-FILM-ALPHA (e323a96e86).
- **Cause:** every post effect that writes the canvas from a linear capture ran `toDisplay` (PBR Neutral and the sRGB encoding) on the premultiplied colour. A partly covered pixel holds colour times coverage (Porter and Duff 1984), and the curve of that product is brighter than the product of the curve. FXAA, SMAA and Glitch were not affected: they filter core's display output, which core encodes per sample before the resolve.
- **Fixed:** `straightDisplay` and `displayFor` in `packages/shared/display.js` rewrite each `vec4f(toDisplay(c),a)` as `toDisplay(c/a)*a` for 0 < a < 1, and every display pipeline in post (SSAO and GTAO, SSGI, SSR, Bloom, Afterimage, Accumulate, LensFlare, Lens, Anamorphic, Blur, HeatHaze, ContactShadows, SSS, MaterialDecals, MotionBlur, SelectiveBloom, EffectMask) builds from it and keys its pipeline on the canvas mark. An opaque canvas keeps its shaders byte for byte. Regression: the GPU test above (within 0.7 of 255, Bloom 1.4, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; the core render alone reads 0.7, the bound is one 8-bit step above it) and `packages/post/test/straight-display.test.js`.
- **Same pattern outside post:** DOF was fixed on 2026-11-27 (KB-ALPHA-TEMPORAL1). Water's composites, post's SurfaceCaustics and the lens drops followed on 2026-11-28 (KB-WATER-ALPHARIM1).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: a thin rod rolling on a default cloth is thrown through it (KB-SOFT-TUNNEL1, physics soft, soft-rigid contact)

- **Repro:** `packages/physics/tests/soft.test.js`, "small and thin rigid bodies dropped on a default cloth rest on it for five seconds and never pass through it": with gravity 9.80665 m/s^2 the 5 mm rod rolls down the sagging sheet at up to 125 rad/s and leaves it at step 163, thrown at 65 m/s; at 9.81 it rolls a slightly different path and passed. It is not tunnelling through a gap: a single pass met one triangle 15 to 30 cm deep and pushed the rod through the sheet.
- **Cause:** a face contact with a round body orients the triangle's normal out of the body. It read the side from the normal the contact was found with. The host finds that normal where the body touches during the step, in the body's frame at the step's start, and turns it with the body. A round body's contact is not fixed in it: as it rolls, the contact slides round its surface (Montana 1988, "The kinematics of contact and grasp", IJRR 7(3)). Under a rod that rolls one or two radians a step, the normal found lay almost in the sheet's plane, or, turned with the rod past a quarter turn, pointed back into it. The side was then a coin toss, and when it fell wrong the sheet was met from below.
- **Fixed:** a round face contact (radius of curvature above 0) keeps for the whole step the side of the triangle its centre of curvature was on at the step's start (`face_sides` in `soft-kernel/src/face.rs`, after Bridson, Fedkiw and Anderson 2002, "Robust treatment of collisions, contact and friction for cloth animation", and Harmon, Vouga, Tamstorf and Grinspun 2008, "Robust treatment of simultaneous collisions", which keep the side a pair was on before the step). A corner or an edge of a body (radius 0), and a round body whose centre lies in the plane itself, go by the normal found, as before: those points are fixed in the body. Regression: the test above, with a rod at standard gravity among its bodies, and `packages/physics/soft-kernel/tests/face.rs`, `a_rod_whose_contact_was_found_beside_it_is_held_on_the_sheets_side` and `a_rod_that_rolled_past_a_quarter_turn_in_a_step_stays_on_the_sheets_side`.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: the glTF report could not decode a Draco file (KB-GLTFREPORT-DECODERS, gltf)

- **Repro:** `reportGLTF` on the Khronos Draco Box gave a `decode` problem ("This file needs the Draco decoder") and
  took its bounds from the accessors' declared min and max (+-0.5004885 against a decoded +-0.5), skipping the
  zero-area, not-finite and inside-out checks for those primitives. `GLTFReportOptions` had no way to pass a decoder.
- **Cause:** the report built its `GLTFAsset` without decoder hooks, so no module held the Draco decoder.
- **Fix:** the report gives the reader the built-in decoders, imported only for a file that needs one, and takes
  `decoders` as `loadGLTF` does (packages/gltf/src/report.ts).
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/report.test.js, "a Draco file is decoded where the report runs" and "the report
  takes decoder hooks"; both fail without the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: one moving caster made Shadows redraw its whole cached still map every frame (GAP-FILM-SHADOWCACHE, shadows)

- **Repro:** `Shadows` with a terrain or road caster and a car added without `static`, the
  car moved every frame: `stats.staticDraws` counted every still caster in every cascade on every frame, and
  `cacheHits` stayed at 0. Output was right; the cost landed on every film frame with a moving object.
- **Cause:** an unmarked caster is cached "while it stays put": its world matrix is part of the still-map hash, so a
  caster that moves every frame changed the hash every frame and redrew the whole cached array.
- **Fix:** `Shadows` tracks each unmarked caster's matrix. One that moves on two frames in a row leaves the cached map
  (one redraw) and draws in the per-frame pass; after 30 frames held still it rejoins the cache (one more redraw). A
  single move, such as placing an object, still redraws the cache once and keeps it cached. A caster added with
  `static: true` is the caller's promise and is not tracked: move it with `invalidate()`. Regression:
  `packages/shadows/test/cache.test.js`, "a caster moving every frame leaves the cached map instead of redrawing it
  every frame".

### Open: the original kiln and turbofan shots await FIRE-06 scene integrations

- Thermal and mechanical output ports use their live signed cell and validate borrowed inputs in the owner's memory. The thermal stress coupling tests cover registered replay and rejection of a late liquid cell or unaligned lease before mechanical publication. A separate civil kiln witness displays radiative cooling and its small-strain thermal deformation on both renderers. The heat-haze renderer accepts the temperature volume.
