### Open (below Margo): the WebGL2 layer on ANGLE Direct3D 11 gives the flood film another state from one browser launch to the next (KB-WATER-FLOODFILM-COMPAT1, water, 2026-11-21)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/water/test/flood-film.browser.mjs` (WebGL2 layer, Intel Arc 140V through
  ANGLE D3D11) failed once in four runs, under load (four agents and a `test:changed` run on the 8-core machine): the
  two 30 fps runs hashed c9b4539d (volume 4,535.639080 m^3) and the 60 fps run 2859cbf7 (4,535.639329), so "1,200
  frames at 60 fps equal 600 at 30 fps" failed. The other three runs, two of them on the code before
  KB-WATER-SURGEVOL1's change and one after, hashed eee49ae9 (4,535.639200) for every run and the seek. The flood's
  kernels take no surf WGSL (dist/flood.js imports swell-wgsl only). The check stays bit for bit as it is.
- **Cause:** below Margo, in what the browser's WebGL2 stack (ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end, the HLSL compiler or the
  driver) makes of the same GLSL and the same inputs. Upstream draft: `docs/upstream-reports/KB-WATER-FLOODFILM-COMPAT1/report.md`.
  Evidence (2026-11-21, renderer string `ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) Arc(TM) 140V GPU (16GB) (0x000064A0) Direct3D11
  vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)`, the check's scene with each 4 s reading hashed too, up to four GPU runs at once on the
  8-core machine):
  - The state is not the same from one launch to the next. In 32 WebGL2 launches the first 30 fps run ended at
    eee49ae9 (26), c9b4539d (4), d9a15081 (1) and a1e8cf94 (1); the 10 s restore leg at 362bba19 (28), 867ef247 (3)
    and 92525196 (1). The launches already differ at the first reading, 4 s in. 20 of 20 native WebGPU launches in
    the same hours gave 43f2d001 (restore 2e640161) exactly.
  - Inside a launch the legs agree in 31 of 32: the two 30 fps runs, the 60 fps run, the seek and the device restore.
    In one launch the first 30 fps run (a1e8cf94) differed from the rest (eee49ae9), as the logged run's 60 fps leg did.
  - What Margo hands WebGL2 is the same in every launch: the GLSL of the stage, first and record kernels compared equal
    across launches; ANGLE's translated HLSL of the stage's two programs (WEBGL_debug_shaders, Edge started with
    `--enable-privileged-webgl-extensions`) hashed daee9534 and 4db8f6b2 in all 7 launches captured; the uniform ring's
    bytes (2,886 writes), the float texture uploads and the kernels' size uniforms hashed the same in all 7 launches
    measured. No clock, timer or random number reaches the flood, Water or core (none in their sources), and the stage
    is a gather that writes only its own texel of render targets no draw also reads, so no read can race a write in
    GL's in-order command stream.
  - Gap: the 6 varying launches were the first 6 after the build; every launch after them gave eee49ae9, including all
    those with the HLSL and GL-stream probes, so no HLSL or GL-stream capture exists yet from inside a varying launch.
    Which layer gives the other rounding (ANGLE's pixel executable, the HLSL compiler or the driver's compile) is not
    known, and GLSL ES 3.00 has no `precise` to pin it.
- **Fix condition:** an ANGLE or driver change that compiles the same GLSL to the same rounding in every launch, or a
  standalone page that shows the varying launch and names the layer; until then the check can fail on this layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: Blender's TANH math node gave NaN for large inputs on native WebGPU (KB-BLENDER-TANH1, blender)

- **Fix:** `TANH` is `tanh(clamp(a,-10.0,10.0))`. For |x| over 9.01, 1 - |tanh x| = 2 / (e^2|x| + 1) is under 2^-25, so
  f32 tanh rounds to +-1 (IEEE 754-2019 round to nearest) and the clamp changes no correctly rounded value. It is the
  only tanh the blender package emits.
- **Regression:** `packages/blender/tests/nodes.test.js` fails on a bare tanh in the emitted WGSL;
  `packages/blender/tests/nodes-browser.mjs` renders TANH of 100, -100 and 395 and expects +-1, not NaN.
- **Repro (before):** a WGSL compute shader writing `tanh(x)` for runtime x on native WebGPU (adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`): 1 at
  x = 50, NaN at x = 100, 395 and -100 (sinh and cosh return infinity there; found under KB-WATER-SURGEVOL1).
  `packages/blender/src/nodes-wgsl.ts` mapped the math node's `TANH` to a bare `tanh(a)`, so a node graph feeding it a
  value over about 88.7 in size got NaN where Blender gives +-1.
- **Cause:** the GPU's tanh overflows f32 in sinh or cosh for |x| over about 88.7.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: the surge check's sea held half its water on native WebGPU (KB-WATER-SURGEVOL1, water)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/water/test/surge.browser.mjs` (native WebGPU, adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`) failed
  "the surge brings water in from the sea": volume 1,679.1 m^3 at the peak against 1,430.8 calm (1.17 times; it asked
  over 1.2). The same numbers, bit for bit, on the code before KB-SCENES-DUNE-ARCHANG1's change; the WebGL2 layer
  passed.
- **The physics:** the beach (64 rows, ground -2.95 + 0.1 i m) at rest at level L holds 64 x sum (L - ground) over the
  cells below L: 2,880 m^3 at 0 and 5,120 m^3 at 1 m, a ratio of 1.78 (the 5 mm swell adds under 0.3%). The WebGL2
  layer measured 2,880.2 and 5,133.9, and test/coast-reference.js (the flow in float64, no surf) 2,880 at rest. So 1.2
  was a loose bound, not a wrong one: native WebGPU had lost half the sea at rest, and the beach probe alone (0.607 m at
  ground 0.45 m) still passed.
- **Cause:** the surf's WGSL (`packages/water/src/surf.ts`) took tanh of unbounded arguments, and native WebGPU on this
  GPU returns NaN for tanh(x) once sinh and cosh overflow f32 (measured: 1 at x = 50, NaN at x = 100). The Ruessink et
  al. 2012 wave phase `tanh(0.815 / Ur^0.672)` passes x = 89 where the Ursell number is under about 1e-3, as under the
  test's 5 mm, 20 m swell in water 2.4 m deep or more. There `surfSea` returned NaN; the integrate kernel's relaxation target `max(0, sea - ground)`
  read 0, so the open sea next to the map's deep edge relaxed toward empty (the edge column held 0 m over 2.95 m of
  ground) and the beach cells sloshed meters deep. Found by writing `surfSea` into the state's spare channels: NaN in
  the six columns 2.45 m deep or more, finite beyond. Fenton and McKee's `tanh((k0 d)^0.75)` (in `surfK` and the field
  builder's `waveK`) would do the same at k0 d over 397, a 20 m swell over 1.26 km of water.
- **Fix:** every tanh in the surf's WGSL takes `min(x, 10.0)`. For x over 9.01, 1 - tanh x = 2 / (e^2x + 1) is under
  2^-25, half an f32 ulp below 1, so tanh x rounds to 1 (IEEE 754-2019 round to nearest) and the clamp changes no
  correctly rounded value; the Ruessink phase then reads 0, the symmetric wave of its Ur -> 0 limit. The water surface
  and the wave queries share this WGSL, so a calm deep sea's surface no longer reads NaN there either.
- **After:** native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer give the same volumes to six digits: 2,880.15 m^3 at rest, 5,133.87 at
  the peak, 2,881.35 after the fall; the beach floods to 0.606 m and drains to 0.008 m.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/surge.browser.mjs` now asks for the still-water volumes themselves (within 1% at
  rest and 2% at the peak, in place of the 1.2 ratio; the drained run's 1,430.8 fails it), and
  `packages/water/test/coast-runup.test.js` fails on any tanh in water's sources whose argument is not bounded by `min(`
  or `clamp(` (it lists the three bare ones before the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-21: the dune coast's camp view hung the WebGPU device on a laptop GPU (KB-SCENES-DUNE-ARCHANG1, water)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --views=camp-buildings` (native WebGPU, laptop
  GPU, adapter `intel` `xe-2lpg`): within about 3 s of the page's start "the page's WebGPU device was lost
  (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG)", the restore's `requestDevice` then failed with DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED and the frame was
  black. Three runs out of three on 2026-11-20 (with and without KB-SCENES-DUNE-GTAO1's scatter change); small WebGPU
  pages passed between them, and the WebGL2 layer ran the view.
- **Cause:** found by timing every render and compute pass of the page's frames with timestamp queries: on the first
  frame one compute pass, the `Water` coastal flow's `step` (`packages/water/src/coastal.ts`), ran 4,403 ms; every other
  pass was under 61 ms, and later frames' `step` 7 ms. On its first step the flow records its whole set-up into the
  frame's one command buffer: the initial state and the sea's connectivity, the surf field's 2 + 1,024 relaxation sweeps
  of the 512 x 512 shore grid and the 40 s spin-up (600 frames of 3 substeps, 3,600 flow dispatches), about 4,600 grid
  dispatches. Windows resets a GPU that cannot finish or preempt one DMA packet within 2 s (Microsoft, "Timeout
  detection and recovery (TDR)", https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/drivers/display/timeout-detection-and-recovery,
  and "TdrDelay", https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-hardware/drivers/display/tdr-registry-keys), so the packet hung
  the device whenever the scheduler asked to preempt it (another process's GPU work, the desktop) and it could not yield.
  A quiet run of the page can survive it, as one probe run here did; the scene's check did not.
- **Fix:** `CoastalFlow.setUp` (`packages/water/src/coastal.ts`, with `SurfFieldBuilder.build` in `surf.ts`) records
  the same set-up commands in the same order, but into command buffers of at most `SETUP_WORKGROUPS` (2^18, 64 grid
  dispatches of a 512 x 512 map) workgroups, each submitted on its own (Dawn records the buffers of one submit into one
  D3D12 command list) ahead of the frame's commands; the frame's own three substeps stay in the frame. On this GPU the
  first frame is now 74 submissions of the set-up, none over 84 ms, 4.4 to 4.8 s of GPU time in all as before. The
  set-up reads the heightmap and the uniform as the queue holds them when the step runs (the upload, and the uniform
  written just before), not a heightmap the same frame's encoder writes earlier on the GPU; no package feeds Water one.
- **After:** the camp check passes on native WebGPU on this GPU ("dune coast still check passed": ground sRGB 154, 141,
  110; occlusion mean 177.2 against 180.6 open, 10.2 percent of pixels darker), which finishes verifying
  KB-SCENES-DUNE-GTAO1 there. `packages/water/test/surf.browser.mjs` gives the same swash run-up as before (0.126 m, in
  the first wave period too).
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/surf.browser.mjs` counts the compute workgroups of every queue submission of the
  first frame: none holds more than 2^18 and all of them hold at least the set-up's (fails on the code before: one
  submission of 18,986,279 workgroups).

### Fixed 2026-11-21: disposing a GeometryGenerator left its plugin and frame pass in the scene (KB-GEOMETRY-GENDISPOSE1, geometry)
- **Repro:** `const generator = GeometryGenerator.attach(engine); generator.dispose();` then `engine.sceneOf(generator)` still returned the scene and its compute pass stayed registered; the new owner fixture `packages/geometry/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` failed with "releases its registration" in every direct-disposal case.
- **Cause:** `dispose()` freed the items' buffers and cleared the engine and device but never called `removePlugin`, unlike every other plugin's `dispose` (Scatter, SculptView). It also kept the read-back copy pipeline of the old device.
- **Fix:** `dispose()` clears its fields, then removes the plugin from its scene (the repeated dispose that `removePlugin` triggers finds nothing to do) and drops the copy pipeline.
- **Regression:** `packages/geometry/tests/gpu.test.js` "disposing the generator takes its plugin out of the scene, once"; `npm run check:owners -- --packages=geometry` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: disposing a machinery plugin left it registered in its scene (KB-MACHINERY-DISPOSE1, machinery)
- **Repro:** `const view = ExplodedView.attach(engine, parts); view.dispose();` then `engine.sceneOf(view)` still returned the scene; the same for Kinematics, SurfacePhysics, TelemetryChannel, FeatureEdges, SectionPlanes and EngineeringAnnotations. The new owner fixture `packages/machinery/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` failed with "releases its registration" for each. Dimensions removed its plugins from the active scene, not the one it was attached to.
- **Cause:** `dispose()` cleared the plugin's own fields but never called `removePlugin`, unlike Scatter and SculptView; Dimensions called `engine.removePlugin(name)`, which uses the active scene.
- **Fix:** each `dispose()` clears its fields, then removes the plugin from its own scene (the repeated dispose that `removePlugin` triggers finds nothing to do). FeatureEdges and SectionPlanes keep their device-restore path on a private release that does not unregister.
- **Regression:** `packages/machinery/test/scene.test.js` "disposing Kinematics, ExplodedView, SurfacePhysics or TelemetryChannel takes the plugin out of its scene"; `npm run check:owners -- --packages=machinery` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: FeatureEdges and the SectionPlanes caps ignored the view's viewport and scissor (KB-MACHINERY-VIEWPORT1, machinery)
- **Repro:** render a view with a viewport smaller than the canvas with FeatureEdges (or SectionPlanes with caps) attached; the owner fixture `packages/machinery/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` failed in the browser leaf with "draw restores the current viewport".
- **Cause:** their render passes never set the pass viewport and scissor, so edges and cap fills were drawn over the whole target instead of the view's rectangle.
- **Fix:** both passes set `context.view`'s viewport and scissor the way core's own draw does.
- **Regression:** `npm run check:owners -- --packages=machinery` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (the harness checks every draw's viewport and scissor).

### Fixed 2026-11-21: disposing ToonShading or Stars left them registered, and the starfield ignored the view (KB-CREATIVE-DISPOSE1, creative)

- **Repro:** `ToonShading.attach(engine).dispose()` or `Stars.attach(engine).dispose()`, then `engine.sceneOf(plugin)` still returned the scene and the frame pass kept running on freed buffers (ToonShading's pass then threw on `this.entry!`). With two views, the starfield also drew over the whole target (the harness: "draw restores the current viewport").
- **Cause:** both `dispose()` freed their buffers and never called `removePlugin`, which `onDeviceRestored` shared with them; Stars' pass never called `applyView`.
- **Fix:** a private `release()` for the device resources (used by `onDeviceRestored`), and `dispose()` removes the plugin from the scene it was attached to, then releases. Stars and Planet set the view's viewport and scissor.
- **Regression:** `packages/creative/tests/dispose-scene.test.js` "ToonShading.dispose takes it out of its own scene, once" and the Stars twin; `npm run check:owners -- --packages=creative`.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: GrassField and Planet refused an offscreen target of the other 8-bit canvas format (KB-CREATIVE-TARGETFMT1, creative)

- **Repro:** on a device whose preferred canvas format is `bgra8unorm` (Windows), draw a GrassField or Planet into an `rgba8unorm` texture: "Unsupported grass target format". The owner harness' target is `rgba8unorm`.
- **Cause:** the variant check allowed only `navigator.gpu.getPreferredCanvasFormat()` and the HDR formats, though the pipeline and shader are the same for both 8-bit formats WebGPU defines for a canvas.
- **Fix:** `rgba8unorm` and `bgra8unorm` are both accepted (other formats and sample counts are still refused).
- **Regression:** `tests/modern-grass.test.js` "GrassField builds only its initial variant" (draws both formats); `npm run check:owners -- --packages=creative` on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: horse crowds and army crowds drew into the active scene and leaked their coat atlas on scene disposal (KB-HORSES-CROWDOWN1, horses, armies)

- **Repro:** `addHorseCrowd`, `addHorse`, `PersonCrowd.attach` and `addArmy`, called from inside a scene (a plugin setup of a non-default scene), put their model and crowd draws into whichever scene was active after the lazy imports finished; the new owner fixtures failed "exercises a real registration". Disposing the owner scene or engine of a horse crowd, with `herd.dispose()` never called, left the coat atlas texture alive ("no leaked GPU buffers, textures or query sets").
- **Cause:** the calls did not keep the scene they were made for across their awaits (`captureScene` in gltf and blender does); the atlas was owned by the herd handle only, not by the draw plugin the scene disposes.
- **Fix:** each call captures its scene before the first await and runs the registration in it; the herd's crowd draw is a subclass whose `dispose()` also releases the atlas, once.
- **Regression:** `packages/horses/test/horses.test.js` "crowd: the coat atlas goes with the draw however the draw is let go, once"; `npm run check:owners -- --packages=horses,armies`.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: formatting moved the visual scorch division annotation (biomes)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/biomes/tests/no-raw-division.test.js` flagged the float division in `disturbanceStates` after `5757affe45`.
- **Cause:** the annotation was attached to the end of a render-state object. Formatting put the annotated division and the comment on different lines.
- **Fix:** name the scorch height calculation and keep its float-division annotation on the same line. The formula still runs only during the burn window.
- **Regression:** the existing no-raw-division test checks the formatted source and still rejects unannotated variable division.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: Water's WebGL2 browser suite could exhaust one GPU step (water tests)

- **Repro:** run `npm run check:gpu-packages -- --select=water/test:gpu --no-build` with `MARGO_COMPAT=1` on the RTX A6000 workstation. The old step reached the surf check and was ended at 600 s.
- **Cause:** the GPU runner assigned one ten-minute limit to all 49 browser launches. The elapsed time included WebGL2 shader compilation, browser startup and teardown for each check.
- **Fix:** run the same checks in three package scripts of 16, 16 and 17 checks. The runner still gives each script ten minutes. The preview script keeps its separate slot.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/browser-root.test.js` checks that each browser command appears exactly once across the groups, including both underwater modes.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: the bow wave extended sideways in a straight line (water/ships)

- **Repro:** a 68 m hull at 3 m/s leaves a raised stripe at the same distance aft of the stem across the near-field bow wave.
- **Cause:** the longitudinal contact profile used the same phase at every lateral position. The outboard falloff only reduced its height.
- **Fix:** sweep the profile aft and fade its height and foam to zero as it leaves the current hull. Use the current hull frame for the waterline mask when a ship turns.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/ships.test.js` and `packages/water/test/ships.browser.mjs` test separation of the hull crest, swept shoulder and old transverse line.

### Fixed 2026-11-21: turbulent foam was already old at the stern (water/ships)

- **Repro:** move a 72 m hull at 3 m/s with a 9.5-second foam life. Sample within one metre aft of the transom after the ship has moved one hull length.
- **Cause:** the foam used the time at which the bow passed each point. The newest churning water was treated as roughly 24 seconds old. Stationary samples in a path also fell back to a due-north heading and could put a false turn in the wake near the berth.
- **Fix:** sample the position and time of the stern as it passed. Keep the bow trajectory for the Kelvin and bow wave systems. Carry the last moving heading through stationary history samples.
- **Regression:** `packages/water/test/ships.test.js` and `packages/water/test/ships.browser.mjs` check fresh and aging foam and reject points outside the trail. The CPU test also checks that an eastbound ship leaves no diagonal wake at its starting berth.

### Corrected 2026-11-24: a box resting on a soft contact gave 0.4 micrometre less than g over omega squared (KB-PHYS-SOFTGIVE1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** a 1 m cube or ball of density 1000 dropped 0.1 m onto a fixed floor, `setSolver({contactHertz: 60, contactDamping: 10, allowedPenetration: 0.03})`, 900 steps with canSleep false: the resting depth less the allowed 0.03 is 68.67 micrometres, where the soft contact's equilibrium is g / omega^2 = 69.03. At `contactDamping: 1` it is 68.96.
- **Cause:** not a fault of the solver. The soft step of Catto (GDC 2011; Solver2D 2024) has the spring's own equilibrium for every damping ratio: with the substep ending at rest, mass_scale / impulse_scale = h omega (2 zeta + h omega) times bias_rate = omega / (2 zeta + h omega) is h omega^2, so C = g / omega^2. A scalar model of the full step (`packages/physics/scripts/soft-step-model.mjs`), with the warm start, the biased pass, the position update and the relax pass, reaches 1.0000 of that for zeta 0.3, 1 and 10. The kernel's gap is a difference of positions near 0.5 m in float32, spacing 3e-8 m, and a few operations of it round to up to 0.4 micrometre: at a tenth of the size (coordinates near 0.05 m) the depth agrees to 0.05 micrometre at zeta 10 (ratio 0.9993 against 0.9948), and the pair's impulse is exactly m g / 60 N s a step in both.
- **Fix:** none needed. `next-parameters.test.js` asserts the analytic depth to 4e-7 m (13 float32 spacings at the box's size), to 2e-7 m at a damping ratio of 1, and to 1e-7 m in the small scene.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a body a joint or a contact was still pulling home fell asleep short of it (KB-PHYS-SLEEP-PUSH1, physics kernel)

- **Repro:** a fixed body and a 10 kg ball at y = -2 with a spherical joint whose anchors lie 1.5 m apart (`anchorA: [0, 0.5, 0]`, `anchorB: [0, 1, 0]`, canSleep default); `physics.step()` 200 times. The ball closes the error at the joint's push speed (3 m/s, 0.05 m a step) and stopped at y = -0.55, asleep, 0.05 m from the joint's home at -0.5. With `canSleep: false` it reached -0.5.
- **Cause:** the soft solver closes a joint's or a contact's error by moving the pose and leaves no velocity behind, and the sleep test (Erleben 2005, 6.5) read velocity alone, so the ball counted as at rest while it moved 0.05 m every step. The 0.5 s window ended before the 0.5 s of travel had.
- **Fix:** `begin_step` in `kernel/src/integrate.rs` resets a dynamic body's sleep timer when the pose it moved through in the last step, over the step, has kinetic energy per unit of mass above the body's own sleep threshold (`pose_energy` in `kernel/src/island.rs`); a body asked to sleep (`sleep`) is ready at once whatever its pose last did (`ASKED_TO_SLEEP`). Regression: `packages/physics/tests/next-sleep-pushed.test.js` "a body a joint pulls home from 1.5 m away does not fall asleep on the way", which fails without it. A box on a ground with `allowedPenetration: 0.03` now rests at 0.030017 m (the contact's 17 micrometres of give) in place of the 0.03 m or less it read when it slept early, so `next-parameters.test.js` bounds it at 0.0301.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a character standing on a slope steeper than minSlopeSlideAngle did not slide down it (KB-PHYS-CHARACTER-SLIDE1, physics character controller)

- **Repro:** a fixed box (halfExtents 10, 0.05, 10) turned 25 degrees about z; a kinematic position capsule (halfHeight 0.4, radius 0.3) above it; `physics.createCharacterController(capsule, {minSlopeSlideAngle: 20 degrees, maxSlopeClimbAngle: 60 degrees, autostep: false, snapToGround: 0.2})`; every step `controller.move([0, -0.08, 0])`. The capsule stayed where it landed with `movement` [0, 0, 0]; Rapier 0.21's controller on the same scene slides it downhill by about 0.031 m a step. With `minSlopeSlideAngle` 40 degrees (above the slope) both hold still.
- **Cause (traced):** after the first downward hit the capsule rests exactly at the controller's `offset` from the slope. The next cast, along the slide direction (parallel to the slope), is already within the target distance of the surface and reports a hit at distance 0 with the same normal, although the motion does not approach the surface. Each of the eight loop iterations then travelled 0, and its slide step re-added the tangent part of the remaining motion, so the loop ended with the remaining motion longer than it began and nothing moved.
- **Fix:** `move` in `packages/physics/src/character.ts` casts again with a target distance of 0 when a hit at distance 0 is not approached (`dot(direction, normal) > -1e-3`), so only what really lies ahead stops the motion. On the repro the own controller now moves -0.031 m, -0.014 m a step and ends at x = -6.25 after 210 steps against Rapier's -6.26. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/next-character.test.js` ("a slope at or above minSlopeSlideAngle slides the character down it, a gentler one holds it, as Rapier does", own solver and Rapier, 20 against 40 degrees; fails without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a cone joint with a rest pose off its frames drives itself to its limit under a rotation motor (KB-PHYS-SWITCH-CONE1, physics, ragdoll)

- **Repro:** as the entry stood: body A fixed at identity; body B a rod rotated by 0.15 rad about X; a cone with `frameA: R * fB`, `frameB: fB` (a quarter turn about Z), and every step a rotation motor aimed at identity. The rod swung to the 3 rad limit within 20 steps.
- **Cause:** two faults of the cone's rotation drive. (1) The motor impulses a joint carries from one substep to the next were pushed along the joint's own rows (a cone's twist and swing rows), not the drive's rows, which agree only when the rest pose lies on the frames. (2) The target was read in the joint's frame coordinates, so a cone whose frames are not identity (which hold its axis, as a ragdoll's do) turned a target given as a rotation of body B in body A's frame, as a spherical joint takes it, into the wrong pose; the spherical and cone motors now mean the same thing by `rotation`.
- **Fix:** `carry` and `drive_rows` in `kernel/src/joints.rs`. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/next-cone-motor.test.js` ("a cone whose rest pose lies off its frames holds that pose", "a driven cone holds a swing against gravity with its anchor where it was"), which fail without them; the ragdoll's powered tests on the cone joint (head turned 0.71 rad, hips drift) pass with them.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: core + stage measured 24,811 B gzip on macOS against 24,797 B on Windows after the sorted compaction (KB-SIZE-PLATFORM2, core, build)

- **Repro:** on this Mac (arm64, APFS, Node 26.13.0, zlib 1.3.2.1-motley-456ae73), at a83c7a8f2 with 84304f128 included, `npm ci` then `npm run build:packages` prints "Core and stage together: 24,811 B gzip", and `node scripts/measure-size.js` gives 24,811 B gzip / 60,994 B raw. The workstation and local CI measure 24,797 / 60,984 at the same commits, so `tests/public-size-claims.test.js` fails on macOS and passes on Windows.
- **What is ruled out:** the committed kernel blueprint is kept (KB-SIZE-PLATFORM1), and compaction sorts its file names (84304f128); `packages/core/dist/index.js` and `packages/stage/dist/index.js` are byte-identical across two Mac worktrees.
- **Cause:** `compactPackage` bundles a package's files as one multi-entry library build and left imports between those
  entries external by their relative path. On Windows the bundler kept them external; on Linux and macOS it recognised
  the sibling entry, bundled it and moved `camera`, `renderer` (and in the stage `gltf-route`, `viewer-element`,
  `viewer-extras`) into hashed chunks behind facade files. Found by printing Linux CI's core and stage output into its
  log and comparing it file by file with a Windows build; bundling the sibling imports on Windows reproduced the Linux
  files byte for byte.
- **Fix:** b1584af9e: a sibling import resolves to an id that names no file, so every platform leaves it as written.
  Windows output is unchanged (24,820 B gzip / 61,038 B raw), and Linux CI (run 45708085423) now prints 24,820 B with
  all 38 core and stage files byte-identical to a Windows build. macOS was not measured here: it showed the Linux
  figure before the fix.
- **Regression:** `tests/compact-package-order.test.js` (core and the stage keep each entry's code in its own file and
  its imports of other entries as written; the facade it forbids is what Linux and macOS built).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: core + stage measured differently on two machines because a from-source build re-deflated the kernel with the host's zlib (KB-SIZE-PLATFORM1, core, build)

- **Repro:** this Mac (arm64, Node 26.13.0, zlib 1.3.2.1-motley-456ae73) built core + stage at 24,811 B gzip / 60,994 B raw (core 22,163 B); the Windows workstation at 24,797 B / 60,984 B (core 22,179 B, 095c281e9), at the same commits. `measure-size.js` is a function of `packages/core/dist/index.js` and `packages/stage/dist/index.js` alone (no other module enters the bundle; vite 8.3.4 and rolldown 1.2.13 are pinned), so the dist bytes differed.
- **Cause:** raw deflate output is not defined by its settings: the same 9,055 B kernel at level 9, memLevel 6, windowBits 12 is 3,471 B in Node's zlib (Chromium's fork, which hashes with CPU specific instructions) and 3,419 B in stock zlib 1.2.12. `npm run build:packages` embeds the committed `packages/core/src/wasm.ts` untouched, but a from-source build (`build-modern.js` without `--precompiled`, which local CI runs) went through `buildCoreKernel`, which deflated the kernel again with the host's zlib and rewrote `wasm.ts`; `build-modern.js` also measured its kernel record from a fresh deflate. A machine whose zlib deflates differently therefore embedded a different string (about 7 B smaller on the workstation: 9 to 10 B of raw). `physics/scripts/build-kernel.mjs` and `machinery/scripts/build-kernel.mjs` had the same shape (machinery already pinned the gzip OS byte for this reason).
- **Fix:** `scripts/committed-blueprint.mjs`: a build keeps the committed string when it still inflates to the wasm just built, and compresses only a changed kernel. `build-core-kernel.mjs`, `build-modern.js`, the physics kernel build and the machinery kernel build use it; the core Wasm, `wasm.ts` and the core source are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `tests/committed-blueprint.test.js` (every committed deflated blueprint is kept whatever the compressor would give, a changed kernel is compressed again, and the four builds call it).
- **Second cause, and the figures (workstation, 2026-11-24):** the committed blueprint is the one this workstation's zlib makes (a fresh deflate here equals `wasm.ts` byte for byte, and the string in `packages/core/dist/wasm.js` is that string), and a build from the committed tree here measures 24,797 B gzip / 60,984 B raw (core 22,179 B), as local CI did on 2026-11-19 and 2026-11-24. So the 24,811 / 60,994 figures were not what the committed blueprint gives; they could not be reproduced here (no CRLF effect: a rebuild from LF copies of core, stage, shared and scripts gives the same bytes; installed packages match the lock file exactly), and the fleet's Mac mini has no Node install or checkout of that commit to compare with. One input that does change the bytes by machine was found: `scripts/compact-package.js` bundled core and the stage with their files as library entries in the directory listing's order, and that order belongs to the file system. Three other listing orders changed core + stage by 3 to 4 B raw and 9 to 45 B gzip; in reverse order `camera.js` and `gltf-route.js` came out with another import order and other local names. The names are now sorted by code unit, so the listing order no longer matters; for today's names the sorted order is NTFS's, so the figures stay 24,797 B / 60,984 B. Regression: `tests/compact-package-order.test.js` (core and the stage compact to the same bytes with their listing reversed; it fails without the sort).
- **Candidate, not landed:** a deterministic compressor whose bytes our own code defines would give a blueprint about 50 B smaller; it changes core's embedded bytes, so it is a separate core change.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: ragdoll push recovery at 1.5 m/s relied on ankle limits that did not hold (KB-PHYS-SWITCH-BAL1, ragdoll)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/ragdoll/tests/balance.test.js`: on the kernel's cone joint the four "pushed ... it steps that way, catches itself and stands" tests ended in `fallen` after a 1.5 m/s push of the upper body; "motors alone sink" expected Rapier's ankles to roll over.
- **Cause:** the A/B of `packages/ragdoll/scripts/balance-ab.mjs` showed the two solvers agree (the kernel with the ragdoll's earlier ball joint and limit projection recovers all four pushes as Rapier did). On Rapier the projection did not hold a cone under a planted foot: the stance ankle turned to a twist of -2.76 rad against a +-0.2 limit and a swing of 1.36 rad against 0.6, and the controller's recovery leaned on it. With limits that hold, three controller faults showed: the swing foot's target ignored the body's heading and the joint limits; a planted foot that a push lifted set its own target in the air, so the body had no support; and every step took the full `stepTime` while the capture point ran away from the stance foot as e^(omega t), so steps landed short.
- **Fix:** both feet take a level target inside the ankle's cone, the swing foot heading with the hips (SIMBICON); a planted foot's target stays on the ground and a lifted foot steps next; each step's time follows the capture point, ln(reach / d) / omega, no less than 0.4 / omega (step timing adaptation, Khadiv et al. 2020). "Motors alone sink" is an accepted difference (`docs/limits.md`). The four push tests pass at their 1.5 m/s, and the acceptance sweep (`--sweep`) recovers all 120 cases. Regression: the four push tests and "a swing foot is sent a level target inside its ankle limits" in `packages/ragdoll/tests/balance.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-20: ambient occlusion no longer darkened the dune coast's grass (KB-SCENES-DUNE-GTAO1, scatter)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --views=camp-buildings` failed
  "the occluded camp view is darker: mean 181.1 against 180.7": with the default `occlusion` 1.5, 0.4 percent of the
  camp view's pixels were darker than with `occlusion: 0` (on 2026-11-19, 193.8 against 193.3 and 0.7 percent; before
  KB-SCATTER-SUBPIXEL1, 186.4 against 193.2 and 20 percent).
- **Cause:** found by bisecting scenes, post, sky, terrain, environment, shadows, core, shared, water and scatter: the
  first bad commit was KB-SCATTER-SUBPIXEL1's, which draws grass blades by their prefiltered pixel coverage, blended
  over the scene. Blended blades wrote no depth (only the near ring's opaque cores did), and GTAO finds occluders only
  in the depth buffer (Jimenez, Wu, Pesce and Jarabo 2016), so the grass did not occlude: the dark grass feet and the
  shade the clumps cast on the sand were gone.
- **Fix:** `packages/scatter/src/index.ts` and `cover.ts`: after all the blended draws a depth-only pass draws every
  covered ring again with the same pose (`coverCode(code, lit, at, true)`, colour write mask 0) and keeps a fragment
  whose coverage passes the pose's threshold, `scatterCover.w` (now a `vec4f`; 0.5 by default). `GrassScatter` sets it
  to a hash of the blade (`grass.ts`), an object-space hashed alpha test of the coverage (Wyman and McGuire, "Hashed
  Alpha Testing", I3D 2017; the alpha-tested depth pass of blended hair: Nguyen and Donnelly, GPU Gems 2, 2005), so a
  pixel keeps depth with the chance of its coverage and overlapping blades leave it bare with the chance over leaves
  its colour bare (stochastic transparency: Enderton, Sintorn, Shirley and Luebke, I3D 2010), and the pattern holds
  still on the blade as the camera moves. Drawn after the blending, the depth hides no blade that blends later, so the
  colour and the anti-aliasing are unchanged: `packages/scatter/test/grass-pixel.browser.mjs` still reads 0 ppm speckle,
  mean luma 184.54 against 184.90 (diffuse) and 185.12 against 185.41 (PBR) on WebGPU. The camp check on the WebGL2
  layer now reads mean 177.0 against 180.6 open and 10.5 percent of pixels darker; the open frame is the same as before
  (180.6 against 180.7). On native WebGPU, once KB-SCENES-DUNE-ARCHANG1 let the view run (2026-11-21, adapter `intel`
  `xe-2lpg`): mean 177.2 against 180.6 open, 10.2 percent of pixels darker.
- **Regression:** `packages/scatter/test/grass.test.js` ("coverCode depth: ...", fails on the code before: no depth
  stage) and `packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --views=camp-buildings` (fails on the code before, above).
- **Limit:** a pixel the depth pass leaves bare keeps the ground's depth, and the grass is not in GTAO's ambient replay,
  so it occludes the sand but is not darkened itself; recorded in `docs/limits.md`.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: the Fauld store's bulbs drew a 30 mm sphere at the lamp's whole candela, past the half-float headroom (KB-FAULD-GLOBE1, scenes)

- **What:** `@margoengine/scenes/fauld-tunnels` drew each mains lamp as a 30 mm glowing sphere at the light's candela over its projected area: about 26,000 in the pre-exposed frame (36,000 at night), past the /8 headroom the store keeps under half-float's 65,504 for bloom and the 3,200 K white balance. Hand lamps were 40 mm sources (147,000 in the after state) and the cradle's bowl lamp a hand lamp's.
- **Cause:** the emitter was the filament bulb. A 60 or 100 W lamp in a 140 mm opal well glass glows over the globe, a hand lamp over its 104 mm lens and a deep bowl over its mouth. Also, after, flooded and sealed were set to EV 1 by hand when the hand lamps were lifted to chest height: their key card (2 m along the first hand lamp's beam, the lighting plan's key_after) read 7.4, 2.9 stops over; the night yard's read 1.33.
- **Fix:** the lamps hang in `tn_wellglass` (a 1940s well-glass bulkhead modelled in Blender, channel-films tunnels_kit_blender.py `well_glass`; the globe measured at 0.07 m), whose glass is the emitter at the same lumens (`WELL_GLASS_RADIUS`, 4,700 to 7,900); `HANDLAMP_LENS_RADIUS` 0.052 and `DEEP_BOWL_RADIUS` 0.16; after, flooded and sealed metered to EV 3.9, the night yard to 1.9 (Lagarde and de Rousiers, Moving Frostbite to PBR, SIGGRAPH 2014, section 5.1, pre-exposure).
- **Test:** packages/scenes/test/fauld-tunnels.test.js, "the well glass is the emitter, each lamp keeping its luminous power" and "the key card of each lamp-lit state reads 1.0 at its EV"; the /8 headroom test unchanged.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: LightBounce bounced the first four of a row of equal lamps wherever the camera stood (KB-BOUNCE-NEAREST1, clustered)

- **What:** in the Fauld store's 56-lamp rows the lamps by the camera bounced nothing, so the arch and the stack sides near the camera stayed black.
- **Cause:** `LightBounce` kept the most powerful lights; equal lamps tied and list order won.
- **Fix:** it ranks by power over the squared distance from the camera, the many-light importance of Lightcuts (Walter et al., SIGGRAPH 2005) and the many-light survey (Dachsbacher et al., CGF 2014).
- **Test:** packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js (the nearest lamps of an equal row bounce).

### Fixed 2026-11-19: on the WebGL2 layer a page's first frames with a large shadow map threw "stopped at its work budget" (KB-COMPAT-CPUBUDGET1, shadows)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs` (dune coast, 4,096 shadow map, four
  cascades): the first view failed with "A compute dispatch on the WebGL2 layer's CPU tier stopped at its work budget of
  100000000 invocations and loop iterations (128 x 128 x 4 workgroups)". It looked intermittent: a page that waited
  between attach and its first frame passed.
- **Cause:** the first `Shadows` on a page loads its nearest-depth route (`./compat.js`) by `import()`. Frames drawn before
  it settled ran the WebGPU reduction (workgroup atomics), which the layer can only run on its CPU tier; a 4,096 map with
  four layers is 67 million texels, past the tier's budget. Smaller maps fit the budget but cost about 0.5 s a frame.
- **Fix:** packages/shadows/src/index.ts: while the route loads on the layer the reduction waits (`nearestStale` stays
  set) and runs on the route on the frame after it arrives, as DOF waits for its route. Until then the PCSS search spans
  its widest, as before any map was reduced. A failed load falls back to the WebGPU kernel and reports the error.
- **Regression:** `packages/shadows/test/compat-route-wait.test.js` (frames before the route settles compile no atomics
  kernel and the first frame after it reduces on the route; fails on the code before).

### Fixed 2026-11-19: test:changed ran every package's CPU tests when more than 12 packages were affected (KB-TESTCHANGED-CAP1, scripts)

- **Repro (before):** `node scripts/test-changed.mjs --plan --files=packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/index.ts` printed
  "every package: 18 packages affected, more than 12" and ran 108 packages (about 24 min of test time), so the fast
  gate's 20 min cap stopped it. No package came near the 15 min per-package limit: the longest were water (5.0 min) and
  humans (4.1 min).
- **Cause:** `testPackages` in `scripts/test-changed.mjs` took check:merge's decision whole, and `analyse`
  (`scripts/support/affected-gpu.mjs`) turns more than MAX_AFFECTED (12) affected packages into a full run, a rule for
  the GPU steps. The CPU tests of the changed packages and their dependents are exact at any count.
- **Fix:** `planFiles` takes the cap as an argument and test:changed passes no cap, so the same change runs the 14
  affected packages that have tests. A full reason (core, stage, check code and the rest) still runs every package.
  Regression: `tests/check-merge-affected.test.js` ("test:changed picks the changed packages ...").

### Fixed 2026-11-24: parseGLTFAsync of a file in memory fetched its external URIs from the page's directory (KB-GLTFA B7, gltf/pbr)

- **Repro (before):** `parseGLTFAsync(engine, docWithImageUri)` from `@margoengine/gltf/pbr` on a page at
  `https://app.test/editor/` with `images: [{ uri: 'secret/tex.png' }]` requested `https://app.test/editor/secret/tex.png`
  and failed with `glTF download request failed: HTTP 404`, which did not say that the file has no location.
- **Cause:** `loadAsset` (`packages/gltf/src/asset.ts`) resolved URIs against `globalThis.location` when no URL was given.
- **Fix:** `AssetOptions.baseURL` names what a file in memory resolves against; without it an external buffer or image
  URI (not `data:`) is refused with a coded `state` error that names `baseURL` and `loadGLTF`, and nothing is fetched.
  `loadGLTF` and the other loaders that fetch the file know its location and ignore the option. This changes the
  documented "resolves against the page" behaviour on purpose (manager ruling 2026-11-24).
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/in-memory-base.test.js; test/download-budget.test.js now passes `baseURL`.

### Fixed 2026-11-19: loadAuto held a large file twice while gltf/pbr loaded it (KB-GLTFA B14, gltf)

- **Repro (before):** `loadAuto(engine, url)` on a 100 MiB file streamed in 1 MiB chunks: while gltf/pbr held its
  bytes, 209,724,900 B of ArrayBuffers were reachable (two copies), counted after a full collection.
- **Cause:** the fetch cache in `packages/gltf/src/auto.ts` kept each URL's original `Response` and handed out
  clones; the original body was never read, so it buffered every byte a clone read, for as long as anything held the
  wrapped `fetch` (a light model fetching images later did).
- **Fix:** the cache reads each URL once, under gltf/pbr's 512 MiB budget for the whole load, and keeps the chunks as
  they arrived, with no copy; each caller gets a response that replays them with the original status, headers, `url`
  and `redirected`. When loadAuto moves to gltf/pbr, the cache hands each kept response over once and drops it, and
  when loadAuto returns it forgets everything. The same load now holds 104,867,300 B (one copy). Regression:
  `packages/gltf/test/auto.test.js` ("downloaded once and held once"; the declared-length move keeps the redirect URL).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: loadAuto on an engine with no GPU device reported gltf/pbr's error, not the light loader's reason (KB-GLTFA B17, gltf)

- **Repro (before):** `loadAuto` on an engine without WebGPU or the WebGL2 layer and a file with a base colour map:
  `gltf/textured` refused with `unsupported` (naming `install()` from `@margoengine/webgl2-compat`), `loadAuto` moved to
  gltf/pbr, which failed with `PBRModel requires WebGPU`, and the first reason was dropped.
- **Cause:** the move to gltf/pbr rethrew its error as it was.
- **Fix:** when gltf/pbr also refuses with `unsupported`, `loadAuto` throws an `unsupported` MargoError whose message is
  the light loader's reason followed by `gltf/pbr cannot load it here either: <gltf/pbr's message>`. The move itself is
  unchanged, so engines with a device still reach gltf/pbr (the existing "a texture on WebGL does too" test holds).
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/auto.test.js ("with no GPU device for gltf/pbr either ...").

### Fixed 2026-11-19: a node with a zero scale on any axis stopped the whole glTF load, in both loaders (KB-GLTFA B1, core + gltf)

- **Repro (before):** `parseGLTF(engine, doc, [bytes])` from `@margoengine/gltf` or `@margoengine/gltf/pbr` with
  `nodes: [{ mesh: 0, scale: [1, 0, 1] }]` threw `RangeError: Scale nonzero` (also `[0, 0, 0]`); a `matrix` with a zero
  column threw `RangeError: Singular glTF matrix`, and `@margoengine/animation` stopped on a zero scale key.
- **Cause:** core refused a zero scale (`Mesh.setScale`, the `scale` VectorRef and the Wasm kernel), and core's vertex
  shader and about 15 package shaders turned normals by the cofactor matrix times `sign(det)`, which is 0 for a
  flattened node, so the normal was zero and the lit colour NaN.
- **Fix:** 635e518ea7, 8a6317003a and 8c71da0556. Core, its kernel, the loaders, `@margoengine/scene` and the animation writers accept a zero scale;
  every cofactor stage uses `select(-1.0, 1.0, det >= 0.0)` and turns a zero normal into +Y; gltf/pbr writes the
  cofactor matrix as the normal matrix of a node with no inverse. Class check: tests/modern-zero-determinant-normals.test.js.
  What stays refused is in docs/limits.md ("Zero scale").

### Fixed 2026-11-19: glTF files the specification allows were refused, and failed textured loads leaked bitmaps (KB-GLTFA, gltf)

- **Repro (before):** a primitive without POSITION, `asset.version: '2.1'`, an OPAQUE `baseColorFactor` alpha below 1,
  an unused BLEND material, a GLB whose second buffer has no URI (accepted by `loadGLTF` only), a file over 64 MiB
  through `loadAuto`, a `206` reply with `Content-Range: bytes 0-65535/*` to `loadGLTFProgressive`, and three 30 MiB
  images through `loadGLTF` with `textured` (each read under the whole 64 MiB). A textured load that was aborted,
  refused, failed in `finish` or at upload, or lost one decode while another was in flight kept its `ImageBitmap`s
  open, and a failed upload left the `gltf-textured` plugin attached.
- **Cause:** checks stricter than glTF 2.0 sections 3.2, 3.6.1.2, 3.7.2.1 and 3.9.4; the light loader's size limits
  were `RangeError`s, not the `unsupported` refusal `loadAuto` moves on; bitmaps were closed only by `model.dispose`;
  the stream's Content-Range pattern wanted a numeric length; concurrent downloads checked the budget before any of
  them counted.
- **Fix:** 42b6839371 and the commit after it (B4, B5, B8 to B13, B15, B16 of the audit); a new optional
  `GLTFExtension.abandon(file)` releases what `load` held when a load fails.
- **Regression:** `packages/gltf/test/audit-gltfa.test.js`, `packages/gltf/test/auto.test.js` ("a file over the light
  loader 64 MiB goes to gltf/pbr"), `packages/gltf/test/progressive.test.js` ("a range reply whose complete length is *").

### Fixed 2026-11-19: views side by side in one target showed a stretched part of the voxel path tracer's image (KB-VPT-VIEW-RECT, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** `engine.render({ views })` with two views at `[0, 0, 0.5, 1]` and `[0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]` and a
  `VoxelPathTracer` attached: each view traced an image of the whole canvas's size through its own camera (whose aspect
  is its rectangle's) and drew it by canvas pixel, so the left view showed the left half of its image stretched over its
  rectangle and the right view the right half.
- **Cause:** the tracer sized its image from `PassContext.width` and `height` (the whole target) and its display shader
  mapped the fragment's target position over that size; neither read the view's rectangle (`PassContext.view.viewport`).
- **Fix:** the image is traced at the rectangle's size, and the display shader maps the pixel within the rectangle
  (the fragment position less the rectangle's origin, passed in the display uniform) to the image and to its depth.
  XR eyes, each drawn into its own texture, were not affected.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/views.test.js` ("views side by side in one target each trace and draw
  their own rectangle": image buffers of the rectangle's size and the rectangle in the display uniform; fails on the
  code before).

### Fixed 2026-11-19: on the WebGL2 layer an XR session with the voxel path tracer showed no traced image (KB-VPT-XR-VIEWS, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** `node scripts/composition-browser-tests.mjs --packages=voxel-pathtracer`: row c2-031
  (transitions + voxel-pathtracer + sky + vfx + xr) passed on WebGPU at 1x and 4x and failed on webgl2-compat 1x with
  "trace samples 0" (tests/composition/harness.ts, the checks after the XR session steps). Dev PC, RTX A6000, Edge 157,
  ANGLE Direct3D 11. Any frame drawing two views with different cameras (`engine.render({ views })`) did the same.
- **Cause (confirmed by a CPU probe, two views drawn in turn for 80 frames with `maxSamples: 6`):** the tracer kept one
  accumulation (buffers, key, sample count, epoch, route job, denoiser history) for one camera, so every view restarted
  the other's image. On WebGPU each view then traced its one sample a frame and never more (the probe's count stayed at
  1); on the WebGL2 route a trace runs across tasks and lands frames later, and the other view's restart dropped it
  first, so no sample ever landed (the count stayed at 0). The two views also shared one display uniform and one set of
  denoiser parameters, written twice in a frame and read by both draws.
- **Fix:** each view (`PassContext.view.id`; the plain frame is one too) keeps its own image: targets, frame and
  display uniforms, sample count, accumulation key, restart epoch, denoiser history and corner rays, route job, and its
  sums on the WebGL2 route under its own keys (`TraceRoute.release` frees them). `reset`, `setScene`, option changes and
  a device change restart every view. A view not drawn for 4 engine frames (`onPreUpdate` calls) is released with its
  buffers, so memory stays bounded by the views being drawn. `samplesPerFrame: 'auto'` paces once per engine frame.
  The composition harness waits, during the XR session too, until the tracer's samples have landed.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/views.test.js` (two alternating views reach `maxSamples` on WebGPU
  and on the WebGL2 route; a view no longer drawn frees its image buffers and route sums; `reset` and `setScene` reach
  every view; all fail on the code before).

### Fixed 2026-11-19: a fire front's smoke columns took no smoke look family (KB-VFX-FRONTSMOKE-LOOK1, vfx, scenes)

- **Repro (before):** `applySmokeSettings(front, SMOKE_LOOKS.animatedFeature)` on a `FireFront` wrote the smoke rows onto
  the front's own options (deleting its wind) and left its columns as built; timber-valley's look family gave its fire
  front the flame rows only, so its smoke never took the family.
- **Cause:** `applySmokeSettings` writes a column's whole state (heat and radius included) onto one options object. A
  front sets each column's heat and source radius from its segment every step and makes its columns after attach, so
  it could take neither the whole state nor a look given before its columns existed.
- **Fix:** a `FireFront` is a target of `applySmokeSettings` as it is of `applyFlameSettings`: its `setSmokeLook` keeps
  the look and writes it onto every column it has and makes later, every row but `heat` and `radius`; a row left out
  gives back what the front built the column with. `applyLookFamily`'s `smoke` part takes a front, and timber-valley
  gives its front as the smoke part.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/smoke.test.js` (KB-VFX-FRONTSMOKE-LOOK1, fails on the code before) and
  `packages/scenes/test/look-family.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-19: TAA's raster jitter restarted the voxel path tracer every frame (KB-VPT-TAA-RESTART, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** composition row c2-010 (taa + creative + voxel-pathtracer + lines + sprites) on webgl2-compat 1x:
  "trace samples 0" at tests/composition/harness.ts (`node scripts/composition-browser-tests.mjs
  --packages=voxel-pathtracer`); on WebGPU the row passed, but the tracer never held more than one sample under TAA.
- **Cause:** TAA hands later passes a wrapper camera whose matrix carries a new Halton offset each frame (its source
  camera under the shared symbol of packages/shared/temporal-camera.js). The tracer keyed accumulation on that matrix,
  so every frame was a camera move and a restart: one sample forever on WebGPU, and on the WebGL2 route, whose trace
  lands frames after it starts, every trace was dropped before it landed. The composition harness also checked the
  sample count two frames after the pipelines, before a route trace could land (c2-003 passed or failed by timing).
- **Fix:** the tracer's pass keys, traces and reprojects with `unjitteredCamera(c.camera)` (the same helper
  ProgressiveStill uses) and hands the raster camera back after it; it jitters its own pixels. The harness waits, with
  the pipelines, until the tracer's samples have landed (60 s limit). Rows c2-003 and c2-010 now pass on both backends
  at 1x and 4x.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/tracer.test.js` ("a temporal pass's raster jitter is no camera
  move": 8 jittered frames keep accumulating, a real move still restarts; fails on the code before).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: visual:check failed earth-phone; the earth baselines predated bloom's temporal firefly default (KB-VIS-EARTH-BLOOM1, tests/visual)

- **Repro (before):** `node scripts/visual-regression.js --only=earth` on main 796219d1df, RTX A6000, Edge
  157.0.4341.60: earth-phone changed 0.000911 (limit 0.0005), hot 0, max 1; earth-high 0.000339 and earth-light
  0.000425 passed under the limit. The same figures on `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, and on the workstation's AMD RDNA 2 iGPU
  (`MARGO_GPU=amd`, profile amd-rdna-2-msedge-157) earth-phone 0.000863. Every changed pixel is 1 level brighter, all
  on the sunlit half of the planet and the glow round it.
- **Cause:** 26451c21fb (KB-CABIN-BLOOM1) made `fireflies: 'temporal'` Bloom's default: a pixel whose energy the
  previous frame's coarsest level already held (a steady emitter) keeps the plain linear prefilter instead of the
  Karis 1/(1+luma) weight, so steady bright pixels keep their full glow (99.3% against 57% for a small flame in that
  commit's test). The earth demo's sunlit limb and city lights are steady, so their bloom gained energy. The commit
  did not re-record the earth views (recorded at d9fa86e5bc and 6a527e1bd9). Proof: the same tree with only the earth
  demo's Bloom given `fireflies: 'karis'` (the old prefilter) matches all three old baselines with changed 0 on the
  A6000 and on the AMD iGPU. No defect in Margo; a stale baseline after an intended change.
- **Fix:** the three earth views re-recorded with `visual:update -- --only=earth --runs=4` on nvidia-ampere-msedge-157
  and amd-rdna-2-msedge-157 (noise 0 in 4 runs each); docs/limits.md ("Earth visual baselines re-recorded") has the
  proof. The Arc laptop's intel-xe-2lpg-msedge-156 profile needs the same re-record on that laptop.
- **Regression:** the re-recorded baselines in tests/visual/profiles (a build without 26451c21fb's default fails
  earth-phone again); tests/visual-baselines.test.js checks the manifests.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the WebGL2 layer's sky route test read past the light buffer after the sky gained its ground (KB-ROUTES-SKYGROUND1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `npm test -w packages/webgl2-compat` on 31adbf4d0a and later: "Sky: the light projection runs on the
  GPU and adds the same terms in the same order" failed with "RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView".
- **Cause:** KB-SKY-FLOOR1 grew the projection's light buffer from 10 to 11 vec4f (light[10] is the ground's albedo and
  the sun's E / pi) in the kernel and its route, but the test still handed the CPU runner a 40-word buffer, so both
  kernels read light[10] out of bounds. The sky commit's gate ran sky's tests, not this one, which imports the sky source.
- **Fix:** the test hands 44 words and compares the route with the kernel word for word with the ground off (albedo 0)
  and on (albedo 0.2 and a sun term), so the ground terms the route adds are checked too.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/routes.test.js` ("Sky: the light projection ...").

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the WebGL2 layer ran the VFX update kernel of a simulation with events on the CPU tier (KB-VFX-EVENTS-CPU, vfx, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `planCompute({ source: routeShaders(events.simulation(simulationShader, { on: 'death' })).update, entryPoint: 'main' })`
  returned tier `cpu`, "an invocation reads back 'eventData' after storing to it"; with `on: 'collision'` it was
  "an invocation reads back 'particles' after storing to it". A frame of `new VFX({capacity: 600, rate: 200, events})`
  on the layer's route dispatched 1 kernel on the CPU tier (`update`, every slot in JavaScript); without events, 0.
- **Cause:** (1) the death edit stored the slot's event into this frame's half of `eventData` before the birth block
  read last frame's half of the same buffer, and the layer's analysis sees one buffer, not two halves; (2) the
  collision edit read the slot's generation, `particles[cold+1].w`, after the birth block had stored `particles[cold+1]`.
  A point draw reads its buffers as they were before the draw, so the layer must refuse any read after a store
  (W3C WGSL, "Memory Model": an invocation sees its own stores in program order).
- **Fix:** packages/vfx/src/events.ts keeps a raised event in the invocation (`raiseEvent`, private `eventPosition` and
  `eventVelocity`) and `storeEvents(i)` writes it to `eventData` once `update` has returned, in WebGPU's `main` and in
  the route's `update` entry (packages/vfx/src/compat.ts); the slot's generation is read once into a local before any
  store and follows the birth's store. The same values reach the same words, so the WebGPU output is unchanged. Work
  count: CPU-tier dispatches a frame on the route, 1 before and 0 after, for death and for collision events.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/route-loading.test.js` ("a frame of an effect with death events dispatches no kernel
  on the layer's CPU tier", the collision twin, and the death and collision rows of "no route kernel runs on the layer's
  CPU tier"); `packages/webgl2-compat/test/routes.test.js` (the events `update` plans as `scatter`).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the overcast sky lit every side alike, and no sky's ground lit surfaces facing down (KB-SKY-FLOOR1, sky)

- **Repro:** Wilbur on `@margoengine/scenes/dune-coast` (overcast), the eye white in ten bands from the upper lid to
  the lower: the lower white read 1.02 and 0.80 of its middle, against 0.58 and 0.49 in the CC0 eye photographs. A
  probe that drew the white with one light term at a time found the sky's irradiance equal toward up, down, forward and
  sideways: the day floor `lighting.ambient` of `DAY_PRESETS.overcast` (0.26, 0.27, 0.29) was above the sky's own
  spherical harmonics in every direction (raw zenith 0.75, forward 0.32 and nadir 0.03 of the floor), so the sky's
  light lost its direction (`node packages/sky/test/night-check.mjs day-presets`: a ceiling's underside got 0.69 of
  the ground's light overcast). Every sky had the opposite fault below: the light map's ground is a fixed dark colour,
  so a surface facing down got 0.04 of the ground's light at noon.
- **Cause:** the overcast floor, a design value, was set above the light the overcast sky gives (it stood in for the
  ground's light, which the sky never computed), and `skyIrradiance` takes the larger of the two per direction.
- **Fix:** the sky's projection (`packages/sky/src/project.ts`, and its WebGL2 route) adds the ground's light: a level
  Lambertian ground of albedo `lighting.ground` (default 0.2, the CIE and Perez daylight models' ground) lit by the
  sky's upper half and the engine sun, radiance rho (E_sky + E_sun) / pi over the lower half, which adds 2 pi and -pi
  of it to the first two coefficients (Liu and Jordan 1961, isotropic ground-reflected term). The overcast floor is
  now (0.03, 0.031, 0.033), under that light. Undersides read 0.18 to 0.21 of the ground in all four presets; the eye
  white's lower bands 0.81 and 0.60, its upper bands unchanged in shape.
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/night-check.mjs day-presets` (underside 0.1 to 0.35 of the ground in every
  preset) and `packages/sky/test/day-presets.test.js` (the overcast floor under its ground's light).
- **Limit:** reflections still show the sky map's dark ground below the horizon; a scene on bright sand sets
  `lighting.ground` itself (dune-coast keeps 0.2 until it does). Recorded in `docs/limits.md`.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: CameraBrain is no seek clock (KB-FILM-BRAIN1, cinematic)

- **Repro:** attach a `CameraBrain` with a `FocusTracker` stage, run 600 frames, then seek a fresh world to the same time
  with `@margoengine/cutscene/seek`: `seek` lists the brain as unseekable and the brain's blend, its cameras' stages and
  the focus pull start over from their first frame.
- **Cause:** `CameraBrain` has `onPreUpdate` but no `advanceTime`, and its update emits `change` and `blended`, which a
  seek step must not call (packages/cinematic/src/brain.ts). Found reviewing cinematic/lens.ts for KB-FILM-SCANGAP1.
- **Fix:** the brain's update is a step that queues its events and a live part that sends them after the step;
  `CameraBrain.advanceTime(delta)` runs the step and sends none, so `seek` replays the brain, its cameras' stages and
  their focus pulls (the FocusTracker review in scripts/film-time-reviewed.json now names it). A listener now reads the
  frame's own pose. Regression: packages/cinematic/test/brain-seek.test.js (1, 600 and 54,000 replayed steps with
  camera switches, a mid-blend disable and a noise stage equal a continuous run; fails on the old build, which has no
  `advanceTime`).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the film-time check missed a clock written `this.x = f(this.x + delta)` (KB-FILM-SCANGAP1, scripts; post, cinematic, transitions and others)

- **Repro:** widen scripts/check-film-time.mjs's `delta` rule to a field assigned from an expression that reads the same
  field and a delta (`this.elapsed = Math.min(1e7, this.elapsed + delta)`, `this.focus = goal + (this.focus - goal) *
  Math.exp(-rate * delta)`): 14 lines in files with no `advanceTime` that the check passes today, among them
  post/src/stylize.ts:95, cinematic/src/lens.ts:107-108, transitions/src/index.ts:159 and live.ts:283,
  studio/src/pathtrace.ts:177, tween/src/inertia.ts:196, voxel/src/query.ts:512, ragdoll/src/balance.ts:366,
  controls/src/walk.ts:453 and presentation.ts:633, ui/src/meters.ts:128, physics2d/src/physics.ts:272 and
  voxel-net/src/client.ts:358.
- **Cause:** the rule's second form matches only `this.x = (this.x + ... delta`, with the field first inside the
  brackets; a clamp, an ease toward a goal or a decay wraps it and passes. Found while fixing KB-CHECKS-WAITS-FILMTIME1.
- **Fix:** the rule's second form is any field set from an expression that reads the same field and a delta, in any
  order and wrapped in any call (tests/film-time.test.js, a test of each form and of what is not a clock). Of the 14
  lines, Stylize's wave clock gains `advanceTime` (packages/post/test/stylize-seek.test.js: 1, 600 and 54,000 replayed
  steps equal a continuous run to the bit); physics2d and controls walk were already reviewed; the other ten files are
  reviewed in scripts/film-time-reviewed.json with their reasons (a camera stage, interactive controls, physics on
  hold, the still's idle timer, transitions over a frozen frame, a drag fling, UI widgets that seek already replays, a
  player controller, network prediction). The review of cinematic/lens.ts found KB-FILM-BRAIN1.

- **Repro:** any `@margoengine/scenes/dune-coast` frame with the grass in view past about 20 m, rendered at MSAA 1:
  `@margoengine/headless` `speckle` read 64 to 198 ppm against its bound of 50 (round 8: face 121.4, close 133.5,
  sunny 197.8), nearly all on the grass band between 20 and 230 m. A bare field of the same grass to 230 m at
  480 x 270 without MSAA (`packages/scatter/test/grass-pixel.browser.mjs`) read 4,902 ppm.
- **Cause:** `GrassScatter` (`packages/scatter/src/grass.ts`) widened a blade by a fixed share of distance that did not
  know the pixel, and drew every blade opaque. The leaves are 1.6 cm at the root and taper to a point, so past about
  20 m most of a blade is under a pixel and rasterized as broken runs and lone pixels; a pixel floor with a hashed keep
  (898 ppm) and then coverage-blended middle and far rings (242 ppm) still left opaque near blades with stepped edges,
  thin curved tips widened along the wrong axis, and far blades only a pixel or two tall.
- **Fix:** every ring is drawn by prefiltered coverage (`packages/scatter/src/cover.ts`): a blade is widened by the
  filter's radius across its screen axis (perpendicular to its spine and the eye), and each pixel takes the share of a
  tent filter the true strip covers as alpha (Gupta and Sproull 1981; Chan and Durand 2005), blended by over (Porter
  and Duff 1984). A blade under 8 pixels tall turns to the two-pixel tent over 4 pixels (prefiltered far vegetation,
  Bruneton and Neyret 2012). The near ring is split (`Scatter.coverRing` 'split'): each blade's core, a filter radius in
  from its edges, is opaque and writes depth, then the whole blade is blended over it. A lit stage whose varyings are
  not named `i` (PbrMaterial's `varyings`) is now covered too. The bare field reads 0 ppm on WebGPU and 7.8 on the
  WebGL2 layer (diffuse and PBR), mean luma within 0.31 codes of the 4 x 4 supersampled view.
- **Regression:** `packages/scatter/test/grass.test.js` (the split and covered stages, the tent sums) and
  `packages/scatter/test/grass-pixel.browser.mjs` (under 50 ppm, mean within 2 codes, both backends).
- **Limit:** a covered ring writes no depth, so a mesh drawn after the scatter pass behind far grass paints over it;
  blending is in the target's space (linear with post, display-encoded without). Recorded in `docs/limits.md`.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: a shot's page loaded twice and its first load's fetches aborted ("Failed to fetch") (KB-SHOT-DOUBLELOAD1, tools/shot)

- **Repro:** any `tools/shot/cli.mjs` run on a page that fetches while it loads: Wilbur's shot log printed
  `[vite] (client) [Unhandled error] TypeError: Failed to fetch` at the page's `fetch(ccURL)` before the first frame.
- **Cause:** `tools/shot/render.mjs` opened the browser with `openBrowser({ startPath: '/' + page.path })`, which loads
  the page (with no shot query) to probe the hardware; `renderOnce` then loaded it again with the shot's query, which
  aborted the first load's requests and built the whole scene once for nothing.
- **Fix:** `openBrowser` takes `openPath`, the page it first loads (default `startPath`), while the dev server still
  pre-bundles `startPath`'s imports; `openShotPage` opens on `tools/shot/blank.html`, so the shot's page loads once.
  Regression: `tests/shot-page-load.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: five corpus kernels took ANGLE's Direct3D 11 compiler 38 to 98 s each on the WebGL2 layer (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1, robot-planning, lightmap, sciviz)

- **Repro:** time each pipeline of `packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus-draw-browser.mjs` cold (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11,
  RTX A6000): robot-planning's three clearance kernels (`main`, FRAMES 3, 7 and 14) took 89.5, 85.4 and 80.9 s,
  lightmap's `bake` 48.4 s and sciviz's mapped volume (`vertex`/`fragment`) 38.3 s (2026-11-18, other lanes on the
  machine; 46 to 135 s on earlier runs). The time is the program link, so an app on the layer on Windows waited that
  long, cold, for each of these pipelines.
- **Cause:** fxc, the HLSL compiler ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end calls, inlines every call and unrolls every loop it
  can count, so each call site is a copy of its callee's whole call tree, once per unrolled trip. Counted with a
  call-graph walk that does the same (`scripts/support/wgsl-inline.mjs`): the robot kernel called `measure` from two
  loops, `gjk` from `measure` and the hull field, `support` six times a GJK step and `closerEdge` sixteen times a
  `reduce`, inside a 64-round loop the compiler could count: 528 copies of `support` and 4,096 of `closerEdge`,
  3,409,747 characters of function body (FRAMES 7). The bake called the BVH walk from six sites (`bvhAny` twice in
  `directLight`, `directLight` and `bvhClosest` twice each): six walks of an open loop over a node stack. The
  mapped volume's inverse map (a 32-step bisection per axis, 24 Newton steps over 8 corners) and the gradient's
  three-axis sample loop were all countable: 21 inverse maps, 168 corner reads, 310,068 characters.
- **Fix:** each costly function has one call site, in a loop whose bound the shader reads, in its own package.
  robot-planning: one `measure` over every shape and collider then the pairs, one `gjk` for point sets and hull cells,
  one `supportPair` (one `support`) per GJK step with the seed direction and first vertex as steps 0 and 1, one face
  and one edge test in `reduce`, one `fieldRead` per segment; every fixed bound adds `params.zero`, a uniform that is
  always 0. lightmap: one `directLight`, `bvhAny` and `bvhClosest` call for every path vertex (vertex 0 is the
  texel). sciviz: every fixed bound adds `u.zero.x` (floats 44 to 47 of the uniform, always 0) and the gradient reads
  its six samples through one call; the volume writes only the first four of the eight classification floats, since
  the rest (the voxel spacing) would land in `u.zero` and run the Newton loop for as many steps as the spacing (a grid
  in 1e20 units hung the GPU, DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG, before it landed). The same operations run in the same order.
- **Evidence:** same output: the old and new robot kernels on the CPU WGSL interpreter give 1,088 of 1,088 gaps
  bit-identical (mixed robot with self-collision, an early-stop batch and a baked field); the lightmap bake gives 3,072
  of 3,072 irradiance floats bit-identical on WebGPU (3 bounces and AO); the mapped volume draws the same bytes in four
  scenes (shaded, gradient-classified, MIP, spherical) and in two grids of voxel spacing 4 and 4e6. Work: inlined function body (the walk above) 3,409,747 to
  30,566 characters (robot, FRAMES 7), 40,480 to 15,540 (bake; walks 6 to 2), 310,068 to 37,631 (mapped volume;
  inverse maps 21 to 6). Cold link, before and after (same machine, same day, busy): robot 89.5 to 6.3 s, 85.4 to
  7.2 s and 80.9 to 7.2 s; bake 48.4 to 6.7 s; mapped volume 38.3 to 11.9 s. The corpus holds the new sources of the
  five modules (the same pipelines), and robot-planning keeps its three corpus-draw parts.
- **Sources:** Microsoft, "Function Declaration Syntax" (HLSL `inline` is the default: one copy of the body per call),
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-function-syntax ; Microsoft, "for
  Statement" (`unroll` copies the body, `loop` keeps flow control; with neither the compiler unrolls a loop it can
  count), https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-for ; Robert W. Scheifler, "An
  Analysis of Inline Substitution for a Structured Programming Language", CACM 20(9), 1977,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/359810.359830 (code grows with the call sites of each callee, multiplied down the call
  graph); Jack J. Dongarra and A. R. Hinds, "Unrolling Loops in Fortran", Software: Practice and Experience 9(3), 1979,
  https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.4380090307 (an unrolled body is copied once per trip); Google, ANGLE project, "ANGLE"
  (GLSL ES translated to HLSL and compiled with the D3D compiler on Direct3D 11),
  https://chromium.googlesource.com/angle/angle/+/main/README.md .
- **Regression:** `packages/robot-planning/tests/gpu.test.js` "the kernel calls each costly function from one site, in
  loops no compiler can count (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1)", `packages/lightmap/tests/gpu.test.js` "the bake kernel holds one
  walk per kind of ray (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1)", `packages/sciviz/tests/curvilinear.test.js` "the mapped volume shader has
  no loop a compiler can count and one sample call per gradient (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1)" (each fails on the old source:
  528 `support` copies, 6 walks, 6 gradient samples), and the class check
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus-inline.test.js`: no corpus entry point outside the voxel path tracer inlines past
  250,000 characters or 2 copies of a function holding an open loop and an array of its own (fails on the old corpus).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: `webgl2-compat test:browser` needed more than the 10 minute GPU step limit, on main too (KB-COMPAT-CORPUSTIME1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs --max=10 -- node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --no-build
  --select=webgl2-compat/test:browser`: browser-check and the GLSL corpus passed, then `test/corpus-draw-browser.mjs`
  was killed at the limit. Run alone it took 487 to 510 s (dev PC, RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11, quiet), against the
  87 s `scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs` recorded for the whole step (2026-10-31).
- **Cause:** five recorded pipelines take ANGLE's Direct3D shader compiler 46 to 98 s each, 374 s of the 487
  (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1, above): robot-planning's three clearance kernels (277 s, recorded 2026-11-14 in 3511f7ed34),
  lightmap's `bake` (51 s) and sciviz's mapped volume (46 s, both recorded 2026-11-10 in 8ea7f79c9e). The other
  1,343 pipelines take 113 s. The work grew too (624 render and 396 compute pipelines on 2026-10-31, 830 and 518 now,
  counted from the corpus at each commit), but the five kernels are most of it. One step drew the whole corpus, so
  each heavy kernel recorded made it longer, and nothing split it.
- **Fix:** the draw runs in five parts, one package script each, chosen by `--part`
  (`packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus-draw-parts.mjs`): `test:browser` (browser-check, the GLSL corpus and the 830
  render pipelines), `test:browser:compute` (514 compute pipelines and the invalid one) and
  `test:browser:compute-robot-planning-1` to `-3` (one clearance kernel each). Every pipeline still runs in full and
  the step limit is not raised. Measured on the dev PC (busy, other lanes on the GPU), native and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`:
  247 and 251 s, 86 and 94 s, then 123, 133 and 149 s and 106, 100 and 76 s, each a pass, against the one step killed
  at 600 s before. A first split with the three kernels in one part passed natively in 355 s and was killed at 600 s
  under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` on the busy machine, so each kernel has its own part. A package whose kernels take the
  compiler minutes goes in `OWN_COMPUTE_PART` with its kernel count; a kernel beyond it fails the test and the run.
- **Regression:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus-draw-parts.test.js: the parts together are every distinct corpus
  pipeline, counted on their own, each in one part; no part is empty; each part has its own package script running
  only it, and no other script draws the corpus (fails on the old tree: no parts, one script).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: FM7 ran 1.25 times Albini 1976's chart and Anderson 1982, and FM13 +4.8 percent over Anderson (KB-FIRE-FM7, vfx fire-front)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/vfx/test/fire-front.test.js`: at 8 percent dead, 100 percent live and 5 mi/h midflame
  `fireBehaviour(FUEL_MODELS.FM7)` gave 25.9 chains/h against Anderson 1982's 20, and 1.25 to 1.29 times Albini 1976
  chart 7 (INT-30, read by pixel) at the chart's three readable moisture pairs; FM13 gave 14.15 against 13.5.
- **Cause:** two parts. (1) A data difference: FM7's live surface-area-to-volume ratio was INT-30 table 7's 1,550 1/ft;
  the standard fuel model of Andrews 2018 (RMRS-GTR-371, table 8a, the model as BehavePlus computes it) is 1,500, with a
  characteristic ratio of 1,552 (ours was 1,562). `FUEL_MODELS.FM7` now holds 1,500. (2) The rest is the reference, not
  the code. `fuelBed` and `windFactor` were checked equation by equation against Rothermel 1972 (INT-115) with Albini's
  changes (INT-30 appendix III) and against Andrews 2018 (sections 3 and 4, the same equations), and reproduce Andrews
  2018's computed values: table 8b's characteristic ratio, bulk density and relative packing ratio for all 13 models and
  table 22's wind factors (FM2 20.48 and 72.84 against 20.5 and 72.8; FM9 12.95 and 42.70 against 12.9 and 42.7).
  Albini's nomographs are a 1974 FIREMODS run (INT-30 page 88, its other revisions called "inconsequential"); Rothermel
  1983 (INT-143, appendix A) reprints the same curves with midflame wind labels rather than recomputing them, and its FM7
  chart has no 100 percent live curve below 13 percent dead moisture. Its wind lines, read by pixel on 2026-11-18, give
  1 + phi at 5 mi/h of 15.7 for FM2 (ours 15.67), 17.2 to 18.3 for FM5 (ours 21.6) and 17.6 to 19.3 for FM7 (ours
  21.3): a factor of about 0.85 on phi that keeps Rothermel's B exponent and that no single characteristic ratio
  explains. The chart's heat per unit area axis puts FM7's residence time at sigma = 1,584 +- 2 percent, so it is not
  the particle size. Anderson's FM7 (20 chains/h, 4.9 ft) is one point of that run: 0.79 times our rate at our reaction
  intensity gives his flame length. The 1974 values stay as an accepted reference difference (docs/limits.md), compared
  with FM7 at INT-30's own 1,550 1/ft.
- **Regression:** packages/vfx/test/fire-front.test.js "the 13 fuel models against Andrews 2018 tables 8b and 22" (each
  model's characteristic ratio within 1 1/ft, bulk density within 0.005 lb/ft^3, packing ratio within 0.01, the four wind
  factors within 0.5 percent; the old FM7 fails at 1,561.9 against 1,552) and "fuel models hold the values" (FM7's live
  1,500). The Anderson, chart 7 and chart 13 tests keep their bounds, with FM7 at INT-30's input.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the townsman's four-in-hand read as a plain block (KB-HUMANS-KNOT1, humans)

- **Repro:** `fitOutfit` of `townsman-1910`, the tie at a medium shot (dressed6 in the asset library): the knot a smooth
  tapered wedge with no band or dimple. On the test body its middle rose 1.7 mm from 20 to 60 percent up the knot and
  0.8 mm from 10 to 30.
