- **Still open:** ribbons, mesh particles, billboards drawn through an order-independent pass and core's blended meshes
  register no veil yet (docs/limits.md); SSGI and SSR under blended coverage are not measured.
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/smoke-ao.browser.mjs` (in the package's `test:gpu`, WebGPU and `--compat`).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: smoke in the Fauld tunnels' dusty air read as flat black shapes (KB-FAULD-SMOKEBLACK1, scenes)

- **Repro (before):** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/fauld-fr096.json --stills --out <folder>`: black blobs
  and a black band across the upper half; fr093 black blotches in the doorway, fr091 a dark patch over the flames.
- **Cause:** the scene never added its smoke to its `VolumetricFog`. The fog composites over the opaque scene before
  the particles draw, so each puff covered the lit dust glow with the smoke's own dim colour and none of the air in
  front of it. In fr096 that glow is nearly all the light of the middle of the frame (without the fog the walls there
  are black), so smoke tens of metres off read as holes in it. Ruled out first: occlusion (KB-SSAO-BLENDVEIL1 above,
  0.9 levels at most) and the local shadow maps (white puffs stayed black without them).
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/scenes/fauld-tunnels` calls `fog.add(smoke.effect)` for every smoke column: it draws after the
  fog's composite, each puff behind the in-scattered light and transmittance between the camera and it (Wronski,
  "Volumetric Fog", SIGGRAPH 2014 Advances in Real-Time Rendering,
  https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2014/; premultiplied composite as `VolumetricFog.add` documents).
- **After:** pixels at or under luma 1.5: fr096 21,705 to 0, fr093 17,112 to 0 (960 x 540, RTX A6000, WebGPU); fr092
  unchanged (5 pixels by over 4 levels).
- **Weak spots:** fr096's smoke is now only a faint soft shade in the haze: the columns in view are tens of metres off,
  and none curls past the casings as the shot list asks. Fog-added smoke draws before the flames and embers, so a flame
  behind a column is not dimmed by it (docs/limits.md).
- **Regression:** `packages/scenes/test/fauld-smoke-fog.mjs` (every smoke column is one the fog draws, and fr096 has
  under 200 black pixels: 4 unfogged and 23,371 black before).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the dune coast's grass blades showed black fragments (KB-SCENES-GRASSBLACK1, post and scatter)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --views=camp-buildings`: near and
  middle tufts carried black dashes and dots along the blades (6,400 near-black pixels below the horizon against the
  `occlusion: 0` frame, RTX A6000, WebGPU).
- **Cause:** two, both in the occlusion composite, `scene - ambient * (1 - visibility)`. (1) The ambient replay holds
  the light of the surface that owns a pixel's depth. Covered grass (KB-SCATTER-SUBPIXEL1) blends over the sand without
  owning the depth, so the replay held the sand's whole ambient light under a blade that left only part of the sand in
  the pixel, and the composite took more light than the pixel held, down to black. (2) KB-SSAO-LONEPIXEL1 below: the
  sand pixels in one-pixel gaps between blades read as shut in.
- **Fix:** `packages/shared/ambient-veil.js`: `SSAO` and `GTAO` draw each registered veil over the replay target after
  core's replay, and `Scatter` registers one that draws its covered parts again with the same pose and coverage, black
  and blended, so the light there is multiplied by one less each blade's alpha (the revealage of McGuire and Bavoil,
  "Weighted Blended Order-Independent Transparency", JCGT 2013, https://jcgt.org/published/0002/02/09/, over Porter and
  Duff's over, SIGGRAPH 1984). Screen-space occlusion at the edges of binary-coverage depth is also McGuire and Mara,
  "Phenomenological Transparency", IEEE TVCG 2017
  (https://research.nvidia.com/sites/default/files/pubs/2017-03_Phenomenological-Transparency/McGuire2017Transparency.pdf).
  The blades' own colour is not darkened: replaying their ambient light too was tried and left 274 near-black pixels,
  their one-pixel normals being noise.
- **After:** 6 near-black pixels of 6,400 in the same still; the camp occlusion check reads mean 196.3 against 199.0
  open, 10.4 percent of pixels darker.
- **Regression:** `packages/scatter/test/grass-ao.browser.mjs` (no pixel under its colour without occlusion times its
  visibility: 12,231 pixels before, 0 after, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).

### Fixed 2026-11-27: SSAO and GTAO read a one-pixel gap between two nearer surfaces as shut in (KB-SSAO-LONEPIXEL1, post)

- **Repro (before):** a wall seen through slits one pixel wide between slats 1.5 units in front of it, past the
  occlusion radius: GTAO visibility 0.457 mean, 0.251 least in the slit pixels; SSAO 0.694 and 0.595.
- **Cause:** the extract pass builds a normal from the neighbour with the smaller depth step. A pixel whose two
  horizontal neighbours are both nearer (a slit, or in reverse a one-pixel wire) has no surface neighbour on that axis,
  so the normal faced along the view's side.
- **Fix:** `packages/post/src/shaders.ts`: where both neighbours of an axis lie on the same side of the pixel in depth,
  each over four pixel widths away (a plane's depth is monotonic along a screen line), the axis step is the pixel's own
  at constant depth. Neighbour choice as before otherwise (J. Turanszki, "Improved normal reconstruction from depth",
  2019; five taps an axis, as in https://atyuwen.github.io/posts/normal-reconstruction, would also settle wider gaps at
  four more depth reads a pixel and was not needed here).
- **After:** GTAO 0.999 mean, 0.995 least; SSAO 0.823 and 0.797 (its range check still counts the slats a little).
- **Regression:** `packages/post/test/ssao-silhouette-browser.mjs`, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: ambient occlusion left pale pixels along grass blade edges (KB-SCATTER-AOFRINGE1, scatter and post)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --shots=<file>` with the shots
  `view=camp-buildings` and `view=camp-buildings&occlusion=0`; enlarge the grass at the lower left (pixels 370 to 470
  across, 975 to 1055 down): with occlusion on, pale one-pixel outlines ran along blades over the shaded sand at their
  feet. Counted as pixels over 8 codes of luma above their 5 x 5 median with occlusion and not without, lower 45 percent
  of the frame: 41,520 when filed (mean 19.6 codes; 9,408 under `weather=clear&hour=9`), 20,673 (mean 18.5) and 6,513
  on the main of the fix. RTX A6000, WebGPU.
- **Cause:** a covered blade's depth is written where its coverage passes a hash (KB-SCENES-DUNE-GTAO1), and that pixel
  is mostly sand wherever the coverage is low. The ambient replay, depth-equal against the blade's depth, held none of
  the sand's light there, and the occlusion was worked out at the blade's depth, so the sand's share was not darkened
  while the bare pixels beside it were.
- **Ruled out (same view, measured when filed):** writing no covered depth at all leaves 3,307 pale pixels but also
  takes 90 percent of the darkening grass causes (mean 6.07 to 0.60 codes); no depth on the edges of blades wide enough
  to have an opaque core leaves 36,390 with 11 percent less darkening; a depth threshold of 0.5 or 0.75 leaves 39,255
  and 37,449. A second depth read alone fixes nothing: the replay must hold the light under the blades too.
- **Fix:** while `SSAO` or `GTAO` reads the surface under covered strips (`wantUnder`, packages/shared/ambient-veil.js),
  `Scatter` holds its covered depth back from its colour pass to `<name>:cover-depth` (order 1.52). Between them
  `ssao:under` (1.51) copies the depth under the blades and replays that surface's ambient light with the blades'
  veils; `ssao:covered` (1.53) copies the blades' depth. At extraction a pixel whose depth is a blade's that nothing
  drew over takes the depth under it as its centre, its normal and position come from there and its ambient light is
  that replay, while the kernels search occluders in the scene's depth, blades included (layered depth images: Shade,
  Gortler, He and Szeliski, SIGGRAPH 1998, https://doi.org/10.1145/280814.280882; multi-layer screen-space occlusion:
  Bavoil and Sainz, SIGGRAPH 2009 Talks, https://history.siggraph.org/?p=148934; Mara, McGuire, Nowrouzezahrai and
  Luebke, HPG 2016, https://doi.org/10.2312/hpg.20161195). A frame with no covered blade runs the passes and bindings
  of before.
- **After:** the dune coast view above 6,297 pale pixels (mean 11.8 codes), mean darkening 6.07 to 7.32 codes; clear
  sky 4,132. Regression test `packages/scatter/test/grass-ao-fringe.browser.mjs` (`npm run test:browser:grass-ao-fringe`
  in the scatter package), 320 x 240, before to after: GTAO 4,226 to 1,096 (WebGL2 layer 4,240 to 1,036), SSAO 2,038
  to 155 (2,465 to 448), bounds 1,536 and 921; the grass darkens about 45,000 pixels (31,000 before; bound 2,304); a
  view with no blade is byte-identical to one without grass, and its hash matches the build before the fix on all four
  runs. `tests/ambient-veil.test.js` checks the handshake.
- **Weak spots:** the pale pixels left are no more frequent on blade-depth pixels than elsewhere (279 of 1,096 in the
  GTAO run, against 21,856 of 76,800 pixels): the pixel-scale variation of the occlusion the hashed blade depth casts,
  which the blur only averages. The blades themselves are still not darkened (see docs/limits.md). An `SSAOSource`
  model under a blade's depth pixel gives its ambient light to the under replay but its normal comes from depth.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the wind left no mark on the dune coast's sand (KB-SCENES-SCOUR1, terrain and scenes)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --shots=<file>` with a camera
  round the sheds (`cam` and `aim`): the sand ran level into every wall and no clump of grass had a tail of sand, in an
  11 m/s wind.
- **Cause:** no package shaped sand round obstacles, and the ground mesh's 2.15 m cells could not hold a form that small.
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/terrain/scour` (`windScour`, `refinedHeightfieldGeometry`); the dune coast's `scour` setting
  (default 1) shapes the ground round the sheds and behind grass clumps near the camp and the rail.
- **Weak spots:** under the default grey sky the forms read faintly (they read clearly under `weather: 'clear'` with a
  low sun); only the sheds and grass near the camp carry them, not the rail, the rest of the flat or the big dunes; the
  grass stays on the coarse grid, so fresh sand buries some blade feet by up to the dune's height; depths and cross
  profiles are not measured values.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/scour.test.js` and `packages/scenes/test/scenes.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the dune coast's sand carried no footprints (KB-SCENES-PRINTS1, terrain and scenes)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/scenes/test/dune-coast-still.mjs --w=1920 --h=1080 --views=camp-buildings`: the
  sand between the camp and the rail was untrodden, where LC-W86-15 and LC-W86-38 show it walked over.
- **Cause:** `TerrainDeformation` took only a clipmap `Terrain`; the scene's ground is a mesh with `TerrainColors`, its
  cells 2.15 m wide, so no print could be pressed in it.
- **Fix:** `TerrainDeformation` attaches to a ground mesh (core's standard shader, `openMeshBlock`), lays walking
  trails (`walk`) and keeps prints under a moving camera (`persist`); the dune coast's `footprints` setting (default 1)
  treads them between the sheds, to the rail and along it. Parallax occlusion mapping after Tatarchuk, I3D 2006
  (https://doi.org/10.1145/1111411.1111423); gait means of Murray, Drought and Kory, J. Bone Joint Surg. 46-A, 1964, as
  tabled at https://ouhsc.edu/bserdac/dthompso/web/gait/KNMATICS/stride.htm.
- **Weak spots:** prints are shading, with no shadow of their own and no broken sand round them; the ripples' colour
  bands still cross a print (their relief does not); at 20 m and eye height a print is about a pixel tall.
- **Regression:** `packages/terrain/test/deform-mesh.browser.mjs` and `packages/terrain/test/deform.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-27: the dune-coast scene did not yet look like the 1903 photographs (KB-SKY-OVERCAST1, KB-SCENES-GRASS1, KB-TERRAIN-SAND2, KB-WATER-SURF1; sky, scenes, terrain, water)

### Fixed 2026-11-18: the WebGL2 layer allocated kilobytes of JavaScript heap every frame (KB-COMPAT-FRAMEALLOC1, webgl2-compat, culling, shadows, compute)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/frame-alloc-browser.mjs --no-check` (the check draws its scenes on the
  layer under that flag): median bytes per steady frame, layer against the native floor, were basic 15,652 / 340,
  instanced 12,684 / 292, shadowed 154,856 / 860, post 155,712 / 1,528 and dynamic 497,716 / 396. Every byte is
  garbage the collector sweeps later, a stutter on the phones and old laptops the layer is for.
  `--profile --source` names the functions.
- **Cause, by package:** culling's CPU routes (src/compat.ts), which replace its compute kernels on the layer, called
  Math.hypot per row (V8 boxes its arguments into an array: 484 KB a frame in the dynamic scene), made a subarray view
  per kept record, a forEach closure per frame and a closure around the shape test, and the box shape's CPU test made
  six arrays per instance. The layer's own encoder and draw path (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts) builds
  string keys, iterators, closures, arrays and Maps per pass and per draw (a profile also names shadows' caster draw
  and core's draw, where V8 inlines the layer's recording calls), and the layer's compute runtime adds its own per
  dispatch.
- **Fixed so far:** culling (its routes allocate nothing: dynamic scene 497,716 to 17,840 B on the layer; regression
  packages/culling/test/compat-alloc.test.js, which fails on the old routes with 15,552 to 42,284 B a call). The
  layer's replay of a steady draw (part 2): the GL state cache compares numbers in slots instead of template-string
  keys, each pipeline works out its target blend and mask state once, the texture plan reuses arrays and no Map is
  cleared per draw; a draw went from 1,352 B (1,360 B indexed) to 0 B (regression
  packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js). Median bytes per frame on the layer after it: basic 15,652 to
  7,224, instanced 12,684 to 6,296, shadowed 154,860 to 74,912, post 155,716 to 81,444, dynamic 17,840 to 8,716.
  Passes and queue writes (part 3): subresources and framebuffers are found by identity, one pass state is reused,
  and writeBuffer hands bufferSubData a range of the caller's array; a pass went from 3,281 B to 0 B and a write to
  0 B (same regression test). Median bytes per frame after it: basic 2,824, instanced 2,252, shadowed 36,004,
  post 28,392, dynamic 3,788.
  Command recording (part 4): an encoder's commands are a tape (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/tape.ts: an opcode
  and its numbers in typed arrays, its objects in an array) instead of a closure each, the pass descriptor snapshot,
  the use list and the tape go back to the device's pool once the command buffer has replayed, and a default `{}`
  descriptor is one shared object; a one-draw frame (encoder, pass, bind group, buffers, finish, submit) went from
  2,418 B to 603 B (regression packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js, `encode`, and test/tape.test.js).
  The queue (part 5): `submit` reads an array by index and keeps its list of command buffers between submits (a list
  set to length 0 and refilled, and the iterator of a for-of, were garbage each submit), `flushPresents` keeps an
  array instead of copying and clearing a Set, and a canvas changes the device's `shown` set only when the showing
  device changes; the one-draw frame went from 603 B to 188 B, the three objects WebGPU returns each call (regression
  packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js bound 192 B, and test/queue-paths.test.js). Median bytes per
  frame after it (measured with the profile): basic 656, dynamic 1,128.
  Compute (part 6): a compute pass is on the tape (its pipeline, bind groups and dispatches replay through reused
  slots), each dispatch draw's uniforms are fields of its record and one function writes them, the target slice
  views and word-texture views are made once, a storage group reads its rows by index and a mirror's helper program is
  kept; a pass of one dispatch went from 2,347 B (fragment tier) and 3,139 B (scatter tier) to 202 B, its encoder,
  compute pass encoder and command buffer (regression packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js,
  `dispatchTexture` and `dispatchBuffer`, and test/tape.test.js). Median bytes per frame after it: shadowed 3,668,
  post 5,892.
  Framebuffers (part 7): the post scene's sampled multisampled depth made a new resolved-copy subresource (a key string,
  closures, a view) every frame, so every frame rebuilt a framebuffer's attachments; no GL object was made, so it was a
  rebuild and not a leak (createFramebuffer, deleteFramebuffer and createTexture counted 0 over 60 frames). The renderbuffer and
  resolved-copy subresources are now made once, a mip level's size is read without an array (`levelWidth`, `levelHeight`,
  `levelDepth`), and `blit` allocates nothing. Regression packages/webgl2-compat/test/framebuffers-browser.mjs
  (the device's framebuffer() builds over 60 steady post frames: more than 0 before, 0 now). Median bytes per frame after it:
  post 2,176 (from 5,892).
  Copies and closures (part 8): `copyBufferToBuffer` and `copyTextureToTexture` are tape opcodes with their regions as
  numbers (they made a closure and two descriptor copies each, and the replay made arrays for origins and sizes), the
  encoder's `copyBufferToBuffer` reads its two overloads into plain variables, a copy out of a CPU-shadowed buffer writes
  a range and makes no view, a copy that waits behind query results lives in a method of its own, the canvas's
  `getCurrentTexture` hands `setTimeout` one callback made once, a compute buffer's word textures are made in a method
  of their own (the closure it holds cost every call a context) and the shadows package's nearest-depth route walks its
  dispatches by index. Regressions packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js (`copyBuffer` 350 B before, `copyTexture`
  1,072 B before, both 145 B now, an encoder and a command buffer) and packages/shadows/test/compat-alloc.test.js (the
  route 192 B a call before, 0 B). Median bytes per frame after it, against the native floor: basic 388 (340),
  instanced 424 (292), shadowed 988 (860), post 2,128 (1,528), dynamic 860 (396).
  Part 9 (2026-11-17): a float colour clear passes a `Float32Array` (WebGL read a JS array of fractional doubles through
  one heap number each, 36 B a pass), a buffer that keeps a CPU copy reuses the view of its last write window when the
  range and staging array repeat (a view a write, 60 B), an indirect draw or dispatch reads its words from the CPU copy
  with no sliced buffer or typed array (336 B a draw before, 0 now), and a command buffer and a command encoder keep
  their flags in one field (36 B to 24 B each; the tape knows its pool). Regression
  packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js (`drawIndirect`, `writeStorage`; the first read 336 B on the old code).
  Median bytes per frame after it, against the native floor: basic 332 (340), instanced 308 (292), shadowed 920 (860),
  post 1,976 (1,528), dynamic 344 (396). Basic and dynamic are within their floors.
  Part 10 (2026-11-18): the objects WebGPU hands back each call are one field (two for an encoder and a command
  buffer), as a browser's 16 B wrappers are: a label is the prototype's `''` unless one is given, an encoder and a
  compute pass reach the device through the tape's pool (`TapePool.device`) and a compute pass keeps whether it set a
  pipeline on the tape. A view made with no descriptor (core's view of the canvas texture, every frame) shares its
  texture's default range (`ViewRange`): 80 B a view to 16 B, a browser's size. A texture's copies are found by a scan
  of their format, target, layer and alias instead of a key string per lookup (124 B a frame in the post scene), and
  the pass state's stand-in list keeps its length, so a pass of fewer targets no longer trims it and the next grows
  it. Regression packages/webgl2-compat/test/replay-alloc.test.js (`view` 160 B, `sampledLayer` 232 B and `passMix`
  16 B a call on the old code, now 32, 0 and 0 B on Node 26; `encode` 146 B to 113 B, a dispatch 161 B to 113 B, a
  copy 105 B to 80 B, under tightened bounds) and test/tape.test.js (labels and default ranges read and set as their
  own). `scripts/frame-alloc-browser.mjs` now installs the layer itself under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (it ran native WebGPU
  in that mode before, so its compatibility leg tested nothing of the layer; it is off
  `scripts/support/compat-owed.json`). Median bytes per frame on the layer (Edge 156, RTX A6000), before part 10 and
  after, against the native floor: basic 332 to 252 (340), instanced 308 to 228 (292), shadowed 920 to 800 (860),
  post 1,912 to 1,464 (1,528), dynamic 344 to 264 (396). Every scene is within its native floor; the check holds the
  layer to them on every `MARGO_COMPAT=1` run.
- **Left (not a defect):** the layer's present hands the page canvas one ImageBitmap a frame
  (`transferToImageBitmap`, 16 B), the zero-copy way to show a WebGL2 frame on a page canvas; a 2D `drawImage` instead
  would allocate nothing in JavaScript but add a GPU copy every frame.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the entry size record measured whatever dist a tree held, so lanes rewrote each other's Gzip column (KB-API-SURFACE-CHURN1, scripts)

- **Repro (before):** in a tree rebased onto a newer `main`, `node examples/package-benchmarks/entry-sizes.mjs` measured
  the old builds of every package `main` changed; a full `npm run api:update` then rewrote the Gzip column of
  `docs/api-surface.md` from that record (16 rows differed from `main` at 4825426cd0, such as cameras 3,766 against
  3,919 B, vfx 36,086 against 36,403, webgl2-compat 118,091 against 119,671), and every push conflicted on the file.
- **Cause:** `measureEntries` bundled `dist/` as it found it. `api-report.js` already rebuilt stale packages before
  reading declarations; the size measurement did not, so its figures depended on the tree's last build and not on the
  sources. The column itself is a copy of the committed `entry-sizes.json`, so the report was never the writer.
- **Fix:** `scripts/support/fresh-dist.mjs` (`rebuildStalePackages`: packages whose stamp is stale are rebuilt under the
  build lock, a current dist is left alone) is the one step both tools run first. `api-report.js` uses it in place of
  its own copy, and `measureEntries` runs it before measuring (its `ensureFresh` option is the test seam). The same
  source now gives the same figures in any tree: a full measurement in lane E at cbeea83aa6 differed from the committed
  record only where `main` had changed sources since (lighting2d, post, scenes, webgl2-compat). The record's `commit`
  line still names the commit measured, so two lanes that both commit a new record still meet on that line.
- **Regression:** `tests/fresh-dist.test.js` (fails on the old code: no `fresh-dist.mjs`, and `measureEntries` ignores
  `ensureFresh` and measures at once).

### Fixed 2026-11-19, last file 2026-11-25: other scripts that end with `process.exit` share the exit deadlock of KB-OWN-EXIT1 (KB-OWN-EXIT2, scripts)

- **Repro:** the KB-OWN-EXIT1 fixture's conditions (`--stress-concurrent-allocation`, a 16 MB heap, a worker thread
  that holds the exit) stall plain `node -e "setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 300)"` 16 runs in 16; in a normal
  process the race is rare (a V8 background allocation must ask for a collection after the main thread's last
  JavaScript).
- **Cause:** the same as KB-OWN-EXIT1: `process.exit` shuts the V8 platform down while the isolate lives, and a V8
  task waiting on the collection barrier is never woken (nodejs/node#54918). Many files under scripts/ call
  `process.exit`. `scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs`, the bounded one, is fixed (KB-OWN-EXIT1).
- **Done so far:** `scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs`, the one wrapper around GPU and gate commands, sets its exit code and
  ends by its event loop, usage errors included (test: `tests/run-with-timeout-exit.test.js`, through
  `tests/support/end-recorder.js`). `scripts/gate-step.mjs` and its test were deleted with the GPU lock (KB-GPULOCK-ALL).
  Since 2026-11-18 `npm run hygiene` fails on a `process.exit(` call without a `// process.exit: <reason>` on its line
  (a watchdog ending a hung run, an interrupt) in any tracked file not listed in scripts/support/exit-owed.json, and on
  a listed file that no longer calls it (scripts/support/process-exit.mjs; test: `tests/process-exit-check.test.js`).
  Fixed: api-report, quality-gate, check-wgsl, frame-alloc-browser, frame-alloc-nodes and public-truth set the exit
  code and end by their event loop; the watchdogs of run-readme-examples, check-owner-lifetime(-browser), test-watch
  and run-with-timeout's interrupt keep the call with their reason.
  Part 2: check-rapier-parity, check-parity-table, errors/page, generate-all-entries, umbrella, supply-chain,
  check-xr-runs, check-film-time, check-wall-budgets, check-fixed-waits, the two codemods and core-stress, each run
  through the end recorder by the same test.
  Part 3: check-dev-servers, library-index, mutation, record-wgsl-corpus and site-check set the exit code and end by
  their event loop (the first three run through the end recorder in the same test); quickstart-timing's hard-limit
  watchdog keeps its call with the reason.
  Part 4: the 61 benchmark and rival-bench entries skipped their body in the build phase with a prologue
  `if (isSpeedEntry(...) && deferSpeed(...)) process.exit(0)`. They now wrap the body in
  `if (!deferSpeedEntry(import.meta.url, label)) { ... }` (scripts/support/speed-phase.mjs), so a deferred run ends by
  its event loop with code 0 (a top-level await that never settles would end with code 13); the four that export keep
  their exports outside the block. bench --list, the rival benches' failure checks and child exits, and
  visual-compat-budget's end set the exit code; its chunk watchdog keeps its call with the reason. Tests: every
  deferred entry and bench --list run through the end recorder (`tests/process-exit-check.test.js`), and
  deferSpeedEntry's cases (`tests/speed-phase.test.js`).
  Part 5: scripts/support/help.mjs's `exitOnHelp` became `showHelp`, which prints the usage and returns true; its 13
  callers skip their work in `if (!showHelp(usage)) { ... }` (or add it to their entry guard), so a --help run ends
  by its event loop with code 0 (test: every caller's --help run through the end recorder, `tests/script-help.test.js`).
  Part 6: the 37 real-GPU checks of taa, lod, quality, post, toon, oit and shadows (colored) called process.exit only
  from their hard-limit watchdog, which ends a run still going past its limit; each call keeps it with its reason (test:
  `tests/process-exit-check.test.js` holds the list exact).
  Part 7: the same for the hard-limit watchdogs of the eight biomes WebGPU checks, voxel-net's native server fixture
  and WebRTC browser proof, the Dawn blend repeat, fetch-skip-assets, test-gallery-browser and the child processes of
  `tests/vite-cache-isolation.test.js`.
  Part 8: the stand-in programs and fixtures of the root tests (build-lock, parallel-check, server-url, rendezvous)
  and of headless (ffmpeg stand-ins), fsm's outside check and the biomes globals probe set the exit code their caller
  reads and skip the rest; ecs's exiting system keeps its call with the reason, since ending its worker thread at once
  is what it tests. The fake browser host keeps its call for now: without it the host waits on its fake browser's pipes
  (test: the rendezvous fixture left alone ends by its event loop with code 3, `tests/process-exit-check.test.js`).
  Parts 9 to 18 (lane D, 2026-11-18 and 19) took the rest of scripts/, the example and package benches, the voxel-net
  shard and router (with the start/stop race fixed in VoxelServer.listen and PlazaShard.start) and the proofs off the
  list, each run for real. Part 19: a pinned proof this clone cannot run unwinds with a `Historical` signal and ends
  with code 0 (examples/package-benchmarks/proofs/history.js, test in `tests/proofs-golden.test.js`), and the physics2d
  reproduction returns from the stages not asked for. Part 20: build-modern, the voxel-sandbox play test, loadtime and
  measure. Part 21: the voxel-net remote bench and its bot processes (a closed VoxelBot no longer keeps a resume
  socket that opens late, test in packages/voxel-net/tests/resume-client.test.js), vfx's readback child, the Jupyter
  check, check:gpu-packages (its side-by-side stop ends by the loop, every suite already ended) and the publish
  rehearsal (importing all 1,471 entries leaves no handle). Hard run limits and a SIGTERM keep the call with their
  reason.
- **Last file (2026-11-25, lane D):** scripts/test-boulder-browser.mjs ends by its event loop; only its last line
  changed, so no people work. Its run still fails first on KB-BOULDER-ARMBODY1, and that failing run, leaving through
  the same `finally` that closes the browser and preview server, ended by its event loop in 24 s.
  scripts/support/exit-owed.json is empty, so hygiene now fails on any new unjustified `process.exit(`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a passing leaf exited 1 because its `run` wrapper deadlocked in `process.exit` (KB-OWN-EXIT1, scripts)

- **Repro:** seen 6 times on 2026-11-15 (5 of 884 `check-owner-lifetime` runs, once in owners-b10's gltf/pbr
  extensions test), never in 855 plain scratch runs: the leaf printed PASS and exited 0, then its command wrapper had
  not exited 30 s later and was ended, so the step exited 1. On demand: run a wrapper under V8's own
  `--stress-concurrent-allocation` with a 16 MB heap (`--initial-heap-size=1 --max-old-space-size=16`) and a worker
  thread that holds the exit for a second in a synchronous child run: 6 stalls in 6 runs.
- **Cause:** the wrapper ended with `process.exit(code)`. In Node, `process.exit` shuts the V8 platform down while the
  main isolate is still alive, so a background V8 task that waits for the main thread to collect is never woken (the
  main thread is already in the exit and never collects); the join then waits for ever. The race needs a background
  allocation to ask for a collection after the main thread's last JavaScript, which a loaded machine makes likelier.
  Node tracks the same shutdown deadlock as nodejs/node#54918. Not a child, pipe or console handle: the wrapper had no
  child left and no thread waited on one.
- **Fix:** the wrapper sets `process.exitCode` and lets its event loop end (`scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs`), so nothing
  keeps the loop alive and a natural end disposes the isolate first, whose heap teardown wakes a waiting task.
  Measured with plain node under `--stress-concurrent-allocation` while the main thread allocates: `process.exit`
  stalled 47 of 200 runs, the natural end 0 of 200 (slowest 228 ms); with the held worker and the 16 MB heap 16 of 16
  against 0 of 16.
- **Regression:** `tests/run-with-timeout-exit.test.js` records through `tests/support/end-recorder.js` whether the wrapper
  ends by its event loop or through `process.exit` (fails on a wrapper that calls `process.exit(2)` for a usage error).
- **Sources:** Node.js, "process.exit([code])" and "process.exitCode" (v26 docs, 2026),
  https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#processexitcode; nodejs/node issue 54918, "Deadlock at process shutdown"
  (2024, open), https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/54918; nodejs/node issue 47748, "Infinite loop at shutdown"
  (2023; an embedder disposes the isolate to join concurrent tasks), https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/47748.
  No Node or V8 source was copied.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: timing tests ran inside the correctness gate again after the lock removal (KB-TIMING-INGATE1, scripts, biomes)

- **Repro (before):** with `scripts/speed-phase.json` at `deferred`, `node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --list` listed
  `biomes test:gpu:flythrough:speed` and `biomes test:gpu:objects-frame:speed` as steps of `check:gpu-packages`. Each started
  a browser step only to exit at its own `deferSpeed`, and nothing named them deferred or ordered them last and alone once
  the phase is active.
- **Cause:** 80ca93fe2c removed the `// timing test: runs alone` header and the exclusive-last ordering together with the
  lock, so the gate no longer knew which tests are timing tests.
- **Fix:** the header is `// timing test: deferred in the build phase` (no lock named). `plan()` flags a test whose file
  carries it, `splitTiming` leaves flagged steps out of a deferred run with a `SPEED DEFERRED:` line each, and an active run
  does them after every shared step, one at a time, nothing beside them. No lock of any kind.
- **Regression:** `tests/gpu-timing-deferral.test.js` (fails on the old plan: both steps listed, nothing named deferred).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: four unit reds left on main after the GPU lock sweep (KB-FILMTIME-LOADERS1, KB-README-HUE1, KB-DECODERS-DRACOCHUNK1, KB-TEST-MODULEMOCKS1; loaders, tonemap, decoders, scripts)

- **film-time:** `packages/loaders/src/types.ts` `httpRefusal(response, now = Date.now())` turns a Retry-After HTTP-date
  into seconds for a `LoaderError`; nothing drawn depends on it. It is on `scripts/film-time-reviewed.json` with that
  reason. Regression: `tests/film-time.test.js`.
- **package-readmes:** tonemap `./hue` is named in its README, so `scripts/support/readme-entries-known.json` no longer
  lists it. Regression: `tests/package-readmes.test.js`.
- **dist-dynamic-imports:** `packages/decoders/src/node-thread.ts` loaded `draco-codec.js` with `import()` while
  `codec.ts` imports it statically, so the `import()` split nothing. The Node decode step is now `draco-here.ts`
  (`decodeHere`), which only `node-thread.ts` loads, and only with `import()`; `draco-codec.js` is reached only by static
  imports, so a page still loads none of it. Regression: `tests/dist-dynamic-imports.test.js`.
- **module mocks in bulk runs:** a test that calls `mock.module` dies with "mock.module is not a function" unless node
  runs with `--experimental-test-module-mocks`, and a hand-made `node --test tests/*.test.js` (a lane gate) lost the
  flag; every script in the repository already carried it. `npm run test:files -- <files>` is the one command for chosen
  files, and the test fails when a package script runs a file that mocks a module without the flag. Regression:
  `tests/module-mocks-flag.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: an edit to a document ran no test in a lane gate (KB-GATE-DOCREADERS1, hygiene)

- **Repro (before):** edit `docs/whitepaper/claims.md` or `docs/limits.md` and run the fast gate: nothing ran that reads them, though `tests/claims-file.test.js` does. 80ca93fe2c (31 rows lost an opening backtick) and f7a229b5ad ("LIM-001 to LIM-659" left stale) reached main with that test red.
- **Cause:** the fast gate runs the tests of changed packages; a document is in no package, and `check:merge` classes every .md file inert.
- **Fix:** `npm run hygiene` (every lane gate runs it) runs every root test whose source, comments removed, names a changed document by path or by its quoted file name (`scripts/support/unit-readers.mjs`), and fails naming them.
- **Regression:** `tests/unit-readers.test.js` (the map of claims.md and limits.md to `claims-file`, a failing reader fails the gate, hygiene wires it). Shown by corrupting claims.md with a duplicate limit row: the gate fails naming six tests.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Cabin Hearth's ground-edge rise depended on which pixel the 8-bit read picked (KB-CABIN-EDGEPHASE1, cabin-hearth test)

- **Repro (before):** `colour()` picks the pixel by `Math.round`, up to a pixel from the point it reads. The
  KB-CABIN-GROUNDEDGE1 profile reads the snow across the lantern's right-jamb edge 5 mm a step, one pixel each, so
  its 10 to 90% rise followed the sub-pixel phase: 0.0943 m with `Math.round`, 0.1412 m with `Math.floor` (bound
  0.057 to 0.106 m, the 22 mm flame's 0.0816 m), on both backends.
- **Cause:** point reads of single 8-bit pixels on a ramp 9 pixels wide, against a lit level taken as the mean of a
  stretch 0.2 to 0.3 m from the edge. The lit level beside the penumbra is not flat (0.0393 down to 0.0343 from s
  -0.3 to -0.12 m: the snow's slope, the lantern's cosine and inverse square), so the 90% crossing sat on that slow
  fall. Read in float and bilinear at each point (`hdrRead`), against the old level, the rise was 0.1234 m, still
  over its bound for that reason alone.
- **Fix:** the profile is read in float bilinearly at each point's own projection (the 8-frame HDR capture), and the
  level the edge rises from is the shoulder's straight line fitted over s <= -0.12 m, outside the penumbra's half
  width (0.06 m), carried to each step. Float rise 0.0637 m (0.78 of the flame's 0.0816 m), both backends; the 8-bit
  read stays as `measured8` (0.0539 m). The 0.7 to 1.3 bound is unchanged. A new check reads the line as three
  interleaved sets 15 mm apart and 5 mm out of step: the float rises agree within 5 mm (0.0642 to 0.0658 m), the 8-bit
  picks spread 0.0623 to 0.1017 m with the old level.
- **Regression:** `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` (`edge` and `edgePhase` lines).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Cabin Hearth's crest check read the frame half a pixel off the crest (KB-BOUNCE-FRAMETWIN1, cabin-hearth test)

- **Repro (before):** `node scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` (WebGPU or `MARGO_COMPAT=1`) failed "the frame's
  bounce at the crest, 0.0092 ..., is its twin's 0.0089" (frosted, 2.9% over a 2% bound; clear 1.5%).
- **Cause:** the check read an 8-bit 3 x 3 box centred on pixel round(X), round(Y), whose centre lies up to a pixel
  from the crest's projection (0.48 px below it here), and on the log the bounce changes 4.2 to 4.7% per pixel down
  the curve; one 8-bit code there is about 3% of the bounce. Read in float (the post stack's rgba16float scene capture,
  8 frames), the same box is 2.2 and 2.5% over the twin, and the frame interpolated at the crest's own point is 0.9989
  and 0.9991 of it: the renderer and the twin agree; the measurement was off the point.
- **Fix:** the test reads the frame in float at the crest itself (`hdrRead`: the capture over TAA's whole 8-frame
  jitter cycle, bilinear between texel centres) and keeps the 8-bit box as `measured8`, reported. The 2% bound is
  unchanged.
- **Regression:** `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` (the crest check fails at 2% with the 8-bit box, passes with
  the float read; both readings are printed every run).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: an opening's bounce capture looked out from inside its glazing bars and lit their inner faces (KB-BOUNCE-CAPEYE1, clustered)

- **Repro (before):** a window of four lites (Cabin Hearth's: 1.2 x 1.1 m, bars 45 mm wide and 50 mm deep centred on
  the glass) with its `openingLight` given to `LightBounce`: the opening's capture looked out from the rectangle's
  centre, the light's position on the glass's outdoor face, which lies inside the crossing of the bars. The capture
  draws back faces (`cullMode: 'none'`), so it saw the bars' inner faces and reduced them to texels the opening's light
  lights (the CPU capture of `packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js` counts lit bar texels from the old eye).
- **Cause:** `bounceViews` put a rect source's eye at its `position`; nothing told `LightBounce` the opening had bars.
- **Fix:** `BounceOpeningLight` takes the window's `lites` and `barDepth` (as `openingLight` takes them, checked);
  with bars the rect source gets `front`, half the bar depth plus the capture camera's near plane, and `bounceViews`
  moves the eye out along the normal by `front` or `recess`, whichever is further: the opening's mouth, in the open
  air. Cabin Hearth passes its sash.
- **Regression:** `packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js` ("an opening's capture looks out from in front of its
  glazing bars", and the options test's `lites` / `barDepth` cases; both fail on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: on the WebGL2 layer a VFX effect never drew: its visibility kernel bound bindings its entry point does not use (KB-VFX-COMPATBIND1, vfx)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/vfx/test/seek-check.mjs --compat` throws before the page is ready,
  "createBindGroup: binding index 5 not present in the bind group layout", and so does the cabin hearth check on the layer.
- **Cause:** the compatibility route (vfx/src/compat.ts) builds each kernel with an automatic layout, which holds only
  the bindings its entry point statically uses (WGSL 7.7). The `marks` kernel bound the tickets (5) and every feature
  entry although its entry point only calls onScreen; once the layer's createBindGroup applied WebGPU's entry rules
  (KB-COMPAT-PHONY1) it refused the group.
- **Fix:** each kernel binds exactly the bindings its entry point reaches (`usedBindings`: the variables named in
  `main` and every function it calls). Regression test: `packages/vfx/test/compat-bindings.test.js` (six feature sets,
  checked against the layer's own WGSL front end; fails on the old code); `seek-check.mjs --compat` passes.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the GPU locks cost two weeks of waiting, so they were removed (KB-GPULOCK-ALL, scripts)

- **Repro:** the usage record from 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-16 counted thousands of waiter-minutes behind a lock, and the
  clients disagreed on its capacity (a setting of 3, 4 and 5 at once, KB-GPULOCK-SLOTS1) and its recorded
  commands asked for then refused (KB-GPULOCK-DOCS1).
- **Fix (Scott, 2026-11-16: "No more GPU locks"):** the command runner takes nothing. `run` starts the command
  at once and keeps a hard timeout (exit 124). Slots, admission, queues, exclusive mode,
  heartbeat, refusals and usage records were deleted with their tests. KB-GPULOCK-SLOTS1 and KB-GPULOCK-DOCS1 closed
  with them (no slots, no hold cap). Speed work stays deferred by its own gate (`bench/cli.mjs`); a benchmark is no
  longer kept alone on the GPU by a lock.
- **Regression:** `tests/run-with-timeout.test.js` (the runner starts the command at once and ends a hung one at its
  timeout, exit 124) and `tests/no-gpu-lock.test.js` (fails when a tracked file names or imports the lock again).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a lamp's bounce ignored its IES profile, projector image, cube cookie and layers; a spot of half angle pi / 2 bounced behind itself (KB-BOUNCE-TERMS1, clustered)

- **Repro:** a point light with an IES wall-washer profile (dark straight down, bright from 30 to 60 degrees) over a
  floor bounced off the floor as a plain point light: at a wall point 1.2 m out its bounce was over 30% from the
  quadrature of its own direct term; a spot projecting a half red, half blue image bounced white light, red equal to green
  equal to blue (`scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js` on the old code: 0.03709 in each channel at x 0.5); a light
  off layer 0 bounced off core meshes it does not light; a spot of half angle pi / 2 pointing up bounced off the floor
  behind it.
- **Cause:** `LightBounce` weighed each captured texel's flux by the plain point or spot falloff (`pointFalloff`)
  alone: the light loop's per-light terms (`Clustered.ies`, `.projector`, `.layers`) had no CPU form, so the bounce
  never saw them. Separately, `select()` dropped a spot's direction when its outer angle was pi / 2, while the light
  loop keeps its cone (a half space).
- **Fix:** `packages/clustered/src/bounce-terms.ts` (bounce entry only) holds the CPU twin of each built-in term's
  factor, read from the words the shader reads (`IESLights`' unorm16 grid filtered bilinearly, `ProjectorLights`'
  rgba8 texels with sRGB decode and alpha, `CubeProjectorLights`' face-crossing filter, `LightLayers`' mask against
  core meshes' layer 0); a term of one's own gives `ClusteredLightTerm.emission` and `revision`. `bounceLightSource`
  builds a light's source with that weight (`lightEmission`), `reduceBounce` weighs each texel's flux by it, and a
  term set again (new words) captures its sources afresh. Every light given a `direction` keeps its cone.
- **Regression:** `packages/clustered/test/bounce-terms.test.js` (IES, projector, cube cookie and layer bounces against
  quadratures of the lamps' direct terms within 5%, from independent references; the half-angle spot; each case fails
  on the old code), and the projector case of `scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `chamferGrid` gave triangles palette 0 and reported clamped faces after the bevel rewrite (KB-VOXEDIT-CHAMFER1, voxel-edit)

- **Repro (before):** `chamferGrid({ size: [2, 1, 1], voxels: Uint8Array.of(2, 9) }, { bevel: 0.15 })` returned a
  `trianglePalette` holding 0 as well as 2 and 9, and a unit cube with `bevel: 0.4` reported `stats.clamped` 6.
- **Cause:** chamferGrid (packages/voxel-edit/src/mesh.ts) filled the palette in blocks of 10 triangles per face, the
  count of the old `@margoengine/voxel/bevel`. Since a41e04d759 bevelQuads builds the Doo and Sabin (1978)
  face-edge-vertex chamfer (a panel, half strips on creased edges and corner fans per face), so a face owns a
  varying number of triangles (18 on a lone cube) and every triangle past the first ten per face kept palette 0. The
  `clamped` count still applied the old corner clamp, which the new construction never needs: each unit edge is inset
  by the full bevel, below half a cell.
- **Fix:** each face passes its palette as the bevel `material`, which bevelQuads copies onto every vertex of the
  triangles that face owns, and the palette of each triangle is read from its first vertex; `clamped` is 0.
- **Regression:** packages/voxel-edit/tests/mesh.test.js ("chamferGrid insets a cube...", which also checks the cube
  is closed, has the chamfered cube's exact area and the full inset; "chamferGrid keeps distinct palettes on adjacent
  cells", which checks each triangle's palette against the cell it lies on), failing before the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the WebGL2 layer refused views of another dimension of a compressed texture (KB-COMPAT-DECODERS1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/decoders/scripts/test-browser.js` (with the layer shim on its page)
  threw MargoError `unsupported` "WebGL2 compatibility cannot do a bc7-rgba-unorm-srgb layer or cube view of a
  bc7-rgba-unorm-srgb texture, which WebGL2 would copy": layerMeans reads a KTX2 cube transcoded to BC7 through a
  `2d-array` view in a compute pass. Native WebGPU allows it (WebGPU "createView()": a `2d-array` view of any 2D
  texture, a `cube` view of 6 square layers, a `2d` view of one layer). Past that, its stream check waited until the
  600 s limit: `KTX2Streamer` grows a texture by `copyTextureToTexture` between BC7 textures, the layer refused it, and
  the failed level went only to the streamer's `onError`, which the check did not watch.
- **Cause:** the layer stores a 6-layer square texture as a GL cube map; any view of another target reads a copy of
  its own, and a copy was made only for formats GL can render into. GL cannot copy compressed blocks between texture
  objects at all, nor read them back.
- **Fix:** such a view of a compressed texture reads a decoded copy (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/resources.ts
  `copy`, render.ts `decodeBlocks`): a draw fetches each texel through the GPU's decoder into `rgba32float` storage
  (`rgba16float` where 32-bit floats cannot be filtered), restoring the running pass's viewport afterwards (a decode
  made at a draw is inside a pass; the first build of the fix drew that pass's later draws into a 4 x 4 corner). Any
  compressed format, any of the three target changes, twin sRGB views and later block writes are covered. A compressed
  texture made with `COPY_SRC` keeps its blocks in memory (resources.ts `blocks`), so `copyTextureToTexture` and
  `copyTextureToBuffer` copy them as WebGPU does, and encoder copies with a `bytesPerRow` that is not a multiple of 256
  are validation errors as on WebGPU (the layer accepted them). The decoders stream check now fails at once with the
  error of a level that does not load. The decoders check passes natively and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1` and is off
  `scripts/support/compat-owed.json`.
- **Regression:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/features.html `compressedViews` and `compressedCopies` (checked by
  features-browser.mjs against native WebGPU, bit for bit, plus their own assertions), which throw on the old layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: two MSAA audits counted nothing on the WebGL2 layer (KB-COMPAT-AUDIT1, creative and scripts)

- **Repro (before):** with the layer shim on its pages, `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/creative/scripts/test-browser.js`
  failed "Desktop high-tier globe did not render with 4x MSAA", and `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/margo-module-tests.js`
  passed its phone page's "0 MSAA textures, pipelines and resolves" only because it counted nothing.
- **Cause:** both audits are init scripts that patch `GPUDevice.prototype` (and `GPUQueue`, `GPURenderPassEncoder`,
  `GPUCommandEncoder`) when the page starts. The layer installs its own classes on the first `requestAdapter()`, after
  that, so the patched classes were the browser's, which the layer's devices never call.
- **Fix:** `compatShim` (scripts/support/compat-shim.js) runs the patches an init script queues on
  `globalThis.__margoOnLayer`, once, right after the layer installs; both audits queue theirs there in a
  compatibility run and patch at once otherwise, and both scripts now install the shim on the pages they open
  themselves. Each audit also proves it saw work: creative's light tier must have made textures and bound 1x
  pipelines, its phone page made pipelines and textures, and the module phone page must have counted textures,
  pipelines and passes (69, 52 and 113 on the layer, 56, 50 and 113 natively; RTX A6000, ANGLE D3D11) before its
  zero-MSAA assertion counts. Both scripts pass natively and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1` and are off
  `scripts/support/compat-owed.json`.
- **Regression:** tests/compat-on-layer.test.js (the queued patch runs once after the install, on the layer's
  classes, and counts the layer device's work), failing on the old shim.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the WebGL2 layer's automatic layouts dropped phony-read bindings and typed `texture_external` as a plain texture, and its createBindGroup checked no entries (KB-COMPAT-PHONY1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro (before):** on the layer, a render pipeline with `layout: 'auto'` whose fragment entry reaches a uniform only
  through a phony assignment (`_ = u;`) had no entry for it in `getBindGroupLayout(0)`, and a bind group that carried
  the uniform, or any binding its layout does not declare, was accepted. A device refuses that group ("binding index 5
  not present in the bind group layout"), so KB-OWN-TONE3 passed with `MARGO_COMPAT=1` and failed on WebGPU. A
  `texture_external` binding came out of the 'auto' layout as a `texture` entry rather than an `externalTexture` one.
- **Cause:** the render pipeline built its 'auto' layout from the GLSL binding tables (packages/webgl2-compat/src/
  device/render.ts). The GLSL emitter rightly drops a phony assignment's value, which has no effect, so its resource
  never reached those tables; WGSL counts it as a static use (WGSL section 7.7 "Phony Assignment"), and WebGPU's
  default pipeline layout gives every resource an entry point statically uses an entry of its declared type (WebGPU
  "default pipeline layout"). The GLSL tables also know an external texture only as a sampled 2D texture.
  `CompatBindGroup` (device/resources.ts) bound whatever it was given.
- **Fix:** the render pipeline's 'auto' layout starts from each stage's checked WGSL entry point (the same resource
  list the compute path already used, now one `layoutEntry` in device/compute.ts) and adds the GLSL tables' entries
  after it. `createBindGroup` applies WebGPU's createBindGroup rules for entries against the layout: as many entries
  as the layout, each binding given once and declared, each resource of its entry's kind (a buffer, a sampler, a
  texture view, or for an `externalTexture` entry an external texture or a texture view); a group that breaks one is
  invalid with a validation error, as on a device. The corpus draw check binds a texture view to `externalTexture`
  entries, as WebGPU allows.
- **Regression:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/device.test.js ("a binding reached only through a phony assignment
  stays in the 'auto' layout...", "a texture_external binding is an externalTexture entry of the 'auto' layout",
  "createBindGroup refuses entries the layout does not declare..."), each failing before the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a voxel renderer with VoxelGI or a caller's GpuVoxelMesher broke after a device restore (KB-RESTORE-VOXGI1, KB-RESTORE-VOXMESH1, voxel)

- **Repro (before):** a `VoxelRenderer` given a `GpuVoxelMesher` and lit by `VoxelGI`, then `engine.gpu.destroy()` and
  `await engine.rebootDevice()`. Every frame drawn before the next `VoxelGI.update()` made a bind group with the lost
  device's GI volumes (validation error, thrown by core from the next frame), and every chunk the renderer meshed again
  went to the mesher's lost device: each `mapAsync` failed with "The Device was lost before mapping was resolved",
  reported through `engine.onError`, and the world never drew again (0 draws).
- **Cause:** `VoxelGI.pbr` and `bindings` handed out its GPU state without checking its device (only `update` did).
  `GpuVoxelMesher` kept the device it was made with and its pipelines; the renderer's restore hook re-dirtied every
  chunk but had no way to move a mesher the caller gave it.
- **Fix:** `VoxelGI` frees state of an older device whichever of `update`, `pbr` or `bindings` asks first, so until
  the next `update` the renderer draws without the effect, as before the first one. `GpuVoxelMesher.setDevice(device)`
  moves the mesher to a new device (pipelines and scratch made again there); while its device is lost, jobs wait and
  none runs on it. `VoxelChunkMesher` gains an optional `setDevice`, which `VoxelRenderer.onDeviceRestored` calls with
  `engine.gpu` before it meshes again. The renderer keeps the caller's mesher (it never owns or disposes one) rather
  than refusing it.
- **Regression:** packages/voxel/tests/restore-browser-check.mjs (WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1; before the fix 3
  validation errors and 3 mapAsync reports, after it none and the settled picture equal to the one before the restore);
  CPU: packages/voxel/tests/gi.test.js ("a restored device"), packages/voxel/tests/gpu-mesher.test.js ("a lost device").

### Fixed 2026-11-16: an inline colour array rebuilt `TextureMaterial`'s mesh on every render (KB-REACT-COLOR2, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<TextureMaterial map={texture} color={[1, 0, 0]} emissive={[0, 1, 0]} />` (and a mapped
  `<PbrMaterial color={[...]}>` or `<MappedPbrMaterial>`, which render it) in a component that re-renders: each render
  disposed the material mesh and built a new one a microtask later, so the surface flickered and its GPU resources
  were remade. KB-REACT-COLOR1 fixed the same pattern in the plain PbrMaterial only.
- **Cause:** the effect keyed every object option by identity, and an array literal is a new object on each render.
- **Fix:** number arrays count by value with numbers and strings; textures and other objects keep identity.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/textures.test.js ("an inline colour or emissive array with the same values
  keeps the material mesh; a new value replaces it").

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a glTF or FBX `<Model>` inside a named `<Scene>` was drawn in the default scene (GAP-REACT-SCENEMODELS, react, gltf/pbr)

- **Repro (before):** `<RenderView scene="item" /><Scene name="item"><Gltf src="a.glb" /></Scene>`: the model joined the
  default scene, so the item view did not show it; under a `<Mesh>` inside that Scene the load failed with core's
  `Foreign parent` TypeError, reported through `onError`.
- **Cause:** `PBRModel` created its meshes with `engine.createMesh()` (the default scene) and `instantiateModel` added it
  with `engine.use`; neither took a scene.
- **Fix:** `PBRModel`'s constructor takes an optional last `scene` argument that its root and nodes are created in, and
  `<Gltf>`/`<Fbx>` inside a `<Scene>` build their own model there and add it with `scene.use(model)` (the loader's
  first model lives in the default scene and is not reused). Plugins other than models, and `<Hud>` and
  `<RenderTexture>` proxies, still hand `use` the default scene (not changed here).
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/scene-loaders.test.js ("a Gltf inside a named Scene is built and added in that
  Scene").

### Fixed 2026-11-21: react bindings other than models attached to the default scene inside `<Scene>`, `<Hud>` and `<RenderTexture>` (GAP-REACT-SCENEPLUGINS, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<Sky>`, `<Clouds>`, `<Text>`, `<BatchedMesh>`, `<Voxels>` or another binding that called
  `engine.use` or `X.attach(engine)` directly, placed inside `<Scene name="item">`, landed in the default scene, so the
  item view did not draw it.
- **Cause:** those bindings used the engine's default scene (`engine.use`, `engine.removePlugin`) instead of the
  enclosing scene's world, as `attachBinding` (packages/react/src/package-binding.ts) does.
- **Fix:** `sceneOwner(scene)` (the world, else the engine) adds and removes the plugins the bindings build themselves
  (Sky, ContactShadows, the shared Text renderer, now one per scene, Animation, Physics), and `inScene(scene, work)` runs
  `X.attach(engine, ...)` inside `sceneScope`, the scope `instantiateModel` uses (Clouds and its soft-particle depth,
  BatchedMesh, Voxels, AmbientShadows, Caustics, ModelOutlines and MeshOutline). `useCreated` recreates its object when
  the world changes. `<Hud>` and `<RenderTexture>` pass their world the same way.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/kit-helpers.test.js ("Sky and Text inside a named <Scene>"),
  packages/react/tests/extras.test.js ("BatchedMesh and Voxels inside a <Scene>") and
  packages/react/tests/clouds.test.js ("Clouds inside a named <Scene>", on a real core scene).
- **Second change (2026-11-21), the rest:** `<Environment>` (its lighting, background, captured children and the
  default sun and ambient it writes), `<CubeCamera>` (its `envMap` background and private fog) and the environment
  capture attach to, and write the lighting of, the enclosing scene (`sceneOwner`), and leave the Canvas's glTF models
  alone inside a named Scene. `<DepthTexture>`, `<SceneTargets>`, the `<EffectComposer>` stack and its effects,
  `<SpriteLayer>` and `<Figure>` attach with `inScene`. `<Shadows>` and `<SoftShadows>` inside a `<Scene>` make that
  scene's own cascaded shadows (`useSceneShadows`, packages/react/src/scene-shadows.ts); a mesh's `castShadow` and
  `receiveShadow` in that scene go to them, where they went to the default scene's shadows before.
- **Canvas-wide on purpose (documented in the react README, "Views and scenes"):** `<Html>` is one DOM overlay per
  canvas; the devtools (`<Stats>`, the inspector) read the engine, not one scene; picking and XR pointers route one
  pointer to whichever scene's mesh it hits (`engine.meshes` holds every scene's meshes, so XR pointers and Controller
  already reach a mesh in a named Scene); the audio listener is one per canvas and follows the camera; the ViewCube is
  an overlay of one camera; `<CameraShake>` moves the Canvas camera. None of these draws into or reads a single scene.
- **Regression (second change):** packages/react/tests/lightformer.test.js ("Environment inside a named <Scene>"),
  cube-camera.test.js ("CubeCamera inside a named <Scene>", private fog), extras.test.js ("DepthTexture and
  SceneTargets inside a <Scene>", "SpriteLayer and Figure inside a <Scene>"), post.test.js ("an EffectComposer inside a
  <Scene>") and scene-loaders.test.js ("Shadows inside a named <Scene>").
- **Still open:** nothing. ContactShadows, AccumulativeShadows, Caustics, outlines, Animation and Physics have no
  named-scene test of their own; they use the helpers the tests above cover.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a `<Scene>` reset and unmounted its children when one of them suspended under a Suspense above it (KB-REACT-SCENESUSPEND1, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<Canvas><Suspense><Scene name="item"><Gltf src="a.glb" /></Scene></Suspense></Canvas>`: while the
  model loaded, React hid the boundary, `Scene`'s commit cleanup set its world to null, its children unmounted, and on
  reveal they mounted and suspended again until React reported "Maximum update depth exceeded".
- **Cause:** `Scene` (packages/react/src/views.tsx) cleared its world state in the commit cleanup, which also runs when a
  boundary above it is hidden, and rendered nothing while the world was null.
- **Fix:** the cleanup no longer clears the world; the effect that runs again on reveal makes a new scene and the
  children follow it.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/scene-loaders.test.js ("a Gltf that suspends under a Suspense above its Scene").

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `AmbientLight`, `HemisphereLight` and `Fog` inside a `<Scene>` lit the default scene (KB-REACT-SCENELIGHT1, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<RenderView scene="fogged" /><Scene name="fogged"><Fog color="#00ff00" near={0} far={1} />`
  with a white plane in that Scene: the plane drew lit grey (209, 209, 209), unfogged, and the fog went to the default
  scene's meshes instead. AmbientLight and HemisphereLight did the same.
- **Cause:** the three bindings attached with `X.attach(engine)`, which uses the engine's default scene, while
  `<Sun>`, Line, Points and the other scene-aware bindings attach to the enclosing Scene.
- **Fix:** they attach to the enclosing Scene (the default scene outside one) and are recreated when it changes; inside
  a named Scene they leave the Canvas's glTF models alone, since models stay in the default scene.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/extras.test.js ("AmbientLight, HemisphereLight and Fog inside a <Scene> light
  that scene, not the default one"), and on a real GPU, natively and with MARGO_COMPAT=1,
  `npm run test:browser:reflections --workspace @margoengine/react -- --mode=scene-fog` (centre green; grey before).

### Fixed 2026-11-20: loading one environment format pulled all three image decoders (KB-ENVDECODERS2, environment)

- **Repro:** bundle `import { loadEnvironmentImage } from '@margoengine/environment/loaders'` with Vite and load a
  `.hdr` file: the build held the Radiance HDR, OpenEXR and UltraHDR decoders together.
- **Cause:** `load.ts` imported `parseHDR`, `parseEXR` and `decodeUltraHDR` statically, and `dist/loaders.js` was
  one file with all three inside, so no bundler could leave an unused one out.
- **Fix:** `loadEnvironmentImage` picks the decoder from the file signature and `import()`s it, from its own built
  file (`hdr.js`, `exr.js`, `ultrahdr.js`). It lives in a new entry, `@margoengine/environment/load`, with no static
  decoder import: Vite's bundler keeps a module in the entry chunk once any static import reaches it, even an unused
  re-export, so `/loaders` (which re-exports the decoders) cannot be lazy. `/loaders` and the root re-export the same
  function; results, signatures, errors and the direct decoder exports are unchanged. The synchronous
  `parseEnvironmentImage` moved to its own file and keeps the HDR and EXR parsers. `@margoengine/react`'s
  `<Environment src>` first kept `/loaders` for fear of changing the locked `EnvironmentSource` type, then (2026-11-21,
  Scott: "Do whatever is best practice") moved to `/load` with that type unchanged: `environment-asset.ts` only casts
  its `api` object to the declared type, since the code reads just `.Environment` from it. No locked export changed
  (`api:check` clean, no api/breaks.json line).
- **Regression:** environment `tests/lazy-decoders.test.js` (a Vite build of an app that loads files through `/load`
  keeps each decoder in its own lazy chunk; fails without the entry and on a static decoder import), and react
  `tests/subpaths.test.js` "<Environment src> keeps the decoders a file does not need in lazy chunks" (fails on
  `/loaders`, where all three share one chunk).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: react's lazy environment bindings fetched the image decoders they do not use (KB-REACT-ENVDECODERS1, react, environment)

- **Repro (before):** build an app with Vite that renders `<AmbientLight>`, `<Fog>`, `<CubeCamera>` or an
  `<Environment>` with children (`@margoengine/react/environment`). Vite printed `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` for
  `packages/environment/dist/loaders.js`, and the lazy chunk these bindings load held the Radiance HDR, OpenEXR and
  UltraHDR decoders (36 KB raw) although none of them reads an image file.
- **Cause:** each binding loaded the whole environment root, whose `index.js` re-exports `loaders.js` beside `main.js`;
  taking the namespace kept every export, so the decoders joined the chunk and `EnvironmentLighting.load`'s own
  `import('./loaders.js')` split could not happen.
- **Fix:** `@margoengine/environment/main` is a new entry: everything the root exports except the decoders. The lights,
  Fog, CubeCamera and children-capture bindings import it; only `<Environment src>` (which decodes a file) takes the root.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/subpaths.test.js ("lights and fog load the environment entry without image
  decoders"; it fails with the old import) and "an Environment without children ..." no longer expects the warning.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: an `<Environment>` app bundled CubeCamera, Lightformer and the children capture up front (KB-REACT-PURE1, react)

- **Repro:** build `<Environment src="studio.hdr" />` from `@margoengine/react/environment` with Vite: the initial chunk
  held the `CubeCamera` and `Lightformer` components and the children capture binding, 6,762 B gzip minified.
- **Cause:** module-level `export const X = forwardRef(...)` (and `createContext`, `memo`, `lazy`) had no
  `/* @__PURE__ */` annotation, so a bundler kept the call, and with it the whole component, in every build that imported
  anything else from its module (`descendant` from cube-camera, the pending context from lightformer). The capture
  binding was a static part of environment.js.
- **Fix:** every module-level React factory call in react carries the pure annotation, and `<Environment>` loads its
  capture binding (react `environment-capture.tsx`) with `import()` only once it has children. The same app now loads
  4,631 B gzip up front; other react entries shrank too (portals budget 5,317 to 3,977 B).
- **Test:** react `tests/subpaths.test.js` "an Environment without children loads none of the capture binding,
  CubeCamera or Lightformer" (fails on the old build) and "module-level React factories carry a pure annotation"
  (the class check over every react dist file).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `Video` could not crop its picture or move its rectangle (KB-VIDEO-CROP1, video)

- **Repro:** attach a 2:1 video to `rect: [0, 0, 0.5, 1]` of a square canvas: it is squeezed, no option shows its left
  half only, and `rect` could not change after construction (Margo Film Studio drew a contained picture and said so).
- **Cause:** the overlay's vertex stage mapped the whole picture's uv onto the rect, and the rect was fixed.
- **Fix:** `VideoOptions.source` (a crop in 0 to 1 picture fractions, applied to the uv in the vertex stage),
  `setRect`, `setSource`, the `rect` and `sourceRect` getters, and `objectFit` (CSS `object-fit`, W3C CSS Images Module
  Level 3 section 5.5, centred) for the rect and source of a fill, contain, cover, none or scale-down fit.
- **Test:** `packages/video/test/crop.test.js` (fails on the old build) and `packages/video/test/crop-browser.mjs`
  (RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: the cropped half fills the canvas, then the moved overlay the right half).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `fetchBytes` had no guard for untrusted links and lost a custom fetch's own refusal (KB-LOADERS-FETCHGUARD1, loaders)

- **Repro:** `fetchBytes('https://example.com/a', { fetch })` follows a redirect to `http://127.0.0.1/admin` with no
  check, accepts any media type, returns no final URL or type, and an error thrown by `fetch` comes back as a plain
  `'fetch'` LoaderError whose message is all that is left of it. Margo Film Studio kept its own guarded fetch for this.
- **Cause:** fetchBytes was written for trusted asset links: size limits only.
- **Fix:** `fetchResource` returns `{bytes, url, type, status, redirects}`; `protocols`, `publicOnly` (RFC 1918, 3927,
  4193, 4291, 6598 and 6761 hosts, and links with a user name or password), `allowHost`, `maxRedirects` (hops followed by
  hand and checked again) and `accept` (the `Content-Type` essence, WHATWG MIME Sniffing) on `fetchBytes`, `load` and
  `fetchResource`; `LoaderError` keeps the error behind it as `cause`. `isPrivateHost` is exported.
- **Limit:** hosts are read as written; a public name whose DNS answer is private is not caught (docs/limits.md).
- **Test:** `packages/loaders/tests/fetch-guard.test.js` (fails on the old build: the new exports are missing).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a mirror in view stepped the volumetric clouds' march start twice a frame (KB-FILM-CLOUDPHASE1, sky)

- **Repro:** `VolumetricClouds` with `temporal` and a Reflector, Refractor or CubeCamera in view: each capture renders
  the scene with `delta: 0` before the frame's own update (`engine.onFrame`), and `advanceTime` stepped the march start
  counter on every update, so a continuous run stepped it twice a frame and a seek (no captures) landed on another
  march start than the continuous run. Same class as KB-FILM-TAAPHASE1.
- **Cause:** the counter counted updates, zero-delta ones included. TAA's rule (step at the next resolve) does not fit:
  the clouds draw inside the capture, which comes before the frame's own update.
- **Fix:** the counter moves on timed updates only (what a seek replays). A draw after a zero-delta update adds one step
  for that draw only, and the next timed update drops those steps. So the frame's own draw marches from the start a seek
  gives however many captures came first (they draw with one or more extra steps), and still frames drawn again still
  move the start for TAA to average.
- **Test:** `packages/sky/test/seek.test.js` (the three KB-FILM-CLOUDPHASE1 cases fail on the old build).

### Fixed 2026-11-17: glTF images over 4096 x 4096 pixels were refused although every WebGPU device takes 8192 a side (KB-GLTF-IMGCAP1, gltf)

- **Repro:** `loadGLTF` from `@margoengine/gltf/pbr` on a model with one 8192 x 4096 base colour map (the Kitty Hawk
  film's 1903 Flyer wings) threw `RangeError: glTF images exceed decoded size limit`, well inside the 2 GiB decoded
  budget.
- **Cause:** the decode paths (`asset.ts` and the streamed loader in `stream.ts`, plus the KTX2 and DDS checks) each
  held a fixed 16,777,216-pixel cap per image, the 4096 x 4096 of older devices, below the 8,192 a side that WebGPU
  guarantees for `maxTextureDimension2D`.
- **Fix:** one constant, `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` in `packages/gltf/src/image-limit.ts`, 8192 x 8192, used by every path; the
  per-side device check at upload and the decoded budget (4x `maxDownloadBytes`) are unchanged.
- **Test:** `packages/gltf/test/async-images.test.js` ("a 8192 x 4096 image loads", fails on the old build; 8193 x 8192
  is still refused and its bitmap closed).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: raw RGBA8 textures over 16,777,216 pixels were refused with a message about the data length (KB-MATERIALS-TEXCAP1, materials)

- **Repro:** `new Texture({ data: new Uint8Array(6000 * 3375 * 4), width: 6000, height: 3375 })`, data of the right
  length, threw `Raw texture data must be RGBA8 of width*height*4 bytes`.
- **Cause:** one check mixed a fixed pixel count (16,777,216), non-integer or zero sizes and short data into one
  message. The fixed count was a CPU memory guard that guards nothing for raw data (the caller already holds it); the
  real limit is the device's `maxTextureDimension2D` per side (WebGPU, W3C, "Limits": 8,192 by default), already checked
  at upload with a message that named neither size nor limit.
- **Fix:** construction checks whole positive sizes, then the data length, each with its own message and numbers (the
  same for raw cube faces); the upload refusal names the size and the device limit. `loadTexture` keeps its 4096 x 4096
  decode guard for fetched images.
- **Test:** `packages/materials/test/texture-cap.test.js` (fails on the old build: all five cases).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Cabin Hearth's frosted window read as a flat, near-white card with no bars (KB-CABIN-FROST2, procedural, clustered, scenery)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:cabin-hearth` on `origin/main` 510d13e491, frame `cabin-hearth-outside-*`: the window is an
  even, near-white peach rectangle, its cross bars gone.
- **Cause:** (1) the scene's mullion and cross bar stood 0.2 m into the wall, and the frosted pane was drawn at the
  wall's outer face, in front of them; `generateWindowPane` built no bars. (2) `openingLight` and `glazingSurface` gave
  the frost one radiance, each lamp's light averaged over the pane, so it had no hot spot over the lamp and no bar
  shadows (listed in docs/limits.md as simplifications). (3) The hue: the pane's linear colour is the 1,900 K flame's
  (green over red 0.229 against the flame's 0.232, no blue); snowNight's AgX at +0.6 stops takes the even 3.98 linear
  red to display 253/203/173 (saturation 0.31, hue 23 degrees), its designed path to white in the highlights, not a
  colour error.
- **Fix:** `generateWindowPane` takes `lites`, `barWidth` and `barDepth` and returns `bars` in the glass's plane, the
  glass cut round them, its UVs the pane's. `openingLight` takes the same options plus `thickness` and `reveal`: the
  frost on the glass's room face sends out `L(x) = tau_d E(x) / pi`, E(x) each lamp's inverse square and cosine where
  the segment to the lamp clears the bars and the reveal, integrated exactly (solid angles of the lit rectangles) so the
  area light carries the pane's flux. `glazingSurface` returns `emissiveMap`, that radiance over the pane over its
  peak, `emissiveIntensity`. Cabin Hearth sets the glass at the old bars' plane with `lites: [2, 2]` and passes the
  frame's 0.118 m reveal.
- **Now (RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer):** the frost beside the mullion at the lantern's height reads 14.18
  linear red against tau_d E / pi 14.15, the lite centre 5.81 against 5.85, the far corner 1.504 against 1.507,
  centre over corner 3.86 against 3.88; the bars read 15 to 16 times darker than the frost beside them, against at
  least the 2.2 to 5.9 that their wood, the night light and the bloom bound allow. Tests:
  packages/procedural/test/glazing.test.js, packages/clustered/test/opening-light.test.js,
  scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs. Limits: docs/limits.md, "Frosted window glazing".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a failed `HTMLTexture` raster was rethrown as an uncaught exception (html)

- **Repro:** `HTMLTexture.attach(engine, { prepare: () => Promise.reject(new Error('tainted')) })`, add a surface and
  draw a frame (or a `foreignObject` image that fails to decode in the browser): the error surfaced as an uncaught
  exception that no caller could catch, and `engine.onError` never saw it.
- **Cause:** `refresh` caught the raster's rejection and threw it again inside `queueMicrotask`, outside every caller.
- **Fix:** the rejection reaches `engine.onError` as a `MargoError` with code `failed`, the original error as `cause`,
  and a link to the `html-texture` entry of the error page. The surface keeps its last texture and is free to draw
  again after `surface.invalidate()`; a removed surface or a disposed `HTMLTexture` reports nothing.
- **Regression:** `packages/html/test/texture.test.js` ("reports a failed raster through engine.onError"; failing on
  the old code with an uncaught exception).

### Fixed 2026-11-20: `npm run measure:size` printed different core + stage bytes on macOS and on Windows for one commit (scripts)

- **Repro:** at fea5924d5, `npm run build:packages` then `npm run measure:size` on an Apple M6 (macOS, Node 26.13.0)
  prints core + stage 24,859 B gzip / 61,056 B raw and core alone 22,208 B, while the Windows workstation measured
  24,841 / 61,046 and core 22,224 B for the same sources (fea5924d5's message, and
  `examples/package-benchmarks/results/entry-sizes.json` as committed by 073f98cb9 and afc7f204d). The record measured
  on macOS in c6dbebe9f says 24,859, so `tests/public-size-claims.test.js` fails on whichever machine did not write the
  public figures (README, docs/limits.md, site/index.html and the rest still say 24,841).
- **Cause:** `compactPackage` (`scripts/compact-package.js`, run by `build:packages` for core and the stage) took its
  bundler entries from `readdir` of dist and used that order as given. NTFS lists names sorted; APFS does not, so the
  entry order, and with it the order of the shared-helper imports and of the code in the shared chunks, differed
  between the machines. Shown on Windows by listing the entries in reverse: raw 60,984 B became 60,987 B and gzip
  24,797 B became 24,831 B for the same sources. Line endings, the embedded kernel and gzip were ruled out earlier.
- **Fix:** the entry list is sorted, so the bundle no longer depends on the file system. The Windows figure is
  unchanged (24,797 B gzip, 60,984 B raw), so no public figure moves. A macOS rerun of `npm run build:packages` and
  `npm run measure:size` should confirm it prints the same bytes.
- **Regression:** `tests/compact-package.test.js` ("compaction output is the same whatever order readdir lists the
  entries in"; failing on the old code with a different import order in the compacted entries).

### Fixed 2026-11-25: `npm run measure:size` printed different core + stage bytes on macOS and on Windows for one commit (KB-SIZE-PLATFORM2, scripts)

- **Repro:** at fea5924d5, `npm run build:packages` then `npm run measure:size` on an Apple M6 (macOS, Node 26.13.0)
  prints core + stage 24,859 B gzip / 61,056 B raw and core alone 22,208 B, while the Windows workstation measured
  24,841 / 61,046 and core 22,224 B for the same sources (fea5924d5's message, and
  `examples/package-benchmarks/results/entry-sizes.json` as committed by 073f98cb9 and afc7f204d). The record measured
  on macOS in c6dbebe9f says 24,859, so `tests/public-size-claims.test.js` fails on whichever machine did not write the
  public figures (README, docs/limits.md, site/index.html and the rest still say 24,841).
- **Cause, fix and regression:** as in the 2026-11-25 KB-SIZE-PLATFORM2 entry above (b1584af9e).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: displaced terrain relief read as shadowed by its own ground in the sun's shadow maps (terrain displace, shadows)

- **Repro:** `TerrainDisplacement` (30 cm relief) on a terrain added to `Shadows` (`shadows.add(terrain)`), a 14 degree
  sun: 95.2% of the lit relief turned dark (mean sun share 0.052), and a box held over it cast no visible shadow.
- **Cause:** the displaced hit point lies up to `depth` under the clipmap surface the shadow map holds, and the sun
