  shadow lookup (`shadowLit(direct,i.position,...)`, added by `Shadows` and `VirtualShadows`) read it there, so the
  ground's own depth occluded it. Now the displacement moves that lookup to where the point's ray toward the sun leaves
  the clipmap surface (exact for any occluder above the ground; the relief's own shadow stays its maximum mipmap trace),
  through a new optional `TerrainLighting.finish` step that Terrain runs after every effect's `shader`, so the order of
  attachment does not matter. Regressions: packages/terrain/test/displace.test.js ("sun shadow lookups move ...") and
  packages/terrain/test/displace-shadows.browser.mjs (relief darkened 0%, the box shadows 3.9% of it, both orders).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: `Outlines` drew nothing around a skinned parent (GAP-OUTLINES-INSTANCED, toon, react)

- **Repro:** `<Outlines />` inside a skinned `Model`: no line (it threw: it needs a `<Mesh>`). drei outlines
  `skinnedMesh` parents.
- **Cause:** `MeshOutline` (`@margoengine/toon/outline`) draws one hull from the core mesh's matrix and CPU geometry;
  it does not read a deformer's vertices of the frame, and the React binding only looked for a `<Mesh>` parent. Now
  `<Outlines>` directly inside a `<Model>` attaches `ModelOutlines` (`@margoengine/toon/models`, which reads the posed,
  skinned and morphed vertices of each frame) for that model, with a `node` prop for one subtree (the new toon
  `nodes` option); props it cannot draw yet (`transparent`, `toneMapped={false}`, `polygonOffset`, `renderOrder`, an
  `angle` other than 0 or pi) are refused through `onError`. Regressions: packages/react/tests/outlines.test.js
  ("Outlines inside a Model ..."), packages/toon/test/models.test.js and packages/toon/test/models-check.mjs (the
  skinned Fox under its root draws the full ring; under another node, none).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `Outlines` drew nothing inside `<Instances>` (react)

- **Repro:** `<Instances><BoxGeometry /><Outlines /><Instance position={[0, 0, 0]} /></Instances>`: no line.
- **Cause:** the outline took the enclosing mesh, the Instances root, whose geometry Instances clears; the instances
  are their own core meshes. Now each drawn instance mesh gets its own outline (regression:
  packages/react/tests/outlines.test.js, "Outlines inside Instances").

### Fixed 2026-11-16: label and volume fusion mixed two near-transparent samples into NaN or infinity (sciviz)

- **Repro:** two fused sources (or two components) whose samples both have alpha 2^-26 (any alpha up to 2^-25, as a
  transfer function ramping from 0 gives over a short step) in `FusionLayer` with `mix: 'optical'` or `'over'`.
- **Cause:** `labels-shader.ts` took the union alpha as 1 - (1 - a)(1 - b), which rounds to 0 in float32 for such
  alphas, so `'over'` divided by 0; the optical weights -log(max(1e-7, 1 - a)) were both exactly 0 (0 / 0), and
  under WGSL's 2^-21 absolute error for log near 1 the weights of alphas below about 5e-7 could take either sign. The
  1e-7 clamp also gave an opaque sample a depth of 16.1, so 4% of a half-transparent sample showed through it.
- **Fix:** the union alpha is a + b (1 - a); an optical depth below 1/16 is its Taylor series (at least the alpha),
  above it -log(1 - a); a subnormal alpha counts as 0 (WGSL may flush it) and leaves the other sample; an opaque
  sample wins and two opaque samples split evenly. Every weight is a positive normal float by construction.
- **Regression:** `packages/sciviz/tests/labels.test.js` ("fusion mixing stays finite", float32 at the edge alphas
  with log error of plus and minus 2^-21; failing on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: firelight on the snow under Cabin Hearth's side walls (KB-CABIN-SIDEWALL-LEAK1, procedural)

- **Repro:** Cabin Hearth, `view=outside`: an orange strip on the snow under the right side wall, around x 810 to 850,
  y 455 to 490 of `test-results/cabin-hearth-outside-native.png`.
- **Cause:** the side walls are built with `bottom: log`, half a log above the front and back walls as notched corners
  stack them, and `generateLogWall` started a wall at its bottom course, so only the corner posts reached the ground
  and the lit room showed through the half-log gap under each side wall. A bottom course resting on y = 0 also left a
  slit as high as its lowest facet's depth (3.8 mm for 0.3 m logs of 14 segments) for grazing light.
- **Fix:** a wall standing on the ground is closed down to y = 0 by default (`sill`, default true): a raised wall
  stands on a sill log hewn flat underneath, the half-log starter course log builders use (B. A. Mackie, "Building with
  Logs", 1971; Bomberger 1991), chinked to the course above; a bottom course on y = 0 is chinked to the ground.
  `sill: false` leaves the gap for a foundation built up to the bottom course. Regression:
  packages/procedural/test/log-wall-sill.test.js (6,300 segments from the room to the snow under the side wall, 3,750
  of them got out before).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a strip of light above Cabin Hearth's door looked through the wall (KB-CABIN-DOORLEAK1, procedural)

- **Repro:** Cabin Hearth, `view=outside`: above the door's planks a 25 cm strip showed the fire-lit room, mean sRGB
  88, 47, 35 in the box x 400 to 455, y 300 to 312 of `test-results/cabin-hearth-outside-native.png` against the
  moonlit logs' 32, 32, 37, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer alike. Not a shadow leak: it was there with
  KB-LOCALSHADOW-OFFSET1's receiver-plane filter too.
- **Cause:** `generateLogWall` (packages/procedural/src/cabin.ts) cut away every log an opening overlapped at all. The
  door opening ends at 2.15 m, inside the 2.1 to 2.4 m course, so the wall opened to 2.4 m over a door 2.15 m high: a
  real hole. The window's edges (0.95 and 2.05 m) fell inside courses too and opened 5 cm further each way, hidden by
  its frame.
- **Fix:** openings are cut exactly. A log the opening's top or bottom edge crosses keeps the part outside it: the same
  faceted cross-section clipped by the edge's line (Sutherland and Hodgman, "Reentrant Polygon Clipping", CACM 17(1),
  1974, https://doi.org/10.1145/360767.360802), its sides with the log's vertex normals and a flat cut face, and the
  chinking joins its kept face to the next course. After: the box reads 32, 32, 37 on both backends, the logs'
  own colour. Regression: packages/procedural/test/log-wall.test.js (lines through the wall above the door and
  beside the window's edges hit wood; 336 of them passed before).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: sciviz points and other pixel-sized marks drew target pixels on screen, CSS pixels in export (sciviz, points)

- **Repro:** at devicePixelRatio 2 on the light tier (`globalThis.margoLow = 2`, or a mobile browser, where the engine
  draws one sample and a backing store of 2 pixels per CSS pixel), `fig.scatter({ x: [0], y: [0] }, { size: 20 })`
  covered 20 canvas pixels (10 CSS pixels) on screen, while `exportImage` at scale 1 drew it 20 CSS pixels wide. Point
  cloud layers did the same; flow trail widths, geo-vector line widths and point radii, scatter-matrix points, label
  outlines and density bandwidths were target pixels both on screen and in export (a scale 2 export drew them half
  size), and the 3D graph layer scaled its nodes by window.devicePixelRatio.
- **Cause:** `@margoengine/points` sizes points in pixels of the drawn target, and sciviz passed its CSS sizes to the
  point material, scaling the material only during tiled export; the shader-drawn marks used their sizes as target
  pixels without the frame's pixels per CSS pixel.
- **Fix:** every sciviz pixel size goes through `SciRenderer.cssScale` (the drawn target's width over the canvas CSS
  width, or the export's scale while tiles draw): shaders multiply by the frame's `origin.z`, the 3D graph and density
  layers read it in `prepare`, and `PointsPlugin` gained an internal `pixelScale` hook that scales pixel sizes and
  clamps as the cloud uniform is written, so the material keeps the caller's values. Tiled export no longer edits
  scatter materials.
- **Regression:** `packages/sciviz/tests/pixel-density-browser.mjs` (scatter, GPU graph and geo-vector points at
  devicePixelRatio 1 and 2, desktop and light tier backing stores, on screen and in scale 1 and 2 exports, WebGPU and
  the WebGL2 layer), `packages/points/tests/pixel-scale.test.js`, `packages/sciviz/tests/graph.test.js`,
  `packages/sciviz/tests/density.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: GPU graph nodes and edges sized by window.devicePixelRatio, 2x too large on screen and in export (sciviz)

- **Repro:** at devicePixelRatio 2, `gpuGraphLayer(fig, layout, { nodeSize: 20 })` drew a 40 pixel node on a canvas
  the engine backs at 1 pixel per CSS pixel (the desktop 4x MSAA default) and in an `exportImage` at scale 1 (a 40 CSS
  pixel node); at devicePixelRatio 1 a scale 2 export drew it 20 pixels wide, half its size.
- **Cause:** `graph-gpu-draw.ts` scaled CSS pixel sizes by `globalThis.devicePixelRatio`, which neither the engine's
  capped backing store nor a tiled export's image follows.
- **Fix:** the sciviz frame uniform carries the target's pixels per CSS pixel (`origin.z`, from `SciRenderer.cssScale`:
  the drawn target's width over the canvas CSS width, as lines use, or the export's image width over the CSS width
  while `renderMediaTiles` draws), and the graph shader reads it.
- **Regression:** `packages/sciviz/tests/pixel-density-browser.mjs` (`npm run test:browser:pixel-density`, WebGPU and
  the WebGL2 layer at devicePixelRatio 1 and 2: on screen, scale 1 and scale 2 export; failing on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-17: a film rendered scene by scene restarts the sky, wind, water and weather at every cut (GAP-FILM-TIME, sky, weather, scatter, water, vfx, cutscene)

- **Repro:** render two scenes of one film in two processes (Margo Film Studio does) with clouds, wind and rain: scene
  2's first frame shows the clouds, wind and wetness of second 0, not of the cut's film time.
- **Cause:** every engine clock adds up frame deltas (sky cloud drift, volumetric cloud drift, sky weather, scatter wind,
  Water time inside its draw pass, WeatherMachine, Hail, vfx counters), and a fresh process starts each at 0. No closed
  form fixes it: n additions of 1/fps differ from n x (1/fps) in the last bits, and the wind, wetness and storms
  integrate over state that changes on the way.
- **Fix in progress:** `@margoengine/cutscene/seek` (landed) replays every clock's `advanceTime(1 / fps)` without
  drawing; each time-driven package gains `advanceTime` and `time` in its own commit (sky landed: `Sky`, `HillaireSky`,
  `VolumetricClouds`, `AstroSky`, `Weather`; weather landed: `WeatherMachine`, `WeatherDrive`, `Hail`, `Puddles`,
  `GLTFWeather`, `LensDrops`, `WeatherRegions`; scatter and water landed: `Scatter`, `ScatterInstances`, `Water`,
  `FFTOcean`, `WaterFlow`, `WaterRain`; vfx, taa and tonemap landed: `VFX`, `TAA`, `TAAUpscale`, `Tonemap`; animation
  landed: `Animation`, `PlaybackAnimation`, `AnimationGroup`, `AnimationMixer`, `AnimationLOD`, `MorphWeightPlayer`,
  `VATCrowd`, `GeometryCachePlayer`; shadows and dof landed: `Shadows`, `VirtualShadows`, `lightPattern`, `Autofocus`;
  the sweep landed; sheet row 5 landed the last: vfx `Flame` and `Smoke`, which still added frame deltas with no
  `advanceTime` (the gate was red on them), and the weather events `Avalanche`, `SnowDrift` and `Eruption`, which kept
  film time with `update` alone, so `seek` refused them in `extra`; `TornadoCloud`, `GroundChange` and `Flood` had
  their clocks and now have cut tests too). A `Flame`'s noise seed followed the count of every flame the process had
  made, so a scene drawn after another in one process flickered with other seeds; it now follows the flame's place
  among its engine's flames (the first flame of a fresh process keeps its seed). Changed behaviour with it:
  `Water`'s wave clock moved from its draw pass to its frame update, so hidden water keeps time (it stood still) and two
  views in one frame move it once (they moved it twice). `VFX` counts its step in its frame update and the simulate pass
  runs that step once a frame: a second view in one frame no longer simulates a second step (it doubled the speed; it takes a step of 0 s that
  lists and sorts the particles for its camera), and
  updates with no draw move the clock and drop their births. `Tonemap` moves its grain once a frame update, so every
  view of a frame shows the same grain (each view drew the next one); a stacked Tonemap still moves it per draw. An
  engine-updated `TAA` keeps its jitter phase through `reset()` (the history restarts; the phase restarted at 0 too). `VATCrowd` refuses a negative or non-finite frame delta with a RangeError (it added it to its clock), and a disposed `AnimationGroup`, `MorphWeightPlayer` or `VATCrowd` no longer moves its clock. `renderCutscene` and `cutsceneFrames` with `from` > 0 start the
  world at 0 too (checked in render.ts: the player seeks, the engine clocks do not) and get the same seek. Wall clock in
  drawn output, fixed: `lightPattern` scrolled and `Autofocus` eased by `performance.now()`, so an offline render that
  took seconds per frame jumped the mask and snapped the focus, and two views of a frame scrolled it twice; both now
  count frame time, moved once a frame update by `Shadows`, `VirtualShadows` and `Autofocus` `advanceTime`. Exact particles across a cut
  (GAP-FILM-VFXSEED), exact FFT foam (GAP-FILM-FOAM) and a seek back in one process (GAP-FILM-RESET) are later rows.
- **Regression:** `packages/cutscene/tests/seek.test.js` (seek to n plus one frame equals n + 1 frames, bit for bit),
  `packages/sky/test/seek.test.js` and `packages/sky/test/seek-check.mjs` (the sky, field for field and pixel for pixel),
  `packages/weather/tests/seek.test.js` and `packages/weather/tests/seek-check.mjs` (the weather, the same way),
  `packages/scatter/test/seek.test.js` and `seek-check.mjs`, `packages/water/test/seek.test.js` (hidden water and two
  views included) and `seek-check.browser.mjs`; `packages/vfx/test/seek.test.js` and `seek-check.mjs` (births per step
  exact, live count within 5 %), `packages/tonemap/tests/seek.test.js` and `seek-browser.mjs` (grain exact, exposure
  within e^(-1.5 P)), `packages/taa/test/seek.test.js` and `seek-check.mjs` (phase exact, 1 level after 53 frames);
  `packages/animation/tests/seek.test.js` and `geometry-cache.test.js` (poses, loops, fades and LOD turns exact);
  `packages/shadows/test/effects.test.js` (the pattern scrolls by frame time, once a frame) and
  `packages/dof/tests/dof.test.js` (autofocus eases by frame time);
  `tests/film-time.test.js` with `scripts/check-film-time.mjs` lists every package clock with no `advanceTime` and every
  wall clock or unseeded random in package code (failing since the sweep), and names the clocks that must keep
  `advanceTime`; `packages/vfx/test/seek.test.js` (Flame and Smoke to 54,000 steps, two worlds in one process),
  `packages/weather/tests/seek-events.test.js` (Avalanche, SnowDrift, Eruption through `seekSync` `extra`),
  `packages/sky/test/tornado.test.js` and `packages/terrain/test/ground-change.test.js` (a cut through `seekSync`).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the text browser suites reloaded their page when a served dist was rebuilt (KB-DEVWATCH-TEXT1, text and harness)

- **Repro:** run `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/test-browser.js` in packages/text while `npm run build` of packages/loaders
  (or anything that rewrites `packages/loaders/dist/font-opentype.js`, `packages/core/dist/index.js` or a text test
  module) runs in the same checkout. The page reloaded, and the run failed with `page.evaluate: Execution context was
  destroyed, most likely because of a navigation` at packages/text/scripts/test-browser.js:41 (when written; the `page.evaluate` calls are at :44-46 now) after the first 26 checks. A probe that rewrote
  each of those files once under the suite's server counted one navigation per rewrite.
- **Cause:** the suites build their own Vite server from packages/text/vite.config.js, which starts a chokidar watcher;
  a changed module the page had loaded made Vite send a full reload. `server.watch: null` in the inline config cannot
  fix it, because Vite's mergeConfig skips null values.
- **Fix:** `noFileWatcher()` (scripts/support/no-file-watcher.js, also exported by scripts/browser.js) sets
  `server.watch = null` once the config is resolved. Every Vite `createServer` call in the repository now passes it
  (about 45 suites, pages and scripts that had the same watcher, once filed as KB-DEVWATCH-ALL1). Under a loop that rewrote the loaders dist every second, both
  compat suites passed. Regression: tests/dev-server-watch.test.js (the plugin leaves no FSWatcher on the text config;
  a scan fails on any createServer call without it).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `VectorFont` had no kerning in Node and measured it through the browser in a page (GAP-FILM-TEXT, text)

- **Repro:** `new VectorFont(bytes).kerning('A', 'V')` in Node returned 0 for Source Sans 3 (no `FontFace`), and in a
  page it was 0 until the registered `FontFace` had loaded, so the same text laid out differently in a page, before the
  face loaded and in Node.
- **Cause:** `VectorFont` read advances from the file but took kerning from the browser's shaper through a `FontFace`.
- **Fix:** `VectorFont` is now a `GlyphFieldFont` (then named `OutlineFont`): kerning comes from the file's GPOS pair adjustment (or `kern` table) in
  every environment, runs shape through GSUB `liga` with `ligatures: true`, and a decomposed cluster draws the
  precomposed glyph the font has. Behaviour change: page layouts with a `VectorFont` move slightly where the file's
  kerning and the browser's differ (none on the 20 Source Sans 3 test pairs), and the SDF fallback draws fields built
  from the outlines instead of the browser's canvas.
- **Regression:** `packages/text/tests/vector.test.js` "VectorFont measures from the file and builds each glyph once"
  (fails before: A V kerning 0 in Node, expected -14 units).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a smooth terrain chunk whose createMesh threw was left half drawn and no longer pending (voxel)

- **Repro:** `SmoothTerrainView.attach(engine, { terrain, createMesh })` where `createMesh` throws for the second
  material part of a chunk being meshed again: `update()` threw, the chunk's previous meshes were already disposed,
  the first new part stayed drawn on its own, and the chunk's key was gone from `terrain.dirty`, so it was never
  meshed again.
- **Cause:** `SmoothTerrainView.update` in `packages/voxel/src/smooth.ts` deleted the key from `dirty` and dropped
  the old meshes before building the new ones.
- **Fix:** the new meshes are built first (`#build`, which disposes the ones it made and rethrows on a failure) and
  swapped in only once all are made; the key leaves `dirty` after the swap. Regression:
  `packages/voxel/tests/smooth.test.js` "createMesh that throws leaves the chunk pending and its previous meshes
  drawn".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a light wall beside Fire read as bright as its flames (KB-FIRE-RECEIVER1, scenery and vfx)

- **Repro:** `Fire` 0.4 m in front of a `createMesh` wall of albedo 0.5 with post and TAA (RTX A6000, WebGPU): the wall
  inside the fire's 0.634 m light spheres reads about as bright as the flames, so the flames wash out against it; at
  albedo 0.05 they read. First logged as "the flames vanish after `lights.add(model)`": they do draw, the lit wall
  behind them is as bright.
- **Cause:** `Fire` sizes each point's sphere so its radiance equals the flames' (KB-FIRE-GLINT1), 0.634 m for the
  default hearth, so a nearby wall sits inside the spheres. Inverse square lit it far past the flames there, which
  KB-FIRE-WALLHOT1 bounds at pi times the sphere's radiance; with two points and albedo 0.5 that is still about the
  flames' own radiance. The light is right for spheres that large; the spheres are too large for the flame line.
- **Decided fix (Scott, 2026-11-16, brighter flames):** back to the kit's 0.155 m spheres and flames as bright as them,
  3.5 to 58.5 (about 17 times; sphere radiance 4.5 x 0.568 / (pi 0.155^2) = 33.9 in luminance, over the flames'
  brightest colour luminance 0.579). The wall at 0.4 m would read about 5 against the flames' 33.9.
- **Fix (Scott, 2026-11-16, brighter flames; and 03:39, "Yes to both"):** `snowNight`'s flames are as bright as its
  light, 58.5, derived from the light's colour, intensity and 0.155 m share, so `Fire` keeps the 0.155 m spheres. The
  vfx particle `intensity` accepts 0 to 65,504 (the half-float maximum of its target) instead of 0 to 16, and the kit
  test's cap on the flames' brightness is replaced by measured checks on the render (fire-base-gpu.mjs: orange
  silhouette, white only 3 px or more inside it, at least 4 separate tongues on a row). Measured on an RTX A6000,
  natively and on the WebGL2 layer: the wall at 0.4 m is about 0.11 of the flames (0.91 before); the flame base rise
  is 18.2 and 18.6 px (17.8 and 18.2 before, bound 24); the silhouette is 100% orange, white 4 px in at the nearest,
  19 tongues on a row. The kettle mirrors the brighter flames, at most F0 times them (the existing tie test).
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/fire.test.js` ("a light wall 0.4 m behind the fire stays outside the light
  spheres and two stops under the flames", and the 0.155 m spheres tied to the flames), `packages/vfx/test/vfx.test.js`
  ("intensity accepts any finite value from 0 to the half-float maximum"), `packages/sky/test/fire-base-gpu.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: triplanar stone and brick drew streaks and bands on the hearth's faces (KB-TRIPLANAR-SIDES1, materials)

- **Repro (before):** the Cabin Hearth's jambs, mantel and hearthstone as `createMesh` boxes with the procedural stone
  and brick maps (`new Texture(set.albedo)`, default options) and `triplanar: true`: the right jamb's front showed
  horizontal bands, the mantel's front vertical bands, the hearthstone's top streaks along z. A 2 x 2 checker with
  `wrapS`/`wrapT` `'repeat'` on the same boxes projected correctly; so did the stone through the boxes' own UVs.
  The `triplanar` example of the materials README (a `loadTexture` map, default options) drew the same streaks.
- **Cause:** a `Texture` clamps by default (`wrapS`, `wrapT` `'clamp'`), and the triplanar projection reads each map
  at the world position times `triplanarScale`, which passes [0, 1] past the first tile: the clamp repeated the edge
  texels across the rest of every face. The shading was right; the sampler was not.
- **Fix:** triplanar samples each projected map (UV0 maps, alpha, bump, parallax and thickness maps on UV0) with
  repeat on every axis whose wrap the texture leaves unset; a set wrap, a map on UV1, the displacement map (moved by
  the mesh's own UVs) and the matcap keep their sampler. The texture keeps one extra sampler per device for it.
- **Regression:** `packages/materials/test/surface-features.test.js` "triplanar tiles a map whose wrap is unset
  instead of clamping its edges" (fails before: every slot clamp-to-edge) and the GPU scenario
  `triplanarDefaultWrap` in `packages/materials/test/browser-check.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth lantern threw a crisp, window-shaped patch with bar lines on the snow (KB-CABIN-EDGE-SOFT2, procedural, clustered, scenery)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:cabin-hearth` on `origin/main` 6c5ce35331: the lantern's own light on the snow 3.5 m out is
  0.2313 linear red, cut by the mullion's and cross bar's shadows, and its right edge rises over 0.094 m, the 22 mm
  flame's penumbra (KB-CABIN-GROUNDEDGE1). Physically right for a clear window, but not the soft glow the scene wants.
- **Decision (Scott, 2026-11-16, "Frosted window glass"):** a winter window frosts over inside, and the frost spreads
  the light. The packages own the options and the scene picks one.
- **Fix:** `generateWindowPane` (`@margoengine/procedural`, `glazing: 'clear' | 'frosted'`, `frost`: how far frost has
  grown in from the edges) builds the pane, a shadow caster that stops the beam; `openingLight` (`@margoengine/clustered/area`)
  with `glazing: 'frosted'` adds the lamps' direct light on the pane, re-emitted diffusely, `L = tau_d E / pi`
  (`FROSTED_GLAZING`: transmittance 0.637, reflectance 0.292, from ice's optics and the Eddington approximation), and
  `glazingSurface` gives the pane's faces. `hurricaneLantern` gains `globe: 'clear' | 'frosted' | 'sooted'` (radius
  0.011 m or the 0.065 m globe). Cabin Hearth passes `glazing: 'frosted'`; `glazing=clear` shows the window before.
- **Now:** no beam reaches the snow (0.0000), the pane glows at 3.98 linear red against its predicted 3.86, and the
  patch's edge is 2.07 m wide by its light over its slope, against 2.20 m for a Lambertian pane, on WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000). At the test's patch points, 2.2 m out, the snow reads 352/0.32/0.43 (warm, against the
  moonlit 264/0.21/0.31 beside it): the frost's glow is weaker there than the beam it spreads, so the firelight-orange
  check now runs through clear glass. Tests: packages/procedural/test/glazing.test.js,
  packages/clustered/test/opening-light.test.js, packages/clustered/test/flame-light.test.js,
  scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs. Limits: docs/limits.md, "Frosted window glazing".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth lantern's patch on the snow read mauve, not firelight (KB-CABIN-LANTERN1, scenery)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:cabin-hearth` prints the snow in front of the window, past the sill's shadow (x 1.6 to
  2.0, z 4.0 to 4.1), as hue 318 to 324, saturation 0.10 to 0.11, value 0.44, beside moonlit snow 218/0.38/0.38;
  `origin/main` da24866e63 gives the same 318/0.10/0.44. The lantern does light the snow (luminance above 1.2 times
  the snow beside it, asserted) and takes the blue out of it, but the mix stays a pale mauve: the kit's comment that
  the 1,900 K lantern makes the patch "read as firelight" is not met.
- **Cause:** the kit's lamp (intensity 8, colour [1, 0.48, 0.17], range 6 m) adds about as much light at 2 m as the
  moonlit snow already reflects, so orange plus blue gives a near-neutral pink. A fix sets the lamp's power from a
  real oil lantern's output (or a measured ratio to the moonlight) in `snowNight`; it changes the outside shots'
  look, so it needs a maintainer decision on the new visual baseline.
- **First fix, wrong (c904862f57):** the lamp was set to a "rated 12 candlepower" (Dietz #80 listings) with its
  3,000 K colour: the patch went to 15/0.21/0.62, a dusty pink, still not firelight. Measured from physics it was
  neither the right colour nor the right light.
- **Cause, found from physics (KB-CABIN-LANTERN1, 2026-11-16):** every link was checked against an independent
  prediction. The renderer is right: the lantern's linear radiance on the snow matched inverse square x cosine x the
  range window x the glTF Appendix B BRDF of the snow (colour 0.9, 0.92, 0.95, roughness 0.85) to 1 to 4%. The inputs
  were wrong. (1) Colour: [1, 0.48, 0.17] is a 3,000 K blackbody's linear sRGB, not 1,900 K; a kerosene flame is about
  1,900 K (tabulated; measured kerosene flames 1,580 to 2,290 K, Tatsuta, Trans. JSME B 72(720), 2006,
  doi:10.1299/kikaib.72.1875), [1, 0.2325, 0] by Planck's law on the CIE 1931 2 degree functions (CIE 018:2019,
  doi:10.25039/CIE.DS.xvudnb9b) and the IEC 61966-2-1 matrix. (2) Light: hurricane lanterns measured on a
  goniophotometer gave 8 to 82 lm, 9 to 10 cd at the brightest lantern's horizontal peak, about a third of their
  makers' ratings (E. Mills, "Technical and Economic Performance Analysis of Kerosene Lamps and Alternative Approaches
  to Illumination in Developing Countries", LBNL, 2003); 12 cd is above all of them, and the candle flicker averaged
  0.9 of it. (3) Range: the 6 m window gave the snow 3.3 m out 0.83 of the lantern's inverse square. (4) The patch: the
  test's points on y 0.05 land, along the camera's low ray, on the lifted snow at z 4.6 to 4.7, 3.3 m from the
  lantern, in the upper pane's light. Moonlight: the kit's 0.21 lux normal (0.095 lux on the snow, moon 27 degrees up)
  is a full moon's at that height after extinction (Krisciunas and Schaefer, "A model of the brightness of moonlight",
  PASP 103, 1991), though the sky draws a gibbous moon (phase 0.75); the moon's blue colour is the kit's night look.
- **Fix:** `snowNight`'s lamp is a kerosene hurricane lantern: colour [1, 0.2325, 0] (1,900 K), 82 lm as an isotropic
  point light, 82 / 4 pi = 6.5 cd averaged over its `candle` flicker (intensity 19.1 = 6.53 / (0.379 x 0.9)), range
  18 m (the window keeps 0.99 of the inverse square within 4.9 m). Predicted linear radiance of the lantern on the
  patch, from physics alone: 0.2675, 0.0630, 0; measured on an RTX A6000, natively and on the WebGL2 layer: 0.2561,
  0.0606, 0 (-4%; -2.3% with the lantern's shadow map off). The kit before gave 0.22, 0.11, 0.04 there. With the
  moonlight the patch is linear about 0.28, 0.11, 0.07 and displays 10/0.39/0.65 (hue/saturation/value through the kit's AgX
  grade) against 15/0.21/0.62 before and 322/0.10/0.44 first; the moonlit snow beside it 223/0.33/0.38. The lantern now
  lights the snow out to the foreground as its inverse square says, and the outside shots change look (the review images
  and figures are kept outside the repository). The fire's FIRE_GLOW is also 3,000 K, not the 1,900 K it
  claims (KB-FIRE-GLOW-CCT1, open, below).
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js` "the window lantern's colour is a kerosene flame's, a 1,900 K
  blackbody" (Kim et al. 2002 Planckian fit, independent of the kit's CIE table), "the window lantern gives a measured
  hurricane lantern's light, 82 lm (6.5 cd) averaged over its flicker" and "the window lantern's range leaves its
  inverse square alone where its light matters"; `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` measures the lantern's own
  light on the snow in the linear HDR frame (a steady lantern at its mean, minus none) against the physics prediction
  within 5% per channel. On c904862f57 it reads 0.2159, 0.1050, 0.0381 against 0.2559, 0.0603, 0 and fails.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the fire's glow and the whiteout window were 3,000 to 3,500 K, not a fire's or a flame's colour (KB-FIRE-GLOW-CCT1, math, clustered, scenery)

- **Repro (before):** the blackbody's linear sRGB (Planck's law on the CIE 1931 2 degree functions, IEC 61966-2-1
  matrix, normalised to red) is [1, 0.2325, 0] at 1,900 K and [1, 0.4768, 0.1537] at 3,000 K; `snowNight`'s FIRE_GLOW
  was [1, 0.48, 0.17] and `whiteout`'s window [1, 0.56, 0.24] (about 3,450 K).
- **Cause:** the colours were typed, not computed from a temperature.
- **Fix:** `blackbodyColor` (`@margoengine/math/color`, Kim et al. 2002 Planckian locus, within 0.0004 of the CIE 018:2019
  integration) and `flameLight` (`@margoengine/clustered/flicker`) give every flame its colour from its temperature:
  the hearth at 1,860 K firelight (Zukauskas et al., IEEE Photonics Journal 6(3), 2014; 1,700 to 2,500 K, Zabiliute et
  al., Optics Letters 39(3), 2014), the window lamp at a kerosene flame's 1,900 K (Tatsuta 2006). Each keeps its luminous
  output (5.11 cd and 10.09 cd at the peak), so only the colour moved. Regression: packages/math/test/blackbody.test.js,
  packages/clustered/test/flame-light.test.js and the 1,860 / 1,900 K test in packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js, which
  fail on the 3,000 K values.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: directional hard shadows moved their edges 2.4 texels toward the sun (KB-SUNSHADOW-OFFSET1, clustered)

- **Repro:** `DirectionalLights` with `castShadow` and `LocalShadows` defaults: in `scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js`
  a sun at 58 degrees casts a bar's edge onto the floor with a 256 px map (2.42 cm texels); averaged over 16 positions
  of the map's grid, the lit side ran 5.82 cm (2.4 texels) past the true edge, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer alike.
- **Cause:** the directional filter kept the flat compare and its own 1.5 texel normal offset after
  KB-LOCALSHADOW-OFFSET1 (packages/clustered/src/shadows.ts, `sun[j].w`), which moves a hard edge 1.5 tan(theta)
  texels toward the light. Moving it onto the receiver plane alone raised the Cornell box's directional MAE against
  Mitsuba from 567,377 to 575,408: the plane's texels past the 80-degree contact of the red wall with the zero-thickness
  ceiling read "nothing there" and lit the wall, which the old offset had hidden.
- **Fix:** directional cascades use the same receiver-plane filter (`localShadowPCF`, each cascade's own matrix and
  texel), the shared `normalBias` (0.25) and `receiverPlane` / `slopeBias` options, and leave out every texel whose stored
  depth lies behind the receiver's plane by more than its own offsets (bias + normalBias / N.L texels) plus one texel:
  such a texel shows no part of the receiver, which ended at a contact or an edge, so it cannot vote lit. The rest are
  renormalized; all left out is lit. Point and spot lights keep every texel (their filter and records are unchanged).
  Measured on an RTX A6000, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer alike: the edge now sits 0.98 cm out (the 0.25-texel normal
  offset's own 0.97 cm); no acne at 49, 66, 80 and 85 degrees with true normals, or with normals tilted 10 degrees at
  49 and 66 (at 80 and 85 with `slopeBias` 2); the floor behind a 0.1-high pebble stays dark. The directional Cornell
  box against Mitsuba hard visibility went from absolute 567,377 to 478,366 (square 44,838,153 to 29,281,138, max 165
  to 143; WebGL2 layer 478,365), its record and decomposition re-recorded (Scott, 2026-11-16: "Just fix any bugs you
  find"). Regression: scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js (the directional hard-edge check fails on the old filter),
  packages/clustered/test/light-shadows.test.js and tests/reference-cornell.test.js. Per pixel, 2,426 pixels got worse
  by 92,658 in all and the rest better by 181,669. The largest loss: a strip about 4 px wide along the red wall's
  contact with the zero-thickness ceiling stays lit (1 to 2 px before), because the receiver's own offsets put it
  2.4 texels of depth toward the sun at 80 degrees, past the ceiling; a closed (thick) ceiling would not leak there.

### Measured 2026-11-16: point and spot hard shadows keep every texel of the receiver-plane filter (KB-LOCALSHADOW-CONTACT1, clustered)

- **Question:** KB-SUNSHADOW-OFFSET1 leaves out directional texels whose stored depth lies behind the receiver's plane
  (Cornell 575,408 to 478,366). Do point and spot lights (`localShadowPCF` with `behind` 0) leak the same way?
- **Measured** on an RTX A6000 with the same test in each face's own perspective depth (the margin is the depth step of
  the receiver moved bias + normalBias / N.L + 1 texels away from the light): the point Cornell box against Mitsuba went
  from absolute 597,154 to 597,285 (WebGL2 layer 597,155 to 597,282), slightly worse; the point and spot 256 px hard
  edges stayed at 1.14 and 0.58 cm, and the acne and pebble checks passed unchanged. The point scene has no grazing
  thin-occluder contact like the directional box's ceiling over its red wall, so nothing leaks there.
- **Kept:** point and spot lights keep every texel (no extra matrix product per shaded pixel for no measured gain).
  `packages/clustered/test/light-shadows.test.js` pins that the point and spot call passes `behind` 0 while the
  directional cascades pass their margin; the point Cornell record stays 597,154 (tests/reference-cornell.test.js).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: LocalShadows' normal offset moved a shadow's edge 1.5 texels' worth off its caster, lighting 6 cm of the Cabin Hearth's cross-bar shadow (KB-LOCALSHADOW-OFFSET1, clustered)

- **Repro:** Cabin Hearth, `view=outside&fog=0&snow=0`, linear HDR, the lantern steady: on the snow 4.4 to 4.5 m out
  (3.3 m from the lantern, 256 px cube faces) the window's cross bar blocks the lantern from 10% of the old patch's
  pixels; the render darkened them by 1.8% with the default offsets (bias 1, normalBias 1.5 texels), WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer alike. In `scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js` (a bar lit from 3.8 m at 58 degrees, 256 px maps, the
  50% crossing averaged over 16 light positions) the lit side ran 7.09 cm past the true edge for a point light and
  3.85 cm for a spot, and a floor lit at 80 to 85 degrees showed acne (visibility down to 0.87).
- **Cause:** `clusterShadow` moved the receiver 1.5 texels along its normal whatever its angle to the light
  (packages/clustered/src/shadows.ts), which moves a hard edge 1.5 tan(theta) texels toward the light, and compared all
  3x3 taps with one depth, which needs that offset against acne on sloped receivers. Scaling the offset by sin(theta) or
  1 - N.L (Holbert, GDC 2011) barely shrinks it at 58 degrees.
- **Fix:** the hard point and spot filter (`localShadowPCF`) reads the 4x4 texels of the 3x3 bilinear taps
  and compares each with the depth of the receiver's tangent plane on that texel's ray (Isidoro, GDC 2006; per texel as
  Dou et al., I3D and JCGT 2014), lifted 1 + `slopeBias` (default 0) times the plane's rise and never below the
  receiver's depth. Default point and spot `normalBias` 0.25 (was 1.5), which covers shading normals tilted 10 degrees
  at up to 66 degrees; directional cascades kept the flat compare and 1.5 texels (fixed later as KB-SUNSHADOW-OFFSET1). New
  options `receiverPlane` (default true; false is the old filter) and `slopeBias` (2 for normal maps at 80 to 85
  degrees, docs/limits.md). Measured on an RTX A6000:
  the edge now sits 1.14 cm out for the point light and 0.58 cm for the spot (the 0.25-texel normal offset's own
  1.18 and 0.66 cm), no acne at 49 to 85 degrees with true normals or at 49 to 66 degrees with tilted ones, the floor behind a 0.1-high pebble stays
  dark, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer (the same figures).
  The point Cornell box against Mitsuba hard visibility (`scripts/reference-rendering/cornell.mjs --point`) went from
  absolute 730,273 to 597,154 (square 19,557,045 to 14,188,684, max 156 to 135, WebGL2 layer 730,276 to 597,155), its
  record and decomposition re-recorded on Scott's ruling; the directional Cornell still measures its recorded 567,377.
  Regression: scripts/clustered-shadow-gpu-check.js (the
  hard-edge, grazing-acne and pebble checks fail on the old filter) and packages/clustered/test/shadows.test.js.
  `scripts/clustered-shadow-atlas-gpu.mjs` aims its 32 px blue spot at the probe point: aimed straight down the block's
  own shadow edge was 1.4 texels off the point, which the correct filter shades to 0.91; the old offset had moved the
  lookup 1.2 m off it.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth lantern's patch read 4.3% under its physics prediction (KB-LANTERN-SHADOW-DIM1, scenery test)

- **Repro:** `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` before this fix: the lantern-only patch 0.2561, 0.0606, 0 against
  the prediction's 0.2675, 0.0630, 0 (5% tolerance); with the lantern's shadow map off 0.2607.
- **Cause:** not the renderer. The prediction took one ray through each 7 x 7 px box's centre, 2% over the box mean the
  frame gives, and the boxes' top rows lay in the cross bar's shadow (the 1.8% was that shadow, made lighter by
  KB-LOCALSHADOW-OFFSET1, not cube-map filtering darkening a lit point: on a fully lit patch the shadow map changes it by
  under 0.0001).
- **Fix:** the test predicts every pixel of the boxes (its camera ray from the inverse view projection, the kit's range
  window) and the window bars' shadow on each, and samples the patch 0.65 m further out, all lit. Measured 0.2310,
  0.0547, 0 against 0.2319, 0.0546, 0 on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; the tolerance is the measurement's (repeat spread
  0.0001 times 3, plus half an 8-bit code of each frame), about 1% in red, from 5%.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth rug check was borderline on the WebGL2 compatibility layer (KB-CABIN-RUG-RATIO1, scenery test)

- **Repro:** `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` before this fix: the rug's fire-lit to unlit ratio read 3.05, 3.93
  and 3.64 on the WebGL2 layer and 3.90, 3.35 and 3.38 on WebGPU over three runs each, and once 2.94 (bound 3).
- **Cause:** the hearth frames were read with the fire (0.5 to 1 of its intensity) and the lantern (0.8 to 1) still
  flickering, at whatever phase the frame times had reached; the backends render the same scene the same (held steady,
  fire-lit 0.0503 and unlit 0.0140 on both). The lantern's new light (0.25 lux on the rug, the fire 1.10 lux before the
  hearthstone's lip) leaves the steady ratio at 3.60.
- **Fix:** both hearth frames hold the lights at their flickers' means (0.75 and 0.9, measured in
  packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js) and assert no light changed while the frame settled, which fails on the old frames.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth moon lit the snow as a full moon while the sky drew it at phase 0.75 (KB-CABIN-MOON1, sky, scenery)

- **Repro (before):** `snowNight` set its own moonlight, intensity 0.32 in [0.55, 0.66, 1], 0.21 lux on a surface facing
  the moon: a full moon after extinction (Krisciunas and Schaefer 1991), while the sky drew phase 0.75. Without a set
  intensity the sky lit every scene with a tenth of the sun's strength, whatever the phase.
- **Cause:** the sky's moon light was a free number, not the drawn moon's.
- **Fix:** `moonlight` (`@margoengine/sky/moonlight`, used by `Sky` whenever `lighting.moon` has no `intensity`) derives the
  illuminance from the drawn moon's phase, altitude and the air's extinction (Krisciunas and Schaefer 1991, eq. 3 and 20)
  and the colour from moonlight's own (B - V 0.92, 4,943 K) with the night blue shift of Jensen et al. ("Night
  Rendering", UUCS-00-016, 2000). The kit sets `moon: {}`: 0.078 lux at its defaults. Regression:
  packages/sky/test/moonlight.test.js (fails on the old main: no `moonlight`, and the sky's 0.1 default).
- **Followed by:** KB-MOON-EXAMPLES1 (below): cloud cover, brightness and the lightning light in the sky package.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: scenes set their own moon and faked cloud dimming and lightning with numbers (KB-MOON-EXAMPLES1, sky, scenery, examples)

- **Repro (before):** examples/storm-light dimmed its moon by hand with the storm (`1.2 * (1 - 0.5 * ramp)`), pumped it
  with each flash (`moon.intensity = moonLight + flash * 3`) and lit the flash with its own point light (4e6 cd, 420 m
  up); the whiteout kit set `moon: {intensity: 0.18, color: [0.62, 0.7, 0.9]}` for an overcast moon. The sky had no
  cloud dimming, no brightness option and no lightning light, so every scene had to invent one.
- **Cause:** the sky package lacked the options; scenes filled the gap with numbers the package did not understand.
- **Fix:** `lighting.moon.cloudCover` (default the `clouds` sheet's coverage) dims the scene's moonlight by
  `cloudTransmittance`, 1 - 0.75 cover^3.4 (Kasten and Czeplak, Solar Energy 24, 1980), recoloured for the dimmer level
  (`moonlightColor`, Jensen et al. 2000); `sky.lights[1]` stays the light above the cloud and `sky.moonUnderClouds` is
  what the engine light takes. `lighting.moon.brightness` scales the moon. `Weather.lightningLight`
  (`@margoengine/sky/weather`) is a point light at the strike, 700 m up the channel (Jordan and Uman 1983), carrying a
  first stroke's measured light (Guo and Krider 1982, Quick and Krider 2017, a 30,000 K channel by Orville 1968):
  1.43e7 cd at the flash envelope's peak; `lightning.hold` and `lightning.light` adjust it. storm-light keeps its own
  moon (`intensity` 1.2) with the deck's cover as `cloudCover` and lists `weather.lightningLight`; the whiteout kit
  sets `moon: {cloudCover: 1}`. Regression: packages/sky/test/moonlight.test.js (cloud cover and brightness) and
  packages/sky/test/weather.test.js (the lightning light), both failing on the old main.
- **Looks:** Whiteout Pass's moon light 0.172 to 0.025 (0.06 lux of a half moon, a quarter through the overcast) in
  the night blue; storm-light's moon 0.74 to 0.88 at storm 0.78; a held flash now lights the cliffs, sea and froxel fog
  from the strike. No recorded baseline covers these scenes (gameplay-sandbox and windy-meadow baselines are daytime).
  The review images are kept outside the repository.
- **Still open:** storm-light's in-cloud flash (`deck.options.flash`, 1.6e6 per flash) and its fog ambient pump are
  scene numbers for the flash's light in the cloud and the air; the Whiteout Pass moon stood in for twilight, which the
  sky does not light the scene with (the sky's sun light is 0 below the horizon).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Storm Light set its lightning-lit cloud deck and fog by hand (KB-STORM-OPTIONS1, sky, environment)

- **Repro (before):** examples/storm-light/main.ts set `deck.options.flash` to `weather.flash * 1.6e6` at 950 m over
  its own copy of the strike's place, and `fog.options.ambient` to `0.004 + flash * 0.06` (and so on) every frame;
  no package gave either light, so every other storm had to copy the numbers.
- **Cause:** the weather gave only the scene's point light (`lightningLight`); the clouds and the fog had no source
  for a flash's light.
- **Fix:** `Weather.cloudFlash` with `lightning.cloud` (`base`, `peak`, `radius`): the stroke's light given off above
  the cloud base, `lightningCloudShare(base)` = e^(-base / 700 m) of it, centred 700 m above the base (Jordan and Uman
  1983), in candela, for `VolumetricClouds` `flash`. `VolumetricFog` `lightning` (`light`, `albedo`): the deck the
  flash lights adds `albedo E / (2 pi)` to the fog's ambient, `E = I / d^2` at the camera, `CLOUD_ALBEDO` 0.8 (Twomey
  1977). Storm Light passes both as options. Regression: packages/sky/test/weather.test.js (cloudFlash) and
  packages/environment/tests/volumetric.test.js (lightning), failing on the old main.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: twilight scenes were too dark, the sky gave no light once the sun had set (KB-TWILIGHT1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** `Sky.attach(engine, {hours: 18.4, lighting: {intensity: 108437}})` (the sun 6 degrees down):
  `engine.lighting.direction[3]` was 0; the Whiteout Pass at 18.4 h was lit only by the moon behind the overcast,
  0.012 lux (review images kept outside the repository).
- **Cause:** the sky's sun light is the transmitted direct beam, 0 once the disc has set, and nothing stood for the
  twilight sky; the whiteout kit's old moon number (0.18) had stood in for it.
- **Fix:** `lighting.twilight` (default on): USNO Circular 171's sky illuminance against the sun's altitude, coloured
  by single Rayleigh scattering through the ozone layer (Hulburt 1953) with the night shift, from the sun's side 45
  degrees up, `sky.twilightLight`; `brightness`, `cloudCover`, `color`, `false`. `SUN_ILLUMINANCE` (108,437 lux) puts
  the sun on the moon's lux scale. The whiteout kit lights in lux with `twilight: {cloudCover: 1}`: its engine light
  went from the moon's 0.012 lux to the twilight's 1.06 lux facing it (0.75 lux on the ground, a quarter of 2.99), the
  snow on roofs and trees now reads (review images kept outside the repository). The twilight takes the sky's light
  over from the environment by the sky's night blend (the environment draws the day sky times one minus it), so it
  grows in from the sun 4.6 degrees up instead of switching on at 756 lux at sunset, and the engine light is the
  beam plus the twilight summed as irradiance vectors (it turns up toward the glow as the disc sets, in the sun's
  vertical plane); the moon takes over as a body only while both are dim, under 0.05 of a 6 noon. Regression:
  packages/sky/test/twilight.test.js and packages/sky/test/sky.test.js (the dusk handover), failing on the old main.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a scene could not call a half, waning, bright, dim or red moon by name (KB-MOON-PRESETS1, sky)

- **Repro (before):** `Sky.attach(engine, {night: {moonPhase: 'full'}, lighting: {moon: {color: 'blood'}}})` threw a
  RangeError; the phase was a bare number, a waning moon could not be drawn (the lit limb was always the right one, a
  documented limit), and a bright or red moon was a hand-picked `brightness` or RGB that left the drawn disc as it was.
- **Cause:** the sky had no presets: `night.moonPhase`, `lighting.moon.brightness` and `lighting.moon.color` took
  numbers only, the night shader had no flag for the limb, and `brightness` and `color` never reached the disc.
- **Fix:** `night.moonPhase` takes the eight phase names (and `'half'`, `'quarter'`) at the synodic octants (Meeus
  1998, ch. 49); a waning name sets flag 3, which turns the lit limb in the night shader (WGSL and its WebGL2 twin).
  `lighting.moon.brightness: 'bright' | 'dim'` and `color: 'blood' | 'reddened'` come from `moonLook`: the perigee
  supermoon (x1.164 light, disc 1.079 wide; Meeus ch. 50), thin cloud (x0.5; USNO Circular 171), the eclipsed moon
  (x1.06e-4, V -2.8 at totality against -12.74, reddened along a limb chord 12 km up; Garcia Munoz and Palle 2011)
  and the moon 5 degrees up (Kasten and Young 1989 airmass 10.3). Each changes the light and the drawn disc, the
  disc as the eye judges it (Stevens 1961); a number `brightness` now scales the disc too. The option types are
  string-literal unions (api/breaks.json records the widening). Regression: packages/sky/test/moonlight.test.js
  (named phases, the waning limb in WGSL and GLSL, bright and dim, red moons), failing on the old main.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a still TAA view never settled, and its history was resampled every frame (KB-TAA-STILL1, KB-TAA-CLAMP1, taa)

- **Repro (before):** `packages/taa/test/still-browser.mjs` on a bright scene with the camera still: 2.4% of the pixels
  changed between frames, up to 189 sRGB levels at thin wires and small highlights (the Orrery: 0.23% to 0.36%, max d 241).
  `packages/taa/test/converge-browser.mjs` with `settle: false`: 8 px sine stripes converged on 113.91 against the
  equal-weight mean of the 8 jitter phases, 103.4 (KB-TAA-CLAMP1).
- **Cause (STILL1):** the per-frame resolve blends one jitter phase into a history clamped to that phase's
  neighbourhood, so it cycles through the 8 phases forever; a colour range cannot tell that from a moving object.
- **Cause (CLAMP1):** not the min/max box. The resolve fetched history by the whole velocity, which holds the jitter
  difference (both matrices are jittered), so a still view's history was bilinearly resampled up to 0.8 px away every
  frame and blurred. A 1D model of the resolve (fetch in place: the clamp converges on the mean; shifted: 114.08) matched
  the GPU's 113.91.
- **Fix:** `settle` (`packages/taa/src/settle.ts`, default true): a pixel whose 3x3 render footprint has matched its own
  sample of the phase a cycle ago for a whole cycle shows the mean of one jitter cycle and keeps it; any mismatch, a
  camera move, a reset or a reactive pixel hands it back. The resolve fetches history at the pixel centre minus the velocity
  plus `taa.velocity.jitter` (`Temporal.offset`); `taa.velocity` is unchanged. Still frames change on 0% of pixels (max 0);
  the per-frame resolve converges on 103.25 (102.90 to 103.43); a reactive trail is -1.33.
- **Regression:** `packages/taa/test/still-browser.mjs`, `settle-reactive-browser.mjs`, `converge-browser.mjs`,
  `rejection-browser.mjs` (GPU, in `test:gpu`), `packages/taa/test/settle.test.js` and `converge.test.js` (CPU). Docs:
  `packages/taa/README.md`, `docs/limits.md`, `docs/architecture/operational-playbook.md`, `docs/whitepaper/claims.md`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the Cabin Hearth kettle mirrored a fire 17 times brighter than its flames (KB-FIRE-GLINT1, vfx)

- **Repro:** the kettle spout over `Fire`'s flame line peaked at linear luminance 10.44 (clustered-shadow fixture,
  tarnishedCopper) and clipped white on screen (display 254.6), brighter than the flames above it.
- **Cause:** each fire point was a 0.155 m sphere light of intensity 4.5: radiance 4.5 x 0.568 / (pi 0.155^2) = 33.9
  in luminance, while the flames it stands for show at most 3.5 x 0.579 = 2.03. Clustered bounds a sphere light's
  highlight by F0 times the sphere's radiance, so the kettle mirrored a source 17 times the drawn fire.
- **Fix:** `Fire` sizes each point's sphere so its radiance equals the flames' brightest radiance (0.634 m for the
  default hearth; the shadow keeps 0.155 m; `power` scales both, so the size does not change with it). Spout peak
  0.887 against the bound 0.92 (tarnishedCopper's F0 for the firelight's colour, 0.453, times 2.03).
- **Regression:** `packages/vfx/test/fire.test.js` "the sphere each light shows on a metal is no brighter than the
  flames, at any power" (fails before: sphere 33.87 against flames 1.01 at power 0.5).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `shadows.add(mesh)` cast the mesh and not the meshes parented to it (KB-SHADOW-GROUP2, shadows)

- **Repro (before):** a Blender car whose body mesh has geometry and parents the wheels: `shadows.add(body)` cast the
  body and none of the wheels, the same trap as KB-SHADOW-GROUP1 one level over. A wheel parented after the add never
  cast either.
- **Cause:** KB-SHADOW-GROUP1 walked only nodes with no geometry; a mesh with its own geometry was registered as one
  caster and its children were ignored.
- **Fix:** `add(node)` on `Shadows` and `VirtualShadows` has one rule for every node: it casts itself (when it has
  geometry) and every mesh with geometry below it, parented now or later (packages/shared/shadow-group.js). A mesh with
  no children costs one property read a frame; the steady-frame GPU calls of scenes that add childless meshes are
  identical (1, 200 and 1,000 casters: same calls and draws before and after; first frame and still frame). A child
  also added by hand is cast once, in either order: the hand add takes over from the walk, and removing it leaves the
  child cast through its parent.
- **Regression:** packages/shadows/test/parent-mesh.test.js (6 of its 8 cases fail without the fix); docs:
  packages/shadows/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a mirror in view stepped TAA's jitter twice a frame (KB-FILM-TAAPHASE1, taa, tonemap, vfx)

- **Repro (before):** `scripts/env-mirror-gpu-check.js`, 1x, "TAA mirror after a move under history equals a fresh
  history (no ghost)": p99 5 against 4 (mean 0.137, max 21, 7,509 px), the same on WebGPU and the WebGL2
  compatibility layer.
- **Cause:** a `Reflector`, `Refractor` or `CubeCamera` capture renders the scene with `engine.render({camera, delta:
  0})`, and every render calls each plugin's `onPreUpdate`. Since TAA's phase followed frame updates (GAP-FILM-TIME 5),
  that zero-delta update stepped it too, so with a mirror in view TAA drew only the even Halton phases (4 jitter samples,
  not 8) and its still-view settle, which compares each phase with the same phase one cycle ago and counts matches from
  the previous phase's slot, read slots one frame stale: settle counts in the mirror never passed 3 to 15 and two
  identical runs after `reset()` differed by up to 142 levels. Tonemap's grain frame and VFX's birth seed number moved
  on the same update (VFX also dropped its prewarm when a capture came first).
- **Fix:** an update with a delta of 0 is the same instant drawn again and moves no counter; the next resolved (TAA,
  TAAUpscale) or drawn (Tonemap) frame takes the one step a frame gets if no timed update came first, and VFX lets the
  pass take its 0 s step. Seeks, which replay timed steps, are unchanged. The mirror check now reads p99 0, max 0 at 1x
  and 4x on both backends.
- **Regression:** packages/taa/test/seek.test.js, packages/tonemap/tests/seek.test.js, packages/vfx/test/seek.test.js
  (each new case fails without the fix) and scripts/env-mirror-gpu-check.js; docs: packages/taa/README.md,
  packages/tonemap/README.md, packages/vfx/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `UiRenderer.attach` threw in headless Node with its defaults (KB-FILM-UI-NODE, ui)

- **Repro (before):** `UiRenderer.attach(engine, ui)` on a `@margoengine/headless` canvas threw
  `e.addEventListener is not a function` (default `input: true`), and with `input: false` threw
  `reading 'createElement'` (default accessibility mirror). Only `{ input: false, mirror: false }` drew a lower third
  (`packages/text/tests/outline-scene.mts`).
- **Cause:** `UiRenderer.setup` attached input and the mirror to any canvas, though a headless canvas has no event
  listeners and no document.
- **Fix:** `setup` skips input when the canvas has no `addEventListener` and the mirror when it has no
  `ownerDocument`; the README attach works in Node as written, and a DOM canvas is unchanged.
- **Regression:** packages/ui/tests/headless-attach.test.js (fails without the fix); docs: packages/ui/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `LensDrops.attach` refused a scene that already had a PostStack (GAP-POST-ADD1-WEATHER, weather)

- **Repro (before):** `PostStack.attach(engine, [bloom])`, then `await LensDrops.attach(engine)` rejected with
  `TypeError: Invalid plugin` (the plugin name `post:stack` repeated): the lens made its own one-effect stack.
- **Fix:** `attach` joins the scene's stack with `PostStack.join(engine, lens)` (after the last HDR effect), as the
  water, creative, cameras and shader effects do; `dispose()` takes the lens out with `removeEffect`, and a stack made
  for it goes with it.
- **Regression:** packages/weather/tests/lens-stack-join.test.js (fails first with `Invalid plugin`); docs:
  packages/weather/README.md, docs/conventions.md, docs/limits.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `shadows.add(group or model root)` was accepted and cast nothing (KB-SHADOW-GROUP1, shadows, gltf/pbr)

- **Repro (before):** a glTF car loaded with `@margoengine/gltf/pbr`'s `loadGLTF`, a floor, the sun at 32 degrees:
  `shadows.add(car.root)` raised no error and changed 0 pixels; `shadows.add(car)` darkened 4,565. The same for any
  mesh that only parents others. `add()` took the node itself, and a node with no geometry that is no glTF PBR
  primitive node has no casters. Its error text promised a group. A bench that looped over `car.meshes ?? []` also
  cast nothing, since `@margoengine/gltf/pbr`'s `loadGLTF` returned `nodes` and `primitives` where the light
  `@margoengine/gltf` returns `meshes`.
- **Cause:** `Shadows.casters()` and `VirtualShadows` read only the added node. There was no walk below a group,
  and the two loaders named `loadGLTF` returned different shapes.
- **Fix:** `add(group)` on `Shadows` and `VirtualShadows` casts every mesh with geometry below the group and each
  glTF PBR model below it once (packages/shared/shadow-group.js). The group is walked once a frame before the casters
  are read, so a mesh parented later casts from the next frame, a mesh moved out stops, and the remover or disposing
  the group drops them; the casters are ordinary registrations with the group's options. No group added: no walk, and
  the steady-frame GPU calls of scenes that add single meshes are identical (1, 7, 200 and 1,000 casters, still and
  moving, the first, a steady and an orbiting frame: same calls, bytes and draws before and after). A mesh with its own
  geometry cast itself only (changed by KB-SHADOW-GROUP2). `PBRModel` gains a `meshes` getter (its primitive nodes, once each), the shape the
  light loader returns.
- **Regression:** packages/shadows/test/group-casters-browser.mjs (real GPU, WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer; on the old
  code the group, model-root and late checks read 1.0 of the open light), packages/shadows/test/group.test.js (draws
  equal adding each mesh, late and leaving meshes, the remover, a duplicate, a disposed group) and
  packages/gltf/test/meshes.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: the sky showed through the seams between a log cabin's logs (KB-CABIN-SEAM1, procedural)

- **Repro (before):** `tools/shot/shots/cabin-window-snow.json`, open probe at 1080 x 1920 on the RTX A6000: the sky
  coverage record (`sky-coverage`) marked 413 pixels in one-pixel lines on the back wall seen through the window
  (rows 863 to 963) and more at the right-hand corner, 451 in all: no geometry covered them, and the frame showed
  them as light lines.
- **Cause:** Cabin Hearth and Whiteout Pass stacked their own faceted cylinders (14 and 12 segments) at a pitch of one
  diameter. A facet's flat sits r (1 - cos(pi / n)) inside the log's circle, so every course line left a slit straight
  through the wall, 0.75 cm for the 0.3 m logs, about 1.5 pixels at the shot's distance.
- **Fix:** `generateLogWall` in @margoengine/procedural builds a log wall with chinking along every course line where
  both logs exist, inside the logs' inscribed circles so it shows only where it fills the slit; both demos build
  their walls with it. After: 0 sky pixels inside the wall (451 fewer, none added). Regression:
  packages/procedural/test/log-wall.test.js (lines through every course line, straight and oblique, 6 to 24 segments
  and a gable; 45,568 of 87,576 pass the bare logs) and tests/log-wall-demos.test.js (both demos use it).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a thin spot beam through VolumetricFog drew as a row of separate blocks (KB-FOG-BEAM1, environment)

- **Repro:** `examples/storm-light/index.html?tour=0&beam=0.3&storm=0.78&temporal=0` at 1080 x 1920, camera at
  (38, 3.5, 58) looking at (2, 26, 0): the lighthouse beam, two ClusteredLight spots (half-angle 0.045 rad, penumbra
  0.55, range 600 m) seen through the froxel fog, crosses the frame as evenly spaced soft blocks with dark gaps on both
  sides of the lantern. Measured along the right beam's screen path: 15 gaps, worst dip 0.98 of the beam's level. The
  published Storm Light short shows it; temporal accumulation hides it only while camera and beam stand still.
- **Cause:** `packages/environment/src/volumetric.ts` took each clustered light at four points per slice on each
  froxel's centre ray. A cone narrower than the spacing of those points in depth, or than a froxel row across (about
  0.63 m at 70 m in portrait), lit only the froxels whose points fell inside it and missed the rest.
- **Fix:** each slice is split in four parts with a cluster lookup each, and every light is integrated over each
  part instead of sampled: the part's chord inside the range sphere and the outer cone is solved exactly (Eberly,
  "Intersection of a Line and a Cone", 2000), the inverse-square term is the closed form (atan(b) - atan(a)) / h (Sun,
  Ramamoorthi, Narasimhan and Nayar, "A Practical Analytic Single Scattering Model for Real Time Rendering", 2005;
  Pegoraro and Parker, "An Analytical Solution to Single Scattering in Homogeneous Participating Media", 2009) and the
  smooth rest is taken at 2 jittered equiangular points (Kulla and Fajardo, "Importance Sampling Techniques for Path
  Tracing in Participating Media", 2012). A cone thinner than the froxel is widened by the froxel's size seen from the
  light with its energy kept, footprint prefiltering after Toksvig ("Mipmapping Normal Maps", 2005) and Kaplanyan,
  Hill, Patney and Lefohn ("Filtering Distributions of Normals for Shading Antialiasing", HPG 2016). 8 points per part
  measured the same within run noise (continuity check 0.760 to 1.184 against 0.762 to 1.186; Storm Light worst dip
  0.14 against 0.13) at four times the light evaluations, so 2 stay. Storm Light after the fix, bearings 0.3, 0.6 and
  0.9 with temporal off: 0 gaps, worst dip at most 0.205.
- **Regression:** `npm run test:fog-beam-continuity:browser -w @margoengine/environment`
  (packages/environment/tests/volumetric-beam-continuity-browser.js, WebGPU then the WebGL2 layer: a beam 0.2 m across
  in froxels 0.4 m wide and 1.3 m tall; each column must hold 0.7 to 1.3 of its true light and L1 under 0.2; the old
  code held 0 to 0.511, now 0.762 to 1.186, L1 0.140). `npm run test:fog-beam:browser` now compares with the
  scattering averaged over each froxel's area (beam L1 0.044, bulb 0.004, limit 0.05 unchanged).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a surface drew infinite heights as spikes and wrote its destroyed buffer after dispose (sciviz)

- **Repro:** `figure.surface(z)` with some heights `Infinity` or `-Infinity` drew triangles out to infinity there,
  while `vectorGeometry()` and the colour range (`extent`) skip those heights as holes, as they do NaN. Separately,
  `surface.setHeights(values)` after `surface.dispose()` wrote to the destroyed height buffer (a WebGPU validation
  error) instead of throwing like `readValues`.
- **Cause:** the surface shader's hole test in `packages/sciviz/src/surface.ts` matched NaN bit patterns only
  (`> 0x7f800000`), and `setHeights` did not check `#disposed`.
- **Fix:** the hole test (`missing`) matches every non-finite height (`>= 0x7f800000`), for culling and for the
  one-sided normals beside a hole; `setHeights` throws a `disposed` error. Regression tests:
  `packages/sciviz/tests/surface-repeat-browser.mjs` (an Infinity or -Infinity hole draws the same pixels as a NaN
  hole, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) and `tests/updates.test.js` "a disposed surface refuses setHeights ...".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the table aggregation kernel broke WGSL's function-variable limit and ran on the CPU on WebGL2 (sciviz)

- **Repro:** `aggregateTable(table, { x: { column: 'x', bins: 4096, range }, value: 'v', gpu })` built a kernel with
  five 4,096-entry function arrays (80 KB, past the 8,192 bytes WGSL section 2.4 lets an implementation cap function
  variables at); on the WebGL2 compatibility layer every call over 204 bins stored more than 1,024 words per
  invocation and ran on the CPU (`device.dispatches.cpu` grew).
- **Cause:** the kernel in `packages/sciviz/src/table-aggregate.ts` gave each 256-row tile one invocation holding
  count, valid, sum, min and max arrays for every bin, then stored all of them.
- **Fix:** the host sorts each tile's finite values by bin in row order (counting sort); one invocation per
  (tile, bin) reduces its contiguous run with three stores and no arrays, so results are unchanged (same f32 order).
  Regression tests: `packages/sciviz/tests/table-browser.mjs` (4,096 bins, 64 x 64 and 4,096 x 1, GPU equal to the
  CPU path on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer, no CPU dispatch) and `tests/table.test.js` "the GPU aggregation kernel
  keeps no per-bin arrays ...".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Parquet FLOAT16, JSON and ENUM columns read as hex text (sciviz)

- **Repro:** `readParquet` on a file with a `FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY(2)` column annotated with the FLOAT16 logical type
  returned hex strings such as `'003c'` instead of 1; a `BYTE_ARRAY` column annotated JSON or ENUM returned hex instead
  of its UTF-8 text. pyarrow and pandas read them as half floats and strings.
- **Cause:** `field()` in `packages/sciviz/src/table-parquet.ts` treated only the STRING logical type and the UTF8
  converted type as text and knew no FLOAT16 logical type, so every other byte array fell through to hex.
- **Fix:** following the Parquet format's `parquet.thrift` and `LogicalTypes.md` (Apache Parquet, read 2026-11-15),
  FLOAT16 (logical type 15, FIXED[2]) reads as a little-endian IEEE binary16 number; JSON (12) and ENUM (4), and the
  JSON (19) and ENUM (4) converted types, read as UTF-8 text; UUID (14, FIXED[16], big-endian) reads as its
  8-4-4-4-12 hex text with unit `uuid`. A FLOAT16 or UUID annotation on another width is refused. Regression test:
  `packages/sciviz/tests/table.test.js` "Parquet FLOAT16 reads as half floats ..." on a hand-built file
  (`annotatedParquet` in `tests/table-writers.js`).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: voxel faces shaded from the wrong ray in any view not covering the whole target (voxel render)

- **Repro (before):** `engine.render({ views })` with two views side by side through one camera
  (`viewport: [0, 0, 0.5, 1]` and `[0.5, 0, 0.5, 1]`) over a `VoxelRenderer` world: the halves should match, but
  23,209 of 38,400 pixels differed (textures, AO and light taken from another pixel's ray).
- **Cause:** `voxelHit` in `packages/voxel/src/render.ts` mapped a fragment position to NDC with the whole target's
  size, but fragment positions count from the target's corner and each view covers only its own rectangle.
- **Fix:** the frame uniform carries the view's size and corner (the whole target without views) and `voxelHit` takes
  the corner off before mapping into the view. Regression: `packages/voxel/tests/render-browser-check.mjs`
  "two views side by side through one camera" (0 pixels differ, WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility layer).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a voxel tick rule that threw dropped the rest of its tick's updates (voxel ticks)

- **Repro (before):** `VoxelTicks.attach(world, { rules: { marker: { scheduled } } })` with two updates scheduled for
  the same tick and a `scheduled` hook that throws on the first: after the throw `pending` stayed 1 forever and the
  second update never ran. A `placed` hook that threw likewise dropped every later change of that tick.
- **Cause:** `tick` in `packages/voxel/src/ticks.ts` took the tick's scheduled list and neighbour list out of their
  queues before running them and put back the remainder only after the loop, which a throwing hook skipped.
- **Fix:** both loops put back the updates after the one that threw (or past the budget) in a `finally`; the error
  still propagates. Regression: `packages/voxel/tests/ticks.test.js` "a scheduled update that throws ..." and "a
  placed hook that throws ...".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a model mesh that failed to build left the chunk's other model meshes in the scene (voxel models)

- **Repro (before):** `VoxelModelRenderer` over a chunk with two model types, the second `createMesh` throwing (an
  allocation failure): the first surface's mesh was neither destroyed nor kept, so the retry on the next `update`
  drew it twice and `dispose` never freed it (3 live meshes for 2 surfaces, 1 after dispose).
- **Cause:** `update` in `packages/voxel/src/models.ts` stored a chunk's new meshes only after all of them were made.
- **Fix:** the meshes made are stored in a `finally` and a chunk leaves `pending` only once built, so the retry replaces
  them. Regression: `packages/voxel/tests/models.test.js` "a model mesh that fails to build ...".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: beveled voxel chunks met with slivers where a crease reached a chunk seam (voxel)

- **Repro (before):** `VoxelRenderer.attach(engine, { world, bevel: voxelBevel(0.15) })` with a block whose side
  stands on a floor exactly in a chunk's boundary plane (a block at x = 32 on a floor at x = 31): the concave edge
  between the floor (chunk 0) and the block's -x face (chunk 1) stayed sharp, and at lattice points of the seam where
  a crease ended the two chunk meshes left slivers up to `bevel` wide. Even with the neighbours' faces as `context`,
  two chunks that merged their seam rows differently (as AO and light split runs) left T-junctions along the seam.
- **Cause:** the renderer beveled each chunk layer from that chunk's own quads only (`#bevelLayer` in
  `packages/voxel/src/render.ts`), so the faces that decide the creases and corners on the seam were missing and those
  edges fell back to flat; and `bevelQuads` in `packages/voxel/src/bevel.ts` inserted only its own pieces' corners into
  its edges, while the other chunk's vertices on the seam depend on how that chunk merged its quads.
- **Fix:** the meshers return `ChunkMesh.border` when asked (`VoxelMesher.mesh` and `GpuVoxelMesher.mesh`, fifth
  argument): the whole box faces of the one-cell shell that touch the chunk, read by `meshBorder`
  (`packages/voxel/src/border.ts`) from the same shell the mesher reads, so no chunk meshes another. A beveled
  renderer asks for it and passes each layer's border faces as `context`. On a seam (a lattice point a context face
  meets) `bevelQuads` inserts every point of the corner walk into the edges through it, the points a unit-face mesh of
  either side has there, so both chunks share their vertices on the seam whatever their merges. Regressions:
  `packages/voxel/tests/bevel-silhouette.test.js` "chunks that merge their own faces their own way meet exactly",
  `packages/voxel/tests/bevel-seam.test.js` (the border lists exactly the neighbours' chamfered faces; eight chunks
  beveled with their borders form the same surface as one chunk), the seam pixels of
  `packages/voxel/tests/bevel-browser-check.mjs` (a lump at the corner of eight chunks draws as the same lump inside
  one) and the border and beveled-picture checks of `packages/voxel/tests/gpu-mesher-browser-check.mjs`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: beveled voxel chamfers cracked where a merged quad met a face split in two (voxel)

- **Repro:** `bevelQuads([{ x: 0, y: 0, z: 0, face: 2, w: 3, h: 1 }, { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0, face: 5, w: 1, h: 1 },
  { x: 1, y: 0, z: 0, face: 5, w: 2, h: 1 }], 0.15)` (a top merged three cells long over a -z side the mesher split at
  x = 1, as it does where AO or light changes): the top's chamfer edge ran straight from (0, 0.894, 0.106) to
  (3, 0.894, 0.106), but the two side quads met at (1, 1, 0.15), leaving a sliver open to the sky. Two coplanar quads
  (a material or light change on a flat floor) also got a groove between them that one merged quad did not have.
- **Cause:** `bevelQuads` in `packages/voxel/src/bevel.ts` moved each quad corner along the sum of the normals of the
  quads whose corners met at that point, so a point in the middle of a merged quad's edge missed that quad's normal,
  and coplanar neighbours always chamfered the edge between them.
- **Fix:** `bevelQuads` now follows the cells' silhouette. Each unit edge of a quad's outline is classified by the
  faces around it (convex, flat or concave, a pair kept only when both faces pick each other); each face keeps a
  panel inset from its creased unit edges, each crease becomes a 45 degree strip (half per face, for its material and
  light), and each lattice point where creases meet a corner polygon, the face, edge and vertex pieces of Doo and Sabin
  (1978). Corners that lie inside another piece's edge (greedy-mesh T-junctions, Lysenko 2012) are inserted into it,
  so the mesh is closed. A lone face with nothing across its edges stays flat, and concave edges are filled by the same
  45 degree strip. Regression: `packages/voxel/tests/bevel-silhouette.test.js` (the repro closed into a bar has no open
  edge; split and merged coplanar tops have equal area and no vertex below the top; random cell sets give the same
  closed surface for every merge; two halves meshed with each other as `context` meet exactly).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: `<Physics>` left its engine plugin installed after it unmounted (KB-REACT-PHYS-UNMOUNT1, react)

- **Repro:** `npm run build:packages`, then `npm --prefix packages/react run test:browser`: the page failed with
  `Unmounted feature plugin remains: physics` (`packages/react/tests/scene-browser.tsx`, the unmount check after
  `features={false}`) from e19e03141 on.
- **Cause:** the react binding (`packages/react/src/physics.tsx`) installs a wrapper plugin that steps the world and
  its body syncs, not the world itself, and its unmount called only the world's `dispose`. Since e19e03141 the world's
  `dispose` removes a plugin only from the scene `engine.sceneOf(this)` names, which is none for a world the engine
  does not own, so the wrapper stayed installed under the world's name.
- **Fix:** the unmount removes the wrapper from the scene the engine reports for it (`engine.sceneOf(wrapper)`),
  which disposes the world through the wrapper; the world's `dispose` then covers the paths where the wrapper was
  never installed. The browser check above is the regression test.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a surface, mesh or graph colour range past the float32 limit coloured every value NaN on the GPU (sciviz)

- **Repro:** `figure.surface(z, { range: [-1e308, 1e308] })` (likewise `meshLayer` and `graphLayer` with that range):
  the drawn colours differ from the same values drawn with `range: [-1, 1]` on every pixel, while the
  `vectorGeometry()` export spreads the values over the map.
- **Cause:** the range reached the shader as float32 (the surface's `style.xy`, the mesh's and the graph's range
  uniform), so -1e308 and 1e308 became -Infinity and Infinity and `(value - lo) / (hi - lo)` was Infinity / Infinity.
  The surface also shaded NaN: its normal matrix was the inverse scale, and the z scale of such a range rounds to 0 in
  float32. `dataToScene` took `(lo + hi) / 2`, Infinity for bounds such as [1e308, 1.7e308].
- **Fix:** `rangeUniform` in `packages/sciviz/src/color-lookup.ts` computes in doubles, from halved values as
  `mapColours` does, the range start held inside float32, the reciprocal half span and the fraction at that start;
  the shaders read them through the WGSL `colourFraction` (the span term rounds to 0 when the span dwarfs every float32
  value, the right float32 answer). The surface's normal matrix is the cofactor matrix, and `dataToScene` takes halved
  bounds. Regression: `packages/sciviz/tests/range-overflow-browser.mjs` (surface, mesh and graph, WebGPU and the
  WebGL2 layer) and `packages/sciviz/tests/range-overflow.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: contact shadows drew dithered acne on every lit slope (post)

- **Repro:** `packages/post/test/contact-shadows-browser.mjs`: a bare 20 m floor under a light about 7 degrees up,
  seen at a slant, nothing above it. With `ContactShadows` on, 5,925 of 76,800 pixels darkened by more than 2 levels on
  WebGPU and 6,104 on the WebGL2 layer (RTX A6000, Edge), in the dither pattern of the march's start offset. The
  Orrery showed the same grain on its sunlit window sill and dial.
- **Cause:** the march in `packages/post/src/contact-shadows.ts` counted a hit whenever the ray sat behind the depth
  texel at all. A depth texel holds one depth for the whole pixel (the nearest of its four MSAA samples on WebGPU, one
  sample on the layer), so on a slope the surface the ray starts on sits up to about a pixel's depth change in front of
  the ray, and the ray shadowed its own surface wherever the start offset put it close.
- **Fix:** a hit needs the ray behind the depth by more than 1.5 pixel spans of depth, read once per pixel from the
  start pixel's flatter neighbour on each axis (four more depth loads a pixel; no added pass, buffer or binding): the
  slope-scaled bias of shadow mapping (L. Williams, "Casting Curved Shadows on Curved Surfaces", SIGGRAPH 1978;
  H. Dou, Y. Yan, E. Kerzner, Z. Dai, C. Wyman, "Adaptive Depth Bias for Shadow Maps", JCGT 3(4), 2014) applied
  to screen-space depth. 1.5 spans bound the start texel's error (at
  most 0.375 of a span either way for the nearest sample or sample 0) plus a hit texel's (the ray's point anywhere in
  its pixel, 0.875). Regression: `packages/post/test/contact-shadows-browser.mjs`, "a bare floor under a grazing light
  keeps every pixel" (0 darkened pixels after, native and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`; the floating box still darkens 449 and 456
  pixels). Contacts closer than that bias (well under a pixel's depth) are no longer drawn (docs/limits.md).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an odd-sized frame could not be written as H.264 or H.265 (headless)

- **Repro:** `encodeWithFFmpeg` of 17 x 9 frames to `clip.mp4`: libx264 stops with "width not divisible by 2" and the
  call rejects `failed`. `encodeVideo` asked the runtime for H.264 at 17 x 9, which encoders refuse.
- **Cause:** H.264 and H.265 4:2:0 crop the coded picture in units of two luma samples (H.264 7.4.2.1.1, H.265
  7.4.3.2.1), so no odd picture size can be stated; neither path made the frame even.
- **Fix:** for H.264 and H.265 both paths repeat the last column and row up to the even size (`rgbaToI420` in
  `packages/headless/src/video.ts`, `padFrame` in `ffmpeg.ts`) and report the size written; VP9 and AV1 keep odd sizes.
  Regression: `H.264 and H.265 take an odd size` and `encodeWithFFmpeg gives H.264 an even size` in
