  `packages/headless/tests/video.test.js`; ffmpeg 9.0.2 wrote a 17 x 9 render as an 18 x 10 MP4 and a 17 x 9 WebM.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: headless video chroma sat half a pixel off its label, and the two video paths stated different transfers (headless)

- **Repro:** `encodeVideo` of a 4 x 2 frame, red in columns 0 and 1 and blue in 2 and 3, to MP4 with H.264: the encoder
  got Cb and Cr of pure red then pure blue (a centred 2 x 2 mean), while H.264 with no chroma location in its VUI means
  chroma on the even luma columns, so a player drew the colour edge half a pixel right of the luma edge. A VP9 file said
  `vpcC` chroma 1 (co-sited with the top-left luma sample) for the same centred samples. `encodeWithFFmpeg` stated
  transfer BT.709 (H.273 code 1) for the same sRGB renders that `encodeVideo` states as sRGB (code 13).
- **Cause:** `rgbaToI420` in `packages/headless/src/video.ts` averaged each 2 x 2 block, which is H.273 chroma location
  1 (centre), and `video-mux.ts` labelled VP9 with chroma 1 and Matroska with nothing; `ffmpeg.ts` tagged `bt709`.
- **Fix:** chroma is made at chroma_sample_loc_type 0 (columns 2x - 1, 2x, 2x + 1 weighted 1, 2, 1; rows 2y and 2y + 1
  equally) and stated: VP9 `vpcC` and CodecPrivate chroma 0, Matroska ChromaSitingHorz 1 and ChromaSitingVert 2,
  ffmpeg `out_chroma_loc=left` and `-chroma_sample_location left`; ffmpeg states transfer `iec61966-2-1`. H.273 13 is the
  code for IEC 61966-2-1 encoded samples, which the renders are. Regression: `encodeVideo places chroma on the even luma
  columns` and `ffmpegArguments picks the codec from the file name` in `packages/headless/tests/video.test.js`, the VP9
  CodecPrivate test in `tests/containers.test.js`, and `npm run test:real-ffmpeg` (ffmpeg 9.0.2 reads
  `bt709/bt709/iec61966-2-1`, colours within 2 of 255 levels).

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a far-level node of fine 3D noise left a few cap edges unclosed (KB-VOX-CAP1, voxel)

- **Repro:** `meshSmoothLodNode(density, 2, x, 0, z)` for a cave field such as `(x, y, z) => 3 + sum of five
  amp * sin(a x + b y + c z + ph)` with |a|, |b|, |c| up to 0.3 and amp 2 to 12, or level-1 nodes of overhanging ground
  (`20 + noise - y`): 15 of 120 seeded nodes had edges used once (3 to 12 each, all on or beside a box edge).
- **Cause:** in `packages/voxel/src/smooth-clip.ts` each face decided its cap on its own, from the solid side of its own
  border segments and, for a slab no segment crossed, from the nearest segment. Where the Surface Nets surface folds
  inside one cell at a box edge, the two faces meeting there disagreed about which stretch of the box edge was solid,
  so one face's cap stopped where the other's went on. Two rounding faults added to it: border points a rounding apart
  (1e-14 cells) stayed separate points, so a cap corner met a border vertex only through a sliver, and the ear clipper
  called a triangle in line when its angle was under 1e-9 radians, which dropped real slivers a few cells long and
  1e-9 wide that float32 positions keep.
- **Fix:** caps are counted by winding number (Jacobson, Kavan and Sorkine-Hornung 2013): the mesh's border is taken as
  a chain (each edge's uses counted with direction), each box edge's winding numbers are found once, from the border
  points on it and its density samples (a sample's winding number is its solid flag), both faces start from those
  numbers, and each face carries them up its slabs, stepping by each border segment's count; a region is covered as
  many times as its number. Every triangle on a border edge takes the cap's points on it. Coordinates of points on the
  boxes' surfaces within 1e-9 cells of each other are made equal over all boxes of the node at once, and the ear
  clipper calls three points in line when the triangle's least height is at most 1e-11 cells. Regression:
  `packages/voxel/tests/smooth-lod.test.js` "closed for any field" (40 seeded cave and overhang nodes, 10 part-masked:
  6 had open edges on the old code) and "rays along box edges" (segments between neighbouring box-edge samples, moved
  about 0.001 cells into the box, cross the surface as often as their end samples differ; the old gaps had almost no
  area, so this one passed on the old code too).

### Open 2026-11-15: voxel debris with physics cannot take an `origin` (KB-VOX-ORIGIN2, voxel, waits on physics)

- **Repro:** `new VoxelDebris(world, { physics, engine, origin })` throws MargoError `unsupported`; without `origin` a
  piece 16,000,000 blocks out is simulated and drawn at float32 world positions (2-block steps).
- **Cause:** `@margoengine/physics` and `@margoengine/voxel/physics` simulate in world coordinates and write world
  poses into the meshes they drive (`Physics.addBody`, `packages/physics/src/physics.ts`); they take no origin, and the
  physics packages are on hold. Debris refuses the combination instead of drawing pieces 16 million blocks away.
- **Fix to build:** when physics resumes, give `Physics` and `VoxelPhysics` an origin (bodies near the origin, poses
  written as world minus origin), then let debris pass its origin through.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: voxel effects read engine positions as world cells under a renderer `origin` (KB-VOX-ORIGIN1, voxel)

- **Repro (before):** `VoxelRenderer.attach(engine, { world, textures, origin })` with `origin.origin` at
  [16000000, 0, 0] and `VoxelGI` or `VoxelColorLight` added: the light window sat around `camera.position` (engine
  space, near zero), so nothing around the camera got bounce or coloured light; a `SmoothTerrainView`,
  `VoxelObjects`, `VoxelModelRenderer` or `VoxelDebris` placed its meshes at world blocks, 16,000,000 blocks out.
- **Cause:** `gi.ts` and `light-rgb.ts` placed their windows from the engine camera and wrote the corner in world
  cells; `smooth.ts`, `objects.ts`, `models.ts` and `debris.ts` wrote mesh positions in world blocks.
- **Fix:** `/gi` and `/light-rgb` read the origin of the renderer they were added to with `add(voxels)`: the window is
  placed around the camera's world cell, and the shading uniform holds the corner minus the origin and the origin mod
  the volume size, so the wrapping volume is sampled at small numbers. The smooth view, objects, models and debris take
  an `origin` option (live field): meshes sit at their corner minus the origin in float64 (model chunk meshes now hold
  chunk-local positions) and move when the origin moves. Regression: the "origin:" tests in `gi.test.js`,
  `light-rgb.test.js`, `smooth.test.js`, `objects.test.js`, `models.test.js` and `debris.test.js` (the same world near
  zero and at 2^24 blocks writes the same uniforms and places the same meshes), and the far panel of
  `models-browser-check` (the same pixels as near zero).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: weather noise seeds shared streams, a random walk aliased seeds, and VFX JSON refused an effect with shadows

- **Repro (before):** `weatherNoise(8000, 0).rain` equalled `weatherNoise(8000, 1).rain`, and the rain of seed 2 was the
  white noise under the wind of seed 1 (correlation 0.99999); a second thunder rumble of seed 1 was the first of seed 2.
  `new WeatherMachine().randomWalk('clear', {seed: -1})` walked the same weather as seed 4294967295, and 1.5 as 1.
  `serializeEffect(effect)` of an attached `VFX` with `shadows` threw "effect.options.shadows.buffer.destroy cannot be
  embedded".
- **Cause:** `packages/weather/src/audio.ts` started its generator at `seed >>> 0 || 1` and gave the sounds the streams
  seed, seed + 1 and seed + 2 (rumbles seed + 7 + n); `packages/weather/src/machine.ts` took `seed | 0`;
  `packages/vfx/src/shadows.ts` writes its light list's GPU buffer into the options as `shadows.buffer`, an output
  `packages/vfx/src/json.ts` tried to save as a setting.
- **Fix:** each sound's (and each rumble's) start state is a hash (MurmurHash3's fmix32 finaliser) of the seed and the
  sound; the walk's state is a hash of the seed's whole 64-bit value (-0 is 0); `serializeEffect` leaves `shadows.buffer`
  out and keeps the effect's own options unchanged.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/weather/tests/audio.test.js` ("every seed gives its own noise"),
  `packages/weather/tests/weather.test.js` ("random walk seeds that differ walk differently"),
  `packages/vfx/test/json.test.js` ("an attached effect with shadows saves its settings").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: weather snow did not lift a model's MToon outline, and a shader without the standard projection lost the lift silently

- **Repro (before):** `GLTFWeather` with `snow: {cover: 1}` on a VRM model with an MToon outline: the body rose by the
  snow depth while the outline hull stayed at the ground, and `effect.shader(source, 2)` on a source without
  `o.clip=f.camera*p; o.position=p.xyz;` returned a shader with no lift and no error.
- **Cause:** `packages/rigging/src/mtoon-shader.ts` replaced that standard projection with the outline hull built from
  the raw vertex, so weather's edit of the projection (`packages/weather/src/gltf.ts`, applied after MToon) found
  nothing to edit, and weather's `replace` ignored a missing anchor.
- **Fix:** the outline keeps the standard projection and builds its hull on `o.clip` and `o.position` after it, so a
  later world edit moves the outline with its body; weather throws `MargoError` `'unsupported'` when the projection is
  absent.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/rigging/tests/mtoon-shader.test.js` ("the MToon outline hull builds on the projected
  o.clip and o.position") and `packages/weather/tests/gltf.test.js` ("snow lifts an MToon outline hull with its body");
  both fail on the old source. `packages/rigging/tests/mtoon-outline.browser.mjs` passes on WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a weather listener's refused call still changed the weather, schedules checked a step's ease late, a refused random walk stopped the schedule, and disposed WeatherAudio stayed attached

- **Repro (before):** (1) `machine.on(() => machine.transitionTo('rain'))`, then `machine.transitionTo('snow')`: the
  call threw MargoError `'state'`, but the weather then went to rain. (2) `machine.schedule([{to: 'rain'}, {to: 'snow',
  ease: 'cubic'}])` was accepted and threw from `update` when it reached the second step; a bad first ease threw but
  left the machine holding a schedule with no transition. (3) With a schedule running, `machine.randomWalk('clear',
  {seed: NaN})` threw, and the schedule had stopped. (4) `WeatherAudio.attach(engine, listener, {weather})` then
  `sounds.dispose()`: the engine's next frame threw `'disposed'` from the sounds' `onPreUpdate`.
- **Cause:** `packages/weather/src/machine.ts` checked for a running listener only when the new transition's event
  was emitted, after the transition was replaced; `schedule` checked each step's target, hold and seconds but not its
  ease; `randomWalk` cleared the schedule before checking its seed. `packages/weather/src/audio.ts` kept no engine,
  so `dispose` could not leave its scene.
- **Fix:** `transitionTo`, `schedule`, `randomWalk` and `update` refuse a call from a listener before they change
  anything (`set` and `stop` stay allowed); `schedule` checks every step's ease up front; `randomWalk` checks its seed
  before it stops anything; `WeatherAudio` keeps the engine from `setup` and leaves `engine.sceneOf(sounds)` on
  dispose, as the other weather plugins do.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/weather/tests/weather.test.js` ("a listener cannot change the weather it is called
  from, and its refused call changes nothing", "schedule checks every step's ease before it starts", "a randomWalk
  refused for its seed leaves a running schedule going") and `packages/weather/tests/audio.test.js` ("disposing
  attached sounds removes them from their scene"); all four fail on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: VFX `overLife.spin` moved the birth angle that ribbons, random atlas frames and mesh axes key on

- **Repro (before):** a `VFX` with `overLife: {spin: [2, 10]}`: the particle's stored birth angle (`rotation.x`, float
  `8n+8i+4` of `gpuState.particles`) changed every step, so a ribbon's record stamp no longer matched its earlier
  points, a `frames: 'random'` atlas frame changed every frame and a `mesh` (`align: 'random'`) tumble axis jumped.
- **Cause:** `packages/vfx/src/over-life.ts` added the spin curve's integral to `rotation.x` each step, while
  `ribbons.ts` (the record stamp), `texture.ts` (the random frame hash) and `mesh.ts` (the axis hash) read `rotation.x`
  as the fixed birth angle.
- **Fix:** the simulation leaves `rotation.x` alone; the billboard and mesh vertex stages add initial life x the
  curve's integral over the life lived (`drawnSpin`, the same sum the steps telescoped to), reading the curves uniform
  at binding 27. `overLife` passes its WGSL and binding to the mesh draw through `VFXState.spin`; every feature of an
  effect now shares one `VFXState`.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/vfx/test/over-life.test.js` ("the spin curve turns the drawn billboard and mesh")
  and `checkDrawnSpin` in `packages/vfx/test/parity.mjs` (the birth angle stays fixed over five steps and a sprite red on
  its left half and green on its right is drawn at birth + 2 rad, within 0.05 rad, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer;
  on the old source the birth angle moved). Both fail on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: VFX ribbons kept their points across `reset()`, a plain sprite lost its top corners, and `burst` after `dispose()` threw a RangeError

- **Repro (before):** (1) a `VFX` with `ribbons` and `reset()` mid-run: the next frame did not record as a fresh start
  does (the recording clock ran on), and the points recorded before the seek stayed in the ring, where the replayed
  births, which take the same birth angles, matched them. (2) A `texture` without an `atlas`: the corners of the
  sprite's top row were not drawn (the billboard's triangle edges cross x = +-1 at y = 0.27). (3) `effect.burst(1)`
  after `dispose()` threw "Particle burst must be a whole number up to capacity".
- **Cause:** (1) `packages/vfx/src/ribbons.ts` had no `reset`; (2) `packages/vfx/src/texture.ts` widened the triangle to
  hold the unit square for atlases only, though every sprite fills the square; (3) `burst` in
  `packages/vfx/src/base.ts` folded the disposed check into its range check.
- **Fix:** (1) the ribbons' `reset` zeroes the ring and restarts the record count and clock; (2) every sprite takes the
  square's triangle; (3) `burst` throws `MargoError` `'disposed'`, as `reset` does.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/vfx/test/ribbons.test.js` ("reset clears the recorded points"),
  `packages/vfx/test/vfx.test.js` ("burst after dispose", and the plain sprite's triangle in "a texture atlas draws"),
  and the `plain sprite` cases of `packages/vfx/test/browser-check.mjs` (each corner's quadrant at 1x and 4x MSAA; on
  the old source the top corners read black).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: VFX sub-emitters gave no children on the WebGL2 layer

- **Repro (before):** on the WebGL2 compatibility layer, a `VFX` with `events: {on: 'death'}` (or `'collision'`) whose
  route has loaded: no child is ever born. `packages/vfx/test/features-check.mjs --compat` read the parent's dead slot
  where four children should start.
- **Cause:** WebGPU lists each frame's events in the simulation's main kernel with a workgroup scan. The layer's route
  (`packages/vfx/src/compat.ts`) runs `update` alone and drops that kernel, so the events feature's scan summed counts
  nothing had written and the list stayed empty.
- **Fix:** the route's `update` stores each slot's event flag, a prefix count places it and a compaction kernel writes
  the same list in slot order with its total; the events feature's own scan does not run on the route.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/vfx/test/events.test.js` ("on the WebGL2 route the route lists the events") and the
  events cases of `packages/vfx/test/features-check.mjs --compat`, which now wait for the route.

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a caller's GPU object held at a device restore stopped the frame loop, warned or failed silently, by package (KB-RESTORE-BORROWED1, sprites, tilemap, points, shader, post, shadows, terrain, environment, clustered, water, lighting2d, pixel, loaders, gltf/pbr, materials, tonemap and others)

- **Repro:** `SpriteLayer.attach(engine, { atlas: engine.gpu.createTexture(...) })`, draw a frame, destroy the device
  and `await engine.rebootDevice()`: the next frame throws `'state'` and the frame loop stops. The same with a plain
  `GPUTexture` for a tilemap atlas, a decal atlas, a terrain heightmap or most other options: the new device rejects the
  old object, core throws the validation error from the next frame and the loop stops, or the package warns in the
  console (points, shader/raw) or says nothing.
- **Cause:** a WebGPU object belongs to the device that made it, and nothing can ask an object for its device (W3C
  WebGPU 3.2.1, 3.5.2). Each package handled the case on its own. The rule is now one, in docs/conventions.md,
  "Borrowed GPU objects": a function form called once per device, a plain object dropped and reported once through
  `engine.onError` (margoengine.com/errors#borrowed-lost) while the frame keeps drawing, and a setter for a new one.
  `packages/shared/borrowed.js` holds it (`tests/borrowed.test.js`). `tests/borrowed-gpu.test.js` finds every public
  member that can hold a caller GPU object and holds it to `scripts/borrowed-registry.json`; this entry stays open
  while any row there is `pending`, and each package's push rules its rows with a GPU regression test on WebGPU and
  the WebGL2 compatibility layer.
- **Progress:** ruled so far: voxel (2), post (5, 2026-11-16: decals, material-decals, lens-flare, lens), shader raw (4, 2026-11-16: raw textures, raw storage buffer, GLSL sampler uniforms), Shadertoy channels (5, 2026-11-16: a texture channel holds its texture in a slot named for the channel, `toy.setChannel` replaces it; the toy's own buffers, Cube A and feeds are made again by themselves); exempt after a check, vfx (9, 2026-11-16: VFXState's buffers and `shadows.buffer` are the effect's own, the soft and sort features are factories called with each device, a skinned primitive's `deformed` is the deformer's per-frame record; ### Fixed 2026-11-15: validateMachine listed problems a machine document does not have (KB-FSM-DOC1, fsm)

- **Repro (before):** `validateMachine(42)` returned the issue `document: A machine is an object` twice.
  `validateMachine({version: 1, initial: 'a', states: {a: {parent: 'b'}, b: {parent: 'zz'}}})` reported
  `states.a.parent: Hierarchy cycle` beside the real `states.b.parent: Unknown parent`; a state hanging below a cycle
  (`a.parent = 'b'` with `b` and `c` parents of each other) was reported as a cycle member; and
  `{x: {initial: 'y', parent: 'zz'}, y: {parent: 'x'}}` refused `x.initial` although `y` is a child of `x`. Found by
  the fsm mutation run (`document.ts` survivors on lines 118 and 160).
- **Cause:** the parent walk returned null both for a cycle and for a chain that left the states, and either result
  was read as "this state is in a cycle" or "the initial is not below it"; `validateMachine` added the not-an-object
  issue itself and then again through the region check.
- **Fix:** the walk stops at an unknown parent (reported on the state that names it) and at a cycle further up
  (reported on the states in it), and returns null only when the state is its own ancestor; the region check alone
  reports a value that is not an object. A valid document gives the same empty list as before.
- **Regression test:** `packages/fsm/test/document-issues.test.js` (three of its four tests fail on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Box3 centre and bounding sphere of an unbounded box were NaN (KB-MATH-UNB2, math)

- **Repro (before):** with `I = Infinity`, `new Box3(new Vector3(-I, 10, -2), new Vector3(I, 20, 4)).getCenter(new Vector3())`
  gave (NaN, 15, 1), and `getBoundingSphere` on the same box gave a NaN centre x. A box from (I, 0, 0) to (I, 2, 2)
  (both x bounds at the same infinity, which is not empty) gave a NaN radius as well. Found while fixing KB-MATH-UNB1.
- **Cause:** the centre was `(min + max) / 2` on every axis, and `-Infinity + Infinity` is NaN; the radius took
  `max - min` per axis, which is NaN when both bounds are the same infinity.
- **Fix:** an axis with an infinite bound has centre 0 and the other axes keep the midpoint; the sphere radius is
  `Infinity` whenever a bound is infinite. Empty boxes keep centre (0, 0, 0) and radius -1. No caller in the repository
  passes an unbounded box to either method (`Capsule` uses `Line3.getCenter`), so no answer elsewhere changes; finite
  boxes take the same arithmetic as before. Rule in `packages/math/README.md` and `docs/limits.md`.
- **Regression test:** `packages/math/test/box3-unbounded.test.js` (the two centre and sphere tests fail on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: guided voxel path tracer coverage cases missed by over 6 standard errors on the WebGL2 layer, ANGLE Vulkan (KB-VPT-GUIDE-COMPAT, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:gpu:guiding --workspace packages/voxel-pathtracer` on Windows (Edge 157, RTX A6000, NVIDIA
  617.42): the native leg passed, the script's own WebGL2 leg (`--use-angle=vulkan`) failed every run on a different
  coverage case (overlapping guide bounds 0.701 against 0.7307, unit furnace 0.961 against 0.9936), with a standard error
  of 0.028 where native has 0.0011.
- **Not the estimator, not the statistics:** the same seeds on the layer gave the native values to 7 or more digits in
  every image but one or two of the 16 batch images a case averages, which came out 15 to 95 percent dark; the test's
  standard error, taken from the spread of the batch means, grew because of those images. Reading the image back after
  each of a render's 16 dispatches showed 2 to 7 consecutive dispatches adding almost nothing, about 0.3 s of GPU work,
  running on from one image into the next. It struck base and guided tracers alike (a base tracer too, once the attach
  timing changed), a few seconds after the layer moved from one tracer's programs to another's: 1 to 4 dark images in
  every 64 when base and guided tracers alternate, none when every tracer runs the same programs. No GL object was
  deleted and no program linked inside those windows (traced through `device.collect` and `gl.linkProgram`), and it
  stayed with ANGLE's graphics pipeline library off, monolithic pipelines preferred and the GPU disk cache off.
- **Cause:** the fault of the entry below, still present: ANGLE Vulkan writes other words through fragment output
  location 7. Every staged program wrote 8 outputs, one per layer of a state page.
- **Fix:** a state page holds 7 layers (`LAYERS` in `src/compat-staged.ts`), so no route program writes location 7.
  0 dark images in 512 (two 4-round runs of the alternating sequence, 256 guided and 256 base images), against 1 to 7
  dark guided images in each of 9 earlier runs of 64 to 96; every other image's mean the same to 6 digits. Cost: the base tracer's state takes 7 pages instead of 6; a 480 x 300 render replays
  390,804 layer passes for 256 samples against 365,716 (36,478 against 34,142 for 16), the same pixel sums, the same
  time on ANGLE Vulkan (9.27 against 9.26 s, busy machine). Regression:
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js` "never write fragment output location 7" (fails with 8
  layers), and the guiding GPU test's own WebGL2 leg.

### Fixed in part 2026-11-15: the voxel path tracer's staged programs took tens of seconds each to compile on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (KB-D3D11-NEST, KB-L5a-10, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro:** any `MARGO_COMPAT=1` voxel-pathtracer GPU step on Windows (Edge 157, RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11, the
  browser default): each staged program is a cold `fxc` compile at its first draw, and steps sized on WebGPU ran past
  their limits. Measured offline on the HLSL ANGLE emits for the base tracer (`fxc.exe` 10.0.26100, `ps_5_0`, default
  flags, CPU seconds): the `hit` program 35.1 s, `shadow` 23.1 s, the trace module's compute kernel 24.7 s.
- **Cause:** fxc inlines every call, and its time grows several times over for each loop nested around the voxel walk
  (the walk alone, outside its callers' loops, compiles in 2.5 s; `[loop]`, `[fastopt]` and `/Od` do not help, and a
  walk with a single exit is no faster). `closest()` and `shadow()` looped over a leaf's instances inside the hierarchy
  loop, and `march()` and `marchShadow()` looped over a brick's cells inside the brick loop, so the innermost voxel step
  sat under four loops.
- **Fix:** both levels are flattened, with the same visiting order and the same values on every backend: the hierarchy
  walk runs a leaf's instances in its own loop (`hit` 35.1 to 13.3 s, `shadow` 23.1 to 8.3 s, compute kernel 24.7 to
  6.7 s), and each voxel walk steps bricks and a brick's cells in one loop (`hit` 15.1 to 9.3 s and `shadow` 10.0 to
  5.4 s in a paired run on the same loaded machine; the compute kernel 9.1 to 3.8 s, vs_5_0, paired 2026-11-15). Regressions: `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js`
  ("walk the hierarchy and a leaf's instances in one loop", "walk a model's bricks and cells in one loop"); both fail on
  the nested shaders.
- **Still open (KB-L5a-10):** a 480 x 300 reference at 16384 samples takes about 555 s on the layer over Direct3D 11
  against 14 s on WebGPU (449 s once switched-off light kinds draw no pass, 2026-11-16, the entry below), so the compat legs of `denoise`, `denoise-materials`, `media`, `sky`, `mesh-pbr-lobes` and the
  `resampled` lifecycle case still run past limits sized on WebGPU. That run-time half is not fixed by the compile work.

### Open 2026-11-15: Chrome 124 in the Android emulator shows no WebGL canvas at all (emulator defect, not Margo; browser matrix)

- **Repro:** Pixel_8 emulator image (Android 15, user build, `ro.debuggable=0`; GPU "Android Emulator OpenGL ES
  Translator" over SwiftShader through ANGLE on Vulkan), Chrome 124.0.6367.219. A plain page with no engine makes a
  64 x 64 `webgl2` canvas (with or without `preserveDrawingBuffer`, and a `webgl` one) and clears it red:
  `gl.readPixels` reads 255, 0, 0, 255, but `drawImage` of the canvas into a 2D canvas reads 0, 0, 0, 0, `toDataURL`
  is a 294-byte empty PNG, a CDP screenshot shows the page background there, and `adb exec-out screencap` of the
  device screen has no red pixel. A 2D canvas next to it shows its colour. `navigator.gpu` exists but
  `requestAdapter()` answers null.
- **Cause:** the emulator's GLES translator path does not give Chrome's compositor (or Chrome's canvas readback) the
  WebGL drawing buffer; the drawing itself is right, as readPixels shows. Not Margo code: no Margo code runs in the
  repro. Real Android phones with a hardware GPU are not affected as far as we know; none was measured.
- **Margo side:** nothing in the engine can make the canvas visible there. The browser matrix
  (`packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs`) checks for this first with a plain canvas cleared to red
  (`canvasShotsWork`) and records picture rows as `unmeasured` with the reason instead of as wrong colours; the
  layer's feature probes, GTAO and voxel traversal, which read results back, run and pass there. Pinned by
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/browser-matrix.test.js` ("a coded start-up refusal is a refusal, and a browser that
  shows no WebGL2 canvas leaves picture rows unmeasured").
- **Way out:** measure pictures on a real Android phone, or on an emulator image with host GPU rendering where it
  draws WebGL canvases.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the browser matrix could not drive Chrome on a user-build Android image (webgl2-compat, browser matrix)

- **Repro (before):** with Chrome's first run finished on the Pixel_8 emulator (Android 15, `ro.debuggable=0`),
  `node packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs --browser=android-chrome` failed "Chrome on
  sdk_gphone64_arm64 opened no DevTools socket in 180 s", while `/proc/net/unix` on the device listed Chrome's own
  `@chrome_devtools_remote`. With that fixed it recorded 46 bug rows: the engine's coded `webgpu` refusal plus an
  empty canvas as a bug, every layer feature probe as "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'features')", and every
  layer picture as white.
- **Cause:** Playwright's `launchBrowser` writes a Chrome command line naming its own DevTools socket; a user build
  ignores that file, so the socket it waits for never opens. The cases then assumed a native adapter: the features
  page's `run` opens a native device first, and basic-scene judged a refused start by its empty picture. The white
  pictures are the emulator defect above.
- **Fix:** on a user build the matrix starts Chrome itself, forwards a local port to `chrome_devtools_remote`
  (`adb forward`, removed on close and on a failed start) and connects over CDP; it takes the full Chrome build from
  `/json/version`. A start whose page errors are all coded refusals is a refusal; without a native adapter the native
  rows are `unmeasured` and the layer's probes run alone (`runCompat`), inverseTrig against float64 and bitmapCopies
  against its two copy rules.
- **Regressions:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/browser-matrix.test.js`: "Chrome on a user-build Android image is
  driven over its own DevTools socket, and every mapping is removed on close", "a DevTools socket that never answers
  fails in time with the last error, and the forward is removed", "without a native adapter the layer feature probes
  run alone, judged by their own bars".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: toPNG and toSVG could paint the tick labels away from the frame after a page layout change (sciviz)

- **Repro (before):** `examples/sciviz-parcoords.html`, `figure.toPNG()` while the page's accessibility panel attaches (its scan runs every 250 ms and makes the canvas parent `position: relative`). About one run in three of `npm run test:browser:parcoords` in sciviz failed `resource restoration preserves row geometry` or `line mode restores original geometry` with the WebGL2 layer, and one in five overall: 684 pixels of tick label text moved, nothing in the plot.
- **Cause:** toPNG drew the frame, which places the HTML labels beside the canvas, then read the label, swatch and colour bar boxes only after the GPU copy was mapped, tasks later (the WebGL2 layer replays later still). A layout change in between moved the label root by the new containing block's offset (70, 238.5 px here) until the next frame, so the labels were painted where the frame had not put them. toSVG read the canvas box before its frame and the text after its raster image; tiled media export read colour bar boxes per tile.
- **Fix:** packages/sciviz/src/figure.ts reads every overlay box in the task that draws the frame (toPNG through its capture callback, toSVG straight after `render()`); `placedBars` in packages/sciviz/src/export.ts keeps each colour bar's box from then, also for tiled media export.
- **Regression:** `packages/sciviz/tests/parcoords-browser.mjs` flips the canvas parent's containing block straight after the frame inside toPNG and requires the image to equal the one before; it fails with the old toPNG and passes natively and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Open 2026-11-15: TIFF LERC (Compression 34887) is refused; no public bitstream specification exists (decoders)

- **Repro:** `parseTIFF` or `openTIFF(...).read(0)` on a GDAL GeoTIFF written with `COMPRESS=LERC` throws `MargoError`
  `failed`, "TIFF compression 34887 is not supported". geotiff.js and GDAL read such files.
- **Cause:** Esri publishes LERC only as its reference library and a high-level explainer (doc/MORE.md: the
  quantisation idea and one worked 4 x 4 block, no header layout, versions, mode codes, mask or Huffman layout). The
  bitstream is defined by that source and ports of it, which the clean-room rule forbids reading. No writer was
  available here to build fixtures either.
- **Next:** build it when Esri or a standards body publishes the format, or from a clean-room description written by
  someone who has not worked on Margo; record the source in docs/clean-room.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: openTIFF read subsampled YCbCr pages outside JPEG as interleaved pixels (decoders)

- **Repro:** a 4 x 2 TIFF, PhotometricInterpretation 6, YCbCrSubSampling 2 2, uncompressed: `openTIFF(bytes).read(0)`
  returned 24 "samples" made of the file's data units (four Y then Cb and Cr), which are not per-pixel samples.
- **Cause:** raw pages copy stored samples row by row, but TIFF 6.0 Section 21 stores subsampled YCbCr in data units.
  `parseTIFF` converted them; the page reader did not check for them.
- **Fix:** raw pages refuse subsampled YCbCr unless it is JPEG-compressed (whose frames carry their own sampling), with
  a coded error that names the fix; regression in packages/decoders/tests/tiff-libtiff.test.js, failing on the old
  source.

### Fixed 2026-11-18: 46 check scripts opened their own browser page without the WebGL2-layer shim (KB-SKY-COMPATCHECK1, scripts and package tests)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/taa/test/reactive-browser.mjs`: the script launches its own browser and
  calls `browser.newPage()`, so no init script installs the layer and the run is native WebGPU, passing as a layer leg.
- **Cause:** only `openBrowser` (scripts/browser.js) and `postBrowser` (packages/post/test/post-browser.mjs) install
  `compatShim`; files that open pages themselves were never checked. Found while checking `sky features-check`, which
  does honour MARGO_COMPAT=1 (through openBrowser: its 2026-11-16 compat run drew on "WebGL2 compatibility layer
  (full) on ANGLE ... D3D11"; its weather and sleet counts match native because they count covered pixels, and its TAA
  streak means differ in the fourth digit). Its report now keeps a `-compat` file of its own.
- **Guard:** `tests/gpu-compat-honoured.test.js` fails on any new such file and on a listed file that is fixed but not
  taken off. **Owed:** each file in `scripts/support/compat-owed.json` gets `compatShim` (or a
  `MARGO_COMPAT not applicable: <reason>` line where the page makes no GPU calls or runs the layer itself) and comes off
  the list, with its GPU run native and MARGO_COMPAT=1.
- **Progress:** taa's eight scripts (converge, deform, reactive, rejection, settle-reactive, sharpen, velocity-only,
  xr) install the shim and pass under MARGO_COMPAT=1 on the layer (RTX A6000, ANGLE D3D11, 2026-11-16). Nine name
  why the layer has nothing to do there: netcode's signalling, voxel-net's WebRTC, cache, the pointer-lock probe and
  the catalog make no GPU calls; webgl2-compat's browser-check, glsl-corpus, package-tiers and preview checks run
  WebGL2 or the layer themselves. Four run a layer leg of their own beside native WebGPU and pass both: core's
  empty-geometry, road's browser check, wfc's assembly and procedural's PBR textures. Nineteen more are done
  (2026-11-16): controls (three scripts), labels, mixer, physics (two), bvh, lightmap, wfc's browser check,
  procedural's caves, poisson, textures and tree-mesh, the glTF compression consumer, the gallery check and the
  lifecycle check install the shim and pass on the layer (the preview-served ones build the layer beside the page
  with `compatBuild`; the gallery serves the package's dist under `/__compat/`); audio's pages run their own layer
  leg and exporters' PNG check makes no GPU calls, so both say so. The Jupyter check (the notebook pages serve the
  layer under `/__compat/`) and physics2d's kernel browsers (the WebGPU leg on the layer; its Firefox WebGL2 leg fails
  natively too) also honour it, which makes 21 more. Creative and margo-module-tests followed (KB-COMPAT-AUDIT1,
  below), then decoders (KB-COMPAT-DECODERS1, below). The last, frame-alloc, installs the shim since 2026-11-18, once
  the layer came within the native floors (KB-COMPAT-FRAMEALLOC1, part 10): `scripts/support/compat-owed.json` is
  empty, and the guard keeps it so.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Grade with HueGrade in one Tonemap built invalid WGSL (KB-OWN-TONE2, tonemap)

- **Repro:** `Tonemap.attach(engine, { extensions: [new Grade(), new HueGrade()] })` on a real device: the presentation
  shader failed with "redeclaration of 'Grade'". Found by the tonemap owner fixture's GPU leaf.
- **Cause:** `HueGrade` extends `Grade` (packages/tonemap/src/hue.ts), and each extension patched in `struct Grade`,
  `var grading` and the same function names, so any two grades in one list (two `Grade`s too) collided.
- **Fix:** each grade names its WGSL by its binding (`Grade5`, `gradeColor5`, ...) and `HueGrade` edits only its own
  code, so the list combines the way every extension list does: in the order given, before the LUT. Regression in
  packages/tonemap/tests/hue.test.js (the WebGL2 layer's WGSL checker rejects the old shader for the same
  redeclaration) and the owner fixture's `Tonemap.Grade+HueGrade` entry; doc packages/tonemap/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: a WGSL CustomCurve that ignored curveParams failed to bind on a real device (KB-OWN-TONE3, tonemap)

- **Repro:** `new CustomCurve({ wgsl: 'fn reinhard(x: vec3f) -> vec3f { return x / (x + vec3f(1.0)); }' })` in a
  Tonemap's `extensions`: the first frame failed "binding index 5 not present in the bind group layout". The CPU model
  does not validate layouts. Found by the tonemap owner fixture's GPU leaf.
- **Cause:** the bind group always carries the `customCurveData` uniform, and the automatic pipeline layout dropped it
  when the curve never read it (packages/tonemap/src/custom.ts).
- **Fix:** the WGSL path's `customCurve` starts with the phony read `_=customCurveData.params;`, which keeps the
  uniform in the fragment entry's resource interface at no cost per pixel. Regressions in
  packages/tonemap/tests/custom.test.js (the fragment entry reaches binding 5, by the WebGL2 layer's WGSL checker),
  packages/tonemap/tests/custom-browser.mjs (the curve draws without a validation error and matches x / (1 + x)) and
  the owner fixture's `Tonemap.CustomCurve.wgsl-no-params` entry; doc packages/tonemap/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: PartInstancer's pack draw ignored the view it was drawn in and wrote outside its scissor (KB-OWN-CAD3, cad)

- **Repro:** `PartInstancer.attach(engine)` and `engine.render({ views })` with a view whose viewport or scissor is not
  the whole target: the packed parts drew across the whole target, over neighbouring views. Found by the cad
  owner/lifetime fixture on a real device ("no pixel writes outside either view scissor").
- **Cause:** the pack's own pass (packages/cad/src/pack.ts) set a viewport and scissor only when the draw call passed
  them; core's draw falls back to the view's rectangles, the pack draw did not.
- **Fix:** the pack draw resolves its rectangles exactly as core's draw does (the call's own, else the view's viewport
  and scissor).
- **Regression:** packages/cad/test/pack.test.js, "the pack draw keeps to the view it is drawn in..." (fails on the old
  source); packages/cad/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: loadCAD and parseCADAsync built their model in the scene active when they finished, and a disposed PartInstancer stayed registered (KB-OWN-CAD1, KB-OWN-CAD2, cad)

- **Repro:** `loadCAD(engine, url)` or `parseCADAsync(engine, bytes, format)` called while a second scene is set up:
  after the download (loadCAD) or in the worker's replies (parseCADAsync) the root and parts were made in the active
  scene. `PartInstancer.attach(engine)` then `instancer.dispose()`: the plugin stayed in its scene and kept its passes.
  Found by the cad owner/lifetime fixture (secondary scene; every case's registration check).
- **Cause:** both made their meshes with `engine.createMesh()` after an await or in a worker message, where the
  active scene is whatever the app last drew (KB-OWN-CAD1); `PartInstancer.dispose` freed its packs but never left
  its scene (KB-OWN-CAD2).
- **Fix:** loadCAD and parseCADAsync capture the calling scene before their first await (`captureScene`) and make every
  mesh in it; `PartInstancer.dispose` removes the plugin from `engine.sceneOf(this)` once and is safe to call twice.
- **Regression:** packages/cad/test/pack.test.js, "loadCAD builds its model in the scene it was called for...",
  "parseCADAsync builds the parts its worker sends in the scene it was called for" and "disposing a PartInstancer takes
  it out of its scene..." (all fail on the old source); packages/cad/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a destroyed WebGL2-layer device kept its context-loss listener on the canvas (KB-OWN-COMPAT1, webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** `device.destroy()` on a device of the WebGL2 compatibility layer (an XR's own device on the layer, disposed
  with its XR), then a `webglcontextlost` event on its canvas: the destroyed device's listener still ran and called
  `preventDefault()`. Found by the xr owner/lifetime fixture on the WebGL2 layer (a leaked listener per XR).
- **Cause:** `CompatDevice` (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/device.ts) added the listener in its constructor and
  never removed it, so a canvas that outlives the device kept the device reachable and claimed the loss that
  `destroy()` itself asks for (`loseContext()`) for a restore no device would make.
- **Fix:** the listener is kept and removed once, when the device is lost or destroyed (`lose`).
- **Regression:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/destroyed-use.test.js, "a destroyed device takes its context-loss
  listener off the canvas, which may outlive it" and "a context loss loses the device once and then leaves the canvas"
  (both fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: XRModels made its controller and hand meshes in whichever scene was active when a frame arrived (KB-OWN-XR1, xr)

- **Repro:** an `XR` in a second scene with `XRModels.attach(xr, engine)`: the first XR frame that sees a controller or
  hand builds its meshes in the active scene (an XR frame callback runs outside any render), and disposing the XR's
  scene left those meshes behind. Found by the xr owner/lifetime fixture (secondary scene, scene disposal).
- **Cause:** `XRModels` (packages/xr/src/models.ts) called `engine.createMesh()` from its frame hook, and `createMesh`
  makes the mesh in the active scene; nothing tied the models to a scene.
- **Fix:** `attach` finds the XR's scene (`engine.sceneOf(xr)`, or for a host that is no plugin the scene captured at
  attach), makes every mesh inside `sceneScope(...).run`, and registers an `ownScene` release, so the models are disposed
  with that scene.
- **Regression:** packages/xr/tests/models.test.js, "models are made in the scene their XR is in, whatever scene is
  active when a frame arrives, and go with it" (fails on the old source); packages/xr/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a Physics2D world and a Ragdoll in a second scene left the active scene's plugin instead of their own (KB-OWN-PHYS-SCENE, physics2d, ragdoll)

- **Repro:** a `Physics2D` registered in a second scene, disposed while the default scene is active: it stayed in its
  scene and a default-scene plugin named `physics2d` was removed instead. `Ragdoll.attach(physics, ...)` for a world of
  a second scene joined the active scene (its duplicate check looked there too), and `ragdoll.dispose()` removed a
  same-name plugin from the active scene.
- **Cause:** `engine.use`, `engine.hasPlugin` and the one-argument `engine.removePlugin` act on the active scene
  (packages/physics2d/src/physics.ts `dispose`, packages/ragdoll/src/ragdoll.ts `attach` and `dispose`).
- **Fix:** both dispose through `engine.sceneOf(this)`; `Ragdoll.attach` checks and registers inside
  `sceneScope(engine, engine.sceneOf(physics))` (packages/shared/scene-scope.js). Plugin lifecycle only: no solver
  code changed. Their rows leave the OPEN list of scripts/support/plugin-scene-owner.mjs.
- **Regression:** packages/physics2d/tests/physics2d.test.js "dispose removes the world from its own scene, not the
  active one" and packages/ragdoll/tests/ragdoll.test.js "attach and dispose use the physics world scene, not the
  active one" (both fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: applyLightmap on a glTF PBR model installed its plugin in the active scene, not the model's (KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP2, lightmap)

- **Repro:** `applyLightmap(model, bake)` from `@margoengine/lightmap/imported` for a `PBRModel` of a second scene while
  another scene is active (or after an await, once the app has switched scenes): the `ImportedLightmapInstallation`
  joined the active scene, so it was set up, restored and listed there, apart from the model it lights.
- **Cause:** `applyLightmap` (packages/lightmap/src/imported.ts) called `model.root.engine.use(result)`, and
  `engine.use` registers in the active scene.
- **Fix:** it registers inside `sceneScope(engine, engine.sceneOf(model)).run(...)` (packages/shared/scene-scope.js),
  the scene that holds the model; an engine with no scenes still uses `engine.use`. The stale "Open" entry for
  KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP1 (fixed by 5f84817b39) is removed from this file.
- **Regression:** packages/lightmap/tests/imported.test.js, "applyLightmap installs in the model scene, not the active
  scene" (fails on the old source).

### Corrected 2026-11-15: two CI timeouts in one loaded run were machine stalls, not a lost worker reply (KB-WORKER-RPC1, worker; KB-VOX-SETTLE1, voxel)

- **Report:** local CI cpu run 2026-11-15T19-00-42-821Z (ddcf9a6eda, mean CPU load 0.93 over the step) timed out
  packages/worker/tests/rpc.test.js "RPC progress is ordered, channel-isolated, transferable and stops after settlement
  or abort" (3 s limit, 4,201 ms; 17 to 21 ms in the six neighbouring runs) and packages/voxel/tests/render.test.js
  "drawShadow: opaque and cutout chunks inside the cascade only..." ("renderer did not settle" after its 20 s loop;
  46 to 78 ms elsewhere). A 300-fold slowdown looked like a lost or reordered message.
- **Evidence it is load:** in that run 46 tests in about 20 packages were over 1 s and at least 20 times slower than in
  any of three neighbouring runs, and none of them in those runs: a 1 ms test took 5,964 ms, a 90 ms test 62,214 ms,
  `real worker pool executes tasks` 8,511 ms (28 to 40 ms elsewhere), and a dev-servers probe in the same run got no
  answer in 30 s. The RPC test's own 3 s timer fired 1.2 s late, so its process got no event-loop turn for at least that
  long. The RPC test runs on one thread over a `MessageChannel`, so it has nothing to wait for but the scheduler.
- **Code read:** every RPC message on one port pair is FIFO, the server runs a handler in the task that delivers its
  call, a cancel only aborts a running handler (which still replies), progress is dropped after settlement on both
  sides, and an abort or a throwing observer rejects at once while the slot (`done`) waits for the reply. The voxel
  settle path does not use @margoengine/worker: `VoxelRenderer` meshes through `VoxelMesher` and `JobPool`
  (packages/shared/worker-pool.js) on worker_threads in the test, its worker script sets `onmessage` synchronously, and
  a worker failure would have reached `engine.onError`, which the test asserts empty every frame.
- **Stress (dev PC, 32 threads, bounded busy-loop children, CPU only):** with 48 children for 240 s, 392 runs of the
  RPC file, 177 of the voxel test and 242,100 rounds of a trace of the RPC test's steps (every round asserted all 17
  messages arrived, in order); with 64 children for 200 s, 348 RPC runs (the progress test at most 538 ms, median 84),
  186 voxel runs (settled in at most 1,635 ms, median 147) and 81,300 trace rounds. No message was lost and no call
  stayed pending. The one failure was `real worker pool executes tasks` passing its 10 s limit at 48 children:
  worker_threads startup (5 to 6 s at 64 children) is the load-sensitive part, a time-only miss.
- **Regression:** packages/worker/tests/rpc.test.js "every delivery order of call, progress, cancel, result and abort
  settles once and releases the slot" drives a hand-scheduled transport through all 40 orders of call, progress,
  handler finish, result and caller abort, and all 7 with a throwing observer, and asserts one settlement, a released
  slot, ordered progress, nothing sent after settlement and a working client afterwards. It fails if a cancel drops the
  reply, if the client forwards progress after its observer failed, or if the server sends progress after its reply.
  Both CI tests stay on the busy-machine retest list with their limits unchanged.
- **Voxel pin (2026-11-16, lane E):** tests/worker-pool.test.js "a held reply is waited for ..." holds both workers'
  replies through 50 event-loop turns and 100 ms and asserts nothing settles, no worker is retired (the voxel mesher sets
  no job `timeout`), the two other jobs wait in the queue and every reply later settles its own job in order. It pins
  accepted behaviour and passes on the old code, because the pool had no lost-reply defect; the 20 s settle miss is
  worker_threads start time under load (a time-only failure), so `render.test.js` keeps its 20 s limit and stays on the
  busy-machine retest list.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: applyLightmap on a glTF PBR model drew a lost device's texture view after a device restore (KB-OWN-LIGHTMAP1, lightmap)

- **Repro:** `applyLightmap(model, bake)` on a `PBRModel`, then `engine.rebootDevice()` (or a real loss): the model's
  restore built its bind groups from the material extension, whose view and sampler were the old device's, and WebGPU
  refused them ("TextureView ... is associated with [Device], and cannot be used with [Device]"). The same with a live
  `GPULightmapBaker`. Found by the lightmap owner fixture on a real device (loss-attached, both scenes).
- **Cause:** `onModel` (packages/lightmap/src/apply.ts) uploaded the bake once for the attach-time device and put a
  fixed `{ view, sampler }` in the extension. WebGPU objects are valid only with the device that made them (W3C WebGPU,
  section 3.2.1).
- **Fix:** the extension's `textures` is read for the device drawing now: a CPU bake binds the application's own
  `Texture` (one GPU copy per device, uploaded again from its pixels, clamped at the edge); a live bake's texture went
  with its device, so on a restored device the model binds a black 1 x 1 texture and draws no baked light until a new
  baker made on `engine.gpu` is applied (README).
- **Regression:** packages/lightmap/tests/apply.test.js (two fake devices; fails on the old source),
  packages/lightmap/tests/gpu.browser.mjs (restore, same pixels, no validation error, native and WebGL2 layer), and
  the lightmap owner fixture packages/lightmap/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: math box queries gave wrong answers for unbounded and empty boxes (KB-MATH-UNB1, math)

- **Repro (before):** with `I = Infinity` and the cube frustum -1..1 (six planes such as `new Plane(new Vector3(0, -1, 0), 1)`),
  `frustum.intersectsBox(new Box3(new Vector3(-I, 10, -I), new Vector3(I, 20, I)))` was true for a box fully above
  it, and so was `frustum.intersectsBox(new Box3())` (an empty box). `new Triangle(a, b, c).intersectsBox(box)` and
  `new Capsule(a, b, r).intersectsBox(box)` were true for shapes well outside a box unbounded on some axis, such as a
  triangle at y = 0 against the slab y 10..20. `new Ray(o, d).intersectsBox(new Box3())` was true for any direction
  with no zero component. Found by the math mutation run (`frustum` survivors, then a sweep of every math query that
  takes a box).
- **Cause:** `Frustum.intersectsBox` multiplied every normal component by its corner, so a zero component times an
  infinite bound gave `0 * Infinity`, NaN, and a NaN distance never rejects (the class `Box3.intersectsPlane` had,
  fixed in 4abf5d9d6b). `Triangle.intersectsBox` and `Capsule.intersectsBox` work on the box centre and half sizes,
  which an infinite bound makes NaN or infinite, so no axis could separate. `Ray`'s slab test swapped the infinite
  entry and exit times of an empty box into a slab that holds every t.
- **Fix:** a zero normal component adds nothing in `Frustum.intersectsBox`; `Triangle` and `Capsule` cut each infinite
  side back to the shape's own extent on that axis, which leaves the overlap unchanged and keeps every finite box on
  the old code path; `Ray` rejects an empty box first, as `Triangle` and `Capsule` already did. `OBB.fromBox3`
  already refuses non-finite boxes with a coded error, and the `bvh` and `culling` box tests only see finite bounds
  (`MeshBVH` rejects non-finite positions). The voxel renderer, the one user of `Frustum.intersectsBox` outside math,
  culls finite chunk boxes, which take the same path as before.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/math/test/frustum-unbounded.test.js`, `packages/math/test/shape-box-unbounded.test.js`,
  `packages/math/test/ray-box-edges.test.js` (each fails on the old code).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: sheen roughness 0 drew a cyan spike where the terminator crosses the silhouette (KB3297d, gltf/pbr, materials, clustered)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/reference-rendering/run.mjs --case=sheen`
  (and `--like-for-like`), as in docs/whitepaper/reproduce.md. On the RTX A6000 at 512 x 512 the largest error
  against the Khronos glTF Sample Viewer, 171 (205 like for like), sits on two pixels, (382, 167) and (393, 144),
  where Margo draws 74/173/174 (like for like 3/198/200 and 0/205/205) and the viewer 2/2/32 and 0/0/8.
- **Where:** both pixels are on the sheen roughness 0 spheres of SheenTestGrid (sheen colour 0.66 and 1), where the
  terminator crosses the silhouette. A CPU model of gltf/pbr's shader on the sample's own mesh (interpolated normals,
  pixel centres) gives Margo's like-for-like bytes within 3 levels and puts them at n.v 0.083 and 0.104, n.l 0.05 and
  0.01. The normals there face the viewer; the spike is the sheen lobe itself, near its Charlie peak (n.h about 0.07).
- **Cause:** gltf/pbr raised sheen roughness to 0.03 (alpha 9e-4), a Margo design choice that KHR_materials_sheen
  (no floor, default roughness 0), @margoengine/materials and voxel-pathtracer do not have. At roughness 0 the Charlie
  lobe and its albedo vanish away from exact grazing. Which side is right was settled from the BRDF, not from the
  viewer: averaging the radiance over pixel (382, 167) on the analytic sphere (64 x 64 samples, then the display
  transform) gives 83/200/204 at the 0.03 floor, 83/156/161 at 0.01 and 83/85/95 at 0.002, the base alone. The
  viewer shows no sheen anywhere on the three coloured roughness 0 spheres (green minus red is 0 on every pixel);
  Margo drew it on 83, 344 and 359 summed levels of their rims.
- **Second cause, same class:** the sheen lobe raised n.v to 1e-4 but took dot(n, h) as it was. An interpolated
  normal that faces away from the viewer on a silhouette, with n.v = -n.l, gives n.h = 0, the Charlie peak: about
  1.85e6 at roughness 0 (materials already had no floor, so it could draw a white pixel there). n.h is now taken from
  the clamped cosines, (n.v + n.l) / |v + l|, which equals dot(n, h) wherever the normal faces the viewer.
- **Fix:** shared/sheen.js `sheenHalfWGSL` used by gltf/pbr, materials and clustered, and no
  sheen roughness floor in gltf/pbr. Regression tests: packages/gltf/test/sheen.test.js (the two KB3297d
  tests), packages/materials/tests/sheen-backfacing.test.js, packages/clustered/test/clustered.test.js.
- **Effect and re-pin (Scott approved it 2026-11-15):** measured on the A6000 the fix moves the sheen row from absolute 1,056,434, square 32,408,128,
  max 171 to 1,057,125, 32,409,491 and 119 on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer, and like for like from 217,478,
  3,061,310 and 205 to 218,842, 2,944,566 and 103. The maxima and the like-for-like square fall; the absolute sums
  and the main-path square rise slightly, so tests/reference-rendering.test.js and
  docs/whitepaper/results/batch-160-sheen.json were re-pinned once to the measured figures. Where they rise: like for like, the rims of the three roughness 0 spheres move 467 levels closer and the ring inside them
  1,831 further, where the floor's albedo (E(0.05, 0.03) = 0.71) darkened the base near grazing as the viewer's
  encoded albedo lookup darkens it everywhere at roughness 0 (the accepted difference under KB3297c: 102 against 132
  blue at n.v = 1); on the main path also 84 MSAA edge pixels whose spurious cyan from the second cause had covered
  the accepted antialiasing difference (KB3267), 66 of them closer and 16 further.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the imported weather GPU check wanted zero weather bit-identical across two programs (weather)

- **Repro (before):** `node packages/weather/tests/parity-browser.mjs gltf` on WebGPU on Apple silicon (Metal 3)
  failed with `unchanged` 2 (expected 0): GLTFWeather attached at wetness 0, snow cover 0 and snow depth 0 changed
  2 values of the scene colour against the plain gltf/pbr draw. Deterministic; the WebGL2 layer gave 0.
- **Cause:** the check, not the weather maths. The plain gltf/pbr program and the weather-edited one are different
  programs, and WGSL lets an implementation fuse or reassociate f32 operations (WGSL 15.7.5); only an `@invariant`
  position is promised to be the same across programs (WGSL 12.10). Metal rounds one f32 result after the surface
  block differently in the edited program. The weather terms do not leak: with every weather edit behind a branch
  that is never taken the same 2 values still differ. The same class as the sheen albedo check above (KB3297e).
- **Fix:** packages/weather/tests/gltf-check.html proves zero weather inside the weather program. After the first
  zero-weather draw, coverage, rain, puddle size and start, ripple size and strength, ring time, snow depth,
  variation, drift, colour, roughness and grain each move in turn with wetness and snow cover still 0; every picture
  must equal the first bit for bit, and the page counts shader modules and pipelines to require that none is made
  after the first weather draw. A colour term of 0.001 times the puddle coverage added in the shader changes 107,241
  values and fails it. Disposal returns to the plain program and stays a bit-for-bit comparison with the baseline;
  the cross-program difference is printed as `crossProgram` only. The wet, puddle, ring and snow bounds are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `npm run test:browser:parity -w @margoengine/weather` (gltf on WebGPU and with `--compat`), which
  fails on its parent on Apple silicon and passes with the fix on both backends.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the sheen albedo GPU check wanted bit-identical black sheen from two different programs (KB3297e, materials, scripts)

- **Repro (before):** `npm run test:gpu:sheen-albedo -w @margoengine/materials` on WebGPU on Apple silicon (Metal 3)
  failed with "lobes with black sheen: sheen off changed 1 pixels (max 0.0000152587890625)": pixel (68, 133), blue,
  0.0300445556640625 with the shipped albedo table against 0.030029296875 with the previous closed form, neighbouring
  binary16 values. `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/sheen-albedo-gpu-check.js --reference=5cef0a120b^`
  on main 97411fd0b8 (RTX A6000, ANGLE on Vulkan) failed the same way with max 0.0001220703125.
- **Cause:** the check, not the shader. It drew black sheen once with the shipped albedo and once with the previous
  one and wanted the two pictures bit-identical. With black sheen `materialLobesDirect` and `materialLobesAmbient`
  return the layer underneath before any albedo call, so the albedo is never evaluated: an albedo that returns NaN
  moves the same pixel by the same step and leaves no NaN on screen, and one that returns a constant moves nothing.
  But the two pages compile different programs, and WGSL lets an implementation fuse or reassociate f32 operations
  (WGSL 15.7.5 "Reassociation and Fusion"); only an `@invariant` position is promised to be the same across programs
  (WGSL 12.10). Metal, and the driver behind the WebGL2 layer, round one f32 result that never touches the albedo
  differently in the program that holds the other albedo, and the binary16 target turns that into one step on one
  pixel. Bit-identical pixels across two programs were never guaranteed.
- **Fix:** scripts/sheen-albedo-gpu-check.js checks "black sheen changes nothing" inside one compiled program. Black
  sheen, alone and over specular, is drawn at sheen roughness 0.5, 0, 0.25, 0.75 and 1 with only the material
  factors changing; the check requires that those draws create no shader module or pipeline, and that every picture
  equals the first bit for bit. The sheen BRDF and its albedo both depend on the roughness, so any part of them that
  reached the picture would move it: a sheen colour of 0.001 added in the shader changes 8,456 to 10,713 pixels by
  up to 0.00061 and the check fails. With no lobes both pages compile one program and must still match bit for bit.
  The cross-albedo comparison stays where it means something, sheen on, with its bound unchanged (largest change
  0.0632 at roughness 1). Nothing is loosened: every comparison left is exact or keeps its old bound.
- **Second cause, same check:** the previous albedo was taken as the parent of the last commit touching
  packages/shared/sheen.js. Once a later sheen fix (the lobe's n.h from its clamped cosines) edited that file, the
  derived reference already held the shipped table and the check stopped with "already has the shipped fit; pass
  --reference" on a correct tree. The reference is now the closed form the table replaced, pinned byte for byte in
  scripts/sheen-albedo-fit.mjs (`closedFormAlbedoWGSL`, the parent of `closedFormAlbedoCommit` 5cef0a120), and the
  page swaps only that one function into the current shader, so later sheen changes reach both pictures alike and
  neither move nor void the comparison. `--reference=<rev>` still reads another revision from git when asked.
- **Regression:** `npm run test:gpu:sheen-albedo -w @margoengine/materials` (and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`), which fails
  on its parent on Apple silicon and passes with the fix on WebGPU and on the WebGL2 layer;
  packages/materials/test/sheen-albedo-fit.test.js (the pinned closed form equals the one shipped before the table,
  differs from the shipped table, and the check takes no reference from the file's history).

### Fixed 2026-11-18: voxel-pathtracer's mesh-pbr-lobes browser test ends with exit 1 under MARGO_COMPAT=1 (KB-VPT-LOBES-COMPAT, webgl2-compat, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- npm run test:gpu:mesh-pbr-lobes -w @margoengine/voxel-pathtracer`
  (RTX A6000, 2026-11-15, twice). The first leg prints "lobes phase image" and the run ends about 640 s later with
  exit 1 and no error. Without MARGO_COMPAT the test passes, its own WebGL2 leg included.
- **Cause (found 2026-11-15):** under MARGO_COMPAT=1 scripts/browser.js puts the script's first leg on the WebGL2
  layer too, over ANGLE Direct3D 11 (the Windows default), while its log called it `compat: false`. That leg's staged
  programs compile in fxc for minutes with the GPU idle, and a 3 minute idle rule ended the process
  tree with exit 1 and no message. That D3D11 coverage is kept on purpose; the label is fixed: every row and log line
  of the 14 voxel-pathtracer scripts with their own layer leg now names its device (`webgpu`, `webgl2-layer on ANGLE
  D3D11` or `webgl2-layer on ANGLE Vulkan`), and their closing lines name the devices. Regression:
  `tests/compat-ignored.test.js` ("a leg names the device that drew it", "every voxel-pathtracer script with its own
  layer leg labels its legs by device").
- **Then (2026-11-15 to 2026-11-18):** with the compile fixes and no idle rule, the D3D11 leg got past "lobes phase
  image" and the page's own 120 s render signal ended it (`page.evaluate: TimeoutError: signal timed out`); on
  2026-11-18 (RTX A6000, Edge 157) `ready` took 99 s and the signal's error came 259 s after "lobes phase image",
  139 s late, because the page's thread was held.
- **Root cause (2026-11-18):** not the render. ANGLE's Direct3D 11 back end compiles a program's pixel shader at link
  for its first colour output only, and compiles it again, synchronously on the browser's one GPU thread, at the first
  draw into a framebuffer with more colour targets bound. The staged route's programs write several state layers, so
  every one compiled twice and the second compile fell inside the first `renderImage`: a probe of one tracer (26
  programs) measured `ready` 65 s, the first 8 x 8 image 206,354 ms and the second 24 ms. Raw WebGL2 on the same
  browser shows it without the layer: a fragment shader with 4 outputs linked in 64 ms and its first draw took 67 ms
  more, the same shader with 1 output 2 ms; a draw with rasterizer discard on compiles the variant as well. WebGPU
  promises a pipeline from `createRenderPipelineAsync` that draws without a stall, and the layer resolved it at link.
- **Fix:** packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts (`LinkedProgram.warmed`): on ANGLE Direct3D, a program with
  more than one colour target draws once, rasterizer discard on, into 1 x 1 targets of its outputs' base types bound
  at the attachment points its passes use (a buffer for each uniform block, no texture on any unit, so WebGL 2.0 draw
  validation passes and nothing is read or written), and an async pipeline resolves once the GPU has passed that draw.
  Each program's warm draw follows its own link, so the serial compiles overlap the parallel links. Measured, the same
  probe: `ready` 223 s, the first image 78 ms, no GL error (271 s before for ready and first image). The whole
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 test:gpu:mesh-pbr-lobes` passes in 3 min 53 s: its D3D11 leg 220 s to `ready`, then its 11 images
  and the Box snapshot in 4 s, its Vulkan leg 7 s. Sources: W3C WebGPU, `createRenderPipelineAsync`; Khronos
  `KHR_parallel_shader_compile`; Khronos WebGL 2.0, draw validation (uniform blocks, fragment output types).
- **Regression:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-warm.test.js (fails without the fix: the pipeline resolved at
  link with no warm draw), and `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:gpu:mesh-pbr-lobes -w @margoengine/voxel-pathtracer`.
- **Later (2026-11-21, KB6016e):** on an Intel Arc 140V (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11) a draw with rasterizer discard on
  compiled nothing: a warmed 1-output pipeline still paid 131 to 152 ms at its first real draw. The warm draw now
  rasterizes into the 1 x 1 targets (scissor test off, viewport 1 x 1, all colour channels written), and a program
  with no colour target is warmed too, into a 1 x 1 depth-stencil buffer. Its own entry, KB6016e, has the figures.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a Tonemap removed by its scene kept its LocalExposure textures (KB-OWN-TONE1, tonemap)

- **Repro (before):** `Tonemap.attach(engine, { extensions: [new LocalExposure()] })`, draw a frame, then remove the
  Tonemap with its scene (or `dispose()` it, or lose and restore the device): LocalExposure's three `r32float` textures
  and its uniform buffer stayed alive with nothing to draw them. Found by the tonemap owner/lifetime fixture.
- **Cause:** Tonemap freed its own GPU objects only; an extension's were freed only when the app disposed the
  extension itself, which nothing does when a scene or the engine removes the Tonemap.
- **Fix:** `TonemapExtension` gains an optional `dispose()`; Tonemap calls it for each extension when it is disposed,
  removed or restored. LocalExposure makes its objects again on its next encode.
- **Regression:** packages/tonemap/tests/scene-owner.test.js ("releases what its extensions made"),
  packages/tonemap/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js (Tonemap.LocalExposure).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: parseMargoComponents, parseMargoLightmap and glTF physics started in a second scene put part of their work in the default scene (KB-OWN-BLEND2, blender, gltf/pbr, physics)

- **Repro (before):** `scene.use({ name: 'loader', setup: () => (started = parseMargoComponents(engine, componentsBytes, { scripts })) })`
  with packages/blender/tests/fixtures/components.margo built the model in the default scene, and glTF PBR's
  `applyGLTFPhysics` attached its `physics` world there too, even for a model already in the second scene.
  `loadMargoComponents`, `parseMargoLightmap` and `loadMargoLightmap` did the same, the lightmap plugin included.
  Disposing a world in a second scene while the default scene was active left the world in its scene and removed the
  default scene's own plugin named `physics`, if it had one.
- **Cause:** components and lightmap captured no scene before their first await; `applyGLTFPhysics` called
  `World.attach(engine)` after `await import('@margoengine/physics')` and the solver load; the physics wrapper's
  `dispose()` called `engine.hasPlugin` and `engine.removePlugin`, which act on the active scene.
- **Fix:** components and lightmap capture their scene (`captureScene`, packages/shared/scene-scope.js) before the
  first await and build the model, lights, lightmap plugins and script work in it; `applyGLTFPhysics` attaches its
  world in the model's scene (`engine.sceneOf(model)`, else the scene active when it was called), read before its
  first await; `Physics.dispose()` removes the world from `engine.sceneOf(world)`. The solver is unchanged.
- **Regression:** packages/blender/tests/async-scene.test.js (components rows), packages/blender/tests/lightmap-scene.browser.mjs
  (GPU leaf, native and `--compat`), packages/gltf/test/pbr-scene.test.js (applyGLTFPhysics rows),
  packages/physics/tests/physics.test.js ("dispose removes the world from its own scene, not the active one").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: parseMargo and the .margo parse and load functions built in the scene active when they finished (KB-OWN-BLEND1, blender)

- **Repro (before):** `scene.use({ name: 'loader', setup: () => (started = parseMargo(engine, bytes)) })` built the
  model in the default scene: parseMargo built after its image await. `loadMargo`, `loadMargoNodes` and `loadMargoPBR`
  did the same for any scene, since each fetched first and then called its parse function, which captured the scene
  active by then. `parseAnimatedMargo`, `parseMargoCurves`, `parseMargoKTX2` and their load functions, and
  `loadMargoMeshopt`, did the same. Found while writing the blender owner/lifetime fixture (same class as
  KB-OWN-ASYNC1).
- **Cause:** no scene captured before the first await.
- **Fix:** each captures the scene it started in (`captureScene`, packages/shared/scene-scope.js) before its first
  await and builds or parses inside it.
- **Regression:** packages/blender/tests/async-scene.test.js (every function named above).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an inline colour array rebuilt the material on every render (KB-REACT-COLOR1, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<PbrMaterial color={[1, 0, 0]} />` (or `MeshTransmissionMaterial`) inside a component that
  re-renders: every render replaced the mesh's material, and `MeshTransmissionMaterial` released and reloaded its
  transmission model (an async import and a model rebuild), so the surface flickered while the parent re-rendered.
- **Cause:** the effects listed `color` in their dependencies by identity, and an array literal is a new object on each
  render.
- **Fix:** the colour is compared by value (`colorKey` in src/internal.ts: the string, or the array's numbers).
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/react.test.js ("an inline colour array with the same values keeps the material;
  a new value replaces it").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: KeyboardControls let go of a held letter when Shift went down (KB-REACT-KEYS1, react)

- **Repro (before):** `<KeyboardControls map={[{ name: 'forward', keys: ['w'] }]}>`: hold W, then press Shift. The
  next auto-repeat keydown carries `key: 'W'`, so `forward` went false while W was still held; Shift then W never set
  it. With an empty `code` (some virtual keyboards and synthetic events), W pressed, Shift pressed, W released left
  `forward` true until blur.
- **Cause:** entries compared `event.key` exactly, and a held key with no `code` was stored under its `key`, which
  Shift changed between keydown and keyup.
- **Fix:** a one-character key is folded to lower case in the entries and in each event, so a letter is the same key
  in either case. Digits and symbols change with the layout under Shift; the README says to name them by code.
- **Regression:** packages/react/tests/controls-extra.test.js ("a letter key stays held when Shift changes its key
  value, with or without a code").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: loadOBJ kept its materials and textures after its scene removed the mesh (KB-OWN-LOAD1, loaders)

- **Repro (before):** `const h = await loadOBJ(engine, url); engine.sceneOf(h.mesh).removePlugin(h.mesh.name);` left
  the MTL materials, their textures (and their GPU copies) and the fallback material loadOBJ made alive until
  `h.dispose()`; a scene or engine disposal did the same. Found by the loaders owner/lifetime fixture (detach, scene and
  engine leaves of `loadOBJ`).
- **Cause:** only the handle's `dispose()` released them; the mesh, which a scene disposes, did not know about them.
- **Fix:** loadOBJ ties their release to the mesh (`mesh.onDispose`), once; a fallback the app passed is left alone.
- **Regression:** packages/loaders/tests/mtl-lifetime.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a face or VRM avatar whose scene removed its plugin stayed live (KB-OWN-RIG2, rigging)

- **Repro (before):** `const face = addFace(animation); engine.removePlugin('face:' + model.root.id); addFace(animation)`
  threw "already has a face", and the first face kept its model disposal listener until `face.dispose()`. `addVRM`
  kept its listener and still took pose sources after its `vrm:` plugin was removed.
- **Cause:** both registered a plugin with no `dispose`, so removing the plugin (removePlugin, scene or engine
  disposal) never ended the binding.
- **Fix:** the plugin's `dispose` ends the binding (as its own `dispose()` does), and detaching removes the plugin only
  while it is the one registered under the name in its scene.
- **Regression:** packages/rigging/tests/face.test.js and packages/rigging/tests/vrm.test.js ("whose scene removed its
  plugin ends").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a pose-tracking binding or VRMA player whose scene removed its plugin stayed live (KB-OWN-RIG1, rigging)

- **Repro (before):** `const h = await addPoseTracking(animation, avatar); scene.removePlugin(name);` left `h` live
  (its model listener and saved pose kept), and after `scene.use({ name, setup() {} })` a later `h.dispose()` removed
  that new plugin. `playVRMA` behaved the same. Found by the rigging owner/lifetime fixture (detach leaves of
  `addPoseTracking` and `playVRMA`).
- **Cause:** both registered a plugin with no `dispose` and detached with `scene.removePlugin(name)`, by name, whatever
  plugin held it by then.
- **Fix:** the plugin's `dispose` ends the binding (as its own `dispose()` does), and detaching removes the plugin only
  while it is the one registered under the name.
- **Regression:** packages/rigging/tests/pose-tracking.test.js and packages/rigging/tests/vrma.test.js ("whose scene
  removed its plugin").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: loadFBX and the FBX worker loaders started in a second scene built the model in the default scene (KB-OWN-FBX1, fbx)

- **Repro (before):** `const s = engine.createScene('b'); s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = loadFBX(engine, url); } });`
  then `(await p).root.scene` was `engine.scene`, not `s`, and the model plugin went to the default scene too.
  `parseFBXInWorker` and `loadFBXInWorker` did the same, with a Worker and without one. Found by the fbx
  owner/lifetime fixture (secondary-scene leaves of `loadFBX` and `parseFBXInWorker`).
- **Cause:** the KB-OWN-ASYNC1 fix covered `parseFBX` only. `loadFBX` called `parseFBX` after its download, the worker
  loaders after their lazy `import('./index.js')`, and `modelFromPrepared` after the worker reply, so each captured or
  built in the scene active at that moment.
- **Fix:** each of them calls `captureScene(engine)` before its first await and starts `parseFBX` or
  `modelFromPrepared` inside `scope.run`, as the usdz loaders do (KB-OWN-USDZ1).
- **Regression:** packages/fbx/test/load-scene.test.js (the worker loaders through an in-process Worker as well as
  without one).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an async USD load started in a second scene built its model in the default scene (KB-OWN-USDZ1, usdz)

- **Repro (before):** `const s = engine.createScene('b'); s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = parseUSDA(text).create(engine); } });`
  then `(await p).root.scene` was `engine.scene`, not `s`, and the model plugin went to the default scene too.
  `loadUSDZ`, `parseUSDInWorker` and `loadUSDZInWorker` (with and without a Worker) behaved the same, and an
  extension's `created` hook (`previewSurface()` adds a plugin there) ran in the default scene. Found by the usdz
  owner/lifetime fixture (secondary-scene leaves of `USDAsset.create` and `USDAsset.create.previewSurface`).
- **Cause:** `create` builds after awaiting its textures and the extensions' decoders, `loadUSDZ` after its download
  and parse, and the worker loaders' `finish` after the worker reply, each with `parseGLTF` / `modelFromPrepared`,
  which act on the scene active at that moment.
- **Fix:** each of them calls `captureScene(engine)` (`packages/shared/scene-scope.js`, as KB-OWN-GLTF1) before its
  first await and builds the model and runs every `created` hook inside `scope.run`. A loader that hands on to
  another (`loadUSDZ` to `create`, `loadUSDZInWorker` to `parseUSDInWorker` or `loadUSDZ`) starts it inside
  `scope.run`, so the callee captures the same scene; the public signatures are unchanged.
- **Regression:** packages/usdz/tests/scene.test.js (the worker loaders through an in-process Worker as well as
  without one).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: async attach and create functions added their plugin in whichever scene was active after the await (KB-OWN-ASYNC3, machinery, splats, environment, transitions, staging, creative, xr, mcp, animation, save)

- **Repro (before):** `const s = engine.createScene('b'); s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = SurfacePhysics.attach(engine, parts, carriers); } });`
  then `engine.sceneOf(await p)` was `engine.scene`, not `s`. The same held for `TelemetryChannel.attach`,
  `SplatModifier.attach`, `loadProgressiveSplats`, `EnvironmentLighting.load`, `createCustomTransition`,
  `ProgressiveStill.attach`, `createTerrainGrass`, `XR.create` and the model and hdri paths of mcp's `AssetInstaller.load`.
  Two more were found on the way: `cloneModel` (animation) built the clone in the active scene instead of its source's,
  and `restoreScene` (save) loaded its default models in the active scene instead of the `scene` it restored into.
- **Cause:** each added its plugin or built its meshes with `engine.use` or `engine.createMesh` after an await, which act
  on the scene active at that moment; nothing remembered the scene the call started in.
- **Fix:** `captureScene` (or `sceneScope` where the scene is known from an object) from `packages/shared/scene-scope.js`
  before the first await, and `run` around the `engine.use`. `GeometryCachePlayer.attach` (animation) and
  `GPULabelLayer.attach` (labels) already kept their scene, and gltf/pbr's texture stream registers synchronously from
  scoped code; their existing tests pin that. The test fakes of `tests/support/postfx-gpu.js` and staging's pathtrace
