  tests now match the real engine (optional `registerPasses` and `dispose`, scenes with `use`).
- **Regression:** packages/machinery/test/scene.test.js, packages/splats/test/scene.test.js,
  packages/environment/tests/attach-scene.test.js, packages/transitions/test/custom.test.js,
  packages/studio/test/pathtrace.test.js, packages/creative/tests/grass-terrain.test.js, packages/xr/tests/xr.test.js,
  packages/mcp/tests/dispose-scene.test.js, packages/animation/tests/clone.test.js,
  packages/save/tests/default-loader-scene.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an async glTF load started in a second scene built its model in the default scene (KB-OWN-GLTF1, gltf, gltf/pbr)

- **Repro (before):** `const s = engine.createScene('b'); s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = parseGLTFAsync(engine, doc, [bytes]); } });`
  then `(await p).meshes[0].scene` was `engine.scene`, not `s`, and the textured draw (or gltf/pbr's model plugin) was
  added to the default scene too. `loadGLTF`, `loadAuto`, gltf/pbr's `loadGLTF`, `parseGLTFAsync`, the worker and
  progressive loaders behaved the same. Sync `parseGLTF` was right.
- **Cause:** the loaders built after their awaits with `engine.createMesh` and `engine.use`, which act on the scene active
  at that moment, and nothing remembers the scene that was active when the call started. gltf/pbr's static batch node and
  its Gaussian splat clouds had the same flaw.
- **Fix:** `packages/shared/scene-scope.js` (`captureScene`) records the scene before the first await and `run` builds
  inside a temporary plugin of it, as `GeometryCachePlayer.attach` does. gltf and gltf/pbr use it at every point
  where a load turns into engine objects; `batchNode` now makes its node in the model's own scene.
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/scene.test.js, packages/gltf/test/auto.test.js (three loadAuto tests) and
  packages/gltf/test/pbr-scene.test.js.
- **Not covered by a CPU test:** `loadGLTFInWorker` and `parseGLTFInWorker` (Node has no Worker, so they run
  `loadGLTF` and `parseGLTFAsync`, which are covered); their post-worker step goes through the same `scope.run`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: BiomeView attached from a second scene registered in the default scene, and outlived its registration (KB-OWN-BIOMES1, KB-OWN-BIOMES2, biomes)

- **Repro (before):** `s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = BiomeView.attach(engine, world, options); } })` with a second
  scene `s`: once `p` settled, the view's terrain, its streaming plugin and the scatter parts of BiomeObjects and
  FarForest were in `engine.scene`, not `s`. And `engine.scene.removePlugin(<the biomes-view plugin>)` (or a scene or
  engine disposal) left the view streaming, with its terrain, textures and the abort listeners of its tile jobs.
- **Cause:** the three async attaches registered after awaiting their imports with `engine.use` and other packages'
  sync attaches, which act on the scene active at that moment; and the view's own plugin had no `dispose`.
- **Fix:** each captures its scene before the first await with `captureScene` (packages/shared/scene-scope.js) and
  registers inside `run`; the view's plugin disposes the view.
- **Regression:** packages/biomes/tests/view-scene.test.js (fails on the old source, three tests), and the biomes
  owner fixture packages/biomes/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: BiomeView with objects bound a lost device's texture after a device restore (KB-OWN-BIOMES3, biomes)

- **Repro:** the biomes owner fixture's `BiomeView objects` and `BiomeView objects far` entries, loss-attached, on a real
  device (both scenes): after the restore a scatter cull bind group got the lost device's texture view at binding 7.
- **Cause:** binding 7 of scatter's cull pass is the density map (binding 6 is the exclusion buffer, then the density
  view, packages/scatter/src/index.ts `cull`), not the heightmap, which scatter reads anew every frame. BiomeObjects
  made each detail map once (`entry.texture ??= ...`, packages/biomes/src/objects.ts) and FarForest each kind's cover
  map once at attach (`densityMap: () => texture`, packages/biomes/src/far.ts), and kept them across the restore;
  tile writes then went to the old texture through the new device's queue. WebGPU objects are valid only with the
  device that made them (W3C WebGPU, section 3.2.1).
- **Fix:** both maps are made for the device drawing now, as scatter's `DensityBrush.texture(device)` does: on first
  read and again on a restored device, from their CPU copy (the detail data, the newest cover raster), the old copy
  destroyed; writes go only to the current device's copy.
- **Regression:** packages/biomes/tests/objects.test.js (two fake devices; fails on the old source), and the biomes
  owner fixture packages/biomes/tests/owner-lifetime.fixture.js (loss-attached on a real device, 52 leaves).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the sheen lobe used the Neubelt visibility and an albedo fitted to it (KB3297c, shared, gltf/pbr, materials, voxel-pathtracer)

- **Repro (before):** evaluate `margoSheenBRDF` from gltf/pbr's physical shader (packages/gltf/test/sheen.test.js
  does it on the CPU) against the KHR_materials_sheen Charlie lobe with its default shadowing: at sheen roughness 1,
  n.l = n.v = 0.2 Margo gave 0.70 times the spec's value, at roughness 0.3, n.l = n.v = 0.5 it gave 1.63 times.
- **Cause:** packages/shared/sheen.js, which gltf/pbr, materials and voxel-pathtracer inline, divided the Charlie
  distribution by 4 (n.l + n.v - n.l n.v) clamped to 1 (Neubelt and Pettineo 2013), the form the spec says is not
  energy conserving with albedo scaling, and its albedo E, which darkens the layer underneath by 1 - max3(sheen) E,
  was a closed form fitted to that lobe. Refitted to the spec's lobe the same closed form misses by up to 0.30 and is
  not monotonic.
- **Fix (5cef0a120b):** the lobe divides by (1 + Lambda(n.v) + Lambda(n.l)) 4 n.l n.v with Lambda from Estevez and
  Kulla 2017 (eq. 3, Table 1). E is a 16 x 16 table of ln(E R) read bilinearly (layout and comparison in
  docs/clean-room.md): within 0.04109 of the integrated min(E, 1) anywhere, 0.01426 for roughness 0.03 and up, against
  0.98646 for a plain table over (n.v, alpha). The base darkening 1 - max3(sheen) E is unchanged. Each entry that
  inlines it grows by 839 to 1,005 B gzip (materials 64,975 to 65,980 B); core + stage stay 24,843 B.
- **Effect on the SheenTestGrid reference (RTX A6000, 512 x 512, all pixels):** absolute error 1,086,074 to
  1,056,434 on WebGPU and 1,088,183 to 1,056,434 on the WebGL2 layer (which now draws the same picture), square
  32,897,050 to 32,408,128, MAE 1.3810 to 1.3433. Like for like (the viewer's pow(x, 1/2.2) and one sample, first row
  pinned): MAE 0.3410 to 0.2765, absolute 268,164 to 217,478. Of the pixels that changed, 4,618 moved closer to the
  viewer and 3,630 further. The maximum moves from 167 to 171 (like for like 188 to 205) on the same two silhouette
  pixels, (382, 167) and (393, 144), where Margo draws a bright cyan sheen rim (74/173/174) and the viewer nearly
  black (2/2/32); the lobe is brighter at grazing angles, as the spec's shadowing is, and those two pixels were the
  maximum before as well. Why the viewer is dark there: KB3297d, above.
- **Accepted difference:** the viewer's base darkening measures as 1 - sheenColor sRGB_encode(E), its albedo lookup
  read through an sRGB encode the spec does not ask for (a model with that encode matches its spheres within 0.2 to
  0.4 levels for roughness 0.3 and up; at roughness 0.05 it looks like E at about 0.22). Margo keeps E in linear light
  as KHR_materials_sheen and Enterprise PBR define it, so the viewer darkens the base more than Margo does.
- **Regression:** packages/gltf/test/sheen.test.js (the lobe against Charlie with Estevez and Kulla shadowing at
  four roughness values and six angle sets; the table against an integration), packages/materials/test/sheen-albedo-fit.test.js
  (the table within its measured bounds, small roughness and grazing included). GPU: `npm run test:gpu:sheen-albedo
  -w @margoengine/materials` (the table on the GPU within 0.0411 of the integral; 0.04108 measured).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a rightward line's round caps pointed into the segment on Apple's Metal (lines)

- **Repro (before):** `@margoengine/lines`, a segment from (-6, 5.6, 0) to (-2, 5.6, 0) and one from (2, 5.6, 0) to (6, 5.6, 0), width 24, caps `butt` and `round`, WebGPU on an Apple M6 (Chrome, Metal): both drew 86 px long, where a round cap adds half the width at each end. sciviz's `replace-quiver` case differed from the WebGL2 layer in 0.26% of pixels (mean 0.147), since the layer's own atan2 is right there.
- **Cause:** the cap and round-join fan started at `atan2(start.y, start.x)`. A rightward segment's normal is (-0, 1); WGSL's atan2 of it is pi/2, Metal's is -pi/2, so the half fan was drawn turned half a turn, inside the segment.
- **Fix:** packages/lines/src/shader.ts `arc` turns the normalised start direction by the step angle with one cos and one sin, which needs no atan2.
- **Regression:** `packages/lines/scripts/test-browser.js` (`npm run test:browser` in lines) draws the two segments and requires the round one to be longer than the butt one by its thickness (old shader: 87 against 86 px; fixed: within 3 px), natively and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`; sciviz `entries-browser.mjs` `replace-quiver` matches again.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: exporters `GeometryData` required `normals`, which points, lines and the docs leave out (exporters, fbx)

- **Repro (before):** type-check the exporters README POINTS and LINES example, `{positions: [...]}` with no `normals`: TS2741. At run time a triangle list without normals threw `Normals needs N values`, while the doc comment promised the face normal for missing ones. main worked round it by adding unused normals to the example (f23b36d4a9).
- **Cause:** `GeometryData.normals` was typed as required, and `normalizeGeometry` filled missing normals only for points and lines. fbx relied on the required type for geometry it always builds with normals.
- **Fix:** `normals` is optional; a triangle vertex without one takes its faces' area-weighted normal, a point or line keeps none (glTF 2.0 section 3.9.7). fbx names its own `NormalGeometryData` (geometry with normals). The README example passes no normals again. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/geometry-data-normals.test.js and the README example under `npm run check:readmes`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: gltf/pbr's colour vertex was not @invariant under depth-equal replays (KB-INV-GLTF, gltf/pbr)

- **Repro (before):** register a gltf/pbr model with SSAO (`ssao.add`) or TAA (`taa.add`). SSAO's occlusion draw and
  TAA's object velocity redraw its primitives with `depthCompare: 'equal'` against the depth gltf/pbr's colour pass wrote.
- **Cause:** the `Out` structs of gltf/pbr's standard and extended PBR shaders (`packages/gltf/src/shader.ts`; every
  physical variant is built from them) did not declare their clip position `@invariant`. WGSL lets each program fuse or
  reorder its float work (W3C WGSL 15.7.5) and guarantees equal positions only when both programs declare the attribute
  and compute the same expression (12.10), so a replay could drop pixels of the surface it redraws. Core's side of this
  class was fixed earlier the same day (entry under the shadow-caster invariant fix).
- **Fix:** both structs declare `@builtin(position) @invariant clip`. TAA's PBR velocity already computes
  `camera*(model*p)` (`world=f.model*p`, then `camera.current*world`), the colour vertex's order. Regression:
  `tests/invariant-casters.test.js` ('every depth-equal replay vertex and the colour vertex it replays are @invariant')
  now names gltf/pbr's `Out` for SSAO's and TAA's replays and fails on the parent.

### Open 2026-11-15: page screenshots of a WebGPU canvas are blank in a browser started over SSH on Windows (dev PC, session 0)

- **Repro:** over `ssh dev`, `node packages/taa/test/upscale-browser.mjs` (and the velocity-only, reactive, rejection,
  sharpen and deform checks of packages/taa): every `locator(...).screenshot()` of the WebGPU canvas decodes to one
  flat colour, so PSNRs read Infinity and trails 0.0 levels, and the checks fail. The same page on the WebGL2 layer
  (`--compat`) screenshots correctly, and a copy of the canvas texture made in the task that drew it
  (`copyTextureToBuffer`, as packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs, xr-browser.mjs and upscale-velocity-browser.mjs
  read their frames) holds the right pixels on the RTX A6000 there. A 64 x 64 page that clears its WebGPU canvas green
  every animation frame screenshots white.
- **Cause (not proven):** the browser runs in session 0 (see the session 0 entry below); its display compositor there
  does not receive the WebGPU canvas's frames, while WebGL frames reach it. Not Margo code. Also seen the same day: SSH
  logons to the dev PC reset after key exchange for 5 to 20 minutes at a time while GPU checks ran there; cause not
  found.
- **Way out:** run screenshot-based GPU checks in the signed-in desktop session (as the render queue runs shots), or
  read frames from the canvas texture as the checks named above do.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: TAAUpscale silhouettes flickered while the camera moved (Orrery l11 gear posts, lane OF2)

- **Repro (before):** the Orrery shot l11 (fast camera past the brass gear posts, TAAUpscale at scale 0.72): the right
  post edge alternated 0.363 luma levels a frame in step with the Halton jitter, against 0.057 with a slower camera
  and 0.043 with TAA off (lane OF1, dev PC). `packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs` reproduces it on a bare post:
  0.361 with the camera orbiting at 0.01 rad a frame against 0.142 at 0.001 rad.
- **Cause:** the resolve compared the reprojected nearest depth with the one history depth texel it landed on. Both
  depths are the 3x3 nearest at render size, and the jitter moves that dilation by up to one render pixel a frame, so
  at a silhouette fringe that texel held the post on some frames and the far wall on others; history was rejected on
  those frames and the pixel showed the raw jittered frame. With the camera moving the reprojected point lands on new
  texels every frame, so the rejections rose with camera speed.
- **Fix:** `packages/taa/src/upscale.ts` tests the depth against the min/max of a 3x3 history footprint, taps one
  render pixel apart (the velocity entry shares the resolve). Edge alternation 0.195 on WebGPU and 0.201 on the WebGL2
  layer (0.200 there before: the layer already reads each depth as the nearest of five texels), no trail behind a
  box crossing the wall. Regression: `packages/taa/test/stability-browser.mjs` (fails at 0.361 on WebGPU before; both
  backends, in test:gpu and test:gpu:compat; bound in docs/limits.md). Sources in packages/taa/README.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: DynamicInstances.pick on the WebGL2 layer answered null right after the first frame (culling)

- **Repro (before):** on the WebGL2 compatibility layer, attach a `DynamicInstances` with one instance at the centre,
  render one frame, wait for the queue and `pick` the centre: null. Ten frames before the pick answered 0.
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/culling/test/gpu/pick-clear-check.mjs` failed "the centre picks instance 0".
- **Cause:** on the layer the CPU culling route is a lazy import. The first frame culls on the GPU route, which leaves
  `world` (the rows picking and shadows read) to the `fill` pass; the import then resolved before the pick, and `fill`
  skipped whenever a CPU route was set, although that cull had not written `world`. The pick drew an empty `world`.
- **Fix:** `packages/culling/src/dynamic.ts` keys `filled` to the route each cull took: a CPU cull marks `world`
  written, a GPU cull leaves it to the next `fill`, whatever loads in between. No wait or frame count is involved.
- **Regressions:** `packages/culling/test/dynamic.test.js` ("a route that loads after a GPU cull still gets `world`
  built") and `packages/culling/test/gpu/pick-clear-check.mjs` under `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: every pick in Firefox found the first mesh, even over empty background (KB-FX273, core and culling)

- **Repro (before):** in Firefox 157 on Windows (RTX A6000), `engine.pick(1, 1)` over the clear colour of a scene
  with one box returned that box, and so did every other pixel; `CulledParts.pick` and `DynamicInstances.pick` answered
  part 0 and instance 0 the same way. `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` with
  `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox` failed "pick finds nothing off the mesh"; the browser matrix
  (`packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs --browser=firefox`) found it.
- **Cause:** the pick passes cleared their r32uint id target to 4294967295 to mean "nothing". Firefox clears an integer
  target through float32: measured, a clear of 4294967295 read back 0 and 16777217 read back 16777216 (7 and
  4294967040 came back exact). 0 is the first mesh's id. Edge and Safari keep the full value.
- **Fix:** core's pick pass (`packages/core/src/renderer.ts`) and the culling pickers (`packages/culling/src/parts.ts`,
  `packages/culling/src/dynamic.ts`) write each id one up and clear to 0, which every browser keeps. Core and stage
  stay at 24,843 B gzip before and 24,841 B after (`npm run build:packages`).
- **Regressions:** `tests/deep-core-pick-clear.test.js` (the real `GPURenderer.pick` on a fake device that clears as
  Firefox does), `packages/core/tests/pick-clear.browser.mjs` and `packages/culling/test/gpu/pick-clear-check.mjs`
  (real GPU, with clear values rounded through float32 by `tests/support/float32-clears.js`, so they fail without the
  fix in any browser).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a small raster's default chunk read back all zeros on the WebGL2 layer (sciviz/aggregate)

- **Repro:** `aggregateRaster` with `gpu` on the WebGL2 layer (Chrome, ANGLE Metal, Apple M6), an 8 x 8 raster and
  4096 or more segment rows in one chunk (the default `chunkRows` is 32768): every bin's count read back 0 where the
  CPU reference counted 27,324 in all, with no page error. 3,000 rows were right, 3,500 were zeros; with the earlier
  hardware-float coverage 4096 rows were right and 32768 were zeros. WebGPU on the same GPU was right.
- **Cause:** the kernel gave each bin one invocation that tested every row of the chunk, so a raster with few bins
  ran a few long invocations. Chrome on ANGLE's Metal back end drops a draw (the layer runs this kernel as a point
  draw) whose single invocation runs too long: nothing it stores lands, `gl.getError()` stays 0, the context is not
  lost (`isContextLost()` false, no `webglcontextlost` within 9 s), so the layer has nothing to report and the
  readback held the buffer's zeros. Raw WebGL2 repro with no layer:
  `node packages/sciviz/tests/webgl-long-invocation-repro.mjs` (not a gate): 65,536 points of 4,000 loop
  iterations each land and 64 points of 100,000 are dropped, in two runs out of two (64 points of 40,000 were
  dropped in some runs and not others). Once a draw has been dropped, later draws in the same browser, even on a
  new context, were sometimes dropped too. Not reported upstream from here (this repository does
  not read or file against Chromium or ANGLE code).
- **Fix:** an invocation now owns a bin and a slice of at most 512 rows (`SLICE_ROWS` in
  packages/sciviz/src/aggregate-shader.ts), and a second pass folds each bin's slice records in row order into the
  same record one invocation over the chunk produced. The slice records must fit one storage binding, or the chunk
  is shortened. docs/limits.md records the same rule for any compute kernel on the layer.
- **Regression:** the pixel-centre tie check in `packages/sciviz/tests/aggregate-browser.mjs` (`npm run
  test:browser:aggregate`) runs 32768 lines, triangles and quads (one default chunk) on an 8 x 8 raster on both
  backends, compares every statistic with the CPU reference and checks the chunk ran as slices and one merge; with one
  invocation per bin the WebGL2 layer read all zeros.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a tree stand-in showed the inside of its crown and half of its trunk (procedural standin)

- **Repro (before):** `generateTreeStandIn('broadleaf')` (also conifer and palm): all eight canopy triangles wound
  clockwise seen from outside, against their own vertex normals, and the trunk was a cross of two one-sided quads. Core
  culls back faces with front face 'ccw', so the biomes far forest (single-sided material, `Scatter`) drew the far side
  of each crown from inside, lit as if facing away, and no trunk from half the directions. `generateTreeStandIn('constructor')`
  passed the kind check and returned NaN positions.
- **Cause:** packages/procedural/src/standin.ts listed the canopy faces in the opposite order to the trunk's, and the
  kind check read an inherited key of the crown table.
- **Fix:** the canopy winds counter-clockwise from outside, the trunk is an open three-sided prism (14 triangles in
  all, each facing out), and the kind must be the table's own key. Regression: packages/procedural/test/detail.test.js
  "a tree stand-in faces out everywhere".

### Fixed 2026-11-16: marchingCubes placed vertices off the surface, up to 23% out for a metaball (procedural)

- **Repro (before):** a 28^3 grid of `-max(0, 2 / (d^2 + 1e-6) - 12)` over the default bounds, `marchingCubes(grid,
  { resolution: [28, 28, 28], level: -80 })`: vertices up to 1.229 times the exact radius sqrt(2 / 92); the same field
  as a function gave the same misplaced vertices, and a plain sphere `x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - 0.25` at resolution 16 was held only
  within 0.02.
- **Cause:** packages/procedural/src/index.ts `extract` was marching tetrahedra: each cube cut into six tetrahedra, so
  vertices also lay on face and body diagonals (sqrt 2 and sqrt 3 cells), where linear interpolation of a curved field
  strays furthest; and a density function was only ever read at the grid points, never at the vertex.
- **Fix:** Marching Cubes on the cube's axis edges (Lorensen and Cline 1987), each cube's polygons traced on its faces
  with alternating faces split by the asymptotic decider (Nielson and Hamann 1991), so neighbouring cubes agree and the
  mesh stays closed; with a density function each vertex is the function's root on its edge by the Illinois method
  (Dowell and Jarratt 1971), as Bloomenthal (1988) converges vertices on a known function. Grid vertices are now at
  most 1.073 times the radius in the repro and function vertices exact to 1e-6. Regression:
  packages/procedural/test/procedural.test.js "Marching Cubes puts vertices on the surface".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: marchingCubes gave zero-area triangles where the surface passes through a grid point (procedural)

- **Repro (before):** `marchingCubes((x, y, z) => Math.hypot(x, y, z) - 0.5, { resolution: [13, 13, 13] })`: 252 of
  888 triangles had zero area (36 at resolution 9 and 17). The poles, and points such as (1/3, 1/3, -1/6) where the
  field rounds to within 1e-17 of the level, are grid points.
- **Cause:** packages/procedural/src/index.ts `extract` made one vertex per grid edge, so every edge from a grid point
  on the surface put its own vertex on that point, and a triangle with two of them has no area. The face orientation
  was also measured from a triangle corner to the outside cube corner, which is zero when that corner is the point.
- **Fix:** a crossing on a grid point, exactly or within the float32 output's precision, takes the point's own slot and
  sits on it, so the edges from it share one vertex, and triangles with a repeated vertex are dropped: the corner
  snapping of regularised marching tetrahedra (Treece, Prager and Gee, "Regularised marching tetrahedra: improved
  iso-surface extraction", Cambridge CUED/F-INFENG/TR 333, 1998, fetched and read). Faces are oriented by an inside
  and an outside corner of their tetrahedron, whose difference always has a positive component along the face normal.
  Regression: packages/procedural/test/procedural.test.js "a surface through grid points exactly".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an SDF surface through a grid point gave zero-area triangles (procedural sdf)

- **Repro (before):** `createSdfModeler()` then `mesh({ type: 'sphere', radius: 0.8 })` at the default resolution 24
  with the default bounds: 30 of 3,708 triangles had zero area (two of their vertices coincide at a pole, (0.8, 0, 0)
  and the like). The default bounds put each pole on a grid point whenever the resolution is a multiple of 12.
- **Cause:** the field at that grid point rounds to about -1e-16, so the point counted as inside: every edge from it
  to an outside neighbour crossed on the point itself, or 1e-8 from it along the tangent, and the cells around it put
  their QEF vertices on top of each other, so the dual quads between them collapsed
  (packages/procedural/sdf-kernel/src/lib.rs, `build`).
- **Fix:** a sample within the bisection's own resolution (2^-40 of a step) of zero takes zero, which counts as
  outside, so rounding no longer decides its side; sdf.wasm 41,121 to 41,233 B. Regression:
  packages/procedural/test/sdf.test.js "a surface through grid points" (spheres at 12, 24 and 36, boxes on grid planes:
  no zero-area triangle, no two vertices within 1e-6).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: SDF meshes folded triangles inward at CSG seams (procedural sdf)

- **Repro (before):** 300 random unions of two spheres at resolutions 4 to 43 gave 87 triangles that faced inward from
  both spheres at their centroid (3 to 10 a mesh at the seam, for example the six cases in the regression test).
- **Cause:** `build` in packages/procedural/sdf-kernel/src/lib.rs always split each dual quad along its 0-2 diagonal.
  A dual quad's four vertices sit anywhere in their cells, so the quad is rarely planar or convex, and splitting a
  non-convex quad along its outside diagonal folds one triangle back over the other.
- **Fix:** the split takes the diagonal whose two triangles keep the larger smaller area projected on the quad's edge
  axis, which a simple quad always has; the same scan now finds 8, left where a QEF vertex sits across a sharp seam
  (docs/limits.md, LIM-632). Regression: packages/procedural/test/sdf.test.js "no folded triangles".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: building shells had T junctions at every window, floor line, base and roof edge (procedural buildings)

- **Repro (before):** `createBuildingGenerator().generate()` (defaults): 428 of the shell's 1,272 directed edges had no
  matching opposite edge. The wall strip beside each window ran floor to ceiling as one quad while the sill and head
  quads put vertices on its side, and the base, flat roof, gables and slopes were single polygons whose edges passed the
  wall's bay corners. Projected, those vertices land off the long edge, so the shell rasterises with pinholes along the
  lines, and it cannot be welded into a closed solid.
- **Cause:** `generate` in packages/procedural/buildings-kernel/src/lib.rs emitted five independent quads a bay and one
  polygon for each cap.
- **Fix:** each wall side is one grid cut at every bay end, window side, floor line, sill and head (shared vertices,
  exact corners); base and flat roof are fans from the centre over every wall column; gables fan from the apex over the
  top floor's columns; each slope fans from the ridge over its eave. Areas, volume, bays and materials are unchanged.
  buildings.wasm 31,252 B to 38,840 B raw. Regression: packages/procedural/test/buildings.test.js "the shell is closed".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: usdz `curves()` attached its Lines and Points plugins to the default scene (wrong-scene follow-up)

- **Repro (before):** import a USD stage with `curves()` into a model that is in a second scene: the hook attaches its plugins after dynamic imports, when the active scene is the default one, so `usd-curves-lines-0` and `usd-curves-points-0` landed in the default scene while the model drew in the other. (Name probing for a free id read the active scene too.)
- **Cause:** `Lines.attach(engine, ...)` and `engine.use(...)` act on the active scene.
- **Fix:** `packages/usdz/src/curves.ts` attaches through the model's own scene (`engine.sceneOf(model)`) and probes names there; dispose already removed through `sceneOf`. The tiles points plugin was fixed the same way earlier (`TilesRenderer.loadPoints` joins `engine.sceneOf(this)`). Regressions: `packages/usdz/tests/dispose-scene.test.js` (curves case, fails on the old source), `packages/tiles/tests/dispose-scene.test.js` (points plugin joins and leaves the renderer's scene).

- **Repro (before):** `curl -sIL https://margoengine.com/errors` answered 404, and so did `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt`,

### Fixed 2026-11-15: space-colonisation trees stacked copies of the same branch node (procedural trees)

- **Repro:** `(await createTreeGenerator()).generate({ seed: 1 })` returned 682 nodes, 315 of them at exactly the
  position of a sibling; `attractionPoints: [1, 0.05, 0, -1, 0.05, 0]` grew 20 copies of one child from the root.
- **Cause:** the growth rule of Runions et al. (2007, eq. 2) moves a node a distance D toward its points, and a point
  that lies less than D/2 along that direction stays nearer the parent than the new child. The parent kept the same
  points, computed the same direction and added the same child every round (packages/procedural/trees-kernel/src/lib.rs).
- **Fix:** a node never grows a second child at the position of one it already has; those points stop growth and the
  result reports `stalled` with them in `remainingAttractions`. Regression: packages/procedural/test/trees.test.js "a node
  never regrows a child" and the kernel test `a_node_does_not_regrow_an_existing_child`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: plant trunks widened toward the top, cactus arms sheared, tree base caps mirrored their normal map (procedural)

- **Repro:** `generatePalmMesh().trunk` was 0.13 m in radius at the root and 0.22 m under the crown (birch 0.06 to 0.16,
  snag 0.07 to 0.3); `generateCactusMesh()` arms reached 0.166 m from their axis where a 0.14 m column with a 6 percent rib
  reaches 0.148; `meshTree` wrote tangent w = +1 on every base-cap vertex, whose UV disc is mirrored as seen from below,
  so a bark normal map lit the base caps from the wrong side.
- **Cause:** `trunk()` in packages/procedural/src/plants.ts put its first radius at the root while every caller passed
  the tip first; the cactus ribs were applied after the parts were merged, about the world Y axis instead of each
  column's own; `Builder.vertex` in tree-mesh.ts always wrote w = 1.
- **Fix:** `trunk(height, tip, base)` tapers from base to tip, ribs are applied to each cylinder before it is placed, and
  the base cap writes w = -1 (flat shading keeps each vertex's sign). Regression: packages/procedural/test/plants.test.js
  ("trunks and limbs taper", "cactus arms are ribbed") and test/tree-mesh.test.js ("store the tangent sign").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a new WeatherRegions base left partial fronts and cells filled from the old one

Repro: `new WeatherRegions({base: 'clear', fronts: [{origin: [0, 0], direction: 0, speed: 0, behind: {fog: 1}}]})`,
then `map.base = 'snow'`: `stateAt(0, -1000).snow` was 0, the clear base's, though a partial front takes its missing
fields from the base. Cause: `packages/weather/src/regions.ts` resolved each partial state once, when the front or cell
was added, and the `base` setter changed only the base. Fix: the setter resolves every front and cell again over the
new base (all checked first, so a bad base changes nothing), in place, so the removers keep working. The
`RegionWeather` doc said "the weather beneath it"; the tested contract is the base, and the doc now says so.
Regression: `packages/weather/tests/regions.test.js` ("a new base refills the missing fields").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an FBX Stingray material's UV offset and scale reached only its base colour map

- **Repro (before):** `@margoengine/fbx` with `pbrMaterials`, a Maya Stingray PBS material with `Maya|uv_scale` 2, 3, a colour map and a normal map: the glTF base colour texture carried `KHR_texture_transform`, the normal texture had none, and the same held for the metallic-roughness, occlusion and emissive maps.
- **Cause:** `MaterialData` in `@margoengine/exporters` had a transform slot for the base colour texture only (`baseColorTextureTransform`), so the FBX import had nowhere to put the Stingray transform for the other maps, which the shader applies to all of them.
- **Fix:** `MaterialData` gains `metallicRoughnessTextureTransform`, `normalTextureTransform`, `occlusionTextureTransform` and `emissiveTextureTransform` (type `TextureTransform`, the shape of `baseColorTextureTransform`; KHR_texture_transform allows the extension on every textureInfo). The glTF writers write each and the GLB reader reads each back; the FBX import sets the Stingray transform (V turned) on every map it writes. Regressions: `packages/exporters/tests/texture-transforms.test.js` (all slots, round trip, refusals) and `packages/fbx/test/pbr-rules.test.js` "reach every map the shader samples". The USDZ, OBJ and Roblox writers still use the base colour transform only (`packages/exporters/README.md`).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a browser close past its budget left its host and browser running (KB-P3h, scripts)

Seen once: `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/blender/tests/nodes-browser.mjs` printed its passing result beside two other busy
GPU jobs and then did not exit for over 20 minutes (its 1,500 s limit killed it, exit 124); alone it exits in
about 62 s. The step after the result is `browser.close()`.

Repro (before): `node tests/fixtures/stuck-close-suite.mjs 1000`, a suite whose browser host never acknowledges the
end and whose client close never returns, which reports the close error and goes on, as
`scripts/visual-regression.js` does. The close threw `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` at its budget and the suite never ended.

Cause: `withBoundedClose` in `scripts/lib/browser.mjs` bounded the wait, not the browser. Past the budget it threw
while its hosted close was still waiting, so the step that releases the host never ran: the host and the browser
under it kept running and the host's pipes stayed referenced. The host waits for an end request that never comes and
the suite waits for the host, with nothing printed.

Fix: a hosted close has a hard limit, `CLOSE_LIMIT_MS` (20,000 ms, sized from closes of 0.25 s alone and 0.28 to
2.03 s under load). Past it the close kills the host and the browser with their process trees, waits up to
`CLOSE_KILL_MS` (8,000 ms), releases the host and fails with `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` carrying `open`, `killed` and
`survivors`, inside the 30,000 ms shutdown budget (docs/limits.md, "Browser close limit"). A normal close never takes
the kill path. Regression: `tests/browser-teardown.test.js` (a real stuck host and browser are killed at a 1,000 ms
limit and the suite exits on its own; with the old code it was still running 45 s later).

Not proved: that this is the path the nodes-browser run took. That suite does not catch the close error, and an
uncaught error ends Node at once, so a timed-out close there would have exited 1 with a message. Twelve runs of it
with MARGO_COMPAT=1 beside other GPU suites and 10 to 12 CPU hogs (2026-11-15) all exited, closing in 0.25 to 2.03 s.
Two other ways a Node process on Windows stops with no output were measured on the way: a write to a stdout or
stderr pipe its reader is not draining blocks the whole process, timers included (a 4 MiB write held a 500 ms timer
for good), and `process.exit` waits for a worker thread blocked in a system call.

### Open 2026-11-27: the one unexplained stop of the Blender nodes browser check (KB-P3h-stop, scripts, not reproduced)

- **Repro:** none. The run above under KB-P3h is the only sighting. 6 more runs of
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 MARGO_TRACE_SHUTDOWN=1 node packages/blender/tests/nodes-browser.mjs` on 2026-11-27 all exited (70 to
  102 s), their longest browser teardown step 309 ms.
- **Cause:** not known. Every close step of `openBrowser` is bounded and throws, which this suite does not catch.
- **Rerun 2026-11-28:** 3 more traced runs on main (RTX A6000) all exited (101, 88 and 93 s) with no `[linger]` line.
  Still not reproduced.
- **Instrumented 2026-11-27:** a process still running 60 s after its last browser suite closed prints one `[linger]`
  line naming its open resources (`reportLinger`, scripts/support/shutdown.mjs; tests/linger-report.test.js). A silent
  stop with no such line means the event loop itself was blocked, for example by an undrained output pipe.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: committed Wasm blueprints differed by build system

Repro (before): read a blueprint listed in `scripts/wasm-blueprints.mjs` for a
Rust path with a backslash: erosion, compute-cpu, compute-decomp, compute-onnx,
draco-encoder, basis-encoder, buildings, caves, dungeon, poisson, sdf, trees,
sciviz-fallback, sciviz-flow, machinery-kernel and trace-mesh held `src\...rs`
panic locations, and so did physics-kernel, navmesh-raster and wfc, which the
first report missed. The same sources built on Linux or macOS give `src/...rs`,
so `node scripts/wasm-blueprints.mjs --rebuild --compare` could not match them
there. Two more differences by system were found on the way: the machinery
blueprint's gzip header held the compressing system's OS code (RFC 1952
2.3.1: 10 on Windows, 3 on Linux, 19 on macOS), and every build script passed
the shell's own `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` (which replaces `RUSTFLAGS`),
`CARGO_PROFILE_*`, `CARGO_BUILD_*`, `RUSTC` and `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` through to
Cargo, any of which changes the bytes or the compiler.

Cause: Cargo names a crate's own files relative to it with the host
separator, and the per-crate remap had been added to the decoders' native
build only. Fix at the root: one build environment,
`scripts/rust-wasm-env.mjs`, which every blueprint build script uses and every
record hashes. It maps each source folder onto itself with forward slashes
(`--remap-path-prefix=src=src/`, one mapping per nested folder, the same flags
on every system), drops the variables above and pins the target folder. The
machinery gzip header carries 255 (unknown). `writeRecord` refuses a module
holding a backslash Rust path and hygiene reports one in any committed
blueprint, so it cannot come back. All 19 modules were rebuilt: each differs
from its old bytes only in the separators (92 to 47), and the next full rebuild
with `--compare` matched all 24 blueprints byte for byte. `--compare` now
compares the committed file without its checkout line endings (a deflated or
gzip TypeScript blueprint is what git holds) and puts a differing file back.
`npm run check:wasm-repro` runs that rebuild over every blueprint where the
pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml) is installed and says so where it is
not; local CI runs it in verify before the package build. Regression:
tests/wasm-blueprints.test.js (no committed blueprint, and no `.wasm` file git holds, holds a host path, a
backslash path is stale and refused, the build environment's remaps and
dropped variables, every build script uses it, the gzip OS byte), each failing
on the old code or blueprints.

Sources: The rustc book, "Command-line arguments", `--remap-path-prefix`
(Rust Project, 2026, https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/command-line-arguments.html);
The Cargo Book, "Environment variables" and "Configuration" (Rust Project,
2026, https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html);
The rustup book, "Overrides" (Rust Project, 2026,
https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/overrides.html); P. Deutsch, RFC 1952,
"GZIP file format specification version 4.3" (IETF, 1996,
https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1952); Reproducible Builds, "Build path"
(reproducible-builds.org, 2024,
https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/build-path/).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Event Horizon drew a ring of streaked stars round the shadow on the WebGL2 layer (shader/black-hole)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/shader/test/black-hole-check.mjs` on the RTX A6000 (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11
  for the layer) failed with "stars: stretched (median axis ratio 2.0644882521065133)"; native WebGPU passed (1.14).
  The frame showed a ring of bright streaks just outside the shadow that WebGPU does not draw, and the disk's fine
  detail measured 0.0232 against WebGPU's 0.0177 (its footprint filter was off).
- **Culprit:** c3d9c49926 (the entry's first commit) took `dpdx(rd)` in uniform control flow after the march but used
  it only inside `if (escaped)`, and the disk footprints only inside `if (k < crossings)`. The star check came with
  634e730538 and was run on the Radeon 680M only, where the layer passed; it failed on the A6000 from then on (the
  parent of 6ad1bf12e2, 8a552c3818, fails the same way: median 3.42), so 6ad1bf12e2 did not cause it.
- **Cause:** below the shader text: the compiled program evaluates a derivative inside the one branch that uses it.
  Inside a branch some invocations of a 2x2 quad do not run, and there a derivative is undefined (GLSL ES 3.00.6,
  section 8.9; WGSL "Derivatives"); on this driver it is 0. At the shadow's edge every quad mixes escaped and captured
  rays, so J was 0, the magnification hit its cap of 40 and each star cell drew its star at full flux on the pixel.
  Minimal repro and the layer's own fix: the entry "a derivative used only inside a per-pixel branch read 0", below.
- **Fix:** the fragment uses every value made from a derivative in uniform control flow: the disk images past the
  crossings and the sky of a ray that did not escape weigh 0 instead of being skipped (`packages/shader/src/black-hole.ts`).
  WebGPU's numbers are unchanged; the layer now reads stars 1.136 and disk 0.01769 (WebGPU 1.143 and 0.01769).
  Regressions: `packages/shader/test/black-hole.test.js` "no ray-dependent branch is the only user of a derivative"
  (fails on the old shader: branches `k < crossings` and `escaped`) and the star check above on MARGO_COMPAT=1.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a derivative used only inside a per-pixel branch read 0 on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (webgl2-compat)

- **Repro:** a fragment shader on the WebGL2 layer, RTX A6000, Edge, ANGLE Direct3D 11: `var r = f(p); var esc =
  false;` set in a loop by pixel, then `let d = dpdx(r);` after the loop and `if (esc) { a loop that uses d; return
  d; }`. WebGPU returned the true differences; the layer returned 0 for every pixel in a quad the branch splits, for
  all nine dpdx, dpdy and fwidth forms, a vector derivative, one taken in a helper function, and `textureSample` and
  `textureSampleBias` (their implicit derivatives: level 0 where WebGPU reads level 2). The translated GLSL kept
  `dFdx` before the `if`. With a straight-line branch body, or with one more use of `d` after the `if`, it was exact.
- **Cause:** below Margo's text: the Direct3D 11 compile moves a derivative, or a sample that takes implicit ones,
  into the only branch that uses its value, where the quad's other invocations do not run, and there it is undefined
  (Khronos, "The OpenGL ES Shading Language 3.00.6", 2016, section 8.9,
  https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/es/3.0/GLSL_ES_Specification_3.00.pdf). WGSL defines a derivative taken in
  uniform control flow wherever its value is used (W3C, "WebGPU Shading Language", "Derivatives" and "Uniformity
  Analysis", https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#derivatives). HLSL's own rules make gradients inside varying flow illegal and
  have the compiler reorder them (Microsoft, "tex2D (HLSL reference)", Remarks,
  https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-tex2d-s-t-ddx-ddy; "HLSL errors and
  warnings", X4014), and a compiler that does not treat derivatives as convergent operations sinks them like any other
  value (LLVM Project, "Convergent Operation Semantics", https://llvm.org/docs/ConvergentOperations.html, whose first
  example is a textureSample sunk into an if; O. Anderson, "RFC: Convergent attribute", llvm-dev, 2015,
  https://lists.llvm.org/pipermail/llvm-dev/2015-May/085531.html). Which branches are per pixel is the divergence
  question of D. Sampaio, R. Martins de Souza, S. Collange, F. M. Q. Pereira, "Divergence Analysis", ACM TOPLAS 35(4),
  2013, https://doi.org/10.1145/2523815; the fix does not need it.
- **Fix:** the GLSL back end (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/glsl/emit.ts`, `pin`) adds every derivative-made value of a
  fragment (dpdx, dpdy, fwidth in each form, and textureSample, textureSampleBias, textureSampleCompare and
  textureSampleGrad results) into a vec4 `_dk`, and every output's existing select on a run-time value
  (`gl_FragCoord.w > 0.0 ? value : _dk`, never false for a rasterized fragment) takes it as the other operand; integer
  and depth outputs get the same select, and a shader with no output but a discard gets a discard that never runs.
  The value is then needed on every path to the outputs, so the compile must evaluate the derivative where WGSL does,
  and no output changes on any driver. A derivative inside `select()` is now evaluated eagerly (it was a GLSL ternary).
  Correct by construction, not a pattern match: no branch analysis decides what is pinned. Cost: one add per
  derivative or implicit sample; no draws, buffers or bindings change; webgl2-compat/glsl 44,389 to 44,683 B gzip.
  The black hole shader before f0596dd265 now passes its star check on MARGO_COMPAT=1 (median axis 1.136, disk
  0.01769, the same as the reworked shader).
- **Regressions:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/features.html` case `derivativeBranch` (run by features-browser.mjs in
  `npm run test:gpu`; failed on every variant before), and `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js` "every
  derivative and implicit-derivative sample of a fragment is pinned into an output" and the three tests after it.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: saved Unity mesh and clip assets kept main-object names that differed from their file names (exporters, Unity companion)

Found by the batch 132 line-by-line read of packages/exporters (audit p12d), then run in Unity.

- Repro: `npm run test:unity` in packages/exporters with com.margo.mesh 0.3.0 before the fix (Unity 6000.6.7f1,
  glTFast 6.20.0, a bundle with mesh `Art` and clip `Walk-loop`). Unity warned "Main Object Name 'Walk-loop' does
  not match filename 'Animation_0'" and "Main Object Name 'Art(Clone)' does not match filename 'Mesh_0_0'" at
  generation and again on a forced reimport. The forced reimport left every saved file, .meta and `IsCurrent`
  unchanged, so the hash comparison was not broken; the names and the warnings were the defect.
- Cause: src/unity/Editor/ImportCompanion.Resources.cs `Save` created each single-object native asset
  (AssetDatabase.CreateAsset) at its stable file name and then set the main object's name back to the clone's name
  (the glTF clip name, or the mesh clone's `Art(Clone)`). A single-object native file's one object is its main
  asset, and Unity expects that main object to carry the file's name.
- Fix: `Save` names the main object after its file (`Mesh_0_0`, `Animation_0`); the saved-clip check
  follows it. The glTF clip name stays where users pick it: the controller state is created from the ordered clip
  identity, so `Animator.Play("Walk-loop")` still plays the source clip. After the fix the run shows every main
  object named after its file before and after the forced reimport, no warning, unchanged hashes and `IsCurrent`
  true. Sources: Unity Scripting API, AssetDatabase.CreateAsset
  (https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.3/script-reference/unityeditor/assetdatabase/createasset); Unity Manual,
  Customizing the Asset Database workflow, on the main asset of a file
  (https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/AssetDatabaseCustomizingWorkflow.html).
- Regression: packages/exporters/tests/unity-check.test.js (the companion source, and the judge of the real before and
  after Unity runs kept in packages/exporters/tests/unity/), plus the opt-in native check `npm run test:unity`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: exporters audit fixes (exporters, batch 132 audit)

- **exportModel dropped loaded points and lines.** Repro: load a GLB with a mode 0 or mode 1 primitive and
  `exportModel` it: the mesh was gone. Cause: gltf/pbr keeps them in `model.pointsAndLines`, which src/model.ts never
  read. Also an unindexed triangle or line strip was written unindexed with its decoded list mode, so it read back
  as a list of its vertices. Fixed: they go back into their mesh in source order as glTF POINTS and LINES, and
  strips, loops and fans are written as the indexed lists gltf/pbr decodes them to (glTF 2.0 3.7.2.1). The engine
  exporters, which write triangles only, call `onWarning` (code `unsupported`) instead of dropping them silently.
  Regression: packages/exporters/tests/points-lines.test.js.
- **flatten under a shear wrote the unbaked base.** Cause: src/gltf.ts `bake` kept `geo.base`, which `primitive()`
  then wrote as the owner. Also a matrix node could carry a weights channel (glTF 2.0 3.5.3). Fixed in 95451cf56d.
  Regression: packages/exporters/tests/exporters.test.js.
- **weldVertices took an out-of-range index as vertex 0**, a 1 or 2 vertex triangle primitive got a 0-count index
  accessor, and texture dedupe renumbered only material references (glTF 2.0 3.7.2.1, 5.1, 5.11). Fixed in
  3f05edf826. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/optimize.test.js.
- **A skin listing one joint twice was accepted by usdz-anim** (glTF 5.22). Fixed in ca5977c07e. Regression:
  packages/exporters/tests/usdz-anim.test.js.
- **A base colour texture on TEXCOORD_2 or above mapped with TEXCOORD_0**, and `attributeBytes` counted too few
  bytes. Fixed in eeafa8f414. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/obj-held-textures.test.js,
  packages/exporters/tests/glb-limits.test.js.
- **The Roblox runtime verifier skipped the basename rules, and roblox-chunks compared a triangle with itself** with
  an absolute degeneracy bound. Fixed in ae234d1cfd. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/precision-bundles.test.js.
- **Unreal precision preflight passed a rotation verify always refused**, a hook without a newline broke the Python
  helper, and the verifiers did not check byteStride or the restart index (glTF 3.6.2.4, 3.7.2.1). Fixed in
  d827996456. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/precision-bundles.test.js,
  packages/exporters/tests/precision-native.test.js.
- **KTX2 padded before global data that does not exist**, and the BasisLZ coder did not check endpoint widths (KTX
  2.0 section 2, Appendix D.2). Fixed in 072d4ba2d4. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/basis-native.test.js.
- **Build and tool scripts**: no `--locked`, no Wasm validation, a timeout that killed only cargo, stale records, and
  no hard limit on the browser page run. Fixed in 855dbc0ee9. Regression:
  packages/exporters/tests/build-scripts.test.js.
- **Unity package**: declared `"unity": "6000.0"`, checked accessor alignment without the view offset, leaked a failed
  setup and missed plug-in payload types. Fixed in 88fb6f8f41. Regression:
  packages/exporters/tests/unity-support.test.js. The main-object names are the open entry above.
- **Unity and Unreal precision verifiers assumed quads.** Repro: a valid bundle with a one-triangle face failed
  "Complete indexed attribute inventory". Cause: `faces.length * 6` indices. Fixed in ee8eca97e0. Regression:
  packages/exporters/tests/precision-bundles.test.js.
- **The precision wide-index check was off by one and allowed restart values.** Repro: a 65,536-vertex bundle on
  32-bit indices was refused; 256 vertices on 8-bit indices with index 255 passed. Cause: `p.count > 65535 &&

- **One failed Draco encoder load failed every later call.** Cause: src/draco.ts cached the rejected promise. Fixed in

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Milky Way and aurora lost hundreds of float32 ULPs to cancellation, so the WebGL2 layer differed from WebGPU (sky)

- **Repro:** `node packages/sky/test/compat-gpu.mjs` on an RTX A6000 (Edge, ANGLE Direct3D11 for the layer): the
  frames without `MilkyWay` or `Aurora` match exactly; with them, 667 of 196,608 values of the star field and 673 of the
  aurora's differed, the largest by two half-float steps.
- **Cause:** found by writing the shaders' intermediate values as float bits to an rgba32uint target on both devices.
  The interpolated NDC is identical; the ray through it already differs by one rounding of the matrix product's terms
  (the two shader compilers fuse and order the multiply-adds differently, which both specs allow). Three formulas in
  Margo's shaders then amplified that: (1) the pixel's solid angle was the cross product of differences of the rays
  through the pixel's edges, two nearly equal unit vectors, so it came out 382 ULPs apart (3.7e-5) and 4.3e-5 off
  float64 on either device, and worse at a higher resolution; (2) the aurora's shell distances were
  -b + sqrt(b^2 - |c|^2 + r^2), which cancels when looking up (64 ULPs apart, 8.7e-6 off float64); (3) its height
  above the ground was |p + R up| - R, 5.8e-4 km off. Cancellation turns a relative error of the operands into a far
  larger one of the result (Goldberg, "What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic", ACM
  Computing Surveys 23(1), 1991, section 1.4, https://doi.org/10.1145/103162.103163; Higham, "Accuracy and Stability
  of Numerical Algorithms", 2nd ed., SIAM, 2002, section 1.7, https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9780898718027).
- **Fix:** `pixelSolidAngle` in packages/sky/src/night-backdrop.ts takes the solid angle from the Jacobian of the ray's
  direction, |q . (qx x qy)| / |q|^3 with the derivatives from the inverse matrix's columns (the area element of a
  parametrised surface, do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces", Prentice Hall, 1976, section 2-5),
  4.3e-5 to 5.7e-7 off float64; `shell` in packages/sky/src/aurora.ts writes the quadratic's constant term without
  the squares of R and takes each root in the form that adds same-signed terms (Haines, Guenther and Akenine-Moeller,
  "Precision Improvements for Ray/Sphere Intersection", Ray Tracing Gems, Apress, 2019, chapter 7,
  https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4842-4427-2_7), 8.7e-6 to 2.2e-7; `height` writes |p + R up| - R as
  (|p|^2 + 2R p.y) / (|p + R up| + R), 5.8e-4 to 6.6e-5 km (two ULPs at 450 km). The differing values fell to 25 and 38
  of the star field's and 153 of the aurora's (the aurora's thin curtains, 1.5 km at 300 km, magnify a ULP of the
  position by their own sharpness).
- **Accepted rest:** the ray keeps its one-rounding difference, which both specs allow, and any difference at all can
  reach two half-float steps in the capture; see docs/limits.md, "Sky layers on the WebGL2 layer". So the test keeps
  the two-step bound, now proven rather than measured.
- **Regression test:** packages/sky/test/compat-gpu.mjs with packages/sky/test/precision-check.html checks the
  solid angle (under 2e-6 of float64; 4.4e-5 before the fix fails it), the shell distances (under 1e-6) and the height
  (under 1.5e-4 km) on native WebGPU and on the layer, and a blend pair one float32 ULP apart.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: MToon UV animation steps after about a day of running (rigging/mtoon)

- **Repro:** attach `MToon` to a material with `uvAnimationScrollXSpeedFactor: 0.1` and run `onPreUpdate(1 / 60)` for
  86,400 s of scene time: the time written to the uniform (`values[23]`, and the caster uniform's `out[3]`) is float32,
  whose step at 86,400 is 1/128 s, so the scroll offset advances in steps of 1/128 s instead of 1/60 s and the texture
  judders; it gets worse with uptime.
- **Cause:** packages/rigging/src/mtoon.ts sends the growing `this.time` and the shader (`mtAnimate`) and the shadow
  caster (packages/shared/caster.js `animatedDepth`) compute speed x time x mask in float32. Wrapping time by a period
  is not exact: the specification scales the animation by the mask texture ("the value multiplies to UV animation
  speed"), so a fractional mask has no period, and the three speeds share one time. Found by the audit p4 review
  (R22), 2026-11-15.
- **Fix:** `uvAnimationPhases` in packages/rigging/src/mtoon-data.ts multiplies speed and time in float64 and sends
  per channel a phase and a whole count k (scroll in UV units with period 2, rotation in turns with period 1);
  `mtAnimate` and shared/caster.js `margoAnimatedUV` both form phase x m + period x fract(k x m) from the mask value m,
  so binary masks are exact, fractional ones are off only by the rounding of k x m, and shadow cut-outs match the
  colour pass. Scroll wraps on an axis only when `scrollWraps` finds every moved map sampling the same texel after a
  step of 2 (whole-number transform column, no clamp on an axis it reaches); otherwise that axis keeps the full
  scroll (docs/limits.md). Sources: VRMC_materials_mtoon 1.0 UV animation (VRM Consortium, 2022), KHR_texture_transform
  (Khronos, 2017), Goldberg 1991 (cited in docs/rigging-mtoon.md). Regression tests: packages/rigging/tests/mtoon.test.js
  "MToon UV animation keeps 1/60 s steps after a day of running (audit p4 R22)" (fails on the old uniform) and "MToon UV
  animation phases wrap scroll by 2 only where every map samples the same texel"; the test:mtoon:browser uv-animation
  and uv-shadow suites pass on WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a repeated point in a line strip replaces its join with two caps (lines)

- **Repro:** `expandLine([0, 0, 0, 100, 0, 100, -100, 100], { join: 'miter', cap: 'butt', width: 10, antialias: false })`
  (up, then the corner point given twice, then left) leaves the miter corner at (3, 103) and the bevel point
  (1.5, 101.5) uncovered, while the same path without the repeat covers both; with `cap: 'round'` a miter or bevel
  join comes out round. The GPU expansion in packages/lines/src/shader.ts does the same: any `Line` whose points
  repeat (GPS tracks, data with stops, a loop closed by repeating its first point) or two points that fall on one
  pixel draws a notch or the wrong join shape there.
- **Cause:** each segment instance reads only the point before its start and the point after its end
  (`segmentIndices` in packages/lines/src/geometry.ts, `ip` and `inx` in the vertex shader). A neighbour that
  coincides on screen gives a zero-length direction, so `hasPrev` or `hasNext` turns false and that end draws a
  cap; the zero-length segment itself draws joins toward an arbitrary +x direction. A join across the repeat needs
  the nearest distinct point, which the instance cannot see. Found by the batch 132 second pass, 2026-11-15.
- **Fix:** `distinctNeighbours` in packages/lines/src/geometry.ts gives each point the index of its nearest distinct
  point on either side (one CPU pass, exact equality, wrapping for loops); `Lines` uploads them after the points
  (8 bytes a point) when the points or the mode change, the vertex shader reads them through `near()` for `ip` and
  `inx`, and a segment between two copies of one point draws nothing unless the whole line is one point (its caps
  then draw the dot SVG 2 gives a zero-length subpath). `expandLine` does the same. Sources: WHATWG, HTML Living
  Standard, "trace a path" (2026, https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#trace-a-path: zero-length
  segments are pruned before joins); W3C, Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) 2, painting, stroke-linecap on zero-length
  subpaths (2018, https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/painting.html#LineCaps). Regression tests:
  packages/lines/tests/lines.test.js "a repeated point in a strip joins across it instead of drawing two caps" and
  "distinctNeighbours skips repeats and wraps loops", and packages/lines/tests/lines-browser.js "A repeated point in
  a strip joins across it, pixel for pixel" (fails on the old shader with 42 to 82 pixels changed per join and cap).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: savePrefilteredEnvironment could save a file that mixed two lighting states (KB-A3d, environment)

- **What:** `savePrefilteredEnvironment` (`packages/environment/src/prefiltered.ts`) read the cube and specular mips
  one awaited readback at a time and checked only `environment.version` at the end. `EnvironmentBlend.update` and
  `Environment.refresh` rewrite an environment in place without bumping `version`, so a save that spanned either one
  wrote a header and SH from one state and later mips from the other, and resolved as if it had succeeded.
- **Repro (before the fix):** in `packages/environment/tests/blend-browser.js` section 1, start
  `savePrefilteredEnvironment(blend.environment)` and set `blend.t = 0.6` before it resolves: the loaded file's cube
  mip 1 held 1.113 where t 0.25 gives 1.864 (RTX A6000, WebGPU, 2026-11-15).
- **Cause:** the save's reads spanned many tasks while the lighting could change in place between them.
- **Fix:** the save takes one snapshot: rotation, intensity, radianceScale and the CPU SH are copied, and every mip
  and LUT copy is recorded into one command buffer and submitted, all before the first await. GPU work runs in
  submission order (WebGPU, "Queues"), so the copies see the textures as every earlier submit left them and nothing
  queued later; `EnvironmentBlend.update` changes its SH, scale and texels inside one task, so it lands wholly before
  or wholly after. A refresh is different: it writes texels first and its SH only after an awaited readback, so no
  instant of it is whole. The new `Environment.refreshPending` is true from `refresh()` until it settles, and a save
  then rejects with MargoError `state`. The proposed alternative, a public `revision` checked after the awaits, would
  reject every save of a blend animated each frame; the snapshot cannot be torn and needs no counter. The same idea
  as HTML's `toBlob`, which encodes the canvas as it was when called.
- **Test:** `packages/environment/tests/blend-browser.js` section 1 (save, then `blend.t = 0.6`: the file equals t
  0.25 in every mip and its SH; fails on the old code at cube mip 1) and `tests/prefiltered-browser.js` (a save
  while a GPU-cube refresh runs rejects with code 'state'; after it settles the file holds the refreshed lighting),
  native and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.
- **Sources:** W3C GPU for the Web WG, "WebGPU" (2026), queue timeline and `GPUQueue.submit`,
  https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#queues; WHATWG, "HTML Living Standard" (2026), `HTMLCanvasElement.toBlob`,
  https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-canvas-toblob.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a hole, dissolve or bridge loop of over 125,000 border vertices overflowed the call stack (mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** a flat fan of 130,000 triangles: `fillMeshHoles` on its rim, `dissolveMeshComponents` of every face, or
  `bridgeMeshEdgeLoops` with the rim as a loop threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Dissolving a fan
  of 5,000 triangles reported "folds over itself".
- **Cause:** `planarUV` in `holes.ts` and the loop walks of `dissolve.ts`, `bridge.ts`, `bevel-edges.ts` and
  `exact-kernel.ts` spread one value per border vertex into `Math.min` or `Math.max`, and V8 overflows its call
  stack past about 125,000 arguments. Separately, a dissolved region whose border has more than the 4096 corners the
  convex splitter takes fell through to the fold error. Filling also checked each new neighbour with
  `rings[v].includes(w)`, so the fan's center (valence 130,000) cost its valence squared (9.7 s before the overflow).
- **Fix:** every min and max in the package is a loop (`leastOf`, `greatestOf`, `indexOfLeast` in `least.ts`);
  dissolve names the 4096-corner border limit with `MargoError` `unsupported`; filling keeps a set of joined pairs.
  Regression: `packages/mesh-edit/tests/large-boundary.test.js`, whose last test fails on any `Math.min(...` or
  `Math.max(...` left in the package source.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a long grab with dynamic topology left stretched triangles (mesh-edit sculpt)

- **Repro:** a 4 times subdivided plane, `dynamicTopology: true`, `detailSize: 0.1`, radius 0.3, a `grab` dragged 2.0
  along the normal in 20 dabs: 156 edges over 4/3 of the detail, the longest 0.85.
- **Cause:** `endStroke` remeshed a grab only within 1.25 radii of where it started, with at most four split passes,
  so the dragged part of a pull longer than about two radii was never remeshed.
- **Fix:** the end of a grab remeshes the held vertices wherever they went and the vertices its splits add, splitting
  longest edge first until none there is long (Rivara, 1984). Regression: `packages/mesh-edit/tests/sculpt.test.js`
  "dynamic topology leaves no stretched edge after a grab many radii long".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a boolean gave a's faces fresh IDs when b used the same IDs (mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** `booleanMeshesExact(a, b, 'difference')` with two `createPrimitiveMesh('cube', 'box')` cubes, b scaled and
  offset: five of a's surviving faces lose their `box-face-n` IDs to b's pieces.
- **Cause:** `finishBoolean` named loops in the order they came out of the trees, so a b piece could claim a shared ID
  first, against the documented "b's only when a does not use it".
- **Fix:** IDs are claimed for a's loops, then b's, before any face is named. Regression:
  `packages/mesh-edit/tests/boolean-exact.test.js` "a keeps its face IDs when b uses the same ones".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the array, screw and exact boolean threw on large meshes (mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** the array modifier on a 130,321-vertex grid, the screw on a 58,081-vertex grid, or `booleanMeshesExact` on
  an input with a 131,000-vertex shell beside another shell: `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`.
- **Cause:** each spread every coordinate into one `Math.max` or `Math.min` call (`modifiers.ts` array bounds and screw
  extent, `exact-kernel.ts` `boundsMeet`).
- **Fix:** loops. Regression: `packages/mesh-edit/tests/modifiers.test.js` "array and screw take meshes too large to
  spread into Math.max", `boolean-exact.test.js` "an input with a shell of over 125,000 vertices".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the array modifier's merge collapsed close vertices inside one copy (mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** two quads with a 0.004 slot between them, `{type: 'array', count: 2, merge: 0.01}`: the slot closes in
  both copies (10 vertices where 14 are right).
- **Cause:** the merge welded every pair of vertices within the distance; the documented merge joins neighboring
  copies only.
- **Fix:** the weld takes an internal pair filter and the array allows only pairs one copy apart. Regression:
  `packages/mesh-edit/tests/modifiers.test.js` "array merge joins neighboring copies only".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: an unwrap pin with one uv number was reported as outside the unit square (mesh-edit)

- **Repro:** `unwrapMesh(cube, {pins: [{vertex: 0, uv: [0.5]}, {vertex: 1, uv: [0.9, 0.9]}]})` threw RangeError "pins
  put a chart outside the unit square".
- **Cause:** pin validation checked every entry but not that there are two, so the missing v became NaN in the solve.
- **Fix:** a pin uv must be a pair, else the documented TypeError. Regression:
  `packages/mesh-edit/tests/unwrap-pins.test.js` "a pin uv that is not exactly two numbers".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the Blender add-on read the editing UV map and wrote spot and range values glTF refuses (KB-P15a to KB-P15c, blender)

- **Repro:** `tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_uv_lights.py` in Blender 5.3 (`npm run modern:test:blender` with
  `MARGO_BLENDER`). (a) A mesh with two UV maps whose render map (camera icon) is not the one selected for editing:
  the export placed every texture by the editing map, and Cycles baked node materials onto that map too. (b) A spot
  light with Spot Blend 0 (Blender's range is 0 to 1): the file held `margo:inner_cone` equal to `margo:outer_cone`, and
  `@margoengine/blender/components` refused it. (c) A light with Custom Distance on at 0 (Blender's minimum): the file
  held `margo:range` 0, which the components entry refuses too.
- **Cause:** (a) `exporter.py` took `TEXCOORD_0` and its tangents from `mesh.uv_layers.active`, and `bake.py` let
  Cycles bake on its default map, also the active one; Blender renders with the map marked `active_render` (a probe
  render in Blender 5.3 of a two-map plane shows the render map's texel). `TEXCOORD_1` was always `uv_layers[1]`, the
  same map as `TEXCOORD_0` when that was the second one. (b) the inner cone was outer times (1 - blend), equal to outer at
  blend 0, while KHR_lights_punctual needs inner below outer. (c) Custom Distance was copied without the range rule
  (range above 0).
- **Fix:** `bake.render_uv` (the render map) is `TEXCOORD_0`, the tangent map, the bake's `uv_layer` and the map a live
  UV Map node must name; `bake.second_uv` (the first other map) is `TEXCOORD_1` and the lightmap bake's target. The
  inner cone is at most 0.999 of the outer (the FBX importer's rule), so a hard edge keeps glTF's narrowest blend. A
  Custom Distance of 0 fails by the light's name. Regression: `tools/blender-addon/tests/blender_uv_lights.py` (each
  part fails on the code before). The add-on's pure-Python tests (`test_format.py`, `test_live.py`, `test_package.py`)
  ran only in the GitHub workflow, which is off; `packages/blender/tests/addon-python.test.js` now runs them with the
  package tests.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: stop() or dispose() inside engine.pace left a frame waiting, so start() ran two loops (KB-STRESS-3, core, B6 class)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_STRESS_SEED=182 node --test tests/deep-core-stress.test.js` (family reentrant-loop): `pace` calls
  `stop()` and returns false, then the app calls `start()`.
- **What:** a frame stayed scheduled after the stop; `start()` scheduled another beside it, so two frame loops ran and
  every display refresh drew twice. `dispose()` inside `pace` left a frame waiting for a disposed engine.
- **Cause:** the pace branch of `frame()` in `packages/core/src/engine.ts` rescheduled without testing `running`; the
  frame's tail did test it. B6 (1a8ad9370e) fixed `stop()` plus `start()` there, not `stop()` alone.
- **Fix:** one reschedule at the end of the frame for a drawn and a skipped frame alike, behind `if (this.running)`.
  Core 22,188 to 22,176 B gzip. Regression: `packages/core/tests/pace-stop.test.js` (both tests fail before).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: dispose() inside a plugin's onPreUpdate reported "Transforms disposed" (KB-STRESS-2, core)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_STRESS_SEED=2654435943 node --test tests/deep-core-stress.test.js` (family reentrant-loop), also
  `MARGO_STRESS_SEED=1462 node --test packages/stage/tests/stress.test.js`.
- **What:** a plugin that disposes the engine in `onPreUpdate` got `onError(MargoError disposed: Transforms disposed)`
  from the same frame and the loop stopped; `render()` threw it to a direct caller. With views the next view threw
  "Engine disposed", and a `fallback` renderer that does not ignore draws after its dispose was drawn through.
- **Cause:** `update()` in `packages/core/src/engine.ts` ran on into the resize, the camera and the kernel tick on the
  freed store after the plugins' `onPreUpdate` loop, and `renderViews` went on to the next view.
- **Fix:** `update()` returns after the `onPreUpdate` loop when the engine is disposed, `render()` does not draw then,
  and `renderViews` stops at that view. An error the plugin itself throws is still reported. Core 22,176 to 22,190 B
  gzip. Regression: `packages/core/tests/pre-update-dispose.test.js` (three of its four tests fail before).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: dispose() did not stop an automatic device restore in flight (KB-STRESS-1, core)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_STRESS_SEED=3668340200 node --test tests/deep-core-stress.test.js` (family dispose-during-async):
  the device is lost, the restore waits at one of its startup steps, the engine is disposed, the step settles.
- **What:** the restore carried on after dispose: it asked for a device, compiled both pipelines and built a renderer
  (`createBuffer`, `createBindGroup`, `addEventListener`) on the new device, and only then destroyed it.
- **Cause:** `rebootDevice` in `packages/core/src/engine.ts` passed no `signal` to `GPURenderer.create`, and `dispose()`
  had no way to stop it; the disposed test ran only after the renderer was built.
- **Fix:** the engine keeps one AbortController whose signal every restore passes as its startup signal; `dispose()`
  aborts it with `MargoError` code `disposed` (a caller's `rebootDevice()` rejects with it) and the automatic restore
  reports nothing once disposed; a dispose after the last startup step rejects the same way. Core 22,190 to 22,220 B
  gzip, after nine more private members were compacted first (22,218 to 22,188 B); no limit raised. Regression:
  `packages/core/tests/restore-dispose.test.js` (two of its three tests fail before) and the dispose case of
  `tests/deep-core-allocation-failure.test.js`, which now expects the `disposed` rejection.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a device lost during startup or during a restore was never restored (B3, core)

- **Repro:** a device that `requestDevice` returns already lost, or one lost at any later startup step (the pipeline
  compiles, `getContext`, `configure`), at `Engine.create` or inside an automatic restore. `node --test
  tests/deep-core-stress.test.js` family startup-loss (seeds 179 to 190) and stage seeds 1460 to 1464 in
  `packages/stage/tests/stress.test.js` find it.
- **What:** nothing restored the device and nothing was reported; every later frame drew nothing. A device lost while
  the restore that brought it in was still ending (in a plugin's `onDeviceRestored`) was dropped the same way.
- **Cause:** `GPURenderer` in `packages/core/src/renderer.ts` called its `onLost` hook from a `device.lost`
  reaction made in its constructor. A device lost by then resolved that reaction before `Engine` (in `Engine.create`,
  or `rebootDevice` before `watchDevice`) had set the hook, so the loss went nowhere. A loss reported while
  `rebootDevice` was still in flight got that same restore back, which had already swapped in the lost device.
- **Fix:** setting `onLost` attaches its own `device.lost` reaction, so a device lost before the hook was set still
  calls it; the engine's handler, met while a restore is still in flight, waits for that restore and then restores
  the device it watches if that device is still the current one. Core 22,174 to 22,218 B gzip. Regression:
  `packages/core/tests/startup-loss.test.js` (all three fail before: one device is asked for, or two, where a lost
  device needs another).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a pass's InvalidStateError or OperationError was taken as a device loss (B2, core)

- **Repro:** a frame-graph pass, a plugin's `onPreUpdate` or an `onFrame` callback throws
  `new DOMException(..., 'OperationError')` (or 'InvalidStateError') on a healthy device, as a buffer mapped twice or a
  canvas not configured does. `MARGO_STRESS_SEED=2654435939 node --test tests/deep-core-stress.test.js` (family
  errors-in-passes) finds it.
- **What:** the error was never reported; the renderer marked its healthy device lost, so no later frame drew, and the
  engine asked for a new device.
- **Cause:** `GPURenderer.render` in `packages/core/src/renderer.ts` caught every DOMException with either name as a
  loss (since the first commit). WebGPU never signals a loss that way: a lost device makes its calls no-ops and resolves
  `device.lost`, and the WebGL2 layer throws these names only for wrong calls.
- **Fix:** the catch is gone: such an error fails its frame and is reported once like any other, and the next frame
  draws on the same device; a real loss still restores through `device.lost`. Core 22,219 to 22,174 B gzip.
  Regression: `packages/core/tests/pass-error-not-loss.test.js` (fails before: the render does not throw, and a second
  device is asked for).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: points readers looped, misread colours and trusted counts in COPC, LAZ, Potree and E57 files (points)

- **Repro:** (1) A COPC hierarchy entry with count -1 naming its own page made `CopcSource.open` fetch without end.
  (2) A COPC child with 16-bit RGB values below 256 decoded as bright 8-bit colours. (3) `decodeLazChunk(chunk, 2 ** 50,
  ...)` on a layered chunk failed with "Invalid typed array length" instead of naming the bad count; -1 was taken.
  (4) A Potree 2.0 hierarchy chunk whose first record is a proxy looped an eager open. (5) An E57 file with
  `colorGreenMaximum` 127 read green with the red range and wrapped 255 past it; a ScaledInteger without limits read
  as a constant; a scan name holding `]]>` broke the XML; an unclosed comment or declaration was not reported.
- **Cause:** packages/points/src/copc.ts kept no set of read pages and chose the colour depth per node; laz.ts
  allocated from the table count before reading the chunk's own; potree.ts did not check the first record type;
  e57.ts used one colour range, gave ScaledInteger no 64-bit default, wrote CDATA unescaped and let indexOf's -1 move
  the parser back.
- **Fix:** repeated pages throw, the depth is chosen once, counts are checked before allocating, a leading proxy
  throws, per-channel limits with clamping, 64-bit defaults, `]]>` split across CDATA sections, named errors.
  Regression: packages/points/tests/audit-132.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: buildOctree, PointCloud and the CPU pick took bad input or picked hidden points (points)

- **Repro:** `buildOctree({positions, colors: [0.5, ...]})` stored the colours as bytes 0; `maxDepth: NaN` or -1 was
  taken; `new PointCloud({positions: 6 values, normals: 3 values})` was taken; `classificationColors([21])` gave the
  grey of an unknown class; with `setMask(mask, {mode: 'filter'})` the CPU `pick` still returned a hidden point.
- **Cause:** packages/points/src/octree.ts kept any colour array as bytes and never checked maxDepth; cloud.ts did not
  compare the normals length; attributes.ts stopped at class 18 of LAS 1.4 R15 table 17; math.ts `pickPoint` had no
  way to skip points and plugin.ts did not pass the mask.
- **Fix:** floats stay Float32Array, maxDepth must be 0 to 64, normals must match positions, classes 19 to 22 named and
  coloured, `pickPoint` takes an optional `hidden` test the plugin fills for 'filter'. Regression:
  packages/points/tests/audit-132.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: netcode's transports broke RFC 6455 close rules and left channels and sessions open (netcode)

- **Repro:** (1) A client close frame with code 999, 1004, 1005, 1006, 1015, 2000 or 5000, a one-byte body or a reason
  that is not UTF-8 was echoed and reported as given; `connection.close(1004)` put 1004 on the wire; a request with
  `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 8` got 400 with no `Sec-WebSocket-Version`. (2) Over WebRTC, the far end closing only the
  unreliable channel left the reliable one open. (3) `openWebTransport` or `acceptWebTransport` on a session with no
  datagram writer rejected and left the session open; the reliable stream ending left the connection `open`.
- **Cause:** packages/netcode/src/node.ts checked neither the received code (RFC 6455 7.4) nor the reason (8.1) and
  folded the version check into the 400 answer (4.4); webrtc.ts finished the connection on a channel close without
  closing the other channel; webtransport.ts closed the session only when the abort signal fired, and returned from
  the stream reader without closing.
- **Fix:** bad close frames fail with 1002 or 1007, codes no endpoint may send go as 1000, another version gets 426
  naming 13; either data channel closing closes both; every failed open closes its session, and a stream that ends
  closes the connection one task later, so a peer's own close code still wins. Regressions:
  packages/netcode/tests/transports.test.js "the WebSocket server checks a received close frame" and "either channel
  closing closes both", packages/netcode/tests/webtransport.test.js (three cases).
