### Fixed 2026-11-15: netcode rooms, relay and signalling mishandled closes during hooks, aborts and junk bytes (netcode)

- **Repro:** (1) A `Room` with an async `onJoin`: the client leaves while it runs; `onLeave` ran first and `onJoin`
  then added the player for good. (2) A `RoomsClient` join whose signal aborted while `connect()` ran still joined.
  (3) Two rooms drawing the same random id: the second replaced the first in the server's map. (4) Junk bytes from the
  relay, or a FRAME before WELCOME, threw out of `relayPeers` and `RollbackSpectator` into the transport callback; a
  hello after `RollbackRelay.close()` was seated. (5) A `SignalServer` `authorize` that throws or rejects was an
  unhandled rejection; junk JSON from the server threw out of `SignalClient`. (6) `openSqlitePresence` with a
  namespace holding a character outside the BMP found no keys.
- **Cause:** rooms.ts dropped a client without waiting for its running join hook, added the abort listener after the
  signal had already fired, and never checked a new id; relay.ts and signal.ts decoded without catching and greeted
  without checking `closed`; signal.ts ran `join` detached with no catch; presence.ts passed the UTF-16 length to
  SQLite substr(), which counts characters.
- **Fix:** a drop waits for the running hook (a hook that returns at once stays synchronous); an abort during connect
  closes the connection and rejects; ids are redrawn until unique; decoding errors close with `CloseCode.protocol`; a
  closed relay refuses; a failing authorize refuses the peer; the prefix length is counted in code points.
  Regressions: packages/netcode/tests/rooms.test.js (three cases), relay.test.js (two), signal.test.js (two) and
  presence.test.js "SQLite adapter finds keys under a namespace with characters outside the BMP".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: netcode migration stalled, interest hung far out and generated TypeScript failed to compile (netcode)

- **Repro:** (1) `HostMigration` with A as host: `a.handoff(3)`, peer 3 leaves, and the A to B link is slower than
  3 to B; recovery never finished and timed out. (2) `InterestManager` with `cell: 1` and an entity at x = 2^54:
  `view()` never returned. (3) `generateTypeScript` for a schema with a struct named Map (or Writer, Reader,
  Uint8Array, DataView, RangeError) wrote a module that does not type-check.
- **Cause:** migrate.ts took a host's STATUS only one epoch ahead, while a host whose handoff target left is two ahead
  of a follower that dropped the TRANSFER; interest.ts stepped float cell indices, and past 2^53 `x++` does not move;
  generate.ts named its runtime classes Writer and Reader and used Map and Uint8Array as types, which an exported
  interface of the same name shadows.
- **Fix:** a host's STATUS of any later epoch starts recovery at it; cell indices are clamped to +-2^30, which keeps
  every in-radius entity in a scanned cell; the generated runtime is Wire_Writer and Wire_Reader (no struct can be
  named with an underscore) and globals in type positions go through globalThis. Structs X and XDelta, whose
  generated functions would clash, are refused with a TypeError. Regressions: packages/netcode/tests/migrate.test.js
  "a follower that hears the handoff target leave before the transfer still joins the recovery", interest.test.js
  "a viewer far from the origin, past 2^53 grid cells", generate.test.js (two cases).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: voxel-net's WebSocket broke RFC 6455 close and version rules (voxel-net)

- **Repro:** (1) `conn.close(4000, 'é'.repeat(100))` sent a close frame with a 202-byte payload; a control frame holds
  at most 125. (2) A peer's close frame with code 1005, 1006, 999, 1004, 1016 or 2999, or a reason that is not UTF-8,
  was taken and reported as given. (3) A request with `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 8` got 400 with no
  `Sec-WebSocket-Version` header.
- **Cause:** packages/voxel-net/src/websocket.ts cut the reason at 120 UTF-16 units instead of 123 bytes, checked
  neither the received code (RFC 6455 7.4) nor the reason's UTF-8 (section 8.1), and folded the version check into
  the 400 answer (section 4.4 asks for 426 naming the versions the server speaks).
- **Fix:** the reason is cut to 123 bytes on a whole character; a code a peer may not send fails the connection with
  1002 and a reason that is not UTF-8 with 1007; another version gets 426 with `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`.
  Regressions: packages/voxel-net/tests/websocket.test.js "a long non-ASCII close reason is cut to fit a 125-byte
  control frame on a whole character", "a close frame with ... fails the connection with ..." (7 cases) and "a request
  for another WebSocket version gets 426 naming version 13" (all fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: voxel-net over WebTransport reported a server's close as the client's and leaked sessions (voxel-net)

- **Repro:** (1) `joinOver(connection, world)`, then the server closes the session with 1001: `client.onClose` got
  `byClient: true`. (2) `connectVoxelNetWebTransport(url, world, { inputCopies: 99 })` rejected with a RangeError and
  left the session it opened open. (3) `acceptVoxelNetWebTransport` on a server not started rejected and left the
  accepted session open.
- **Cause:** packages/voxel-net/src/webtransport.ts read `byClient` after `client.close()`, which ends through
  joinOver's own close and set it; connect and accept did not close the connection when joining or `server.accept`
  threw (the WebRTC path already did).
- **Fix:** `byClient` is read before the client is closed; connect and accept close the connection and rethrow.
  Regressions: packages/voxel-net/tests/webtransport-close.test.js (3 tests, all fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: cinematic stepped a camera twice a frame and moved a below-target look with shake

- **Repro:** (1) a `CameraBrain` switching a, b, a, b inside long blends, then `a.enabled = false`: each update ran
  a's stages twice, so its springs and noise moved at double speed. (2) `new Cinematic({offset: [0, -1, 4], ground:
  () => -100})` with `shake(1, 1)`: `engine.camera.target` rose and fell with the shake although no ground was near.
- **Cause:** (1) packages/cinematic/src/brain.ts updated a disabled camera once per blend layer that showed it, and a
  switch back and forth puts one camera in two layers. (2) packages/cinematic/src/index.ts raised the look by the
  camera's whole height above its requested arm whenever `ground` was set, which includes shake and spring lag.
- **Fix:** (1) each camera of the blend stack steps once a frame; (2) the raise is capped at what the ground lifted
  (the arm goal plus the camera lift). Regressions: packages/cinematic/test/brain.test.js "a disabled camera shown by
  two layers of one blend steps once per update" and packages/cinematic/test/cinematic.test.js "a below-target orbit
  with ground out of reach keeps its look-at point through a shake" (both fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: toon model outlines drew one view's hulls with another view's rows

- **Repro:** two views in one frame on different render layers (`setRenderLayers`), the first seeing two outlined
  models and the second one of them: the first view drew the hidden-from-the-second model's hull with the other
  model's matrix, colour and width.
- **Cause:** packages/toon/src/models.ts wrote every view's draw rows at offset 0 of one storage buffer;
  `queue.writeBuffer` lands before any recorded command runs, so the last view's rows were what every view read.
- **Fix:** each view of a frame writes its rows after the earlier views' rows (`currentFrame` of shared/frame-resources)
  and draws from that base. Regression: packages/toon/test/models.test.js "each view of a frame keeps its own draw
  rows" (fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the transitions GLSL importer rejected or miscompiled valid GLSL ES 1.00

- **Repro:** `translateGLSLTransition` on `int a=0x1F;`, `float ratio=ratio*2.0;`, `precision mediump float;` inside a
  function, `const int N=2; float w[N*2];` in a function, `m=-m;`, `m*=2.0;`, `v*=m;`, `m++;`, `float(uv)`,
  `(f(),x)` with a void `f`: a parse error or WGSL the checker rejects; `c ? x : y = 2.0;` dropped the store to y.
- **Cause:** packages/transitions/src/glsl-parser.ts lexed decimal literals only, folded array sizes over globals only,
  had no precision statement in function scope and parsed the conditional's last operand above assignment level;
  glsl-emit.ts defined a name before its initializer, used WGSL compound forms that do not exist for matrix shapes,
  negated matrices with unary minus, treated scalar constructors of vectors as conversions and bound void calls.
- **Fix:** each lowered per GLSL ES 1.00 (sections 4.1.3, 4.1.9, 4.2.2, 4.5.3, 5.4.1, 5.8 to 5.11); inverse now
  rejects at translation, as WGSL has no builtin. Regression: packages/transitions/test/glsl-audit.test.js (8 tests,
  each fails on the old source); docs/limits.md "Batch 218 GLSL transition import".

### Fixed 2026-11-15: assembled WFC tiles lost rotation precision near pitch 90 degrees (wfc)

- **Repro:** a tile model node set with `setQuaternion` to Rx(x) Ry(p) Rz(z), p a little short of 90 degrees, then
  `assembleWFC`: the placed copy's quaternion differed from the source by up to 1.4e-6 per lane.
- **Cause:** packages/wfc/src/assemble.ts copied `node.rotation` (the store's Float32 Euler lanes) with
  `setRotation`; going from the quaternion to Euler and back is ill-conditioned near the pole.
- **Fix:** the copy takes the node's stored quaternion with `setQuaternion` (3e-8 worst). Regression test:
  packages/wfc/test/assemble.test.js "assembly copies each node quaternion, not its Float32 Euler lanes, ..."
  (fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: disposing a GPUMemory unhooked any tracker attached to the device after it (stats)

- **Repro:** `const a = GPUMemory.attach(device), b = GPUMemory.attach(device); a.dispose();` then create a buffer:
  `b.bytes` stays 0. `StatsPanels` attaches its own `GPUMemory`, so disposing the panels (or a device restore,
  which rebinds them) stopped a user's own tracker the same way.
- **Cause:** packages/stats/src/report.ts `GPUMemory` wrote the device's original `createBuffer` and
  `createTexture` back on dispose whether or not its wrappers were still the outermost ones; phases.ts and
  compile.ts already guard this.
- **Fix:** dispose restores the device only while its wrappers are outermost; otherwise its wrapper stays below the
  later one and passes calls through without counting. Regression test: packages/stats/test/report.test.js
  "disposing a GPUMemory leaves a tracker attached after it counting" (fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: VRM 1.0 firstPerson has no runtime (rigging/vrm)

- **Repro:** read a VRM 1.0 avatar with `firstPerson.meshAnnotations` (for example `thirdPersonOnly` on the head mesh)
  and render it from an XR or first-person camera: the head and hair still draw in front of the eyes. `readVRM` and
  `convertVRM0` keep the annotations as data only; nothing hides a mesh per camera.
- **Cause:** VRMC_vrm 1.0 firstPerson.md asks for per-camera visibility (`thirdPersonOnly` hidden from the first-person
  camera, `firstPersonOnly` shown only to it, `both`) and an `auto` split of each unannotated mesh into the triangles
  with weight on the head or its children (third person only) and the rest (both). No rigging entry applied the
  annotations, nothing split `auto` meshes, and XR eyes had no layer mask. Logged by the audit p4 review (R27).
- **Fix:** the new entry `@margoengine/rigging/vrm-first-person`: `splitVRMFirstPerson` / `loadVRM` split each `auto`
  mesh by its skin weights before the file loads, and `addVRMFirstPerson` puts the annotated nodes on render layers
  (shared/layers.js `FIRST_PERSON_ONLY_LAYER` 29, `THIRD_PERSON_ONLY_LAYER` 30) and returns the view masks. The
  `separate` and `engine` XR routes gained `xr.layers`, so both eyes filter too. No core change. Regression tests:
  packages/rigging/tests/vrm-first-person.test.js (the Twist sample split, built files, masks and dispose),
  packages/rigging/tests/vrm-first-person.browser.mjs (Seed-san and the Twist sample, native and WebGL2: the masked
  view equals the render with the head hidden, pixel for pixel), packages/xr/tests/xr.test.js "xr.layers filters what
  both eyes of the 'separate' route draw" and packages/xr/tests/view-layers.browser.mjs (both routes, both backends).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: four Crate value types read wrong (usdz)

- **Repro:** a text layer with `int64 i64 = -5`, `half2 v2h = (1, 2)` and `asset[] aa = [@a.png@, @b.png@]`, exported
  to `.usdc` by OpenUSD 26.11 and composed: -5 came back as 4294967291, (1, 2) as [0, 60] and the assets as `;-)` and
  `A`.
- **Cause:** packages/usdz/src/crate.ts returned an inlined int64 or uint64 as its raw 48-bit payload instead of its
  low 32 bits with the sign of its type, read an inlined half2 (which fits in 32 bits as it is) as one int8 per
  component like the other vectors, and read the indices of an asset array as token indices where the file holds
  string-table indices.
- **Fix:** each read as OpenUSD writes it. Regression test: packages/usdz/tests/crate-types.test.js (48 value types,
  text and Crate, against tests/oracle/crate-types-truth.py; fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: list edits composed in another order than OpenUSD's (usdz)

- **Repro:** a weaker layer with `rel r = [</a>, </x>, </b>, </y>]` and a stronger one with
  `reorder rel r = [</b>, </a>]`: OpenUSD gives b, y, a, x; Margo gave b, x, a, y. An item both added and prepended
  was listed twice.
- **Cause:** `apply` in packages/usdz/src/stage.ts moved each listed item into another listed item's slot, where a
  reorder carries the unlisted items that follow each listed one, and dropped prepended and appended items before the
  add step instead of moving them after it.
- **Fix:** delete, add, prepend, append, then reorder, as pinned black-box on usd-core 26.11 over 1,900 random edits.
  It serves every list-edited field: references, payloads, inherits, specializes, variant sets, targets, connections
  and clip sets. Regression test: packages/usdz/tests/list-edit.test.js (300 stages from
  tests/oracle/list-edit-truth.py; 122 differed on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: text layers with -inf, byte escapes or relocates failed or read wrong (usdz)

- **Repro:** `float neg = -inf` or `relocates = { </A/B>: </A/C> }` failed the layer with a syntax error, and
  `string esc = "a\x41\101\a"` read as `ax41101a` where OpenUSD 26.11 reads `aAA` and a bell.
- **Cause:** packages/usdz/src/layer.ts read `-inf` only inside arrays, knew no `\x`, octal or `\a \b \f \v` escapes,
  and had no rule for the `{ <source>: <target> }` form of relocates.
- **Fix:** scalar `-inf`; escapes as TfEscapeString reads them, a run of byte escapes decoded as UTF-8; relocates read
  past and dropped, as the Crate reader already drops them (relocates stay unsupported, docs/limits.md). Regression
  test: packages/usdz/tests/layer-text.test.js (fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-19: the static USDA reader read strings as JSON (loaders, KB-USDA-S1)

- **Repro:** `readUSDA('#usda 1.0\ndef Xform "A" { string s = "a\x41" }')` from `@margoengine/loaders` failed with
  `invalid string escape` where OpenUSD reads `aA`; octal `\101` and `\a` failed the same way, a single-quoted string
  was `invalid token`, and `relocates = { <a>: <b> }` failed as `invalid token` instead of a named refusal.
- **Cause:** `string()` in packages/loaders/src/usdz.ts handed double-quoted tokens to `JSON.parse` and returned
  triple-quoted text as written; the tokenizer had no single-quoted form; relocates was missing from the refused list.
- **Fix:** strings in single, double and triple quotes decode escapes as TfEscapeString reads them (the full reader
  packages/usdz/src/layer.ts already did, entry above), a run of byte escapes decoded as UTF-8; `relocates` is refused
  with `LoaderError` code `unsupported`. Regression test: packages/loaders/tests/usda-strings.test.js (fails on the old
  source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: 0 minus an image read as the image (usdz/materialx)

- **Repro:** a Standard Surface whose `base_color` is `ND_subtract_color3` with `in1 = (0, 0, 0)` and `in2` an image:
  the glTF material took the image as its base colour texture.
- **Cause:** `Network.node` in packages/usdz/src/materialx.ts treated add and subtract alike, taking the image from
  either side when the other side was 0.
- **Fix:** subtract keeps the image only as its first input; 0 minus an image is listed as having no PBR form.
  Regression test: packages/usdz/tests/materialx.test.js "0 minus an image ..." (fails on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the audio listener handed Web Audio no right axis when looking along its up vector

- **Repro:** the camera straight above its target with up +Y, `listener.setPose(p, [0, -1, 0])`, or
  `listener.follow(mesh, [0, 1, 0])`: a source at +X sounded in the middle (equal-power, Chromium and WebKit: equal
  channels) instead of on the right.
- **Cause:** packages/audio/src/listener.ts `setPose` normalised forward and up separately and passed both through,
  and `followTarget` took the mesh's Y column as up whatever its forward axis; Web Audio's right = forward x up was
  then zero.
- **Fix:** up keeps only its part across forward (Gram-Schmidt); an up along forward becomes the up of that view
  pitched from level ([0, 0, -1] looking down, [0, 0, 1] looking up), in the mesh's axes for `follow`, which also takes
  a local `up`. Regression tests: packages/audio/tests/audio.test.js "the listener hands Web Audio an up at right
  angles to forward", the top-view check of tests/audio-browser.js, and tests/ambisonics.test.js (a manual pose looking
  down now decodes as the top view).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: every Firefox suite exited 3 on macOS ("Could not find profile folder.")

- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox npm run test:browser --workspace @margoengine/audio` from the desktop app's agents
  on macOS: "cannot start firefox", exit 3, before any check.
- **Cause:** Firefox's profile service creates `~/Library/Application Support/Firefox` even when `-profile` names the
  profile, and macOS refuses that folder (EPERM) to a process without access to other apps' data; Firefox then exits
  1. Not an audio defect: scripts/lib/browser.mjs started every Firefox that way.
- **Fix:** on macOS `launchBrowser` gives Firefox `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` set to a folder of its own under the temporary
  folder (`firefoxHome`), so CoreFoundation resolves the home there. Regression test: tests/browser-selection.test.js
  "Firefox on macOS starts with a private home". The audio suite then reached its own Firefox gaps, now named by the
  runner (docs/limits.md, "Audio browser checks in Firefox") and the two open entries below.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Firefox rounds loop points and start times to whole frames, so AudioMusic drifted off its beat grid

- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox npm run test:browser --workspace @margoengine/audio` (Playwright Firefox 157,
  macOS) failed `measureLoopGrid` with "8000: loop 9 marker drifted off the grid". A plain page shows the browser
  behaviour: a buffer whose sample i holds i, looped with `loopEnd = 10.25 / sampleRate` in an 8 kHz
  OfflineAudioContext, plays 0..9, 0..9, ... in Firefox (the loop is 10 frames) and 0..10, 0.75, 1.75, ... in
  Chromium (10.25 frames, read between samples); `start(3.5 / sampleRate)` begins at frame 4 in Firefox and at 3.5
  in Chromium.
- **Cause:** the Web Audio API's "Playback of AudioBuffer Contents" algorithm keeps `actualLoopEnd` and the start
  time in fractional frames; Firefox truncates the loop end to a whole frame. `AudioMusic.start`
  (packages/audio/src/music.ts) looped every stem on one source with `loopEnd` set to the loop length in seconds, a
  fraction of a frame for most tempos (130 bpm, 4 beats at 8 kHz: 14,769.23 frames), so in Firefox each loop ended
  0.23 frames early and the stems drifted together off the grid that `transition()` quantises to: about 15 ms after
  an hour at 48 kHz and 130 bpm.
- **Fix:** each loop of each stem is its own one-shot source, `start(origin + k * loop, 0, loop)`, anchored on the
  audio clock, so a rounding browser is off by under a frame at every loop and never accumulates. Loops are
  scheduled ahead: an OfflineAudioContext's whole render at `start`, otherwise max(1 s, 2 loops) past
  `currentTime + leadTime`, refilled on every listener frame and on every loop's `ended` event (hidden tabs keep
  time); a loop whose start passed during a main-thread stall starts now at its matching offset. Firefox 157 now
  runs the audio browser suite to the end: loop grid max phase error 0.96 frames over an hour at 8 kHz and five
  minutes at 44.1 and 48 kHz (Chromium 0.5), and the pan, binaural, voice, sprite and gesture checks pass.
  Regression tests: packages/audio/tests/music.test.js "every loop is its own source anchored at origin + k *
  loop" and "a loop whose start passed during a stall", plus the browser `measureLoopGrid`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the WebGL2 layer refused Firefox on macOS, which reports 24-bit highp ints

- **Repro:** in Playwright Firefox 157 on an Apple M1 class GPU, `gl.getShaderPrecisionFormat(gl.FRAGMENT_SHADER,
  gl.HIGH_INT)` answers rangeMin 24, rangeMax 24 (HIGH_FLOAT answers 127, 127, 23; Chromium and WebKit answer 31, 30
  for ints), and `install({ force: true })` from `@margoengine/webgl2-compat` rejected with code `unsupported`,
  "missing highp-fragment". Found by the audio occlusion and music browser checks.
- **Cause:** the refusal was too strict. GLSL ES 3.00 sections 4.1.3 and 4.5.1 make highp ints 32-bit two's
  complement that wrap, in every shader stage, and the OpenGL ES 3.0.6 specification (section 6.1, GetShaderPrecisionFormat)
  spells that format as range (31, 30); Firefox's (24, 24) is its own report, not the hardware: the same context
  draws a fragment shader's 32-bit wrapping multiply, add, signed multiply, arithmetic shift and division exact
  (0x9e3779b9 * 0x85ebca6b reads back 3238976083, as in Chromium and WebKit). `webgl2Capabilities`
  (packages/webgl2-compat/src/index.ts) trusted the report alone.
- **Fix:** a context whose HIGH_INT report falls short is measured: one point drawn into an RGBA32UI target with that
  arithmetic on uniform inputs, read back and compared with the 32-bit results; it is accepted only when every word
  matches, and the context's framebuffer, program, vertex array, texture, pack buffer, viewport, colour mask, scissor
  and rasterizer-discard state are put back. A context that reports (31, 30) is not drawn on. Firefox on macOS now
  reaches the full tier: the audio occlusion and music checks run on the layer there, and
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/tiers-browser.mjs` passes in Firefox and Chromium. Regression tests:
  packages/webgl2-compat/test/capabilities.test.js "a short highp int report ... is measured" and "... stays refused
  when the measurement is wrong or cannot run".

### Apple M-series: multisample values of a multi-million-triangle frame depend on draw order (2026-11-14, outside Margo)

Release exception: Apple M-series GPU multisample resolve depends on draw order (upstream hardware).

- **What:** gltf/pbr's `test:gpu:parts` never passed on the Apple M6 (Chromium 156, WebGPU on Metal; checked back to
  the test's first commit): the 10M-triangle field split into parts drew 3,187 low-view pixels and 188 close-view
  pixels whose multisample samples were 1 LSB off the reference pre-split into 20 row bands. The far view and the RTX
  A6000 and Radeon 680M runs were exact. The parts are the same triangles with the same vertex data; they draw in
  Morton order, the reference in row order.
- **Repro (no Margo code):** `packages/gltf/scripts/draw-order-probe.mjs` draws row bands of the same field with
  one plain WebGPU pipeline (4x MSAA, reverse-Z depth32float, greater-equal), the fragment writing a function of the
  world position, and counts pixels whose samples differ from the first frame. On the M6 with the default output: all
  20 bands (9,999,392 triangles) drawn in reversed band order differ in 203 pixels, while the same command stream
  repeated differs in 0; bands 6 to 9 (2,075,008 triangles) differ in 180 reversed and in 41 and 105 repeated; band 6
  alone (518,752 triangles, one draw) differs in 0, 3 and 41 across four identical frames. A smoother output
  (`SCALE=1,1,1`) gives 25 pixels reversed for all bands. Inside Margo the effect is the same: the row-band reference
  drawn in reversed band order differs in 40 low-view pixels from itself in band order, and a part drawn twice changes 7.
  A 2D grid of up to 4.5M triangles in one draw is exact forward and reversed (rasterization is watertight), and coverage
  never changes: unlit per-band colours in reversed band order are exact.
- **Cause:** below Margo, in the Apple GPU (tile-based deferred rendering) or its Metal driver: at millions of
  sub-pixel triangles a sample's value depends on the order of the draws, and in the probe's frames now and then on
  nothing Margo controls. Not pinned further; no Apple document was read. WebGPU does not promise bit-identical
  rasterization across different draw sequences.
- **Same stream, too (2026-11-15):** the order-matched reference drawn lit by the same command stream differed from its
  own first frame in 1 low-view pixel in 1 of 20 frames (`PARTS_SELF=20 PARTS_LIT=1`), which flaked the exact
  comparison now and then. A flat output is repeatable: `draw-order-probe.mjs` with a flat per-triangle id in place of
  the position function was exact over all 9,999,392 triangles in 20 repeats and in reversed band order, so which
  triangle wins a sample never changes; only interpolated values do.
- **What Margo does:** `test-parts-browser.mjs` draws each sample's winning triangle (a hash of its provoking vertex
  position, passed flat through a `model.addLighting` shader patch) instead of lit shading, and compares each split with
  a reference pre-split at export into the same parts in the same order (exact samples, draws and triangles), and the
  row-band reference by coverage only; a mutation leg proves the exact comparison still fails for a part dropped, two
  parts' index lists swapped or a part drawn twice. On the M6 it was exact in 20 native and 20 WebGL2-layer runs, and
  `PARTS_SELF=40` (each reference against its own first frame, 40 times per view) found no sample changed. Regression:
  `packages/gltf/scripts/test-parts-browser.mjs` (`npm run test:gpu:parts`).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a first material mesh that failed to register left an empty draw pass behind (materials)

- **Repro:** the scene's first `createMesh` call whose model `engine.use` refuses (a throwing plugin setup): the call
  throws, but a `materials:` plugin stays registered with no member, a pass that runs every frame and draws nothing.
- **Cause:** `createMesh` in `packages/materials/src/built-material.ts` made the scene's draw queue before building and
  registering the model, and its error path disposed the model without leaving the queue, which only leaves when its last
  member does.
- **Fix:** the queue is taken just before registration, and a failed registration deletes the entry from it, so an empty
  queue leaves with the failed mesh. Regression: the draw-queue test of `packages/materials/test/material-usage.test.js`,
  which fails before.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: hashed alpha's shadows cut at a fixed cutoff instead of by the noise (materials/alpha-hash, shadows)

- **Repro:** a `PbrMaterial` with `features: [alphaHash()]` and `color[3] = 0.3`, casting onto a plane under `Shadows`: no
  shadow is drawn (0.3 is below the default `cutoff` 0.5), and at 0.6 a full one. PlayCanvas's `opacityShadowDither` makes
  a 30% material cast about 30% of its shadow texels, so a fading object's shadow fades with it.
- **Cause:** `castMaskOf` in `packages/materials/src/built-material.ts` handed shadow casters the map, alphaMap and the
  material's `alphaTest`; the caster record (`ShadowCasterRecord` in gltf/pbr's `model.ts`) had no hashed flag, so every
  caster shader (shadows, clustered local shadows, staging's contact shadows) cut at one value.
- **Fix:** materials records report `castHashed`, gltf/pbr's caster record carries it as `hashed`, and `Shadows`,
  `VirtualShadows`, clustered's `LocalShadows` and integrated maps and staging's contact shadows cut such a caster with
  `hashedDepth` (shared/caster.js): the colour pass's object-space hash (shared/alpha-hash.js, now one copy for both) at
  one cell per shadow-map texel. Regression: `packages/shadows/test/cutout-casters-browser.mjs` (each pass darkens the
  floor by the opacity's share of the whole shadow, at 0.3 and 0.7; a fixed cutoff gave 0 and 1) and
  `packages/clustered/test/caster-flags.test.js`.
- **Found with it:** clustered `LocalShadows` read its pipeline flags from a key that ended with the displacement's own
  key, so materials fur's `fur:1:map` turned on the `a` flag and kept vertex alpha out of the cut-out (a key with `l`,
  `t` or `o` would have drawn lines or bound maps that are not there). The flags now end at a `|`. Regression:
  `packages/clustered/test/caster-flags.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a KHR_animation_pointer channel animated an IOR of 0 (animation/pointer)

- **Repro:** a glTF material with `KHR_materials_ior` `{ "ior": 0 }` and an animation channel whose pointer is
  `/materials/0/extensions/KHR_materials_ior/ior`; playing it wrote the sampled values into the material's IOR. A sampler
  keying 0 on a material with IOR 1.5 switched it into the infinite-index mode mid-clip, and keys from 1.5 to 0 passed
  every IOR between them.
- **Cause:** `packages/animation/src/pointer.ts` mapped the pointer to gltf/pbr's `ext[1]` and wrote every sample. The
  extension makes 0 a mode set once in the file: "updates of it MUST be ignored", and no sampler targeting the IOR may
  key a value below 1, 0 included.
- **Fix:** a channel on a material whose file IOR is 0 is skipped with a warning; a sampler with an IOR key below 1
  throws RangeError; a cubic spline dipping below 1 between keys of 1 or more writes 1, so the mode is never reached.
  Regression: `packages/animation/tests/ior-pointer.test.js`, which fails before.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: materials refused IOR 0, KHR_materials_ior's specular-glossiness mode

- **Repro:** `new PbrMaterial({ ior: 0 })`, `materialLobes({ ior: 0 })` or `transmission({ factor: 1, ior: 0, ... })`
  threw RangeError, and installing a glTF material with `KHR_materials_ior` `{ "ior": 0 }` plus lobes or transmission
  threw the same way.
- **Cause:** every IOR check took "at least 1", but the extension allows exactly 0 as an infinite index (Fresnel 1 at
  every angle, dispersion with no effect, later updates ignored). The shader paths also read 0 as IOR 1: the extension
  surface hook gave F0 0 (`max(ior, 1)`), and the native refraction and transmission passes bent nothing.
- **Fix:** 0 is accepted in Material (permanent once set), materialLobes (F0 1) and transmission (written to the
  uniform as 1e30, which gives F0 1 and a ray that cannot leave in float32); gltf/pbr's hook and the native volume tint
  and transmission pass treat 0 as infinite. Regression: `packages/materials/test/ior-zero.test.js` and the IOR 0 test of
  `packages/materials/tests/transmission-ior.test.js`, which fail before.

### Radeon 680M: a negated component of a constant-scaled vector loses its sign in a division (list 5, 2026-11-14, worked around in shader/black-hole)

Release exception: Radeon 680M driver loses a sign in a division, worked around in shader.
- **What:** on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, RDNA2, driver 32.0.21030.2001, Edge 157.0.4341.46, WebGPU on D3D12) the
  Event Horizon camera frame looked half a turn away from the hole when the camera sat just off the z axis.
- **Repro:** `packages/shader/test/negated-division-check.html` (run by `negated-division-check.mjs`): a fragment
  shader reads (x, 0, -y) from a uniform, `let cm = u.pos * 2.0;`, and returns `atan2(-cm.z, cm.x)` and
  `(-cm.z) / cm.x`. For (y, x) = (-25, 0.02) the 680M returns 1.570 and 1250 where the answers are -1.570 and -1250, and
  for (-25, -0.02) atan2 returns -4.712, outside [-pi, pi]. The same holds for `-(cm * 0.5).z`, `-(cm * 3.0).z`, a
  `let t = -cm.z`, `0.0 - cm.z`, `-cm` as a whole vector and a negated denominator (`cm.z / (-cm.x)`). Products, sums,
  `atan2(-u.pos.z * 2.0, u.pos.x * 2.0)`, a scale read from a uniform, a vector negated before the scale, a divisor
  of `length(cm)` and `-atan2(cm.z, cm.x)` are exact. The same page is exact on the RTX A6000 (same Edge build, D3D12),
  on raw WebGL2 (ANGLE D3D11) and on Margo's WebGL2 layer.
- **Cause:** below Margo: the 680M's D3D12 shader compiler cancels the constant scale of numerator and denominator and
  drops the negation with it. WGSL defines both expressions exactly (atan2 within 4096 ULP for normal x).
- **Workaround:** the black hole builds its camera frame without atan2: phi counts from the camera's own meridian,
  whose cosine and sine are `cm.x / length(cm.xz)` and `-cm.z / length(cm.xz)` (`packages/shader/src/black-hole.ts`).
  Every other atan2 in Margo's shaders was checked (2026-11-14, `grep -rn "atan2" packages/*/src`): none divides a
  negated component of a constant-scaled vector. The equirect lookups (environment, materials, shader `equirectUV`)
  negate through a `select`, the voxel path tracer's `envUV` takes unit ray directions, the transitions wipe offsets
  a varying; the check above runs those formulations and asserts them on every adapter. User shaders with the pattern
  are still affected on this driver (docs/limits.md). Regression: `packages/shader/test/black-hole-check.mjs`, camera
  frame (fails on the 680M with the atan2 frame: no disk on the middle row, 0 against 218).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: Event Horizon defects (shader/black-hole, lanes SC8 and SC9)

- **Repro:** the old `examples/event-horizon.ts`, side on: two bright columns stood beside the shadow to |y| = 12;
  inclined: rings and streaks banded the disk and wound tighter the longer the page ran; close to the hole the stars
  were dashes. Building the Kerr version found three more: a notch where rays passed over the spin axis, steps on the
  inner rim and the camera frame above.
- **Causes and fixes (`packages/shader/src/black-hole.ts`):** the jet was a hollow cylinder of constant brightness with
  a made-up Doppler term, now a parabolic funnel with |y|^-2 emissivity and D^(2 + 0.7) beaming, sampled four times a
  step; the disk's `sin(r * 22)` and `cos(r * 11)` rings sat above the Nyquist limit and Keplerian shear wound its
  noise without bound, now band-limited fbm faded by the ray-differential footprint with two advected phases
  crossfaded every 24 s; stars were Gaussians on the sky stretched by the lens, now points through the inverse
  footprint jacobian; theta was clamped at the pole instead of reflected; a captured ray stopped marching before it
  crossed the inner disk, now it stops only inside the ISCO.
- **Regressions (each fails without its fix):** `packages/shader/test/black-hole.test.js` "a ray over the spin axis
  goes on to the far side" (fails with the reflection removed) and "a captured ray still crosses the disk on its way
  in" (fails with the early stop back); `packages/shader/test/black-hole-check.mjs`: jet band 0.7 (124 with the old
  sheath, limit 40), star median axis ratio 1.06 (4.03 point sampled, limit 1.5, asserted as the control), disk detail
  ratio 1.05 between 1 s and 120 s (7.8 with the old unbounded winding and no band limit, limit 1.25; with the winding
  alone back the footprint fade hides it, 0.83).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: rain and snow jumped across the box whenever the wind changed (sky/weather, lane SC3)

- **Repro:** attach `Weather` (`@margoengine/sky/weather`) with `wind: [3, 0]`, let it snow for a minute, then change
  `weather.options.wind` (a gust, or `WeatherDrive` writing the wind field each frame): every flake moves by the change
  of wind times the seconds so far in one frame, so gusting snow churns instead of blowing. Found building Whiteout Pass.
- **Cause:** the drift of the particle box was `wind * time`, right only for a wind that never changes.
- **Fix:** the drift is the running sum of wind times delta, kept in double precision by `onPreUpdate`
  (`packages/sky/src/weather.ts`). Regression: "a wind that changes moves the particles on from where they are" in
  `packages/sky/test/weather.test.js` (fails without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: the horizon seam check measured walls on an interior with no horizon in view (headless/look, lane SC7)

- **Repro:** the Cabin Hearth push-in's `hearth` probe (an interior) failed `horizonSeam` at 15.8 codes, and the
  wireframe shot at 10.9 to 65.5 codes.
- **Cause:** `horizonSeam` measured the luma step along the camera's analytic horizon in every column, whatever stood
  across the line: on an interior the line crosses the mantel, a real edge, not a seam between sky and ground.
- **Fix:** the check counts only columns with sky 3 rows above the line, from the `sky` mask, and `checkProbe` runs it
  only with a sky mask (named in `lookBounds` without one, it fails as missing). Regression: "horizonSeam counts only
  columns where the sky meets the line" in `packages/headless/tests/look.test.js` and the interior case of
  `tests/shot-look.test.js` (both fail without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: Tonemap's white balance brightened every temperature but 6500 K and flipped colours below 1903.4 K (tonemap)

- **Repro:** `Tonemap.attach(engine, {temperature: 3200})`: white came out 1.0165 times as bright as at 6500 K (one
  kelvin off 6500 K brightened the picture 1.65 percent). `temperature: 1800` (candle light) turned a grey card lit by
  1800 K light pure blue; `whiteBalanceGain(1667)` returned [-0.87, -4.66, 62.6].
- **Cause:** white balance was a per-channel gain on Rec.709 RGB, the ratio of the 6500 K and the scene's Planckian
  whites. Its luminance normalisation divided by a stray factor (the reference white's luminance over its green, 1.0165).
  And below 1903.4 K the Planckian white lies outside Rec.709 (its blue is negative), so the gains changed sign; the
  shader's clamp then zeroed red and green.
- **Fix:** white balance is now a chromatic adaptation: von Kries scaling in the linearised Bradford cone space (whose
  responses to every Planckian white from 1667 to 25000 K are positive), applied as one 3x3 matrix in the effects shader
  and normalised so a grey card lit by the light keeps its luminance (`packages/tonemap/src/effects.ts`,
  `whiteBalanceMatrix`, which replaces `whiteBalanceGain`). Regression: "white balance maps the light colour to neutral
  over the whole range, below 1903.4 K too" and the luminance cases in `packages/tonemap/tests/effects.test.js`, and
  `packages/tonemap/tests/white-balance-browser.mjs` (`npm run test:gpu:white-balance -w @margoengine/tonemap`, WebGPU
  and the WebGL2 compatibility layer: the 1750 K card matches the CPU matrix to the 8-bit code, no channel black).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: LocalExposure cut its blur short above a 10.7-texel sigma (tonemap)

- **Repro:** `new LocalExposure({radius: 0.1})` on a 1080-row view (sigma 27 quarter-resolution texels), or the default
  radius 0.02 on a 2160-row view (sigma 10.8): the bilateral blur stopped at 32 taps a side, so the kernel ended at 1.18
  sigma, or just under 3 sigma, instead of 3, and regions came out smaller and harder edged than `radius` documents. On a
  320 by 1400 view at radius 0.1 the frame was up to 91 8-bit levels off the full-kernel oracle.
- **Cause:** `packages/tonemap/src/local.ts` capped the taps at `TAPS` (32) whatever the sigma.
- **Fix:** the base is built from larger blocks (8 by 8, 16 by 16, ...) whenever three sigma would need more than 32
  taps a side, the downsampled bilateral of Durand and Dorsey (2002), and the blur always reaches three sigma; the
  shader samples the base at the block size. Regression: "LocalExposure blurs three sigma a side at any radius by
  building its base from larger blocks" in `packages/tonemap/tests/local.test.js` and the radius 0.1, 1400-row case of
  `packages/tonemap/tests/local-browser.mjs` (91 levels off without the fix, within 0.45 with it, WebGPU and WebGL2
  compatibility layer).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: Tonemap's contrast above 1 crushed every dark channel to black, and left banded flat runs (tonemap, lane SC7)

- **Repro:** `Tonemap.attach(engine, {curve: 'agx', contrast: 1.08})` (the `snowNight` kit's grade) on a night scene:
  Cabin Hearth's outside view at 540 x 960 on the 680M was 7.7 % black (max channel at or under 2) and 1.2 % banded;
  the same frame at contrast 1 was 0 % and 0.14 %. The A6000 shots measured crush 30 to 50 % outside, 3.4 to 4.3 %
  at the kettle, and banding 1.1 to 1.5 % on the push-in's interior probes (flat runs of `39,0,0` beside `0,0,0`).
- **Cause:** contrast was linear about grey in display-linear light, `(x - 0.18) k + 0.18`, clamped at 0. Every channel
  below `0.18 (1 - 1/k)` went to 0: display-linear 0.0133, sRGB code 30, at k = 1.08. The clipped channels were
  exactly 0 over whole areas, so the dither had nothing to break up: long identical runs that the banding check
  counts, and pure-red firelit wood whose green and blue had been cut away.
- **Fix:** contrast is a power about grey, `0.18 (x / 0.18)^k`, a slope of k in log exposure as in a log grading space
  (ACEScc, Academy S-2014-003; the ASC CDL's power), which keeps black at black and clips nothing below
  (`packages/tonemap/src/shaders.ts`, `margoContrast`; contrast 1 is untouched). Regression: the contrast 1.08 frames
  of `packages/tonemap/tests/curves-browser.mjs` (every one of 1,456,524 dark channels was 0 without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: contrast 0 ran pow(0, 0), which WGSL and GLSL leave undefined (tonemap, creative, lane SC13)

- **Repro:** `Tonemap` or creative's `PostProcessing` with `contrast: 0` (the documented range is 0 to 4) on a frame
  with black in it. The documented form `0.18 * (x / 0.18) ** contrast` is flat 18% grey at contrast 0, black
  included, because `0 ** 0` is 1 in JavaScript as `pow(x, 0)` is in IEEE 754. On the 680M the black pixels stayed
  black instead: 115,920 of 230,400 channels with Tonemap, every channel with `PostProcessing` (sRGB code 0, not
  118 and 105).
- **Cause:** both shaders evaluated `pow(0, 0)`. WGSL defines pow as exp2(y log2 x), and log2 0 has no finite value;
  GLSL ES 3.00 (section 8.2) leaves pow undefined when x = 0 and y <= 0. The result is whatever the driver returns.
- **Fix:** contrast 0 is defined as flat 0.18 and returned before the power (Tonemap's `margoContrast`, the
  `PostProcessing` shader). 0 stays in the valid range, as the docs and the option checks already had it, so no
  error code is needed: the docs now say what contrast 0 gives. Regressions, on WebGPU and the WebGL2 compatibility
  layer: `packages/tonemap/tests/contrast-zero-browser.mjs` (`npm run test:gpu:contrast-zero -w
  @margoengine/tonemap`) and `packages/creative/tests/post-contrast-zero-browser.mjs` (`npm run
  test:gpu:post-contrast-zero -w @margoengine/creative`), every pixel the flat grey with the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: creative post's contrast clipped scene-linear colour below 0.18 (1 - 1/k) to black (creative, lane SC10)

- **Repro:** `@margoengine/creative`'s `PostProcessing` with `contrast` above 1: every scene-linear channel below
  `0.18 (1 - 1/contrast)` was 0 before its display transform. On lit boxes at exposures -4 to 1 and contrast 1.2,
  695,400 of 698,258 dark channels that should show (sRGB code 3 and up) were black on the 680M, 37 levels off.
- **Cause:** the same linear contrast about grey that Tonemap had until 2026-11-14,
  `max(0, (c - 0.18) contrast + 0.18)` in `packages/creative/src/post.ts`.
- **Fix:** the power about grey Tonemap now uses, `0.18 (c / 0.18)^k` (ACEScc, Academy S-2014-003; the ASC CDL's
  power), so black stays black and nothing below grey clips; contrast 1 is untouched. Regression:
  `packages/creative/tests/post-contrast-browser.mjs` (`npm run test:gpu:post-contrast -w @margoengine/creative`:
  0 black channels and within 3 levels of the power with the fix). The other contrast controls were checked:
  `@margoengine/math`'s `gradeSRGB` scales sRGB display values about 0.5 unclamped, the CSS Filter Effects form
  its docs state, and sciviz's LIC stretches its noise texture about 0.5 (not a colour), so neither clips light.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: a sloped shelter sheltered its own top from snow in stripes a texel apart (weather/cover, lane SC6)

- **Repro:** Cabin Hearth outside (`examples/cabin-hearth/index.html?ui=0`): the lower roof slope shows dark bands
  parallel to the eave, bare roofing between strips of snow, in every outside shot; the bands stay with `fog=0`.
- **Cause:** `PrecipitationCover`'s `weather_exposed` shelters a point under the highest occluder of the four map
  texels around it. Those texel centres lie up to a texel from the point on each axis, so a sloped occluder's own top
  (the roof is both a shelter and a receiver) reads up to sqrt(2) texels times its slope above itself there, far over
  the 0.02 m bias: the roof sheltered itself wherever its texel phase put the higher texel in the four.
- **Fix:** a receiver facing up (normal y 0.5 or more) adds that rise, `sqrt(2) * texel * tan(slope)`, to the bias,
  the slope-scaled depth bias of shadow maps (Williams 1978, "Casting curved shadows on curved surfaces";
  Dou, Yan, Kerzner, Dai and Wyman 2014, "Adaptive Depth Bias for Shadow Maps", JCGT 3(4)); steeper receivers keep
  the plain bias so walls under an eave stay dry (`packages/weather/src/cover.ts`). Regression: the 30 degree slope
  probes of `packages/weather/tests/cover-check.html` (`node packages/weather/tests/parity-browser.mjs cover`: 24
  points on the slope's own top all exposed, a sloped point under the flat roof still sheltered; without the fix 21 of
  the 24 read sheltered) and the shader text assertions in `tests/cover.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: Cabin Hearth's walls and chimney rendered black and its window patch read pale (examples, scenery, tools/shot, lane SC6)

- **Repro:** `node tools/shot/cli.mjs tools/shot/shots/cabin-window-snow.json` (dev PC, RTX A6000, f647cfae8): look
  checks fail `crush` at 30.3, 33.9 and 37.7 % (bound 3 %) and `nan` on every probe of all five Cabin shots; the log
  walls and the chimney are black, and the lantern's patch on the snow below the window reads pale beige.
- **Cause:** three. The page used the kit's default moon, low behind the cabin, so every outside view saw the front
  wall and the chimney backlit, and the fresh dark logs (`#5b3a22`, albedo 0.06) reflected almost none of the blue
  moonlight. The kit's lantern was a 2,700 K bulb's colour (`[1, 0.62, 0.3]`), which next to the moonlit snow read
  pale, not as firelight. The shot files asked for the `nan` check, whose float frame the shot tool does not write.
- **Fix:** the page sets `moonDirection` [0.6, 0.45, 0.66] (front right, over the outside views' shoulder) and
  weathered logs, roofing and frame (`examples/cabin-hearth/main.ts`); the kit's lantern burns at the fire's flame
  colour, about 1,900 K (`packages/sky/src/scene-kits.ts`); the shot file check refuses `nan` and unknown check names
  (`tools/shot/shot-file.mjs`) and the Cabin shots drop `nan`. Regression: `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs`
  (`npm run test:cabin-hearth`, the moonlit log wall is not black; it replaced the source-reading `tests/cabin-hearth.test.js`), `packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js` "the window lantern burns with a flame colour",
  `tests/shot-file.test.js` (`lookBounds` `nan` and `clipping` refused); each fails without its fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the stone round Cabin Hearth's fire read flat tan, and the first frame showed no fire (examples, scenery, lane E)

- **Repro (before):** `examples/cabin-hearth/index.html?ui=0&view=hearth` (680M and RTX A6000): the hearthstone and the
  firebox jambs and back, all soot dark (`#3a3530`, `#1b1714`), rendered a flat light tan; a 540 x 960 hold of the
  kettle shot's opening camera read the stone at the mouth `#b4835b` (hue 27, saturation 0.49, value 0.70) and at the
  front 0.57. The kettle shot's `open` probe (time 0) showed an empty grate.
- **Cause:** the fire was one point light 0.3 m in front of the flames and 0.42 m above the stone, so the stone, the
  jambs, the back and the logs all sat 0.3 to 0.7 m from it and came out alike, and the logs behind it shadowed
  nothing. AgX's path to white desaturates those levels to tan (documented behaviour: the hue stays at 26 degrees).
  Ruled out: Clustered's BRDF and falloff, fog, bloom and local exposure. The particles were born from time 0 and a
  shot's warm-up draws that instant without moving the clock, so the flames filled in only over their lifetime.
- **Fix:** the fire is now its flame line: two points over the logs at the 2-point Gauss-Legendre nodes of the 0.62 m
  flames (0.18 m either side, half the kit's intensity each), shadowed by `LocalShadows` with a shadow radius of
  0.15 m (PCSS), so the stand's legs and the logs cast one soft shadow, not two hard copies (two hard points did:
  the largest luminance step across the floor's leg and log shadows was 0.42 of the lit side; now 0.07, the old single
  light 0.04). On the A6000 the stone now reads mouth `#9e6d45` (27/0.56/0.62), middle 0.47, front 0.39: warm orange
  falling off toward the room. The fire's power is unchanged, so the room beside the hearth is darker (rug display
  value 0.41 to 0.39 in the hold, back-corner view mean luminance 0.0253 to 0.0191), accepted. The kit's fire,
  embers and steam prewarm their longest lifetime (`schedule.prewarm`, `@margoengine/vfx/schedule`), and the fire's
  capacity follows the `fire` option (a fixed 4,000 capped the flames from `fire` 2.3 up).
  `examples/cabin-hearth/main.ts`, `packages/sky/src/scene-kits.ts`.
- **Regression tests:** `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` (`npm run test:cabin-hearth`, the frame's pixels; it replaced the source-reading `tests/cabin-hearth.test.js`: "the hearthstone reads soot-dark and warm", "the rug and the back
  corner stay lit", "the fire is its flame line"; a CPU prediction of the stone's display colour through the kit's
  white balance, exposure, AgX and contrast, which fails on the old page at mouth saturation 0.44 and rug 0.74),
  `packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js` ("start full on the first frame", the capacity over the `fire` range).
- **Sources:** Abramowitz and Stegun 1964, Handbook of Mathematical Functions, 25.4.29 (Gauss-Legendre nodes);
  Fernando 2005, "Percentage-Closer Soft Shadows", SIGGRAPH sketch; de Ris 1979, "Fire radiation: a review", Proc.
  Combustion Institute 17; Snyder 1996, "Area light sources for real-time graphics", MSR-TR-96-11; Blender 4.0
  release notes, Color Management (AgX); Gilchrist et al. 1999, "An anchoring theory of lightness perception",
  Psychological Review 106(4):795-834.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: Cabin Hearth flames soft and smeary at the base, around the logs (scenery, lane B)

- **Repro (before):** the Cabin Hearth close-up (`tools/shot/shots/cabin-hearth-kettle.json`, its last camera key) at
  1920 x 1080, one held, prewarmed frame: the base of the fire was a soft, half-transparent haze over the log faces.
  The flame layer (the frame with the fire minus the same frame without it, bloom off) rose from 10 to 90% of its peak
  over 35.2 px on average on five lines up across the upper log's top (36.0 on the WebGL2 layer), three frames 0.1 s
  apart on an RTX A6000.
- **Cause:** births under the log tops and in front of the logs. `snowNight().hearth.fire` was born in a 0.2 x 0.02 x
  0.08 m box plus a 0.16 m cone disc around the page's point 0.16 m under the log tops, so a third of the flames rose
  in front of the upper log's face, still fading in (the alpha curve starts at 0), and lay over it. Measured one switch
  at a time (native / layer): births on the fuel's top 3.4 / 3.6 px; soft particles off 36.4 / 40.0; TAA history off
  35.2 / 35.0; alpha curve's first key at 0.85 35.2 / 36.0. So TAA is not a cause (the per-engine reactive-mask registry
  stays with the elements plan), nor softness or the alpha curve.
- **Fix:** the kit's flames are born on the fuel's top: a 0.28 x 0.045 x 0.05 m box and a 0.02 m cone disc, 0.6 m along
  the logs, 0.14 m across their tops and 0.09 m high around `position`, which the kit now documents as the centre of
  the fuel's top; the page passes it (0.46 m, between the log tops at 0.415 and 0.505). The close-up rise is 3.8 px (4.0
  on the layer). `packages/sky/src/scene-kits.ts`, `packages/sky/README.md`, `examples/cabin-hearth/main.ts`.
- **Regression tests:** `packages/sky/test/fire-base-gpu.mjs` (the kit's flames over the hearth's logs, native and
  layer: 46.4 / 46.0 px before, 17.8 / 18.2 after, bound 24 with its reason in the file),
  `packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js` ("the flames are born on the fuel top").
- **Sources:** Nguyen, Fedkiw, Jensen 2002, "Physically Based Modeling and Animation of Fire", SIGGRAPH; Lorach 2007,
  "Soft Particles", NVIDIA; Karis 2014, "High Quality Temporal Supersampling", SIGGRAPH course.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: froxel fog with Clustered's own shadows lost the device on the first frame (environment, lane SC1)

- **Repro:** `Clustered.attach(engine, {shadows: {maxLights: 1}})` with a light that sets `shadow`, then
  `VolumetricFog.attach(engine, {lights})`: the first frame warns "binding index 28 not present in the bind group
  layout" and every later frame fails ("Invalid CommandBuffer", `gpu-lost`). Found building Cabin Hearth.
- **Cause:** the fog's light loop called only `clusterShadow` (LocalShadows' function), not `clusterShadowVisibility`
  (Clustered's own shadows). The shadow bindings 28 to 30 were declared but unused, so the inject pass's automatic
  layout left them out and the light group, which carries them, failed to build. The light also passed through walls
  into the fog.
- **Fix:** the loop calls whichever shadow function the light source declares (`packages/environment/src/volumetric.ts`,
  `localShadow`). Regression: "shadows and clustered lights compose" in `packages/environment/tests/volumetric.test.js`
  (fails without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: snow's lift left a gap under the top face of a flat-shaded box (weather/snow and gltf, lane SC1, fixed lane SC2)

- **Repro:** `Snow.attach(engine, {cover: 1, depth: 0.35})` over `box()` meshes (core's box has its own four vertices
  per face): the top face rises 0.35 m and floats above the box's sides, a visible gap from the side (Cabin Hearth's
  chimney at depth 0.35; the kit now uses 0.12, where the gap is smaller but still there).
- **Cause:** the vertex stage lifts each vertex by `weather_snow_depth` of its own normal: an up-facing top-face vertex
  rises, the side face's vertex at the same corner has a horizontal normal and stays. Meshes with shared, smooth
  vertices (a terrain, a ground plane) do not show it.
- **Fix:** the lift is the snow's depth on flat ground at the vertex's place, whatever way its face turns
  (`weather_snow_depth(p.xz, 1.0, ...)` in `packages/weather/src/snow.ts` and `gltf.ts`), so vertices that share a
  place rise together and a hard edge stays joined. Under a `PrecipitationCover` the sheltered vertices stay down:
  a shelter's top and the top edge of its sides rise, the foot of its sides does not. Regression: the "seam" case of
  `packages/weather/tests/snow-check.html` (`npm run test:gpu -w @margoengine/weather -- snow`, a box seen side on from
  between its top and the snow's top: no background row down its middle column), which fails without the fix, and the
  lift assertions in `tests/snow.test.js` and `tests/gltf.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: shot frames came out black over SSH on the dev PC (tools/shot, lane SH2)

- **Repro:** `ssh dev`, then in a checkout with `BROWSER_ARGS=["--disable-gpu-sandbox"]`: `npm run test:shot`. Before the
  fix case 1 failed with 1 distinct frame of 30: every frame black, while the masks (read on the GPU) were right.
- **Cause:** in a Windows session with no desktop the browser's composited copy of a WebGPU canvas (`drawImage`) is
  black although the GPU draws. The shot driver copied frames that way.
- **Fix:** the driver reads a WebGPU canvas from its own texture on the GPU in the frame's task (it adds `COPY_SRC` to
  the canvas configuration); `manifest.capture` says `gpu`. Regression: case 1 of
  `tools/shot/test/determinism-check.mjs` (30 distinct frames of 30 on the RTX A6000 over SSH, and the `gpu` capture).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: encodeWithFFmpeg left BT.709 primaries and transfer unspecified with ffmpeg 9 (headless)

- **Repro:** `encodeWithFFmpeg` of `@margoengine/headless/ffmpeg` to an .mp4 with the BtbN ffmpeg n9.0 build, then
  `ffprobe -show_entries stream=color_transfer,color_primaries`: both `unknown` (code 2 in the bitstream and the MP4
  `colr` box), while range and matrix are right. Found by the shot master encode's `colr` check (lane SH3).
- **Cause:** `packages/headless/src/ffmpeg.ts` tags with `-color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709`, but its `scale`
  filter leaves the frames' primaries and transfer unset and ffmpeg 9 writes the frames' own tags over those options.
- **Fix:** the filter chain ends in `setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv`, as
  `tools/shot/encode.mjs` does, so ffprobe reads `tv,bt709,bt709,bt709` (lane SH4, checked with ffmpeg 9.0.2 and
  n9.0, H.264 and VP9). Regression: `ffmpegArguments picks the codec from the file name, and tags BT.709` in
  `packages/headless/tests/video.test.js` asks for the whole filter, and `npm run test:real-ffmpeg` of the package now
  needs all three of matrix, transfer and primaries to read bt709 (its old pattern also matched `bt709/unknown/unknown`).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: over SSH on the dev PC a browser launch now and then gets no WebGPU adapter (tools/shot)

Release exception: Windows OpenSSH session: browser launch sometimes gets no WebGPU adapter (driver/session).
- **Repro:** `ssh dev`, `BROWSER_ARGS=["--disable-gpu-sandbox"]`, `npm run test:shot` twice: one run of two failed at its
  third browser launch with `no-webgpu-adapter` while WebGL (ANGLE D3D11) had the RTX A6000; the other passed.
  Without `--disable-gpu-sandbox` no launch gets an adapter there.
- **Measured (lane SH3, 2026-11-14):** `node tools/shot/test/adapter-probe.mjs 12` launched Edge 157 twelve times
  over SSH the way the shot tool does (`--disable-gpu-sandbox`), asking for a high-performance adapter at 0, 0.5, 2
  and 5 s after load: 9 launches answered NVIDIA at once, 1 answered only on the second ask 0.5 s later, and 2 stayed
  null for all four asks over 7.5 s. Every launch's edge://gpu, null or not, read the same WebGPU status ("Hardware
  accelerated but at reduced performance", its Dawn list opening with the AMD iGPU's D3D12 adapter; the PC has the
  A6000 and that iGPU), so the null answer comes from Edge's GPU process in the SSH logon session (no desktop),
  outside Margo. A retry inside the page does not fix it: two launches in twelve never answered.
- **Cause:** outside Margo: the Edge GPU process started from an SSH (non-desktop) logon on a two-adapter Windows PC.
  Not seen in the signed-in desktop session.
- **Fix in place:** the render queue (`tools/shot/queue.mjs`, docs/shots.md, Render queue) runs renders in the signed-in
  desktop session through the "Margo Shot Runner" scheduled task (`tools/shot/runner-task.ps1`). Open until that task
  is registered on the dev PC (it needs an administrator to register for the signed-in account) and a run of the
  Orrery dolly through it passes; over SSH a shot that hits this exits 1 before drawing and the same command run again
  goes on from its saved progress.
- **Root cause found (2026-11-15):** a process started over SSH on the dev PC runs in Windows session 0
  (`tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>" /FO CSV` answers `"Services","0"`; the same command from the signed-in desktop answers
  session 1). Win32-OpenSSH's sshd is a service, and every service and its children run in session 0, which Windows
  isolates from the signed-in desktop; a WDDM GPU's display belongs to the console session. Edge's GPU process started
  there is what answered null. Sources: Microsoft Learn, "Interactive Services" (Microsoft, 2024,
  https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/services/interactive-services) and "Remote and console terminal
  differences" (Microsoft, 2024, https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/termserv/consoles-vs-terminals).
- **Fixed:** `openBrowser` (scripts/browser.js) looks up the process's session when a probe gets no adapter
  (scripts/support/windows-session.mjs) and, in session 0, throws `no-webgpu-adapter` with `reason:
  'windows-session-0'` and a message that names the session and the way out (the render queue, or a task that runs
  only while the user is signed in), instead of pointing at a driver reset or a browser update. Regression:
  tests/browser-startup.test.js (session 0 named, a desktop session keeps the old reason) and
  tests/windows-session.test.js (the tasklist lines as measured). Renders over SSH still go through the render queue;
  it needs the "Margo Shot Runner" task registered on the dev PC by an administrator.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a RECTANGULAR_TRIMMED_SURFACE with usense or vsense false was read with its normal unturned (brep)

- **Repro:** none in the corpus (no file there writes a .F. sense on one). The side of a cylinder written on
  `RECTANGULAR_TRIMMED_SURFACE(..., .F., .T.)` of its cylinder, its face against the trimmed normal (same_sense
  false), through `bodiesFromSTEP` in `@margoengine/brep`: the side came out inside out, its mesh enclosing -V / 3,
  while `massProperties` still gave V; an `OFFSET_SURFACE` of such a trimmed surface moved the wrong way.
- **Cause:** ISO 10303-42 (rectangular_trimmed_surface) has usense and vsense say whether each parameter of the trimmed
  surface runs with the basis surface's or against it, so the trimmed surface's normal, Su x Sv of its own parameters,
  is the basis surface's turned where exactly one is false. `packages/brep/src/model/import.ts` read the basis surface
  and ignored both senses.
- **Fix:** the importer reads the trimmed surface as a copy of its basis surface, marked as against STEP's normal
  (`Importer.inverted`) where usense differs from vsense (and unmarked where the basis surface was marked), so the face's
  sense and an offset's distance are turned for it, as for swept surfaces below.
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/import-sense.test.js`: `a rectangular trimmed surface with one sense false faces
  against its basis surface, as STEP says` (all four sense pairs: side sense, `checkBody` clean, mass and mesh volume)
  and `a plane trimmed with one sense false faces against the plane; a trimmed offset moves with it` (cap normal, and a
  trimmed cylinder of r + d with vsense false offset by d to radius r). Both fail on the code before.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: faces on swept surfaces read as analytic ones came out silently inside out (brep)

- **Repro:** a STEP cylinder whose side is a `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` of a line running down the axis, or a
  `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` of a circle swept against its turn, through `bodiesFromSTEP` in `@margoengine/brep`:
  the side face's sense is turned, so its mesh is wound inward and encloses -V / 3. `massProperties` and `checkBody`
  integrate the surface as it is and give V and no problem. The same for a plane from a line turned running out from
  its axis, cones, and spheres and tori from a circle turning the other way; an `OFFSET_SURFACE` of one moved its
  distance the wrong way (a cylinder of radius r + 2d).
- **Cause:** `packages/brep/src/model/import.ts` read these surfaces as the modeler's analytic ones, whose normals
  point out, and took the face's same_sense (and the offset's distance) against that normal. STEP gives both against
  its own normal, Su x Sv of the swept surface's parameters, which points in for these cases.
- **Fix:** the importer marks a surface whose normal is against STEP's (`Importer.inverted`, `against`): the face's
  sense and an offset's distance are turned for it; a plane gets its frame's z turned instead.
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/import-sense.test.js`: the faces' normals, the offsets' radii, and `a solid with
  a side swept against STEP normal meshes to its own volume, not a negative one` (mesh volume positive and within
  1e-3 of V). Before the fix the mesh volume is negative.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: a B-spline whose end knot repeats more than degree + 1 times evaluates to NaN at that end (brep)

- **Repro:** abc 00000011 (curve #81932, a cubic whose knot list gives 0.0 twice, multiplicities 4 then 3: seven knots
  at t = 0) through `bodiesFromSTEP` in `@margoengine/brep`: `curveEvaluator(curve).at(0)` is NaN, and a vertex at the
  curve's start projects to t = 1, so the vertex lands on the far end of the curve, 2.38 mm from where it is. Small: the
  hairpin cubics in `packages/brep/tests/spline-end-knots.test.js`.
- **Cause:** `findSpan` (`packages/brep/src/geometry/nurbs.ts`) returned span p for u at or below U[p] and n at or above
  U[n + 1]. With more than p + 1 knots at an end, that span has zero length: its basis is 0 / 0. `Spline.nearest` then
  compares distances with NaN, which is never smaller, and drops the start.
- **Fix:** at the ends, `findSpan` steps to the first (last) span of non-zero length; ordinary clamped knot vectors get
  the same span as before.
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/spline-end-knots.test.js` (a curve with the repeat at one end and at both, and a
  surface with it at its u start): the ends evaluate to their control points and project to t = 0 and 1. Before the
  fix `at(0)` is NaN and the start projects to 1.
