### Fixed 2026-11-15: the body check took a vertex's tolerance along the whole edge, and a sliver face held everything but itself (brep)

- **Repro:** abc 00000044 step_007 body 91 (316 faces, the upper head) through `bodiesFromSTEP` and `checkBody` in
  `@margoengine/brep`: four "lies inside ..., which it does not bound" (edges #223689 and #213548 in face #8419, #206970
  in #17481, #206971 in #16577), all round the vertex #233982.
- **Shape:** the cylinders #16577 (radius 7.5 mm) and #8419 (6 mm) have parallel axes 13.5000 mm apart, so they touch
  along a line (they do not overlap; the 3 um of the first reading was rounding), and the plane #10877 (x = -32.5 mm)
  is tangent to #16577. Between the three runs a cusp at most 7.4 um across. At y = 15.1 mm its foot is the sliver face
  #17481 (between the plane and #16577, 0.33 mm long) and the spline #206970 across the rest; the vertex #233982, where
  they meet, is 3.7 um off each curve, so the import gives it a tolerance of 5.6 um.
- **Cause:** the body is sound (every edge is on its faces within its tolerance, and no two faces come within the sum
  of their tolerances away from a common vertex); the check was wrong in two places. First, `checkBody`
  (`packages/brep/src/model/check.ts`) took an edge for touching a face within ten times the largest tolerance of the
  edge and both its vertices, along the whole edge. A vertex's tolerance is a ball round its point (Jackson 1995; the
  curves of its edges end somewhere in it), so for three of the four, lines 0.1 um tolerant running 7.4 to 46 um off a
  face, the 5.6 um of the vertex at one end made them lie in it. Second, `FaceUV` (`packages/brep/src/model/faces.ts`)
  samples each edge from its start, so its points cut across the 7.4 um between the line's end and the arc's at
  #233982; the sliver is no wider than that, the points wound the other way, and `contains` held everything but the
  sliver, so the spline, 0.11 mm off it in its plane, lay inside it.
- **Fix:** the check allows ten times the edge's tolerance along the edge and ten times a vertex's only within that
  reach of the vertex (a crossing there is the edge meeting its neighbours, as before). A loop's sense is taken with
  each edge's curve end put in where it lies apart from the next edge's start (by more than a millionth of the face's
  size); the points themselves are unchanged. Body 91 now checks clean; no verdict of the CAD corpus changes otherwise
  (48 STEP files, the brep fixtures and both brep inputs, old and new code side by side).
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/check-tolerance.test.js`: the cusp built in code from body 91's numbers (a fin
  7.44 um across between the two cylinders and the plane, its foot the sliver and the cusp edge, its corner vertex
  5.6 um tolerant) checks clean, and so with larger cylinders; the same fin with one edge's own tolerance raised to
  take in the face it runs beside is reported lying inside it, and the cylinders moved 50 um into each other are
  reported. Before the fix the fin reports both false problems.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: a B-spline face whose corner has a zero derivative is refused as a loop over a pole, or meshes open (brep)

- **Repro:** abc 00000044 step_007 (validity check: "a loop over a pole between its vertices is not supported yet" on
  face #18937, a degree 5 B-spline whose last two control points of its v = 0 row meet at the corner the loop starts
  from). Small: the cube's top written as a quadratic in u whose first two control points of the row v = 0 meet at the
  corner (0, 0, 10) (the test below): `model.checkBody` threw that RangeError, and `tessellateSTEP` left the top's edge
  along y = 0 open (four edges used once).
- **Cause:** Su vanishes at that corner, and only there: the line of u through it still runs away from it, so the
  corner has its own (u, v) like any corner. `FaceUV.close` (`packages/brep/src/model/faces.ts`) refused every loop
  point where `singular` held, and the tessellator's bounds (`packages/brep/src/mesh/tessellate.ts`) took every such
  point for a pole and walked a line of the domain from it along v = 0, whose points it made up on the edge beside it:
  the plane next to it has none of them, so the seam stayed open.
- **Fix:** `onPole` (`packages/brep/src/geometry/surfaces.ts`): a point is a pole only where `singular` holds and the
  whole line of the vanishing parameter through it lies at the point. Both use it.
- **Regression:** `a B-spline face whose corner has Su zero there (two control points met) is a corner, not a pole` in
  `packages/brep/tests/step-tessellate.test.js`: the mesh closed and outward, `checkBody` clean, the exact volume and
  area to 1e-9. Before the fix it fails on the open mesh, and with the tessellator's half alone on the RangeError.

### Fixed 2026-11-13: a surface of revolution whose profile ends tangent to its circle folds the mesh at that rim (brep)

- **Repro:** `tessellateSTEP` in `@margoengine/brep` on a cylinder (radius 10 mm, height 20 mm) whose side is written
  as `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` of half an ellipse on it running from (-r, 0, 0) over +y to (r, 0, h), the cylinder cut by
  the plane through its two rim points (the fixture `revolvedSide` in `packages/brep/tests/step-tessellate.test.js`
  with `tangent` set), deflection 0.01 mm: 12 triangles along the bottom rim wound backwards, about 195 rim vertices
  took a normal along the axis instead of outward, and the side's mesh came out 0.08% larger than the side.
- **Cause:** at each end the profile runs along the circle it turns on, so Su and Sv are parallel all round that rim
  (a singular line of the parametrization that is not a pole). `normalOf` (`packages/brep/src/geometry/surfaces.ts`)
  stepped off only when Su x Sv was exactly zero, so a rounding-sized cross product gave an arbitrary normal, and
  refinement chasing those normals' turn packed slivers against the rim. Under them, the face was laid out in (u, v),
  where a profile off its meridian plane shears the surface (u lines are helices that turn flat along such a rim) and
  squeezes it (height grows as v squared there): triangles across the u lines stood off the side and turned over.
- **Fix:** `normalOf` treats Su x Sv within 1e-10 of |Su| |Sv| as degenerate and steps across the line, inside the
  profile's own domain, taking Sv's part along Su back in u. A Revolution whose profile is in no plane with its axis has
  `twist` (the turn of its u lines about the axis) and `meridian` (length along its meridian section): the tessellator
  lays such a face out at (u + twist(v), meridian(v)), as the surface lies, with its rows evenly along the meridian, and
  edges on it follow their chords there.
- **Regression:** `a surface of revolution whose profile ends tangent to its circles` in
  `packages/brep/tests/step-tessellate.test.js`: closed, outward, inscribed (short by no more than the deflection's
  reach), every side normal radial, with and without a seam, at 0.005 and 0.001 mm. Before the fix it fails (12
  triangles wound backwards; with the normals alone fixed, the side's area over).

### Fixed 2026-11-13: Storm Light's sky, rain, moon, beam and sea for the video (sky, taa, environment, water, lane S1m)

- **TAA kept no history over the sky (taa).** Repro: `VolumetricClouds` with `temporal` under TAA at a still camera:
  the deck's march grain stands unaveraged over the sky. Cause: `cameraVelocity` gave depth 0 (the reversed-Z far
  plane) a history depth of -1 and the resolve took history only above 0. Fix: the sky keeps depth 0 and history from
  sky alone. Regression: `packages/taa/test/rejection-browser.mjs` (settled stripes at depth 0 change 17.0 levels a
  frame, as on a surface; 24.7 before).
- **TAA then averaged the rain over the sky away (sky).** Repro: Storm Light with the sky's history: the streaks over
  the sky vanish. Cause: rain draws no motion vectors, and the dark sky's history pulled each streak down. Fix:
  `Weather` `reactive: true` draws the particles' coverage into `reactiveMask`, which Storm Light hands TAA as
  `reactive`. Regression: the `weather` case of `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs` (streaks over the sky under
  TAA 2.30 levels with the mask, 0.87 without, at 4x; WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer).
- **Weather's and VFX's particles reached TAA's reactive mask only by hand (sky, vfx; KB-TAA-PARTICLEMASK1).** Repro: a
  plain stage with `Weather` (or a fast `VFX` spray) and `TAA.attach(engine)`: the streaks average into the sky, as
  above, unless the scene sets `reactive: true` and hands `weather.reactiveMask` to TAA; VFX drew no mask at all.
  Cause: Water published its mask on the pass context (`packages/shared/reactive-mask.js`), Weather and VFX did not.
  Fix: TAA's read of the registry counts as demand; Weather draws and publishes its mask while TAA reads, and VFX draws
  its billboards' alpha into one shared r8unorm particle mask (`reactiveTarget`) the same way. Storm Light, Cabin
  Hearth and Whiteout Pass lose their wiring. Regression: the `weather` case of `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs`
  (now two plain `TAA.attach(e)` rigs: streaks 1.59 levels with the default, 0.76 with `reactive: false`, at 4x),
  `packages/vfx/test/reactive-check.mjs` (a spray keeps 86% of its no-TAA brightness against 48%; WebGPU and the WebGL2
  layer), and `packages/taa/test/reactive-mask.test.js` (the demand signal and the shared target).
- **Local lights lit froxel fog undimmed by the fog on their path (environment).** Repro: Storm Light tour view t2
  (`view=10,34,26,-6,30,-4&beam=2.5`): 5.9% of the right sky at 255 along the beam. Cause: `localLight` in
  `volumetric.ts` left out the transmittance from the light to the sample. Fix: exp(-extinction x distance) with the
  sample's extinction. Regression: `npm run test:fog-beam:browser` (its reference now dims the light along the path;
  L1 0.014, 0.575 without the fix). Storm Light's fog round the tower was also three times heavy rain's extinction;
  with both fixed, t2 clips only at the lens.
- **Whitecaps read as grey blotches (water).** Cause: a soft 0.12 edge and at most 0.6 foam away from the crest core.
  Fix: a 0.04 edge, 0.9 foam through the cap with bubble holes. Regression: `packages/water/test/whitecaps.browser.mjs`
  (38.1% of the foam within a quarter of its brightest; 16.1% before).
- **No spray where swell hits a cliff or stack in deep water (water).** Cause: spray was born only on shallow
  breakers. Fix: `impact()` throws soft, small clumps up a wall where the swell's orbital velocity drives into it.
  Regression: the stack case of `packages/water/test/flow.browser.mjs` (1,461 clumps rising 1.88 m; none before).
- **The moon was a flat grey disc with no glow through the deck (sky).** Cause: the clouds took no forward
  diffraction lobe of the moon, and Storm Light's disc was dimmer than its own cloud. Fix: a 0.5 x HG lobe in the
  moon's first octave; the disc as bright over the night sky as the moon is. Regression: the `volumetric` case of
  `features-check.mjs` (glow inner 38.6 against outer 11.9; 1.13 before).

### Fixed 2026-11-13: the volumetric cloud deck is missing from the sky's reflection map and scene light (sky, lane S1g)

- **Repro:** `examples/storm-light` before 2026-11-13 S1g (night zenith `[0.004, 0.007, 0.016]`, night ambient
  `[0.02, 0.026, 0.04]`), 1920x1080, `?tour=0&storm=0.78`. The moonlit `VolumetricClouds` deck fills the sky at a
  mean luma of about 95, yet the near sea measures 1.7 and the cliffs 0.4 (with the volumetric fog off): the water
  reflects `sky.reflectionTexture` and `lighting.ambient` lights the meshes from the same 64 x 32 map, and both show
  only the stylized night gradient behind the deck.
- **Cause:** `packages/sky/src/reflection.ts` fills the map from `skyEnvironment` (the day model, `night` and the
  sky's own 2D `clouds`); `VolumetricClouds` reads that map to light itself but never writes into it, so nothing that
  reflects or takes sky light sees the deck.
- **Fix:** `VolumetricClouds` march their deck from the camera into a 64 x 32 map in the sky's layout each frame (four
  rays a texel, the view's own light, moon and flash) and hand it to the sky as `Sky.environmentLayer`. The sky draws
  its reflection map clear at order 2, where the clouds take their own light from it, and again with the deck over it
  at 3.5, before Water reflects it at 4; its `lighting` map takes the deck before the mips and harmonics. Coverage 0
  and `dispose()` take the layer back. Storm Light drops its stand-ins: the night zenith and night sky light are back
  to `[0.004, 0.007, 0.016]` and `[0.02, 0.026, 0.04]`, and a flash no longer raises the sky light floor.
- **Regression:** the `volumetric` case of `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs` (sky's test:gpu; passes on WebGPU
  and on the WebGL2 layer): the map is the sky through the deck plus the deck's light, texel for texel; a dense deck
  changes the upper half and leaves the lower half alone; a flash in the deck brightens the map (upper mean 1.72 to
  25.3) and a pillar lit only by the sky light (0.254 to 0.358; 0.227 with no clouds); coverage 0 and dispose give
  the plain map back exactly. Before the fix it fails: the map never changes with the clouds.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: offset, shell and draft refused a half torus made by a Boolean (brep)

- **Repro:** cut a torus in half with `model.boolean` (a box whose face runs through the axis) and pass the body to
  `model.offsetFaces`, `model.shell` or `model.draft` in `@margoengine/brep`: a `RangeError` said the edge is a
  spline. The same for a frustum cut through its axis.
- **Cause:** two. The Boolean's intersections (`packages/brep/src/model/intersect.ts`) had no closed form for a plane
  through the axis of a torus or a cone, so their meridians (two circles, two lines through the apex) were traced as
  splines; and the offset core (`resurface` in `packages/brep/src/model/offset.ts`) re-solved only line and circle
  edges, so a spline edge, or a circle whose faces move apart into another curve (a cut plane moved off the axis: a
  shell moves every face), was refused.
- **Fix:** `planeThroughAxis` gives those meridians exactly: circles of the minor radius centred the major radius
  either side of the axis, and the two generator lines crossing at the apex. `resurface` keeps a line or circle where
  the moved faces still meet in one, and otherwise traces the moved faces' own intersection (`intersectSurfaces` in a
  box round the old edge, padded by four times the largest move), takes the curve through both new ends nearest the old
  edge, keeps its stretch between them, and checks it on both faces as before.
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/offset-curved.test.js`: `offset, shell and draft: a torus and a frustum cut in
  half by a Boolean through their axis` (the meridians are circles; the tube thinned, the cut planes moved out, a 0.5 mm
  hollow and wall, and a draft of the cut planes, each `checkBody` clean, against the exact volumes, the torus past a
  plane by quadrature of its tube; the frustum's lines, its thinned side against the closed form, a shell and a draft)
  and `a quarter torus ... its end moved off the axis cuts the tube anew` (was a refusal; the volume against the
  quadrature). Both fail on the code before.
- **Found beside it, open:** a plane through a cylinder's or a frustum's seam line (the box face along the primitive's
  x axis) makes the Boolean throw "a loop does not bound a region on its left" (`boolean` of `cylinder('y', 5 mm,
  8 mm)` less a box whose -y face is the plane y = 0 through the axis); turned off the seam it cuts cleanly. Fixed
  2026-11-15, below.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a Boolean whose cutting plane holds a cylinder's or a cone's seam line throws (brep)

- **Repro:** `model.boolean('h', 'subtract', model.cylinder('y', 5 * mm, 8 * mm), model.box('b', [30 * mm, 15 * mm,
  30 * mm], model.frameOf([-15 * mm, 0, -15 * mm], [0, 0, 1], [1, 0, 0])))` in `@margoengine/brep`: RangeError
  "splitting face b/face:-y: a loop does not bound a region on its left". The same with `cone`; the box turned 0.5 rad
  about z cut both cleanly.
- **Cause:** `curveSurfaceCrossings` (`packages/brep/src/model/distance.ts`) took an interval whose ends and middle
  lie on the surface for a stretch lying on it, and returned no crossing. An end circle of the primitive starts and ends
  at its seam vertex, so against the plane y = 0 (which holds the seam and the axis) its start, its middle (half a turn
  round, where it crosses the plane) and its end all lie on the plane: the circles were never cut at x = -r, so the
  other line the plane cuts from the side found no stops and the -y face kept only the seam, a loop round nothing. It
  showed only where the rounding at the circle's end fell on the face's side of the plane (the box's -y face, not a
  plane facing +y).
- **Fix:** that shortcut now also needs the curve unable to bend further from the surface than the resolution over the
  interval (the bound on the distance's second derivative the search already has, k w^2 / 8); otherwise the interval
  is halved as any other.
- **Regression:** `Booleans whose cutting plane holds a cylinder's or a cone's seam line: cut along it` in
  `packages/brep/tests/boolean.test.js`: the circle against a plane through its start and centre facing either way
  crosses it once, at half a turn; a cylinder, a frustum and a cone to its apex, less and in common with a box above and
  one below the plane, each `checkBody` clean and half the exact volume to 1e-9. Before the fix the circle facing
  -y finds no crossing and every Boolean throws.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the validity check flags the body of one fuzz file although its volume is right (brep)

- **Repro:** the kernel's fuzz case `m162.step` (a damaged copy of the 80 x 50 x 8 mm plate of
  `packages/brep/tests/fixtures/step`) through `bodiesFromSTEP` and `checkBody` in `@margoengine/brep`: `checkBody`
  reports a problem while the mass volume matches the file's own 32000 mm3.
- **Cause:** the body is at fault and the check is right. The fuzzer pointed the top face `#70` at the plane `#74` (y = 0,
  the front face's) in place of its own `#47` (z = 8 mm); its edges `#56`, `#61` and `#66` run up to 50 mm off y = 0,
  and `#51` lies in it. The volume is right because `massProperties` integrates, besides each face, strips from each edge's
  foot on its face to the edge (a tolerant edge's gap counts), so it is the volume the edges bound. One flaw was in the
  report: `validateBody` (`packages/brep/src/model/validate.ts`) gave an edge's offset at its first sample past the
  tolerance, 12.5 mm for `#56` and `#66` (a quarter of the way from the end on the plane), not the 50 mm they reach.
- **Fix:** the report gives the most the edge's samples are off its face.
- **Regression:** `STEP: a face on the wrong surface is flagged, each edge by the most it is off, while its volume
  follows its edges` in `packages/brep/tests/step-malformed.test.js` (the fuzz case made from the plate fixture by its two
  changes): exactly those three edges, each 5.00e-2 m off, the same in the import's problems, the volume 32000 mm3, and
  the plate with its own top clean. Before the fix `#56` and `#66` read 1.25e-2 m.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: IGES parametric spline surfaces (entity 114) were refused; their coefficient order was not checked (brep)

- **Repro:** an IGES 5.3 file with a parametric spline surface (entity 114) through `parseIGES` or `igesToSTEP` in
  `@margoengine/brep`: the 114 was refused with `MargoError` code `unsupported` (beside other surfaces, left out and
  named in `warnings`).
- **Cause:** the reader was written without the text of the 114 formula, so it did not know which power of s and t
  each of the 16 coefficients per coordinate multiplies, nor how the patches are laid out, and refused the entity.
- **Fix:** read from the specification's section 4.15 (Parametric Spline Surface Entity) and Appendix B.5 (Spline
  Surfaces), in the text of the IGES 6.0 draft of 1998-01-05, which keeps the 5.3 entity unchanged: X(u, v) = AX + s BX
  + s^2 CX + s^3 DX + t EX + t s FX + t s^2 GX + t s^3 HX + t^2 KX + ... + t^3 s^3 SX for s = u - TU(i), t = v - TV(j)
  (s fastest, letters I, J and O skipped); per patch the 16 X, then Y, then Z coefficients; patch (i, j) from parameter
  7 + M + N + 48 ((i - 1)(N + 1) + j - 1), the (N + 1)-th patch of each row and the (M + 1)-th row placeholders to
  ignore. `polynomialSurface` (`packages/brep/src/iges/shapes.ts`) turns each patch's power basis over its rectangle
  into a bicubic Bezier patch (b_r = sum C(r, k) / C(3, k) c_k h^k in each direction) and joins them in one B-spline
  surface with knots of multiplicity 3 at the breakpoints, so the surface and its parameters are exact. Patches that part
  on a shared edge by more than the file's tolerance are refused as malformed (the specification's surface is
  continuous); within it the net takes their mean.
- **Regression:** `packages/brep/tests/iges.test.js`: `a parametric spline surface (114) reads exactly, its
  coefficients in the order section 4.15 gives` (x = u, y = v, z = u^2 v^3 over 2 x 2 patches of unequal sizes, written
  as each patch's Taylor coefficients: every mesh vertex on z = x^2 y^3 to float32 rounding, the box, the area against
  Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the exact surface within 1e-3, and the STEP knots) and `... whose patches part on a
  shared edge is refused, and left out beside others`. Both fail on the code before (the refusal).
- **Source:** IGES/PDES Organization, "Initial Graphics Exchange Specification IGES 5.3", US PRO/IPO-100-1996, section
  4.15 and Appendix B.5; the same sections in "IGES 6.0 draft", 1998-01-05.

### Accepted 2026-11-15: the Orrery draws a different picture on the WebGL2 compatibility layer (depth resolve)

- **Repro:** `npm run build:packages && npm run build:site && node scripts/visual-compat.mjs --no-build --only=orrery`
  (RTX A6000, Edge 157.0.4341.60, 2026-11-16 at 26e0d25c81): `differs (d>2 3.54%, mean 0.454, max 80; native noise
  d>2 0.23%, mean 0.0721)`. The difference lights the geometry edges (arms, rings, gears, dome rim, bookcase) and a
  ring round the lamp.
- **Cause:** the PostStack's 1x depth, which `ContactShadows` and `DOF` read, is filled differently on the two
  backends. Native WebGPU keeps the nearest of each pixel's four MSAA samples (`depthCopy` in
  `packages/shared/msaa.js`); the WebGL2 layer cannot read single samples (GLSL ES 3.00 has no multisample sampler), so
  its resolved depth is sample 0, at (-0.125, -0.375) px from the pixel centre. A silhouette pixel the object only
  partly covers then holds the background depth on the layer and the object's depth natively. DOF's WebGL2 route
  (`packages/dof/src/compat.ts`) takes the nearest depth of each pixel and its four neighbours to put those pixels
  back on the object; it narrows the gap (all effects 3.11% with it, 3.51% without) but cannot rebuild the samples.
- **Scott's ruling (2026-11-15):** an accepted difference. Native keeps the nearest-of-4 depth, which keeps every
  partly covered silhouette pixel on its object for DOF, contact shadows, SSAO and TAAUpscale; the layer keeps sample
  0; the native resolve does not change.
- **Measured** (`.lane` runtime switches, 1280 x 720 high view, d > 2; the native run-to-run noise of each method in
  brackets). Free running, as the visual check captures: all effects 3.48%, DOF's layer widening off 3.81%, DOF off
  3.01% (noise 0.33%, max d 241). With TAAUpscale's jitter phase held (`taa.frame` set to 0 every frame), which
  removes that noise: all effects 3.11%, widening off 3.51%, DOF off 2.26% (noise 0.00%, max d 1). A probe build
  whose native `depthCopy` keeps sample 0 like the layer (never landed): all effects 1.24%, widening off 0.00% (mean
  0.022, max d 4), DOF off 0.00% (max d 10), phase held (free running 1.53%, noise 0.29%). With the same depth on both
  sides the Orrery is within the parity rule, so DOF adds no difference of its own: its share is the layer-only
  widening, which answers the same resolve. The contact-shadow acne fix ("contact shadows drew dithered acne", above)
  does not touch this cause.
- **Ruled out:** a one-sided neighbourhood for the widening (the pixel, +x and +y: the side of samples 1 and 3, away
  from sample 0). On the Orrery it measured 3.00% against the four neighbours' 3.11% (phase held), but it fails
  `packages/dof/tests/gpu/compat-check.mjs` on the RTX A6000: the `focus` case goes from 0.009% to 0.217% of pixels
  with d > 2 and `tilt` from 0.024% to 0.107%, past the 0.1% parity rule; the four neighbours pass every case. The
  opposite side (-x, -y) measured 3.50%, as with no widening.
- **Native noise:** the two native captures differ because the page keeps drawing and TAAUpscale's output cycles
  through its 8 jitter phases (Halton 2, 3) with the camera still, so the captures land on different phases (d > 2 on
  0.23% to 0.36%, max d up to 241 on small specular highlights). The date and the animation clock are held (the date
  by `?date=`, reduced motion stops the planets). Holding the jitter phase or switching `temporal` off on the same page
  leaves max d 1 four seconds apart. This is the jittered accumulation residue `docs/limits.md` states for TAAUpscale,
  so the Orrery is recorded without an exact still frame.
- **Pinned by:** `scripts/support/visual-compat-expected.json` (orrery `differs`, 3.54%, mean 0.454, no exact still
  frame), `tests/visual-compat-status.test.js` "the orrery is recorded as the depth-resolve difference and fails the
  gate if it gets worse", and the accepted-difference section of
  [webgl2-compat-demos.md](webgl2-compat-demos.md#accepted-difference-per-sample-reads-of-multisampled-textures).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: lines-perspective named a pre-rebase commit, so proofs-golden failed on every clone but one

- **Repro:** on any clone of main at 9bd835e909, `node --test tests/proofs-golden.test.js` failed "every commit a stored
  baseline names resolves" with `lines-perspective: b6e6955f50`.
- **Cause:** the round cap fix was captured at `b6e6955f50` and then rebased onto main as `a63f7433a1`. The old id still
  resolved in the checkout that made it, so the check passed there; resolving is not the same as being on main. The
  same slip happened before (5d701a3f6c).
- **Fix:** the proof and its baseline name `a63f7433a1`, captured again with byte-identical outputs. The test now asks
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD` for every named commit, so an amended or rebased-away commit fails in the
  checkout that still holds it. Regression: `tests/proofs-golden.test.js`, "every commit a stored baseline names is in
  the history of HEAD" (an amended commit that still resolves is reported). Run it after the final rebase.

### Fixed 2026-11-14: a golden capture on a clone without the pre-rewrite history emptied the stored baselines (lane BB3)

- **Repro:** on a clone that lacks the pre-rewrite commits, `node examples/package-benchmarks/proofs/capture.mjs
  --only=color-output,post-stack` printed FAIL and "nothing was stored", yet both `baselines/*.json` (and `.gz`)
  now held the new ref with no outputs and no facts.
- **Cause:** color-output's `ignoreAgx` fact asks Git for eaddd64 and post-stack builds creative at 5b1fe66^; for a
  commit the clone lacks, `history.js` printed HISTORICAL and exited 0, and `golden.js`'s exit hook, seeing exit 0 in
  capture mode, stored what had been captured by then: nothing.
- **Fix:** while capturing (`strict.capture`, set by `golden.js` `begin`), a missing commit throws, so the run fails
  and the stored baseline stays byte for byte. Regression: `tests/proofs-golden.test.js`, "a capture that needs a
  commit this clone lacks fails and leaves the stored baseline as it was". Lane BB4 then moved every commit those proofs
  (and math-consolidation and selection-xray-off) asked for to its id on main, so every clone can capture them; a test
  in the same file fails when a stored baseline names a commit that does not resolve (claims.md, 2026-11-14).

### Fixed 2026-11-14: DOF near field drew stepped blocks along a bright surface far in front of focus (lane S2)

- **Repro:** `examples/orrery/index.html` on the Radeon 680M (WebGPU, 1920x1080), camera
  `orrery.controls.transitions.setLookAt([1.3, 0.52, 0.66], [-0.06, 0.24, 0], {duration: 0})`, then
  `orrery.focus.options.target = [0, 0.33, 0]; orrery.dof.options.aperture = 2.2`. The brass calendar ring at the
  front left, well in front of the focus and lit by the window, shows hard steps about 8 px tall along its outer edge
  and round its engraved ticks instead of a smooth blur. The same steps show with TAAUpscale disposed; with
  `orrery.dof.enabled = false` the ring is clean.
- **Cause (isolated 2026-11-13 on a CPU model of the gather):** the near and far gathers read a fixed spiral of 64 taps
  from the sharp scene, so a wide disk is a sparse kernel: over a 32 px `maxRadius` the taps stand about 7 px apart,
  and a sharp edge blurred through it carries the kernel's staircase along the edge. A CPU copy of `cocShader` and the
  full-resolution `bokehShader` on a bright plane receding in front of focus, with a slanted edge, gives the blurred
  edge's position per row second differences up to 7 px (mean 1.2); the same model with 4,096 taps gives at most 1
  (mean 0.58). Ruled out: the 8x8 workgroup's `nearMax` tap count (all 64 taps at every pixel give the same image, as
  the shader comment argues) and, mostly, the 1% depth band (no band: max 5, mean 1.0). Taps read from a copy of the
  scene pre-blurred by half the tap spacing give max 3 (mean 0.66).
- **Done here:** the Orrery focuses on its mechanism at f/4, where the ring's blur stays small; nothing in the dof
  package changed.
- **Needed to close:** a prefiltered tap source (a depth-aware downsampled scene whose texel matches the tap spacing,
  read at the level of the disk) for the near and far gathers, with a GPU check in `packages/dof` that measures this
  staircase (largest second difference of the blurred edge per row) on a receding plane. It changes every wide-disk
  DOF picture, so the dof proofs advance and DOF picture baselines are re-recorded.
- **Fix (`d9c965dc7`, lanes BB2, BB3 and BB4; levels blended in the shader in `40dcf8a22`, lane DF1):** the near pass writes a
  4-mip chain (premultiplied colour and weight, radius and depth, scene) at the gather's size, and each 8x8 tile spreads
  its 64 taps over the largest near disk reaching it, read at the two whole levels around the tap spacing's level and blended in the shader, so every sampler draws it as
  the WebGL2 layer does. Regression:
  `packages/dof/tests/near-steps.test.js` (the CPU model's per-row second difference of the blurred edge: at most 1
  step, lens 2; its small-disk case fails on the old code) and the GPU `lens-check` receding case. The far gather was
  measured free of steps by the same model (max 2 against the dense 1) and is unchanged. color-output and post-stack
  advanced to `40dcf8a22` (claims.md); the dof visual baselines were re-recorded for amd-rdna-2 and are owed on the
  other GPU profiles.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the sciviz bricks weight-model bound depended on the GPU's sin

- **What:** `packages/sciviz/tests/bricks-browser.js` check "each hardware-filtered march stays within the 8-bit weight
  model of exact filtering" failed on a Radeon 680M (native WebGPU) and on an Apple M6 under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (the
  WebGL2 layer, Chrome, ANGLE Metal): bound 3, hardware 4 on both marches (M6: whole 841, bricked 843 of 172,800 pixels
  differ from exact). Native WebGPU on the M6 passed. Every other brick check passed.
- **Cause:** the bound, not the filter. The bound was the largest difference one sign pattern of the test-only weight
  model (filter mode 2: every axis weight one 1/256 step off) makes from exact filtering, and the sign came from
  `fract(sin(dot(x, k)) * 43758.5453)` with arguments near 5,000 radians. WGSL bounds `sin` (absolute error 2^-11) only
  inside [-pi, pi] and GLSL ES 3.00 states no accuracy for it at all, so each GPU and each shader translation drew its
  own pattern (the 680M matched a double-precision CPU evaluation at only 51 to 53% of 262,144 positions). And one
  random pattern's largest difference is not the model's worst: over 16 patterns it ranges from 3 to 8 on the same
  picture, so a GPU whose pattern landed low failed a filter that was closer to exact than the A6000's (4 against 6).
- **Fix:** `filterSign` in `packages/sciviz/src/volume.ts` (shared by the whole and bricked marches) floors the
  position to the 1/256 sub-texel grid (a power-of-two scale, exact in float) and hashes it with pcg3d (Jarzynski and
  Olano, "Hash Functions for GPU Rendering", JCGT 9(3), 2020, https://jcgt.org/published/0009/03/02/), whose wrapping
  u32 arithmetic WGSL and GLSL ES 3.00 both specify exactly; the pipeline constant `filterSeed` picks the pattern. The
  check takes as its bound the worst over 16 patterns, not one sample. Same tight model on every GPU: on the M6 the 16
  per-pattern maxima are identical natively and on the WebGL2 layer (whole 7, 4, 4, 3, 4, 3, 4, 3, 4, 3, 8, 4, 3, 3,
  6, 3), bound 8, hardware 4 on both backends. The bound was not raised by hand; it is the model's measured worst.
- **Regression:** new check "the weight model draws the same sign pattern as the CPU on this GPU" draws the march's own
  `filterSign` source at 262,144 probe positions for three seeds and requires all 786,432 signs per seed to equal a CPU
  evaluation. With the former `sin` pattern against its double-precision CPU evaluation it fails on the M6 natively
  (385,473 of 786,432 signs differ per seed); with pcg3d it passes natively and on the WebGL2 layer (0 differ). Run:
  `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/sciviz/tests/bricks-browser.mjs`, with and without
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1`.

### Fixed 2026-11-12 in `f0004d6c8e`: probe reflections over-blurred roughness below 0.2; probes-gpu "mirror floor vs walls" p95 4/255 (KB-A3c)

- **What:** `examples/package-benchmarks/probes-gpu.mjs` check 4 compares each mirror floor pixel with the wall its
  reflected ray hits, p95 within 3/255. With Scott's ruling (option a, tolerance kept) the truth is the room radiance
  seen from the floor point, GGX-prefiltered at the floor's real roughness (core's 0.045 floor) times the split-sum
  weight 0.975 (`examples/package-benchmarks/parts/probe-truth.mjs`, test `tests/probes-wall-truth.test.js`). The
  check then failed on the Radeon 680M: median 1, p95 4, p99 7, max 9/255 over 2657 pixels, while the GPU matched the
  CPU mirror of the WGSL within 1/255.
- **Repro (before the fix):** `node examples/package-benchmarks/probes-gpu.mjs`:
  `FAIL mirror floor vs walls: p95 4/255`.
- **Cause:** `probeRadiance` in `packages/environment/src/probes.ts` read lod `roughness * (levels - 1)` and mixed the
  two levels around it linearly in roughness. A 128 probe has 6 levels prefiltered at roughness 0, 0.2, 0.4, ..., so
  0.045 (GGX alpha 0.002) took 22.5 % of the level prefiltered at 0.2 (alpha 0.04): a lobe about 20 times too wide,
  pulling neighbouring wall colours into every probe-lit surface below roughness 0.2.
- **Fix (`f0004d6c8e`):** the levels and their prefilter are unchanged (same texel layout, bake and live refresh); the
  lookup still reads each level alone at its own roughness but blends the two around a roughness by GGX alpha, the
  lobe width: weight `(x^2 - k^2) / (2k + 1)` in level units x. 0.045 now takes 5.06 % of the 0.2 level. WebGPU and
  the WebGL2 layer run the same WGSL. A CPU model of the room probe (300 directions per roughness) put the mean
  error against a true GGX prefilter at 0.0117 (was 0.0224) at roughness 0.045, 0.0123 (0.026) at 0.1, 0.0109
  (0.0194) at 0.15 and within 0.002 of before from 0.25 to 0.9; squared level spacing also passed check 4 but doubled
  the error from 0.25 up, and cubed spacing failed check 4 (p95 6). probes-gpu's CPU mirror reads the same blend (`probeLevelBlend` in probe-truth.mjs).
- **Test:** `tests/probes-level-blend.test.js` pins the WGSL to that blend and models check 4 on the CPU (the old blend
  gives p95 above 3/255, the new one within it). The environment-hemisphere proof advanced to `f0004d6c8e`.
- **Measured after the fix (Radeon 680M, WebGPU, 2026-11-12):** mirror floor vs walls median 0, p95 1, p99 1, max
  2/255 over 2657 pixels (2406 near wall edges skipped); GPU vs CPU mirror median 0, p95 1, max 1 on the diffuse,
  mirror and rough floors; probes-live-gpu passes. No stored picture baseline holds a probe-lit surface, so none was
  re-recorded and none is owed by the dev PC.

### Fixed 2026-11-13 in `97bd9b4818`: Environment IBL and the materials envMap blended prefiltered mips linearly in roughness (KB-A3e)

- **What:** the KB-A3c over-blur, in the other prefiltered-mip lookups. `iblPrefiltered` in
  `packages/environment/src/ibl.ts` sampled `textureSampleLevel(..., roughness * (mips - 1))` with mip m prefiltered
  at roughness m / (mips - 1), so hardware trilinear mixed the two mips linearly in roughness: with 6 mips, 0.045
  took 22.5 % of the 0.2 mip. It also feeds LightProbes' environment fallback, EnvironmentLighting's clearcoat and
  post's SSR replacement. `packages/materials/src/env-map.ts` read the same `roughness * (levels - 1)` lookup for
  standard shading and the clearcoat.
- **Cause:** blending in roughness instead of GGX alpha (see KB-A3c).
- **Fix (`97bd9b4818`):** both lookups read `lod = k + (x^2 - k^2) / (2k + 1)`, `x = roughness * (mips - 1)`,
  `k = min(floor(x), max(mips - 2, 0))` (`iblPrefiltered`, materials' `margoEnvLod`), so the trilinear mix of the two
  mips equals the material's alpha; 0.045 now takes 5.06 % of the 0.2 mip. The mips, their prefilter and every saved
  environment are unchanged. The WebGL2 layer runs the same WGSL (no GLSL twin). Regression:
  `packages/environment/tests/ibl-level-blend.test.js` and `packages/materials/test/env-map.test.js` ("reads its mips
  by GGX alpha"), which pin the WGSL and check that each mip is read alone at its own roughness and the mixed alpha
  equals roughness squared. Picture baselines holding Environment-lit low-roughness surfaces move with it and are owed
  on their recording machine.
- **Sky, checked and left:** `packages/sky/src/lighting.ts` reads its 64 x 32 light map at `rough * 3.0`, but its levels
  are box downsamples of one render, not GGX prefilters at roughness m / 3, so the alpha blend has no prefilter
  roughness to match. How well its level widths follow GGX lobe widths is not measured.

### Fixed 2026-11-12 outside core, 2026-11-14 in core: direct diffuse weighted by the metal-mixed Fresnel outside gltf/pbr (KB3240b, found 2026-11-12)

- **What:** glTF 2.0 Appendix B defines material = mix(dielectric_brdf, metal_brdf, metallic); only the dielectric has a
  diffuse lobe, weighted by 1 minus the dielectric Fresnel (F0 0.04). gltf/pbr's base direct light was fixed for this in
  864051383 (KB3240, MetalRoughSpheresNoTextures MAE 1.7865 to 0.6997), but the other copies of the direct light wrote
  `(1 - F(mix(0.04, base, metallic))) * (1 - metallic) * base / pi`, which darkens every part-metal surface (at
  metallic 5/6 the smooth diffuse is half the spec's).
- **Cause:** the KB3240 fix was made in gltf/pbr only; the other copies of the same direct light kept the old weight.
- **Fixed 2026-11-12 outside core (hunt K1):** every non-core site weights the diffuse by 1 minus the dielectric Fresnel
  `0.04 + 0.96 (1 - vh)^5`: `packages/shared/light-terms.js` `clusterBrdf` (clustered's point, spot and extra
  directional loops; materials, shader and rigging key on its text; voxel's sun), `packages/animation/src/vat.ts` (unlit
  and lit), `packages/lod/src/imposter.ts`, `packages/post/src/material-decals.ts` and
  `packages/webgl2-compat/src/preview.ts`. `clusterBrdf` takes the dielectric F0 and F90 its loop already has, so a
  KHR_materials_specular or IOR F0 weighs the diffuse by its largest channel, as gltf/pbr's physical shader does.
  Regression tests run each shipped text on the CPU against the specification's mix (a head-on part-metal case has the
  closed form ((1 - metal) 0.96 base + F0 / 4) / pi: 0.0978817 at base 0.5, metal 0.5, against 0.0795775 before):
  packages/clustered/test/metal-mix.test.js, packages/animation/tests/vat-metal-mix.test.js,
  packages/lod/test/imposter-metal-mix.test.js, packages/post/test/material-decals-metal-mix.test.js,
  packages/webgl2-compat/test/preview-metal-mix.test.js, packages/voxel/tests/metal-mix.test.js (helper
  tests/support/metal-mix.js). Clustered's sampling-text pins and materials' GGX loop text moved with the BRDF text
  (the clustered sampling text with the old BRDF text put back hashes to the old pins); six --current proofs advance.
  Landed: fix 1fdb55908, proof advance 8d6b26b84 (size budgets of materials mips and skin moved 4 and 10 bytes with
  the reason). GPU on the AMD mini PC, WebGPU and compat: clustered, animation, lod, post, voxel, materials and
  webgl2-compat (test:gpu with its path tracer step excluded by profile, see 1974f0bc0) 100 of 100 runs pass.
- **Fixed 2026-11-14, core:** `packages/core/src/shaders.ts` writes w = 1 - (1 - vh)^5, F = 1 - (1 - F0) w and the
  diffuse weight 0.96 w, so a part-metal core mesh matches the same surface lit by a clustered light, a material decal

  `packages/core/tests/metal-mix.test.js` (fails on the old text: the head-on case gives 0.0795775).

### Fixed 2026-11-20: Vite test servers keep the HMR socket, and a failed one fails the test (AMD GPU hunt R7 row 38)

- **Repro:** on the AMD mini PC, with two other helpers testing, `decoders test:browser` (packages/decoders/scripts/test-browser.js)
  failed once with page console errors only: `WebSocket connection to 'ws://127.0.0.1:61962/?token=...' failed: ...
  net::ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE`, then `ws://127.0.0.1:0/` `net::ERR_UNSAFE_PORT` and `[vite] failed to connect to websocket`.
  Every decoder check passed; it passes alone. Not AMD and not time.
- **Cause:** the script starts its Vite dev server with `server: { port: 0 }` and HMR on, which the test never uses.
  Windows refused the socket (WSAENOBUFS: the machine was out of socket buffer space), Vite's client then retried on the
  configured port 0, which Chromium refuses, and the test counts every console error. The same pattern (a Vite
  `createServer` with HMR on) is in the browser scripts of audio, bvh, controls (3), creative, decoders (4), environment,
  exporters (3), html, labels, lines, loaders (2), mesh-edit, mixer, physics (2), points, post (4), taa (8) and text (3);
  `scripts/browser.js` keeps its socket on purpose (it counts full reloads).
- **Fix:** every package browser script that starts a Vite server (44 of them, found by a search of `packages/`) now passes
  `server: { host: '127.0.0.1', port: ..., hmr: false, watch: null }`, as cache's, the README runner's and the visual suites'
  servers have; `scripts/browser.js` keeps its socket on purpose and is not touched.
- **Regression:** `tests/vite-test-servers-no-hmr.test.js` fails on any package script that imports Vite's `createServer`
  without `hmr: false`.

### Fixed 2026-11-12: Radeon 680M, biomes flythrough on the WebGL2 layer took 0.5 to 0.75 s a frame (AMD GPU hunt row 34)

- **Repro:** on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, Chromium with ANGLE D3D11),
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 MARGO_MACHINE_PROFILE=mini-pc node packages/biomes/tests/flythrough-check.mjs` passed every
  scheduling check, then was ended by its own 15 minute limit after 916 s; it needs about 2,000 frames and could not
  fit the 12.5 minute (750 s) suite limit. On WebGPU it passes in 286 s. Not a hang: the cost was the same every frame.
- **Fixed on the way:** `183a68ed1` checkFramebufferStatus ran on every per-frame framebuffer attach (14.9 of 15.7 s of a
  CPU profile); `b6f23290c` a command that runs past its time limit now prints the limit before it is ended.
- **Cause (webgl2-compat):** counted per frame with page hooks on the layer (hunt worktree `.lane/diag/fly-count6.mjs`):
  1,140 texSubImage2D (1,138 from `CompatBindGroup.storageTexture()`, 863 MB) and 362 readPixels (288 MB). Each bind
  group kept its own storage texture and copied every changed storage buffer whole into it out of the GL buffer
  (PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER): 756 binding uploads a frame for 295 buffer versions, since the ScatterTiles rings and the
  ordered cull's buffers (up to 12.8 MB) are rewritten by compute every frame and read by 2 to 6 groups each; and every
  compute write was first read back into its GL buffer (readPixels into a pack buffer), only to go up again.
- **Fix:** `5fddb9daa`. A storage buffer's data texture is its mirror, brought up to date once per version however many
  groups read it; groups copy their rows from it texture to texture (copyTexSubImage2D, rows laid out so a binding
  copies in at most three rectangles). A compute write to a buffer of one word texture is drawn straight into the data
  texture, and the GL buffer is read back from it only when something reads the GL buffer itself (`CompatBuffer.gl`:
  vertex, index, uniform, indirect, copies, mapping, CPU writes). Same flight after: 6 to 10 texSubImage2D, 14
  readPixels (the indirect commands and copies) and 986 copyTexSubImage2D a frame; the check passes under compat in
  676 s alone, the limit unchanged. Regressions: `test/storage-mirror.test.js` (two groups reading one changed buffer
  upload it once, an unchanged one costs nothing; fails before: 4 uploads and no copies) and `compute-browser.mjs`
  `mirrorReads` (a compute write read by two groups' dispatches: no readPixels while they run; fails before).
- **Tried, not landed:** ScatterTiles drawing counted (lane H2) removed the indirect read-backs but added about 570 M
  vertex invocations a frame; it was not measured again after the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-12: the voxel path tracer's tiled capture test flaked on a loaded machine (KB-L4-vpt)

- **What:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/tracer.test.js` "capture renders the requested size in tiles and encodes a
  PNG of the tone-mapped image" failed once during a CPU run beside GPU suites ("pixel 1024,1024 (tile seams must not
  show)", green 253 for 247) and passed alone on the same code.
- **Cause (the test's fake GPU, not the tracer):** the tracer splits each capture tile into row bands sized by the
  measured GPU (`Pacer` in `src/dispatch.ts`, from wall-clock submit times; bands change no pixel's sums) and writes the
  frame uniform before each band's submission, in queue order. The fake GPU filled a tile's whole read-back from the
  uniform as it stood at map time, the last band's, so when a slow, loaded run shrank the bands the second tile row
  read rows further down the image.
- **Fix:** the fake records the frame uniform at each submission and fills each band's rows from the uniform that band
  saw, as a GPU does. The test runs twice: with the paced bands, and with 8-row bands forced by the `voxelTraceWork`
  switch that browser-check's determinism case already uses.
- **Regression:** the forced-band run of that test in `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/tracer.test.js` fails every time
  with the old fake (pixel 0,0) and passes with the new one.

### Fixed 2026-11-17: six checks read as new fixed waits, so the fixed-wait test was red on main (KB-GLTF-FIXEDWAIT1, tests)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:files -- tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js` failed on main 2c034ac13f, one file at a time:

  by count); `packages/biomes/tests/view-clock.test.js` slept 400 ms for its tile jobs; the vfx and weather settings

  nothing may happen.
- **Fix:** the gltf check waits with `waitForPipelines` (scripts/support/gpu-ready.js) and reads the last frame; the

- **Regression:** `tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js` ("a helper that renders with its parameter as the delta...") fails

### Fixed 2026-11-11: toGraph was never compared with MaterialX, and a float image mixed by R, G, B and A apart (KB3108)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/loaders/tests/materialx-reference.test.js` on the old loaders: the `mix` fixture, a
  float image as the mix factor, was 215 of 255 sRGB codes from MaterialX's own bake of it.
- **Cause:** no MaterialX output was in the repository to compare with. Once it was, the `mix` case showed that a
  `float` image became a vec4 texture node, so a mix factor (or a roughness or metal input, which read G and B of a
  vec4) took each colour channel from a different image channel. MaterialX reads a float image's first channel.
- **Fix:** a texture node of `@margoengine/materials` takes `channel` (0 to 3), which reads that one component as a
  scalar, and `toGraph` sets `channel: 0` on every `float` image.
- **Reference:** eight of our own documents (image in sRGB and linear, multiply, add and subtract, mix by a float image,
  base weight, `gltf_image` into `gltf_pbr`, `UsdPreviewSurface`) on two generated 16 x 16 images, each baked to a
  texture by MaterialX 1.39.5's GLSL baker (`packages/loaders/tests/oracle/materialx-bake.py`, which rebuilds the
  fixtures byte for byte). On the CPU every converted graph matches its bake within 1 sRGB code on every texel; on the
  GPU the node material draws the source and the bake within 1 of 255 per channel (A6000, native and WebGL2 layer). The
  26 example materials of MaterialX v1.39.5 all convert, each skipping only named inputs with no node material slot.
- **Accepted difference:** the bake checks the graph (nodes, colour spaces, operand order), not the lit picture: the
  light and BSDF on both sides are Margo's, and no MaterialXView render is compared, so no lighting parity is claimed.
- **Regression:** packages/loaders/tests/materialx-reference.test.js (CPU), packages/loaders/tests/materialx-reference-check.mjs
  (in loaders `test:gpu`, native and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`), packages/materials/tests/nodes.test.js (texture channel).

### Firefox on Windows rejects a WGSL function named `dx` (browser defect, found 2026-11-11, open upstream)

Release exception: Firefox WGSL to HLSL keeps name dx (browser defect).

- **Repro:** in Playwright Firefox 157 on Windows (RTX A6000, headed, `dom.webgpu.enabled`), a render pipeline whose
  fragment module is `fn dx()->f32 {return 1.0;} @fragment fn f()->@location(0) vec4f {return vec4f(dx());}` fails
  with "DXC compile error: redefinition of 'dx' as different kind of symbol". `fn dy`, and a local `let dx` or
  `var dx`, compile. Chromium compiles all of them.
- **Cause:** Firefox's WGSL to HLSL step keeps the name `dx`, which DXC reserves as a namespace. Valid WGSL, so the
  defect is the browser's. No Margo package declares a WGSL function `dx` (checked over `packages/*/src`); the WebGL2
  layer's features check named its gradient helpers `dx` and `dy` and now names them `gx` and `gy`, as what it tests is
  the order the layer evaluates `textureSampleGrad`'s arguments in, not the browser's naming.
- **Next:** report it to Mozilla with the shader above; an app that hits it renames the function.
- **Upstream report (draft, nothing filed):** `docs/upstream-reports/KB0003/report.md` with the repro page `dx.html`; still reproduces in Firefox 157 on 2026-11-11 (Edge 157 compiles all five cases) and on 2026-11-27 (`fn dx` fails, the other four compile).

### Open: `MARGO_COMPAT=1` voxel-pathtracer steps cannot finish on ANGLE Direct3D 11, on main too; the serial compile is ANGLE's, proven 2026-11-25 (KB-L5a-10)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --no-build --keep-going
  --select=voxel-pathtracer/test:gpu:<step>` on the dev PC (RTX A6000, Edge 157) for the steps below. Under
  MARGO_COMPAT=1 the browser runs the WebGL2 layer over ANGLE Direct3D 11, the Windows default; a script's own
  `--use-angle=vulkan` leg runs over ANGLE Vulkan. Both trees launch the browser the same way (scripts/browser.js and
  scripts/lib/browser.mjs are identical), so every pair below ran on the same backends.

  at the same load. Per step: main, stack, cause.
  - `denoise` (600 s limit): main stopped at 607 s, stack at 608 s, both still in the first case's first 16384-sample
    reference. Cause: the reference's cost on the staged route (below).
  - `denoise-materials` (900 s): main still in its first reference after 758 s; the stack stopped at the limit in the
    3-slot gate. Cause: as `denoise`.
  - `denoise-caustics` (900 s): fails on both at the limit. Cause: as `denoise`.
  - `resampled` (600 s): main exits 1 at its limit with no output (KB-L5a-3, which the stack fixes); the stack passes
    both RIS legs, then its third part, the `viewport` lifecycle case with `?resampled=1`, is still running at the

  - `media` (in-page `renderImage` signal of 120 s): fails on both (main 83.7 s, stack 108 s of step time). Cause:

  - `sky` (60 s signals): fails on both in 2 of 2 paired runs (125 s and 137 s, the same second on each side); main

  - `mesh-lights` (300 s): main's in-page `page.evaluate` signal timed out after phase 1 of its lifecycle (228.7 s);
    the stack stopped at the limit at phase 5 (300.9 s). Cause: as `media`.
  - `mesh-pbr-lobes` (420 s): main gave no result at the limit; on the stack the 120 s signal fired at 355.6 s
    (KB5451's single filter call shortened the compile). Cause: as `media`. Passes since 2026-11-18 (3 min 53 s,
    KB-VPT-LOBES-COMPAT: the first render waited for a second compile of every program, now made before `ready`).
  - `mesh-pbr` (300 s): stopped at the limit on both (main 300.9 s alone, stack 301 s in the 3-slot gate), no
    result. Cause: as `media`.
  - `mesh-attributes`: the in-page signal times out on both (main 208.6 s). Cause: as `media`.
  - `mesh-instances` (120 s `renderImage` signal per image): three alternating rounds, CPU 44 to 93 % busy with other
    lanes: main FAIL 207.4 s, PASS 168.5 s, PASS 165.3 s; stack PASS 159.0 s, FAIL 198.0 s, FAIL 207.3 s. Every
    failure is the Direct3D 11 leg's first image, on both. Work counts for that image (a counting page, the same

    hash, 1,012 against 1,125 layer draws (the stack's 8 state pages of 7 layers, KB-L5a-4). Cold compile time summed
    over the programs, alternating main, stack, main, stack: 233, 280, 392 and 339 s. Cause: the first image waits
    for about 120 s of cold fxc compiles, right at its signal, and the machine's load decides; not a stack
    regression.
  - `mesh` (600 s): passes on both on a quiet GPU (280 s and 275 s) and failed in the gate beside other GPU jobs, a busy-machine
    time miss.
  - `denoise-ml` (180 s): main's in-page signal timed out at 175.5 s; the stack stopped at the limit. Cause: as
    `media`.
  - `stall`: fails on both while the first tracer compiles: main "the page did not answer within 30000 ms while the
    suite waited for its WGSL compilation reports" (69.4 s); the stack's 10 s stall limit fired at "compiling the
    tracer", 28 s into `denoise-diffuse`, before its first render. Cause: an fxc compile blocks the page and the GPU

    (KB-L5a-11, fixed). With the fix the stack's step passes on Direct3D 11 (277.9 s, limit 600 s).
- **Cause:** the step limits and in-page signals were sized on WebGPU and ANGLE Vulkan (A6000: `test:gpu:denoise`
  46 s, `denoise-materials` 99 s, `denoise-caustics` 109 s; the 2026-10-30 split above). On Direct3D 11 every staged

  `mesh-lights` (383 s) pass their checks but run past their 300 s step limits (dev PC, other lanes busy).
- **Progress 2026-11-19 (cheaper programs to compile, the same values):** fxc copies every call site and unrolls every
  loop it can count, and `shapeCut` (a cut-out shaped cell) ran three counted rounds of two half-block walks
  (`octWalk`, a loop of its own) and two texel reads, inside the voxel walk's loop; `march()` called `octWalk` from two

  and then each program's draw-time pixel shader compile (the warm draw, `LinkedProgram.warmed`) on the GPU process's
  one thread (`CrGpuMain`, 1.5 to 6.1 s each, one after another), while the page's thread waits 8.6 s inside a
  garbage-collector sweep task (`cppgc` IncrementalSweepTask, `CommandBufferHelper::Finish`) for that thread. So
  nothing the layer compiles or links blocks the page: the wait is Blink's collector behind ANGLE's draw-time
  compiles, and the 10 s stall limit then sees no finished pipeline for 13 s. Cheaper programs shorten it.

  - A Chrome trace of the denoise tracer's first compile (categories `gpu`, `blink.gc`, `toplevel`) showed the page's
    thread held 18.0 s in one `getUniformBlockIndex` (`ImplementationBase::GetBucketContents`,
    `CommandBufferHelper::Finish`): the layer read the next program's binding table, a synchronous call, while the GPU
    thread was compiling another program's warm draw. A linked program now reads its link status and binding table
    only once no other program's warm draw is on the GPU (`LinkedProgram.waiting`, packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts;
    the fences are polled without blocking). The same trace after: longest page-thread task 0.84 s (a 0.73 s collector
    sweep still waits in `CommandBufferHelper::Finish`). Regression: d3d11-warm.test.js "a linked program makes no

  each program's pixel shader at link on its worker threads with only `SV_TARGET0` in the output struct (fxc then drops
  the other outputs' code) and again, with all seven outputs, at the first draw on CrGpuMain, the browser's one GPU
  thread: 3.1, 5.8, 6.7, 5.1, 12.7 and 21.8 s for the denoise tracer's programs, one after another, 55 s in all. The
  two texts differ only in the output struct and its copies. A probe of 7-output programs (new text each run, three
  rounds) found no WebGL state that makes the link-time compile the one the draw uses: with nothing bound at link, with
  the 7-target framebuffer bound during `linkProgram`, and with one output array, the first draw took 28 to 31 ms and
  the second 1 to 2 ms every time. Splitting the programs into 1-output programs would let the link-time compile serve
  the draw but multiply the passes a sample (seven writes a page) and the compile work, so it was not done. With this
  serial compile, `test:gpu:stall`'s 10 s limit still fires in "compiling the tracer" (no pipeline finished for 10 s, 10
  pipelines compiling; the page now answers), and the three `denoise` steps' 16384-sample references cost the route's
  passes, not compiles. Sources: Khronos, "KHR_parallel_shader_compile" (WebGL extension, 2018),
  https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/extensions/KHR_parallel_shader_compile/ (link status is polled, the compile may
  finish later); Microsoft, "D3DCompile function", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3dcompiler/nf-d3dcompiler-d3dcompile ;
  Microsoft, "Semantics" (`SV_Target[n]` outputs of a pixel shader),
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-semantics ; The Chromium Projects,
  "GPU Command Buffer" (synchronous calls wait for the GPU process),
  https://www.chromium.org/developers/design-documents/gpu-command-buffer/ .
- **Proven below Margo 2026-11-25 (the draw-time compile; standalone repro, no Margo code):**
  `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs --max 10 -- node packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-mrt-compile-repro.mjs`
  (page `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-mrt-compile-repro.html`, raw WebGL2; options `--angle`, `--size`,
  `--programs`, `--trace=<file>`). It links three programs of new text at once (KHR_parallel_shader_compile, polled)
  and times each one's first and second draw (a 1-pixel `readPixels` after it). Intel Arc 140V laptop, Chrome 157:
  - ANGLE Direct3D 11: 1 output into 1 target, first draws 1,351, 373 and 166 ms (1.9 s in all; the compiles ran side
    by side at link and the first draw waits for them); 7 outputs into 7 targets, 1,921, 1,917 and 1,794 ms (5.6 s, one
    after another); the same 7-output programs drawn into 1 target, 1,506, 796 and 161 ms (like 1 output). Second
    draws 1 to 2 ms in every case.
  - ANGLE Vulkan, same machine and page: 3.13, 3.05 and 3.08 s in all for the three cases, the first program of each
    paying it and the other two 2 to 18 ms; more outputs cost nothing extra.
  - Its Chrome trace (`--trace`, category `gpu.angle`, whose D3DCompile events carry the HLSL as `source`): all nine
    links compile their pixel shader on ThreadPoolForegroundWorker with one `SV_TARGET` in the output struct (146 to
    169 ms each); only the three 7-target draws compile again, on CrGpuMain with seven `SV_TARGET` (169, 176 and
    206 ms). Those draws hold CrGpuMain about 1.9 s each, so most of their time is the driver building the new shader
    for the GPU at that draw, after fxc; both are behind ANGLE's draw-time compile.
  So the serial cost is ANGLE's Direct3D back end: it compiles at link for a default output layout of one render target
  and compiles again at the first draw for the layout of the bound targets, on the browser's one GPU thread. ANGLE's
  own design note says so (The ANGLE Project, "Dynamic Shader Compilation",
  https://chromium.googlesource.com/angle/angle/+/main/doc/DynamicShaderCompilation.md : "Changing render target
  setups may trigger a shader recompile at draw time"). No upstream bug number was found for the one-target link
  layout; nothing was filed from here. A program with one output avoids it, but splitting the staged programs (seven
  outputs a page) into 1-output programs would multiply each sample's passes and the fxc work by up to seven, which
  the repro's 1-output figures do not pay back, so the layer keeps its pages. Margo-side causes found on this path
  (the reverted warm draw, the synchronous query behind a warm draw) are fixed above. What stays open here is the
  serial compile's length against limits sized on WebGPU (`stall`: a single program compiles longer than its 10 s
  window) and the denoise references' pass cost, which is speed work under the build phase.
- **Measured 2026-11-27 (dev PC, RTX A6000, other lanes busy, one run each, diagnostic): what is left of the
  `denoise` steps is the staged route's cost on the layer, on both ANGLE backends.** The `denoise` case's diffuse scene,
  milliseconds a sample of one `renderImage` after a 4-sample warm render:

  | Size, samples | Direct3D 11 | ANGLE Vulkan | Native WebGPU |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 120 x 75, 64 | 2.61 | 1.90 | not run |
  | 480 x 300 (the case's size), 64 | 22.5 | 17.0 | 3.3 (mostly the call's own overhead) |
  | 480 x 300, 1,024 | 22.0 | 24.6 | 0.64 |
  | 960 x 600, 64 | 69.9 | not run | not run |

  At 480 x 300 the page's WebGL calls take 1.7 (Direct3D 11) and 2.1 ms (Vulkan) of a sample, about 6,400 calls with
  735 draws; the rest is waiting for the GPU. Calls a sample grow with the pixels (505, 6,417 and 21,243 on Direct3D
  11). So one 16,384-sample reference of this scene is about 360 s on Direct3D 11 and 400 s on ANGLE Vulkan (11 s
  native), and two such references alone pass the 600 s limit of `test:gpu:denoise`, which also renders an opaque
  scene's reference and four more cases (arithmetic: the step was not rerun, and the opaque scene was not timed). Direct3D
  11 measured 0.9 to 1.4 times Vulkan, so the remaining cost is not a Direct3D 11 fault; the serial compile above is.
  It is Margo's own: compute run as fragment passes (`packages/webgl2-compat`) over the staged tracer
  (`packages/voxel-pathtracer`), about 35 times native WebGPU a sample here. Which part of a pass costs most on the GPU
  was not measured. Closing the steps takes a staged route several times cheaper a sample, which is speed work under
  the build phase, or a ruling like KB6016e's. `stall` passes since e88457054c; no other step was rerun for this note.

### Accepted 2026-11-26: the path tracers' WebGL2 layer runs over ANGLE Direct3D 11 cannot finish inside their limits (KB6016e, KB6016f; voxel-pathtracer, staging; browser)

Release exception: ANGLE Direct3D 11 compiles each multiple-output program again at its first draw, one program after another (browser behaviour).

- **Scott's ruling (2026-11-26):** an accepted difference. The Direct3D 11 layer runs of voxel-pathtracer's
  `test:gpu:compose-native` and staging's `test:gpu:materials` under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` are not required to finish
  inside their limits; the native WebGPU and ANGLE Vulkan legs stay. No test, limit or tolerance changed. Repro below
  Margo: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-mrt-compile-repro.mjs` (dcd85799aa), where small 7-output programs drawn
  into 7 targets take 1.8 to 1.9 s each at their first draw.
- **KB6016f (staging):** `MARGO_COMPAT=1` `pathtrace-materials-browser` on the dev PC missed its run time: a link of
  360 s and a draw-time compile of 680 s on Direct3D 11 (2026-11-11), and `pathtrace-browser` and
  `pathtrace-materials-browser` failed on time on 26cf6ccf44 (2026-11-15). The same compile is the cause the first
  measurement names; staging was not remeasured after the 2026-11-25 proof.
- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --no-build --select=voxel-pathtracer/test:gpu:compose-native`
  on the dev PC (RTX A6000, Edge 157, GPU shared). Under MARGO_COMPAT=1 the test's "native" leg runs on the WebGL2
  layer over ANGLE Direct3D 11, the Windows default. Seen 2026-11-11 on 62c01a47aa (L2: killed at the 720 s limit,
  each pipeline 60 to 165 s) and on the L5a stack (ended after 210 s with no GPU work: the
  first three `ids` pipelines were ready at 166.8 s, 243.6 s and 377.6 s).
- **Cause so far:** `compose.html` makes all 32 subsets of five features, and each subset is its own staged trace
  program set; on Direct3D 11 every one is a cold fxc compile of 77 to 165 s with the GPU idle meanwhile, so the 32
  cannot fit the 12 minute limit and one compile can outlast a 3 minute idle rule. The same test passes on
  native WebGPU and `test:gpu:compose-compat` covers the layer on ANGLE Vulkan. Not KB6016 (the tracer imports only
  `ggxDenominator`, unchanged), and not KB5451 (no subset composes mesh PBR).
- **Count (2026-11-19):** the 32 subsets make 320 staged programs (9 loop programs and the census each), 289 of them
  distinct GLSL (only the census is shared; the layer keeps one program per text): 16,111,975 characters of fragment
  GLSL. Sharing cannot close the gap: with the path-state layout lines removed each loop program still has 16 distinct
  texts (32 for `vertex` and `sample`), because the mesh, media, guiding and spectral features each change the code of
  every stage, and their state words move every field of the layout. Each subset's programs are about 26 s of fxc on
  their own (the base tracer, offline), so the 32 cold sets need several times the 12 minute limit on one GPU process.
  The per-program cost is the lever (KB-L5a-10's progress of 2026-11-19 cut `hit` and `shadow` by a fifth).
  Later on 2026-11-19 the motion rotation copies went down in every subset's programs (KB-L5a-10's second progress note:
  the base tracer's eight loop programs 23.1 to 19.6 s of fxc). Rerun the same day (`MARGO_COMPAT=1`, Direct3D 11, busy, one
  run): still stopped at 600 s, with 16 of the 32 subsets' tracers past their program compiles by 367 s (before: the
  first three `ids` pipelines at 166.8, 243.6 and 377.6 s). The entry stays open.
- **Later on 2026-11-19:** each subset's `surface` program holds one `localX` and every mesh subset's programs one
  triangle walk (KB-L5a-10's third progress note: with every feature `hit` 14.1 to 10.4 s and `shadow` 52.9 to 45.2 s
  of fxc).
- **Later on 2026-11-19, again:** each subset's light program `sample` takes an instance's two transforms from one
  motion rotation and the guided `post` builds its guide boxes once (KB-L5a-10's fourth progress note: with every
  feature `sample` 30.6 to 25.3 s of fxc).
- **Reproduced 2026-11-21 on a laptop** (Intel Arc 140V, Edge 157, ANGLE Direct3D 11 as the run printed it; three
  other agents' jobs on the machine, so the seconds are loaded figures) on fa9dd5ee7, with
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compose-browser.mjs
  --backend=native`:
  - The default run (8 subsets at once, the native default, since the leg is not the script's own layer leg): subsets
    0 to 3 started together and rendered at 635 s; the media subsets 4 to 7 waited inside
    `ComposedVoxelPathTracer.create` until then, and their programs were still compiling at 1,226 s. About 160 s a
    subset.
  - `--parallel=1 --phase=ids`, the layer's own default: subsets 0, 1 and 2 took 104, 206 and 210 s; the run stopped at
    its 10 minute limit in subset 3. About the same rate, so choosing 1 for this leg would not close the gap and was
    not changed.
  - Where the time goes: every subset's programs (`ids`, the nine loop programs, the census) become ready one after
    another, never side by side, with the page idle between. A probe page (one 160-step loop program, the shader text
    new each time) showed this backend's pattern: the link reports complete after 58 to 74 ms and the first draw then
    takes 194 to 346 ms more (later draws 2 to 4 ms), for 1 and for 4 colour outputs alike, and binding the 4-target
    framebuffer before `linkProgram` changed nothing (draw 264 to 339 ms against 268 to 336 ms). So the shader compile
    that counts runs at first use on the browser's GPU thread, one program at a time, whatever the layer binds at link.
    The probe also shows that here a 1-output program pays that compile at its first draw too, which
    `LinkedProgram.warmed` (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/render.ts) did not warm, as it assumed only programs with
    2 or more colour targets compile again (measured on an RTX A6000, where a 1-output first draw took 2 ms). Fixed
    2026-11-21: every program with a colour target is warmed there, so its compile falls before `ready`, not in the
    first frame after it (regression: packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-warm.test.js and
    packages/webgl2-compat/test/first-draw-browser.mjs). This moves compiles, it adds none, so this entry's total is
    unchanged.
  - Depth-only programs, measured later on 2026-11-21 (same laptop, a probe of a 256-step loop, new shader text each
    run, three runs a kind): a program with a fragment stage and no colour output (it discards) reported its link
    complete after 45 to 53 ms and its first draw then took 128 to 174 ms more; a program with no fragment stage took
    1 to 4 ms at its first draw. The same probe found the warm draw itself compiled nothing here: with rasterizer
    discard on, a warmed 1-output pipeline still took 131 to 152 ms at its first real draw. Fixed the same day: the
    warm draw rasterizes into its 1 x 1 throwaway targets, and every program is warmed there, a program with no
    colour target into a 1 x 1 depth-stencil buffer. After it the link-to-ready time is 179 to 205 ms for both kinds
    and the first draw 1.2 to 2.1 ms (regression: packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-warm.test.js and
    packages/webgl2-compat/test/first-draw-browser.mjs, which count rasterizing warm draws). This also moves
    compiles and adds none.
  - So at this rate the 32 subsets need about 85 minutes against the 12 minute limit, about 7 times over. Nothing
    hangs: each compile finishes, and every subset that rendered passed its checks. No Margo-side defect was found
    beyond the program sizes the entry already names.
- **Proven below Margo 2026-11-25:** the compile that counts here is ANGLE Direct3D 11's draw-time compile of each
  multiple-output program on the browser's one GPU thread, one program after another, which a raw WebGL2 page with no
  Margo code reproduces (`packages/webgl2-compat/test/d3d11-mrt-compile-repro.mjs`, Intel Arc 140V, Chrome 157:
  three 7-output programs drawn into 7 targets 5.6 s one after another, the same programs into 1 target or three
  1-output programs about 1.9 to 2.5 s side by side, and no difference on ANGLE Vulkan). KB-L5a-10 has the figures,
  the trace and the upstream design note. The 289 distinct programs of the 32 subsets each pay it once; the step's
  scope on Direct3D 11 was Scott's decision (escalated 2026-11-21, ruled 2026-11-26, above).
- **Still worth doing:** smaller programs (`surface`, `hit`, `shadow`, `vertex`) shorten every compile on this back
  end. A gap of about 7 times will not close by trimming alone.
- **2026-11-26 (FG-17-EMITTERS):** the mesh emitter proposal builds a moving light point's model transform once, one
  more motion rotation copy in `sample` (`tests/compat-staged.test.js` counts it). Its text grew from 87,426 to
