### Fixed 2026-11-25: a package build that Windows could not start left only "npm error code 3221225794" (KB-FILM-HEADLESS1)

- **Repro:** seen once (2026-11-16 about 05:00 EST, Film Studio lane gate at f9b02fc1bf, other lanes' GPU and CPU
  jobs running): `npm test --workspace=packages/headless` stopped in its `build` step, `node
  ../../scripts/build-optional.js headless`, with "npm error code 3221225794" and nothing else. The same suite run alone
  right after passed 158/158.
- **Cause:** 0xC0000142 (STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED): Windows could not start npm's cmd.exe child or its node, which
  failed while loading its DLLs, before any of build-optional.js ran; under load that is the session's desktop heap
  running out (the same class as KB-L5a-6). build-optional.js cannot name it, since it never started, and the runner
  that saw the code printed it bare, with no cause and no record of how loaded the machine was.
- **Fix:** `scripts/support/start-failure.mjs` names the code with the machine state of the moment (the running
  process count from `tasklist` and the session's configured desktop heap, `SharedSection`, from the registry; a probe
  that cannot start is reported as such). `npm run test:changed` lists such a package as `packages/<dir> (exit
  0xC0000142, STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED: ...)`, and `scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs` prints the same note for its
  command. Nothing retries the step. If it recurs, the note gives the process count to compare against a normal run.
- **Sources:** the three Microsoft sources of KB-L5a-6 below (NTSTATUS values; the desktop heap limitation; the
  winsdk note on 0xc0000142).
- **Regression:** `tests/start-failure.test.js` (an npm script whose child exits 0xC0000142 reaches the runner with
  that code, and test:changed and run-with-timeout name it with the process count and SharedSection).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a git that Windows could not start stopped the dev server with a bare "Command failed" (KB-L5a-6)

- **Repro:** seen once (2026-11-11 18:58, 4 GPU jobs running, many browsers open): the lifecycle page of
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding-browser.mjs` did not start because the root `vite.config.mjs` ran
  `git ls-files` and git exited 3221225794 (0xC0000142). The next run passed.
- **Cause:** 0xC0000142 is STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED: Windows could not start the git process (a DLL failed to
  initialise), which is what a session out of desktop heap gives when many processes are open. It is not a git, Vite
  or Margo logic error. The tooling did not retry or hide it (the suite failed at once, exit 1, and nothing reruns a
  failed suite), but the message was Node's bare "Command failed: git ls-files ...", which named neither cause.
- **Fix:** `ignoredRootFolders` in `vite.config.mjs` turns any failed git into `ERR_DEV_SERVER_GIT_LIST` with the
  cause in words (0xC0000142 and the desktop heap, git missing from PATH, or git's exit status and stderr) and the
  original error as `cause`. Nothing retries it. If it recurs, count the open processes and browsers first.
- **Sources:** Microsoft, "NTSTATUS values" (0xC0000142 STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED),
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55 ;
  Microsoft, "You may receive an error 'Out of Memory' because of the desktop heap limitation",
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/windows-server/performance/desktop-heap-limitation-out-of-memory ;
  Microsoft winsdk blog, "What is up with 'The application failed to initialize properly (0xc0000142)' error?",
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/winsdk/what-is-up-with-the-application-failed-to-initialize-properly-0xc0000142-error .
- **Regression:** `tests/dev-servers.test.js` "a git that cannot start stops the root Vite config with a coded message
  (KB-L5a-6)" (fails on the old config, which ignored the failing runner).

### Fixed 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3a): three WebGL2 layer defects in views, multisampled aspects and CPU compute

- **KB1042d, sRGB view of a compressed texture refused:** materials makes every KTX2 texture with its sRGB twin in `viewFormats`, and a twin view of a block-compressed texture threw `unsupported` on the layer: a view in another format reads a copy, made by rendering, and GL can neither render into nor reinterpret a compressed texture. Now such a texture keeps the blocks it was written with (a later write that covers an earlier one replaces it) until a twin view is first made; then a storage of the twin format is filled with them, every later write goes to both, and the kept blocks go. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/features.html` case `compressedSrgbView`, compared with native WebGPU by `features-browser.mjs`.
- **KB4990c, depth and stencil views of one multisampled texture in one draw:** the layer resolves a multisampled texture into one single-sample copy before sampling, and GL keeps one sampling aspect (`DEPTH_STENCIL_TEXTURE_MODE`) per texture object, so the last binding's aspect won for both. A depth-stencil texture's stencil aspect now resolves into a copy of its own. Regression: `features.html` case `msaaAspects` (depth 0.5 and stencil 77 through one draw, equal to native).
- **CPU compute storage into a later layer only:** a CPU-run kernel publishes its stores by a masked draw per written layer from two scratch textures, whose storage was made only while filling layer 0; a kernel that stored nothing in layer 0 uploaded into textures without storage, GL refused it and the stores were lost. Storage now comes with the first written layer. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/compute-planes.test.js`.

### Firefox prints WebGL advisory warnings that the lod and materials browser checks count as errors (found 2026-11-11, open)

Release exception: Firefox advisory warnings counted as errors by lod/materials checks (browser behaviour).

- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox node packages/lod/test/browser-check.mjs --compat` and
  `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox node packages/materials/test/browser-check.mjs --compat` (Firefox 157, RTX A6000, WebGL2
  layer): the pages draw correctly (every `ok` line passes) but the checks end on `assert.deepEqual(pageErrors, [])`
  because they collect every console `warning`. Native WebGPU runs of both pass, and so do gltf/pbr, postfx, lines and
  points on the layer.
- **What Firefox prints:** (1) `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info is deprecated ... Please use RENDERER`: the layer reads the
  extension for the GPU name (`webgl2Capabilities`, reports and driver workarounds); Firefox's `RENDERER` answers the masked
  `WebKit WebGL` here, so the advice does not give the same string. (2) `WebGL context was lost.`: the probe and
  `device.destroy()` call `loseContext()` on purpose. (3) `texSubImage: Uploads from a buffer with a final row with a byte
  count smaller than the row stride` (142 calls of one 2048x12 `RGBA_INTEGER` upload from a 393,216-byte pixel buffer,
  alignment 1, in the lod page) and, in materials, `Tex image TEXTURE_2D level N is incurring lazy initialization`. Cause
  of (3) not found: the same call in a plain page (exact, larger or partly filled buffer, any usage) prints nothing.
- **Fixed 2026-11-11, video uploads in points and xr:** the canvas fallback materials got for videos Firefox refuses as a
  copy source is now `packages/shared/copy-external.js`, used by materials, points maps and xr layers. Regression:
  `packages/points/tests/mipmaps.test.js`, `packages/xr/tests/layers.test.js` (both threw the TypeError on the old
  source), `tests/shared-copy-external.test.js`.
- **Fixed 2026-11-15, video channels in Shadertoy:** `packages/shader/src/shadertoy.ts` copied a media channel's frame
  (an `HTMLVideoElement` among them) with `copyExternalImageToTexture` directly, so a Shadertoy video channel threw the
  same TypeError in Firefox. It now copies through `packages/shared/copy-external.js` like the others. Regression:
  `tests/video-copy-sources.test.js` (failed with `shadertoy.ts` as a new direct caller).
- **Fixed 2026-11-11, (1):** Firefox 157's `RENDERER` names the GPU (the same string as the extension, measured in a plain
  page under Playwright), so the layer asks for `WEBGL_debug_renderer_info` only where `RENDERER` is empty or the masked
  `WebKit WebGL` (Chromium, WebKit). Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/capabilities.test.js`, "the unmasked
  renderer is asked for only where RENDERER is masked".
- **Measured 2026-11-11, (3):** a plain Firefox 157 page prints the "final row" advisory for every `texSubImage2D` from a
  pixel buffer, full rows from an exact buffer included, and "partial upload ... lazy initialization" for a partial
  upload into a `texStorage2D` texture. Earlier "prints nothing" runs did not catch the console.
- **Measured 2026-11-11, (3), KBL3c:** unpack alignment 1, 4 and 8 all print it for an exact 4 x 4 RGBA8 upload from a
  64-byte buffer; the same upload from a `Uint8Array` prints nothing, and every upload lands. So it is a Firefox defect,
  not the layer's alignment. Minimal repro and Mozilla draft (not filed):
  [docs/upstream-reports/KBL3c](upstream-reports/KBL3c/report.md). The layer's buffer uploads stay; whether it uploads
  data textures from memory in Firefox, or the checks accept that exact line, is an open coordinator call.
- **Done 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3a), (3) final row, coordinator call:** the checks accept that one exact line on Firefox
  157 only (`acceptedAdvisory` in `scripts/support/browser-advisories.mjs`); every other line fails, and the layer keeps
  its pixel-buffer uploads (no CPU copy path). `packages/webgl2-compat/test/pbo-upload-browser.mjs` (in `test:gpu`) runs
  the KBL3c page and proves every texel exact at unpack alignment 1, 4 and 8. Firefox also capped WebGL warnings at 32 a
  context ("After reporting 32, no further warnings will be reported"), which hid every later warning: the harness now
  lifts the cap (`webgl.max-warnings-per-context`, `scripts/lib/browser.mjs`). Regression: `tests/browser-advisories.test.js`,
  `tests/browser-selection.test.js`.
- **Done 2026-11-11, (2):** Firefox's "WebGL context was lost." from the layer probe's deliberate `loseContext()` is
  counted, and the lod and materials checks assert it exactly once on the layer (`watchConsole`,
  `expectedContextLosses`); any other loss fails. With both, the lod check passes in Firefox on the layer.
- **Fixed 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3a), lazy initialisation:** with the cap lifted the imposter and materials checks
  showed "Tex image TEXTURE_2D level N is incurring lazy initialization" (texSubImage and draws, levels 0 to 4) and
  "Texture has not been initialized prior to a partial upload". Cause: the layer left every new level for the browser,
  which zeroes it at the first partial upload or draw that touches it, and Firefox warns each time. The layer now
  writes zeros into every level and layer when it allocates a texture (`Replayer.zero`): a framebuffer clear for
  colour-renderable, depth and stencil formats, a whole-level upload from a zero-filled pixel unpack buffer for the
  rest, nothing for compressed formats (an all-zero block is not a zero texel). Data, storage and readback helper
  textures too. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/zero-init.test.js`.
- **Fixed 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3a), fence polls:** the imposter check's "ClientWaitSync with timeout=0 (or
  GetSyncParameter(SYNC_STATUS)) called 100 times without SYNC_FLUSH_COMMANDS_BIT". Cause: readbacks polled their fence
  with `getSyncParameter`, which cannot ask for a flush, and `onSubmittedWorkDone` with `clientWaitSync(sync, 0, 0)`;
  Firefox counts polls without the bit whatever `gl.flush()` calls came between. Every poll is now
  `clientWaitSync(sync, SYNC_FLUSH_COMMANDS_BIT, 0)` (`fenceDone` in `device/tasks.ts`). Regression: the fence test in
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/zero-init.test.js`.
- **Accepted 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3a), depth comparison filter:** materials' "Depth texture comparison requests (e.g.
  `LINEAR`) Filtering, but behavior is implementation-defined" comes from the shadow map's comparison sampler (compare
  `less-equal`, linear filters, `packages/shadows`). The package is right: WebGPU defines such samplers and leaves the
  filtering to the implementation, as GL does, and the layer maps them to GL's LINEAR comparison, the hardware
  percentage-closer filter native WebGPU uses on the same GPU. Emulating it in the shader would take four taps for one
  and could differ from native. The checks accept that exact line, once per context, on Firefox 157 only
  (`FIREFOX_DEPTH_COMPARE_LINES` in `scripts/support/browser-advisories.mjs`). Regression: `tests/browser-advisories.test.js`.
- **Checked 2026-11-15, lod side closed:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox node packages/lod/test/browser-check.mjs --compat` (Firefox 157, WebGL2 layer) passes through `watchConsole`, which drops only the exact accepted advisory lines and counts the layer probe's one deliberate context loss; every other error or warning still fails. The other lod checks collect console errors only. Regression: `tests/browser-advisories.test.js` (fake console of each kind: accepted advisory, context loss, other warning, error). The materials side stays open (Mac).

### Fixed 2026-11-12 in the packages, 2026-11-14 in core: height-correlated Smith G2 was too dark on smooth surfaces at grazing angles (KB-G2guard)

- **Repro:** visual:check voxel-night-high at 29d79d3774 against its parent b19009b802: 3,536 pixels of the distant
  night water darker, up to 5 levels, while every other change of that commit is brighter.
- **Cause:** `smithGCorrelated` (packages/shared/light-terms.js, also in `ggxNamed` and core's copy since edcb6debb7)
  divides by `max(den, 0.0001)` with den = nl sqrt(a2 + (1 - a2) nv^2) + nv sqrt(a2 + (1 - a2) nl^2). On a smooth
  surface at grazing angles den falls far below 1e-4 (a2 = 1e-6, nl = nv = 0.001: den 2.8e-6), so G2 comes out 0.02
  against 0.71 exact and 0.69 for the separable G it replaced. den is never below 2 nl nv, so a floor near the
  smallest normal float is enough to stop 0/0 at nl = a2 = 0.
- **Effect:** voxel-night-high keeps its old baseline and fails visual:check until this is fixed (docs/limits.md,
  KB2224b). Core's copy is a core change: Scott's call.
- **Fixed 2026-11-12 (hunt K1), packages, `675ee2476` (proofs advanced in `cdfdd3b77`):** the floor is now 1e-30 in `smithGCorrelated`, `smithGCorrelatedFloat` and
  `ggxNamed` (packages/shared/light-terms.js) and in materials' anisotropic `materialG2`
  (packages/materials/src/lobe-shader.ts, the same guard): far above the smallest normal float32 (1.2e-38), so no backend
  flushes it, and below 2 nl nv for every lit pixel, so G2 is the exact value down to nl = 1e-5, nv = 1e-4, a2 = 1e-10.
  Regression: `tests/smith-shaders.test.js`, "every G2 text keeps the exact value on smooth surfaces at grazing angles"
  (fails before: 0.00002 against 0.83).
- **Fixed 2026-11-14, core:** core's own copy (packages/core/src/shaders.ts, since edcb6debb7) takes the same 1e-30
  floor (Scott approved the core change; core +5 B gzip, see docs/limits.md). Regression:
  `packages/core/tests/smith.test.js` (core's G2 text against the exact value at a2 = 1e-6, nl = nv = 0.001).
  voxel-night-high needs its baseline re-recorded on the workstation (visual baselines are per machine): the old one
  predates the brighter G2 pixels of 29d79d3774.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a BatchedMesh over 262,144 vertices threw, so the batched-mesh demo never got ready (KB-VIS-bm)

- **Repro:** `npm run visual:check -- --only=batched-mesh`: both views waited 120 s for the ready signal and failed;
  the page showed `RangeError: Invalid prepared PBR geometry; run prepareAsset again`.
- **Cause:** f9410d4500 made gltf/pbr split any primitive over `asset.partVertices` (262,144 by default) into load
  parts. Materials' `createMesh` builds its mesh through that path, so every group above the limit was split too. The
  demo's batch holds 398,680 vertices; its placeholder indices all point at vertex 0, so each part held one vertex and
  failed the prepared-geometry check. Any larger `createMesh` geometry also broke the one-primitive-per-group layout
  its material slots, `setGeometry` and BatchedMesh ranges rely on.
- **Fix:** `createMesh` raises its placeholder asset's part limit to the geometry's vertex count, so each group stays
  one primitive (the prepared-geometry cap of 1,000,000 vertices still applies).
- **Regression:** packages/materials/tests/batched.test.js "a batch larger than one glTF part stays one primitive
  (KB-VIS-bm)" (threw without the fix). The two views now capture; their pictures are compared under KB2224b.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: water's coastal topology shader failed to compile in Firefox (KB-FF1)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox node packages/biomes/tests/water-check.mjs`: Firefox rejects the coastal topology
  module ("return expression None does not match the declared return type"), so the biomes GPU suite fails there.
- **Cause:** packages/water/src/coastal.ts `fn root(index:u32)->u32` ended in a `loop` whose only exit was a
  `return` inside it. The WGSL behavior analysis accepts that (a loop with no `break` never falls through; Chromium
  and the WebGL2 layer compile it), but Firefox's front end requires a value-returning function to end in a statement
  that returns on every path.
- **Fix:** the loop breaks when it reaches the root and the function returns after it; same result on every backend.
- **Regression:** tests/wgsl-returns.test.js (KB-FF1b made the rule repo-wide and replaced the water-only test) fails
  on a value-returning WGSL function that does not end in `return`, an `if`/`else` that returns on both sides, or a
  `switch` whose clauses all return (the `coastal.ts root` shape is its first case).
- Source: W3C WebGPU Shading Language, section "Behavior Analysis" (function return rules),
  https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#behaviors.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: float32 GGX D lost tens of percent on smooth surfaces (KB6016c)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/core/tests/ggx-precision.browser.mjs` on the
  old core: at roughness 0.03 core's D was 125,995 against an f64 98,243 for the same float32 vectors (+28 %), 3.2 % at
  0.05 and 0.28 % at 0.1; WebGL2 layer the same.
- **Cause:** every GGX D in the engine wrote its denominator `nh^2 (a2 - 1) + 1`. Near the peak of a narrow lobe
  `1 - nh^2` is a few float32 steps while `a2` is about 8e-7 at roughness 0.03, so the rounding of `nh` alone moved D
  by tens of percent (and gave 0/0 at roughness 0, nh 1). Found while fixing KB6016b: the same form in a reference
  script biased smooth spheres by -13 %.
- **Fix:** the denominator is `|n x h|^2 + a2 nh^2`, equal for unit vectors by the Lagrange identity
  (|n x h|^2 = 1 - nh^2); the cross product keeps its relative precision. Core's mesh shader (Scott's ruling "fix C the
  core"; core 22,207 B -> 22,225 B, core + stage 24,808 B -> 24,825 B) and the shared `ggxD` / new `ggxDOf(n, h)` in
  packages/shared/light-terms.js, used by animation (VAT), clustered, gltf/pbr, lod imposters, materials (base, coat,
  eye, skin), post material decals, terrain, voxel and the WebGL2 preview. After the fix the worst error is 6e-5. Where the half vector faces away (dot(n, h) < 0, nh clamped to 0) the identity holds for the raw dot only: |n x h|^2 fell below 1 and reached 0 as h turned to -n, so D was unbounded on back-facing shading normals lit from the front (found by terrain's crest check on the WebGL2 layer, "weightedUncapped: 9 specks uncapped"); the term is max(|n x h|^2, step(nh, 0)), so D is a2 / pi there as before (+10 B, core 22,225 B).
- **Fixed since (KB6016d, 2026-11-26, above):** the scalar `ggxDenominator(nh)` callers (environment prefilter and probes, water glints,
  voxel-pathtracer) and materials' `ggxNamed` lobes, and water's ship lamps and FFT ocean, kept the old form; they now pass the vectors.
- **Regression:** packages/core/tests/ggx-precision.browser.mjs (core's own D statements on the GPU against f64, bound
  0.2 %, in core's test:gpu, native and WebGL2 layer, back-facing half vectors included); packages/core/tests/smith.test.js and
  tests/smith-shaders.test.js (D = a2 / pi where dot(n, h) < 0, for core and the shared ggxD, ggxDFloat, ggxDOf).
- Sources: Walter, Marschner, Li and Torrance 2007, "Microfacet Models for Refraction through Rough Surfaces", EGSR,
  eq. 33; Guy and Agopian, "Physically Based Rendering in Filament", section 4.4.1 (the same cross-product form),
  https://google.github.io/filament/Filament.html; Goldberg 1991, "What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About
  Floating-Point Arithmetic", ACM Computing Surveys 23(1) (cancellation).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: no gate held the Firefox return-path rule outside water (KB-FF1b)

- **Repro:** before this change, a WGSL function in any package other than water could end in a `loop` left only by
  `return` (the KB-FF1 shape) and pass lint, hygiene, check:wgsl and every Chromium and WebGL2 GPU suite; only a
  Firefox run would catch it.
- **Cause:** the KB-FF1 regression test read water's source alone, and check:wgsl compiles on Chromium, whose WGSL
  front end follows the spec's behavior analysis and accepts that shape.
- **Fix:** one rule, three layers. `npm run hygiene` scans every `.wgsl` file under packages/ and every WGSL function
  written out whole in packages/*/src and packages/shared (scripts/support/wgsl-returns.mjs); check:wgsl runs the same
  analyzer on every module the shader builders return, flags both ways; the WGSL guard every browser check installs
  (scripts/support/wgsl-guard.js `wgslReturnGaps`) reports a gap in any module a page creates as a `[wgsl] error`, so
  assembled shaders are checked as the GPU receives them. On landing the source scan read 1,719 functions and check:wgsl
  every builder output, with no other gap.
- **Regression:** tests/wgsl-returns.test.js (the analyzer cases, the source scan on a planted gap, and the guard
  reporting a planted module).
- Source: W3C WebGPU Shading Language, section "Behavior Analysis", https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#behaviors.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: check:wgsl failed on sciviz's flow trail template (found by KB-FF1b)

- **Repro:** `npm run check:wgsl` on main: `/packages/sciviz/src/flow-shaders.ts flowDraw 23:1 unexpected token |
  FLOW_PROJECT`, so the gate in check:merge was red for every run that reached sciviz.
- **Cause:** `flowDraw` was exported as a WGSL constant that still held three text slots (FLOW_PROJECT,
  FLOW_APPEARANCE, FLOW_COLOUR) which flow-particles.ts filled at draw time; check:wgsl compiles every exported
  constant with an entry point as it is.
- **Fix:** `flowDraw(globe, appearance)` is a builder that holds the template and fills every slot (the same text
  flow-particles.ts wrote). check:wgsl now compiles it with `globe` both ways. Drawn output is unchanged.
- **Regression:** packages/sciviz/tests/flow-draw-shader.test.js (no exported flow shader holds a slot; each filled form
  is checked).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: gltf/pbr parts culled one by one only under CulledModels (bug sweep L2, KB0027)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:gpu:parts` in packages/gltf: without `CulledModels`, a 20-part 10M-triangle field draws
  all 20 parts in a close view where 9 are in the frustum (`draws` in test-results/gltf-pbr-parts.json).
- **Cause:** the frame's own culling tests a gltf/pbr node's bounds, not each primitive's; parts of one primitive share
  a node.
- **Fix to build:** test each primitive's sphere on the CPU in the PBR draw loop (work count: spheres tested per frame).
- **Fix:** the PBR draw loop tests each primitive's bounding sphere against the camera planes (`outsideView` in
  packages/gltf/src/model.ts): one sphere test per primitive per draw call, measured once per vertex array, and a
  part out of view issues no draw. Primitives whose vertices may move (instanced, skinned, morphed, deformed, own
  shader, displacement map) are not tested. Regression: packages/gltf/test/parts.test.js ("each part culls on its
  own"): a strip in 3 parts with a frustum over the first draws 1, not 3.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: compressDraco could not encode a 10M-triangle mesh with normals and UVs (KB0035)

- **Repro:** `encodeNativeMesh` in `packages/exporters/src/draco-native-encode.ts` with a 5,004,169-vertex,
  9,999,392-triangle grid carrying float positions, normals and UVs: its packed input is 280 MB, over the 256 MiB
  ceiling. Measuring that ceiling showed it was also too high: the encoder peaked at 20.8 bytes of Wasm memory per
  input byte, so a 243 MB positions-only mesh passed the check and trapped (`RuntimeError: unreachable`) at 4 GiB.
- **Cause:** the clean-room encoder (`packages/exporters/draco-kernel`) held a map with a vector per edge
  (`corners`), a map keyed by a copy of every point's bytes (`compact`), a full clone of the attributes while
  compacting, the packet and its parsed copy for the whole encode, the first candidate's topology beside the grouped
  one, and the corner table while building each group's.
- **Fix:** a sorted edge array, an in-place hash table, no attribute clone, the packet freed once parsed
  (`encoder_encode` now owns it), and each topology dropped once used. Output is byte-identical; peak memory is 12.9
  bytes per input byte at most (positions only), 9.1 with normals and UVs. The ceiling is now 280 MiB, the most whose
  measured peak fits 90% of 4 GiB (docs/limits.md). Regression: packages/exporters/tests/draco-encoder-memory.test.js
  (the ceiling against the measured peak, the 280,126,152 B scan passing the check, the packet freed by the encoder).

### Path tracer viewport: the converged image after a device restore differed once on the WebGL2 layer under GPU load (KB-C34h, 2026-11-11, open, not reproduced)

  saw "clear glass" 0.7623 against 1 once, also on the layer under load).
- **Ruled out, by experiment (RTX A6000, ANGLE Vulkan and native WebGPU, every converged image hashed):** band sizing
  (seven fixed band budgets from 400,000 to 201,326,592 path-iterations give one hash on each backend); readback and
  queue timing (every `mapAsync` and `onSubmittedWorkDone` delayed by a seeded 0 to 40 ms); GPU load (three loaded pages
  at once, 48 images, one hash); the suite's own order on one page (`traversal analytic textures shapes transparent
  determinism viewport`, twice beside each other). The denoiser is not involved: the case traces with `denoise` off
  (the default). The NVIDIA driver resets that day (event 153 at 08:04, 08:12 and 09:23) do not line up with the failure.

  limit of 120 s each, and `npm run test:gpu:slow-compile-viewport` keeps that path covered
  (packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.html). This flaw cannot give the 5,723-pixel result, where both
  images had converged.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: OpenEXR chromaticities were read as sRGB (Rust finding R10)

- **Repro:** an EXR whose `chromaticities` attribute names ACEScg (AP1) primaries and one pixel (1, 0, 0): `parseEXR`,
  `/exr-tiled` and the `/exr-codecs` worker returned (1, 0, 0), where linear sRGB is about (1.705, -0.130, -0.024).
- **Cause:** `packages/environment/src/exr.ts` skipped the attribute, so every decode path treated the data as Rec.709.
- **Fix:** `packages/environment/src/exr-primaries.ts` reads the attribute from any part's header and converts RGB with
  the RP 177 plus Bradford matrix `parseHDR` uses for Radiance PRIMARIES, in all three readers; images report
  `primaries` and `primariesConverted`, and `encodeEXR` writes `chromaticities`. Regression:
  `packages/environment/tests/exr-chromaticities.test.js` (5 of 5 on 2026-11-27). Source: OpenEXR, "Standard Attributes",
  https://openexr.com/en/latest/StandardAttributes.html (`chromaticities`: CIE xy of the RGB primaries and white).

### Radeon 680M: pixel's `screen` blend lands one step below the exact result (list 5 R6 row 14, 2026-11-10, open)

Release exception: screen blend one step low (driver).

- **What:** `packages/pixel/tests/browser-check.js`, case `screen`, on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, RDNA2, driver
  32.0.21030.2001, Chrome on D3D12): 80 pixels one step below the CPU image, the first at (44, 4), red 157 where the
  CPU image has 158. The other blend cases pass.
- **Repro:** source 151 composited over destination 16 with `screen`, the fixed-function blend `color: one,
  one-minus-src` of `LayerCompositor` (`packages/pixel/src/index.ts`). Exact: 151 + 16 x (1 - 151/255) = 151 + 16 x
  104/255 = 157.5255, which the CPU model rounds to 158. The 680M writes 157, as if it took the destination product
  (6.5255) to a whole byte before the add.
- **Cause:** below Margo, in the blend unit's precision. WebGPU leaves blend arithmetic precision undefined, so a GPU
  may round the intermediate product; every whole-byte `screen` result is at least 1/510 of a step from x.5, so a GPU
  that blends in float gets the CPU image exactly, and this one does not. The test's tolerance and the test stay as
  they are (Scott's ruling, 2026-11-10).
- **Why the blend stays in the blend unit:** an exact blend in the shader needs the destination as a texture, and the
  compositor does not have it: `composite()` draws every layer, in order, into the frame's colour attachment in one
  render pass, so the destination of a `screen` layer is that pass's own attachment (a canvas texture configured by
  core for rendering only, and multisampled when the engine is). Reading it would need, per `screen` layer, the pass
  ended, the covered region copied (or resolved) to a texture, and a new pass begun, or the whole composite moved to
  an extra target: a new copy and an extra render pass per frame, which Scott's ruling (2026-11-10) does not allow.
- **Upstream report (draft, nothing filed):** `docs/upstream-reports/KB0171/report.md` with the raw WebGPU and WebGL2 page `screen-blend.html`. Reproduces on 2026-11-11 on this PC's AMD RDNA2 iGPU (19 of 1024 pixels off, including source 151 over destination 16: 157 instead of 158) and not on the RTX A6000.
- **Gate:** on the AMD mini PC this case is recorded and not counted; pixel's GPU step runs on the workstation or Mac (Scott, 2026-11-12).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the transitions GLSL oracle and the WGSL port disagreed at a texel edge (list 5 R6 row 21)

- **What:** `packages/transitions` `test:gpu` (`test/glsl-browser.js`) on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M): fixture `matrix`
  at p = 0.25, texel (12, 2) channel 0: the native WebGL2 oracle gives 145, the WGSL port 133.
- **Repro:** the rotated lookup of `matrix` lands at x = 10.99938 texels of a nearest-filtered gradient, 6e-4 of a texel
  below the edge between texels 10 and 11. 133 is texel 10 (167 and 32 mixed at 0.25), 145 is texel 11.
- **Cause:** the two read the texture differently near an edge. The oracle samples through the hardware (GL `NEAREST`):
  a sampler snaps the coordinate to its subtexel grid (1/256 of a texel in D3D11) and on this GPU the snap rounds up to
  texel 11. The product's `sample()` (`src/custom-code.ts`, `src/builtin.ts`) floors exactly with `textureLoad`, and the
  harness mirrors the product, so it reads texel 10. Neither is wrong for its own rule; a lookup within one snap step of
  an edge picks a different texel.
- **Not done:** a harness that samples through a nearest sampler would pass, but the product does not sample that way,
  so the harness would no longer test the product (manager's ruling, 2026-11-10). Fixing it means choosing one rule for
  the product: keep the exact floor (and give the oracle comparison a documented edge allowance) or sample through a
  nearest sampler as GLSL transitions do.
- **Fix (coordinator ruling 2026-11-11, under Scott's "fix everything else"):** the product keeps its rule, the WebGPU
  spec's nearest texel selection (the texel containing the coordinate: truncate uv * size, clamp), and the oracle now
  applies the same rule with `texelFetch` (`margoFetch` in `test/glsl-browser.js`, the GLSL bottom-left flip included,
  `texture2D` and `texture2DProj` mapped to it), so oracle and port agree exactly at the edge. No allowance added. New
  fixture `texel edge` reads 6e-4 of a texel either side of an edge. Regression: `test/glsl.test.js` "the GLSL oracle
  reads texels by the product rule, not through a sampler"; the GPU fixture passes native and compat on the RTX A6000
  (whose sampler truncates, so the old oracle passed there too); the Radeon 680M rerun is the hardware proof still owed.

### Radeon 680M: the 4x MSAA resolve rounds an exact .5 average by draw history (list 5 R6 row 8, 2026-11-10, worked around in the checks)

Release exception: 4x MSAA resolve rounds .5 by draw history (driver).

- **What:** `packages/culling` `dynamic-check.mjs`, `parts-check.mjs` and `lod-check.mjs` on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M,
  driver 32.0.21030.2001, Chrome on D3D12) found 1-level channel differences on 6 to 67 resolved pixels between the
  culled engine and core, which draws the same instances in another order once a mesh hides.
- **Cause:** below Margo. The multisampled colour samples of both engines are equal bit for bit (read before the
  resolve); only the resolved pixel differs, where the four samples average to exactly x.5 and the resolve rounds it
  one way or the other depending on what was drawn before. WebGPU does not define the resolve's rounding.
- **Workaround:** those checks compare the samples before the resolve (`test/gpu/msaa-samples.js`, `msaa.mjs`; Scott's
  decision 2026-11-09), with a control that drops one box from the culled engine alone and must show. `meshlets-check`
  compares A and B without MSAA instead. On the WebGL2 layer the resolved frames are compared as before.

### Radeon 680M: a colour attachment's export narrows the shader output to binary16 by truncation (list 5 R6 row 25, 2026-11-10, worked around in webgl2-compat)

Release exception: colour export narrows to binary16 by truncation (driver).

- **What:** `packages/webgl2-compat` `test:gpu:preview-contract` (`test/package-tiers-browser.mjs`) on the AMD mini PC
  (Radeon 680M, driver 32.0.21030.2001, Chrome, WebGL2 on ANGLE D3D11): the procedural texture baker (bricks,
  16 x 16) stored red 133 at texel (3, 0) on the WebGL2 layer where native WebGPU stores 134; the other 15 texels of
  the row matched.
- **Repro:** a CPU model of the bake in f32 (the bricks shader, op by op): texel 3 is 133.5204 / 255. Rounded straight
  from f32, as a WebGPU storage texture store does, that is 134, and the model gives native's whole row. Truncated to
  binary16 first (11 significant bits: 0.523609 becomes 0.5234375, 133.477 / 255) and then rounded, it is 133, and
  that model gives the layer's whole row. `compute-browser.mjs` case `fragmentUnormRound` stores (k + 0.52) / 255 and
  three other near-half values into an rgba8unorm storage texture: before the fix the layer stored k on many texels
  (the first at texel 8, blue 8.505 / 255) where native WebGPU stores k + 1.
- **Cause:** below Margo. The layer runs a compute store into rgba8unorm as a draw into a colour attachment, and the
  680M's driver exports the fragment output to an 8-bit target as binary16, truncating, before the UNORM conversion
  (the same truncation as R6 row 7's half targets). WGSL's inverse channel transfer function for 8unorm only clamps
  (WGSL, "Texel Formats"), so which of the two nearest steps a GPU stores is its own choice, and GPUs differ: the
  workstation's RTX A6000 (Chrome, D3D12 and ANGLE D3D11 alike) stores k for (k + 0.52) / 255 when k % 16 is 0 to 10 and
  k + 1 otherwise, and only from k + 0.57 up on every k (probe of 256 x 21 values, storage store, render target and
  raw WebGL2 all equal), where the 680M's storage store rounds to the nearest.
- **Workaround (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/compute/glsl.ts`):** the fragment and scatter tiers round a float texel to
  the 255 steps in the shader before an 8-bit UNORM target stores it, as the CPU tier's quantize already did. A value
  on the k / 255 grid survives any narrowing to 11 or more bits (under 0.13 of a step), so every GPU stores exactly
  the nearest step. Because native WebGPU's own rounding differs by GPU, `fragmentUnormRound` and
  `scatterUnormRound` check the layer against the nearest step computed in f32 and native against the two nearest
  steps; comparing the layer to native byte for byte failed on the A6000 (layer 1, native 0 for 0.52 / 255) after the
  first version of this fix. The procedural texture baker (`texture-shader.ts`, `textures-webgl.ts`) rounds to the
  255 steps itself, as its PBR baker already did, so the store's rounding no longer depends on the GPU or tier;
  before that, the preview-contract baker comparison failed on the A6000 (layer 134, native 133 at texel (3, 0)).
  Not rerun on the Radeon 680M (the AMD mini PC was unreachable on 2026-11-10): by the spec both checks hold there, since
  its native store rounds to the nearest and the layer's grid values survive its truncation.

### Radeon 680M, ANGLE Direct3D 11: a clear of a texture level or layer whose last write was a clear is lost (list 5 R6 row 26, 2026-11-11, worked around in webgl2-compat)

Release exception: clear of a level after a clear lost (driver).

- **What:** `packages/creative` `test:gpu:targets` under compatibility mode on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, driver
  32.0.21030.2001, Chrome, WebGL2 on ANGLE D3D11): `cube texel 0,0 layer 4: 0 != 255`. Every level and layer of an
  rgba8unorm cube is cleared once by a render pass to its own colour and read back; native WebGPU passes.
- **Repro (raw WebGL2, no Margo code):** a fresh 4 x 4 RGBA8 2D array or cube (3 levels, 6 layers), each subresource
  attached in turn to one framebuffer and cleared with clearBufferfv to (0, 0, 0, 1), reads 17 of its 18 subresources
  back unchanged; 2D mips lose levels 1 and 2 when each level was cleared before. After a draw or an upload into every
  subresource the first round of clears lands, and a second round (to white) again keeps 1 of 18. Uploads after a draw
  or a clear all land.
- **Cause:** below Margo: the driver keeps the clears of one subresource of a texture only, where the subresource's
  last write was a clear (a fresh texture counts as cleared). A clear followed by a draw is not affected, so a pass that
  clears and draws each frame works; clear-only passes over levels or layers lose their clears.
- **Workaround (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/fresh-clears.ts`, `render.ts`):** the adapter probes once (a 4 x 4
  texture with 2 levels, both cleared to 0 and then to (0, 0, 0, 1); level 1 reads 0 where clears are lost). There the
  layer clears the colour subresources of float and normalized textures with more than one level or layer by draws,
  both its own zeroing of new textures and render pass `loadOp: 'clear'`; integer, depth and stencil formats and
  single-subresource textures keep clearBuffer. Regression: `features-browser.mjs` `freshClears` (two rounds over a
  cube, an array and 2D mips; fails without the workaround), `layerView` (a zero draw inside a pass gives the pass its
  viewport back), `test/fresh-clears.test.js`. Depth and stencil clears were not probed.
- **Follow-up (audit A2, 2026-11-12):** the clear draws stored one step below native WebGPU's clear in 16 of 60 clears
  (`features-browser.mjs` `clearByDraw`: rgba8unorm 0.1 stored 25, native 26; rgb10a2unorm and rgba8unorm-srgb
  likewise; rgba16float and rgba32float equal): the colour export narrows the float to binary16 by truncation before
  the UNORM conversion (the row 25 entry above), where native's clear rounds to the nearest step. The draw now writes
  the clear colour rounded to the format's own steps on the CPU (`drawnClear` in `fresh-clears.ts`; sRGB targets the
  linear value of the nearest encoded step), which survives that narrowing. Regressions: `clearByDraw` (fails without
  the rounding) and `test/fresh-clears.test.js`.

### Radeon 680M, ANGLE Direct3D 11: acos is 6.75e-5 off (list 5 R6 row 31, 2026-11-11, worked around in webgl2-compat)

Release exception: acos 6.75e-5 off (driver).

- **What:** `packages/shader` `test:gpu` `utils-check.mjs` under compatibility mode on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, driver
  32.0.21030.2001, Chrome, WebGL2 on ANGLE D3D11): the equirect of the forward axis is (0.5, 0.5000215), 2.2e-5 off in
  v against the check's 1e-5; native WebGPU passes.
- **Repro (raw WebGL2, no Margo code):** a fragment shader writing `floatBitsToUint(acos(x))` into an RGBA32UI target
  reads acos(0) = 1.5707288, 6.75e-5 below pi / 2; asin is 6.76e-5 off at 0 and 4.6e-5 at 0.5, atan2 up to 1.1e-5.
  The equirect's v is 1 - acos(0) / pi = 0.5000215.
- **Cause:** below Margo: the Direct3D HLSL compiler under ANGLE evaluates acos and asin with a short polynomial. WGSL
  takes acos's accuracy from atan2 (4096 ULP, about 4.9e-4 here) and GLSL ES 3.00 leaves it unspecified, so the driver
  is within both specs; Margo's shaders expect 1e-5, which native WebGPU gives on every GPU measured.
- **Workaround (Scott's ruling 2026-11-11, `packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/inverse-trig.ts`,
  `glsl/helpers.ts`):** the adapter probes once (acos, asin and atan2 at 65 inputs against float64); where any result
  is more than 1e-5 off, every translated shader calls the layer's own `_acos`, `_asin` and `_atan2` (octant
  reduction and an odd polynomial of degree 17 for atan on [0, 1], error under 1e-6 in a float32 model over the whole
  domain). Other drivers compile unchanged shaders; the utils-check tolerance stays 1e-5, and utils-check passes under
  compatibility mode with the workaround. Regression: `features-browser.mjs` `inverseTrig` (the whole domain against
  float64 to 1e-5: 2.86e-7 on the 680M; without the workaround it fails, atan2(-0, -1) reads +pi), and
  `test/inverse-trig.test.js`.
- **Follow-up (audit A2, 2026-11-12):** the one-argument atan stayed the driver's built-in, and it is 1.16e-5 off over
  [-8, 8] on the 680M (native WebGPU 1.4e-7), past the same 1e-5. Where the probe flags the driver, atan is now the
  layer's `_atan` (atan2 of x and 1). Regressions: `inverseTrig` sweep 4 (atan over [-16, 16) and its extremes, fails
  without the change) and `test/inverse-trig.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: in WebKit a check's first run could be the previous document's, at 300 x 150 (KB-L4-W1)

- **Repro:** on the Apple silicon Mac, `MARGO_BROWSER=webkit node packages/sky/test/browser-check.mjs` in a freshly copied
  checkout failed `night-citadel 4x frame 0 scene vs control` in about 1 run in 10 (3 of 21, then 1 of 19 and 1 of
  12): the `full` frames were 300 x 150 (45,000 pixels) against 256 x 192. Smaller: tests/stale-document.test.js
  under `MARGO_BROWSER=webkit` fails both its cases without the fix.
- **Cause:** Playwright's WebKit keeps resolving the WebGPU promises of a document after the tab has navigated away
  from it. openBrowser loads the check's page, and the check navigates to it again at once; on a first load (Vite
  transforms every module) the first document was still starting up, so it finished in the background with no page
  (hidden, innerWidth 0, devicePixelRatio 0, so the engine kept the canvas default 300 x 150). Every document of a tab
  shares one `window` object, so its `window.ready = true` and `window.check = {...}` landed on the new document, and
  the check's first `check.run` was the old document's. Traced by logging each document's `performance.timeOrigin`
  and state inside one run: the run started in a 346 ms old hidden document and its frames read the 48 ms old one. No
  canvas size was ever written to 300; core's resize is not involved and needs no change. No page reload happened, and
  the dependency scan message was a separate defect (fixed below).
- **Fix:** openBrowser installs `holdStaleDocumentGpu` (scripts/support/stale-document.js) first in every page: once a
  document's `pagehide` has fired, each WebGPU promise it settles is held, so its script stops at its next GPU wait; a
  document the back/forward cache shows again gets the held results. Chromium and Firefox already stop a left
  document's script. Before the fix 5 of 52 fresh-folder sky runs on the Mac failed; after it 60 of 60 passed.
  Regression: tests/stale-document.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the browser teardown test failed on main over a standalone upstream repro runner

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/browser-teardown.test.js` after c456fb6d05 named `docs/upstream-reports/run-page.mjs`
  as a script that starts a browser and a server without `closeAll`.
- **Cause:** the runner opens repro pages for other projects' bug trackers and must carry no Margo code, so it cannot
  import `scripts/support/shutdown.mjs`; the checker covered every tracked script.
- **Fix:** the checker skips `docs/upstream-reports/`, with the reason beside the rule (49e7d087c5). Those scripts run
  by hand, never in a suite or gate. Regression: tests/browser-teardown.test.js.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: every suite dev server scanned every HTML page in the checkout for dependencies

- **Repro:** `startDevServer({ startPath: '/LICENSE', port: 0 })` from `scripts/browser.js`; its
  `server.config.optimizeDeps.entries` held the root `vite.config.mjs` list (`'**/*.html'` and its exclusions) as well
  as the start page.
- **Cause:** startDevServer passes `optimizeDeps.entries: [startPath]`, but Vite's mergeConfig concatenates arrays, so
  the root config's whole-checkout pattern came along. Each suite server scanned every page before its first load, and
  one unresolvable import in any other page (an untracked local page, for example) failed the scan ("Failed to run
  dependency scan"), which skips pre-bundling for the suite's own page.
- **Fix:** the start-owner plugin sets the resolved `optimizeDeps.entries` to the start page alone, next to the watcher
  setting it already overrides for the same reason. The root dev servers keep the root config. Regression:
  tests/dev-server-watch.test.js ("a suite dev server scans only its start page").

### Fixed 2026-11-12: Radeon 680M, environment fog-all `fog.enabled = false` one binary16 step from no fog on the WebGL2 layer (list 5 R6 row 28)

- **What:** on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, driver 32.0.21030.2001, Chrome, ANGLE D3D11), `environment`
  `test:gpu:fog-all` under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` finds `fog.enabled = false` differing from no fog in 55 VFX pixels by one
  binary16 step (max 2^-11, mean 5.2e-8, at 4x and 1x), and the two canvas variants report `{}` (4 of 87 checks).
  Native WebGPU passes.
- **Repro (raw WebGL2 and raw WebGPU, no Margo code):** 65,536 float32 values
  drawn into a 256 x 256 RGBA16F target (0.25 up in float32 steps, 8 binary16 steps): native WebGPU (Dawn, Direct3D
  12) and raw WebGL2 (ANGLE Direct3D 11) both store the half toward zero for every inexact value (32,764 of 65,536
  truncated, the rest exact); into RGBA8 (i / 65536), both store 2,573 of 65,536 one below round(x * 255) (the
  truncated half before the UNORM rounding). So this GPU's colour export truncates under both APIs, and the layer
  stores what native stores.
- **Cause (below Margo, worked around in webgl2-compat):** ANGLE D3D11 on this GPU folds a float add or multiply that a
  fragment shader writes straight to a 16-bit float or 8-bit UNORM colour output into the export, and stores the step
  below at a few texels; the same value after any identity operation the compiler cannot fold away (times a uniform 1,
  plus a uniform 0, a mix at a uniform 0) stores what native WebGPU stores. The unfogged billboard wrote
  `colour * texel` (and the plain one the colour) straight to its output; the disabled-fog program passes it through
  `mix(c, fog, 0)` first, so only the unfogged program folded. Bisected on the fog-all page by rewriting the disabled-fog
  program's GLSL at shaderSource (hunt worktree `.lane/diag/r28-bisect.mjs`): dropping its mix, or a mix by the
  literal 0 (which FXC folds), gives 0 differences; its vertex shader's extra world-position output is not involved
  (still 55 pixels without it); `rgb * (1 - u)` and `rgb + 0 * u` with u a uniform 0 keep the 55; a select on
  `gl_FragCoord.w > 0` in every particle program gives 0. Raw repro (no Margo code, hunt worktree `.lane/diag/r28raw2.html`,
  `r28raw3.html`): a 256 x 256 RGBA16F target, one full-screen triangle, a vertex-constant colour times a linear sample
  of fog-all's 2 x 2 RGBA8 texture: written straight it differs from native WebGPU at 3 to 66 texels for 9 of 12
  colours, always one half below; `* k`, `+ z` or `mix(x, f, a)` with uniforms k = 1, z = a = 0 equal native at
  every texel of every colour, on both APIs. `c + d` (d a smooth varying) and `d * d.gbr` fold too, and 8-bit UNORM
  targets (10 texels); RGBA32F targets, a fused `c * d + e`, a division and a plain sample or varying do not.
  Identities FXC removes (`+ 0.0`, `* 1.0`, `-(-x)`, a bit cast round trip) keep the fold; a select on a value known
  only at run time (`gl_FragCoord.w > 0.0 ? x : 0`, `gl_FragCoord.x < -1.0 ? 0 : x`, `max(x, -FLT_MAX)`) removes it.
- **Fix (`packages/webgl2-compat/src/glsl/emit.ts`):** every float fragment output is written as
  `_oN = gl_FragCoord.w > 0.0 ? value : 0.0`. For every rasterized fragment w is 1 / clip w, above 0, so the select is
  the value itself on any GPU, bit for bit (NaN included); integer outputs are written straight. fog-all passes under
  `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (87 of 87). A startup probe was tried first and dropped: on this GPU which texels fold depends on
  the context and draw, and the probe found no fold in the adapter's own context while the pages folded.
  Regressions: `features-browser.mjs` `foldedExports` (the raw repro through the layer, twelve colours: without the
  select 8 of 12 targets differ from native, with it all equal) and `test/folded-exports.test.js` (the emitted writes).
  Not covered: the compute fragment tier's own storage-texture writes (`src/compute/glsl.ts`), not probed.
- **Not a fix:** `3adffdee0` rounded every such export to the nearest binary16 in the shader. fog-all then passed, but
  the layer no longer stored what native stores on the same GPU: `dof` `compat-check.mjs` "a one-sample capture blurs
  the same" read max 1 for 0, and `features-browser.mjs` `halfExport` had the layer store 0x3800 for 0.49999997 where
  native stores 0x37ff. The rounding code (`HALF_ROUND_GLSL`, `roundHalfExports`, the adapter's `halfExportRounding`)
  was removed on 2026-11-12 (API break approved by Scott); the dof check and `halfExport`, now layer equals native
  exactly, are its regressions.

- **Compute stores checked (hunt H4, 2026-11-12):** the compute fragment tier writes storage-texture stores straight
  (`src/compute/glsl.ts`), without the select. A raw probe through the layer (hunt worktree `.lane/diag/fold-stores.mjs`):
  a compute shader storing a uniform colour times a texel into a 256 x 256 rgba16float storage texture equals native
  WebGPU at every texel for twelve colours (0 of 786,432), so these stores hold. Storing colour times a bilinear blend
  computed in the shader (`mix`) differs at 1 to 76 texels per colour, and still at 0 to 9 through the select: the two
  compilers round the blend differently, which is not the export fold, so the select was not added.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: Playwright's headed Chromium and Firefox would not start from a packaged app's redirected %LOCALAPPDATA%

- **Repro:** from a process of an MSIX-packaged app on Windows (the Claude desktop app), start
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright\chromium-1248\chrome-win64\chrome.exe --headless --dump-dom about:blank` with Node's
  `spawnSync`: `spawn UNKNOWN`, and the Application event log reports a side-by-side error. The same file by its
  real path (`fs.realpathSync.native`, inside the package's `LocalCache` folder) starts.
- **Cause:** the package redirects `%LOCALAPPDATA%` for its own processes, but Windows builds the new process's
  side-by-side activation context from the path it was given, outside the redirection, and finds no private assembly
  beside it. Firefox (`mozglue`) and full Chromium hit it; Chromium's headless shell, Edge and Chrome do not.
- **Fix:** `scripts/lib/browser.mjs` starts Playwright's Firefox (`firefoxExecutable`, 34fe47227a) and its headed
  Chromium (`chromiumExecutablePath`) by their real paths. Headless Chromium, Edge, Chrome, WebKit and an executable named
  by the caller or `BROWSER_EXECUTABLE` start as before. Regression: tests/browser-selection.test.js. Checked from the app:
  headed `MARGO_BROWSER=chromium` failed with `spawn UNKNOWN` before and starts now.

### Fixed 2026-11-12: a draw after copyTextureToBuffer read the buffer's old contents on the WebGL2 layer (audit A2)

- **Repro:** copy textures into a vertex, a uniform, a storage and an index buffer, then draw with them in the same
  submit (`packages/webgl2-compat/test/features.html` case `texelCopyReaders`): native WebGPU draws the triangle in the
  copied colour, the layer drew nothing (the buffers' old zeros) on the AMD mini PC (Radeon 680M, ANGLE D3D11); any GPU.
- **Cause (webgl2-compat):** the layer lands a copy from a texture a task later (readPixels into a pixel pack buffer
  behind a fence, applied when the fence passes). Only CPU readers (mapping, `bytes()`, copies out of the buffer)
  applied a waiting copy first. Vertex, index and uniform bindings read the GL buffer as it was, and a bind group that
  had copied the storage rows kept them, since the buffer's version moves only when the copy lands. A buffer destroyed
  with a copy still waiting also kept that copy's pixel pack buffer and fence for the life of the context.
- **Fix:** `CompatBuffer.drain()` applies the waiting writes (texture copies forced, a counted stall; query results
  not available yet still wait) without reading the buffer back into its CPU copy; `gl`, indexed draws, the data
  texture, bind groups' storage copies and the compute word textures call it first. `destroy()` frees a waiting
  write's pack buffer, fence or held queries. A write landing in an element buffer binds the draw's vertex array
  again after (it binds none to write). Regressions: `features-browser.mjs` `texelCopyReaders` (both targets
  differ from native without the fix) and `test/pending-copies.test.js` (fails without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the no-adapter check failed every WebGL2 compatibility leg on ANGLE Vulkan (KB-L5a-7)

- **Repro:** on main at 6e254d26e9, `node packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding-browser.mjs` passed its native leg and
  failed its compatibility leg at once with `no-webgpu-adapter` (WebGL renderer "ANGLE (NVIDIA, Vulkan 1.4.351 ...)").
  27 GPU test files launch a leg with `--use-angle=vulkan` (voxel-pathtracer, staging and others).
- **Cause:** the KB-C34i check below requires a WebGPU adapter on every Chromium launch, but Chromium gives a page
  launched on ANGLE Vulkan no WebGPU adapter (Edge 157 on Windows, every such run that day). Those legs test the
  WebGL2 compatibility layer there on purpose.
- **Fix:** `scripts/browser.js` `noAdapterReason`: a launch with `--use-angle=vulkan` needs a hardware WebGL renderer
  instead. A lost GPU process (no renderer, or SwiftShader) still fails at once; every other launch still needs the
  adapter.
- **Regression:** `tests/browser-startup.test.js` "an ANGLE Vulkan launch needs a hardware WebGL renderer, not a WebGPU
  adapter" (fails without the fix).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: an Edge auto-update swapped the browser under a starting GPU suite (KB-C34i)

- **Repro:** shadows `test:gpu` (`scale-browser.mjs`) at 17:29:02 on 2026-11-11: `engine.create` threw "WebGPU adapter
  unavailable", then the suite waited 120 s for `window.ready`. EdgeUpdate had installed 157.0.4341.46 beside the
  running 157.0.4341.42 with a pending `new_msedge.exe`; its rename over `Application\msedge.exe` landed 1.6 s before the
  page error, inside the launch. Forced on a copied Edge install: swapping the top-level file 30 to 160 ms after launch
  ended the browser during launch, 200 to 1500 ms after made every new renderer crash, and a GPU process restart after
  the swap ended the browser; the same three with Edge started from `Application\<version>\msedge.exe` kept working
  (6 of 6, adapter present). Ruled out: a driver reset, memory, a stale adapter LUID, a probe/page race (0 null adapters
  in 140 fresh launches and 30 real suite sessions with 3 other GPU jobs running).
- **Cause:** `launchBrowser` started Edge through Playwright's `msedge` channel, which runs the top-level file the
  updater replaces in place. A second defect let it cost 120 s: `openBrowser` accepted a probe with no WebGPU adapter
  (`softwareAdapterReason` returns null for one), and a wait on `window.ready` ignored the page's startup error.
- **Fix:** `scripts/lib/browser.mjs` starts a Windows channel from the folder of the installed version (the top-level
  file's own file version, never a pending `new_msedge.exe`), falling back to the top-level file only when no version
  folder holds the executable (Chrome's case). `openBrowser` fails at once with code `no-webgpu-adapter`, and a wait on
  `window.ready` fails at once with code `page-startup-error` on an uncaught error or crash before the page is ready.
  Regression: tests/browser-channel-install.test.js (fake install: top-level exe, two version folders, pending
  new_msedge.exe), tests/browser-startup.test.js (null adapter), tests/page-startup.test.js. The forced swap needs a
  copy of the whole Edge install (about 600 MB) and a timed rename, so it stays a manual check, not a GPU test.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: SSR and SSGI kept a clear-colour buffer after disposal

- **Repro:** SSR or SSGI in a partial view (a viewport smaller than the canvas), then dispose it: the 16 byte uniform
  buffer behind its material clear stayed alive until 64 newer colours evicted it or the device went. With
  `ssr: ['SSR'], ssgi: ['SSGI']` in `packages/post/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js`, all 22 `SSR.attach` and
  `SSGI.attach` cases of `check:owners` failed 'no leaked GPU buffers, textures or query sets'.
- **Cause:** `packages/shared/clear-color.js` caches one buffer per colour per device, and nothing released post's
  entries when the pass that made them went away.
- **Fix (0 B in core + stage):** post bundles its own copy of the cache, used only by its material clears. The new
  `releaseClears(device)` export (core never imports it, so core's bundle drops it) hands back the device's cached
  colour buffers; `MaterialClear.dispose()` retires them, and SSR and SSGI call it whenever they release their targets
  (resize, device restore, dispose). Another live clear on the device makes its colour again on its next partial view.
  Tests: `packages/post/test/material-clear.test.js` (fails on the old build: dispose and restore left the buffer),
  `tests/clear-draw.test.js`, and SSR and SSGI in the post owner fixture.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: per-object `device.lost` reactions kept disposed objects alive as long as their device

- **Repro:** make and dispose an object below many times on one live device, then collect garbage: the disposed objects
  stayed reachable from the device's `lost` promise (a heap snapshot shows `GPUDevice.lost` -> PromiseReaction ->
  closure context -> the object). `VoxelPathTracer` grew a test page to 4.7 GB of JavaScript heap over 204 renders
  until it stalled.
- **Cause:** a reaction on `device.lost` cannot be removed, so a closure made per object (and the closure context it
  shares with the object's other closures, which often holds `this`) lived as long as the device.
- **Fix:** one reaction per device over a set the objects leave on dispose, each with a test that fails on the old
  build: the path tracer (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/tracer.test.js`), `@margoengine/inspector` texture capture
  (`test/textures.test.js`), `@margoengine/toon` model hatching (`test/hatch-models.test.js`), `@margoengine/xr`
  (`tests/xr.test.js`), the `@margoengine/biomes` placement and flow session (`tests/gpu-placement-flow.test.js`),
  `@margoengine/materials` texture copies and material uniforms (`test/device-lost.test.js`) and the
  `@margoengine/react` separate roughness map (`test/roughness-feature.test.js`). `packages/biomes/src/gpu.ts`,
  `packages/shader/src/compute.ts`, `packages/shared/frame-resources.js` and `packages/environment/src/environment.ts`
  already kept one reaction per device; `@margoengine/procedural` bakes hold only a `WeakRef` to their controller.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a video texture threw in Firefox (copyExternalImageToTexture refuses video sources)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=firefox node packages/materials/test/browser-check.mjs` (WebGPU, Firefox 157): the `video`
  scenario threw `GPUQueue.copyExternalImageToTexture: 'source' member of GPUCopyExternalImageSourceInfo could not be
  converted to any of: ImageBitmap, HTMLImageElement, HTMLCanvasElement, OffscreenCanvas`.
- **Cause:** Firefox's `copyExternalImageToTexture` takes no `HTMLVideoElement` or `VideoFrame`, which the spec and
  `ImageSource` allow. **Fix:** materials copies the frame through a canvas when the queue throws that TypeError, once per
  queue. Regression: packages/materials/test/texture-region.test.js. Other packages that pass a video to
  `copyExternalImageToTexture` (points, voxel, xr, video) are not checked in Firefox yet.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: README examples stalled behind the previous example's shader compiles in a shared browser

- **Repro:** `npm run check:readme-run -- --packages=voxel-pathtracer` on main c37980e173: the resampled emissive
  lighting example missed its 20 s deadline while waiting for module completion, and the runner then failed closing the
  browser (`browser host ... did not acknowledge the end`). Run alone (`--only=resampled-emissive`) it passed.
- **Cause:** every page example shared one browser; closing a page does not end its GPU process, so shader-compile
  teardown left by the example before held the GPU process the next example's `requestAdapter` waited on.
- **Fix:** `scripts/run-readme-examples.mjs` gives each page example its own browser and closes it, within the same
  20 s deadline; a browser that arrives after the deadline is closed without a page. 27 of 27 examples of the path
  tracer and the WebGL2 layer pass. Regression: `tests/run-readme-examples.test.js` (two tests that fail on the old
  runner).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: every `onSubmittedWorkDone()` on the WebGL2 layer took about 270 ms when no frame was shown

- **Repro:** `npm run check:owners -- --packages=materials` on ANGLE Direct3D 11 (Chrome 157, RTX A6000): the native
  leg passed its 44 cases, the WebGL2-layer leg stopped at its 180 s limit (`OWNER_GPU_TIMEOUT`), the same on main's
  own materials code. Timed per case it was no hang and no shader compile: every case took 2.8, 5.5 or 7.7 s whatever
  the fixture, one step of about 0.28 s per wait after a render, and 44 cases need about 230 s.
- **Cause:** the owner check renders into its own texture and waits with `onSubmittedWorkDone()`, which the layer
  answers with a fence and `gl.flush()`. On Direct3D 11 that fence reported signaled only after about 17 polls (about
  270 ms) on a context that showed no frame; raw WebGL2 with no layer does the same, also for a fence with no work
  before it. A frame shown on a page canvas, or any command after the fence (a 4-byte buffer copy, a pixel-buffer
  `readPixels`), makes it signal on the next poll.
- **Fix:** the device's fence (`fence()` in `packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/tasks.ts`) sends a 4-byte copy between
  two buffers of its own after the fence, before the flush. The fence then signals on the first poll (7 of 7), and the
  materials owner check passes on both legs in 26 s together. No limit changed. Regressions:
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/task-polling.test.js` ("a device fence is followed by a command of its own ...") and
  `packages/webgl2-compat/test/idle-fence-browser.mjs` in `test:gpu` (18 fence checks before, 1 after).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the voxel path tracer's `native4k` check made a timestamp query set the WebGL2 layer refuses (KB-L5a-11)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --no-build --keep-going
  --select=voxel-pathtracer/test:gpu:viewport` on the dev PC (RTX A6000, Edge 157): after `largemodels` the step
  failed with "MargoError: WebGL2 compatibility cannot do timestamp query sets (WebGL2 offers occlusion queries only)",
  on origin/main 152af73651 and on the L5a stack alike.
- **Cause:** `native4k` in `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.html` (from 2db582e970) called
  `createQuerySet({type: 'timestamp'})` with no feature check. The layer has no timestamp queries and refuses them
  with its coded `unsupported` error, as docs/limits.md says, so the case threw before it traced anything. Its
  dispatch check also counted only compute dispatches, and the layer traces through the route's parts instead. The
  library does not make query sets itself: no voxel-pathtracer option reaches the refusal.
- **Fix:** without the `timestamp-query` feature the case asserts the refusal (a `MargoError` coded `unsupported`
  naming timestamp query sets), renders the same 4K frames raw and denoised without GPU times, and checks the
  route's parts instead of trace dispatches: each part's `start` program is counted with the paths its place
  covers, at most 2^17 (`PART_PATHS`, src/compat.ts). The traced size, `limitedBy`, errors and messages are checked
  on both backends as before. On the layer, 2026-11-15: 105 route parts for each tracer, the largest 61,440 paths,
  3840 x 2160 traced at its native size; the step passed in 277.9 s (Direct3D 11), and natively in 25.4 s.
- **Regression:** `npm run test:gpu:viewport --workspace @margoengine/voxel-pathtracer` under `MARGO_COMPAT=1`
  (fails on the old page at `native4k` with the refusal above).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: `MARGO_COMPAT=1 test:gpu:resampled` died with no output about 5 minutes in (KB-L5a-3)

- **Repro:** `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/gpu-package-tests.mjs --no-build --only=voxel-pathtracer`, or the same test
  alone: exit 1 about 5 minutes after start with no line from the test, 4 times of 4
  (RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11, 2026-11-11 10:16 to 10:36 local). The native run of the same script passes; its own
  WebGL2 leg runs on ANGLE Vulkan. No driver reset (nvlddmkm 153) happened after 09:23 that day, so not those.
- **Cause 1 (tooling, the silence):** each exit is an `ERR_GPU_IDLE_RECLAIM` line in the run's log
  at the same second. The old runner's idle monitor ended the whole tree, the holder first, so the runner and
  gpu-package-tests were killed by `taskkill /F` before they could print anything; the reason went only to that log.
  That half is the old runner's own row, KB-GPULOCK-SILENT-RECLAIM (removed with it on 2026-11-16, KB-GPULOCK-ALL).
- **Cause 2 (the tracer, the idle GPU):** `ResampledVoxelPathTracer` looped its proposals (8 by default) inside one
  pass of the light kinds, around `directionalEmitter()` (a `closest()` walk) and `shadow()`, so the WebGL2 route's
  staged `sample` program held two traversals. fxc compiled it for minutes with the GPU idle, past the old runner's 3-minute
  idle window: about 645 s with the literal bound; with the bound read from the frame (an unlanded first fix, which
  also rendered the variant black: its proposal count never reached the kernel) 254 s at link plus 356 s again at
  the first draw. ANGLE Direct3D 11 compiles every program with two or more colour outputs twice (probe in
  `docs/architecture/operational-playbook.md`, the staged route), so code size counts double there.
- **Fix (the tracer):** the resampled kernel runs one proposal per pass of light kind 1
  (`const KIND_REPEAT=vec2u(1u,P)`; natively the loop returns to kind 1 until all P ran; the WebGL2 route draws kind 1's
  `sample`, `shadow` and `gather` P times, `StagedTrace.steps`), the reservoir in private state, so no staged program
  holds more than one traversal. Same proposals, random numbers and sums in the same order. Regressions:
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js` ("no staged program of ... reaches more than one traversal
  call", "the route runs one pass of light kind 1 per resampled proposal"), which fail on the old code.
- **After:** RTX A6000, ANGLE Direct3D 11, cold (`MARGO_COMPAT=1`, 2026-11-11 17:00): the RIS page's 8-proposal programs
  link in 49 s and compile at first draw in 127 s (610 s before), the whole page in 416 s, inside the 3-minute
  idle window then in use, no reclaim. The image is the same bit for bit on WebGPU against the old kernel (10 scenes, 2 to 64
  proposals, 768 values each); on ANGLE Vulkan too, except 78 of 768 values 1 unit in the last place apart at 2
  proposals (the driver's contraction of the same expression in another program).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the path tracer sampled light at one surface vertex past `maxBounces` (KB-L5a-1, found by KB0986b)

- **Repro:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/resampled.html`, case `scattering media vertices` (a density-1.5,
  albedo-0.8 half-block media slab between an orthographic camera and a white floor under an emissive ceiling,
  `maxBounces: 1`, 16 batches of each tracer): `ResampledVoxelPathTracer` read 0.2729 against the root tracer's 0.2469
  (six standard errors 0.0032). Rough metal and plastic receivers matched.
- **Cause:** the root kernel (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/shaders.ts`, the path loop) counts a medium's scattering
  event before its light sampling and ends the path when the count passes `maxBounces`, but at a surface it sampled
  light first and counted after. A surface reached after `maxBounces` events (the floor under a medium vertex at
  `maxBounces: 1`) therefore added the light-sampled MIS share of a path one event too long, while the limit cut that
  path's BSDF share. The root tracer added a fraction of that path (0.0013 here), the RIS reservoir, whose proposals
  partition the whole integral, all of it (0.0273). The RIS weights themselves were right: with the root fixed the two
  agree at 1, 2 and 4 bounces, with and without half-block shapes (0.2456 against 0.2455; 0.3626 against 0.3623;
  0.6028 against 0.6032; standard errors 0.0003 to 0.0008).
- **Fix:** a surface vertex samples light only while fewer than `maxBounces` events lie behind it; a medium already
  checked its count where it scatters. The light it met on arrival still counts, so a path holds at most `maxBounces`
  scattering events, as `maxBounces` is documented. Every tracer built on the root kernel (resampled, guided, media,
  mesh, spectral and the WebGL2 route) takes the same rule.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs` `bouncelimit` (a floor lit only off the ceiling
  by an up-facing see-through panel is exactly black at `maxBounces: 1`; the old kernel lit it), and
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/resampled-browser.mjs` (the rough metal, plastic coat and scattering media receivers
  of KB0986b against the root tracer, six standard errors and under 0.02).
- **Sources:** J. Talbot, D. Cline, P. Egbert, "Importance Resampling for Global Illumination", EGSR 2005,
  https://doi.org/10.2312/EGWR/EGSR05/139-146; B. Bitterli, C. Wyman, M. Pharr, P. Shirley, A. Lefohn, W. Jarosz,
  "Spatiotemporal reservoir resampling for real-time ray tracing with dynamic direct lighting", ACM TOG 39(4) 2020,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/3386569.3392481 (sections 2 and 3: the RIS weight p-hat over the proposal density);
  C. Wyman, M. Kettunen, D. Lin, B. Bitterli, C. Yuksel, W. Jarosz, P. Kozlowski, "A Gentle Introduction to ReSTIR",
  SIGGRAPH 2023 course, https://doi.org/10.1145/3587423.3595511 (section 3.3: balance MIS over mixed proposals);
  E. Veach, L. Guibas, "Optimally Combining Sampling Techniques for Monte Carlo Rendering", SIGGRAPH 1995,
  https://doi.org/10.1145/218380.218498 (multi-sample balance heuristic); M. Pharr, W. Jakob, G. Humphreys, Physically
  Based Rendering, 4th ed., 2023, section 13.4, https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Light_Transport_I_Surface_Reflection/A_Better_Path_Tracer
  (the depth test before light sampling); J. Novak, I. Georgiev, J. Hanika, W. Jarosz, "Monte Carlo Methods for
  Volumetric Light Transport Simulation", Computer Graphics Forum 37(2) 2018, https://doi.org/10.1111/cgf.13383
  (free-flight sampling and next-event estimation at medium vertices).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the guided path tracer's test used the guided tracer as its own reference (KB0986a)

- **Repro:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding.html` took its convergence reference from
  `GuidedVoxelPathTracer` at 16,384 samples, so a bias in the guide's mixture PDF would appear in both the reference and
  the image under test and pass; the coverage scenes compared single images against an absolute 0.02.
- **Cause:** the test was written before the root tracer could render the caustic scene at enough samples in time.
- **Fix:** the reference is the root `VoxelPathTracer` (no guide) at 65,536 samples in 8 seeds, each tracer attached once
  for all its seeds; every coverage scene compares 16 batch means of each estimator and the difference must stay under
  0.02 and under six standard errors, so dim scenes (coloured glass, 6 SE 0.004 to 0.010) are held to their own noise.
  Passed on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/guiding-browser.mjs` (with `tests/guiding.html`).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a voxel path tracer run could overrun a small GPU's watchdog (KB-BL1, AMD mini PC Radeon 680M)

- **Repro:** a path tracer GPU suite on the AMD mini PC mini PC (Radeon 680M, integrated) crashed the machine. The tracer's
  bound was 2^20 paths a dispatch (bug 25), measured on the RTX A6000 at the default 8 bounces: it did not count the
  path loop (1,312 iterations a path at `maxBounces` 64 against 192 at 8, 6.8 times the work), nor the GPU (the 680M
  runs the tracer about ten times slower), and the viewport put all of a frame's bands in the frame's one submission,
  which a GPU that preempts only between submissions (AMD reports packet boundaries; KB4037 above) runs as one piece
  against Windows' 2 s watchdog. `renderImage` dispatched a whole tile (up to 1,088 x 1,088 paths) at once.
- **Cause:** the work bound counted paths, not path-iterations, per dispatch rather than per submission, and was fixed
  to one GPU's speed.
- **Fix (`packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/dispatch.ts`, `src/tracer.ts`):** a submission carries at most 2^20 x 192
  path-iterations (`SUBMIT_WORK`; fewer paths at more bounces), and a tracer starts at a sixteenth of that, then sizes
  its row bands to what its own GPU finished in 50 ms (`WorkPacer`, from submission to completion, at most twice the
  step before). Every viewport band and every `renderImage` band is a submission of its own. Bands change no pixel's
  sums and sample runs follow the fixed figure, so images do not depend on the GPU's speed: the browser check's
  `determinism` case renders with one 8-row band a submission and gets the same image bit for bit. The WebGL2 route
  already submits one part (2^17 paths) for one window (8 iterations) at a time, within the first budget. A converged
  viewport submits nothing; a hidden tab draws no frames. Every shader loop is bounded by structure: the path loop by
  `limit`, light loops by uniform counts, brick and cell walks step one cell along one axis each turn and stop outside
  the grid (a NaN distance steps z), the instance tree visits each node once.
- **Regression:** `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/dispatch-budget.test.js` (work per submission at 64 bounces, one
  submission a band, the first budget a sixteenth, renderImage bands, converged frames submit nothing, the route's
  window); three of its tests fail on the old code. `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs` `determinism`
  (bands change no value). The machine-profile fallback that let the suite run there is fixed separately. `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/tracer.test.js` capture
  (paced and with the smallest bands): its fake GPU filled a tile's read-back from the last band's frame uniform, so
  under CPU load, when the pacer chose several bands a tile, the check saw a seam at 1024,1024 that the tracer did not
  make; the fake now takes the tile's first band, and the smallest-band variant fails on the old fake every run.
- **Sources:** Microsoft, [Timeout Detection and Recovery (TDR)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/timeout-detection-and-recovery)
  (2 s default, per scheduled packet); Microsoft, [DXGI_COMPUTE_PREEMPTION_GRANULARITY](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dxgi1_2/ne-dxgi1_2-dxgi_compute_preemption_granularity)
  (DMA buffer, dispatch, thread group, thread boundaries); S. Laine, T. Karras, T. Aila, "Megakernels Considered
  Harmful: Wavefront Path Tracing on GPUs", HPG 2013 (bounded work per launch).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the path tracer's transparent render never compiled on Direct3D 11 (WebGL2 layer)

- **Repro:** `transparent` of `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/browser-check.mjs` with `MARGO_COMPAT=1` on ANGLE
  Direct3D 11, a fresh browser profile: the CPU sat in the driver's shader compiler with the GPU idle, and the case was
  stopped at the 22 minute limit without finishing; the whole compat check never passed.
- **Cause:** the `coverage` kernel in `packages/voxel-pathtracer/src/shaders.ts` looped a constant 64 times around a
  traversal (`closest()`), and fxc unrolled it into 64 traversals.
- **Fix:** the loop takes its bound from the frame uniform (`tile.w`, written as 64 by the tracer), so the program holds
  one traversal; the same image hashes on WebGPU, and `transparent` passes in 89.4 s. Regression:
  `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/compat-staged.test.js` ("layer-compiled kernels ... hold no constant-bound loop around
  a traversal").

### Fixed 2026-11-11: VirtualShadows lost a centimetre model's shadow, and a model framed from kilometres

- **Repro:** `node packages/shadows/test/scale-browser.mjs --virtual`: before the fix the 1 mm, 2 cm, 1 km, 2 cm with
  core's default camera and BoomBox cases kept every umbra pixel lit (4,626 of 4,626; the BoomBox shaded 0 pixels).
- **Cause:** `VirtualShadows` defaults were fixed world lengths: a depth bias of 0.002 and a normal offset of 0.02 (the
  whole size of a 2 cm model), a 500 unit reach (a camera 3 km away was outside it) and with it level 0 texels of 4.4 mm.
- **Fix:** each receiver moves a quarter texel of the page it reads along its normal and compares 2^-20 of the depth
  range nearer the light, a range that scales with the reach (`bias` and `normalBias` add to them, default 0); an unset `distance` and `casterMargin` scale by powers of two
  with the camera's target distance (`reachScale` in `packages/shadows/src/pages.ts`: 1 from 1 to 25 units, finer
  closer, at least 20 times it farther), the pool rebuilt on an octave change. Regression:
  `packages/shadows/test/scale-browser.mjs --virtual` (1 mm to 1 km, the default camera and the BoomBox, WebGPU and
  MARGO_COMPAT=1) and `packages/shadows/test/virtual-pages.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a model a few centimetres across cast no visible directional shadow

- **Repro:** the loading-gltf guide with the Khronos BoomBox (about 2 cm) at its own size: the floor showed no shadow.
- **Cause:** three `Shadows` defaults were fixed world lengths, right for a model of about a metre and wrong at other
  scales. A model (`loadGLTF`, materials' `createMesh`) never fitted the cascades, which fit only core meshes, so they
