### A blurred edge of DOF spreads to one side only

**Status:** closed (KB1843 fixed in 049b4107e; proof: packages/cinematic/test/browser-check.mjs).

- **What:** a card out of focus in `@margoengine/dof` should spread across its outline, half inside and half outside. A far card
  fades inward and stops dead at its outline (row values 20, 154, 164 and on up to 208, RTX A6000); a near card spreads outward and
  keeps its full value inside (147, then 208).
- **Repro:** `node packages/cinematic/test/browser-check.mjs` draws both cards; print the middle row of the picture in `edge`.
- **Cause:** by design of the gathers, not yet fixed. The far gather takes only samples at the centre's depth or behind it, so sky
  behind a far card takes nothing from the card. The near gather always counts the foreground centre, at full weight.
- **Needed to close:** decide from the published work on gather depth of field how a pixel behind a blurred edge takes its share
  without a sharp subject leaking onto its background, build it in `@margoengine/dof` and test the edge profile on the GPU.

Lane A sweep reproduces the original card profiles on current main, with no
GPU errors. At far-card x=464 with near focus, the green row jumps directly
20 -> 154 -> 164 -> 173: background pixels receive no far-card contribution.
With far focus, the near-card x=244 reaches 147 immediately before 208 and
stays full-strength inside. Source audit confirms the far depth predicate and
forced full near coverage still own these two asymmetries. A correction needs
source-footprint coverage and a distinct background estimate at silhouettes;
simply removing the depth predicate would not establish sharp-foreground
occlusion. Compared Demers (2004), Hammon (2007) and Potmesil/Chakravarty (1981),
cited in clean-room.md. No speculative shader or weaker edge bar was landed.

Fixed 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L3b, KB1843): the gathers are now scatter as gather in two layers (Jimenez 2014; Kraus and Strengert 2007; clean-room.md D-10). The far gather also counts a far sample in front of the centre where its own disk reaches the centre, weighted by the centre's disk area over its own, laid over the behind layer by the coverage the weights add up to; a near centre counts as one tap's share of its own disk instead of full coverage, and its background is the visible background within its disk. Measured on the RTX A6000, 512 x 512, middle row, pixels more than 4 levels off the sharp picture: far card 11 inside, 0 outside before and 11 inside, 12 outside after; near card 10 inside, 11 outside after (it was 147 then 208, full inside, before). A sharp subject still leaks nothing: its disk is under a pixel. DOFLens shapes follow through the same covers test (polygon, aperture image, cat's eye, anamorphic). Regression: packages/dof/tests/gpu/lens-check.mjs (edge cases, fails before: far 11 in, 0 out), WebGL2 layer packages/dof/tests/gpu/compat-check.mjs.

## Checks

- Fixed 2026-11-27: launch gate 4 (`scripts/basic-scene-network.mjs`) failed on main (c192bdcb2e) with "the build emits no unrelated optional pack", naming `assets/model-B16_Idts-CN0rSkyN.js`, the glTF model chunk the basic scene needs (KB-SCENE-HASHNAME1). Cause: the check matched `sky|particles|post|environment|shadows` and `worker` against emitted file names, which carry Vite's and the packages' content hashes, so any build whose hash spelled one of the words failed; the same test also never caught a pack's root entry, emitted as `dist-<hash>.js`. Fix: `unrelatedFiles` (`scripts/support/basic-scene-graph.mjs`) reads each file's manifest source, so a pack is a chunk from the sky, particles, post, environment or shadows package or one of the stage's feature entries, and a file with no manifest record is read without Vite's 8-character hash. Regression: `tests/basic-scene-graph.test.js` ("an optional pack or a stray worker is read from the manifest source").

- Fixed 2026-11-11: suite dev servers watched files, and a rebuild reloaded a suite's page. check:owners sky on the WebGL2 layer failed once on a loaded machine with "Execution context was destroyed, most likely because of a navigation", passing on rerun (sweep0, 2026-11-11). `startDevServer` asks Vite for `watch: null`, but Vite's mergeConfig skips null values, so the root `vite.config.mjs`'s `watch: { ignored }` won and every suite's server ran a chokidar watcher over the files it had served. Rewriting a served module (a package's `npm test` rebuilds its dist, often beside the checks in one worktree) made Vite send the page a full reload, and the next `page.evaluate` failed. Measured: a page served by `openBrowser` reloaded within 3 s of its module being rewritten. Fix: the server's own first plugin sets `server.watch` to null in `configResolved`, so Vite starts its no-op watcher. Regression: `tests/dev-server-watch.test.js` (both cases fail on the parent).

- Fixed 2026-11-11: check:readme-run: after an example hits its 20 s limit, closing the owned browser threw `browser host <pid> did not acknowledge the end: null` from scripts/lib/browser.mjs (2026-11-10, lane U). Repro: before the companion fix, `npm run check:readme-run -- --packages=worker` on unchanged main. Cause (traced 2026-11-11): the browser was closed twice, once by the example's deadline handler and once more for the shared browser at the end of the run (349243b3d3). The first bounded close released its host; the second asked the released host to end again, and a released host answers `null`. Fix: `withBoundedClose` closes a browser once, as Playwright's own `close()` does, and a second call shares the first one's outcome (since 242e8a7542 each example also owns its browser and one close). Regression: `tests/browser-teardown.test.js` ("closing a browser twice").

### Fixed 2026-11-11: SSAO's orthographic picture moved with the eye (KB1900)

- **Was:** `scripts/ssao-gpu-check.js` failed on main and was the one `*-gpu-check.js` file no check ran (`LOOSE_CHECKS`):
  moving an orthographic eye along its view from 6 m to 0.6 m changed the picture, 87 bytes past 2 levels and one
  pixel at the right screen edge (x = 399) by 17.
- **Cause, two parts:** the kernels read view depth from the gbuffer's half-float `w` (about 0.004 m at 6 m, so the range
  check and the blur's depth weights quantized differently at each eye distance), and the extractor chose the neighbour
  with the smaller depth step even at the screen edge, where the clamped neighbour is the pixel itself, a zero-length
  difference that always read as smaller.
- **Fix (`@margoengine/post`):** the extractor also writes view depth to an `r32float` target that the SSAO and GTAO
  kernels and both blur passes read (a full-precision camera-space depth, as in McGuire, Mara and Luebke, "Scalable
  Ambient Obscurance", HPG 2012, https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2012-06_scalable-ambient-obscurance), and the
  derivative takes only a neighbour that exists. The gbuffer keeps its half-float `w` for sources that write it.
  Native WebGPU is now exact (0 bytes); the WebGL2 layer moves 4 interior pixels by 1 level (0 past 2).
- **The check's IBL bar:** with the direct light on, IBL creases read 4.0 and 2.0 display levels on main (bars: more
  than 4 and 2, set 2026-10-14, before the display curve change of 2026-10-17); the IBL cases now turn the direct light
  off so IBL is the only light, and read 26.9 and 14.9 (perspective) and 23.1 and 15.4 (orthographic) natively. The
  bars are unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/post/test/ssao.test.js` (the view depth target and the edge rule; fails on the parent) and
  `scripts/ssao-gpu-check.js`, now post's `test:gpu:ssao` (eye move over 0 past 2 and worst at most 1; fails on the
  parent with 87 and 17). `LOOSE_CHECKS` is empty.
- **Work:** one more `r32float` target (4 B a pixel, 3.7 MB at 1080p) written once a frame; the occlusion kernel's samples
  read 4 B of it in place of 8 B of the gbuffer, and each blur tap reads it beside the gbuffer. Perspective SSAO pictures move by at most 5 levels (5,340 bytes of 480,000 in the
  check's frame) from the precision change.

### Closed 2026-11-11: KB1926, boulder on the WebGL2 layer is the accepted per-sample MSAA difference

- **Cause:** SSAO. Its extractor reads the post stack's 1x depth, which `SceneTarget.copyDepth`
  (packages/shared/msaa.js) makes from the nearest of the 4 samples natively; WebGL2 cannot read one sample, so the
  layer reads the blit-resolved sample, and SSAO's range check turns that depth step into occlusion on hold, bolt hole
  and robot edges. Proof, one change each on the high tier: SSAO off, 1x MSAA, or a native depth copy that keeps sample 0
  all give 0.000% of pixels with d > 2 (max d 5); Bloom off, PCF shadows or no light probe leave 1.02%. This is the
  accepted difference of 2026-10-31 (docs/webgl2-compat-demos.md, "Accepted difference: per-sample reads of
  multisampled textures"), now with a boulder row; nothing in Margo samples wrongly.
- **Recorded:** `npm run visual:compat -- --only=boulder --write`: differs, d > 2 on 1.02%, mean 0.137, max 66, native
  exact. The gate fails the demo if it gets worse than 1.5 times that. Pin: tests/visual-compat-status.test.js ("boulder is
  recorded as the per-sample MSAA difference").
- **KB-RM3, the same failure:** local CI's full run of 2026-11-11 15:00 (097cf04ab4) failed `visual:compat` on boulder with
  "not in visual-compat-expected.json" at 1.78% (mean 0.473, max 79), the numbers of 2026-11-07. The boulder model
  change 3f258cf9da (KB1914) landed after that run, so it did not cause it. The share fell to 1.02% with bc82057e40
  (KB1900, SSAO reads full-precision view depth), also after that run; the layer before and after KB0477 measures 1.02%.

Earlier record:

- **What:** `npm run visual:compat` fails on `boulder`: the WebGL2 capture differs from the native WebGPU one on 1.78%
  of pixels by more than 2 of 255 (mean 0.473, max 79), while two native captures are identical. The differences are
  spread over the textured climbing walls and the grey side wall, not at object edges. The demo has no entry in
  `scripts/support/visual-compat-expected.json` (it replaced the Light Keeper, whose entry went with it).
- **Repro:** `npm run visual:compat -- --only=boulder` (RTX A6000, Edge 157.0.4341.42, 2026-11-07); the report is
  `test-results/visual-compat/index.html` with `boulder.diff.png`.
- **Cause, not yet found:** the same numbers on the commit before the core instance-row and writePoses commits and
  after them, so those commits are ruled out. The spread over textured surfaces points at texture sampling or shadow
  filtering in `@margoengine/webgl2-compat`, which is where the next look goes.
  Ruled out (2026-11-08): the CPU compute tier's NaN encoding (fixed above), as the comparison is WebGL2 against
  WebGPU drawing, not the CPU tier's two paths, and a NaN's bits change no colour.
- **Needed to close:** the cause fixed in the package that owns it with a regression test, or recorded with
  `--write` as an explained difference, as the other demos that differ are.

### USD composition: stress stages that mix classes, variants and repeated sites

**Status:** closed (fixed 2026-11-26, KB1942c part 36; proof: every stage of both seeds that OpenUSD opens composes as OpenUSD does in values, targets and the order of every prim's specs, and each rule is pinned by its part's black-box test).

- **What:** generated stress stages (`packages/usdz/tests/oracle/generate-stages.py`) against OpenUSD 26.11 (usd-core from PyPI, black box): none of the 149 OpenUSD opens differ in a property of some prim with seed 1942 (44 before KB1942, 33 before KB1942b, 24 before KB1942c, 23 before its part 2, 22 before its part 3, 20 before its part 6, 13 before its part 8, 12 before its part 10, 5 before its part 25, 3 before its part 26, 2 before its part 28, 1 before its part 30), none of 150 with seed 7 (54, then 48, then 40, then 36, then 31, then 29, then 28, then 15, then 3, then 2, then 1 before part 29). OpenUSD itself stops on stage 142 of seed 1942 (`PcpCompareSiblingNodeStrength` reports a failed verification, "Did not find copied specialize node", and the stage does not open), so that stage has no answer to compare and is not counted as a difference. They nest classes, variants and references far past real files. No real file in the corpus shows it. `packages/usdz/tests/stress-stages.test.js` builds both seeds (`tests/stress-stages.js`, the same files byte for byte), compares them with OpenUSD readings recorded in `tests/fixtures/stress/openusd-<seed>.json.gz` and holds the stages that still differ in a list that may only shrink, empty since part 30: a stage that matches today and differs after a change fails it.
- **Fixed (KB1942):** where an authored specializes arc ranks against the copies it implies upstream. Pinned on 42 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-family.test.js`): the implied copies come first, in stack order, unless the arc was authored under a variant or a reference whose own prim sits shallower in its namespace than the stage prim holding the outermost reference (a reference inside a variant counts from the variant's prim). Eleven stages of seed 1942 and six of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942b):** relationship targets reached through a class arc that an ancestor's inherit implies in a stack above. Pinned on 10 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-class-targets.test.js`, fixture `implied-class-targets.json`): the implied arc keeps the ancestor's own pair (the class root to the ancestor), its prim mapped by the arcs on the way where they can and left as authored where they cannot, so `/C/b` maps to `/M/b` and an authored `/M/...` target, which would not map back to itself, drops. Nine stages of seed 1942 and eight of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now. `packages/usdz/tests/fixtures/open-difference` now composes as OpenUSD does (`/Q/b/c/c/c/a/c/a.v0` is 642).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 1):** relationship targets through a chain of internal arcs (an internal reference, or a class arc, under another). Pinned on 10 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/internal-chain-targets.test.js`, fixture `internal-chain-targets.json`): OpenUSD maps a target once through the chain's composed map function, each arc's pairs plus the root identity an internal arc carries, not arc by arc; `/M/a` authored on `/Shared` drops on `/M`, which references `/Shared`, but stays `/M/a` on `/Y`, which references `/M`, and `/Y/c` drops there. Stage 99 of seed 1942 and stages 36, 124, 128 and 135 of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 2):** the specifier of a prim that a class and a weaker `def` both reach through class arcs. Pinned on 6 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-specifier.test.js`): a class reached by an inherit gives way to a weaker `def`, as before, but a class reached through a specializes arc stays a class, even before a `def` that a weaker specializes arc brings (`/R/b` specializes `/C`, `/R/b/c` specializes `/C` again: OpenUSD composes `/R/b/c` as a class, so its default traversal leaves it out). Stage 35 of seed 1942 and stages 70, 72, 80, 81 and 95 of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 3):** where an implied class arc stops. Pinned on 12 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-class-stops.test.js`, read with `Usd.Prim.GetChildren()` and the public prim index dump): a class arc authored in a variant of a referenced prim implies nothing above a node of its own stack that already holds the same site (stage 50: `/M/c/b` specializes `/C/a`, its variant inherits `/C/a` too, and `/P/b/b/c/b` gets no `/C/a`); and a specializes arc whose site an inherit of the same stack already reaches implies nothing upstream unless its node has another class arc of its own (stage 57). Stages 27 and 50 of seed 1942 and 132 and 136 of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 4):** one class site reached twice in a prim index, once by a class arc carried down from the parent prim and once by an arc placed for the prim itself. Pinned on 4 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/carried-class-site.test.js`, values from `Usd.Attribute.Get()`, the later arc marked inert in the public prim index dump): the carried arc keeps the site and its own place, so an inherit carried down makes the class stronger than the variant that authors the later arc and a specializes carried down keeps it weaker, whichever kind the later arc is (the reduced form of stage 25: `/M/a/a.v1` is 28). Stage 45 of seed 7 now matches; stage 25 of seed 1942 still differs elsewhere (`/Q/b`); none that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 5):** two variant sets reaching one class site, one authored on the site (`/C/a`) and one carried down from its parent (`/C`). The Strength Ordering section ranks arcs of one kind by how deep in namespace they were authored; Margo ranked both sets by the depth of the stage prim, a tie, and took the carried set first. Pinned on 3 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/variant-set-depth.test.js`: an inherit, a reference and a specializes to `/C/a`, `/Q.v` is 2 on OpenUSD). The stress values do not change; the prim stacks of stages 103 and 141 of seed 1942 now match.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 6):** one site reached twice in a prim index. Margo built a prim index by copying whole site trees composed earlier; OpenUSD (black box, its public prim index dump) builds it as one list of tasks. Now `tree()` in `stage.ts` does too: references, payloads, inherits and specializes run as tasks, a higher kind always first and nodes in the order they were queued (the nodes carried down from the parent prim in tree order, keeping the order they were made in); then the implied class arcs, strongest node first; then one variant set at a time. An arc to a root prim is a bare node whose own arcs the index follows; one to a deeper prim is that prim's index composed alone. The first live node made for a site holds it: a later inherit to it makes no node, a later specializes leaves an inert placeholder, a grafted index leaves out its class nodes on a held site, and of two nodes for one site reached through class arcs the later gives no opinions. A specializes arc below the index root leaves an inert placeholder where it was authored, which implies its arc upward, and its node goes under the root, ranking in its family from the placeholder. This replaces three rules of `strength()` (a site an authored arc reaches gives no opinions through an implied arc; a class site met again counts once, through the later arc; a class arc placed for the prim on a site carried down gives no opinions). Pinned on 29 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/prim-index-queue.test.js`, fixture `prim-index-queue.json`: every spec of each stage is marked so its values spell out each prim's stack, read with `Usd.Attribute.Get()`). Stages 8 15 26 86 87 132 of seed 1942 and 5 20 38 40 41 56 71 79 111 112 131 142 143 of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now. Prims whose stack of specs differs from OpenUSD's `GetPrimStack()`: 200 of 15,579 (756 before) and 217 of 19,445 (1,337 before).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 7):** which ancestral variants a class site keeps when an ancestor's arc brings it in. A specializes node carried down from an ancestor inside a grafted index now moves under the index root as its site composed alone, so a variant the referencing prim selected on the class's ancestor is left out (`/M` specializes `/C`, selects `vs = y`, `/R/a` references `/M/a`: no `/C{vs=y}a`). An implied class arc that stands for an arc carried down from prim A takes its ancestral variants from A's index in the stack it joins (mapped there where the arcs on the way can, as authored where they cannot): from that index's node of the same kind for the site when it has one, else from the variants of its node for the site's parent, carried down; a stack with no A keeps the class composed alone. Pinned on 15 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/ancestral-variants.test.js`, fixture `ancestral-variants.json`), 7 of which fail without the change. Found on the way: a root prim whose index an earlier prim had already built through an arc (`/A` references `/M/x`, `/M` after it) was left off the stage; it is composed now (`packages/usdz/tests/compose.test.js`). The stress values do not change; the prim stacks of stage 4 of seed 1942 and stages 53 and 82 of seed 7 now match, and stage 139 of seed 7 matches on 1 more prim. Prims whose stack of specs differs: 198 of 15,579 and 212 of 19,448 (seed 7 now composes 3 root prims it left off before).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 8):** which variant selections set the ancestral variants of an implied class arc that stands for an arc carried down from prim A. Part 7 copied them from A's index; OpenUSD (black box) reads the selections of A in context, then the class's own. Below the index root that context is the site that authored the arc into the stack the implied arc joins, at the path A maps to there (`/P/c` references `l2.usda`, whose `/M/a/a` references `l1.usda</M/a>`, where `/M` inherits `/C`: a selection on `/P/c` sets `l2.usda /C`'s set for `/P/c/a/a`, one on `/P`, `/P/c/a` or `/P/c/a/a` does not), and the nodes of other stacks in the index of the stage prim A maps to; at the index root it is A's own index in that stack, only when the stack holds the layer that authored the arc, and never the node that stands for this same arc there. Pinned on 12 more black-box stages in `packages/usdz/tests/ancestral-variants.test.js` (27 in all), 5 of which fail without the change. Stage 5 of seed 1942 now matches; none that matched before differs now. Prims whose stack of specs differs: 194 of 15,579 (198 before) and 208 of 19,448 (212 before).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 9):** the order of one specializes family whose authored arc sits inside a grafted index (a reference or payload to a deeper prim, composed alone). Margo decided once, for the whole tree, whether the implied arcs come before or after the authored one. OpenUSD (black box) decides it per graft: the implied arcs placed inside a graft go by that graft's own reference (authored on a prim no deeper than the arc: before it; deeper: after it), and those outside every graft by the whole tree, as before. In the reduced form of stage 86 of seed 1942, `l1.usda</M/a>` is grafted under a payload to `l2.usda</M>` and its ancestral payload's `/M/a` specializes `/C/a`: `l1.usda /C/a` now comes before the authored `l0.usda /C/a` on `/R/c/a` and `l2.usda /C/a` after it. Pinned on 7 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-family-grafts.test.js`, fixture `specializes-family-grafts.json`), 4 of which fail without the change. The stress values do not change; prims whose stack of specs differs: 190 of 15,579 (194 before) and 200 of 19,448 (208 before).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 10):** where each implied arc of a specializes family ranks against its authored arc. KB1942's rule decided it once for the whole family, from the outermost reference or payload around the authored arc; part 9 decided it per grafted index. OpenUSD (black box) decides it per implied arc: the reference or payload that counts is the outermost one around the authored arc's node up to the node the implied arc hangs from, and when that is the node itself, it counts from the prim that authored it. In the reduced form of stage 16 of seed 1942 (`/Q/a/c` has a payload to `l2.usda</M>`, whose variant's `b` has a payload to `l1.usda`, where a variant's `/M/a/c` specializes `/C`), `l2.usda /C`, implied under that variant, comes before the authored `l1.usda /C` and `root.usda /C` after it. Pinned on 2 more black-box stages in `packages/usdz/tests/specializes-family-grafts.test.js` (9 in all), both stress stages reduced with a black-box reducer, which fail without the change; the 7 there before still hold, and the graft mark of part 9 is gone. Stage 13 of seed 1942 and stages 24, 39 and 115 of seed 7 now match; none that matched before differs now. Prims whose stack of specs differs: 101 of 15,579 (190 before) and 99 of 19,448 (200 before).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 11):** a specializes arc authored on the root of a grafted index whose site the index already holds through an inherit of the same stack (`/Q` references `l0.usda</X/S>`, which specializes `/K`, and an `l0.usda` prim that inherits `/K`). Margo left the arc out of the graft, or let it imply nothing because an inherit of its stack reached the site, so `root.usda /K` came in as an inherit, strong. OpenUSD (black box) keeps an inert placeholder that implies its arc upward all the same: `root.usda /K` comes last, as a specializes, and the inherit implies nothing there. An arc authored deeper in the graft (in a variant, say) already left its own placeholder where it was authored, which carries the arc as before. Pinned on 6 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/held-specializes-grafts.test.js`, fixture `held-specializes-grafts.json`), 5 of which fail without the change. The stress values and prim stacks do not change.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 12):** a class arc implied from a class node that a grafted index (a reference to a deeper prim, composed alone) leaves out because the index it joins already holds the node's site. Margo left out the node and what is under it but kept the arcs implied from it, which hang elsewhere in the graft. OpenUSD (black box) leaves them out too: `/P` references `l0.usda`, whose `/M` inherits `/C`, so `/P/a` holds `l0.usda /C/a`; `/P/a` also references `l1.usda</M/a>`, where `/M` references `l0.usda` and the inherit implies `l1.usda /C`, and `/P/a` gets no `l1.usda /C/a` (with `l1.usda` referencing a copy of `l0.usda` it does). Pinned on 3 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/held-class-implied.test.js`, fixture `held-class-implied.json`), 2 of which fail without the change. The stress values do not change; stage 21 of seed 1942 now differs on 10 prims (22 before), and prims whose stack of specs differs are 89 of 15,579 (101 before) and 99 of 19,448.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 13):** a specializes placeholder carried down to a child prim inside a reference that gets a class arc of its own at that prim. Margo kept the implied inherit carried down from the parent prim on the class site; OpenUSD (black box) implies the placeholder's arc again at the child, and that specializes takes the site: `/P` inherits `/C` and references `l2.usda</M>`, `/P/a` references `l2.usda` (default prim `/M`), `l2.usda /M/a` specializes `/C` and `/M/a/a` inherits `/C`, so at `/P/a/a/a` `root.usda /C/a` ranks after `l2.usda /M/a/a`, as a specializes. With the specializes on another prim whose reference gets no class arc there, or authored on the referenced prim itself (its placeholder is gone one prim down), the carried inherit stays. Pinned on 5 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/carried-placeholder-reimplied.test.js`, fixture `carried-placeholder-reimplied.json`), 3 of which fail without the change. The stress values do not change; stage 47 of seed 1942 now matches its prim stacks (2 prims before); prims whose stack differs: 87 of 15,579 (89 before), 99 of 19,448.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 14):** the ancestral variants of an implied inherit that stands for another implied arc, the chain ending in an arc carried down from prim A. Margo set ancestral variants only on the first implied arc of the chain. OpenUSD (black box) sets them on each one, from the selections at the class's parent in the other stacks of the chain: `l0.usda /M` inherits `/C`, `l1.usda` payloads `l0.usda</M/a>` inside a variant, `l2.usda` references `l1.usda` and `/Q/b/a` payloads `l2.usda`; a selection `vs = "y"` on `/C` in `l2.usda`, `l1.usda` or `l0.usda` gives `/Q/b/a/b/b/c/b` the spec `root.usda /C{vs=y}a`. Only an inherit whose chain starts in a carried arc does this; on specializes families and on arcs authored at the prim itself OpenUSD sets none (seen on stress stages 47, 124 and 125 of seed 1942 and 82 and 133 of seed 7). Pinned on 4 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/ancestral-chain.test.js`, fixture `ancestral-chain.json`), 3 of which fail without the change. Stage 124 of seed 1942 now matches OpenUSD (values and prim stacks); prims whose stack differs: 84 of 15,579 (87 before), 99 of 19,448.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 15):** the order of a specializes family whose authored arc sits in a variant. Margo ranked every implied arc of the family against the authored arc alone, and within a side by the order of the stacks that hold them. OpenUSD (black box) first implies a placeholder for the arc on the node that holds the variant, in the same layer stack, and ranks the arcs implied further up against that placeholder too: `l0.usda /M/a/a{vs=x}b` specializes `/C`, `l1.usda /M/c` references `l0.usda</M/a>`, `l2.usda /M/c` payloads `l1.usda` and `root.usda /P/c/b` references `l2.usda</M>`, so `/P/c/b/c/c/a/b` takes `l1.usda /C`, then `l2.usda /C`, then `l0.usda /C` (Margo gave `l2.usda /C` first). The same arc with no variant keeps `l1.usda /C`, `l0.usda /C`, `l2.usda /C`. Pinned on 4 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-variant-hop.test.js`, fixture `specializes-variant-hop.json`), 2 of which fail without the change. Stage 129 of seed 1942 and stage 138 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD and leave the stress known list.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 16):** the namespace depth of a reference or payload authored inside a referenced prim. Margo ranked it by the depth of the stage prim it composes, while the arcs carried in by the reference around it rank by depths in the referenced stack. OpenUSD (black box) ranks it by the depth of its prim in the stack that authors it: `/Q` payloads `l2.usda</M/a>`, `l2.usda /M/a` references `l0.usda` and `l2.usda /M/a/a` references `l1.usda</M/a>`, so at `/Q/a/a` the reference authored on `/M/a/a` beats the one on `/M/a` and `l1.usda /C/a`, implied from the inherit of `l0.usda /M/a/a`, comes in (Margo left it out, and `/Q/a/a/c`). Inherits and specializes keep the stage depth. Pinned on 3 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/reference-namespace-depth.test.js`, fixture `reference-namespace-depth.json`), 1 of which fails without the change. Stage 21 of seed 1942 now matches OpenUSD in values and leaves the stress known list (2 prim stacks still differ).
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 17):** which specializes arc holds a site that two branches reach. Margo moved a specializes arc carried in by a graft (a reference to a prim below a root prim, composed alone) under the root in its branch's turn, so a stronger graft took the site. OpenUSD (black box) moves it only after the specializes arcs of the index's own nodes: `/Q/c` payloads `l2.usda</M>` and `/Q/c/a` references `l2.usda</M/a>`, each `l2.usda /M/a` has a payload to `l0.usda /M`, which specializes `/C`; the payload's arc holds `l0.usda /C` under the root and implies `l2.usda /C` and root `/C` from its branch, so `/Q/c/a` takes `l2.usda /C` before `l0.usda /C` (Margo gave the reverse, from the reference's branch). Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/grafted-specializes-late.test.js`, fixture `grafted-specializes-late.json`), 1 of which fails without the change. Prims whose stack differs: 92 of 19,448 on seed 7 (94 before), 59 of 15,579 on seed 1942; nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 18):** the order of a specializes family with an implied arc that hangs from a variant. Margo ranked the arcs implied above it against the authored arc alone. OpenUSD (black box) implies a placeholder for that arc on the node that holds the variant, in the same stack, and ranks the arcs implied above against it too: `/P/a/c` references `l2.usda` (which sublayers `l0.usda`), whose `/M/c` holds `a` in variant `vs=y`, referencing `l0.usda</M>`, and `l0.usda /M/c/b` specializes `/C`, so `/P/a/c/c/a/c/b` takes the `l2.usda` stack's `/C`, then root `/C`, then `l0.usda /C` (Margo gave root `/C` first); with `a` outside the variant root `/C` stays first. Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-variant-anchor.test.js`, fixture `specializes-variant-anchor.json`), 1 of which fails without the change. Stages 16 and 128 of seed 1942 and 140 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD in values and leave the stress known list; prims whose stack differs: 23 of 15,579 (59 before), 75 of 19,448 (92 before); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 19):** how the implied arcs of a specializes family rank against the arc implied into the root stack. Margo ranked them by the order of the stacks that hold them. OpenUSD (black box) ranks an implied arc before the root stack's when the node it hangs from has a smaller namespace depth than the node the root stack's arc stands for: `/P/a/c` payloads `l2.usda`, whose `/M/b` payloads `l1.usda`, `l1.usda /M/c/c` inherits `/C` and payloads `l0.usda</M>`, and `l0.usda /M/a` specializes `/C`, so `/P/a/c/b/c/c/a` takes `l1.usda /C` (its node at depth 2), then root `/C` (implied from the `l2.usda` payload at depth 3), then `l2.usda /C` and `l0.usda /C` (Margo gave root `/C` first). Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/specializes-root-rank.test.js`, fixture `specializes-root-rank.json`), 1 of which fails without the change. Stage 106 of seed 1942 and 91 and 139 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD in values and leave the stress known list; prims whose stack differs: 18 of 15,579 (23 before), 64 of 19,448 (75 before); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 20):** the specializes arc of a grafted index whose inherit to the same site is left out. Margo made no node for a specializes arc whose site an inherit of the same prim already held, and kept nothing when a graft left that inherit out because the index it joins holds the site, so an implied inherit took the site above. OpenUSD (black box) keeps the specializes arc as an inert placeholder, which implies a specializes arc upward: `/R/c` payloads `l1.usda</M>`, whose `/M/c` references `l0.usda</M/a>` and selects `vs=x`, `/R/c/c` payloads `l0.usda</M/a>` too, and `l0.usda /M` inherits and specializes `/C`; at `/R/c/c` root `/C/a` is a specializes arc after `l1.usda /M/c`, its variant `vs=x` and `l0.usda /C/a` (Margo gave root `/C/a` as an inherit first, which selected `vs=y`). Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/held-inherit-specializes.test.js`, fixture `held-inherit-specializes.json`), 1 of which fails without the change. Stage 57 of seed 7 now matches OpenUSD and leaves the stress known list; prims whose stack differs: 18 of 15,579, 51 of 19,448 (64 before); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 21):** the order of the implied arcs of a specializes family on one side of the arc implied into the root stack. Margo ordered them by the strength of the stacks that hold them alone. OpenUSD (black box) orders them by the namespace depth of the node each hangs from first: `/P` payloads `l1.usda</M/a>`, `/P/a/a` selects `vs=x`, whose `b` references `l2.usda</M/a>`, `l2.usda /M/a/c` references `l1.usda</M>`, `l1.usda /M/c` references `l0.usda`, and `l0.usda /M/c/a` specializes `/C/a`; at `/P/a/a/b/c/c/c/a` the arc implied into `l1.usda` hangs from a node of depth 3 and the one implied into `l2.usda` from one of depth 4, so `l1.usda /C/a` comes before `l2.usda /C/a` (Margo gave `l2.usda` first, its stack being the stronger). Stages 0, 31 and 46 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD in values and leave the stress known list; prims whose stack differs: 17 of 15,579, 28 of 19,448 (45 before); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 23):** the namespace depth sibling class arcs below the index root rank by. Margo ranked them by the depth of the stage prim. OpenUSD (black box) counts an arc authored at its node from that node's prim in its own stack, and one implied from under a reference or payload of the same prim from that reference's depth: `/P` payloads `l1.usda</M/a>`, `l1.usda /M/a` inherits `/C` and `/M/a/a` payloads `l0.usda</M>`, which inherits `/C`; at `/P/a` the inherit implied into `l1.usda` counts 3 and comes before the ancestral `l1.usda /C/a` (2) (Margo gave `l1.usda /C/a` first). Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-reference-depth.test.js`, fixture `implied-reference-depth.json`), each failing without one half of the change. Stage 10 of seed 7 now matches OpenUSD and leaves the stress known list; prims whose stack differs: 16 of 15,579 (17 before), 21 of 19,448 (28 before); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 24):** which carried class arc takes a site at a child prim. Margo kept every implied inherit carried down from the parent prim on its site, so a stronger carried specializes arc that implies one of those sites at the child left only placeholders. OpenUSD (black box) implies the carried inherits below the index root again, strongest carried authored arc first: `/R` references `l1.usda</M/a>`, whose payload `l0.usda</M>` has `/M/a` inheriting `/C`; `/R/a` references `l2.usda</M/a>`, which reaches `l0.usda /M`, which specializes `/C/a`. At `/R/a/a` the specializes arc takes `/C/a/a` in `l1.usda`, `l2.usda` and the root stack and the carried inherits are gone (Margo gave root `/C/a/a` as an inherit, second). An arc placed for the child prim takes no site from them, and a carried placeholder that made no family at the parent prim takes only the sites of carried inherits made before it, none when its site has no specs at the child or its node authors a specializes arc there. Pinned on 6 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/carried-implied-again.test.js`, fixture `carried-implied-again.json`), each failing without one part of the change. Prims whose stack differs: 14 of 15,579 (16 before; stage 48 of seed 1942 keeps `/R/a/a/c`), 21 of 19,448; nothing that matched differs on either seed.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 25):** relationship targets through a class arc implied from another implied class arc. KB1942b kept the pair of the arc an implied arc stands for only when that arc was authored; OpenUSD (black box) keeps it for an implied arc carried down from an ancestor prim too: `l1.usda /M` specializes `/C`, `l2.usda /M` payloads `l1.usda</M>` (so `l2.usda /C` stands for it, `/C` to `/M`), and `root.usda /P/c` references `l2.usda</M/a>`; the arc implied into the root stack keeps `/C` to `/M`, so `/C/z` authored on `root.usda /C/a/b` maps to `/M/z` on `/P/c/b` and `/M/a` drops (Margo gave `/C/z` and kept `/M/a`). Pinned on 5 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-implied-targets.test.js`, fixture `implied-implied-targets.json`, reduced from stage 114 of seed 1942), 4 of which fail without the change. Stages 24 and 114 of seed 1942 and 134 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD and leave the stress known list; prim stacks do not change (the change moves only target mapping); nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 26):** an implied specializes arc that reaches a placeholder whose site an inherit of the same stack holds. Part 3 made such a placeholder imply nothing, but an arc implied up from a stack below went on through it. OpenUSD (black box) stops it there: `/P/a` references `l2.usda</M>`, whose stack (it sublayers `l0.usda`) specializes `/C/a` and payloads `l0.usda</M>`, which specializes `/C/a` too, and `/P` references `l2.usda</M>`, whose `/M/a` inherits `/C/a`; at `/P/a` root `/C/a` comes in through the inherit, second strongest (Margo gave it as a specializes arc, implied from `l0.usda` through the `l2.usda` placeholder, weak). A placeholder whose node has a class arc of its own still passes the arc on. Stage 9 of seed 1942 and stage 68 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD and leave the stress known list; nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 27, found on the way):** a reference or payload to an ancestor or a descendant of a site on its way up never finished composing. Margo counted an arc as a cycle only when it led back to the same site, so `/M/a` referencing `/M` brought `/M/a` back under itself one prim deeper each time. OpenUSD (black box) reports such an arc as a cycle ("CANNOT reference") and composes the prim without it; Margo now does too, and lists a `cycle` issue. Pinned on 6 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/namespace-cycles.test.js`, fixture `namespace-cycles.json`, composed in a worker with a time limit): a child referencing its parent, a parent its child, a payload to the parent, and the same reached through a reference and through another layer; all 6 fail without the change. The stress values do not change.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 28):** where class arcs implied up from a node under a variant rank, when the variant's holder is in the same stack. Margo ranked such an implied arc by the namespace depth of the stage prim, and the arcs implied from it by where the variant sits among its holder's children. OpenUSD (black box) ranks it from the variant's holder, as it does a specializes family's (part 15), and the arcs implied from it as the placeholder it implies on that holder would rank among the holder's class arcs: `/Q` references `l2.usda</M/a>`, whose `/M/a/b` references `l1.usda</M/a>`; `l1.usda /M` inherits `/C` and selects `vs = "y"`, whose `a` payloads `l0.usda`, where `/M` inherits `/C`; at `/Q/b` root `/C` comes before root `/C/a` and `l2.usda /C` before `l2.usda /C/a` (Margo gave the reverse). Pinned on 3 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-variant-holder.test.js`, fixture `implied-variant-holder.json`, reduced from stage 25 of seed 1942), 1 of which fails without the change, each half of it needed. Stage 25 of seed 1942 now matches OpenUSD and leaves the stress known list; nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 29):** the namespace depth of a class arc implied below the index root. Parts 23 and 28 counted an implied arc from the stage prim, or from the reference or payload it was implied across when that was deeper, and an authored one from its node's prim in its own stack. OpenUSD (black box, its public prim index dump) counts both alike: the depth of the parent node's path, variant selections left out, when the arc was placed there, kept when the node is carried down to a child prim. `root.usda /R/a` selects `vs = "x"`, whose `c` selects `vs = "x"`, whose `b` payloads `l2.usda</M/a>`; `l2.usda /M/a` inherits `/C` and references `l0.usda`, whose `/M` inherits `/C/a`; the inherit implied into `l2.usda` hangs from the payload's `/M/a` and counts 2, not the stage prim's 4, so the authored `l2.usda /C` comes before it at `/R/a/c/b` and `l2.usda /C/c` (754) beats `l2.usda /C/a/c` (512) at `/R/a/c/b/c` (Margo gave 512). One rule now stands for the three in `ns()` of `stage.ts`. Pinned on 4 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-parent-depth.test.js`, fixture `implied-parent-depth.json`, reduced from stage 51 of seed 7), 3 of which fail without the change. Stage 51 of seed 7 now matches OpenUSD and leaves the stress known list, so every stage of seed 7 matches; nothing that matched differs on either seed.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 30):** where an implied class arc that stands for another implied arc reads the selections for its class's ancestral variants. Part 14 read them for a chain of implied inherits only, at the class's parent in the chain's other stacks, and a specializes chain read none. OpenUSD (black box, its public prim index dump) reads them across the prim index built so far, strongest first, the new arc in its place among them: the class's parent maps to the root namespace through the new arc's map function, each node reads at the path that maps back into it, the arcs of the chain at their class's parent, and class arcs off the chain are not read. In the reduced form of stage 48 of seed 1942 the specializes arc implied into the root stack keeps the pair `/C/a` to `/Q/a/b`, so `/Q/a/b` is read across the index, where the reference's `l1.usda /M/b` selects `vs = "x"`, and `/Q/a/b/c` gets `root.usda /C/a{vs=x}a`, whose target `/Shared` now stays. Found on the way: the same stage with an inherit for the specializes arc, where Margo gave the implied inherit of the root stack no variant, and an inherit chain under `/R`, which inherits `/C`, where Margo read `/C/b`'s selection through the inherit carried down from `/R` and OpenUSD reads a payload's. Pinned on 6 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-chain-variants.test.js`, fixture `implied-chain-variants.json`, each checked on values and targets and on its marked prim stacks), 4 of which fail without the change. Stage 48 of seed 1942 now matches OpenUSD and the stress known list is empty: every stage of both seeds that OpenUSD opens composes to the same prims, values and targets; nothing that matched differs.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 31):** which site an implied specializes chain takes from an implied inherit carried down from the parent prim. In stage 48 of seed 1942, reduced to four files, `l0.usda /M` specializes `/C/a`; at `/R/a/a/c` the arc of `l0.usda /M/c` has no specs at its own site and made no family at the parent prim. Margo stopped its implied arc at `l1.usda`, where an implied inherit carried down from `/R/a/a` waits on `/C/a/c` under another node, and kept the inherit carried onto the index root at `root.usda /C/a/c`, so `l1.usda /C/a/c` came before `l0.usda /M/c`. OpenUSD (black box, its public prim index dump) leaves a placeholder at `l1.usda`, goes on through `l2.usda` and takes the root site, and the carried inherit there goes. At `/R/a/c` Margo dropped the carried inherit to `l1.usda /C/a/c` under `l1.usda /M/a/a/c` when the specializes arc placed that site under another node; OpenUSD keeps both. Now, in `placeClass` and `implied` of `packages/usdz/src/stage.ts`: a placeholder left only because a carried implied inherit waits on the site goes on implying upward; past the first live node it places, such a placeholder's lift takes sites as any lift does; an implied specializes arc of a stronger arc takes the site of an implied inherit carried onto the index root; and a carried inherit under another parent node keeps its place. Pinned on 4 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-specializes-claims.test.js`, fixture `implied-specializes-claims.json`, each checked on values and targets and on its marked prim stacks), 2 of which fail without the change; the other 2 (reduced from stage 84 of seed 7 and stage 9 of seed 1942, which two first tries broke) pin that an inherit implied at the prim, and the first hop of such a placeholder, take no root site. Over every stage of both seeds that OpenUSD opens, marked and compared spec by spec, stage 48 now matches and no other stage changed.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 32):** where an implied class arc that stands for another implied arc reads its class parent's selection when a class arc of the index already went into a variant at the path read. In stage 139 of seed 7, reduced to four files, `root.usda` sublayers `l1.usda` and `l0.usda`, its class `/C` holds `a` only in variant `vs = "y"`, `/Q/c` inherits `/C`, and `/Q/c/a` inherits `/C` and references `l2.usda</M/a>`, which reaches `l0.usda /M/a`, whose `/M` specializes `/C`. At `/Q/c/a/a/b` the specializes arc implied into the root stack at `/C/a` reads the selection for `/C` at `/Q/c/a` (part 30), where nothing is authored, and the inherit of `/Q/c/a` already went into `/C{vs=y}` there (`l0.usda /C/a`, reached through `/Q/c`, selects `y`). Margo read only selections authored at `/C{vs=y}` and gave no variant; OpenUSD (black box) takes `vs = "y"` from that node, so `root.usda /C{vs=y}a` and `/C{vs=y}a{vs=y}` come after `l0.usda /C/a`. Such a variant counts in its place in strength order: it beats a weaker authored selection (the full stage 139), loses to a stronger one (`/Q/c/a` selecting `y` beats the `x` that `/Q/c` chose for `/C`), a class arc weaker than the new arc gives none (part 30's `carried-inherit-unread`, where a payload's `y` beats an inherit's `x`), and an implied arc that stands for an authored arc takes none this way (stage 9 of seed 1942, reduced, where an inherit implied into `l2.usda` would have taken the `x` of another `l2.usda` inherit). Now `chainContext` of `packages/usdz/src/stage.ts` marks those variants and `settleVariant` reads their selection from the path (`pathSelection`). Pinned on 5 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/implied-path-selection.test.js`, fixture `implied-path-selection.json`, each checked on values and targets and on its marked prim stacks), 3 of which fail without the change. Over every stage of both seeds, marked and composed before and after the change, only stage 139 of seed 7 changed, and it now matches OpenUSD spec by spec.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 33):** which stack's index of the authoring prim gives an implied class arc on the index root its ancestral variant selections. Part 8 read the index of the prim A that authored the arc in the stack the implied arc joins only when that stack held the arc stack's root layer. OpenUSD (black box) reads it when the stack holds the layer that authored the arc, a sublayer too. In stage 38 of seed 7, reduced to four files, `/R` references `l2.usda</M/a>` and `l2.usda` sublayers `l1.usda`, whose `/M` specializes `/C` and selects `vs = "y"`; the root stack sublayers `l1.usda` too, so the specializes arc implied into it at `/C/a` takes `y` from `/M` there, and `/C{vs=y}a` does not exist: `/R` gets no class spec, where Margo took the root stack's own `x` and gave `l1.usda /C{vs=x}a`. Now `authorOf` in `packages/usdz/src/stage.ts` finds the layer whose list op gives the arc. Pinned on 5 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/authoring-layer-selection.test.js`, fixture `authoring-layer-selection.json`, each checked on values and targets and on its marked prim stacks), 4 of which fail without the change. Stages 38 and 31 of seed 7 now match OpenUSD spec by spec; nothing that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 34):** the ancestral variants of an implied specializes arc carried down inside a grafted index. Part 7 gave an authored specializes node of a graft the variants its site selects composed alone; an implied one kept the variants the graft's own ancestor chose. In stage 8 of seed 1942, reduced to four files, `/P{vs=x}c` references `l2.usda</M/a>`, `l2.usda /M` inherits `/C`, which selects `vs = "x"`, and references `l0.usda</M/a>`, whose `/M` specializes `/C`: in the index of `/M` the specializes arc implied into `l2.usda` at `/C/a` goes into `/C/a{vs=x}` (OpenUSD shows it on `/T`, which references `l2.usda</M>`), but at `/P/c` OpenUSD keeps no `l2.usda /C/a{vs=x}a`. Now such a node takes its ancestral variants from its site composed alone too. Pinned on 3 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/grafted-implied-variants.test.js`, fixture `grafted-implied-variants.json`), all 3 failing without the change. Stage 8 of seed 1942 now matches spec by spec; nothing that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 35):** an implied specializes arc carried down onto the index root against one a variant of the prim implies to the same site. In stage 33 of seed 1942, reduced to four files, `/P/b/b` payloads `l1.usda</M>`, whose `/M` specializes `/C` and selects `vs = "y"`, so `/P/b/b` gets `root.usda /C`; the variant's `a` payloads `l1.usda</M/a>`. At `/P/b/b/a` Margo kept the carried `root.usda /C/a` and its spec. OpenUSD's public prim index dump shows the variant's implied arc as an inert placeholder, its node under the root inert, and no carried node: the site gives nothing. The same holds when the variant's payload goes to another file whose `/M` specializes `/C`; it does not when the payload sits on the prim itself, goes to a root prim (another site), or the other file's arc is an inherit. Now `placeClass` drops the carried arc, with the arcs implied from it, and keeps the inert node holding the site. Pinned on 7 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/variant-specializes-carried.test.js`, fixture `variant-specializes-carried.json`), 3 of which fail without the change; the other 4 pin the cases that keep the carried arc. Stage 33 of seed 1942 now matches spec by spec; nothing that matched before differs now.
- **Fixed (KB1942c, part 36):** the order of tasks in a site composed alone for an arc (a reference or payload to a prim below a root prim). Margo queued the variants carried down from the site's ancestors with the other nodes, so their arcs ran in kind order with the rest. OpenUSD (black box, its public prim index dump marks them direct, not ancestral) chooses them again, after every other task. In stage 18 of seed 7, reduced to four files, `/R/b/c` payloads `l1.usda</M/a>`; `l0.usda /M/a` specializes `/C/a` and `l1.usda /M` selects `vs = "y"`, whose `a` inherits `/C/a`. The specializes arc holds `/C/a`, so `l1.usda /C{vs=x}a` goes under the index root, weakest, after the `l0.usda /M/b/c` that `/R`'s payload carries down; Margo followed the variant's inherit first and put the class under the payload. On the stage itself `/M/a` keeps the inherit, and Margo still does. Pinned on 2 black-box stages (`packages/usdz/tests/grafted-variant-arcs-late.test.js`, fixture `grafted-variant-arcs-late.json`), both failing without the change. Stage 18 of seed 7 now matches spec by spec; nothing that matched before differs now.
- **Closed (KB1942c, after part 36, 2026-11-26):** comparing every stage that OpenUSD opens, marked with `prim-stack-marks.js`, spec by spec: no prim of either seed differs (5 stages differed after part 32: 8 and 33 of seed 1942, 18, 31 and 38 of seed 7). Found on the way, not ours: OpenUSD 26.11 does not finish opening a variant of the reduced stage 33 where `l1.usda /M` inherits `/C` and the variant's payload goes to another file whose `/M` specializes `/C` (killed after 2 minutes); that stage has no answer to compare.
- **Repro:** generate both seeds with `packages/usdz/tests/oracle/generate-stages.py`, mark a stage with `packages/usdz/tests/prim-stack-marks.js` and compose it with `composition()` and with OpenUSD's `Usd.Stage.Open`: the marked values of each prim, read back with `prim-stack-order.js`, give its order of specs (the stress test compares values and targets only, so it does not see this; the per-part tests above pin each rule on reduced stages).
- **Cause:** the AOUSD USD Core Specification v1.1.0 does not say how a path is mapped through an implied class arc that stands for an ancestral one, which index gives its ancestral selections, or the order of tasks in a site composed alone. The rules in `packages/usdz/src/stage.ts` come from watching OpenUSD on our own stages and are marked there as seen, not specified.

## Blocked on hardware we do not have

These features pass their tests against the published specifications, but the only real check is a device the project
does not own. Each entry says exactly what is needed to close it.

### USDZ export with textures: Quick Look on a Mac only

**Status:** open, deferred (Scott: ignore for now): Quick Look on a Mac not run (hardware check).

- **What:** `exportUSDZ` in `@margoengine/exporters` (`packages/exporters/src/usdz.ts`) writes UsdPreviewSurface
  materials with texture readers (base colour with opacity and `opacityThreshold`, metal-rough on the g and b channels,
  normal, occlusion, emissive, `st`/`st1` texcoords with the V flip, a base-colour `UsdTransform2d`, wrap modes) and
  stores each image 64-byte aligned and uncompressed.
- **Verified:** the USDZ tests (`packages/exporters/tests/usdz.test.js`) check the shader graph text, every file's
  alignment, the image bytes and a round trip through our own USD reader (`@margoengine/usdz`). On an Apple silicon Mac with
  macOS 27.2 (2026-11-05, in a remote session), the eight kit files: `usdchecker --arkit` passes all of them, and their Quick Look
  thumbnails draw the alpha mask, the blended texture and the transforms as intended, 07 (+30) leaning clockwise and
  08 (-30) anticlockwise.
- **Open:**
  1. Quick Look ignores `normalScale`: files 03 (scale 1) and 04 (scale 2) give byte-identical thumbnails, and
     `usdchecker` warns `NormalMapTextureValidator.NonCompliantScaleValues` on 04.
  2. The thumbnails were read by eye, not compared with the engine-drawn twins.
  3. Nothing has been opened on an iPhone or iPad, in AR or otherwise.
- **2026-11-28, Mac mini (Apple M6, macOS 27.2.1, screen locked, over SSH):** the eight kit files and 14 textured Khronos
  models exported from their GLB bytes all pass `usdchecker --arkit` (04 and SheenChair with the `normalScale` warning) and
  all 22 draw a 768 px thumbnail through `QLThumbnailGenerator` (`qlmanage -t` itself ran past 60 s on every file tried).
  Compared by eye with Edge renders of the GLB twins: the kit, Lantern, Fox, Corset, BoomBox, the shoe, SheenChair,
  AlphaBlendModeTest, NegativeScaleTest, NormalTangentMirrorTest, OrientationTest and MetalRoughSpheres show the same
  shapes and maps (the lighting differs). Differences: vertex colours with a textureless lit material draw grey
  (BoxVertexColors, below); transmission draws opaque (IridescenceLamp's globe, ToyCar's glass) and sheen is lost
  (ToyCar's red cloth draws near black), as UsdPreviewSurface has neither; ToyCar's cloth maps were wrong (the two
  entries below). Clearcoat and IOR are inputs of UsdPreviewSurface that `exportUSDZ` does not write yet.
- **Needed to close:** `node scripts/make-usdz-quicklook-kit.mjs <folder> --glb` writes the eight files and their twins.
  Open them on an iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later, compare each with the same scene drawn by Margo, and record the
  result here and in `docs/threejs-parity.md` (USDZExporter row).

### Animated USDZ: the fix for the first iPhone failure awaits a retest

**Status:** open, deferred (Scott: ignore for now): iPhone retest pending (hardware check).

- **What:** Fox-Run in AR Quick Look on an iPhone (2026-11-06) went past the top of the screen, showed the bottom of two legs,
  clipped, and could not be moved. robot-expressive ran half off the screen.
- **Cause:** the file held the true size glTF gives, 79 m and 4.46 m, and Quick Look shows real size. No factor of 2 exists:
  RealityKit's bounds on all 76 files read 1.00 times glTF's, robot-expressive's posed parts aside.
- **Fixed in the exporter:** `height`, `ground`, `size` and `bounds`, skin points at rest in the world, `extent` on each
  `SkelRoot`. `packages/exporters/tests/usdz-size.test.js`.
- **Retest so far:** Scott on his iPhone, of Fox-Run and the Robot files at the new sizes: "Both look right". That covers those two
  models' look on one iPhone only. Dragging, in his words "i could drag them", held on the three files he could open. On all 8
  start-here files, in his words: "they all work but the rigged figure still floats and does not make contact with the ground". The
  rest of the 76 files are untested.
- **Not known:** whether the clipping and the failed move had a cause beyond standing inside a huge model.
- **Needed to close:** on an iPhone, open `Fox-Run.usdz` and `RobotExpressive-Dance.usdz` at the new sizes: each stands on the
  floor in view at about 2 m and a drag moves it.

### RiggedFigure first loads off the floor in AR Quick Look on an iPhone

Release exception: RiggedFigure loads off the floor in AR Quick Look (Apple viewer).

- **What:** Scott, on his iPhone, of the 8 start-here files (2026-11-06): "they all work but the rigged figure still floats and does not
  make contact with the ground". He named no fault in the other seven. How far it floated is not recorded.
- **Variant run (Scott, 2026-11-06, one phone, one load each):** "rigged figure control loads with its feet in the ground but when i drag it up
  it sits properly same for root joint the rest look good". The five files: Control (byte for byte the file that floated, text USD inside),
  ControlBinary (the same scene as binary USD), Scaled (the exporter's height option at 1.2 m, root scale 0.8276, text), NoAnimation (binary, clip
  removed), RootJoint (binary, an identity joint added at the origin).
- **Repro:** `exportAnimatedUSDZ` of `examples/assets/khronos/RiggedFigure/RiggedFigure.glb` with `{ ground: true }`, opened in AR Quick Look.
- **Cause:** not found. The numbers and the Mac say it touches, the phone says it does not. Ruled out, on a Mac only: the file's rest points
  (lowest y -6.6e-8), the `SkelRoot` extent (-6.3e-8 at all 39 frames), RealityKit's `visualBounds` (1.3e-8) and mesh bounds, and no joint reaches
  below the feet (lowest 0.022). RealityKit's own renderer, running the clip, puts the soles on a plane at y = 0 within one pixel (about 3 mm) at
  three times, as it does the other files. That renderer is not AR Quick Look, whose floor logic could not be read here.
- **Only this file, among the skinned ones:** root scale exactly 1, first joint at the hips (y 0.686) and not near the origin, first joint rotated at rest.
- **What the variant run shows:**
  - The same bytes floated on one load and sank on another, so one fixed offset in the file cannot be the whole story. A drag up leaves the feet on
    the floor, so the distance from feet to origin is right once Quick Look places the model again. Both point at first placement or load timing.
    Neither proves it: the two loads were on different occasions, with the room and how well the phone had found the floor not recorded.
  - Control and ControlBinary hold the same scene and differed. So either a difference this size appears with no change to the scene, or text
    against binary matters, and one load each cannot say which. Either way, Scaled and NoAnimation looking good is no evidence about root scale or the clip.
  - RootJoint was off too, so a joint at the origin did not cure it on that load. Nothing now supports the first joint's position as the cause.
- **What it does not show:**
  - Which of root scale, size or the clip matters, if any. Scaled changes root scale and size together.
  - Text against binary: text was off in 2 of 3 loads, binary in 1 of 3.
  - That Quick Look does this to any file. The animated 1.45 m figure was off in 3 of 4 loads (the first report plus Control, ControlBinary and
    RootJoint), and the seven other files plus Scaled and NoAnimation in 0 of 9. That split was picked after looking, and those nine were reported as
    fine and not measured, so it is weak, but it leaves something in this figure that makes a bad first placement more likely still open.
- **Smallest run that would settle it:** Control and Scaled, three loads each, alternating (Control, Scaled, Control and so on), on the same floor
  spot. Close Quick Look fully between loads, let the phone find the floor first, and before any drag note floats, sinks or touches, with rough centimetres.
  - Control changes direction or sometimes touches, and Scaled does too: first placement varies whatever the root scale. Record it as Quick Look's own
    behaviour, with the exporter unchanged.
  - Control wrong in 3 of 3 and Scaled right in 3 of 3: a file-side candidate. That split comes up by chance 1 time in 20, and it would still need a
    variant that changes root scale without size before any exporter change.
  - Anything between leaves the question open, and the entry says so.
- **Needed to close:** that run, then either a root-cause fix with a regression test or the phone evidence that it is Quick Look's own behaviour. The
  exporter stays as it is until a file-side cause is shown.

### Fixed 2026-11-28: Quick Look drew every map with the base colour map's texture transform (KB-USDZ-QLTRANSFORM1)

- **What:** AR Quick Look's renderer (macOS 27.2.1 thumbnails) ignores each texture's own `UsdTransform2d` where a
  material's maps differ, and samples every map with the base colour map's. The Khronos ToyCar's cloth (base and normal
  maps tiled 3 times, occlusion map once) showed the dark squares of its occlusion map repeated over the cloth.
- **Repro:** a quad with a `baseColorTexture` that holds one square, `baseColorTextureTransform` scale 3, and an
  `emissiveTexture` with no transform: nine squares of each, where the glow should show one.
- **Cause:** Apple's renderer, which the writer did not allow for. Probes on the same Mac: it follows a map's transform
  where every map has it (also with no base map), and it follows two UV primvars a material, custom names included,
  also when two materials on one shared shape read four between them; a third set draws with another set's coordinates.
- **Fix:** where a material's maps differ in UV set or transform, `exportUSDZ` and `exportAnimatedUSDZ` give each
  transformed map a primvar of moved coordinates (`primvars:stMap0` and on) and no `UsdTransform2d`. Maps all alike
  keep their nodes, and so does a material with more than four differing ones, which would else hold more UV sets than
  the four a glTF reader takes (`packages/exporters/src/usdz-write.ts`).
- **Measured after:** on that Mac, `usdchecker --arkit` passes 10 files and their thumbnails show each map where its
  glTF transform puts it, the ToyCar's cloth included. With three differing sets Quick Look still draws one map on
  another's coordinates (`docs/limits.md`).
- **Regression:** `packages/exporters/tests/usdz.test.js`, "maps of a material that differ read primvars of moved
  coordinates" and "materials sharing one geometry each find their moved primvars on it" (both fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: `parseUSDZ` sampled every map of a mesh with one UV set (KB-USDZ-UVSETS1)

- **What:** `@margoengine/usdz` took one UV primvar for a mesh, the one its first mapped input read, and every map
  sampled it, in the base reader, `previewSurface()` and `materialX()` alike. A file whose maps name different primvars
  (`exportUSDZ` writes `st` and `st1` for `texCoord` 1) loaded with the other maps on the wrong coordinates, and a
  `GeomSubset` read the mesh material's primvar.
- **Repro:** `parseUSDZ(exportUSDZ(scene))` for a material with `baseColorTexture` on `uvs` and `normalTexture` with
  `texCoord: 1` on `uvs1`: the document held no `TEXCOORD_1` and the normal map read `TEXCOORD_0`.
- **Cause:** `uvName` in `packages/usdz/src/index.ts` was a single name for the mesh.
- **Fix:** each material lists the primvar behind each of its texture coordinate sets, each texture info carries its
  `texCoord`, and each primitive gets `TEXCOORD_n` from its own material's list (`packages/usdz/src/uv-sets.ts`).
- **Regression:** `packages/usdz/tests/uv-sets.test.js` (6 of its 8 tests fail on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: `exportUSDZ` dropped every texture transform but the base colour's (KB-USDZ-TRANSFORM1)

- **What:** `metallicRoughnessTextureTransform`, `normalTextureTransform`, `occlusionTextureTransform` and
  `emissiveTextureTransform` (and so those of a GLB's maps) were left out of the file without a word, so a tiled normal
  map drew once across the surface in any USD reader. Found while comparing the ToyCar in Quick Look.
- **Cause:** `sample` in `packages/exporters/src/usdz-write.ts` wrote a `UsdTransform2d` for the base colour map alone.
- **Fix:** each transformed slot gets its own `UsdTransform2d`, in `exportUSDZ` and the animated export alike.
- **Regression:** `packages/exporters/tests/usdz.test.js`, "every USDZ texture slot reads through its own
  UsdTransform2d" (fails on the old source).

### USDZ vertex colours draw grey in Quick Look

Release exception: USDZ vertex colours draw grey in Quick Look (Apple viewer).

- **Status:** worked around 2026-11-11 for paint-only materials (bug sweep L2, KB2028); the Apple defect is open.

- **What:** a painted mesh from `exportUSDZ` is flat grey in Quick Look (macOS 27.2 thumbnail, 2026-11-05). `usdchecker
  --arkit` passes, and `@margoengine/usdz`, `readUSDA` and any reader that follows `UsdPrimvarReader` get the colours.
- **Repro:** `exportUSDZ({ nodes: [{ geometry: { positions, normals, indices, colors, colorSize: 3 }, material: { color:
  [1, 1, 1, 1] } }] })`, then open the file in Quick Look.
- **Cause (measured):** Apple's renderer does not follow a `UsdPrimvarReader_float3` into `inputs:diffuseColor`. `token`
  or `string` for `inputs:varname` makes no difference (byte-identical thumbnails). The same mesh with no material bound
  draws its colours.
- **Plan:** leave the material out when it says nothing but the paint (no textures, metalness 0, roughness 1, no
  emission, opaque), and teach `@margoengine/usdz` to read `displayColor` on an unbound mesh. A material that says more
  cannot show paint on Apple's renderer; it needs the colours baked into a texture.
- **Workaround (landed):** `exportUSDZ` writes a paint-only mesh unbound (no Material, no `MaterialBindingAPI`), and
  `@margoengine/usdz` already read an unbound mesh's `displayColor`. Regression: packages/exporters/tests/usdz.test.js
  ("a paint-only material is left out"). Still open upstream: Quick Look ignores `UsdPrimvarReader_float3` on
  `inputs:diffuseColor`; still owed: a Quick Look thumbnail of the unbound file on a Mac (none on this PC).

### Intel Arc 140V: three GPU-suite failures fixed on this PC and rechecked on Intel by the outside audit

**Status:** closed (three Arc 140V failures fixed and rechecked by outside audit; proof: packages/shared/precise-math.js).

- **Verified on Intel** (Core Ultra 7 258V, Arc 140V, driver 32.0.101.8860, main at 30bea6fa, recheck of 2026-10-27):
  the four failures of the first run (main d000e4b6) are fixed there. FFT: the Stockham passes match the host-twiddle
  f32 reference exactly (0.00 u at n = 1024 and 65536); path tracer `combinedHDR` within 1 sRGB level (was 226),
  converged after 17 frames; the Next client drew the mint cube after 598 ms (past the old 300 ms fixed wait); the voxel
  and path-tracer `test:gpu:slow-compile` twins and `modern:test:browser` with its twin pass.
- **What failed instead** (same run), and the cause and fix of each, measured on the RTX A6000:
  1. compute CPU/GPU parity, `sin, cos, atan2[16]: cpu -0.4964582920074463, gpu -0.49644696712493896` (1.13e-5 off,
     tolerance 1e-5). Cause: the WGSL builtins. WGSL allows `sin` and `cos` 2^-11 absolute error inside [-pi, pi] (and
     none promised outside), `atan2` 4096 ulp, `asin` 6.8e-5; the Arc 140V is 1.1e-5 off near 1.5 where the A6000 is
     within 3.3e-7 (the A6000 is itself 1e-5 off at |x| near 100, 133 ulp for `tanh`, 114 for `pow`). Fixed: element-wise
     functions use precise f32 versions (`packages/shared/precise-math.js`: integer Payne-Hanek reduction, minimax
     polynomials from `scripts/precise-math-coefficients.mjs`), within 1 to 2.5 ulp (pow 5) on every GPU;
     `createCompute({ fastMath: true })` keeps the builtins. The parity check is tighter now (1e-6, plus each function
     in ulp) and the fastMath path is checked against the WGSL bounds. Regression tests: `tests/precise-math.test.js`
     (the bounds over dense inputs with fused and unfused rounding and with division and sqrt at WGSL's limits), the
     GPU check `compute-precise-browser.js` (the A6000 computes the host mirror's values bit for bit), and
     `compute test:browser:spec-math`, which moves every builtin result by WGSL's whole allowed error
     (`--spec-math-error`, scripts/browser.js): the old parity check fails there as on Intel, the new one passes.
  2. voxel normal suite, `4x four-view blue`: the bottom two views black. Cause: the bevel check took "the quad and
     triangle counts did not change for 3 frames" for "every chunk is meshed"; with one mesher worker on a slower CPU
     a bevelled chunk takes several frames, so the last two chunks (the bottom views) were not on the GPU yet. Fixed:
     `VoxelRenderer.stats.pending` counts the chunks not yet on the GPU (changed, meshing, waiting for upload); the
     check waits for a frame with `pending` 0, `compiling` false and draws. Regression test: `voxel test:gpu:slow-mesh`
     delivers every worker message 150 ms late (`--worker-delay`): the old check fails there the same way, the new one
     passes.
  3. voxel-pathtracer normal suite, `traversal fisheye: depth`: 1.17e-3 relative depth error against the CPU raycast
     (assertion < 1e-4), 16379 of 16384 first hits alike. Cause: the fisheye rays came from the builtin `asin`, `sin`
     and `cos`; a ray that far off grazes a different voxel face. Fixed: the panorama and fisheye rays use the precise
     functions. Regression test: `voxel-pathtracer test:gpu:spec-math` (the projections check with every builtin at
     WGSL's error bound) fails with the builtins and passes with the fix.
- **The class:** five checks have now waited "N frames" or "N ms" for something that takes longer on a slower GPU or
  CPU. `scripts/check-fixed-waits.mjs` (run by `tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js` in `npm run verify`) fails on any new
  fixed frame count or sleep in a GPU or browser check unless it carries `// fixed-wait: <reason>`; the ones already
  there are counted in `scripts/fixed-waits-baseline.json` and only go down. `scripts/support/gpu-ready.js`
  (`waitForPipelines`) waits for the pipelines themselves.
- **Rechecked on Intel by the outside audit of 2026-10-28** (a second Intel Arc 140V laptop; the audit is the source
  for this paragraph): the compute spec-math case, the voxel normal and slow-compile cases and the voxel-pathtracer
  spec-math fisheye case all passed. The audit does not say whether the three fixes above (the precise maths, the
  `pending` count and the precise fisheye rays) were what changed them, and it reports no per-function bounds.
- **Not verified:** the precise functions' error bounds on the Intel compiler (`compute-browser.json` from an Intel
  PC), which no recheck has recorded.
- **Needed to close:** the `compute-browser.json` precise-maths results from an Intel PC, then this entry removed or
  turned into the cause found.

### Fixed: steering could turn without a mass, drag or curvature constraint (PA-83, LIFE-04)

- **Repro.** In the old steering point update, the same force moved unequal masses alike. Turning demand could
  rotate the velocity without a lateral or radius constraint. A member coasting in a medium kept its speed.
- **Cause.** The update treated steering as an acceleration and only bounded total speed. The physical update
  applies force to mass, bounds the normal acceleration, and solves drag in the medium frame.
- **Regression.** `packages/behavior/tests/steering.test.js` and
  `packages/physics/tests/coupling/schooling.test.js` check force, curvature, relative coasting, and a school
  responding to a moving predator. BB-4, BB-6 and AVIARY-3 still have open shot checks in the demo review.

## Open defects

### Open 2026-11-28: skeletal JSON physics constraints are kept but never simulated (KB-SPRITES-SPINEPHYS1, sprites, missing feature)

- **What:** `@margoengine/sprites/spine` parses, validates and round-trips physics constraints (inertia, strength,
  damping, mass, wind, gravity, their mix and reset timelines), but posing never runs them. A bone a physics
  constraint drives stays exactly where its animation puts it: hair, cloth and tails do not lag, swing or settle.
  The current runtime reference of the format includes physics constraint simulation, so this is a gap against the
  rivals' Spine runtimes (No partial packages), not a choice.
- **Repro:** load a skeleton with a root bone, a child bone `tail` and `"physics": [{ "name": "tail", "bone": "tail",
  "rotate": 1, "inertia": 0.5, "strength": 100, "damping": 0.85 }]`, and an animation that moves the root 100 units
  along x in 0.2 s and holds. `parseSpineJSON` lists one `warnings` entry, code `'spine-physics-deferred'`. Pose
  the skeleton every 1/60 s: the tail's world rotation is the same on every frame, where a simulated constraint
  swings it against the motion and settles it over the hold.
- **Cause:** never built. The reader landed during the physics hold (batch 245 job 4, docs/limits.md), which kept
  the data and deferred evaluation; the hold ended on 2026-11-24 and the evaluation was not scheduled.
- **To build:** a per-skeleton physics step in posing (time-stepped, with the constraint's reset and the skeleton's
  own world position and wind and gravity), clean room from the public format documentation, with a test against
  measured swing and settle on a fixed step. Then the `'spine-physics-deferred'` warning goes.
