### Fixed 2026-11-28: the WGSL corpus could not name optics, and water's new shaders inlined past the Direct3D limit (KB-CORPUS-OPTICS1)

- **Repro:** `node --test packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus.test.js` fails "not covered: optics" on main. Recording
  optics and water alone (`node scripts/record-wgsl-corpus.mjs --no-build "--suites=check:gpu-packages -- --no-build
  --only=optics"`, then `--merge-only --add`) still leaves optics uncovered, and `corpus-inline.test.js` (KB-COMPAT-FXCTIME1)
  then fails on 11 water fragment modules from `water test:gpu:optics`: 251,507 to 263,801 characters inlined, over
  250,000.
- **Cause, optics:** `optics/screens` draws through `RawShaderMaterial` (`@margoengine/shader/raw`), which creates its
  modules at the first draw inside core's frame; the recorder names a module's packages from the call stack at
  `createShaderModule` (`scripts/support/wgsl-corpus.mjs`, `origin`), so the three modules are attributed to `shader`
  and `core` (label `shader:raw:optics screens:*`). Any package that draws only through `RawShaderMaterial` is
  uncovered the same way. Fix belongs in the recorder (an attribution that survives the lazy compile), with a test.
- **Cause, water:** the surface fragment's repeated `noise()` and `skyTap()` calls (KB-WATER-GL2LINK1, fixed
  2026-11-28): the base fragment went from 251,507 to 157,264 characters inlined. The optics variants are not
  re-measured until the corpus is recorded again.
- **Fix, optics:** the recorder also credits a module to the packages whose WGSL text it holds: `wgslLineIndex` maps
  every trimmed source line of 24 characters or more (no `${}`) of a package source file that declares a WGSL function
  to the packages holding it, and `authorsOf` names each package with at least 3 distinct lines of the module that
  only its source holds (`packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus/store.mjs`, wired in `scripts/record-wgsl-corpus.mjs`).
  They go in the manifest's own `authors` field, so `package` and `packages` stay the call stack's and no settled owner
  moves; the coverage test counts them. A rewrite of the existing corpus gave 1,410 of 3,256 modules authors (gltf
  modules holding shared, clustered and shadows text, for example).
- **Fix, water:** none needed: KB-WATER-GL2LINK1 brought the base fragment to 157,264 characters, and the recorded
  optics variants pass `corpus-inline.test.js`. Recording them found the `rippleAt` clash fixed above ("a Water with
  interactive Ripples failed to compile").
- **Evidence:** `node scripts/record-wgsl-corpus.mjs --add "--suites=check:gpu-packages -- --no-build --only=optics"`
  passes both suites and adds 101 modules (3,357 kept); `corpus.test.js`, `corpus-inline.test.js` and the other corpus
  readers in `packages/webgl2-compat/test` pass (35 tests).
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/corpus.test.js` "a lazily compiled module is credited to the package
  whose WGSL it holds (KB-CORPUS-OPTICS1)" (optics' screens fragment under a shader and core stack; without the
  `authors` option the module names no optics).

### Fixed 2026-11-28: local CI kept CRLF copies of files whose .gitattributes rule became -text or eol=lf (local CI runner, KB-CI-EOL-STALE1)

- **Seen:** local CI's root tests failed `verbatim licensed fixtures keep the SHA-256 their NOTICE.md records` (`packages/ifc/tests/fixtures-verbatim.test.js`, run 2026-11-27T21-00) while every lane checkout passed it.
- **Cause:** git writes a file again only when its blob changes. The CI worktree is long-lived, so files checked out under the old rules (CRLF on Windows) kept their CRLF after `.gitattributes` marked them `-text` or `eol=lf`, and `git status` stayed clean. `git ls-files --eol` there listed 11: `packages/ifc/tests/fixtures/bcf/Architectural.ifc` and its NOTICE.md, seven sciviz zarr metadata files, and kernel-common's `pinned-vectors.txt` and `random-vectors.txt` (`i/lf w/crlf`).
- **Fix:** the local CI runner (`.ci/ci.mjs`, untracked, in the CI worktree) writes again, right after its checkout, every tracked file whose rule forbids CRLF but whose working copy has it, and logs them in `00-eol-rewritten.txt`. The run of 2026-11-28T06-50 rewrote those 11. The SHA test passes in the CI tree; the next run found none.
- **Regression test:** `tests/checkout-eol.test.js` fails in any checkout holding such a file (it named `Architectural.ifc` when made CRLF by hand) and checks the selection rule on fixed `ls-files` rows.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: margoengine/viz cost 264 B gzip more than @margoengine/points for PointsPlugin (package build, splats, KB-INL1b)

- **Repro:** `npm run build:packages`, then `node --test --test-name-pattern="a kit costs only" tests/umbrella.test.js`: `import { PointsPlugin } from 'margoengine/viz'` bundled the same modules as importing it from `@margoengine/points`, but its entry and static chunks gzipped to 27,696 B against 27,431 B, past the test's 64 B.
- **Cause:** the package build put splats' lazy loaders (`src/compressed.ts`: `parseSpz`, `parseSog`, `encodeSpz`, `encodeSog`, each an `import()`) in the shared `data` chunk together with the `ply.ts` helpers the encode, sog and spz chunks import. Each of those lazy targets then imported back the chunk that loads it. Rolldown 1.2.13 (Vite 8.3.4) in an app build emits such targets even when nothing uses them, once two or more of them loop back (a five-file repro does it; one target alone does not; Rolldown 1.3.4 drops them). Since KB-INL1 (acbe01aba) the dead chunks import `@margoengine/math/color`, so the bundler moved `math/color` out of the app's entry into a chunk of its own, and the entry paid for the extra chunk and its import and export names. The dead chunks were never loaded.
- **Fix:** the package build (`scripts/build-modern.js`, `scripts/support/lazy-loader-chunks.mjs`) gives every lazy loader (a non-entry source module that loads two or more of its package's modules with `import()` and has no runtime static import) a dist chunk of its own, so none of its targets imports it back and the dead chunks are dropped on every Rolldown version. Only a package with such a loader gets the option (today splats alone): a first version that passed it to every package moved other packages' chunks and grew `@margoengine/blender/components` by 51 B and `@margoengine/physics/rod` by 7 B. PointsPlugin through `margoengine/viz` is 27,431 B gzip, the same as from `@margoengine/points`.
- **Earlier part:** the same failure first showed `\0rolldown/runtime.js` in the kit's modules. splats `encode.ts` loaded `@margoengine/math/errors` with `await import()`, so the app's bundler built that module's namespace object with its runtime helper. It now imports it statically. Regression: `tests/no-inlined-margo-error.test.js` "no package dist loads @margoengine/math with a dynamic import".
- **Regression test:** `tests/lazy-loader-chunks.test.js` (every lazy loader is a dist chunk none of its targets imports back; no splats chunk is imported back by a chunk it loads), and the kit test in `tests/umbrella.test.js`. Both fail without the fix.

### Fixed 2026-11-25: local CI's GPU package step sat in `vfx test:gpu` until its 120-minute limit (check runner, vfx seek check, KB-VFX-SEEKHANG1)

- **Seen:** local CI full run 2026-11-25T13-31-21-828Z, step `check:gpu-packages-no-build`: `packages/vfx/test/seek-check.mjs` printed its n = 600 case and nothing more; the step was killed at 120 minutes, while other lanes were running GPU tests on the same RTX A6000.
- **Cause (the 120 minutes):** `check:gpu-packages` runs every suite through `runLimited` (`scripts/support/run-limited.mjs`) with a 10-minute limit, so a stalled suite ends at 10 minutes. Past the limit runLimited ended the tree and then waited for the shell's `close` with no bound. When the kill ends nothing (`taskkillTree` answers `[pid]` when taskkill cannot read the process table, which a loaded PC can fail), the shell never closes and the step waits until the outer limit. That wait is the only way a 10-minute suite limit lasts 120 minutes.
- **Fix:** runLimited gives its result as soon as the kill reports what still runs: `timedOut`, the `survivors`, and a message that names their pids ("process tree not ended (pids ... still run; end them by hand)"). A kill that ends the tree still waits for it to be gone, as before.
- **The seek check's own stall (not reproduced):** none of the seek check's waits had a limit before 6eb74615c. Since then every frame wait and read has 30 s, each run 10 minutes and each page load 2 minutes, and a stall fails naming its phase. Runs on 2026-11-25 did not stall: alone on the A6000, four copies at once there, and on an Intel Arc 140V 16 copies on WebGPU (4 at once) and 12 on the WebGL2 layer (4 at once). Every run that loaded passed n = 1800, in 9 to 17 s. The 12th layer run was openBrowser's first page load past 30 s with four compat browsers starting together, and it failed at once. No defect was found in `@margoengine/vfx` or `@margoengine/cutscene/seek`, which runs on the CPU only. If the check stalls again it now fails within its limits naming the phase, and that phase starts a new entry.
- **Regression test:** `tests/gpu-test-limit.test.js` "runLimited resolves with the survivors when the kill cannot end the tree, not on a close that never comes" (a kill that ends nothing; without the fix the test hits its own 60 s limit).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: small and thin rigid bodies passed through, or were thrown off, a ringing default cloth (physics soft, KB-SOFT-LIGHT1)

- **Was:** a 1 cm bead went through a default cloth after about a second; a 26 g box, a thin rod and a 1 kg box were thrown off it or set spinning, and a box at a mass ratio of a thousand passed between its particles.
- **Diagnosis kept from 0a4570d8e** (which fixed part of it first with a pose shift, `SoftBodies.shiftBody`, since replaced): a 1 cm bead (1.7 g on particles of 1 kg) sank into the particle under it a little more every step (1.4 mm at step 18, 34 mm at step 57) and went through at step 96, because a push out of a particle was a change of pose the real body never got; and a contact's lever taken at the particle's surface, inside the body past its radius, pointed the wrong way and spun the bead to 2,000 rad/s.
- **Causes, each found and fixed:** (1) a cloth met rigid bodies only at its particles, so a body smaller than their spacing met spheres whose normals ran up to 73 degrees off the sheet and slipped between them; the triangles now meet bodies too (the rigid kernel's face query, `kernel/src/face.rs`, and the soft kernel's face rows, `soft-kernel/src/face.rs`; Bridson, Fedkiw and Anderson 2002; Mueller et al. 2007, the point and triangle constraint; Shinar, Schroeder and Fedkiw 2008). (2) The push on a rigid body was handed over as a force spread over the step, so a body stopped at the first touch sank on through the rigid step and was thrown out the next; it now lands as an impulse at the start and a force, solved so the rigid world's own substeps carry a free body to where the soft step took it, and its spin as the change the soft step gave it. (3) A contact held a point fixed in the body under a fixed normal while the thing it met slid, so the push on the body and on the particle did not lie on one line and spun light bodies up; each contact now says what the surface is (`contact_feature`: a face held by its plane, which turns with the body, or a round place, corner or edge held from its centre of curvature). (4) The turn of a body in a piece was linearised and capped at a tenth of a radian; it is now a rotation (Mueller et al. 2020, equations 8 and 9), and the body's inertia turns with it. (5) The velocity pass ran on contacts the piece had not pushed on; it now runs on those the position pass made (Mueller et al. 2020, section 3.6).
- **Regression tests:** `physics/tests/soft.test.js` "small and thin rigid bodies dropped on a default cloth rest on it for five seconds and never pass through it" (330 steps, each body's centre over the sheet under it, never thrown; it covers the 150 steps the first fix's test ran), "a cloth draped over a sharp box edge hangs over it, never enters the box and does not pop", "a contact is stable at a mass ratio of a thousand either way, and a cloth holds a body or tears, never lets it through"; `physics/tests/soft-faces.test.js`; `physics/soft-kernel/tests/turn.rs`, `tests/face.rs` (among them "a bead pressed deeper than its radius takes no spin").

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a rigid chain's stiffness depended on the iterations, the substeps and the mass ratio (physics soft, KB-SOFT-ITER1)

- **Repro:** `node packages/physics/scripts/soft-stretch-sweep.mjs` on the commit before the fix: a 3.8 m rope pinned at the top with rigid edges and a 16 kg crate attached to its end hung 4.12 m below the pin at 2 iterations and 8 substeps with particles of 0.01 kg (8% stretch), 3.98 at 8 iterations, 3.85 at 16 substeps, 3.95 at 0.05 kg, 3.82 at 0.5 kg.
- **Cause:** the edges were solved by Gauss-Seidel sweeps in index order (XPBD, Macklin et al. 2016), which move a correction one edge a sweep, and a body attached to a particle was pulled once a piece through the particle's mass, so a heavy load on a light rope was coupled by the particle's momentum and not by the chain's tension.
- **Fix:** every rigid edge of a component with no loop (a rope, a tree of them), and every particle attached to a body, is one constraint of a single linear system K lambda = -C, K = J W J^T, solved to a tolerance by the preconditioned conjugate gradient method, with Newton steps for the curve of the distances (`soft-kernel/src/rigid.rs`; Hestenes and Stiefel 1952, Shewchuk 1994, Baraff and Witkin 1998; Baraff 1996 for the direct tree solve it matches). The attached body is a heavy ghost particle at the end of the chain (its inverse mass at the anchor along each axis); the body takes the reaction as a force over the step, not an impulse at its start (an impulse that cancels a step's weight at its start let gravity pull the body back through the step, and it crept up half a g dt squared each time). Sheets, whose edges form loops, keep the sweep.
- **Now:** the same sweep reads 3.790 m at every setting and every mass ratio from 32 to 1,600 (a rope that does not stretch is 3.8 m; the 0.01 m is a one-step lag in the support of the crate, constant, not stretch).
- **Regression tests:** `packages/physics/soft-kernel/tests/rigid.rs` (a 20-edge chain under 1,600:1 and 16,000:1 loads stretches by less than 1 mm at every setting; a body integrated alongside hangs without stretch or sag) and `packages/physics/tests/soft.test.js` "the stretch of a rope under a heavy load does not depend on the iterations, the substeps or the mass ratio".

### Fixed 2026-11-24: a swept particle probe missed a surface it started touching, and picked the far side of a thin solid (physics, KB-PHYS-PROBE-THIN1, found 2026-11-24)

- **Repro:** a fixed box of half extents 0.01 by 2 by 2 at x = 3, `physics.kernel.probeParticles([2.97, 1, 0], [3.065, 1, 0], 0.02, {flags: 8})` answered `[null]` (the particle's surface exactly on the wall's, moving into it); `probeParticles([2.9701, 1, 0], [3, 1, 0], 0.02)` answered a `started` contact with normal +1 and the point on the far face, x = 3.01, so a solver pushed the particle through the wall.
- **Cause:** the sweep of a ball treats a start that touches at exactly the radius as no hit, and a start inside the radius picked the nearest face of the end position, not the face on the side the move came from.
- **Fix:** `probe_collider` in `packages/physics/kernel/src/probe.rs` classifies the start first: a ball touching a surface or inside its radius at the start meets the surface nearest the start (the side it came from), at time 0, with the depth measured from that plane at the end of the move; only a ball clear of the surface at the start is swept. `softContacts` with any `k` uses the same function. Regression: `packages/physics/tests/soft-probe.test.js` ("a particle that starts exactly touching a thin wall, or inside its radius, meets the near face, whatever its speed": both repros, then a sweep of speeds 0.01 to 600 m/s, start gaps from 1e-6 inside the radius to 0.3 and both sides of the wall; "softContacts with several slots gives a thin wall the same side, from both sides").

### Fixed 2026-11-21: Cabin Hearth's shadowed snow gains the bounce, against its check (clustered bounce, KB-BOUNCE-SHADOWSNOW1, found 2026-11-16)

- **Repro:** `node scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` (WebGPU or `MARGO_COMPAT=1`) fails "the shadowed snow keeps
  its light" once the crest check before it passes (KB-BOUNCE-FRAMETWIN1): clear glazing, at (-1.2, 0.05, 4.0) the
  bounce adds 0.0030 R, 0.0005 G read in float (the 8-bit box read 0.0000 R, 0.0006 G), over the check's 0.0005.
- **Cause so far (lane C, 2026-11-16):** the JS twin over the same bounce data gives the snow under that point (y
  0.156, its drift's normal) 0.0038 R, so the frame does what the model says. Per VPL, with visibility: the window
  jamb's VPL (1.65, 1.67, 2.46, normal -x) gives 0.0019 R, which is physics (the receiver sees the lit jamb through
  the clear opening); three interior wall VPLs give the other 42%: the west wall (-2.84, 1.4, 0.4) 0.0010, the back wall
  (-1.33, 1.55, -2.23) 0.0004 and the east wall (2.68, 0.76, 1.43) 0.0004, which the 0.3 m front log wall must hide.
  Their visibility maps hold the front wall at 2.6 m in neighbouring texels and 4.56 m in the texel toward the snow: a
  hole. A 16 times denser point budget (65536) does not close it, so it is not point sparsity. Hypothesis: the
  surfels of `buildVisibility` are round discs of radius 1.5 sqrt(area / pi), while a texel the lantern sees at a
  grazing angle (the front wall, 0.4 m from it, at 7 degrees) is a strip 1 / cos longer than wide, so the disc
  covers 1.69 sqrt(cos) of its long half-extent, under 1 for cos below 0.35, and gaps open along the wall.
- **Three causes (lane C, 2026-11-17),** measured on a dump of the live inputs and on a synthetic room (box 6 x 2.5 x 4 m,
  a lantern at (3, 2, 3.6), 0.4 m from the z = 4 wall, receivers on the ground outside facing up, exact trace 0):
  1. **Round surfels (fixed 2026-11-17).** A capture texel meeting its surface at cos to its ray is 1 / cos longer along
     the ray's projection; a disc of its area left holes along grazing walls. `BouncePoint.ray` now carries the capture
     ray and `buildVisibility` splats the ellipse of the same area, semi-axes reach sqrt(e) along and reach / sqrt(e)
     across, e = 1 / max(cos, 0.1) (Zwicker, Pfister, van Baar and Gross, "Surface Splatting", SIGGRAPH 2001; Botsch,
     Hornung, Zwicker and Kobbelt, "High-Quality Surface Splatting on Today's GPUs", PBG 2005; Heckbert,
     "Fundamentals of Texture Mapping and Image Warping", 1989). Test: three VPL maps of a wall the lantern sees at
     grazing hold it in every texel (4, 15 and 3 holes before).
  2. **Corner normals (fixed 2026-11-17).** `reduceBounce` took a texel's tangent from the neighbour with the smaller
     distance jump, so a wall's bottom row took the floor's neighbour and tilted up to 38.7 degrees (108 of 2270 wall
     texels over 2 degrees); its surfel stood out of the wall. Now the side whose next two texels run straight on (a
     texel row lies in one plane through the eye, so a flat surface's texels are collinear) gives the tangent; the jump
     decides only without a second texel or a clear difference. Test: every wall texel within 2 degrees of the wall.
  With both, the synthetic room's leak at (0.3, 4.4), (0.6, 4.6), (1, 5), (1.5, 4.5) went from 58%, 10.9%, 17.0%,
  10.2% of the unblocked bounce to 24.6%, 9.4%, 6.8%, 1.8%; Cabin Hearth's shadowed snow from 0.0030 R, 0.0005 G to
  0.0026 R, 0.0004 G (both backends); the crest checks and the bounce GPU check still pass.
  3. **Unsampled surfaces (fixed 2026-11-17).** The occluder points came only from the sources' captures, so a wall no
     source sees (the lower front wall behind the table) was in no map. Imperfect shadow maps sample the scene itself
     (Ritschel et al. 2008), at the detail each view resolves (view-adaptive ISMs, Ritschel, Eisemann, Ha, Kim and
     Seidel, CGF 30(8) 2011; ManyLoDs, Hollander, Ritschel, Eisemann and Boubekeur, EGSR 2011; Christensen,
     "Point-Based Approximate Color Bleeding", Pixar 2008). `sampleSurfaces` now takes every triangle of the frame's
     batches that core draws (the captures' own geometry): a triangle whose circumradius is at least the cell size
     2^floor(log2(2 d / resolution)) (d its distance to the nearest VPL in front of it) is drawn exactly, each texel's
     centre ray against it (Moller and Trumbore 1997), so no disc stands out of a log or past a wall's edge; smaller
     ones merge per cell into one covering surfel; triangles nearer a VPL than 0.02 m are its own patch (a sash 4 mm
     proud of its frame blocked the jamb's VPL before that near plane). Claimed batches (materials glass, gltf-pro,
     terrain) stay out, so the frosted pane passes the window's light as before. A first try with 4,096 uniform
     points on the meshes gave each about 1 m2 of the snowfield and blocked the crest's whole bounce (0.1155 R to 0);
     the per-VPL cell size is what fixed that. Tests (packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js): the table-by-the-wall
     room under 2% of unblocked at five receivers (5.9% to 8.2% with the captures alone; the module does not link on
     the old code), and far small triangles merged into covering surfels. Cabin Hearth: 15,026 occluders from
     1,169,052 triangles; at (-1.2, 0.05, 4.0) the bounce went from 0.0032 R to 0.00245 R, the 0.00246 R an exact ray
     cast from every VPL against the scene's triangles gives (the lit window jamb seen through the clear opening, which
     is physics), so the check moved to snow no lit surface sees, (-2.0, 0.05, 3.2) (cast 0.00003 R), bound 0.0005
     unchanged.
  Still open (the concave-corner receiver plane, one texel of edge placement): at a concave corner the receiver's
  tangent plane runs into the room, so the adaptive bias passes rays the wall stops. The table room at res 32 keeps
  0.9% to 5.5% at (2, 4.2), (0.3, 4.4), (0.6, 4.6), (5.7, 4.3) and (3, 0.05, 4.1), the receivers 0.1 to 0.4 m from the
  wall's foot; Cabin Hearth's snow 0.2 to 0.3 m from the front wall, (-1.5, 3.0) and (-2.5, 2.9), takes 0.0012 R and
  0.0007 R where the cast gives 0.00003 R (the same on the old code). Ruled out, each measured on the synthetic room:
  a 2 x 2 conservative texel test (closes every leak, but the floor under a table loses 14% against the brute-force
  trace, so its existing test fails), bilinear PCF (23% leak), 2 x 2 PCF (3.9%), three of four taps (2.57%, the
  under-table 0.886), normal offset alone or with the plane (leaks stay at (3, 4.1)), neighbour taps near the
  receiver. Depth samples at texel spacing place an edge to about one texel, and a test that never leaks darkens by a
  texel; it needs more map resolution near walls or a receiver-side corner test. The capture-point subset (at most
  4,096) no longer matters for core meshes, which are drawn exactly; surfaces a vertex hook displaces (Snow) and
  claimed batches still occlude only through the captured points.
  4. **The texel's surface (fixed 2026-11-21, the wall or a lower floor).** Measured per VPL, the corner leaks are
     receivers past the texel's depth whose plane test passes while the texel holds another surface: the wall's foot
     where the plane meets it (the table room's (0.3, 4.4): the centre ray meets the wall at y 0.05, the true ray at
     y 0.17), or the floor 5 cm under the plane past it. `buildVisibility` now keeps each texel's surface normal beside
     its depth (one float, hemi-octahedral at 4,095 levels: Meyer, Suessmuth, Sussner, Stamminger and Greiner, "On
     Floating-Point Normal Vectors", EGSR 2010; Cigolle, Donow, Evangelakos, Mara, McGuire and Meyer, JCGT 3(2) 2014),
     as an object-ID shadow buffer keeps which surface it holds (Hourcade and Nicolas, "Algorithms for Antialiased
     Cast Shadows", Computers & Graphics 9(3), 1985), and a receiver past the depth is lit only if one flat or convex
     surface can join it to the texel's point H: normals within 60 degrees, H behind the receiver's plane by at most
     |H - x| sin(angle) + 2 cm (a convex chord runs between its tangents). The test of the normal alone (within 26
     degrees, H within 2 cm of the plane) hid 29% of the window's bounce at Cabin Hearth's log crest, whose texel
     holds the log's lower face 39 degrees round; an offset from H's own plane hid 10% of a faceted log's crest, its
     captured normal 9 degrees off. Tests (packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js): the table room outside the wall at
     y 0.05, flat and on a drift tilted 20 degrees, 0% to 0.09% of unblocked at (2, 4.2), (0.3, 4.4), (0.6, 4.6),
     (5.7, 4.3) (0.9%, 5.5%, 4.0%, 3.8% flat and up to 1.5% tilted with depths alone); the floor inside within 10% of
     the traced visibility; a 0.15 m log's crest over lit snow within 10% of traced for three lights. Cabin Hearth:
     the crest checks as before (see the playbook entry of 2026-11-21).
  5. **The floor level with the snow behind the wall (fixed 2026-11-21).** Cabin Hearth's snow 0.25 to 0.35 m from the
     front wall, (-1.5, 0.163, 3.0) and (-2.5, 0.172, 2.9), took 0.0013 R and 0.0007 R (twin, albedo 0.9 / pi) where
     the cast gives 0.00003 R: the texels of the back wall's VPLs held the plank floor at y 0.15 just inside the wall,
     1.3 to 2.2 cm under the snow and parallel to it, so by one depth the snow's own plane, and the joined-surface test
     passed. The ray to the snow passes the wall about 2 degrees above its foot, under a third of a 32-texel map's 7, so
     finer maps near walls (adaptive shadow maps, Fernando, Fernandez, Bala and Greenberg, SIGGRAPH 2001,
     doi:10.1145/383259.383302; logarithmic perspective shadow maps, Lloyd, Govindaraju, Quammen, Molnar and Manocha,
     ACM TOG 27(4) 2008, doi:10.1145/1409625.1409628) would need some 16 times the texels round every wall and still
     place the edge to a texel. Instead, once the centre texel's surface joins the receiver, `bounceIrradiance` and
     `clusterBounceLighting` (one WGSL for WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) ask the texel beside it on each axis, toward
     the ray to the receiver: where the two texels' points form a valley (each in front of the other's plane by over
     2 cm: the floor and the wall standing on it) and the receiver lies over 2 cm behind the second one's plane, the
     ray meets that wall between them. The two planes place the edge inside the texel pair, as shadow silhouette maps
     store an edge inside a texel (Sen, Cammarano and Hanrahan, ACM TOG 22(3) 2003,
     https://graphics.stanford.edu/papers/silmap/); the taps are percentage-closer filtering's (Reeves, Salesin and
     Cook, SIGGRAPH 1987) but decide visibility only for a valley, since every tap of a 2 x 2 block as an occluder had
     darkened the floor under a table by 14%. A convex edge is never a valley, so a log's crest keeps its bounce. Test
     (packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js): Cabin Hearth's front wall, door, floor and snow with VPLs over its back
     and side walls: 0 at both points where the traced visibility is 0 (5.5% of unblocked at (-1.5, 3.0) before), the
     snow along the wall 0.06% of unblocked, the floor and the wall's foot inside within 10% of traced. The table room
     level with its floor, (0.3, 4.4), (5.7, 4.3) and (3, 4.1): 0%, 0% and 2.8% (1.9% to 5.8% before). Cabin Hearth
     (scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs, both points added to its shadowed-snow check, bound 0.0005): see the
     playbook entry of 2026-11-21.
     Test added 2026-11-25 (packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js, "the snow lights the crests of a log wall"): five
     crests of seven stacked octagonal logs over lit snow, where the normal codes hide no VPL that a ray cast does not
     hide (a pairwise crease test over a texel's 3 x 3 neighbours, tried in a rework, hid the crest behind a log facet
     beside the ray: Cabin Hearth's window bounce at its crest 0.0440 R against 0.0624 R).
  What is left is the depth bias every shadow map has, recorded in docs/limits.md, not a defect: a receiver behind a
  surface thinner than 2 cm and 2% of its distance (the table room's zero-thickness wall: (3, 0.05, 4.05) 5 cm behind
  it, 43%, and (3, 4.1) 10 cm behind, 2.8%) lies within that slack of the texel's depth and is lit; a wall thicker than
  the slack, as every wall of Cabin Hearth is, hides it. On the lit side a receiver within about one texel's footprint of a concave corner loses some (one texel of edge
  placement, the same with depths alone).

### Fixed 2026-11-24: an opening light cast no shadow of its reveal and sill, and its bounce followed (clustered, KB-BOUNCE-REVEAL1, found 2026-11-16)

- **What:** `openingLight` (`@margoengine/clustered/area`) lights what is in front of an opening with the whole rectangle's light, so snow under a deep sill or reveal takes light its reveal hides. `LightBounce` reflects the opening's light from the texels its centre sees, each with that unshadowed irradiance. In Cabin Hearth the window's bounce at the log crest (0.3, 1.35, 2.65) is 0.0917 R against 0.0647 R with the reveal and sill shading the snow (+42%), 0.1196 R with no shading at all.
- **Repro:** `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs`, the `crest.frosted` line: `twinWindow` against `shaded`; `bounceQuadrature('pane')` in that script is the physics.
- **Cause:** the opening light's irradiance is the polygon integral over the full rectangle (`rectIrradiance`), never clipped to what a point sees through the opening's depth.
- **Needed to close:** clip the rectangle to the part each receiver sees past the reveal and sill (both `openingLight` and the bounce's opening source), then hold the crest check to the shaded quadrature within 15%.
- **Package fix (2026-11-16):** `RectAreaLight.recess` and `sill` (and `openingLight`'s) clip the rectangle in `AreaLights` and in `LightBounce`'s `rectIrradiance` (tests: packages/clustered/test/area.test.js, test/bounce.test.js, test/opening-light.test.js, examples/package-benchmarks/area-lights-gpu.mjs). With them, the bounce's 32 VPLs first read the crest 45% under the same capture's texel-by-texel sum (0.0078 against 0.0141), as one cluster mixed the snow, the sill top and a glazing bar's face and was lifted to the bar (KB-BOUNCE-CLUSTER1, fixed).
- **Closed (2026-11-24):** Cabin Hearth's opening passes `recess` 0.218 m (the frame's outer face at z 2.67 in front of the glass) and `sill` 0.09 m (the sill to z 2.76). The window's bounce at the crest is 0.0624 R, 0.0147 G against the shaded quadrature's 0.0647 R, 0.0152 G (-3.6%, both backends, RTX A6000), where it was 0.1035 R (+60%). `scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs` now holds it to the shaded quadrature within 15% (it fails on the old scene); the clear-glazing crest and shadowed-snow checks are unchanged.
- **Fix (2026-11-20):** Cabin Hearth's opening light carries its frame: `recess` 0.218 m (the opening at z 2.452 to the frame's outer face at z 2.67) and `sill` 0.09 m (the sill's front edge at z 2.76), so `AreaLights` and the bounce's opening source (its capture now looks out from the frame's mouth) clip the rectangle to what each point sees past them. The crest check now holds the window's bounce to the shaded quadrature within 15% (it was held between shaded and bare, and to the unclipped capture model): Intel Arc 140V laptop GPU (the browser's default adapter), WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer alike, `twinWindow` 0.0624 R, 0.0147 G against `shaded` 0.0647 R, 0.0152 G (-3.6%; bare 0.1196 R), the frame equal to its twin to 2%. The same script's under-window snow (KB-CABIN-WINDOWGLOW1) and frosted patch edge checks now take their form factor from the part of the pane each point sees past the frame and sill (`paneFormFactor`, traced over 840 patches) instead of the bare rectangle's Lambert form: the snow under the window reads 0.1160 R against the traced 0.1012 R (+15%, the check's band 0.8 to 1.25; the bare form gave 0.1174 R; the clip's sill edge sits level with the opening's lower edge, 2 cm under the real sill top, and the snow's specular adds some), the patch edge 1.517 m against the traced 1.596 m (half of it the bound).
- **Regression:** tests/cabin-hearth-opening.test.js (the demo's opening keeps its recess and sill; fails on the old main.ts), and scripts/cabin-hearth-browser-test.mjs, the `crest.frosted` line (the old scene reads +42% over `shaded`).

### A path near a toggle between two kinematic bodies answers in full, so the joint webs have no gap bar

**Status:** open, deferred (Scott: ignore for now): physics hold.

- **What:** `@margoengine/physics/next` kernel, the random webs of `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` (`packages/physics/kernel/tests/stability.rs`). All 60 stay under its 1e5 m/s, but seed 49 reaches 10,991 m/s and a joint stands 165.8 m open, and seed 35 past step 600 a joint 144.6 m open (on main at a6a767220), where the scene puts every body back inside a 32 m cube each step and no joint could stand open past 56.85 m by the scene alone. Without the n u stop (below) seed 59 reached 22,121 m/s at step 1039 and a joint 326 m open.
- **Repro:** `web(49, 2000)` of `tests/stability.rs`; it returns the top speed, the top spin and the widest joint. The path is a spherical joint from a kinematic body to body 22, a fixed joint to body 8 and a slider to kinematic body 31: 14 rows on 12 freedoms.
- **Cause** (measured on main at 82779ba8c, where seed 49 reached 7,772 m/s at step 1153 and 117 m open after step 1217; the contact changes of a6a767220 moved every web since): two rows depend on the others and are dropped (measured left: 1e-32 of their size). A third is 2.3e-3 rad from depending, a pivot of 5.4e-6 of its size at steps 1152 to 1216 against the stop of 14 u = 1.7e-6, so it is independent and the exact solve gives it the speed of one over that angle, as the kinematic ends ask more than the joints allow; at step 1216 it crosses the stop and is dropped. Checked in rationals: with the f32 epsilon stop the kernel's pivots matched an exact elimination to 1e-13 on every path of seed 49 at step 896 and seed 59 at step 1038 (pivots of 1.35e-7 and 1.76e-7 there, nonzero in rationals), so these are the scene's answers and not rounding.
- **Needed to close:** a design for speeds near a toggle when the ends cannot both be met (damping per singular direction, as Buss and Kim 2005 do for a push, or a bound from what the kinematic bodies carry), then a gap bar in `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` for all 60 webs. `a_path_with_more_locks_than_freedoms_drops_the_row_that_depends` holds seeds 1 and 35 under 56.85 m to steps 400 and 600 now.
- **Since 2026-11-25** (a joint's locked rows no longer run their lever to the anchor on B, below): seed 49 reaches 245 m/s, seed 35 2,639 m/s and seed 59 3,140 m/s, and the widest joint over the 60 webs is 38.8 m (seed 22), measured as the tests now measure it, less what the joint's two bodies travelled in the step. That measure cannot see a near-toggle answer, which moves its body as fast as it asks, so the design above is still owed before this closes.

### Fixed: a joint's locked rows turned their drift into speed (2026-11-25)

- **What:** `@margoengine/physics/next` kernel. A body held by a spherical, revolute or fixed joint to a kinematic body that turns 1.287 rad in one step left at 1.63 times its anchor's speed with one substep, and at 2.3 times a step later (anchor 4 m out: 712.6 m/s against 308.9). In the joint webs of `tests/stability.rs` the same term fed every unclosed gap back as speed on every substep.
- **Cause:** `joint_view` (`kernel/src/joints.rs`) ran the turning part of each linear row on body A to the anchor on body B, `reach = arm_a + gap`. That is the exact derivative of a slider's measure, where the gap along the free axis is where B stands, but across a locked axis the gap is drift. The relaxing pass solves J v = 0 on rows from the new pose, so it held B at its drift as A turned and asked w x gap of it, which no force in the scene makes: after the 1.287 rad turn the pushing pass left B 0.8 m off its anchor, and the relaxing pass gave it (-99.4, 0, -77.2) m/s where the anchor moved at (-74.1, 0, -21.6).
- **Fix:** the lever runs out only along the axes that leave the anchor free: `reach = arm_a + slide`, with `slide` the gap less its parts along the rigidly locked linear axes. A spherical, revolute or fixed joint now gives its body exactly w r at 1, 8, 32 and 128 substeps; a slider still gives a bead on a turning rail its true r0 w sqrt(cosh 2 w t) (198.3 m/s against 198.4 at 128 substeps).
- **Not a bug, measured:** the rest of the webs' growth with substeps (seed 1's knot of two sliders and a spherical joint: 22,899 m/s at 1 substep, 1.2 million at 128) is work the kinematic bodies do. The pair sits where two rails cross, one of them turning, and runs out along them as they close on parallel; in every relaxing pass that sped it up the turning body did more work than the energy it added. The kernel now counts that work in native builds (`solver::DRIVEN`), and no run gains energy over it.
- **Regression:** `packages/physics/kernel/tests/stability.rs` `a_joint_does_not_turn_its_drift_into_speed` (fails on the old lever at 1 substep) and `a_web_of_joints_gains_no_more_than_its_kinematic_bodies_give_it`; the 60 webs of `a_web_of_joints_stays_in_the_numbers` hold the same energy bar.

### Fixed: textured glTF loads in Node (2026-11-10)

Without createImageBitmap, ordinary image bytes now use the existing lazy @margoengine/decoders/image reader. Retained RGBA8 pixels upload with writeTexture, with normal material mip generation and restoration. Material extension maps, MToon and React image copies accept the same pixel source. Browser bitmap decoding stays the default when available.

The real Node binding renders textured primary colours exactly like uniform base colours. packages/gltf/scripts/test-pixel-images.mjs compares PNG bitmap and pixel uploads, including restoration, pixel for pixel on both GPU backends. See gltf-node-images.md for limits and sources.

### A limp ragdoll keeps moving on a floor when a limit and a contact cannot both hold

**Status:** open, deferred (Scott: ignore for now): physics hold.

- **What:** a ragdoll lying where a floor holds a limb past its cone limit never comes to rest: Knight.glb with the humanoid preset and fitted hulls, pushed over, still has a hand at 0.7 to 1 m/s after 20 s, with the limb up to 0.8 rad past its limit. Capsules settle under default limits (0.05 m/s) because they are thin enough to meet the limits on the floor. Limits a body can meet lying down settle hulls as well (`swing` 2.5, under 0.05 m/s).
- **Repro:** `Ragdoll.attach(physics, ragdollOptions(humanoidProfile(model.nodes, { bones }), model.nodes))`, `fitRagdollShapes(ragdoll, model)`, `activate()`, then 300 N s on the chest, as in `packages/ragdoll/tests/profile.test.js`, and read the bodies' `linearVelocity` after 1,200 frames.
- **Cause:** the cone limit pass turns the bone back toward its limit from outside the solver, each step, into the floor that put it there; the solver pushes it out, and the two exchange energy for ever. Hinges use Rapier's own limits and do not do this.
- **Tried, measured on the same falls:** skipping the correction on touching limbs settles it (under 0.1 m/s) but a spine ended 2.3 rad past its limit. A fifth of the correction on touching limbs left 0.2 to 0.65 m/s and 0.5 to 1.6 rad. Pulling the joint back with its motor, inside the solver, settled it (under 0.2 m/s) but left bones 1.1 to 1.9 rad past their limits and tore a pinned joint test apart by 3 cm. Each trades a moving limb for a broken pose, so none shipped.
- **Needed to close:** a cone limit as a real solver constraint, with stiffness that does not depend on the limb's own inertia, so a wrist under a body holds as well as a thigh. Rapier has per axis limits on a generic joint, which make a pyramid rather than a cone.
- **Status:** the own solver has that constraint: `physics/next`'s `cone` joint, whose proof is `a_limb_a_floor_holds_past_its_cone_rests` in `packages/physics/kernel/tests/joints.rs` (at rest, 0.02 rad past the cone). `@margoengine/ragdoll` still runs on the root entry, so this repro stands until the ragdoll moves onto the own solver in batch 128, which closes this entry.

**Status:** open, deferred (Scott: ignore for now): physics hold.

On RiggedFigure pushed forward at 1 m/s both feet stand 0.1 m off the floor at frame 18 with no swing running. `RagdollBalance.landing` gives these two no step at all, as it takes the hips' height for the leg's: `room` reads 0 where Knight's reads 0.253 m. That is wrong, but it is not what throws them: reach from the true hip to ankle line, and reach from the friction cone, both read no better (at 1 m/s RiggedFigure falls in 57 and 58 of 64 against 31, Seed-san in 61 and 59 against 49). - **Remeasured on Margo's solver (lane P, 2026-11-28):** probe `.lane/kb2208-sweep.mjs` in the lane P worktree, seven figures, 1 m/s,
  four directions, seeds 1 and 2, 240 frames: 18 of 56 pushes fall (RiggedFigure 8/8, Seed-san 6/8, Mage 2/8, Barbarian and
  Ranger 1/8, Knight and Rogue 0/8). Every figure takes 0.10 s steps (`stepDuration` reach is 0 or near it, finding of handoff 6).

  the floor (frames 3 to 6), and after three such steps both feet stand 6 to 7 cm up with state 'standing'. So the stance foot
  leaves the floor because the swing leg's upward momentum lifts the whole rigid body, not because the height hold uses it

  stood. The trailing foot steps first on a sideways push (`lifted` wins over the landing check), a crossing step. Each lever,
  measured over the seven figures and four directions, seed 1 (seeds 1 and 2 read the same), falls at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 m/s
  against a baseline of 5 / 9 / 11: a trigger on the capture point leaving the hull of both soles (Pratt 2006; Koolen et al.,
  "Capturability-based analysis and control of legged locomotion, Part 1", IJRR 2012) 21 of 56 at 1 m/s against 18; that
  trigger with the true hip height and 0.998 extension 26 of 56; the true hip height and 0.998 extension alone 5 / 8 / 21; the
  0.998 extension alone 4 / 9 / 12; the trailing-foot rule off 18 of 56; the shortest step at 0.8 or 1.2 of 1/omega (the
  doc says half a natural period, the code 0.4) 17 and 18 of 56; the ankle bound kept through single support 4 / 11 / 13. With
  the hull trigger and the true reach, Seed-san's 0.2 m/s backward step lands 4 cm back and the capture point comes back
  between the feet by frame 30, but both feet stand toe-up on their heels at 0.2 to 0.4 rad and the trailing foot slides
  0.36 m forward on its heel, so the figure falls backward anyway. Next: why a stance foot that the bound holds stays toe-up
  after a step (the foot load `foot` against the real contact force), and step execution for a straight-legged figure; the
  levers above all trade one figure's falls for another's, so none landed.
- **Where it stands, and what a fix needs (lane P, 2026-11-28, write-up; work stopped here on the manager's order):**
  - Measured levers, falls of 56 at 1 m/s (seven figures, four directions, seeds 1 and 2) against 18 on Margo's solver:
    true hip height 27; 0.998 extension 18 (and 4 / 9 / 12 at 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 m/s, seed 1, against 5 / 9 / 11); both 16;
    swing lift capped at 1, 2 or 4 g 17, 17, 19; `stepTrigger` x0.5 or x0.25 16, 23; capture-point hull trigger 21, with
    true hip height and 0.998 extension 26; trailing-foot rule off 18; shortest step 0.8 or 1.2 of 1/omega 17, 18. The best
    total was `stepTrigger` x0.5 with the hull pick, true hip height and 0.998 extension, 12 of 56 at 1 m/s; it was not run
    at 0.5 or 1.5 m/s, it moves falls between figures, and it is four changes for no one cause, so it did not land.
  - Not the cause (each measured): Seed-san's sole fit, `minWeight`, the stance ankle's rod gains (x0, x0.25, x4), the solver
    change (the remeasure on Margo's solver keeps the same two figures failing).
  - Three separate faults are proven, and a fix needs all three: (1) `RagdollBalance.landing` reads the hips' height as the
    leg's, so `room` is 0 on RiggedFigure and Seed-san (97.6 percent of the leg, past the 0.9 factor) and the step lands under
    the hips; (2) the step waits on a fixed `stepTrigger` of 0.2 of the reach while the capture point is already outside the
    sole, 52 frames on Seed-san's 0.2 m/s backward push; the trigger must be the capture point leaving the support hull
    (Pratt et al. 2006, "Capture Point: A Step toward Humanoid Push Recovery", Humanoids; Koolen et al. 2012, IJRR); (3) after
    a step a stance foot stays toe-up on its heel at 0.2 to 0.4 rad and slides, though the ankle bound holds it: the next
    reading is the controller's `foot` load against the contact force the solver really applies on that foot, and a
    straight-legged figure's swing (its knee snap lifts the whole body, the RiggedFigure trace above). (1) and (2) fixed alone
    move the backward step to 4 cm back and bring the capture point home by frame 30, and the figure still falls on (3).
  - So the fix is a controller redesign of step timing and stance-foot control in `packages/ragdoll/src/balance.ts`
    (and the stance ankle in `powered.ts`), judged over all seven figures, four directions, both seeds and all three speeds
    at once, not a tuning lever. It needs a planner before code. Probes: `.lane/kb2208-*.mjs` and `.lane/patch2208.py` in the
    lane P worktree (env switches PICK, HIPH, EXT, TRIG, HULL, SHORT, CLAMP1, ANKS over the built dist).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: npm run verify hung once in its unit test step

- **What:** on 2026-11-06 one `npm run verify` run in a worktree passed every other step and then sat in the unit test step until its 1,500 s limit, where the same tree took 166 s minutes before and the next run passed in 380 s. Nothing named the test, because the step prints only when it ends.
- **Repro:** none yet. Other lanes were running their own checks on the machine at the time.
- **Cause:** not found. The step now names a hang (see Fixed 2026-11-06), so the next one prints `HUNG TEST:` with its file and test.
- **Needed to close:** a run that prints that line, and a fix of the test it names. Every verify run since is a run of this watch.

- **Lane C sweep (2026-11-10):** no demand repro is available. Full verify is reserved for local CI; this entry remains its per-test hang watch, and no lane verify was run.
- **Named (local CI, 2026-11-11 03:00, `16-root-tests.log`):** `HUNG TEST: testsite-cache-isolation.test.js after its last test "a checkout reached through a Windows short path serves its pages" (something keeps the process alive): no event for 361 s`. That test ran its child with `spawnSync` and no limit, so a child that never exited held the runner's event loop. The child starts a suite dev server, and every suite dev server then ran a chokidar file watcher it had asked Vite not to start (below, "suite dev servers watched files"): file system watches are what kept an earlier child of this file alive (the failed-start case).
- **Fix:** suite dev servers start no watcher (`scripts/browser.js`), and the child now has the same 60 s bound as its sibling and prints `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` if it is still open 20 s after its close, so any recurrence fails in the test, naming what stays open. Regressions: `tests/dev-server-watch.test.js` (no FSWatcher), `tests/vite-cache-isolation.test.js`. One occurrence in 10 local CI runs kept (2026-11-10 01:00 to 2026-11-11 03:00).

### Apple M6 sweep, 2026-11-05 (Chrome 157 and Playwright WebKit; Safari not run)

Release exception: Apple M6 sweep: Apple shader compile and WebKit causes proved outside Margo.

Sweep record: every package's tests and browser or GPU tests on the Apple silicon Mac (M6, macOS 27.2). Repro for each: on a Mac,
`MARGO_BROWSER=chrome` or `MARGO_BROWSER=webkit` with the named script.

- **Fixed (2026-11-11, L4, KB2224a): `sky` `test:gpu`, Playwright WebKit only: full Sky and `sky/base` differ by one half-float step.** Up to 2 pixels a frame in `afterlight`, `meadow`, `preetham` and
  `preetham-clouds-fog`, the same on every run and at 1x and 4x. Cause proved (2026-11-06): Apple's compile under WebKit rounds by the shape of the code. The only trigger is the
  day model branch of the full Sky, `if(frame.settings.x<0.5){color=preetham(w,s);}else{...lookup...}`, of which each frame takes one side. With that branch alone patched out of
  the full module, keeping the side in use, all 12 runs (6 configurations, 1x and 4x) give 0 differing pixels. Moving `lookup` ahead of the branch, which is the same maths, moves
  the differing pixels instead of removing them. The night branch changes nothing. Chrome on the same M6 gives 0 with every one of these texts, so the values are right and only
  the rounding of one compile moves. Ruled out: a stale read, inputs, and an empty branch added to `sky/base` (folded away, same pixels). To close it, Sky would compile only the
  day model in use, and a model switch would recompile the sky, fog, reflection and lighting shaders with `reflectionTexture` kept: Scott's call. No tolerance was raised.
  Fix (2026-11-11, Scott approved): Sky compiles only the day model in use (`compose` in `packages/sky/src/base.ts`); editing
  `options.model` live recompiles the sky, fog, reflection and lighting shaders on the next frame, with `reflectionTexture` and
  the lighting map, buffer and bindings kept, and binds the Bruneton tables only for the Bruneton model (auto layouts drop an
  unread binding). Steady frames compile nothing; the recorded traces keep their command and resource counts. Apple silicon Mac M6,
  macOS 27.2, Playwright WebKit, `browser-check.mjs`: origin/main still fails `afterlight 4x frame 1 scene vs narrow` (1 pixel,
  0.0000153); with the fix all 12 runs (6 configurations, 4x and 1x) give 0 differing pixels, so the KB2224b baselines need no
  re-record for this. Regression: `packages/sky/test/sky.test.js` "KB2224a" (fails on the old build: a model branch in every
  shader). A first run in a freshly copied folder once failed `night-citadel 4x frame 0 scene vs control` (44,792 pixels) and
  passed on the rerun; logged as a sweep row (harness, not sky).
- **Fixed (2026-11-10, Mac lane H): `culling` `test:gpu`, Playwright WebKit and Chrome: parts and core meshes differ by 1 level with shadows on.** Chrome 156 on the same M6 shows it too (2026-11-07, `shadows frustum step 2`, 1 pixel). `parts-check.mjs`, `shadows frustum step 2`: 1 pixel reads 145 against 146;
  the close view has 2. Cause proved (2026-11-06): the two engines draw the same surface with two specializations of one shader. A shader patched by Shadows makes core draw single-sided
  meshes with its plain pipeline (`C` false, back faces discarded; the culled pipeline in `renderer.ts` serves only the unpatched shader), while CulledParts keeps its back-culled pipeline
  (`C` true) for them. Apple's compile under WebKit rounds the two differently. With `C` forced false on parts' pipeline every step gives 0; with `C` true and `cullMode` none it stays at
  1 and 2, so the constant decides, not the culling. Without shadows both engines use `C` true, which is why that run gives 0. Ruled out: shadow maps. Parts and mesh casters do round apart
  (12,756 texels by 1 to 24 ulp in WebKit, 139,988 in Chrome), but with both casters rewritten until the maps were bit-identical the frames still differed by the same pixels. Also matrices
  and a shadow edge moving. To close it, either CulledParts follows core's choice, which puts back faces through the rasterizer under shadows, or core culls with patched shaders too, a core
  change: Scott's call. No tolerance was raised.
  Fix (2026-11-10, in culling, the first option without its cost): `CulledInstances` (so `CulledParts` and `MeshletMesh`)
  records core's unpatched shader, format and descriptor in a pass at the lowest order, and its back-culled variant sets
  `C=1` only when the frame is still core's own with no extra bindings, which is exactly when core draws with its own
  `C=1` pipeline. Otherwise the variant keeps `cullMode: 'back'` with core's `C` false: the same fragment code as core's
  plain pipeline, whose discard removes the same back faces. Not the MSAA order effect: the comparison keeps MSAA and
  0 pixels. parts-check now gives 0 on all 32 steps on the M6 (Chromium WebGPU on Metal). Regression: "the back-culled
  variant sets C=1 only when core would draw the frame with its own C=1 pipeline" in packages/culling/test/culling.test.js
  (fails on the old code). Playwright WebKit 27.2 on the M6, 2026-11-14: `parts-check.mjs` gives 0 differing pixels on
  every step, `shadows frustum` included. Open, same cause, outside culling: `packages/scatter/src/index.ts`
  sets `C: 1` on its lit pipeline whenever the shader keeps the switch, patched or not.
  Scatter fixed (2026-11-10, Mac lane E): `Scatter` records core's frame state the same way and sets `C=1` only on its
  back-culled lit pipeline when core would draw the frame with its own `C=1` pipeline; double-sided and patched frames
  keep `C` false. Regression: "the back-culled lit pipeline sets C=1 only when core would draw the frame with its own
  C=1 pipeline" in packages/scatter/test/scatter.test.js (fails on the old code).
- **`visual:check` on the RTX A6000: 16 of 81 views fail against baselines last recorded on 2026-10-31.** `npm run visual:check -- --runs=1`, Edge 156.0.4314.58. All 16 pass at 47e4d7c9c on the
  same browser, so neither the browser nor the GPU moved them. A pass/fail search of the 317 code commits since names three, each a deliberate look change that recorded no baseline: cd345c483
  (shoreline foam cap: `night-citadel`, `gameplay-sandbox`), 6f0836ee3 (the tint draw reads the surface: `flight-helmet`, `FlightHelmet`, `ABeautifulGame`, `IridescenceLamp`, `LightsPunctualLamp`) and
  43b39e9df (specular weight: `AnisotropyBarnLamp`, `DiffuseTransmissionTeacup`, `ToyCar`). The 2026-11-05 lighting2d and scatter fixes changed none of them, and all 20 proofs pass. To close: look at
  the 16 views and re-record them: Scott's call.
  Edge 157 (2026-11-08) moved none of them: in Edge 157, abadfb455 still draws the Edge 156 pictures and its child 6f0836ee3 the Edge 157
  profile's (`flight-helmet` lens mean 72.8 against 11.5 of 255, `LightsPunctualLamp` up to 79 levels, the same commit's), and `gameplay-sandbox`
  at abadfb455 on Edge 156 is bit-identical to the Edge 157 profile. The near-black `flight-helmet` lenses were an asset defect that
  6f0836ee3 exposed, fixed since: the demo GLBs' lens base colour had been composited over black when written as JPEG.
  Fixed 2026-11-11 (KB2224b): the Edge 157 profile was recorded after these three, and the 40 views that later failed were
  bisected to ten named deliberate commits and re-recorded, except voxel-night-high (open, KB-G2guard above); the
  per-commit proof is in docs/limits.md "Site and demo visual baselines re-recorded".
- **Playwright WebKit sometimes drops to 20 or 30 FPS after navigating in the same tab.** `examples/voxel-sandbox`, `quality=high`, 1920 x 1000, 60 Hz display:
  in chains of five same-tab loads, 7 of 30 loads ran at 30 FPS, then the rate came back by itself on a later load. Never on the first load of a browser (0 of 11 chains),
  and not at 1280 x 720 (0 of 11 loads). First seen as 20 (light then high) and 30 (high then high), with the rate of the page's own `requestAnimationFrame` the same, frame CPU
  2 ms and the GPU 24% busy. Cause not found. Ruled out: GPU load, CPU load, the back-forward cache as the only cause, and the old page's device (destroying it on `pagehide`
  still gave 3 of 25). A plain WebGPU page that only clears held 60 in 20 of 20 loads at the same size, so a frame's real work plays a part. Safari not run.
  Upstream report (draft, nothing filed): `docs/upstream-reports/KB2224c/report.md`; no standalone repro exists yet (a plain clear page holds 60).
  Not re-run on 2026-11-14: a frame rate measurement is speed work, deferred in the build phase (`scripts/speed-phase.json`).
- **Not Margo (cause located 2026-11-14): `culling` `models-plain-check.mjs`, Playwright WebKit only: 2 pixels differ at
  `nodes step 3 back out`.** The culled and the plain engine draw NodePerformanceTest.glb (10,000 primitives, all drawn at
  that step) and 2 pixels differ by 1 level ((31, 31, 33) against (30, 30, 32) at (151, 213), and (311, 229)); Chromium on
  the same M6 gives 0 on every step. Cause: WebKit rasterizes a `drawIndexedIndirect` differently from the
  `drawIndexed` with the same five arguments, in this pose. Proof, with the culled run instrumented after the model moved:
  every buffer of the two devices except the culler's own reads back byte for byte the same (20,008 of them, the uniform
  arena included), the two frames record the same commands in the same order (one pipeline, 10,000 draws) except that
  engine A calls `drawIndexedIndirect` where B calls `drawIndexed`, each indirect record holds (index count, 1, 0, 0, 0)
  as B's call does, and no index points past its vertex buffer. With `primitive.culled` blocked, so the culler still
  dispatches but A draws directly, the frames match. Minimal repro without culling:
  `MARGO_BROWSER=webkit node packages/culling/test/gpu/indirect-repro.mjs` draws the model in two plain engines and
  turns engine A's `drawIndexed` calls into `drawIndexedIndirect` on a buffer holding the same arguments for one frame:
  WebKit gives 2 differing pixels on the moved indirect frame, at the same 2 places, and 0 on every direct frame and on
  the overview; Chromium gives 0 throughout. WebGPU defines the two calls to draw the same primitives, so this is
  WebKit's side; Margo keeps the indirect draw (it is how a culled primitive draws nothing) and the check its exact
  comparison. The six `culling` `test:gpu` checks after it (`occluders`, `bounds`, `shadows-cull`, `lod`, `meshlets`,
  `meshes-scale`) pass in WebKit on the M6 with 0 differing pixels.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: three routes broke WebGPU compatibility-level rules (KB2272); surfels at 4x since fixed

Follow-up (KBnew-skyfog-ldr, L4, 2026-11-11): the three 4x cases KB2272 added to the shared adapter scenes made
`webgl2-compat test:gpu:tiers` fail at "sky fog 4x ldr: the package accepts this tier". Cause: the cases get their
4x scene from PostStack's capture (the only 4x route), and PostStack refuses HDR stages on the LDR tier by design,
so the tier check met the documented refusal it did not list. Sky, VolumetricFog and spray have no fault there.
`tier-packages-browser.mjs` now lists the three 4x scenes as LDR refusals and still checks their message; they
render at half-float. Regression: that check (failed on 16fbe3c86c, passes now). Docs: webgl2-compat README.
Same again (bug sweep L3a, 2026-11-11): the surfels case 34f9772d2a added ("points surfels 4x") takes the same
capture, so `test:gpu:tiers` failed at "points surfels 4x ldr: the package accepts this tier" once both were on main.
It is listed with the others as an LDR refusal, message still checked. Regression: that check. Docs: webgl2-compat README.

- **Was:** with `allowCompatibilityAdapters`, `FogPass` in `@margoengine/sky`, the `VolumetricFog` composite in `@margoengine/environment` and the spray in `@margoengine/water` failed pipeline creation at 4x ("sample_index is not supported in compatibility mode").
- **Fix:** each draws once per sample at the level, with the sample index as a constant and `multisample.mask` writing that sample alone (`perSample` in `packages/shared/msaa.js`, the route `SceneTarget.copyDepth` and eye-dome lighting already took). The full level keeps its single `sample_index` draw, so its work is unchanged. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` cases `sky fog 4x`, `environment volumetric 4x`, `water spray 4x` (each threw on the old source) and the fogged-frame check.
- **Fixed later the same day (bug sweep L3), surfels:** `SurfelPlugin` at 4x refused with `unsupported`, as its sums need a multisampled float target to add into and the level multisamples neither `r32float` nor `rgba16float`. It does multisample `rg16float` (probed on the forced level, Chromium, A6000) and `rgba8unorm`, so at the level the front depth goes out as the four bytes of its float in `rgba8unorm` (exact: no blend touches it, as eye-dome lighting packs it) and the sums into two `rg16float` targets, (r, g) and (b, weight): the same half floats the full level adds in `rgba16float`, so no precision is lost (the `rg11b10ufloat` idea would have cut sums to 6 and 5 mantissa bits). The resolve draws once per sample with a one-sample mask. Same 12 bytes a sample as the full level; the resolve is four draws where the full level takes one, the full level's work is unchanged. Regression: `packages/points/tests/compat-level.test.js` (threw `unsupported` on the old source) and `packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` case `points surfels 4x` with the surfel frame within 4 of 255 of the full level's (red 3, blue 4: PostStack's `rg11b10ufloat` capture under it, as on the sky frame).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: surfels drew differently on the WebGL2 layer's half-float tier (red main after 34f9772d2a)

- **Was:** `test:gpu:tiers` failed on "points surfels 4x half-float": 1.2% of pixels (share 0.01196 against the 0.001 bound, at most 15 of 255) differed from the layer's full tier. The `/tiers` entry stores every float target below its full tier as half floats, so the surfel front depth (`r32float`) became `r16float`. Its rounding (about 0.004 at a view depth of 4) moved the blend window, which is one disc radius deep (0.03 here), so discs near the front got other weights. The packed route was keyed on `compatibilityLevel()`, which is false on the layer. The LDR tier would also have stored the sums in 8 bits, clamping each weight sum at 1, and nothing refused it.
- **Fix (`@margoengine/points`):** on the layer below its full tier the front depth goes out as the four bytes of its float in `rgba8unorm` at any sample count (exact, as at the native compatibility level), while the sums stay one `rgba16float` target, which that tier stores unchanged; `SurfelPlugin` refuses a tier below half-float with `unsupported`. The full tier and native WebGPU keep `r32float`, so their work is unchanged. The bound was not touched: the case is now 0 pixels apart.
- **Regression:** `packages/points/tests/compat-level.test.js` (three tests fail on the old source: 1x and 4x half-float formats, the LDR refusal) and `packages/webgl2-compat/test/tier-packages-browser.mjs` case `points surfels 4x` (share 0.01196 before, 0 after).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: eye-dome lighting on the WebGL2 layer below its full tier (KB-L3a-edl)

- **Was:** points with `edl: true` write their view depth into an `r32float` target, which the layer's `/tiers` entry stores as `r16float` on its half-float tier and in 8 bits on its ldr tier. EDL shades by log2 depth steps between neighbours, so the half float's rounding (about 0.004 at a depth of 4) added or hid steps. As for surfels, the packed route was keyed on `compatibilityLevel()`, false on the layer. No tier case drew EDL.
- **Fix (`@margoengine/points`):** below the layer's full tier the eye-dome depth goes out as the four bytes of its float in `rgba8unorm` (exact), in the same pass as the colour, and the lighting pass unpacks it, at 1x and 4x. The full tier and native WebGPU keep `r32float`. `roundsFloatTargets` moved to `packages/points/src/tier.ts`, shared with surfels.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/tier-packages-browser.mjs` cases `points edl` and `points edl 4x` (in `adapter-browser.js`).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: sky and other packages drew HDR as display colour over PostStack's rg11b10ufloat capture

- **Was:** at WebGPU's compatibility level `PostStack` captures 4x in `rg11b10ufloat`. Sky (base, aerial, Hillaire, shafts, volumetric clouds) and 25 more sites in animation, creative, environment, gltf/pbr, lod, materials, scatter, splats, terrain, voxel, voxel-pathtracer and water decided linear HDR output by `format === 'rgba16float'` (some also `rgba32float`), so over that capture they encoded for display and the stack tonemapped again: the sky drew up to 19 of 255 brighter than at the full level.
- **Fix:** one predicate, `linearHdr` in `packages/shared/hdr-format.js` (every float format is linear), at every site; creative's planet and grass passes also accept the `rg11b10ufloat` capture instead of refusing it. The sky now differs from the full level by at most 3 of 255 and the fogged frame by 4, all in blue, the capture's 5-bit blue mantissa against rgba16float's 10 bits.
- **Regression:** `tests/hdr-format.test.js` (fails on the old source: 25 sites compare a pass format with `rgba16float` alone); `packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` asserts the sky and fogged frames within 4 of 255 (19 before); `packages/creative/tests/planet.test.js` draws into `rg11b10ufloat`.

### Fixed 2026-11-26: SSR and SSGI failed every frame on WebGPU's compatibility level

- **Was:** each Hi-Z reduction read mip i-1 and wrote mip i of one `r32float` texture in one dispatch, and that level allows one view of a texture per draw or dispatch ("must not have different views in a single draw/dispatch command"), so every frame of SSR, SSGI, `RTReflections` and `RTGI` was rejected there. Found while testing FG-17 piece 6d.
- **Fix:** `createHiZ` and `encodeHiZ` in `packages/post/src/hiz.ts`, shared by SSR and SSGI: at the compatibility level each level reduces into a texture of its own and is copied into its mip of the pyramid; at the full level the reduction is unchanged.
- **Regression:** `packages/post/test/hiz-compat-level.test.js` (failed on the old source) and `rt-gi-browser.mjs` / `rt-reflections-browser.mjs --mode=compatibility` in post `test:gpu` (validation errors on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: a lone Bloom failed at 4x on WebGPU's compatibility level

- **Was:** `Bloom.attach(engine)` without `PostStack` created a 4x `rgba16float` capture, which the level cannot multisample ("does not support multisampling"); `PostStack` picked `rg11b10ufloat` there, Bloom alone did not.
- **Fix:** both take the capture format from one function, `captureFormat` in `packages/post/src/capture.ts`; Bloom's scene pipelines target the capture's format.
- **Regression:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` case `post bloom alone 4x` (threw on the old source).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: external PBR display passes blend glass in encoded values (KB2281)

- **Was:** `PBRModel.createRenderer(device).draw(context, pass, view)` into a caller-owned, already-open pass on a display-encoded target drew native glass with the tint/add blend in stored values: bright glass over a 128 grey read 197, 221, 239 of 255 against the linear 143, 154, 165. The package cannot end the caller's pass to snapshot the light behind a surface.
- **Fix:** `draw` takes `options.snapshot(pass, target)`: before each glass surface the caller ends its pass, writes the colour into `target` and returns the reopened pass, and `draw` returns the open pass. The glass then composites in linear light as graph-managed scenes do. Without the hook the native blend stays (exact on `rgba16float`), as documented in the gltf/pbr README. Regression: `packages/gltf/test/external-glass.test.js`, `packages/materials/test/native-glass-browser.mjs` (`externalGlass`, 143, 155, 165 with the hook).
- **Fixed 2026-11-11 in `@margoengine/xr` too (KB2281-xr):** the eye passes drew through `createRenderer` without a hook, so glass on a display-encoded layer texture kept the tint/add blend. When a drawn model has a native glass material (the rule gltf/pbr uses, now shared as `nativeGlassMaterial` in `packages/shared/pbr-transmission.js`) and the layer format is not `rgba16float`, the eye pass stores its samples and lends the hook: it ends the pass, resolves the samples into the renderer's snapshot with a resolve-only pass (the layer texture need not allow COPY_SRC) and reopens the eye pass with `load` and the eye's viewport. Scenes without glass keep `storeOp: 'discard'` and one pass per eye. Regression: `packages/xr/tests/xr.test.js` ("XR eye passes lend gltf/pbr a glass snapshot hook").

### Findings of the outside audit (2026-10-28)

- **What:** an outside audit of revision 74a01810 (a source review, canary tests on a second laptop with temporary
  files, mock fetches, fake sockets and loopback servers only, a full verify that passed 6,344 of 6,346 tests with 2
  skipped, a short fuzz run over 36 targets and GPU checks) reported 20 findings, F01 to F20, about input handling,
  the converter command line, the network servers and one slow decoder input. The audit marks each as reproduced, code
  confirmed or project documented, and states its own limits: a short fuzz run, local canaries only, no production
  test, and a passing verify does not show there are no bugs.
- **Status on main (2026-10-28):** 16 of the 20 are fixed with regression tests (F01 to F07 and F11 to
  F19; classes, commits and tests in
  [whitepaper/perf-history.md](whitepaper/perf-history.md#44-an-outside-audit) and the table at the end of this page).
  F20 is being fixed; its details are published once the fix is on main.

  `maxConnections` (1,024) and `firstMessageTimeout` (10 s), with tests in `packages/netcode/tests/transports.test.js`.
