### hygiene gate 6: TypeScript async API threw "getNodeId requires a RemoteNode" once (2026-11-10)

**Status:** closed (fixed 2026-11-11, KB6254a; confirmed on main 2026-11-26: tests/declaration-snapshot.test.js
passes once its source check allows the formatter's line break, which had turned it red; the wrong-scene dispose
sites listed as open below use `sceneOf` and their scene tests in physics, physics2d and ragdoll pass).

`npm run hygiene` in the lane-P worktree (bp-161, branch from 5ecb5ab1a, packages freshly built) failed once at
`scripts/hygiene.js` gate 6 (`checker.getSymbolAtLocation(await program.getSourceFile(dts))`) with
`Error: getNodeId requires a RemoteNode` while 14 packages' CPU tests ran beside it; the rerun on the same files passed,
and a standalone pass over all 1,312 entry `.d.ts` files found every source file. Repro attempt: run
`npm run hygiene` while `npm test` runs in several packages.
Fixed 2026-11-11 (bug sweep L6b, KB6254a): cause found. 81 packages' `npm test` runs `npm run build` first, and
`scripts/build-optional.js` builds with vite `emptyOutDir: true`, so a package's dist (its `.d.ts` included) is gone for
part of each build. A gate 6 project opened in that window has no source file for the entry; `program.getSourceFile`
returns undefined and `checker.getSymbolAtLocation(undefined)` throws "getNodeId requires a RemoteNode" (reproduced with a
project listing a missing `.d.ts`). Gate 6 now checks the source file and fails with the cause by name: the entry, how
many declaration files changed while it read them (modification times before and after,
`scripts/support/declaration-snapshot.mjs`), and that a package build ran beside it. Running hygiene beside package
builds stays unsupported, as the fast gate runs them in sequence. Regression: tests/declaration-snapshot.test.js.

- **Fixed (2026-11-10, Mac lane E): wrong-scene dispose in creative, labels, points, tiles, lod, materials, rigging, usdz,
  gltf/pbr, mcp and scatter.** `engine.removePlugin(name)` acts on the active scene, so disposing a plugin attached to
  another scene removed the active scene's same-name plugin and left the disposed one registered and running. Each
  site now removes through `engine.sceneOf(plugin)` (one `fix(<pkg>): dispose removes the plugin from its own scene`
  commit per package, each with a regression that fails on the old code). Left as is on purpose: react's and ui's
  React effects (attach and detach both run in a React commit, where the default scene is active; react's plugins stay
  in the default scene, and adaptive-resolution uses `engine.scene` both ways), controls' `cadControls` (replaces the
  active scene's stage controls on purpose), environment's `EnvironmentLighting.load` rollback (same synchronous call
  as the attach), and the already scene-scoped sites in animation, audio, inspector, save, shader, xr and the other
  gltf/pbr and materials files. Open, outside the lanes that may edit them: `packages/physics/src/physics.ts:1209`,
  `packages/physics/src/next/physics.ts:896` and `packages/physics2d/src/physics.ts:630` check `hasPlugin` and remove
  by name in the active scene (same bug); `packages/ragdoll/src/ragdoll.ts:1211` compares against the active scene, so
  a ragdoll in another scene is never removed. Sciviz `axes.ts`, `media-tiles.ts` and `pointcloud.ts` had the same
  pattern; fixed 2026-11-11 through `sceneOf` (regression: packages/sciviz/tests/scene-owner-browser.mjs for the axes,
  both backends; the scene cases of packages/sciviz/tests/export-media.test.js and pointcloud.test.js). Fixed 2026-11-15: tiles' points plugin and usdz `curves()` attached after an
  import's await used to land in the default scene; tiles now attaches its points plugin to the renderer's scene,
  usdz `curves()` now attaches to its model's scene.

## Batch 132 audit: gltf/pbr (fixed)

- Fixed: `applyGLTFLightExtensions` (packages/gltf/src/lights.ts, the aimed-profile cache) keyed fixtures by profile format + profile name + aim. Two EXT_lights_ies profiles with the default name "" and the same LM-63 first line, on nodes aimed alike, shared the first profile: input `LightProfile.ies` (peak 8500 cd) and a second profile peaking at 5250 cd; the second fixture drew at 8500 cd with the first one's beam. Cause: the name is optional and not unique. Fix: the loop is now `placeIESLights`, keyed by the parsed profile object (one per `lights` index) and the aim. Regression: packages/gltf/test/lights.test.js, "two unnamed profiles of one format aimed alike keep their own candela" (fails with the old key).
- Settled 2026-11-11 (KB6284a): EXT_lights_image_based says each saved image "must be flipped about its vertical axis"; the reader swaps rows (a flip about the horizontal axis). The real EnvironmentTest decides it: its mip-0 cube projected onto the real SH basis (Ramamoorthi and Hanrahan 2001) has the sign of all 9 l = 1 values and all 9 xy, yz and xz values the file states only with rows swapped; read as saved, with columns swapped, or with both, 6 or more of those signs are wrong. The l = 1 magnitudes are 1.84 to 2.17 times ours, so the file's scale is still unknown and `irradianceCoefficients` stays data. Regression: packages/gltf/test/lights.test.js, "KB6284a" (fails for each of the other three readings).

## Batch 132 audit: animation (fixed, Mac sweep)

Found by lane I's Mac sweep on 2026-11-10 (Apple silicon Mac, Metal; forced compatibility with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`, which runs the WebGPU code on the WebGL2 layer). Both checks pass natively. Neither script asks for a compat pass in package.json, so no gate ran them this way before. Both fixed by lane I the same day; the commit is the one that changed this section.
- `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:gpu:morph` (scripts/animation-morph-gpu-tests.js): every STEP and LINEAR weight read back wrong, worst error 1 (CUBICSPLINE 0.79); first failure STEP loop, copy 1, at 0.4: expected 1, read 0. None of the three first suspects (the scatter tier's `num_workgroups` index, `arrayLength(&items)`, a readback at an offset) was it: the first frame was right and every later frame read the CPU's zeros. **Cause: a browser bug below the layer**, Chrome on ANGLE's Metal back end. When the first draw through a framebuffer after the WebGL2 context's OffscreenCanvas was shown with `transferToImageBitmap` comes after an upload into the framebuffer's texture (`texSubImage2D`, from memory or from a pixel unpack buffer, before or after the frame was shown), that draw is dropped: no GL error, the framebuffer reports complete, the texture keeps the uploaded data. The layer refreshes a buffer's "word texture" with such an upload before each scatter dispatch, so from the second frame on (the first one shown) the morph pass's stores never landed and the Animation's own weight upload (zeros) won. Raw WebGL2 repro with no layer: `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/metal-dropped-draw-repro.mjs` (prints one line per order; not a gate): an R32UI 4096x1 texture attached to a framebuffer; draw 7 into it, read 7; show the canvas; upload zeros; draw 9; read 0 (9 without the frame shown, 9 with no upload, 9 when the texture is attached to the framebuffer again before the draw, 9 when any draw through the framebuffer comes first). Measured with `ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M6, Unspecified Version)`, HeadlessChrome 156.0.8078.4. Not reported upstream from here (this repository does not read or file against Chromium or ANGLE code). **Workaround in the layer** (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/device.ts `framebuffer`, canvas.ts `present`): each shown frame bumps `CompatDevice.frame`, and a cached framebuffer is attached again (its attachments, draw buffers and status check) on its first use in each new frame. Cost: one re-attach per framebuffer used per frame, no new GL objects. Regression: `scatterAfterWrite` in packages/webgl2-compat/test/compute.html (run by `test:gpu` through compute-browser.mjs): a scatter dispatch, a frame shown, 70 small writes into the same buffer, a second dispatch; without the workaround the layer read `second[0..3]` as 0 where native WebGPU read 10, 20, 30, 40. The morph check now passes under `MARGO_COMPAT=1` (worst error 6.0e-6, under its 1e-5 bound; the bound is unchanged).
- `MARGO_COMPAT=1 npm run test:gpu:uploads` (packages/animation/tests/upload-copies-browser.mjs): "a held pose stays certified as uploaded" failed; the page reported `{"skinned":4,"palettes":2,"copies":0,"mismatched":0,"held":false}`. **Cause in animation's design, not a wrong result**: the uploaded-palette and morph weight caches (packages/animation/src/index.ts `reusableWriter`) only trust the browser's own `GPUQueue.prototype.writeBuffer`, because a custom writer could change its input while it copies and restore it before returning, so comparing afterwards could not certify the upload. The layer's `CompatQueue.writeBuffer` is a JavaScript method, so on the layer every held palette and every unchanged morph weight went up again each frame and `bonesUploaded` never held. That method copies its input before it returns (straight into GL, or into a slice that waits its turn) and never changes it. **Fix**: it now carries the mark `Symbol.for('margoengine.writeBuffer.copiesInput')` (non-writable), and `reusableWriter` also accepts a queue whose prototype's own `writeBuffer` is the writer and carries that mark, with the same own-property and getter checks as the native path. Like the native check, it is a host filter, not a security boundary. Regressions: the compat run of `test:gpu:uploads` (held true) and `writeBuffer carries the copies-input mark` in packages/webgl2-compat/test/device.test.js.

## Fixed: webgl2-compat `implicitFootprint` oblique-gradient case differed on the Mac (ANGLE on Metal)

Fixed by `62941de87`: ANGLE Metal's `textureGrad` takes its generic explicit-gradient path even when the gradients are
the coordinate's own `dpdx`/`dpdy`, where native Metal (and WGSL's definition) uses the implicit footprint; the layer
now samples implicitly in that case. `features-browser.mjs` passes on the M6 at `5a6087049` (all `implicitFootprint`
texels match native). The original report follows.

Found 2026-11-10 by the Mac's full `packages/webgl2-compat` `npm run test:gpu` on `main` 5dfe40d1f (Apple silicon Mac,
"ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M6", HeadlessChrome 156.0.8078.4). `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/features-browser.mjs`
stops at `implicitFootprint: compat differs from native`: all eight `.linear/oblique-grad/false` texels read
1054299991 (0.42059 as f32 bits) on the compatibility layer against 1052145270 (0.35637) on native WebGPU. The case
came in with 42d6e24ae and was edited by 43b65e70e (both another machine's sampler-footprint work), and it fails the
same way before and after 60552800e, so the Mac's per-frame framebuffer re-attach is not the cause. The test is not
changed. Repro: `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/features-browser.mjs` on the M6.

## Batch 132 audit: voxel-edit second half (fixed, 2026-11-15)

- Fixed (KB-P11a): `GpuGrid.fill` with a sphere far outside the grid filled cells inside it: the shader's i32 squared distance wrapped negative (centre [50000, 3, 3], radius 2, filled the whole 8-cubed grid). A fill wholly outside now queues nothing, the centre travels as i32 and each axis is refused past 128 cells before the square; box corners are clipped to the grid on the CPU and a grid side is at most 16,777,216 cells, so f32 corners stay exact. Regression: tests/gpu.test.js ('queues nothing for a sphere or box wholly outside') and farSphere/edgeSphere in tests/gpu-browser-check.
- Fixed (KB-P11b): `GpuGrid.brush` took a table entry past 255 (or negative) and a selection that was not a list (it ran on no cell) where `ShaderBrush.run` refuses both. Both now share one input check (`brushInputs` in brush-gpu.ts). Regression: tests/gpu.test.js ('GpuGrid.brush refuses a table entry past 255').
- Fixed (KB-P11c): the brush prelude's `param(i)` clamped the vector but not the lane, so `param(17)` read `param(13)`; it now reads `param(15)`. Regression: paramClamp in tests/gpu-browser-check.
- Fixed (KB-P11d): `thickLineCells` and `taperedLineCells` with `outside: 'clip'` visited every cell of every step's cube or sphere before dropping the ones outside, so a stroke outside the grid ran for hours (about 8e12 visits). Clipped strokes now visit only cells inside the grid; the cells and their order are unchanged. Regression: tests/raster.test.js ('clipped strokes outside the grid finish with no cells').
- Fixed (KB-P11e): `pasteCells` handed out new palette slots in clip order, so a new colour could take a free target slot whose identity a later clip index matched, which then needed a slot and a palette copy of its own. Identity matches are now taken first. The Studio oracle in tests/stamp.test.js changes the same way (Margo Voxel Studio's own pasteAt has the same order). Regression: tests/stamp.test.js ('takes every identity match before handing out a new slot').
- Fixed (KB-P11f): `heightmapToVoxels` read grey samples as alpha 255, so `alphaThreshold: 255` turned a grey image into air; the threshold now applies to RGBA only. `textToVoxels` started its ink box at the pen, so a side bearing left empty columns; it now crops to the ink. Regression: tests/generate.test.js (two tests).
- Fixed (KB-P11g): `fetchLibrary` and `fetchAsset` buffered a body without Content-Length in full before checking `maxBytes`, and a NaN `maxBytes` turned the limit off. Bodies are read in chunks and cancelled at the limit; `maxBytes` must be a whole number. `resolveLibraryUrl` gave a relative index's assets as root paths with no absolute base (`library/index.json` gave `/library/tree.vox`); it now keeps the index URL's form. Regression: tests/studio.test.js (two tests).
- Fixed (KB-P11h): `pickRay` and the screen selections assumed WebGPU reverse depth, but core gives a WebGL2 engine an OpenGL -1 to 1 matrix, so on WebGL2 the ray pointed back at the camera and cells nearer than the middle of the depth range were never selected. Both take `backend: engine.backend`. Regression: tests/select.test.js ('read a WebGL2 camera matrix').
- Fixed (KB-P11i): `raycastGrid` missed a full grid from about 3e8 cells away: the entry point rounded outside the box past the 1e-7 nudge. The first cell is clamped into the grid. Regression: tests/edit.test.js ('enters the grid from far away').
- Fixed (KB-P11j): `paletteUsage` refused a grid past 16,777,216 cells with no way to raise the budget; it takes `maxCells`. Regression: tests/studio.test.js ('paletteUsage takes maxCells').
- Changed by Scott's ruling (2026-11-15, "drop the oldest step"): `VoxelHistory` with `maxBytes` refused a push past the budget; it now drops the oldest steps (the redo branch first) and keeps a single oversized step alone. Regression: tests/studio.test.js ('history over maxBytes drops the oldest steps').

## Batch 132 audit: netcode (fixed)

- Fixed: `GameServer` (packages/netcode/src/server.ts) queued a join on hello and a leave on close, and `step()` runs leaves before joins. A client that said hello and closed before the next tick got `game.leave` first (a no-op) and then `game.join`, so its player stayed in the authoritative state for good, and every client saw it; a hostile client could repeat hello and close to fill the state. A leave now cancels a join that has not run. Regression: "a player who joins and leaves within one tick leaves no ghost in the state" in packages/netcode/tests/netcode.test.js.
- Fixed: `RollbackSession` (packages/netcode/src/rollback.ts) stored every checksum a peer sent, whatever its frame, and only deleted one when it compared it. A broken or hostile peer sending checksums for frames off the exchange interval or far past anything it could have confirmed grew the map without bound (10,000 entries from 10,000 messages in the test). Such checksums are now refused and stale ones pruned with this peer's own. Regression: "checksums a peer sends for frames that can never be compared are not kept" in packages/netcode/tests/rollback.test.js.

## Batch 132 audit: mixer (fixed)

- Fixed: `createEffect` (packages/mixer/src/effects.ts) accepted a filter `q` from -40 to 1000 for every filter type, so an eq band or filter effect took a bandpass, notch, allpass or peaking `q` of 0 or below (alpha = sin(w0) / 2q gives no filter of that kind) and a lowpass or highpass resonance up to 1000 dB, while the reference `biquadCoefficients` refuses all of them. The effect now uses the reference ranges. Regression: the bad-q cases in "effect settings are validated and mapped to node parameters" in packages/mixer/tests/mixer.test.js.

## Batch 132 audit: mesh-edit (fixed)

- Fixed: `simplifyMesh` (packages/mesh-edit/src/simplify.ts) documented `maxError` and `error` as squared distances, but its quadrics are weighted by face area (Garland and Heckbert), so the cost was area times squared distance (length to the fourth): scaling a model by 10 scaled `error` by 10,000, and a `maxError` picked as a squared distance stopped at a different point on every model scale. Each vertex now carries the face area summed into its quadric and the cost is divided by it (an area-weighted mean squared distance). Regression: "simplify error and maxError are squared distances: scaling the model by 4 scales them by 16" in packages/mesh-edit/tests/simplify.test.js.

## Batch 132 audit: mcp (fixed)

- Fixed: `createMcpServer` (packages/mcp/src/server.ts) handled `resources/read` without refusing a request id that was already running. A reused id replaced the running `tools/call`'s cancellation controller and deleted it when the read finished, so a later `notifications/cancelled` for that call did nothing and the tool ran on. `resources/read` now refuses an active id (as `tools/call` already did) and removes only its own controller. Regression: "a resources/read reusing an active tool id is refused and leaves the tool cancellable" in packages/mcp/tests/server.test.js.

## webgl2-compat explicit gradients on ANGLE Metal (lane L, 2026-11-10, fixed)

Fixed: on the Apple silicon Mac, `textureSampleGrad(t, s, uv, dpdx(uv), dpdy(uv))` through the WebGL2 layer chose a
different mip (0.4205882 against native 0.3563725 on the bias-browser oblique map), because ANGLE Metal's GLSL
`textureGrad` takes the generic explicit-gradient path while native Metal returns the implicit footprint for those
gradients. Repro before the fix: `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/bias-browser.mjs` on a Mac (128 of 1280 words
differ, keys `linear/oblique-grad/false` and `/true`). Fix: `packages/webgl2-compat/src/glsl/emit.ts` samples
implicitly when the gradients are the coordinate's own derivatives. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/glsl.test.js`.
Details and numbers: docs/limits.md "webgl2-compat footprint check per platform".

## webgl2-compat bind groups kept their device and engine alive (lane L, 2026-11-10, fixed)

Fixed: `CompatBindGroup.storageTexture()` (packages/webgl2-compat/src/device/resources.ts) registered each shared
storage texture with a module-level `FinalizationRegistry` whose held value was `{ gl, texture }`. A registry holds
held values strongly, and a WebGL2 context reaches its device (the canvas's context-lost listener), the device its
engine, and the engine the plugin that owns the bind group, so neither the group nor anything around it was ever
collected. Repro before the fix: `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node packages/oit/test/gpu/vfx-check.mjs` stopped with "RangeError:
WebAssembly.instantiate(): Out of memory" when the page created its 124th engine with a VFX effect (a heap snapshot
showed the path from the registry's WeakCells through `gl` to the disposed engines). Fix: the held value is a
`WeakRef` to the device and an id into a per-device `WeakMap` of shared textures. Regression:
packages/webgl2-compat/test/bind-group-release.test.js (fails with the old held value), and vfx-check under compat.

### Fixed: ANGLE D3D11 on an AMD driver hung the GPU under the old flipped-blit present (2026-11-10, AMD mini PC)

Repro (Radeon 680M, Windows 11, AMD driver 32.0.21030.2001, Edge 157.0.4341.42): `node
packages/materials/test/features-browser.mjs` failed its compat half 2 of 2 on 48ca54edd, at a different step each run
("eye angle 0.6: 0,256", "white highlight at NaN", "hair shows: 0,0,0"): every pixel of the frame read 0, alpha too.
Cause, from the browser's GPU log (edge://gpu after the run): `Renderer11::testDeviceLost: The D3D11 device was removed,
HRESULT: 0x887A0006` (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG), then `The GPU process crashed! Exit code:
RESULT_CODE_GPU_EXIT_ON_CONTEXT_LOST`. The scene's context was lost and its frames stayed empty; after the third GPU
process restart the browser blocked WebGL for the page (`getContext('webgl2')` null: "WebGPU adapter unavailable").
No Windows TDR event was logged; native WebGPU (Dawn D3D12) never hung. Measured with loops of 30 fresh devices, each a
256x128 PBR sphere (65k triangles): hangs in 12 of 13 runs with the old present (a y-flipped `blitFramebuffer` and a
colour-masked clear, both ANGLE D3D11 shader paths) while frames reached the page through `transferToImageBitmap` and
the layer polled fence syncs. Removing any one ingredient stopped it: a 2D `drawImage` present 0 in 90 devices,
`fenceSync` returning null 0 in 60, a 32x16 sphere 0 in 30, an unlit sphere 0 in 72; `gl.finish()` before each
transfer, never calling `loseContext` or no `keepFrame` copy did not. A plain WebGL2 page with the same mesh, MSAA
resolve, flip blit, fences and transfers did not hang in 240 contexts, so the trigger inside ANGLE or the driver is
not isolated. Valid WebGL calls must not hang the device: below Margo. Not caused by the 2026-11-10 compat commits
first suspected (compat source at 42d6e24ae^ hung the same). 450015cb1 ("present the canvas with a texel-fetch draw,
not a flipped blit", for the NVIDIA uniform-block bug above) removes the old present, and with it the hang: 0 in 60
devices, and the features test passes 2 of 2 on 000a11e1d. Regression: packages/webgl2-compat/test/device-churn-browser.mjs
(in test:gpu; 30 fresh devices must each show their frame) fails at device 1 with compat source at 450015cb1^ on the
AMD mini PC and passes on main. Diagnostics kept outside the repository in lane M1's `.lane/diag` (raw-launch.mjs, wrap.js
GL wrappers, feat.html, min.html).

### Accepted: AMD D3D11 compressed mip blend makes implicitFootprint differ from native (2026-11-10, AMD mini PC)

Repro (Radeon 680M, Windows 11, AMD driver 32.0.21030.2001): `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/features-browser.mjs`
on main 50b7ceddc stopped at `implicitFootprint: compat differs from native`, `.linear/implicit/false[0..7]: native
1051063284, compat 1048608897`. Decoded: native 0x3ea5f3f4 = 0.32413 = level 2 (64/255) plus 25/256 of level 1, so
LOD 487/256 (1.90234); compat 0x3e808081 = 64/255, level 2 alone. Every one of the 20 linear-mip rows fits that one
LOD on both sides (bias -1.25, 0.375 and 1.25 give LOD fractions 0.652, 0.277, 0.152; native blends by the fraction,
compat by 0.6875, 0.21875, 0.0625); nearest-mip rows and the near-integer map are bit-identical. Cause, below Margo:
the layer emits a plain GLSL `texture()` for these footprints and the AMD driver under ANGLE D3D11 blends two mip
levels with weight clamp((frac - 0.1) / 0.8, 0, 1) on a 1/64 grid. Raw WebGL2 without the layer
("ANGLE (AMD Radeon(TM) Graphics 0x1681 Direct3D11)") at LOD fractions 0, .0625, .125, .1875, .25, .3125, .375, .5,
.625, .75, .875, .9375 between a white and a black level returns 1, 1, .96875, .89063, .8125, .73438, .65625, .5,
.34375, .1875, .03125, 0, through `textureLod` and through `texture()` with a bias alike; native WebGPU (Dawn D3D12)
on the same GPU in the same page returns 1 - frac exactly, and so does ANGLE Vulkan. The LOD itself is the same.
Spec: WebGPU 7.1.1 (GPUSamplerDescriptor), "The precise filtering behavior is implementation-dependent."; OpenGL ES
3.0 section 3.8.10.4 gives tau = [1 - frac(lambda)] tau1 + frac(lambda) tau2 for LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR, which the
D3D11 driver does not follow. Exact layer-equals-native bits for hardware-blended footprints is therefore not a spec
requirement; it held on NVIDIA, Intel and ANGLE Vulkan only because their blends are linear.
Scott ruled 2026-11-10: a spec-scoped test. test/blend-check.mjs classifies the backend with a raw WebGL2 probe
(textureLod at every LOD k/256). Linear-blend backends keep the exact bit equality unchanged. On a compressed-blend
backend the linear-mip rows of implicitFootprint and the footprint rows of mipFiltering must pick native's LOD
(nearest-mip sweeps of 512 biases i/256 - 1, compared bit for bit) and each blended texel must equal, bit for bit,
native's own textureSampleLevel and raw WebGL2 textureLod at one shared LOD k/256; every other row stays exact. A
self-test scales the layer's footprint coordinates by 1.01 (LOD 3.7/256 high, inside the clamp, so the blend alone
cannot see it) and must fail through the sweeps. bias-browser.mjs (test:gpu:bias) uses the same scheme: D3D11
compressed, Vulkan linear and exact. Regression: blend-check.test.js (classification and the comparison on synthetic
probes); on the AMD mini PC features-browser.mjs passes with the self-test failing as required. No system or driver
setting was changed (the AMD "Texture Filtering Quality" setting may control the compression; not tried).

### Fixed: Metal mip blend: the compressed-blend oracle took Apple silicon's 1/64 explicit LOD for a driver difference (2026-11-15)

Repro (Apple M6, macOS, Chrome 156 headless, ANGLE Metal and Dawn Metal): `node packages/webgl2-compat/test/features-browser.mjs`
on main stopped at `mipFiltering: compressed mip blend: not native's LOD through the driver's blend`,
`nearest/grad[1]: native 0.8828431 ... is not its own textureSampleLevel at any LOD k/256` (rows 1 to 7 and 10).
Measured with raw WebGL2 and raw WebGPU on the same page (no Margo code), between a white level 2 and a black level 3:
an explicit LOD (`textureSampleLevel`, `textureLod`) is snapped to 1/64, with steps at (q - 1/16) / 64, so a sweep
of 4096 LODs gives 65 distinct blends; a gradient LOD (`textureSampleGrad`, `textureGrad`) keeps 256 steps (runs of 7
to 19 of 4096), so `textureSampleGrad` at LOD 2 + 1/8 returns 0.8828431, a value no explicit LOD returns. Both APIs
return the same bits at every one of the 4096 LODs, nearest and linear min filters alike. The WebGL2 probe's 1/64
steps are up to 3.7/256 off k/256, so `classifyBlend` called the backend compressed and sent it down the
driver-blend path, whose last step (each footprint texel equals the side's own explicit-LOD sample at some k/256)
assumes an explicit LOD as fine as a footprint LOD. WebGPU does not promise that ("The precise filtering behavior is
implementation-dependent", GPUSamplerDescriptor), so the oracle, not the layer, was wrong: the layer's results were
native's bits. Fix (test/blend-check.mjs): `classifyBlend` takes native's probe beside WebGL2's and returns `native`
when the two are equal at every probed LOD; such a backend has no driver difference to excuse and keeps the exact
comparison (every row equal to native, bit for bit), stricter than before. The driver-blend path stays for a WebGL2
blend that differs from native's (the AMD D3D11 curve). features-browser.mjs and bias-browser.mjs (test:gpu:bias)
pass the native probe. On the M6 both now pass on the exact path ("mip blend: WebGL2 equal to native"), and the
self-test's LOD 3.7/256 too high on the layer still fails (`.linear/implicit/false[0]`). Regression:
`test/blend-check.test.js` ("a WebGL2 blend equal to native at every LOD is native"; fails on the old classifier).

### Fixed: Apple silicon Metal: atan2 with x = -0 is a half turn off, and the layer shipped it (2026-11-15)

Repro (Apple M6, Chrome 156): with the mip blend oracle fixed, `features-browser.mjs` stopped at `inverseTrig: the
layer's acos, asin, atan2 or atan is 6.283185394602366 off at {"sweep":3,"index":3,...}`. Raw WebGL2 (`atan(y, x)`,
inputs from a uniform) and raw WebGPU (`atan2`, inputs from a storage buffer) return the same: atan2(1, -0) =
-pi / 2, atan2(-1, -0) = pi / 2, atan2(0.5, -0) = -pi / 2 (IEEE-754: pi / 2, -pi / 2, pi / 2; with the zero's sign
ignored they are the same), atan2(-0, -1) = pi (IEEE: -pi). Every smooth input is exact. Cause: the layer's startup
probe (`src/device/inverse-trig.ts`) tested acos, asin and atan2 at 65 smooth inputs only, so it judged Metal
accurate and the layer kept the built-ins, against the layer's contract (1e-5 of float64 over the whole domain,
Scott's ruling of 2026-11-11). Fix: the probe ends with three signed-zero inputs, (1, -0), (-1, -0) and (-0, -1);
the stand-in guard (`INVERSE_TRIG_IMPLAUSIBLE`) now reads the smooth inputs only, so a half-turn edge flags the
driver instead of reading as a stand-in. On the M6 the layer now calls its own `_acos`, `_asin`, `_atan` and
`_atan2`: inverseTrig 2.86e-7 off float64. Regression: `test/inverse-trig.test.js` ("the probe flags a driver whose
atan2 is a half turn off at x = -0"). Native WebGPU on Metal keeps the driver's answer for a runtime -0 (Tint folds a
constant -0.0 to 0, so the case's native column reads 2.96e-7); see the open entry below.

### Open (below Margo): native WebGPU on Apple silicon: atan2(y, -0) is a half turn off (2026-11-15)

Repro: the raw WebGPU half of the entry above (a fragment shader writing `bitcast<u32>(atan2(v.x, v.y))` for `v`
read from a storage buffer holding (1, -0)) returns -pi / 2 on an Apple M6 under Chrome 156 (Dawn Metal). Cause:
the Metal atan2 Dawn emits; Margo's WGSL calls `atan2` directly. Effect: a Margo shader whose x argument is a
computed -0 (for example `atan2(d.y, -d.x)` with `d.x` = 0) gets the opposite angle on Mac native WebGPU only.
Fix condition: a Dawn or Metal change, or a Margo-wide WGSL atan2 that does not reach the driver at x = 0; not
attempted here (it touches every package with atan2, core included, under the freeze).

### Fixed: weather lens drops lost sub-cell precision far from the origin (2026-11-10)

Repro: `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/weather/tests/parity-browser.mjs lens` on native WebGPU (RTX A6000) failed its unchanged 0.0001 CPU-oracle bound in the 2400 long-time cases at 0.000135468. Cause: the lens shader formed the full drop centre `(cell + offset) * spacing` before subtracting it from the sample, so f32 cancellation dropped the fractional offset bits. It now reduces the sample to its cell with `fma(-cell, spacing, q)` and subtracts only the fractional centre. Regression: the same parity run, native and `--compat`.

### Fixed: stage viewer GPU check captured before the GPU had finished (2026-11-10)

Repro: `node scripts/stage-viewer-gpu-check.js` under a loaded GPU could compare a capture taken while pipelines were still compiling or before the restored environment device was in use. Cause: the fixture (tests/stage-viewer.ts) waited a fixed number of animation frames, which does not establish pipeline readiness or completion of submitted work. It now waits for pipeline quiescence, `queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` and the current environment device before every capture. Regression: tests/viewer-fixture-ready.test.js (runs the real fixture with the submitted-work fence held; fails on the old fixture).

### Fixed: tests/vite-cache-isolation.test.js passed every test and then never exited (2026-11-10)

Repro: `node --test tests/vite-cache-isolation.test.js` on main printed 5 passing tests and then sat until the gate's 1500 s limit killed it. Cause: "a failed start removes its cache folder" starts Vite with a plugin whose `configureServer` throws; `createServer` then rejects after it has opened two file system watches (FSEventWrap), and the rejected call returns no server, so `startDevServer` had nothing to close. `startDevServer` now adds a first plugin that receives the server before any other `configureServer` hook, so a failed start closes it. Regression: "a failed start leaves nothing open, so its process exits" in the same file (a child process making only a failed start exits by itself; on the old code it still holds two FSEventWrap after 20 s).

### Open (below Margo): AMD Direct3D 11 steepens the trilinear blend, so AMD compat IOR stays over its budget (2026-11-10)

Release exception: steepened trilinear blend keeps AMD compat IOR over budget.

Repro: `MARGO_GPU=amd GPU_POWER=low-power node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/reference-rendering/mip-blend-control.mjs` on the workstation's AMD Radeon iGPU (RDNA 2, driver 32.0.21042.62). The page is raw WebGL2 and raw WebGPU with no Margo code: level 0 white, every other level black, one sampler with linear min, mag and mip filters, sampled at LOD fractions 0.125 to 0.875 both by explicit LOD and by implicit derivatives. Raw WebGL2 on ANGLE D3D11 uses level-1 weights 0.03125, 0.1875, 0.34375, 0.5, 0.65625, 0.8125, 0.96875, that is clamp(1.25 f - 0.125), flat below 0.1 and above 0.9 (worst error 0.098), for explicit and implicit sampling alike. Raw WebGPU (Dawn on D3D12) on the same GPU gives exactly f (worst 0 explicit, 1/256 implicit, the hardware's 8-bit LOD fraction), and both APIs give exactly f on the RTX A6000. So the steepened blend is the AMD driver's Direct3D 11 trilinear path under ANGLE, not compat state: compat binds LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR, MIN_LOD/MAX_LOD from the descriptor, base level 0, and no anisotropy for an isotropic sampler, exactly the raw page's state.

Effect: since 42d6e24ae compat keeps the hardware's implicit footprint (the Euclidean derivative estimate chose a different mip from native, J6 ToyCar). On AMD D3D11 that footprint is blended with the steepened weight, which native AMD WebGPU does not do, so batch 160's AMD compat IOR proof scores 2,423,682 against its frozen 2,421,642 while native AMD scores 2,421,894. Compat cannot undo it: WebGL2 exposes no query of the hardware LOD (textureQueryLod is not in GLSL ES 3.00), and the flat zones throw the fraction away, so no shader arithmetic recovers f. Computing LOD in the shader instead brings back the J6 footprint mismatch on every vendor. Coordinator ruling (2026-11-10): the AMD compat IOR budget is not re-frozen; this one AMD D3D11 compat case is recorded here, every other case still stops. Fix condition: a driver or ANGLE change that makes the control print f for WebGL2, then the proof rerun against the unchanged budget.

### Fixed: one live texture more or less after 100 device restores on the WebGL2 layer, in one run of three (2026-11-11)

Repro: `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/device-recreation-soak.mjs` (core meshes, `Shadows` and `LODSystem`, 100 forced losses restored by core, 120 frames between losses), RTX A6000, Edge 157. One run of three had 6 textures live after the first restore and 5 after the hundredth, the picture the same. Logging every restore's live textures by format and size showed the missing one in about one restore in seven: the `r32float` level of `@margoengine/shadows`' WebGL2 nearest-depth route (`src/compat.ts`).

Cause: `Shadows.setup` asked `import()` for that route again on every device, and frames drawn before the import settled ran the WebGPU nearest-depth kernel, whose atomics put it on the layer's CPU tier (the whole map read back and looped over in JavaScript, about 0.5 s a frame at 2048 x 2048). In a still scene the map did not change again, so the route never built its level. The WebGPU kernel's pipeline was also compiled on the layer when the route was there. Fix: once loaded, the route is kept and every later setup (a restore, another `Shadows`) takes it at once, and the kernel is compiled only when the route is missing. Regression: `packages/shadows/test/compat-route.test.js` (three restores, each first frame builds the route's level and compiles no atomics kernel); the soak now names each live texture by format and size and, run 4 times (400 restores), kept 6 textures and 12 buffers after every restore.

### Fixed: a device lost while an environment rebuilt was reported as an error, and a failed restore twice (2026-11-11)

Repro: `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/restore-fault-sweep.mjs` before this fix: after any failure that kept the next settle from finishing, the clean restore reported "Failed to execute 'mapAsync' on 'GPUBuffer': The Device was lost before mapping was resolved", and every environment failure reached `engine.onError` twice. Cause: `Environment.restore` passed on its SH readback's rejection when its device was lost mid-rebuild, though core restores onto the next device and the environment rebuilds there (core reports no loss it recovers from); `Environment` and `EnvironmentLighting` share one restore and both reported its rejection. Fix (environment): a rebuild whose device was lost rejects with a coded `MargoError` (`failed`, help link `gpu-lost`) that the plugins do not report, and a restore's failure is reported once (`src/restore-report.ts`). Regression: `packages/environment/tests/restore-lost.test.js`.

### Fixed: the GPU fault helper fired uncapturederror inside the failing call (2026-11-11)

`tests/support/gpu-faults.js` dispatched `uncapturederror` synchronously, so core, which adds its listener right after its first buffers, never heard of a failed first buffer, and on the WebGL2 layer that failure went unreported. A device fires it in a task of its own (WebGPU, "dispatch error"); the helper now does too. Regression: `tests/gpu-faults.test.js` (no event inside the call). The helper also takes `select(method, descriptor, buffer)` so a plan can count one package's calls.

### Fixed: an allocation failure in core, shadows or culling stopped the engine until the next device restore (2026-11-11)

Repro: `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/restore-fault-sweep.mjs` (and with `MARGO_COMPAT=1`), RTX A6000, Edge 157. Each of the 40 (native) or 42 (WebGL2 layer) allocations a restore makes fails once in turn. Every failure is reported and a clean restore after it gives the same buffers, textures and picture. But a failed allocation of core (10 native, 8 layer), `@margoengine/shadows` (5) or `@margoengine/culling` (13 native, reported at the next frame) stops the engine: the out-of-memory error reaches core's `uncapturederror` listener, and every frame throws the coded `gpu-lost` fault (`engine.start()` stops its loop) until the next device restore. `@margoengine/environment` scopes its allocations, rejects its restore and the frames go on. Cause: those allocations run outside an `out-of-memory` error scope, and WebGPU only reports the failure later, after frames have used the object. Fix needed: scope the allocations of each package's setup and restore, skip the package's passes until the scope resolves, and on failure release, report a coded error and retry at the next restore, with `scripts/restore-fault-sweep.mjs` asserting that the frame after any one failure renders.

Fix (KB6434a, core ce7f1807be): an out-of-memory `uncapturederror` (an allocation made outside an error scope) is reported once through `engine.onError` and destroys the device, so the ordinary restore rebuilds every batch and plugin; validation errors still failed every frame then (fixed 2026-11-11, core and stage audit row B4: the next frame throws one once, then it clears; regression: the two uncaptured validation error cases in `tests/deep-core-allocation-failure.test.js`). Regression: `tests/deep-core-allocation-failure.test.js`. Fix (KB6434c, culling): `CulledMeshes` makes its frame buffer, slot buffers and occlusion set inside error scopes (`packages/shared/error-scope.js` `scoped`) and uses each only once the device confirms it; a failure is reported once and the meshes draw unculled (core draws them) until the next device restore. Regression: `packages/culling/test/alloc-failure.test.js`. The sweep now fails each allocation for one device only and asserts that each failure is reported exactly once, that no frame throws and that the frame after it draws the scene. Fix (KB6434b, KB-C34g, shadows): `Shadows` keeps making its maps, uniform and reduction buffer outside error scopes, so receivers bind them in the first frame after an attach, a restore or a new map size and that frame is shadowed; an out-of-memory failure there reaches core's listener and the KB6434a device rebuild remakes them. Package containment (scoped maps, a 1x1 fallback until the device confirms them, branch core34 3314e8e0b2) was built and dropped: it drew the first frame after every attach, restore and resize unshadowed (`packages/materials/test/browser-check.mjs` catcherSun read 255 for 102, natively and on the WebGL2 layer), and core's rebuild already covers the failure. Regression: `packages/shadows/test/alloc-failure.test.js` (the first frame after attach draws the depth passes and binds the real map; an out-of-memory map or uniform is reported once and the rebuilt device draws shadows). `VirtualShadows` (KB6434d) goes the same way: its pools, page table, uniform and buffers stay outside error scopes, receivers bind them in the first frame, and an out-of-memory one is recovered by the KB6434a rebuild. Regression: the `VirtualShadows` cases of `packages/shadows/test/alloc-failure.test.js` (fail on a contained build, which bound a fallback in the first frame).

### Fixed: on the WebGL2 layer, work on a destroyed object was blamed on the next allocation, and three event and task rules differed from WebGPU (KB-C34c, 2026-11-11)

Repro: `MARGO_COMPAT=1 node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node scripts/restore-fault-sweep.mjs` before this fix: 23 cases failed (11 core, 7 environment, 5 shadows), each failure followed by "WebGL2 error 0x502 at texture 'environment source cube'" or a like error at an unrelated allocation, and core faulted every frame. Causes, all in `@margoengine/webgl2-compat`, found by checking `getError` after every GL call of the sweep: (1) queue writes, passes, bind groups, vertex and index buffers and copies on a destroyed buffer or texture made their GL calls on the deleted objects (`bufferSubData`, `texSubImage2D`, `bindBuffer`, `framebufferTexture2D`, `bindTexture`, `copyBufferSubData`, the compute runtime's `readPixels`); GL answered INVALID_OPERATION, which stayed queued until the next allocation's one `getError` and was reported as an `internal` error of that allocation. (2) `install()` named the layer's `GPUOutOfMemoryError` but left the browser's `GPUUncapturedErrorEvent` and `GPUError`, so `new GPUUncapturedErrorEvent('uncapturederror', { error })` with the layer's error threw a TypeError and the failure was never dispatched. (3) The layer dispatched `uncapturederror` inside the failing call, so validation errors of later calls could reach listeners before the allocation failure raised first. (4) `onSubmittedWorkDone` on a destroyed device (or a lost context) resolved at once, so a page waiting for it in a loop ran on microtasks alone and starved every timer and task for 20 s, core's restore and the layer's pipeline link polls included ("1 pipelines compiling"). Fix: a queue write, or a submit, that uses a destroyed buffer, texture or query set is a validation error and makes no GL call; a failed submit runs none of its command buffers (each command encoder lists what its commands use; the check sees a destroy() at once, though GL objects go after the work queued before it). `install()` names `CompatGPUError` and `CompatUncapturedErrorEvent` as `GPUError` and `GPUUncapturedErrorEvent`, and the device dispatches that event in a task of its own, not after the device is destroyed. `onSubmittedWorkDone` always resolves in a later task. Regression: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/destroyed-use.test.js` and `packages/webgl2-compat/test/device.test.js` ("install() names GPUError and GPUUncapturedErrorEvent too"). The compat sweep now passes (45 calls).

### Fixed: at the WebGPU compatibility level a one-layer shadow map was bound through a view dimension it was not made for (KB-C34f, 2026-11-11)

Repro: `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs` with `Shadows` on one layer (RTX A6000, Edge 157): every compatibility-level frame failed with "[Invalid CommandBuffer] is invalid due to a previous error. While calling [Queue].Submit". On main this was `Shadows` with `bounds` (one cascade); a 1x1 fallback map tried on branch core34 showed it first. Cause: receivers bind the shadow maps as '2d-array' views. A device without `core-features-and-limits` binds a texture only as its `textureBindingViewDimension`, '2d' by default for a texture of one layer, so a one-layer map made bind groups that failed validation. Fix: `packages/shadows/src/index.ts` makes every receiver-bound map (depth arrays and tint maps) with `textureBindingViewDimension: '2d-array'` on such devices; full-level devices get the descriptors they always did (the pinned GPU call proofs are unchanged). Regression: `packages/shadows/test/compat-view-dimension.test.js` (the `bounds` case fails without the fix); real GPU: `packages/webgl2-compat/test/adapter-browser.mjs`. The same held for the `VirtualShadows` page table with `levels: 1` (one layer, bound as '2d-array'): `packages/shadows/src/virtual.ts` makes it with the same hint on such devices (KB6434d; the 'a one-level page table' case of the same test fails without it).

### Fixed 2026-11-11 (KB6438a): sciviz views ResizeObserver callback rendered and resized the canvases it observes (WebKit)

- **What:** `sciviz test:browser:views` in Playwright WebKit fails on some runs with the page error "ResizeObserver loop
  completed with undelivered notifications." (3 of 3 runs at 90f7f7dd0, 1 of 2 at 8ac516006); it passes in Chromium.
- **Repro:** `MARGO_BROWSER=webkit npm run test:browser:views --workspace @margoengine/sciviz`.
- **Cause:** the observer in `packages/sciviz/src/views.ts` (the `#resize` callback of the three-slice view) fits the
  slices and called `figure.render()`, which can change the size of the canvases it observes in the same frame.
- **Fix:** the callback schedules one refit and redraw on the next animation frame (deliveries before it share it;
  dispose cancels it). Regression: packages/sciviz/tests/views-browser.mjs counts renders inside the delivery (must be
  0) and after it. WebKit evidence: on the Apple silicon Mac (Apple M6, macOS 27.2) the views browser test passed 10 of 10
  Playwright WebKit runs at 397545736b, compatibility layer off and on, with no ResizeObserver page error.

## Batch 132b audit: materials (fixed, 2026-11-11, lane N)

- Fixed: `Transmission` (packages/materials/src/transmission-pass.ts) built its scene-copy mip chain with a 2x2 box
  read from texel 2p of the level above. At an odd size the last column and row never reached a coarser level, and
  each level drifted by up to a texel from its footprint; the comment claimed the odd edge repeated. Input: a 37 x 23
  canvas with refracting glass (`npm run test:gpu:transmission-layers`). Wrong output: level 1 off a float64 area filter
  of level 0 by 106 times the half-float tolerance (0.002 + 0.2%). Fix: the chain uses shared/mipmaps.js's area
  filter (each source texel weighted by its overlap, as gltf/pbr's mips since 65098f33f); worst error now 0.16 of the
  tolerance on Metal WebGPU and MARGO_COMPAT=1. Rough glass near an odd-sized frame's right and bottom edges now
  blurs the last column and row in. Size (scripts/quality/baselines/sizes.json, entry of 2026-11-11 for f2cd28c42):
  the transmission entry grew 323 B gzip (8,350 to 8,673) and transmission-layers 271 B (5,193 to 5,464), the shared
  filter's loop in place of the 2x2 box.
- Test that passed whatever the code did: test/physical.test.js asserted "group 0 binds the volume" by finding any
  2-entry bind group whose second entry was binding 1; that matched the old reduce groups (source, sampler), not the
  frame group [0, 3, 1] that holds the volume. It now looks for a buffer at binding 1.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the Rainier virtual-shadow case offset its receivers twice (KB-L6b-rv)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:gpu:outside` in packages/shadows failed on main (f5dd85e6be) with 'rainier-virtual: shadow overlap 0.733, needs 0.75', the same value every run, native and on the WebGL2 layer.
- **Cause:** 9ae0388ee5 made every VirtualShadows receiver move a quarter of its page's texel along its normal and turned `normalBias` into an extra offset on top of that (the cascades did the same in f3af757782). The case still passed `normalBias: 0.1`, written when that was the whole offset, so receivers moved twice as far. Measured on the RTX A6000: overlap 0.733 with 0.1, 0.8002 with no extra normal offset (bias 0.1 kept), 0.7952 with neither; `bias` makes no difference here.
- **Fix:** the case passes no extra normal offset (packages/shadows/test/outside/cases.mjs, with the reason beside it). The 0.75 overlap and 0.05 difference bounds are unchanged. Regression: the `rainier-virtual` row of `npm run test:gpu:outside`, which fails with the old option.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the staging TAA still check counted frames before its pipeline existed, and the WebGL2 route landed a sample every 3 to 4 frames (KB-L6b-ti)

- **Repro:** `npm run test:gpu` in packages/studio failed on main (f5dd85e6be) at pathtrace-browser.mjs:73, 'TAA idleDelay 0.25 converges', with 3 samples (2 on a later run) where 4 were due.
- **Cause:** with TAA attached the still traces into TAA's linear capture target, and the tracer compiles the display pipeline for that format on the first frame it traces. The check's sixteen frames, meant to start after pipeline readiness, started after `still.ready` only: on the loaded RTX A6000 the first row traced nothing for 12 of them (frames read `active, 0 samples` until frame 15) while that pipeline compiled. The second row reused it and converged by frame 5. Not 5f1d85b3c4: the TAA sample phase plays no part in the still's sample count.
- **Fix:** packages/studio/test/pathtrace-browser.html compiles the pipeline first: a one-sample still with TAA attached and `waitForPipelines` until it has traced, then the two rows as before. The sixteen frames, the 0.25 s delay and the four samples are unchanged. Measured after: idle for two frames, active from the third, four samples by the seventh, kept to the end, in both rows.
- **Second cause, on the WebGL2 layer (the check's own ANGLE Vulkan loop):** the same rows failed `stationary temporal frames retain convergence` at main 942f0aa120, 3 runs of 3: a sample every 3 to 4 frames, 3 samples at frame 16. Measured with a timing log: a batch of one sample takes about 13 ms to replay its passes and 10 to 22 ms for its one census read, and the viewport then (a) added a landed batch in one frame and started the next only in the frame after, and (b) made a batch's first submissions in a microtask after the frame, so the frame's `onSubmittedWorkDone` fence came before them and the batch landed a frame later. Fix in `@margoengine/voxel-pathtracer`: `TraceRoute.run` starts at once when no run is in progress (src/compat.ts), and `#execute` adds a landed batch in a submission of its own before the frame writes the next batch's frame uniform, then starts that batch in the same frame (src/tracer.ts). Measured after, 3 runs: a sample every 2 frames, four samples by frame 10 to 12, kept to frame 16, in both rows. Regression: `packages/voxel-pathtracer/tests/route-pace.test.js` (fake WebGL2 device; fails without either change: samples 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 instead of 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4). Native work per frame unchanged; on the route one more submission per landed batch (the add).

### Fixed 2026-11-11: the compute and colour-grading parity adapters refused cases shader can build (KB6250b)

- **Repro:** the parity preflight (batch 159) reported Margo missing on `p-compute-262144` and `p-color-grading`: their builders in bench/scenes/parity/margo-renderer.js and margo-post.js threw `unsupported:`.
- **Cause:** the adapters were written before `@margoengine/shader` had storage inputs, raw point meshes, `ComputePass`, `NodePass` and the hue and saturation utilities, and were not updated when it gained them.
- **Fix:** both builders use those APIs (aa6ffaab01). `node scripts/parity-smoke-browser.mjs --runs=1 --cases=p-compute-262144,p-color-grading --engines=margo` prints ok for both (no timing, speed phase). Regression: `tests/parity-adapters.test.js`, which fails when any Margo adapter throws `unsupported:` without an open known-bugs entry (only `p-light-probe`, KB6250c, is left). Docs: docs/whitepaper/parity-diagnoses.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: three fixed waits had no `fixed-wait:` reason, so the fixed-wait gate was red on main (KB-L6b-fw)

- **Repro:** `node --test tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js` failed on main b19009b802: `scripts/check-fixed-waits.mjs` counted one unmarked fixed wait each in packages/materials/test/fur.html:12 (four TAA frames), tests/dev-server-watch.test.js:41 (3 s) and tests/stale-document.test.js:57 (0.5 s) against a baseline of 0.
- **Cause:** the three checks wait on time on purpose (fur steps its wind time over four frames; the other two prove an absence: no reload, a held GPU promise) and carried no `// fixed-wait:` line saying so; two had a `wall-clock:` note, which the gate does not read.
- **Fix:** be528236c1 gave each its `fixed-wait:` reason; no wait changed length and the baseline stayed 0. Checked again on 942f0aa120: the gate reports none new and the test passes (14 of 14). Regression: `tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js`, which fails on any unmarked fixed wait.

### Fixed 2026-11-11: two root tests failed only in a parallel root run (KB-FL2, KB-FL3)

Found by running the root suite as the full run does (`node --test --test-concurrency=4 tests/*.test.js`) ten times on the workstation beside other lanes. Each cause is shared state or a step deadline, not the code under test being slow. Two more failures of the same run, KB-FL1 and a default-capacity test, were in the tests of the scheduler that was removed on 2026-11-16; both are gone with it (KB-GPULOCK-ALL).

- KB-FL2, `tests/package-browser-root.test.js`. Each cwd probe (a shell running `node -p`) had a 5 s step limit. Measured during parallel root runs: median 85 ms, slowest 2.6 s of 1,340 samples; the original failing run had more load beside it, and the message gave no reason. The probes now run without a step deadline, the test has one 120 s hang bound, and a failed probe reports its exit code, signal and output. Regression: `tests/package-browser-root-load.test.js` holds the first probe back 6 s with a preload (fails on the old test at 5.1 s, passes on the new one). Not reproduced in the ten runs, so the cause is the one load-sensitive step the test had, ruled in by measurement; it shares no temp folder, port or env with other files.
- KB-FL3, `tests/dev-servers.test.js` ("the probe passes a clean server ..."), failed once with EPERM removing the server's folder. `probe()` in `scripts/support/dev-server-probe.mjs` ended the server with taskkill and returned, but taskkill returns while the process is still dying and holding its working folder. The probe now waits for `endTree` (scripts/support/shutdown.mjs), which waits until the tree is gone, and reports any process still running as a problem. Regression: the two new probe tests in `tests/dev-servers.test.js` (the end of the kill is held back, so the order is the same every run).

Ruled out for KB-FL2: a shared temp folder (the test makes its own with `mkdtemp`), a fixed port (none), the build lock (the test does not build), and repository files rewritten by another test (the fixture files kept their checkout times through the runs).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: a clustered light under the sheen took the ambient albedo scaling, and the materials sheen lobe check read the base's highlight (KB3297b)

Repro: `node scripts/run-with-timeout.mjs -- node packages/materials/test/features-browser.mjs lobes` at
5cf4e1223 failed "sheen under a directional light without the hook" on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer: plain 0.14996
against the sun 0.15896, a gap of 0.027 summed over the channels under the check's 0.03 floor. Both are 8-bit sRGB
steps read back as linear: 108 and 111. Cause, measured on the same page: KB3297 (f84608f7e, gltf/pbr) made the sun
under the sheen take the KHR_materials_sheen punctual albedo scaling, which took the sun from step 112 to 111; the sun
on the same surface without any sheen is also step 111. On a black base with the default 0.04 specular, lit along
(0.3, 0.2, 1), the sheen lobe and what the scaling takes off the highlight cancel to within one step, so the check had
been measuring the base's highlight, and passed only on the old, simplified scaling. KB3240f and KB3240b do not move
it (the base is black). The same probe showed the other half of the KB3297 gap: `physicalLobes` (clustered) still
scaled every clustered light's base by the ambient form 1 - max3(sheen) E(n.v), so a clustered directional light
stayed on step 112 while the sun read 111.

Fix: `physicalLobes` hands each light's base to its lobes, which take max3(sheen) max(E(n.l) - E(n.v), 0) of it off
under the coat, the spec's punctual form min(1 - max3(sheen) E(n.v), 1 - max3(sheen) E(n.l)) together with the ambient
form `layers()` applies (clustered). The lobe checks' sheen surface has no specular (`specularIntensity: 0`), as the
page's "black under the lobe" intends, at intensity 512 (was 64) so the lobe clears the tone curve's dark end: plain 0, sun and every
hooked light 0.0595 per channel. The 0.03 floor is unchanged. A second surface, `sheenOver`, keeps the 0.04 specular
and asserts the hooked clustered directional light equals the sun to the step (0.15896 both; 0.16203 against 0.15896
without the fix). Area and shaped lights keep the ambient form (docs/limits.md). Regression:
`packages/clustered/test/clustered.test.js` ("physicalLobes leaves a shader without lobes alone ...") and materials
`test:gpu:features` `lobes`, both failing without the fix.

### Batch 228 job 2 point styles
No open defect found in the new filter and style evaluation; the CPU suite and both-backend pixel checks are in the points tests. Scope limits are in docs/limits.md.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: KB-FW-MATRIX, the fixed-wait check was red on main after the browser matrix scripts (`@margoengine/webgl2-compat`)

- **Repro (before):** `node --test tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js` on 97411fd0b8: "packages/webgl2-compat/scripts/browser-matrix.mjs has a new fixed wait" at its 250 ms readiness poll.
- **Cause:** the poll of a WebDriver page for `window.ready` (bounded by its deadline) carried no `// fixed-wait:` reason; no readiness event crosses WebDriver, so a poll is the right wait.
- **Fix:** the poll carries its reason; no wait changed. Regression: `tests/check-fixed-waits.test.js`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: KB-NODEPASS-ATTACH, NodePass.attach always threw (`@margoengine/shader`, `@margoengine/shader/glsl-pass`)

- **Repro (before):** `NodePass.attach(engine, inputColor().rgb)` on any engine threw MargoError `'state'`. ShaderPass had no attach at all and was exempted from the static-factory rule in `tests/api-conventions.test.js`.
- **Cause:** `NodePass.attach` was `engine.use(new NodePass(node))`, but a NodePass runs only as a PostStack stage and its `setup()` throws `'state'` unless a PostStack joined it first, so the documented factory could never succeed.
- **Fix:** `NodePass.attach(engine, node, options?)` and the new `ShaderPass.attach(engine, shader, options?)` are async, as other packages' stack-only stages are (WideAngle, LensDrops): they load `@margoengine/post/stack` only when called, run the pass alone in a new PostStack, return the pass, and `pass.dispose()` disposes that stack too. `options` adds `signal` to the constructor's options. The ShaderPass exemption is gone. Update (GAP-POST-ADD1): the first version rejected a scene that already had a PostStack with `'attached'`, because a PostStack's effects were fixed when it was made; `PostStack.addEffect` and `PostStack.join` now exist and both factories join that stack (case "joins the scene's PostStack" in the same test file). Regression: `packages/shader/test/pass-attach.test.js` (all 6 cases fail without the fix) and the attach leg of `packages/shader/test/glsl-pass-check.mjs` (both factories invert the scene within 0 levels, native WebGPU and `MARGO_COMPAT=1`).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: KB-NODEPASS-VIEW, NodePass drew over the whole target in a multi-view frame (`@margoengine/shader`)

- **Repro (before):** a PostStack with a NodePass in an engine rendering two side by side views: the second view's pass cleared and redrew the first view's half (owner check: "no pixel writes outside either view scissor").
- **Cause:** NodePass's render pass always cleared its output and set no viewport or scissor, where the other stack stages use the view's load operation and rectangle (`viewLoadOp`, `applyView`).
- **Fix:** NodePass and the new ShaderPass load the colour in a later view and draw inside the view's rectangle. Regression: `packages/shader/test/owner-lifetime.fixture.js` ("PostStack.attach with a NodePass", failing all 12 cases without the fix) under `npm run check:owners -- --packages=shader`.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: KB-GLSLP1, GLSL sized points in a multi-view frame were sized against the whole target (`@margoengine/shader/glsl-material`, `@margoengine/shader/raw`)

- **Repro (before):** draw a ShaderMaterial point list whose vertex stage writes `gl_PointSize = 8.0` in an engine with two views side by side; inside a view half the canvas wide each square showed 4 pixels wide instead of GL's 8. `viewport_size` of the `'matrix_model'` convention read the whole target too.
- **Cause:** the sprite offset divided by `camera.resolution`, which raw's camera block fills with the target size, and the block held no view size. GL sizes a point in pixels of the viewport it is drawn in (OpenGL ES 3.0.6 sections 2.12.1 and 3.4).
- **Fix:** raw's camera block (224 to 240 bytes) gains `viewport`, the drawn view's x, y, width and height in target pixels (the whole target without a view), written by the colour, G-buffer and TAA velocity passes; the point offset and `viewport_size` read it, `resolution` and `screen_size` stay the target. Regression: `packages/shader/test/glsl-material-check.mjs` ("sized points in two views", 32 lit pixels per view before, 64 after, against the browser's WebGL drawn with two `gl.viewport` calls) on both backends, and `packages/shader/test/raw.test.js` ("the camera block holds the target size in resolution and the drawn view in viewport").

### Fixed 2026-11-15: async loaders built in the scene active when they finished, not the one they started in (KB-OWN-ASYNC1, fbx, blender, loaders, lod, tiles)

- **Repro (before):** `const s = engine.createScene('b'); s.use({ name: 'x', setup() { p = parseFBX(engine, bytes); } });` then `(await p).root.scene` was `engine.scene`, not `s`. `parseMargoNodes`, `parseMargoPBR`, `loadOBJ` and `TilesRenderer.load` behaved the same. `autoLOD`, `hierarchicalLOD`, `LevelStream` and a `TilesRenderer` tile made their levels, far meshes, follow plugins, streamed levels and tile models in the default scene even when their source or renderer was in another scene.
- **Cause:** same as KB-OWN-GLTF1: the code ran `engine.createMesh`, `engine.use` or a loader after an await, and those act on the scene active at that moment.
- **Fix:** `captureScene` (before the first await) in fbx, blender and loaders, as gltf does; a new `sceneScope(engine, scene)` in `packages/shared/scene-scope.js` for work that belongs to a scene known from an object: lod uses the scene of the source mesh or the stream, tiles the scene of the renderer.
- **Regression:** packages/fbx/test/scene.test.js, packages/blender/tests/async-scene.test.js, packages/loaders/tests/mtl-scene.test.js, packages/lod/test/auto.test.js (three scene tests), packages/lod/test/stream.test.js and packages/tiles/tests/async-scene.test.js.
- **Checked and fine:** usdz `curves()` (fixed in 4509c26c46), tiles `TileFeatures` (its `engine.use` runs in its constructor, before any await).

### Fixed 2026-11-15: decodeBrotli accepted non-zero fill bits after the last meta-block (decoders)

- **Repro:** `decodeBrotli(Uint8Array.of(0x86))` (window bits 16, ISLAST 1, ISLASTEMPTY 1, then a set fill bit)
  returned an empty array; any stream whose last byte had a set unused bit decoded as if it were valid.
- **Cause:** RFC 7932 section 9.2 (ISLASTEMPTY) and the end of section 9.3 require the bits after the last meta-block,
  up to the byte boundary, to be zero; the decoder stopped reading after the last meta-block without checking them.
- **Fix:** the decoder reads those bits and throws `MargoError` `failed` ("fill bits are not zero") when one is set;
  regression in packages/decoders/tests/brotli.test.js (every bit of the last byte of reference-encoder streams either
  changes the output or fails), failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: meshopt index decoders accepted streams KHR_meshopt_compression makes invalid (decoders)

- **Repro:** `meshoptDecodeGltfBuffer(Uint8Array.of(0xe1, 0x00, ...new Uint8Array(16)), 3, 4, 'TRIANGLES')` returned
  the triangle (0xffffffff, 0xffffffff, 0) instead of failing; a codeaux table holding a 0xf nibble, a codeaux table
  with non-zero last two bytes, and a varint of six bytes (`0xd1 80 80 80 80 80 00 ...` as INDICES) also decoded.
- **Cause:** KHR_meshopt_compression Appendix A (modes 1 and 2) makes a stream invalid when it reads an edge or vertex
  FIFO entry that was not written, when its codeaux table breaks the two structure rules, or when a varint runs past
  5 bytes. Both decoders (meshopt.ts and the meshopt-simd crate) filled the FIFOs with all ones and read on, never
  looked at the codeaux table as a whole, and stopped a varint after 5 bytes without checking the last one ended it.
- **Fix:** both decoders count the FIFO entries written and refuse a read past them, check the codeaux table before
  the first triangle and refuse a fifth varint byte with its high bit set; the TypeScript decoder names each case.
  Regressions in packages/decoders/tests/meshopt.test.js and tests/meshopt-simd.test.js (the Wasm gives the
  TypeScript decoder's error on every case), failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: map tiles above zoom 20 lost their shape (`@margoengine/sciviz/geo` tileLayer)

- **Repro:** `tileLayer(fig, { tiles, zoom: 22, area: [7.0, 46.0, 7.001, 46.001] })` with figure limits around the tile:
  each tile's 16 x 16 grid collapsed to a few vertex positions, so the image stretched across slivers.
- **Cause:** the tile shader placed vertices in float32 at (x + u) / 2^zoom of a world that spans [-1, 1], and the
  figure's float32 data-to-scene translation for a small area is huge. Past zoom 20 neither fits float32's 24 bits.
- **Fix:** relative-to-centre placement (Ohlarik 2008, "Precisions, Precisions"; Cozzi and Ring 2011, ch. 5). Figure
  passes layers its transform in double precision too (`setModel(model, exact)`); the tile layer maps each tile's
  centre and grid offsets into the scene in double on the CPU, and the GPU adds the small float32 offsets to the
  centre. Regression: `packages/sciviz/tests/geo-tiles-browser.mjs` (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer) draws one tile at
  zoom 2, 22 and 24 with the same framing and needs the same picture; 19,078 pixels differed on the old code.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: parseKTX2 reported BC1 RGB files as having alpha (decoders)

- **Repro:** `parseKTX2` on a KTX2 file with `vkFormat` 131 (`VK_FORMAT_BC1_RGB_UNORM_BLOCK`) or 132 (its sRGB form)
  returned `hasAlpha: true`.
- **Cause:** `hasAlpha` was derived from the WebGPU format name, and both BC1 kinds map to `bc1-rgba-unorm`; BC1 RGB has
  no alpha, and WebGPU samples a three-colour block's black texel with alpha 0, which an opaque material must ignore.
  The same fault was fixed for KTX 1 (`COMPRESSED_RGB_S3TC_DXT1`) on 2026-11-15; the KTX2 reader was not checked then.
- **Fix:** `hasAlpha` is false for `vkFormat` 131 and 132; regression in packages/decoders/tests/ktx2-layers.test.js
  (all four BC1 numbers), failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: uploadTexture and KTX2GPUDecoder made invalid textures past maxTextureArrayLayers (decoders)

- **Repro:** `uploadTexture(device, file)` with a 7-layer array file on a device whose `maxTextureArrayLayers` is 6, or
  `new KTX2GPUDecoder({device}).createTexture(cube)` on a device that takes 4 layers: no throw, and the returned
  texture was invalid (a WebGPU validation error went to `uncapturederror`).
- **Cause:** both checked the width and height against `maxTextureDimension2D` but never the layer count against
  `maxTextureArrayLayers`.
- **Fix:** both throw `RangeError` naming the limit before any texture is made; regressions in
  packages/decoders/tests/ktx2-layers.test.js and tests/ktx2-gpu.test.js, failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: createKTX2Texture and the KTX2 streamer made invalid textures past the device's limits (decoders)

- **Repro:** `createKTX2Texture(device, result)` with a 16384 px result on a device whose `maxTextureDimension2D` is
  8192, or `new KTX2Streamer({device}).open(url)` for a 64 px cube on a device with `maxTextureDimension2D` 32 or
  `maxTextureArrayLayers` 4: no throw, and the texture was invalid (a WebGPU validation error went to
  `uncapturederror`).
- **Cause:** neither checked the size against `maxTextureDimension2D`, and the streamer never checked its layer
  count against `maxTextureArrayLayers`, where `uploadTexture` and `KTX2GPUDecoder` check both.
- **Fix:** both throw `RangeError` naming the limit before any texture is made (the streamer checks the file's full
  size, the size it grows to); regressions in packages/decoders/tests/decoders.test.js and tests/ktx2-stream.test.js,
  failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: KTX2GPUDecoder decoded UASTC blocks with an undefined partition pattern (decoders)

- **Repro:** a UASTC KTX2 file whose block is mode 7 (first byte 0x07) with a PAT field of 31, or mode 3 with a PAT
  of 11 to 15, or mode 2, 4, 9 or 16 with 30 or 31, through `new KTX2GPUDecoder({device}).createTexture(bytes)`: no
  error, and the shader read its subsets and anchors from the next table in its table buffer (anchors, weights).
- **Cause:** the UASTC LDR 4x4 specification defines 30 two-subset patterns, 11 three-subset patterns (mode 3) and
  19 for mode 7, but the PAT field holds 5 bits (4 in mode 3); only the reserved mode 19 was refused.
- **Fix:** `uastcBlockValid` in ktx2-gpu-shaders.ts refuses those blocks with the reserved mode, before the texture is
  filled; regression in packages/decoders/tests/ktx2-gpu.test.js, failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-16: readJXLHeader took any 12-byte box typed `JXL ` as the container signature (decoders)

- **Repro:** `readJXLHeader(bytes)` (and `JXLDecoder.decode`) on a container file whose signature box content is not
  0D 0A 87 0A, for example byte 8 changed: no signature error; the boxes after it were read as JPEG XL.
- **Cause:** the reader compared the box size (12) and type (`JXL `) but not the 4 content bytes the image/jxl
  registration gives as part of the magic number.
- **Fix:** all 12 bytes are compared; regression in packages/decoders/tests/jxl.test.js, failing on the old source.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: with native glass under Tonemap, Bloom, SSAO or DOF every frame showed the one before (materials, GAP-FILM-LATE)

- **Was:** a glTF with transmissive glass (the Khronos ToyCar) under `Tonemap` drew each frame into the next: a headless `readPixels` after `render()` returned the previous frame byte for byte, and a fresh engine's first frame was black (Film Studio bench film, 2560x1440: after settling frame 80, the first read of frame 0 was byte-identical to frame 80).
- **Cause:** the native glass capture began at order -64, before the HDR captures (SSAO and Bloom -60, DOF -55, Tonemap -50), and presented its own colour at 29, before they wrote the frame into it at 30 and 31. Captures must nest.
- **Fix:** the glass capture begins at -40, inside every HDR capture, so under one it keeps the linear blend and captures nothing (`packages/materials/src/native-glass.js`). The WebGPU queue and readback were in order: the copy ran after the frame.
- **Regression:** `packages/materials/tests/native-glass-nesting.test.js`; `packages/materials/test/native-glass-browser.mjs` `hdrNesting`, native WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed 2026-11-15: the sky lit each frame with the camera altitude of the frame before (sky, GAP-FILM-LATE, GAP-FILM-READY)

- **Was:** `Sky` with `lighting` set the sun's colour and strength from the eye altitude its passes had stored in the previous frame, and from sea level on a fresh sky's first frame: 1 level on 0.06 % of the bench film's pixels a frame late, and a first frame unlike the same frame drawn later.
- **Fix:** `onPreUpdate` takes the altitude from the engine camera of this frame (`packages/sky/src/base.ts`).
- **Regression:** `packages/sky/test/eye-altitude.test.js`.

### Fixed: a bounce cluster spanned parallel surfaces and its VPL was lifted to the highest (clustered, KB-BOUNCE-CLUSTER1, found and fixed 2026-11-16)

- **What:** `LightBounce` reduces a capture to VPLs by a k-means in position and normal. Surfaces facing the same way at different heights (Cabin Hearth's snow at 0.1 m, the window's sill top at 0.97 m and a glazing bar's face at 1.48 m) fell into one cluster, and the VPL, lifted to its highest member (KB-BOUNCE-VPL-BURIED1), stood 1.5 m above the snow, above the log crest's horizon. On the cabin's own captures 32 VPLs lit the crest at 0.55 (the window, with its reveal clip) and 0.83 (the lantern) of the texels' sum.
- **Fix:** the distance adds 8 times the squared offset from the cluster's plane, the L2 proxy distance of variational shape approximation (Cohen-Steiner, Alliez and Desbrun, SIGGRAPH 2004, doi:10.1145/1015706.1015817): 0.92 and 0.94 now (2 to 128 give 0.87 to 0.98).
- **Test:** packages/clustered/test/bounce.test.js, "32 VPLs light the cabin log crest as the capture texels do" (fixture test/fixtures/cabin-bounce-captures.json, the two captures read back on an RTX A6000; fails at weight 0 with 0.83); scripts/clustered-bounce-gpu-check.js unchanged on WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer.

### Fixed: a WebGL2 layer clear test expected a plain array after the layer moved to a reused Float32Array (webgl2-compat, KB-COMPAT-FRESHCLEARS1, found and fixed 2026-11-17)

- **What:** `packages/webgl2-compat/test/fresh-clears.test.js`, "render pass clears of a layer of a 6-layer texture...", failed on main: it compared the arguments of `clearBufferfv` with `[[1, 0, 0, 1]]`, but since KB-COMPAT-FRAMEALLOC1 part 9 the layer hands the call one reused `Float32Array(4)` so a frame allocates no array of doubles.
- **Cause:** the test, not the code. A typed array is a valid `clearBufferfv` source in WebGL2, and the reused array is what keeps the clear path allocation free.
- **Fix:** the test checks there is one colour clear, that its source is a `Float32Array`, and the values it holds at the call (copied with `Array.from`). A layer that wrote any other colour (tried: every channel 0.5) fails it.
- **Test:** packages/webgl2-compat/test/fresh-clears.test.js.

### Fixed: the whiteout kit's weather states lacked smoke (and now humidity and temperature), so the whiteout example's storm slider threw (sky scene-kits, KB-KIT-WEATHERSTATE1, found and fixed 2026-11-17)

- **What:** `whiteout()` gave `storm` and `lull` states with ten of the weather's fields; `examples/whiteout-pass` blends them with `blendStates` and sets the machine, which gave NaN for every missing field and threw `RangeError` from `WeatherMachine.set`, and `npm run check:examples-types` failed on it.
- **Cause:** `KitWeatherState` was written before the weather gained `smoke` (and, today, `humidity` and `temperature`); nothing checked the kit against the weather's `STATE_FIELDS`.
- **Fix:** the kit states carry every field (smoke 0; the weather's blizzard air, 0.85 humidity at -8 C, and 0.9 in the lull).
- **Test:** packages/sky/test/scene-kits.test.js (every key of `STATE_FIELDS`, and a blend set into a `WeatherMachine`; it fails on the old kit).

### Fixed 2026-11-17: the light under a cloud deck was too bright, and the base of thick cloud too dark (sky, KB-CLOUD-DECKLIGHT1)

- **Repro:** `node packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs cloud-bounds` (also under `MARGO_COMPAT=1`). Under
  `VolumetricClouds({sky, weather: {cloud: 1}})` (stratus, deck share 0.44 at noon) the engine sun was dimmed to 0.44
  (`Sky.deck`), but a grey block's sunlit top read 0.93 of its clear level; a full deck 1,000 to 2,000 m with the sun
  overhead over a black ground passed down 0.09 of the sun at tau 5 and sent back 0.10, losing three quarters of it,
  and its base seen from below was 0.067 of its top at tau 20 (RTX A6000, both backends alike).
- **Cause:** two coupled faults in `packages/sky/src/volumetric-clouds.ts`. (1) `cloudScatter` carried light into the
  cloud by three octaves of exp(-b od) (Wrenninge et al. 2013), b down to 0.25, so at optical depth 20 about 1 percent
  was left where diffusion leaves 40, and the powder term darkened what was left. (2) The deck's sun light, laid into
  the sky's map (`environmentLayer`), lit the scene through the map's harmonics on top of the engine sun the deck had
  already dimmed to its share, so the sun reached the scene twice, and in the sky's units, which run hotter than the
  engine sun.
- **Fix:** the source at each sample is first-order scattering (forward lobe on the delta-Eddington scaled beam, back
  lobe on the unscattered one) plus the two-stream diffuse field of a slab along the light (Meador and Weaver 1980;
  Bohren 1987; Joseph, Wiscombe and Weinman 1976), from the optical depth toward the light and a new three-sample
  column down to the base, in Eddington's angular form; sky light enters as a two-sided diffuse two-stream (from above,
  and from below: the map's ground plus `groundAlbedo`, new, default 0.2, times the deck's share), summed so an even
  surround gives exactly its own radiance. The clouds now write a second map, `Sky.environmentLightLayer` (new), which
  the sky's `lighting` takes in place of `environmentLayer`: the deck without the sun and moon light the engine lights
  carry under `dimLight` (with `dimLight` off, that light matched to the engine lights' units). `sunIntensity` is now the
  sun's irradiance over 4 pi; its default went from 1.6 to 0.55, the sun that makes the clear noon sky 0.165 of the
  light on level ground (Erbs, Klein and Duffie 1982). The sky light the clouds take is the upper and lower half of the
  map (it was the upper half and the horizon band).
- **Now:** the block reads 0.51 of clear against the share 0.44; the deck passes down 0.68, 0.45 and 0.22 of the sun
  (diffuse plus the direct beam through thin columns) at nominal tau 5, 20 and 80 against 0.75, 0.45 and 0.19 from the
  two-stream of its own columns, sends up 0.22, 0.50 and 0.73 against 0.25, 0.55 and 0.81, and keeps 0.90 to 0.95 of the
  sun in all (WebGPU and the WebGL2 layer agree to 1e-3).
- **Regression tests:** `packages/sky/test/features-check.mjs` `cloud-bounds` asserts the block within 25 percent of
  the share, down and up within 25 percent of the columns' two-stream at tau 5, 20 and 80, and the sum within 15
  percent (the old shader fails: block 0.93; down 0.09 at tau 5); `packages/sky/test/volumetric-clouds.test.js` "the
