  deck lights the scene once" pins the light-only map, its sun and moon shares and `groundAlbedo`.

## KB-PHYS-BLOCK1 (fixed 2026-11-25): the exact block solver diverged on a tall pile at one pass a substep

`setSolver({blockSolver: true})` (3D, off by default) solves a manifold's normal rows exactly. On the 465-cube pyramid of 30 rows
at 4 substeps and 1 pass a substep (`packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs`, `a_pyramid_of_thirty_rows_settles_at_one_pass_a_substep`,
sleeping off) the apex box's z velocity grows exponentially: 0.003 m/s at 30 s, 0.07 at 60 s, 150 m/s by 90 s (the box leaves the
pile). It is the same with the block solve in the pushing pass only or in the relaxing pass only, and with a larger diagonal shift;
rows 3 to 20 hold, and the defaults (8 substeps, 2 passes) hold and rest better with it than with the sweeps (0.0003 against
0.001 m/s). Cause as understood: the sweeps stop at convergence, a dissipation the exact solve lacks, and the exact normal loads
meet friction solved afterwards at a point at a time against the load of the pass before, and the 1-pass chain spring
(`CHAIN_LOAD`), so a sliding mode of the top of the pile is not damped. It is opt-in, and the default stays off until the 30-row case holds at 1 pass under
its existing bound (Catto, "Solver2D", 2024, the soft step; Tonge, Benevolenski and Voroshilov, SIGGRAPH 2012; Bender, Erleben
and Trinkle, "Interactive simulation of rigid body dynamics in computer graphics", Computer Graphics Forum 33(1), 2014, for friction
against exact normal blocks).

Fixed with KB-PHYS-PILECREEP1, whose cause it shared: the top of the 30-row slab tipped out of its plane, and an island's contacts
now get the stiffness its structures need not to tip, at a finer level of substeps where a quarter of the substep rate is not
enough (`kernel/src/tilt.rs`). With the block solver the 30-row pile holds at 4.2e-4 to 4.3e-4 m/s from 30 to 90 s (150 m/s at 90 s
before). Regression: `packages/physics/kernel/tests/solver.rs` `the_block_solver_holds_a_pile_of_thirty_rows_still_for_ninety_seconds`.
The block solver is the default since 2026-11-25, with KB-PHYS-SPEC1.

## KB-PHYS-SPEC1 (fixed 2026-11-25): the sweeps threw a cube that a wall stops at 6 m/s 0.115 m up, at 8 substeps and 2 passes

`packages/physics/kernel/tests/voxel.rs`, `a_cube_stopped_by_a_wall_over_the_seam_of_two_grids_is_not_thrown_by_the_cell_under_the_wall`:
a frictionless 0.4 m cube slid at 6 m/s into a one-block wall, with the kernel's defaults (8 substeps, 2 passes) and the sweeps,
rose 0.115 m and spun at 6.8 rad/s after the stop (2 passes: 0.115 m; 4 passes: 0.22; 1 pass: 0.0005). Cause: the wall's points
are speculative rows when the stop begins (the face is still 0.1 m off), and a speculative row only bounds a point's approach by
its gap over the substep. Points solved one after another can meet that bound with one point stopped and the cube turning about
it, an equally valid answer of the same inequalities, and more passes settle on it more firmly. The exact block solve of each
manifold gives the stop to all the points at once. Fixed by making `blockSolver` the default (3D `Physics` and `KernelWorld`),
once KB-PHYS-BLOCK1 was fixed: the cube now stops at the wall face and never stands above its rest height (0.39979 m, a slop
deep) once its 2 mm starting drop has landed, the physical bound for a level, frictionless stop. The test's bound on the throw,
loosened to 0.2 m while the sweeps were the default, is restored to that 0 m. `blockSolver: false` still sweeps, and still throws
this cube 0.115 m: that is the method's own ambiguity, recorded as an accepted difference of the option in `docs/limits.md`.
(The 2.2 cm sink that was KB-PHYS-WALL1 was a different bug, fixed: the floor cell under the wall snapped the cube's foot to
its open bottom.)

The flip needed two fixes first: the joint webs' energy ledger read web seed 17's kinematic work as a gain with the block
solver (KB-PHYS-LEDGER1), and a voxel debris piece on a block's edge rocked without end with it (KB-PHYS-EDGEHOLD1). All 60
web seeds gain nothing with either solver; web seed 23, which spiked through joint 19 with the block solver before
a4a479f17, stays in its bounds.

## Fixed 2026-11-26: a time-zero coupled snapshot predates its accumulator sum region (BIO-01)

Fixed by 13b6c14dd0 (KB-LOADS-FRAMEZERO): the field registry reserves a field's sum region when its first contributor
publishes, so the layout a tick-zero snapshot records is the one restore finds. Checked on 076e7e2cc5 with the repro
below (`PlantSway` and `PlantRigidSolver` with the impact of the regression test, snapshot at tick 0, advance 22,
restore): the restore succeeds, the hash matches the snapshot's and the replay matches the first run. Regression:
`packages/physics/tests/world-frame-zero-accumulator.test.js`. The framework request in physics-work-queue.md also
asks for reservation at setup, which is not needed for this repro.

Add `PlantSway` and `PlantRigidSolver` to a `PhysicsWorld`, snapshot before the first `advance()`, advance
one frame and restore that snapshot. Restore rejects the unequal region count. The field registry allocates the
accumulator's sum region on first use. A snapshot taken after the first step captures the full layout. The
regression in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/vegetation.test.js` restores a frame-two snapshot, taken before the
hit and before either body changes its enabled flag. See BIO-01 in [Framework requests](physics-work-queue.md#framework-requests).

The First Wake diagnostic reproduces the same defect with `HullSolver` and `RigidSolver`. The
tick-zero snapshot contains 368 regions. The first advance creates the `bodyForces` sum, after
which restore expects 369 regions. The same setup-time allocation fixes both repros.

## Open: LIFE-03 swimmer wake and contact consumers in Barrier Bay

The engine's swimmer produces the field data for a pectoral bed jet (BB-7) and the tail wake (BB-8/9).
The bed jet now lifts, carries, and deposits real SEA-15 tracer mass. It is checked from the actual swim port
by `packages/physics/tests/coupling/swim.test.js` and on both graphics backends by
`packages/environment/tests/swim-sediment.browser.mjs`. The tail wake still needs a surface/vortex consumer.
The anemone fixture uses a contact wrench stand-in for BB-3.
A rendered shot check remains open for each row in [physics-demo-review.md](physics-demo-review.md).

## Fixed: world-stepped hail uses particle size and scene geometry (PA-32)

Hail drawn by its camera-centred cycle used one fall speed and bounced from `groundY` regardless of the stone's
size or surrounding geometry. `hailSphere` now converts the measured diameter and local-air terminal law to drag
for each body, and `Hail` can draw poses from a falling-body solver. `fallingBoundaryFromPhysics` sweeps each sphere
against fixed colliders. The two-diameter equilibrium fixture is in `packages/weather/tests/hail-physics.test.js`.
The swept wall and raised platform fixtures are in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/falling.test.js`.

## Open: pedestrian force hand-off in Opening Night and City-to-Street

The frame-independent pedestrian solver publishes per-walker compressed load and net contact force.
The Opening Night clips still need the production ragdoll and foot-placement consumers, and
CITY-TO-STREET-2 still needs vehicle and rail actors. Run
`node --test packages/physics/tests/coupling/pedestrians.test.js` after building Physics and NavMesh
to reproduce the measured contact impulses, doorway release and real route grade.
See LIFE-05 in [Framework requests](physics-work-queue.md#framework-requests).

### Pedestrian speed at steady single-file headway (LIFE-05)

The published single-file diagnostic reaches nearly the free-speed pace with 15 and 20 equally spaced
walkers, while the independent experiment slows to 0.90 and 0.56 m/s. A closing-speed anticipation term
can steer approaching pairs. It leaves an equal-speed pair without a future collision, and the sparse
spacing is below the current compression response. A validated steady following law is still needed.
Run `node packages/physics/scripts/life05-pedestrian-measured.mjs`. [Measured station limits](limits.md#life-05-measured-single-file-walking)

## Fixed: geological erosion lacked physical time and multidirectional routing (PA-39)

Fractional passes through the original biome erosion tool routed each cell to one receiver and did not describe
physical rainfall, duration, uplift or grain mobility. The physical path is `LandscapeEvolution` and the
`evolveRelief` biome adapter. Reproduce the divergent catchment and two-grain threshold fixtures with
`node --test packages/physics/tests/coupling/landscape.test.js` after building Physics. The legacy static relief
operation still reproduces existing authored terrain.

## Fixed: solved contacts excite audio without hand-timed triggers (PA-65)

Previously, dropping a body onto a surface produced no audio unless a caller assigned a sound for
the event by hand. A physics world with `ModalContactRigidSolver` and `ModalSoundSolver` now publishes
an impulse, rolling or scraping excitation, with sound and damping set by the contacted materials.
The drop, silent resting support, rolling/sliding and joint-break cases live in
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/modal-sound.test.js`.

## Fixed: valley fog lacked transported extinction (ATMO-08, PA-34 fog)

A stationary fog box could vary noise without transporting moisture, so it did not resolve a plume carried
against a slope or across a valley. Bind `FogGrid` to `DrainageFog` as the volumetric medium. Its physics and
rendered movement are covered by `packages/physics/tests/coupling/drainage-fog.test.js` and
`packages/environment/tests/drainage-fog.browser.mjs`. PA-34 retains the separate cloud path.

## Fixed: snow lacked melt energy and dense slides ignored obstacles (ICE-01, PA-33)

The visual snow layer could stay in place after warming. The older avalanche modeled plant damage without taking
momentum from the dense flow. Bind Weather's snow cover to `Snowpack` and give `Avalanche` the live pack,
obstacle drag or building footprints. Reproduce the former faults with `packages/physics/tests/coupling/snowpack.test.js`,
`packages/weather/tests/snowpack-check.mjs` and `packages/weather/tests/avalanche.test.js`.

## Fixed: dune and snow rendering lacked a moving surface layer (EARTH-07, PA-46 and PA-63)

A static height seed and a separately prescribed plume could not move terrain or represent an exposed ridge losing
snow. `AeolianTransport` sends resolved bed change to `TerrainBed`, and `BlownSand` can now draw its moving layer.
Reproduce with `packages/physics/tests/coupling/aeolian.test.js` and `packages/vfx/test/blown-sand-check.mjs`.
The [TREE-5 review](physics-demo-review.md) tracks integration into the filmed scene and the atmosphere-side fields.

## Fixed: a later footprint could partially publish a failed soil step (EARTH-05)

The soil kernel wrote load, relief, dust, pressure, unloading state and work into the accepted
banks while processing individual contacts. A later invalid wheel row left the earlier work
partially published. The solver now validates the versioned inputs in their owning memory and
commits its trial only after all rows and the native deposition are finite. The coupled foreign
memory regression checks the complete snapshot through the rejection, origin shift and replay.
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/terramechanics.test.js`

An optional registered wheel pose field now lets the renderer consume restored hub transforms and
loads immediately. Wheel attachment getters describe the last step run by the attachment, which can
be ahead of the restored time until the next step. The paired browser proof draws the registered pose
at the restored time. `packages/physics/tests/terramechanics-film.browser.mjs`

## Fixed: soil drainage had no groundwater storage or spring receiver (HYDRO-06)

Previously HYDRO-02 could export soil drainage, but no aquifer stored that water or passed it back to the surface
through springs and seepage. Connect its recharge port to `GroundwaterSolver` and give the existing shallow-water
solver the aquifer's outlet port. The coupling cases in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/groundwater.test.js`
check the exact exchanged volume, and a fixed-head case verifies lateral discharge independently.

### Avalanche displacement and lahar feedback need connections (PA-25)

Later water response needs an avalanche producer writing the same signed displacement rows as the live ICE-03
and EARTH-10 couplings. SEA-06 already consumes those sources, registered bottom motion and the moving lava front.
The meltwater and steam from lava contact with ICE-05 are measured. Sediment entrainment plus heat and water
return across a lahar remain open. Reproduce the resolved shoreline and heat edges with
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/lava.test.js`.

The engine fixture covers the real TerrainBed-to-contact path. A ground animal placed on an overhang cannot

arbitrary-surface collider field and articulated foot binding. The queue lists the shared contact and terrain
geometry contract needed for independent impulse and animation consumers.

water level into local immersed fraction and uses a prescribed current. Predicting site current and

See [Framework requests](physics-work-queue.md#framework-requests) for the shared layout.

Vehicles sink into a calibrated yielding surface and feel the resulting suspension load. EARTH-05 now transfers the
real wheel and belt loads to TerrainBed and refits the same collider before the next rigid step. Live hoof and biped
pressures produce persistent relief and loft mineral dust. A configured hardpan changes the pressure response
according to local layer thickness. The excavation floor accepts the same spatial data as TerrainBed. Solver
exchange of changing subsurface properties still needs a shared soil contract.
The original city, deck, horse and courier shots still need the production bindings. The mean
and resolved tiers reproduce held-out dry quartz and fire clay plate sinkage. The resolved tier supports
sampled projected contours and reproduces the Wh32 rolling sinkage at zero and moderate powered slip.

The cylindrical raster resolves across-wheel penetration on the live slope. Measured
dynamic cross-slope camber forces remain open.
The steady drawbar and axle torque match the measured 60% tip-slip case. An opt-in wheel
can excavate beyond its initial bearing cut from the live phase. Its exact swept-volume
and floor tests pass. Measured transient contact angles and high-slip sinkage remain open. The optional
cross-track depositor conserves independent bank volumes from the actual cut.
Grouser transport can backfill its solver-owned trench from earlier cuts or feed the opposite bank.
The straight locked condition matches both measured relative bank crests. Absolute scanned
profiles at powered slip and oblique angles remain open.
Forward skidding can opt into signed dry-soil contact including lockup. The closed-form and live
brake cases pass. Oblique rolling publishes shear and sidewall force, with a live opposing chassis
impulse. Directional rolling shear matches FJS-1 side loads around 0.6 slip at four yaw angles.
Reverse travel and the high-slip end of that side-load range remain open.

### The Last Hold ladder and volumetric solver parity (SOFT-04)

The finite-chain rubber model underpredicts Treloar's smallest equibiaxial readings, by about 55% at 2%
extension. The gated held-out traction data in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/volumetric-rubber.test.js`
start at 20% extension and the low-strain miss is recorded in the limits. This remains a constitutive
calibration gap. The large-deformation gelatin and ice measurements also await a hold-out comparison.

The LH-4 rung fixture bends, vibrates and supports a rigid load through live world ports. The filmed
climber and complete tower still need the DYN-07 contact and animation bindings. The fixed-support rung
now runs with a full orthotropic tensor in native vertex blocks. It can tear when independent
tensile, compressive or shear stresses exceed authored strengths. A progressive option softens
tension and shear before tearing. A prescribed tensile seam can open inside a tetrahedron.
Unseeded tensile cracks can nucleate inside a cell from its principal strain and extend
from a tracked front. Authored seams support separate sliding and tearing strains.
Coplanar propagation can use separate opening, sliding and tearing toughness at matched
isotropic lips in small strain. General mixed-mode kinking and orthotropic toughness
remain open.
Automatic fracture evaluates whether each proposed edit fits the native rest mesh before
committing the geometry. Regions below its resolution stay intact for that step.
Dedicated GPU elasticity still needs a same-tick GPU contact and snapshot handoff through the physics framework.
Plane cuts and finite interior incisions work on tetrahedral solids with live rigid anchors and
their own deformable surface colliders. Geometric cutting of bodies with embedded skins, springs,
clusters or separately bound meshes still needs their state transfer.

### Divergence-free narrow-channel surge and boundary exchange (FLUID-01, PA-22)

After building Physics, run `node packages/physics/tests/dfsph-lab.mjs --capillary`.
This coarse setup uses 12 rows across the water column. The interactive and accurate
tiers reach the next Martin–Moyce Table 2 station in normalized intervals of about 0.474 and 0.603 against the
original 0.71–1.14 trial span and measurement allowance 0.149. The coarse accurate profile meets the
first crossing and misses the second, 1.018 against 1.19–1.67 with the same allowance. The interactive
profile remains early at both crossings. The discrete wall correction restores an exact motionless initial lattice.
Both pressure and physical wall viscosity are included. The original release diaphragm still needs an
explicit model for a like-for-like comparison. The parcel contract conserves volume and all momentum components against a closed fixture.
The live HYDRO-01 test also settles whole-particle transfers against a wet periodic cell. Run
`node --test packages/physics/tests/coupling/dfsph-hydro.test.js` for same-tick transfer,
capacity refusal, the last wet depth and snapshot replay. General HYDRO-01 needs a reserve/accept
boundary when its wet/dry limiter can clip signed volume or horizontal momentum. SEA-04 still needs
a paired volume and momentum receipt.

The separated capillary and pressure updates also produce a slow shape oscillation in a free droplet.
Run `node packages/physics/tests/dfsph-capillary-lab.mjs` after building Physics. With 2,176 particles,
20.10 mm equivalent radius and the measured water tension 0.07274 N/m, the first quadrupole period is 0.885 s
against the 0.742 s Rayleigh prediction. Planar energy normalization corrected the earlier 1.481 s result. This fixture starts an equal-volume ellipsoid from rest without
gravity or a container impact. The period provides a separate accuracy check for the planned unified
pressure and surface-energy solve at several resolutions.
The 7,208-particle refined case reads 0.787 s against 0.735 s. Intermediate meshes show non-monotonic period error.

At 18 rows, `--refined` passes both intervals in the accurate profile. Add `--interactive` for the same mesh
using the interactive iteration limits, which reads 0.295 and 0.514 against the two original measurement
spans and their allowances.

The deep-fill standing wave meets the analytic one-frame tolerance. Set the fixture's `ny` to 5 for a
shallower fill that reproduces a period near 1.448 s versus the 1.326 s linear reference. This smaller
depth uses five rows and remains sensitive to the near-surface discretization.

### Energy at a strand contact with a light rigid capsule (SOFT-03)

Fixed for the reciprocal capsule path. Penetration correction previously acted as a
velocity impulse against an effectively immovable capsule. A 1 g sphere sweeping across
an anchored link at 24 m/s could gain more than 2,000 J from an initial 0.288 J. The
contact solve now uses the published rigid inverse mass and inertia and accounts for
the anchored reaction through the witness weights. Tests at 1 g and 2 kg verify the
analytical linear and angular impulse and decreasing kinetic energy.

### Refined thin strand bending (SOFT-03)

Fixed for the default rod solve. A 30 mm fibre with an 80 μm diameter and a 3.45 GPa
Young modulus sagged about 10.55 mm with eight guide links and 60 local constraint passes.
The expected continuum deflection under its own weight is 0.936 mm. Direct banded
constraint projection follows the discrete analytical deflection at 8, 16, 32 and 64 links
within the derived small-angle error. At 64 links it gives 0.906 mm. The regression is
`packages/physics/tests/coupling/strands.test.js`. The optional local profile remains
sensitive to constraint count and is intended for shorter guides.

### The weather's smoke haze is lit as day at night (KB-WEATHER-NIGHTHAZE1)

Fixed (2026-11-26, gap lane B). At 22:00 the timber-valley ridge view showed the night's dark blue starry sky over the
afternoon's tan smoke haze (mean 74.5 against 124.4 at 16:00). Cause: `WeatherDrive.tintFog`
(`packages/weather/src/drive.ts`) lit the sky fog's fixed colour by `hazeLight` of the sun alone, which does not fall
as the sun sets. Fix in weather: the haze's light (`airLight` in drive.ts) hands the day share over to the night's by
the sky's own blend (`Sky.nightFactor`, or the same smoothstep of its sun): (1 - n) times the day share plus n times
the moon under the clouds and the twilight sky (`Sky.moonUnderClouds`, `Sky.twilightLight`, intensity times colour,
each through the load at its own elevation) over the sky's `lighting.intensity`. The timber-valley night moon is 0.19
against the noon sun's 5, so the night haze is about 4 percent of the day's, bluer, as the moonlit ground is. Regression:
`packages/weather/tests/smoke.test.js` ("the smoke haze hands its sunlight over ..."), failing before the fix. Still:
`node packages/scenes/test/timber-valley-still.mjs --views=ridge --query=hour=22 --out=<folder>` gives mean 25.1 (sky
35, 48, 83 over a valley of 3, 1, 0), against 74.5 before. The valley under the blowup smoke now reads black at night:
see KB-WEATHER-FIREHAZE1 for the fire's light the haze still lacks.

### Natural granular runout and bed exchange (EARTH-02)

The new finite-volume entry holds a resting layer on a bank, follows the live terrain around relief, and replays its state after restore. Arrested material can now raise the shared bed through mass-conservative deposition. For a runout over loose saturated sediment, the basal pore-support fraction is fixed and the bed still needs a physical remobilization path. The cause is the constant-density layer and missing sediment transport and effective-stress state. The roughness tier now reproduces dry critical start/stop behavior and two independent bead-bed front speeds. The remaining queue work covers erosion, saturated deposits, additional materials, incoming and outgoing couplings, and use of the new solver in legacy terrain callers. A snapshot taken before the first `bedChange` sum cannot restore after stepping because the world allocates its sum region at the first step. Take the coupled checkpoint after the first completed frame until the setup-time accumulator request is resolved. The coastal edge supplies signed displacement to SEA-06, while water-to-slide feedback still needs a reciprocal momentum model and measured nearshore wave shapes. EARTH-08 now supplies horizontal inertia and changing support load. An evolving pore-pressure state is still needed for saturated material under seismic shaking.

### SEA-10 stiff air-pressure network

**OPEN KB-SEA-AIRSWEEPS1.** After building Physics, run `node packages/physics/scripts/sea10-ruponen-measured.mjs --check-warnings`. The six-room Ruponen pressure graph reaches 200 air sweeps on each of its first five 5 Hz steps. The corrected first-second water residual is at most 5.80e−18 m³ and both initially dry stair apertures have zero water flux. The air residual is still up to 1.91e−6 kg. At 20 Hz the air solve caps on 71 of the first 400 steps. Open dry doors and the narrow vents couple rooms of unequal pneumatic compliance. The separate fixed point air sweep converges slowly near equal pressure. The coded `Flooding.convergenceWarning` surfaces the cap; a coupled pressure solve with a physical residual check remains open.

### SEA-15 submerged jet crater depth and redistribution

**OPEN KB-TRACER-CRATERFLOW1.** Run `node packages/physics/scripts/sea15-jet-scour-measured.mjs`. For two independently metered jets over a granular bed, the resulting final crater deficit is 1.29 and 1.00 cm³ on the 5 mm grid against 57.49 and 116.47 cm³ from the published ultrasonic profiles. The existing bed writer estimates pickup from projected jet momentum. This setup lacks a resolved return current and evolving wall shear over the new crater. The reported gross lift ledger counts repeated entrainment. The experiment measures final morphology, and a directly measured suspended-mass benchmark remains open. [Experiment](https://doi.org/10.1002/aic.70336)

### Fixed zero-acceleration carried-water contact

A zero-gravity frame using a vessel's carried floodwater failed before the contact solve. SEA-10 input validation required positive gravity although the displacement-free carried-water test uses zero. `Flooding` now keeps its pressure and carried mass at a nonnegative prescribed gravity. Zero specific weight contributes zero hydrostatic head. `packages/physics/tests/flooding.test.js` checks the closed tank exactly, and `packages/physics/tests/coupling/crush-contact-inertia.test.js` checks a real hull's wet normal, transverse and sliding impulses.

### Fixed: SEA-03 returned carrier-only normals and pressure below the bed

A placed wave changes the component amplitudes with position. The previous normal used the derivative of carrier phase alone, which disagreed with the derivative of the rendered surface inside the event. The normal now includes both amplitude derivatives in the linear and bound terms. A separate pressure query omitted the wet depth test and evaluated Wheeler stretching below the bed. It now gives zero under the bed consistently with the velocity query. Malformed currents are rejected before writing caller samples. `packages/physics/tests/rogue.test.js` checks both slope axes by converging differences, finite pressure at the bed, zero pressure below it and exact output preservation on rejection.

### Fixed: SEA-01 could accept a partially advanced spectrum after invalid wind

The step wrote its clock, outgoing spectrum and prior cells' friction before reading every wind sample. It also used forcing coordinates as if wind and wave fields always shared an origin. It now advances private candidates through every owed interval, reads wind in its own signed cell, and publishes only after the candidate is finite. The spectrum field reports the current solver cell immediately after origin shifts and restore. A failed JONSWAP normalization also leaves the caller's output untouched. Regressions run in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/waves.test.js` and `packages/physics/tests/waves.test.js`.

### Fixed: SEA-05 could publish partial surf outputs and read stale wave height after restore

The surf previously changed step memory before validating its shallow-water samples, and its height query read output scratch from the last advanced step. It now prepares the energy, roller, radiation-stress forcing, wet sand and shore statistics in candidates before publication. Height and angle queries use the stored directional energy, including after restoring a checkpoint. The coupled rejection and rewind tests are in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/surf.test.js`.

### Fixed: SEA-07 could overwrite pressure and tidal terms before validating the forcing

A nonfinite pressure in a later grid cell previously left some of the surge's saved pressure and tide terms updated, while its output potential still described the previous step. The solver now stages the wet mask, raw terms and potential, validates the full Earth-fixed celestial port and publishes both regions together. It copies the six body coordinates before sampling callbacks. The regression in `packages/physics/tests/coupling/surge.test.js` checks late pressure failure, malformed celestial layout and exact corrected replay.

### Fixed: ATMO-04 rain transport used one arrival path for the whole shaft

A narrow moving rain cell kept its cloud-base peak below the cloud even though large and small drops arrive from different places and times. Precipitation now transports 192 mass-weighted size nodes per active species through the layer wind and uses local temperature for the phase share. A late invalid source or wind sample fails before copying any moments to the caller. The uniform-air characteristic and invalid-source replay regressions are in `packages/weather/tests/precipitation.test.js`.

### Fixed: ICE-04 pack ice read foreign flow from the world arena and exported a stale origin

Registered flow and rigid rows now use the bank declared by the port. The solver stages positions and forcing values before calling a field, then reacquires the arena views for the step. A late bad flow leaves accepted floes, reaction impulses and work intact. New ports name the live host cell, including after an origin shift or restore. See `packages/physics/tests/coupling/pack-ice.test.js`.

### Fixed: ICE-01 could overwrite accepted snow and runoff during an invalid native step

Snowpack copies registered forcing from the owning memory, then samples wind without retaining that bank's views. Native snow, cover, heat and meltwater update candidate regions. A nonfinite candidate leaves the previous publications and render revision intact. After an origin shift, new ports use the live host cell. See `packages/physics/tests/coupling/snowpack.test.js`.

### Fixed: ICE-03 could publish a partial wake when a derived melt flux exceeded its range

Native body rows, pending calving, freshwater and signed wakes stage before acceptance. A malformed foreign calving bank or a late derivative overflow leaves the previous ports, work and bodies intact. The published origin follows the live solver cell immediately after shift or restore. See `packages/physics/tests/coupling/iceberg.test.js`.

### KB-GLACIER-ACCEPTED1 — A glacier could report unrepresentable volume or the wrong origin cell (FIXED)

- **Repro:** Add a two-cell 100 m column grid with 1e153 m spacing and read the ice budget, or set
  a negative origin cell on an ordinary glacier and read its six exported ports directly.
- **Cause:** The native candidate checked each ice column separately, leaving the combined volume
  unchecked. The solver also published a constant origin rather than the host's saved cell.
- **Fix:** The native step validates the total ice volume before publication and the six ports
  read the live host cell through a shift or restore. The coupling test preserves the exact
  accepted state through a rejected tick and replays the next valid ticks.
- **Regression:** [glacier coupling](../packages/physics/tests/coupling/glacier.test.js).

### KB-LOCOMOTION-ACCEPTED1 — Terrain sampling could invalidate a staged ground animal (FIXED)

- **Repro:** Grow plain Wasm memory in a terrain sampler while a group prepares its contacts. A sampler can also
  try to change live leg commands during a step. Direct dispatch to a reported bed in a separate bank could read
  an unrelated host address, and the two direct publications reported the zero origin.
- **Cause:** The caller held trial memory views across the terrain callback and assumed every bed used host
  memory. It allowed mutation from the sampler and tagged both publications with a constant cell.
- **Fix:** Obtain current views after callbacks, refuse reentrant writes, validate the owning bed bank and publish
  the host's live cell. A failed trial leaves the accepted pose, anchors, contacts and work receipt intact.
- **Regression:** [locomotion coupling](../packages/physics/tests/coupling/locomotion.test.js).

### KB-FALLING-ACCEPTED1 — Falling callbacks and output could bypass accepted state (FIXED)

- **Repro:** Return a missing normal from the second sphere's sweep, call the solver recursively from its air
  sampler, or request a draw buffer containing one finite f32 position and one position above f32 range.
- **Cause:** Raw sample access exposed language errors and allowed callbacks to enter the same scratch state.
  Pose publication and f32 conversion wrote directly into accepted or caller-owned buffers.
- **Fix:** Refuse reentry, validate candidate samples and complete pose and draw buffers, and publish all accepted
  rows together. The pose port reports the live signed origin. Previous accepted work remains readable after rejection.
- **Regression:** [falling coupling](../packages/physics/tests/coupling/falling.test.js).

### KB-GROUNDWATER-ACCEPTED1 — A late outlet overflow could publish an invalid aquifer (FIXED)

- **Repro:** Supply a recharge step whose underground volume is finite but whose world-second seepage rate exceeds
  f64. A valid recharge or terrain field in a separate memory also reads the wrong bank.
- **Cause:** The kernel wrote columns and cumulative balances directly to accepted memory. The readers treated
  every field's address as local memory. The reported origin was the last saved solver-step cell.
- **Fix:** Validate the complete trial columns, budgets and storage before accepting them. Use the input bank
  that owns each field and publish the live world cell. The previous state and work receipt survive rejection.
- **Regression:** [groundwater coupling](../packages/physics/tests/coupling/groundwater.test.js).

### KB-VORTEX-ACCEPTED1 — A late forcing error could leave partially updated vortex outputs (FIXED)

- **Repro:** Update a probe with a moving vortex, then supply a late invalid wet-grid depth or a foreign field
  whose words are misaligned. The old step could publish new probes before rejecting the coupled input.
- **Cause:** Wind and pressure, rigid loads and water contributions were written in order directly into
  the accepted banks, and the exported cell was the last sampled cell.
- **Fix:** Read input in owning memory, stage finite outputs across the entire solver and publish the
  live signed cell. Use coded errors with a fix for inconsistent input. The coupled clock is explicit.
- **Regression:** [vortex coupling](../packages/physics/tests/coupling/vortices.test.js).

### Open: SOUND-04 acoustic modes and source coverage

SOUND-04 accepts source-specific resonant frequencies, gains and damping, with authored examples for
four material categories. Contact and joint rupture are live. Geometry-derived modes, location-dependent
excitation and pressure radiation remain open, as do the solid fracture, ice, fluid, combustion and
thunder sources in the coupling map. The simply supported plate comparison reproduces supplied
frequencies in PCM and records discrepancies against independent measurements.
[SOUND-04 measured limits](limits.md#sound-04-simply-supported-aluminum-plates).

### Open: BIO-02 species-specific shade response

The generic defaults overpredict all 16 measured red maple heights in the independent shade-tent
comparison. Above 20% full light the two-year axial extension is identical across treatments once an
internode reaches its configured maximum. Sustained multi-internode production, branch shedding, plastic
deformation of existing wood and explicit root and leaf physiology remain open.
[Shade comparison and sensitivity](limits.md#bio-02-red-maple-growth-under-field-shade).

### Open: BIO-03 competition and survival calibration

BIO-03 uses reduced Q16 crown overlap, growth and mortality with authored site and species settings.
The independent Douglas-fir spacing diagnostic misses three of four reported final survival intervals
and is sensitive to the initial crown radius. Explicit layered light extinction, measured growth-dependent
mortality, crown allometry and full stand succession calibration remain open.
[Measured limits](limits.md#bio-03-douglas-fir-survival-in-the-wind-river-spacing-trial).

### AERO-02 downwind lift and drag deficit

The [S3 rigid-sail diagnostic](limits.md#aero-02-measured-cambered-sail-polar) shows lift and drag underprediction at typical downwind trim after grid and incidence sensitivity. The solver uses instantaneous horseshoes in attached panels and a flat-plate load for separated panels. It has no shed wake state, leading-edge separation history, inter-sail shielding or porous canopy law. A self-excited flag wake, measured cambered-sail agreement and parachute and tent behaviour remain open.
